zh-Hant.title: 暑期設計課 II：環境教育亭
zh-Hant.description:
由塔、平台與水上步道組成的公園展亭，以平面、剖面與木條模型推演。

建築設計｜展亭｜環境教育｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Larger stick model of the tower in basswood, plywood and tracing paper.
以椴木條、夾板與描圖紙製作的大型塔體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The pavilion invites visitors from a busy setting gradually into nature. It needs places to meditate, look out, gather and observe local ecology.
captions: Functional diagram of the five spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座展亭引導訪客從喧囂環境逐步走入自然。它需要提供冥想、眺望、聚會與觀察在地生態的場所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The program was split into a contemplation niche, a watch tower, a group learning deck, an exhibition corner and a sensory walkway. A functional diagram arranged them around a green platform.
captions: Sections through the tower, deck and walkway.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 機能被拆解為冥想角落、瞭望塔、團體學習平台、展示角與感官步道。機能圖將它們環繞一座綠色平台配置。
captions: 穿越塔、平台與步道的剖面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sections test how the tower rises above the trees while the walkway stays low over the water. Basswood and card models check the joints between the parts.
captions: Pavilion model in basswood and card.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 剖面測試塔體如何高出樹冠，而步道則低伏於水面之上。椴木與卡紙模型檢查各部分之間的銜接。
captions: 椴木與卡紙製作的展亭模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A larger stick model develops the tower as an open frame of stairs, trusses and enclosed rooms. Hand sketches study the light and depth inside the structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 大型木條模型將塔體發展為由樓梯、桁架與封閉房間組成的開放框架。手繪草圖研究結構內部的光線與深度。

sections.heading: Summer Studio II - An Education Pavilion Leading from Noise into Nature
sections.body: Visitors are meant to be drawn gradually from a busy setting into nature by this pavilion, which must offer places to meditate, look out, gather and observe local ecology. The programme was first split into a contemplation niche, a watch tower, a group learning deck, an exhibition corner and a sensory walkway, and a functional diagram arranged them around a green platform. Sections then tested how the tower could rise above the trees while the walkway stays low over the water. Basswood and card models checked the joints between each part. Developed finally in a larger stick model, the tower became an open frame of stairs, trusses and enclosed rooms, while hand sketches studied the light and depth within the structure. High and low, open and enclosed are woven together here, so that the very passage into nature becomes a quiet lesson in ecology, taught by height, water and the slow shifting of light.

zh-Hant.heading: 暑期設計課II-從喧囂走入自然的環境教育亭
zh-Hant.body: 這座展亭要引導訪客從喧囂的環境逐步走入自然，並提供冥想、眺望、聚會與觀察在地生態的場所。機能首先被拆解為冥想角落、瞭望塔、團體學習平台、展示角與感官步道，一張機能圖將它們環繞一座綠色平台配置。接著，剖面測試塔體如何高出樹冠，步道又如何低伏於水面之上；椴木與卡紙模型則逐一檢查各部分之間的銜接。最終，大型木條模型將塔體發展為由樓梯、桁架與封閉房間組成的開放框架，手繪草圖研究結構內部的光線與深度。高與低、開與閉在此交織，讓走進自然的過程本身，成為一堂安靜的生態課。

pins.title: Rift Pavilion
pins.description:
A twisted wind tower of rotated floors that turns a sunken city plaza into a quiet green retreat.

Architecture | Pavilion | Wind tower | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 裂隙展亭
zh-Hant.description:
以旋轉樓板構成的扭轉風塔，將下沉的城市廣場轉化為安靜的綠色休憩地。

建築設計｜展亭｜風塔｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Tower model in plywood, frosted acetate and green fibre.
以夾板、霧面醋酸片與綠色纖維製作的塔體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site is a sunken city plaza that feels cut off, underused and short of greenery. The project turns this isolation into a chance for a quiet, green retreat.
captions: The plaza site and its street map.
References for the concept: wind towers, a twisted tower, ruins and lava flow.
Aerial view of the tower in the plaza.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地是一處下沉的城市廣場，與城市隔絕、使用率低且缺乏綠意。這個作品將這份隔絕轉化為打造安靜綠色休憩地的機會。
captions: 概念參考：風塔、扭轉塔、廢墟與熔岩流。
塔體位於廣場中的鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The concept draws on traditional windcatchers that capture air from above and cool it through underground water. A twisted form was chosen to catch wind from all sides.
captions: Floor plans rotating up the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 概念取自傳統捕風塔，從高處擷取空氣，並透過地下水流降溫。扭轉的形體則用來從各個方向捕捉風。
captions: 沿塔身逐層旋轉的平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rotated floors form a spiral void that brings air and light down through the tower. Lower levels stay shaded, middle levels hold plants, and the top opens to the sky through an oval skylight.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 旋轉的樓板形成螺旋狀中空，將空氣與光線引入塔內。下層保持陰涼，中層種植植物，頂層則透過橢圓天窗向天空開放。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A staircase circles the centre and reveals changing light and views on the way up. Models show the planted floors and the water channels that run through the site.
captions: Renders of the tower in the plaza and its lower spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 樓梯環繞中心而上，沿途展現變化的光線與景觀。模型呈現種植樓層，以及穿越基地的水道。
captions: 塔樓在廣場中的透視與下層空間。

sections.heading: Rift Pavilion - A Green Refuge Inside a Twisted Wind Tower
sections.body: The site is a sunken city plaza that feels cut off, underused and short of greenery, and the project chooses to turn this isolation into the chance for a quiet, green retreat. Its concept draws on traditional windcatchers, which capture air from above and cool it through underground water, while a twisted form was chosen to catch wind from every side. Rotated floors form a spiral void that draws air and light down through the tower. Lower levels stay shaded, middle levels hold plants, and the top opens to the sky through an oval skylight. A staircase circles the centre in the final design, revealing changing light and views on the way up, and the models show the planted floors alongside the water channels that run through the site. A forgotten urban rift thus becomes a breathing tower, inviting wind, water and greenery back into the plaza and offering the city a cool, slow interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 裂隙展亭-扭轉風塔裡的綠色避難所
zh-Hant.body: 基地是一處下沉的城市廣場，與城市隔絕、使用率低且缺乏綠意；作品選擇將這份隔絕轉化為打造安靜綠色休憩地的契機。概念取自傳統捕風塔，從高處擷取空氣，再透過地下水流降溫，扭轉的形體則用來從各個方向捕捉風。旋轉的樓板形成螺旋狀的中空，將空氣與光線引入塔內；下層保持陰涼，中層種植植物，頂層透過橢圓天窗向天空敞開。最終，一道樓梯環繞中心而上，沿途展現不斷變化的光線與景觀，模型也呈現了種植樓層與穿越基地的水道。被遺忘的城市裂隙，就此成為一座會呼吸的塔，讓風、水與綠意重新回到廣場。

pins.title: Reimagined Vaultypes
pins.description:
Historic vault types redrawn as light frameworks of rattan, wire and mesh for temporary public rest spaces.

Architecture | Temporary pavilion | Vault structure | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重構拱頂類型
zh-Hant.description:
將歷史拱頂類型重新詮釋為藤條、金屬線與網材構成的輕量框架，作為臨時公共休憩空間。

建築設計｜臨時展亭｜拱頂結構｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model in rattan rods, wire mesh, metal wire and wooden dowels.
以藤條、金屬網、金屬線與木釘製作的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project designs temporary public spaces for people waiting in airport transit zones, such as asylum seekers. These spaces offer rest, social contact and calm through light and geometry.
captions: Transit-hall shelters and historic vaults that inspired the pavilion.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品為在機場轉運區等候的人們，例如尋求庇護者，設計臨時公共空間。這些空間透過光線與幾何提供休息、交流與平靜。
captions: 啟發這座亭子的轉運大廳收容空間與歷史拱頂。
比較各種拱頂類型的草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches compared barrel, cross, quadripartite, fan and sail vaults for structure and proportion. Stripped of stone, each vault was reduced to lines and curves that meet.
captions: Side and top views set on a square grid.
Chipboard study models from bent strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖比較筒拱、交叉拱、四分肋拱、扇形拱與帆拱的結構與比例。去除石材後，每種拱頂被簡化為交會的線與曲線。
captions: 置於方格上的側視與俯視圖。
以彎折紙板條製作的研究模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Chipboard strips bent over moulds tested rib spacing and spatial logic. The vault types were then composed into one system on a grid to keep the scale consistent.
captions: Bending and assembling the rattan arches.
Rattan rib tests on the cutting mat.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以模具彎折的紙板條測試肋的間距與空間邏輯。接著將各種拱頂組合在方格上，形成尺度一致的系統。
captions: 切割墊上的藤條肋測試。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model, rattan forms the quadripartite and fan vaults while bent wire defines the cross vaults. Wooden dowels give vertical support and wire mesh adds depth beneath the ribs.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以藤條構成四分肋拱與扇形拱，以彎折金屬線界定交叉拱。木釘提供垂直支撐，肋下的金屬網則增添層次。

sections.heading: Reimagined Vaultypes - Rattan Vaults for Those Who Wait
sections.body: People waiting in airport transit zones, asylum seekers among them, are the users of this project, which designs temporary public spaces offering rest, social contact and calm through light and geometry. Sketches compared barrel, cross, quadripartite, fan and sail vaults for structure and proportion, and once stripped of stone each vault was reduced to lines and curves that meet. Chipboard strips bent over moulds then tested rib spacing and spatial logic. The vault types were composed into a single system on a grid, keeping the scale consistent throughout. In the final model, rattan forms the quadripartite and fan vaults while bent wire defines the cross vaults; wooden dowels give vertical support, and wire mesh adds depth beneath the ribs. The weight of historic vaulting is thereby made light, raising a gentle canopy over long hours of waiting, where uncertainty might briefly give way to shelter, shade and a sense of being received.

zh-Hant.heading: 重構拱頂類型-為等候者編織的藤拱
zh-Hant.body: 在機場轉運區等候的人們，例如尋求庇護者，是這件作品的服務對象；它設計臨時公共空間，透過光線與幾何提供休息、交流與平靜。草圖比較了筒拱、交叉拱、四分肋拱、扇形拱與帆拱的結構與比例；去除石材之後，每一種拱頂都被簡化為交會的線與曲線。以模具彎折的紙板條，測試了肋的間距與空間邏輯，各種拱頂隨後被組合在方格上，形成尺度一致的系統。最終，藤條構成四分肋拱與扇形拱，彎折的金屬線界定交叉拱，木釘提供垂直支撐，肋下的金屬網則增添層次。厚重的歷史拱頂由此變得輕盈，為漫長的等待撐起一片溫柔的天幕。

pins.title: Labyrinth of Faith and Ruin
pins.description:
A circular maze tower in resin, acrylic and clay that retells a journey through a ruined world.

Spatial Narrative | Model | Maze tower | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 信念與廢墟的迷宮
zh-Hant.description:
以樹脂、壓克力與黏土製作的環形迷宮塔，重述一段穿越廢墟世界的旅程。

空間敘事｜模型｜迷宮塔｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower model lit from within.
由內部照亮的塔體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project was inspired by a post-apocalyptic novel about a father and son on a long journey. It asks how that path can be rebuilt as a maze where life and death seem reversed.
captions: Concept sketch of the circular maze.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品的靈感來自一部描寫父子長途跋涉的末日小說。它探問如何將這段旅程重建為一座生死彷彿顛倒的迷宮。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sketch mapped the journey as rings of walls around a central goal. At the centre sits a fragile belief that keeps the travellers moving forward.
captions: Making the walls, base and resin sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖將旅程描繪為環繞中心目標的層層牆體。中心是一份讓旅人持續前行的脆弱信念。
captions: 製作牆體、基座與樹脂海面的過程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Circular walls and floor plates create a fragmented terrain, linked by small ladders. Dark acrylic and clay give a worn wooden texture, while yellow layers stand for flashbacks breaking through.
captions: The tower on its resin sea base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 環形牆體與樓板構成破碎的地形，並以小梯子相連。深色壓克力與黏土營造出磨損的木質紋理，黃色層次則象徵穿透而出的回憶。
captions: 置於樹脂海面基座上的塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower rises from an epoxy sea that holds the remains of a lost civilisation. Close views show the narrow passages and ladders that make up the journey.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔從環氧樹脂海面中升起，海中留存著消逝文明的殘骸。近景呈現構成旅程的狹窄通道與梯子。

sections.heading: Labyrinth of Faith and Ruin - A Journey Where Life and Death Reverse
sections.body: A post-apocalyptic novel about a father and son on a long journey inspired the project, which asks how that path could be rebuilt as a maze where life and death seem reversed. An early sketch mapped the journey as rings of walls around a central goal, and at that centre sits a fragile belief that keeps the travellers moving forward. Circular walls and floor plates create a fragmented terrain, linked by small ladders. Dark acrylic and clay lend a worn wooden texture, while yellow layers stand for flashbacks breaking through. The finished tower rises from an epoxy sea that holds the remains of a lost civilisation, and close views reveal the narrow passages and ladders that make up the journey. Literary despair and hope are thus compressed into a ruin that can be climbed, where faith glows faintly at the deepest point and every rung becomes a decision to keep going.

zh-Hant.heading: 信念與廢墟的迷宮-生死顛倒的末日旅程
zh-Hant.body: 一部描寫父子長途跋涉的末日小說，啟發了這件作品；它追問的是，如何將那段旅程重建為一座生死彷彿顛倒的迷宮。草圖將旅程描繪為環繞中心目標的層層牆體，而居於中心的，是一份讓旅人持續前行的脆弱信念。環形牆體與樓板構成破碎的地形，以小梯子彼此相連；深色壓克力與黏土營造出磨損的木質紋理，黃色層次則象徵穿透而出的回憶。最終，高塔從環氧樹脂的海面升起，海中留存著消逝文明的殘骸，近景裡狹窄的通道與梯子，構成了整段旅程。文學中的絕望與希望，由此被壓縮進一座可以攀爬的廢墟，信念在最深處微微發光。

pins.title: Between Chaos and Clarity
pins.description:
Plaster blocks and layered clear PVC that turn a personal rhythm of thinking into structure.

Spatial Design | Concept model | Material contrast | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 混沌與清晰之間
zh-Hant.description:
以石膏量塊與層疊透明PVC，將個人的思考節奏轉化為結構。

空間設計｜概念模型｜材料對比｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model in plaster, PVC sheets and PVC rods.
以石膏、PVC板與PVC棒製作的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began from the student's curiosity about their own way of thinking. It treats a restless rhythm of attention as a source of design rather than a weakness.
captions: Tests of layering, material contrast and fragmentation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品源自學生對自身思考方式的好奇。它將不安定的專注節奏視為設計的來源，而非缺點。
captions: 層疊、材料對比與碎裂的測試。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The experience was summed up in three ideas: layering, material contrast and fragmentation. Each idea was tested in a quick model before the final piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生將經驗歸納為三個關鍵概念：層疊、材料對比與碎裂。每個概念都先以快速模型測試，再進入最終作品。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plaster stands for focus while clear PVC expresses scattered thought. Layered and cracked plates show how the mind reorganises information to find order.
captions: Making the plaster and PVC pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石膏代表專注，透明PVC則表達發散的思緒。層疊與碎裂的板片呈現心智如何重組資訊以找到秩序。
captions: 製作石膏與 PVC 構件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Sharp triangular openings in the walls mark moments of heightened awareness. Gaps between the four blocks suggest mental jumps that still connect.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 牆面上尖銳的三角開口標示出感知高度敏銳的時刻。四個量塊之間的縫隙則暗示仍然相連的思緒跳躍。

sections.heading: Between Chaos and Clarity - Mapping Thought in Plaster and PVC
sections.body: Curiosity about a personal way of thinking set the project in motion, treating a restless rhythm of attention as a source of design rather than a weakness. The experience was distilled into three ideas, layering, material contrast and fragmentation, each tested in a quick model before the final piece took shape. Materials were given distinct roles: plaster stands for focus, clear PVC expresses scattered thought, and layered, cracked plates show how the mind reorganises information until order appears. Sharp triangular openings in the walls mark moments of heightened awareness. Between the four blocks, narrow gaps suggest mental leaps that nonetheless remain connected. Inner turbulence is in this way gently translated into space, and difference, rather than being hidden, becomes a clear and singular logic of composition, one in which the very jumps of attention are given form, light and a place to stand.

zh-Hant.heading: 混沌與清晰之間-以石膏與PVC描繪思緒
zh-Hant.body: 作品源自學生對自身思考方式的好奇，將不安定的專注節奏視為設計的來源，而非缺點。這份經驗被歸納為三個關鍵概念：層疊、材料對比與碎裂；每個概念都先以快速模型測試，再進入最終作品。材料承擔了意義的分工：石膏代表專注，透明PVC表達發散的思緒，層疊與碎裂的板片則呈現心智如何重組資訊、從中找到秩序。牆面上尖銳的三角開口，標示出感知高度敏銳的時刻；四個量塊之間的縫隙，暗示思緒雖然跳躍卻仍彼此相連。內在的混亂由此被溫柔地轉譯為空間，差異不再被遮掩，反而成為一種清晰而獨特的構成邏輯。

pins.title: Between Waters
pins.description:
Platforms and paths along a campus stream that let students pause, study and rest beside water.

Landscape Architecture | Campus stream | Learning spaces | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 水之間
zh-Hant.description:
沿著校園溪流配置的平台與步道，讓學生能在水邊停留、讀書與休憩。

景觀建築｜校園溪流｜學習空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Site model in wooden board, stone, wax, acrylic, epoxy resin, clay and foam.
以木板、石頭、蠟、壓克力、環氧樹脂、黏土與泡棉製作的基地模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student often watched a stream outside the campus lounge and found calm in its flow during busy study. The project asks how architecture could merge water and learning.
captions: The campus master plan with the stream running through it.
Watercolour of the stream and its banks.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生常在校園交誼廳看著窗外的溪流，在忙碌的課業中從流水裡找到平靜。這個作品探問建築如何將水與學習融合。
captions: 溪流穿過的校園配置圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Watercolour and pencil studies recorded the banks, bridges and trees along the stream. The stream's movement was then translated into circulation paths and platforms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 水彩與鉛筆研究記錄了溪流沿岸的堤岸、橋梁與樹木。接著將溪水的流動轉譯為動線與平台。
captions: 塑造地形與水道的過程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The topography was shaped in foam and clay, and varied spaces were built from templates. Acrylic sheets stand for waterways while wax and epoxy resin capture the fluid quality of water.
captions: A raised pavilion by the bank.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 地形以泡棉與黏土塑造，多樣的空間則以模板製作。壓克力板代表水道，蠟與環氧樹脂則捕捉水的流動質感。
captions: 跨越溪流的壓克力水道。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Red boxes and long bridges step along the stream and frame places to study and meditate. Clear ramps link the platforms so that nature shapes how people move through the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 紅色盒體與長橋沿著溪流錯落，圍塑出讀書與冥想的場所。透明坡道串連各個平台，讓自然決定人們在基地中的移動方式。

sections.heading: Between Waters - Letting a Stream Shape the Paths of Learning
sections.body: A stream outside the campus lounge, watched during busy weeks of study, once offered the student a sense of calm, and the project asks how architecture might merge water and learning. Watercolour and pencil studies recorded the banks, bridges and trees along its course, before the stream's movement was translated into circulation paths and platforms. Topography was shaped in foam and clay, with varied spaces built from templates. Acrylic sheets stand in for waterways, while wax and epoxy resin capture the fluid quality of water itself. In the final model, red boxes and long bridges step along the stream, framing places to study and to meditate, and clear ramps link the platforms so that nature decides how people move through the site. Learning is no longer sealed indoors here; it unfolds alongside the sound of water, becoming a slow and attentive wandering in which the landscape itself sets the pace of thought.

zh-Hant.heading: 水之間-讓溪流決定學習的路徑
zh-Hant.body: 校園交誼廳窗外的溪流，曾在忙碌的課業中帶給學生平靜；作品由此追問，建築能否將水與學習融為一體。水彩與鉛筆研究記錄了沿岸的堤岸、橋梁與樹木，溪水的流動隨後被轉譯為動線與平台。地形以泡棉與黏土塑造，多樣的空間依模板製作；壓克力板代表水道，蠟與環氧樹脂則捕捉水的流動質感。最終，紅色盒體與長橋沿著溪流錯落，圍塑出讀書與冥想的場所，透明坡道串連起各個平台，讓自然決定人們在基地中如何移動。學習在此不再被封閉於室內，而是順著水聲展開，成為一段緩慢而專注的漫遊。

pins.title: City of Masks
pins.description:
Traditional ritual masks abstracted into spatial models that read the hidden emotions of a fast-moving city.

Shenzhen | Spatial design | Ritual masks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 面具之城
zh-Hant.description:
將傳統儺戲面具抽象為空間模型，解讀快速變動城市中隱藏的情緒。

深圳｜空間設計｜儺戲面具｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final pavilion-like construct in laser-cut board and wood.
以雷射切割板材與木材製作的最終展亭式構築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student grew up in a city of speed, migration and reinvention, but watched traditional ritual opera with grandparents in the countryside. The project asks whether urban spaces, like masks, also hide the emotions of city life.
captions: The four Nuo masks used as the starting point.
Line drawings traced from four ritual masks.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在一座充滿速度、遷徙與更新的城市長大，卻曾隨祖父母在鄉間觀看傳統儺戲。這個作品探問城市空間是否也像面具一樣，隱藏著城市生活的情緒。
captions: 作為起點的四張儺面具。
描繪自四張儺戲面具的線稿。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Four masks were traced, then reduced to geometric lines and abstracted into grids. Each mask carries a character trait, from discipline to care, loyalty and energy.
captions: The four Shenzhen districts paired with each mask.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪四張面具，再將其簡化為幾何線條並抽象為網格。每張面具都承載一種性格特質，從紀律、關懷到忠誠與能量。
captions: 與每張面具對應的四個深圳城區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each trait became a small spatial model, using vertical planes, soft curves, rigid grids or radiating lines. Field research in several districts of the city linked each model to an urban character.
captions: Discipline and protection: balanced planes around an axis.
Kindness and care: soft, enclosed curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每一種特質都被轉化為小型空間模型，運用垂直面、柔和曲線、剛性網格或放射線條。學生在城市多個區域的田野調查，將每個模型連結到一種城市性格。
captions: 紀律與守護：環繞軸線的平衡面。
慈愛與關懷：柔和圍合的曲線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final composition joins the four models into an abstract pavilion of curved ribbons, corrugated towers and reflective floors. It turns the hidden geometry of ritual masks into a sculptural spatial language.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終構成將四個模型結合為由曲面飾帶、瓦楞塔體與反光地面組成的抽象展亭。它將儺戲面具中隱藏的幾何轉化為雕塑性的空間語言。

sections.heading: City of Masks - The Urban Geometry Hidden in Ritual Masks
sections.body: Growing up in a city of speed, migration and reinvention, the student had nonetheless watched traditional ritual opera with grandparents in the countryside, and the project asks whether urban spaces, like masks, also conceal the emotions of city life. Four masks were traced, reduced to geometric lines and abstracted into grids, each carrying a character trait from discipline to care, loyalty and energy. Every trait then became a small spatial model built from vertical planes, soft curves, rigid grids or radiating lines. Field research across several districts linked each model to a distinct urban character. The final composition joins the four models into an abstract pavilion of curved ribbons, corrugated towers and reflective floors. In this way the hidden geometry of an ancient ritual becomes a sculptural spatial language, and a rural memory finds a new face within the restless city.

zh-Hant.heading: 面具之城-儺戲面具中隱藏的城市幾何
zh-Hant.body: 在一座充滿速度、遷徙與更新的城市長大，學生卻曾隨祖父母在鄉間觀看傳統儺戲；作品於是追問，城市空間是否也像面具一樣，隱藏著都市生活的情緒。四張面具被描繪下來，簡化為幾何線條，再抽象為網格，各自承載紀律、關懷、忠誠與能量等性格。每一種特質接著化為小型空間模型，運用垂直面、柔和曲線、剛性網格或放射線條；在城市多個區域的田野調查，則將每個模型連結到一種城市性格。最終，四個模型結合為由曲面飾帶、瓦楞塔體與反光地面組成的抽象展亭。古老儀式中的幾何，被轉化為雕塑性的空間語言，讓鄉野的記憶在都市裡找到新的面容。

pins.title: Geometry of Divinity
pins.description:
A line-and-arc composition lifted into a white and mirror-chrome model of discs, stairs and columns.

Architecture | Concept model | Geometry | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 神性的幾何
zh-Hant.description:
將線與弧的平面構成延伸為由圓盤、樓梯與柱體組成的白色與鏡面鉻模型。

建築設計｜概念模型｜幾何｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model in resin and mirror chrome vinyl.
以樹脂與鏡面鉻貼膜製作的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project studies how simple geometric shapes can create spaces that feel sacred. It began from extracting elements from a modern master's buildings that achieve this effect.
captions: Precedent photos of the architecture that inspired the composition.
Plane composition of parallel lines and arcs.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品研究簡單的幾何形狀如何創造出具神聖感的空間。它從萃取現代建築大師作品中達成此效果的元素開始。
captions: 啟發構成的建築先例照片。
由平行線與弧線構成的平面構成。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The extracted elements were redrawn as a two-dimensional composition of parallel lines and arcs. Circles, bands and stepped lines set up the rules for the model.
captions: Stair and discs rising from the columns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 萃取的元素被重新繪製為由平行線與弧線構成的二維構成。圓形、帶狀與階梯狀線條確立了模型的規則。
captions: 從柱體升起的樓梯與圓盤。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The composition was turned into a three-dimensional model in Rhino. Discs became platforms, bands became stairs and arcs became curved screens.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生在Rhino中將平面構成轉化為三維模型。圓形成為平台，帶狀成為樓梯，弧線則成為曲面屏。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets white platforms on mirror-chrome columns that reflect light and space. Its stairs and discs rise like a small sacred landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將白色平台架設於反射光線與空間的鏡面鉻柱上。樓梯與圓盤層層升起，宛如一處小型的神聖地景。

sections.heading: Geometry of Divinity - A Sacred Landscape on Mirror-Chrome Columns
sections.body: How can simple geometric shapes create a space that feels sacred? The project begins by extracting, from the buildings of a modern master, the elements that achieve precisely this effect. Those elements were redrawn as a two-dimensional composition of parallel lines and arcs, in which circles, bands and stepped lines set the rules for everything that followed. Translated next into a three-dimensional model in Rhino, the composition took on new roles: discs became platforms, bands became stairs and arcs unfolded into curved screens. In the final model, white platforms rest on mirror-chrome columns that reflect light and the surrounding space, while stairs and discs rise in tiers like a small sacred landscape. Abstract geometry is no longer cold here; through order and reflection it summons a stillness close to reverence, showing how a few disciplined shapes can hold the weight of devotion without a single ornament.

zh-Hant.heading: 神性的幾何-鏡面鉻柱上升起的神聖地景
zh-Hant.body: 簡單的幾何形狀如何創造出神聖的空間？這件作品從現代建築大師的作品出發，萃取其中達成此效果的元素作為起點。這些元素被重新繪製為由平行線與弧線組成的二維構成，圓形、帶狀與階梯狀線條，共同確立了模型的規則。隨後，平面構成在Rhino中被轉化為三維模型：圓形成為平台，帶狀化作樓梯，弧線則展開為曲面屏。最終，白色平台被架設在鏡面鉻柱之上，柱身反射著光線與周遭的空間，樓梯與圓盤層層升起，宛如一處小型的神聖地景。抽象的幾何在此不再冰冷，而是以秩序與反光，引出一種近乎肅穆的寧靜。

pins.title: From Batter to Bricks
pins.description:
Baking gestures translated into porous plaster layers and modular bricks that filter light.

Material Design | Plaster bricks | Light | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從麵糊到磚塊
zh-Hant.description:
將烘焙動作轉譯為能過濾光線的多孔石膏層與模組化磚塊。

材料設計｜石膏磚｜光線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Stacked plaster slabs with irregular holes under warm light.
暖光下層疊的多孔石膏板。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student learned from childhood baking how soft batter changes through time and heat. The project asks how simple baking actions can become ways of shaping form and space.
captions: Baking gestures: channel, stack and drizzle.
Channel, stack and drizzle form experiments.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生從童年的烘焙經驗中，學到柔軟的麵糊如何隨時間與溫度改變。這個作品探問簡單的烘焙動作如何成為塑造形式與空間的方法。
captions: 烘焙動作：導流、堆疊與淋灑。
引流、堆疊與淋灑的形式實驗。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three words, channel, stack and drizzle, were tested in three small models. Each piece translated a baking gesture into a physical form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以引流、堆疊、淋灑三個詞，製作三個小模型進行測試。每件作品都將一個烘焙動作轉譯為實體形式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plaster slabs with irregular holes were cast and stacked so that light filters down through the voids. The result feels solid and transparent at the same time.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生翻製帶有不規則孔洞的石膏板並層層堆疊，讓光線從孔隙間向下灑落。成果同時給人實體與通透的感受。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The slabs then became modular bricks that let light in from the side when stacked into a wall. The pattern of holes gives texture and rhythm while letting the wall breathe.
captions: The brick wall lit from behind.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 板片接著發展為模組化磚塊，堆疊成牆時讓光線從側面進入。孔洞的圖案帶來質感與節奏，也讓牆面得以呼吸。

sections.heading: From Batter to Bricks - Baking Gestures Become a Breathing Wall
sections.body: Childhood baking taught the student how soft batter changes through time and heat, and the project asks whether simple baking actions could become ways of shaping form and space. Three words, channel, stack and drizzle, were each tested in a small model, every piece translating one baking gesture into a physical form. Plaster slabs with irregular holes were then cast and stacked so that light filters down through the voids, producing something that feels solid and transparent at once. From there the slabs grew into modular bricks that admit light from the side when stacked into a wall. The pattern of holes lends texture and rhythm while allowing the wall to breathe. A tender memory from the kitchen is in this way baked into an architectural vocabulary, leaving the flowing trace of batter within the hardness of plaster, and turning a domestic ritual into a quiet study of porosity, mass and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 從麵糊到磚塊-烘焙動作化為會呼吸的牆
zh-Hant.body: 童年的烘焙經驗讓學生明白，柔軟的麵糊會隨時間與溫度改變；作品由此追問，簡單的烘焙動作能否成為塑造形式與空間的方法。引流、堆疊、淋灑三個詞，被分別做成三個小模型，每一件都把一個烘焙動作轉譯為實體形式。接著，帶有不規則孔洞的石膏板被翻製並層層堆疊，光線從孔隙間向下灑落，成果同時顯得厚實又通透。板片隨後發展為模組化的磚塊，堆疊成牆時讓光從側面進入；孔洞的圖案帶來質感與節奏，也讓牆面得以呼吸。廚房裡的溫柔記憶，就這樣被烘焙成建築的語彙，在堅硬的石膏中留下了麵糊般流動的痕跡。

pins.title: Life & Preservation
pins.description:
A timber model of a floating memorial shelter that keeps the vernacular of fishing villages alive on the water.

Hong Kong | Model | Floating fishing village | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生命與保存
zh-Hant.description:
以木構模型打造漂浮紀念庇護所，讓漁村的地方語彙在水上延續。

香港｜模型｜水上漁村｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final memorial shelter model in weathered wooden sticks, tarpaulin and painted boats.
以風化木條、帆布與彩繪小船製作的紀念庇護所最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Redevelopment often removes structures with deep cultural value, such as the floating fishing villages of rafts, timber grids and net cages. The project asks how that heritage can live on while meeting present-day needs.
captions: Elevation sketch of the shelter above sculpted reef forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 都市更新常會移除具有深厚文化價值的構造，例如由竹筏、木格架與網箱組成的水上漁村。這個作品探問這份遺產如何在回應當代需求的同時延續下去。
captions: 庇護所立於雕塑礁體之上的立面草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied raft typologies, tying and lashing joints and the way boats are stored around a working structure. A low-carbon marine cement was considered for reef sculptures below the shelter, so coral could settle on its rough surface.
captions: Weathered sticks cut and framed into grids.
Cross-bracing prototype derived from raft types.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究竹筏類型、綁紮與捆接節點，以及小船如何收納在作業構造周圍。庇護所下方的礁體雕塑考慮使用低碳海洋水泥，讓珊瑚能附著於粗糙表面。
captions: 風化木條切割並組成格架。
源自竹筏類型的斜撐原型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Nets and meshes form a breathable plinth that recalls cage-culture farms. A perimeter gantry lets boats be hoisted along the facade, so the shelter doubles as a typhoon-day harbour.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 網與網布構成可透氣的基座，呼應網箱養殖場。外圍吊架讓小船沿立面吊起收納，使庇護所在颱風天也能兼作避風港。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model combines a pitched timber roof, a green tarpaulin and a ring of painted boats into one floating memorial. Its hand-built frames keep the rough character of the village while giving it a new public role.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將斜木屋頂、綠色帆布與一圈彩繪小船結合為一座漂浮紀念物。手作框架保留漁村的粗獷質感，同時賦予它新的公共角色。

sections.heading: Life and Preservation - A Floating Village Reborn as a Memorial
sections.body: Redevelopment often sweeps away structures of deep cultural value, such as floating fishing villages built from rafts, timber grids and net cages, and the project asks how such heritage might live on while meeting present-day needs. Studying raft typologies, tying and lashing joints and the way boats are stored around a working structure, the student also considered a low-carbon marine cement for reef sculptures beneath the shelter, so that coral could settle on its rough surface. Nets and meshes became a breathable plinth recalling cage-culture farms. A perimeter gantry lets boats be hoisted along the facade, allowing the shelter to double as a harbour on typhoon days. The final model brings a pitched timber roof, a green tarpaulin and a ring of painted boats together into a single floating memorial. Its hand-built frames keep the rough character of the village, so that memory is not merely preserved but handed a new public life on the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 生命與保存-讓水上漁村化為漂浮紀念物
zh-Hant.body: 都市更新常移除深具文化價值的構造，例如由竹筏、木格架與網箱組成的水上漁村；作品追問的是，這份遺產如何在回應當代需求的同時延續下去。學生研究竹筏類型、綁紮與捆接的節點，以及小船如何收納在作業構造四周，並考慮在庇護所下方以低碳海洋水泥製作礁體雕塑，讓珊瑚附著於粗糙的表面。網與網布構成可透氣的基座，呼應網箱養殖場；外圍吊架讓小船沿立面吊起，使庇護所在颱風天兼作避風港。最終，斜木屋頂、綠色帆布與一圈彩繪小船被結合為一座漂浮的紀念物。手作框架保留了漁村的粗獷質感，記憶不再只被保存，而是重新獲得公共的生命。

pins.title: Realm of Light and Curves
pins.description:
A clay and timber model of a sacred space where coloured light filters through hand-made translucent films.

Architecture | Model | Sacred space | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光與曲線之境
zh-Hant.description:
以黏土與木材打造的神聖空間模型，讓光線穿過手作半透明膜片染上色彩。

建築｜模型｜神聖空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of curved clay framework and coloured translucent panels.
由彎曲黏土骨架與彩色半透明面板組成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to organic modernist architecture that seems to grow from nature, with curves, mosaics and stained glass. The project asks how a simple model can capture that sense of a sacred, dreamlike space.
captions: Hand sketch of a spired church.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生深受彷彿從自然生長而出的有機現代建築吸引，著迷於其曲線、馬賽克與彩色玻璃。這個作品探問一個簡單的模型如何捕捉那種神聖而夢幻的空間感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches of towers, facades and twisting forms helped the student read how curves radiate with structural strength. Light filtering through coloured glass became the key quality to recreate.
captions: Clay shaped over the frame into organic curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 透過繪製塔樓、立面與扭轉形體，學生理解曲線如何帶著結構力量向外放射。光線穿過彩色玻璃的效果成為最需要重現的特質。
captions: 以黏土包覆骨架塑出有機曲線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden slats formed the base frame, then clay was shaped over it into contorted, vine-like curves. Heat-pressed plastic bags made translucent films in different colours that lock sunlight inside the model.
captions: Coloured film test in the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以木條構成基本骨架，再以黏土塑出扭曲、如藤蔓般的曲線。以熱壓塑膠袋製成不同顏色的半透明膜片，將陽光鎖在模型之中。
captions: 框架中的彩色膜片測試。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model joins towers, a terrace bridge and a vaulted arch, with plants growing along its edges. Light passing through the films casts shifting colours across the interior, so nature and the sacred feel joined in one space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型結合塔體、平台橋與拱頂，邊緣長出植物。光線穿過膜片在室內投下變化的色彩，讓自然與神聖在同一空間中交融。

sections.heading: Realm of Light and Curves - Locking Sunlight Inside Coloured Films
sections.body: Organic modernist architecture that seems to grow out of nature, with its curves, mosaics and stained glass, drew the student in, and the project asks whether a simple model could capture that sacred, dreamlike sense of space. Sketching towers, facades and twisting forms revealed how curves radiate outward with structural strength, while light filtering through coloured glass emerged as the quality most worth recreating. Wooden slats first formed the base frame, over which clay was shaped into contorted, vine-like curves. Heat-pressed plastic bags were then transformed into translucent films of different colours that lock sunlight inside the model. The finished piece joins towers, a terrace bridge and a vaulted arch, with plants growing along its edges, and light passing through the films casts shifting colours across the interior. Ordinary materials are thus made to carry the sacred, and nature and devotion quietly merge within one luminous space.

zh-Hant.heading: 光與曲線之境-把陽光鎖進彩色膜片
zh-Hant.body: 彷彿從自然生長而出的有機現代建築，以曲線、馬賽克與彩色玻璃吸引了學生；作品於是追問，一個簡單的模型能否捕捉那種神聖而夢幻的空間感。藉由繪製塔樓、立面與扭轉形體，學生讀懂曲線如何帶著結構力量向外放射，而光線穿過彩色玻璃的效果，成為最需要重現的特質。製作時先以木條搭起骨架，再以黏土塑出如藤蔓般扭曲的曲線；熱壓的塑膠袋被轉化為不同顏色的半透明膜片，把陽光鎖在模型之內。最終，塔體、平台橋與拱頂結為一體，植物沿邊緣生長，穿過膜片的光在室內投下流轉的色彩。平凡的材料就此承載了神聖，自然與信仰在同一處空間裡悄然交融。

pins.title: Sanctum - Renewal
pins.description:
A biophilic recovery centre model where terraced floors, hanging greenery and a woven timber shelter support healing.

Architecture | Model | Recovery centre | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聖所・新生
zh-Hant.description:
以退台樓層、懸垂綠意與編織木構遮棚支持療癒的親生物復原中心模型。

建築｜模型｜復原中心｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final site model with the terraced tower, woven shelter and garden path.
最終基地模型，包含退台塔樓、編織遮棚與花園步道。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brief is a centre that helps people recover from injury and other health challenges. The project asks how architecture can lower stress and give users calm, autonomy and a sense of belonging.
captions: Spiral concept sketch of stacked circular floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 設計任務是一座幫助人們從傷病與其他健康挑戰中復原的中心。這個作品探問建築如何降低壓力，並給予使用者平靜、自主與歸屬感。
captions: 層疊圓形樓層的螺旋概念草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew on biophilic principles such as large windows, hanging plants and wood finishes. Circular communal spaces with shortened terrace floors were sketched to connect users with nature and with each other.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生參考親生物設計原則，例如大面開窗、懸垂植物與木質飾面。草圖中以縮短的退台樓層構成圓形公共空間，讓使用者與自然及彼此相連。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Foam board, wood and rattan were used to test stacked terraces, curved walls and a layered landscape. A swirling half-shelter of stacked wood was added so filtered sunlight casts soft patterns inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以泡棉板、木材與藤條測試層疊退台、彎曲牆面與分層地景。再加入以木條堆疊的旋轉半遮棚，讓篩落的陽光在室內投下柔和光影。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets the tower among low curved pavilions, linked by a gravel garden path. Open terraces, rigid pillars and the woven shell balance openness with a feeling of safety.
captions: The woven shell around the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將塔樓置於低矮的彎曲展館之間，以碎石花園步道相連。開放的退台、堅實的柱子與編織殼體，在開放與安全感之間取得平衡。

sections.heading: Sanctum Renewal - Healing Through Light, Plants and a Woven Shell
sections.body: The brief is a centre that helps people recover from injury and other health challenges, and at its heart lies a question of whether architecture can lower stress while offering calm, autonomy and belonging. Drawing on biophilic principles, the student looked to large windows, hanging plants and wood finishes, then sketched circular communal spaces framed by shortened terrace floors so that users would meet nature and one another. Foam board, wood and rattan tested stacked terraces, curved walls and a layered landscape. A swirling half-shelter of stacked timber was added along the way, letting filtered sunlight fall in soft patterns across the interior. In the final model, the tower stands among low curved pavilions, joined by a gravel garden path. Open terraces, rigid pillars and the woven shell hold one another in balance, so that openness and safety coexist, and recovery is given a shape in which a body might rest.

zh-Hant.heading: 聖所新生-以光、植物與編織殼體療癒
zh-Hant.body: 設計任務是一座幫助人們從傷病中復原的中心，核心的問題在於：建築能否降低壓力，給予使用者平靜、自主與歸屬？學生從親生物設計原則出發，參考大面開窗、懸垂植物與木質飾面，並在草圖中以縮短的退台樓層圍出圓形公共空間，讓人與自然、人與人彼此相連。泡棉板、木材與藤條接著被用來測試層疊退台、彎曲牆面與分層地景；一座以木條堆疊的旋轉半遮棚隨之加入，使篩落的陽光在室內投下柔和的光影。最終，塔樓坐落於低矮的彎曲展館之間，以碎石花園步道相連。開放的退台、堅實的柱子與編織殼體彼此平衡，讓敞開與安全感同時成立，復原也因此有了可以棲身的形狀。

pins.title: The Lure of Layers
pins.description:
Gestures and water ripples from a classical painting translated into a layered timber structure over a gridded base.

Architecture | Model | Painting translation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 層次之誘
zh-Hant.description:
將古典畫作中的姿態與水波轉譯為立於格狀基座上的層疊木構。

建築｜模型｜畫作轉譯｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of stained timber posts above a gridded base.
立於格狀基座上的染色木柱最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from a classical painting of figures in water and the tension between bodies and nature in the scene. It asks how gesture, movement and visual seduction in an image can become architectural space.
captions: Angular lines from the figure composition.
Fluid curves from gestures, hair and ripples.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品從一幅描繪水中人物的古典畫作出發，關注畫面中身體與自然之間的張力。它探問圖像中的姿態、動作與視覺誘惑如何轉化為建築空間。
captions: 取自人物構圖的角狀線條。
取自姿態、髮絲與水波的流動曲線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Through overlaid diagrams, the student extracted angular lines from the composition and fluid curves from gestures and ripples. These line systems set the rhythm, direction and edges of the space.
captions: Lines extruded into a layered digital structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生透過疊圖分析，從構圖中萃取角狀線條，並從姿態與水波中萃取流動曲線。這些線條系統決定了空間的節奏、方向與邊界。
captions: 線條擠出為層疊的數位結構。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The lines were modelled in 3D software as layers whose height and density follow the tension among the figures. The model was then built from laser-cut and hand-assembled wood, with a gridded lower base and a folded upper lattice.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生在 3D 軟體中將線條建模為層次，其高度與密度對應人物之間的張力。模型再以雷射切割與手工組裝的木構件製作，下層為格狀基座，上層為折疊格架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model suspends cement and wax forms within a dynamic timber frame, like water caught in motion. Hand-stained colours echo the contrast of water and skin, linking the drawn overlays to the built object.
captions: Water surface detail in cement and wax.
Cement forms held in the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型在動態的木構框架中懸掛水泥與蠟製形體，彷彿凝結的水流。手工染色呼應水與肌膚的對比，將疊圖分析與實體構築連結起來。
captions: 以水泥與蠟製作的水面細部。
嵌於框架中的水泥形體。

sections.heading: The Lure of Layers - From Bodies in Water to a Suspended Timber Frame
sections.body: A classical painting of figures in water opens the project, and the tension between bodies and nature in that scene becomes a question of whether gesture and visual seduction can turn into architectural space. Through overlaid diagrams, the student drew angular lines from the composition and fluid curves from gestures and ripples, letting these two line systems set the rhythm, direction and edges of the space. Modelled next in 3D software, the lines became layers whose height and density rise and fall with the tension among the figures. Laser-cut and hand-assembled timber then gave the model a gridded lower base and a folded upper lattice. In the finished piece, cement and wax forms hang within the dynamic frame like water caught mid-motion, while hand-stained colours echo the contrast of water and skin. What began as the pull of an image settles into habitable layers, so that looking and building meet inside a single skeleton of wood.

zh-Hant.heading: 層次之誘-從水中人體到懸浮的木構
zh-Hant.body: 一幅描繪水中人物的古典畫作，是這件作品的起點；畫中身體與自然之間的張力，被追問能否化為建築空間。透過疊圖分析，學生從構圖裡萃取角狀線條，又從姿態與水波中拾取流動的曲線，讓兩套線條系統決定空間的節奏、方向與邊界。隨後，線條在3D軟體中被建模為層次，高度與密度隨人物之間的張力起伏；雷射切割與手工組裝的木構件，構成下層的格狀基座與上層的折疊格架。最終，水泥與蠟製形體懸浮於動態的木框之中，宛如被凝住的水流，手工染色則呼應水與肌膚的對比。圖像的誘惑由此沉澱為可以行走的層次，觀看與構築在同一副骨架裡相遇。

pins.title: Human Doll
pins.description:
A board game about meeting face to face, translated into a stacked timber house whose rooms shift like game pieces.

Architecture | Game and model | Social space | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 人形
zh-Hant.description:
以促進面對面交流的桌遊為起點，轉化為房間如棋子般錯動的層疊木構住宅。

建築｜桌遊與模型｜社交空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of rooms stacked on columns and linked by stairs.
房間疊於柱上並以樓梯相連的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to create a board game that brings people together for real, face-to-face connection. The project then asks how the game's shifting positions could shape a building.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生希望設計一款讓人們真正面對面交流的桌遊。作品接著探問，遊戲中不斷變換的位置能如何塑造一棟建築。
captions: 以 3D 軟體建模的教室版圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Boards for classrooms, hallways, a cafeteria and stairs were modelled digitally and printed. Hand-drawn character cards and game pieces gave each player a role and set of advantages.
captions: Student, advantage and extra game pieces.
The game laid out in play.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 教室、走廊、餐廳與樓梯的版圖先以數位建模再列印。手繪角色卡與棋子讓每位玩家擁有角色與優勢。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Early card models tested simple house volumes with windows. A stacking method was then chosen so rooms could shift position, as pieces do on the board.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 早期的紙板模型測試帶窗的簡單住宅量體。學生隨後選擇堆疊的方式，讓房間能像版圖上的棋子一樣變換位置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model of wooden sticks and printed parts stacks rooms on slim columns, linked by open stairs and balconies. A traditional-style exterior contrasts with more western interiors, seen through clear ceilings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以木條與列印構件製作，將房間堆疊在細柱上，並以開放樓梯與陽台相連。傳統風格的外觀與較西式的室內形成對比，可透過透明天花窺見。

sections.heading: Human Doll - A House Grown from the Moves of a Board Game
sections.body: The student wanted to create a board game that brings people together for genuine, face-to-face connection, and the project went on to ask whether the game's shifting positions could shape a building. Boards for classrooms, hallways, a cafeteria and stairs were modelled digitally and printed, and hand-drawn character cards and game pieces gave every player a role and a set of advantages. Early card models tested simple house volumes with windows. A stacking method was then chosen so that rooms could change position, just as pieces move across a board. The final model, built from wooden sticks and printed parts, stacks rooms on slim columns linked by open stairs and balconies. A traditional-style exterior contrasts with more western interiors, glimpsed through clear ceilings. Play becomes a method of design, and the sociable spirit of the game is carried into a house where movement, encounter and surprise are built into the very structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 人偶-讓桌遊的移動長成一棟房子
zh-Hant.body: 學生想創作一款桌遊，讓人們真正面對面地相聚與連結。作品進而追問：遊戲中不斷變動的位置，能否塑造一棟建築？教室、走廊、餐廳與樓梯的遊戲板先以數位建模並列印；手繪的角色卡與棋子，賦予每位玩家各自的角色與優勢。早期的卡紙模型測試帶窗的簡單房屋量體；隨後，一種堆疊的方法被選定，讓房間能像棋盤上的棋子般移動位置。最終的木棒與列印構件模型，把房間堆疊在纖細的柱子上，以開放的樓梯與陽台相連；傳統風格的外觀與較為西式的室內形成對比，透過透明的天花板得以窺見。

pins.title: Deconstructing Geometry
pins.description:
Triangles of striped PVC are broken apart and reassembled into a floating structure of tension and light.

Spatial design | Model | Deconstruction | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 解構幾何
zh-Hant.description:
以條紋 PVC 三角形拆解再重組，形成充滿張力與光影的懸浮構造。

空間設計｜模型｜解構｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final structure of striped triangles on a stick frame.
條紋三角形與木條骨架構成的最終結構。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to how deconstructivist architecture breaks order into fragments. The project asks whether simple triangles can be split apart and recombined into a new spatial order.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生著迷於解構主義建築將秩序拆成碎片的方式。作品探問，簡單的三角形能否被拆開再重組成新的空間秩序。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Striped PVC sheets were tested for tension and balance against a timber stick frame. Light passing through the strips revealed how layering could make a solid surface feel semi-transparent.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以條紋 PVC 片搭配木條骨架，測試張力與平衡。光線穿過條紋，顯示疊層能讓實體表面變得半透明。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangular units were repeatedly taken apart and recombined into larger clusters. Each round tested how far fragmentation could go while the whole still held together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角單元被反覆拆解並重組成更大的群組。每一輪都在測試碎片化能推進多遠，而整體仍能成立。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model is an open cluster of striped triangles held by a visible stick frame. Its shifting density and shadows turn a basic shape into a dynamic, layered space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型是由外露木條骨架支撐的開放條紋三角群。變化的密度與陰影，讓基本形狀轉化為動態且具層次的空間。

sections.heading: Deconstructing Geometry - Triangles Broken Apart and Gathered Anew
sections.body: The way deconstructivist architecture breaks order into fragments drew the student in, and the project asks whether simple triangles could be taken apart and recombined into a new spatial order. Striped PVC sheets were tested for tension and balance against a timber stick frame, and light passing through the strips revealed how layering could make a solid surface feel semi-transparent. Triangular units were then repeatedly dismantled and reassembled into larger clusters, with each round testing how far fragmentation could be pushed while the whole still held together. The final model is an open cluster of striped triangles carried by a visible stick frame. Its shifting density and shadows transform the most basic of shapes into a dynamic, layered space. Order and disorder are held in deliberate suspension, and the work shows that breaking something apart can be a way of seeing it more clearly, discovering in a familiar figure a richness its intact form had concealed.

zh-Hant.heading: 解構幾何-讓三角形碎裂後重新聚合
zh-Hant.body: 解構主義建築把秩序打散為碎片的方式，深深吸引著學生。作品追問：簡單的三角形，能否被拆解並重新組合，生成一種新的空間秩序？條紋PVC板被放在木棒框架上，測試張力與平衡；光線穿過條帶時，揭示了層疊如何讓實心的表面顯得半透明。三角形單元被反覆拆開，又重新組合為更大的群簇，每一輪都在測試碎裂可以走多遠，而整體仍能維持完整。最終的模型是一組開放的條紋三角形群簇，由外露的木棒框架承托；變化的密度與光影，讓一個基本的形狀，化為動態而層次豐富的空間。

pins.title: Floating Channels
pins.description:
Stretchy fabric channels and floating foam balls flow through a rigid cubic frame of timber sticks.

Spatial design | Model | Structure and flow | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮通道
zh-Hant.description:
彈性布料通道與漂浮的泡棉球，穿流於木條構成的剛性立方框架之中。

空間設計｜模型｜結構與流動｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model: fabric tunnels and foam balls inside a stick grid.
最終模型：木條網格中的布料通道與泡棉球。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The idea began with natural flows such as wind, water and roots that grow past boundaries. The project asks how soft systems can adapt and reshape themselves inside a rigid framework.
captions: Hand drawing of flows across a grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 構想源自風、水與樹根等會越過邊界自由生長的自然流動。作品探問，柔軟的系統如何在剛性框架內調適並重塑自身。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A cubic frame of timber sticks was built first as the fixed order. Stretchy fabric was then pulled through it to test how far a channel could bend between levels.
captions: Frame taking shape on the cutting mat.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以木條搭出立方框架，作為固定的秩序。再將彈性布料穿拉其中，測試通道在樓層之間能彎曲到什麼程度。
captions: 尚未加入布料的立方框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Fabric tunnels were stretched to link different levels with tensioned, twisting surfaces. Foam balls were hung along the paths to suggest movement drifting through the grid.
captions: A holographic panel among the channels.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 布料通道被拉伸，以扭轉的張拉曲面連接不同樓層。泡棉球沿路徑懸掛，暗示穿越網格漂移的動態。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model balances solid frame and organic surface in one spatial system. Holographic film on some panels catches light and gives the space a vivid, shifting atmosphere.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型在同一空間系統中平衡了實體框架與有機曲面。部分板面貼上全像膜捕捉光線，讓空間呈現鮮明而變幻的氛圍。

sections.heading: Floating Channels - Softness Finding Its Way Through a Rigid Frame
sections.body: The idea began with natural flows such as wind, water and roots that grow past boundaries, and the project asks how soft systems might adapt and reshape themselves within a rigid framework. A cubic frame of timber sticks was built first to establish a fixed order. Stretchy fabric was then pulled through it to test how far a channel could bend between levels. Fabric tunnels were stretched to link different floors with tensioned, twisting surfaces, and foam balls were hung along the paths to suggest movement drifting through the grid. The finished model balances solid frame and organic surface within one spatial system, each giving meaning to the other. Holographic film on some panels catches the light and lends the space a vivid, shifting atmosphere. Rigidity and flow, often cast as opposites, are revealed as partners, and the frame becomes not a cage but the very condition that lets softness find its form.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂浮的通道-讓柔軟在剛硬中找到出路
zh-Hant.body: 構想始於風、水與根系這些越過邊界生長的自然流動。作品追問：柔軟的系統，如何在剛硬的框架內調適並重塑自身？木棒構成的立方框架先被建立，作為固定的秩序；具彈性的布料隨後被拉穿其中，測試一條通道能在樓層之間彎折到什麼程度。布料隧道被拉伸開來，以繃緊而扭轉的曲面串連不同樓層；泡棉球沿著路徑懸掛，暗示在格網中漂移的運動。完成的模型在實心框架與有機曲面之間取得平衡，成為一套完整的空間系統；部分板面上的全像膜捕捉光線，為空間帶來鮮明而變幻的氛圍。

pins.title: Bark Lattice
pins.description:
The rhythms of tree bark are translated into stacked timber and holographic strips that glow like a forest.

Spatial design | Model | Material texture | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹皮格構
zh-Hant.description:
將樹皮的紋理節奏轉譯為層疊的木條與全像紙條，如森林般閃耀。

空間設計｜模型｜材料紋理｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Stacked strips lit to glow like a forest at night.
層疊條片在燈光下如夜間森林般發亮。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student noticed how tree bark records growth in its cracks, fibres and folds. The project asks how that natural texture can become a clear building logic of lines and layers.
captions: Ink imprint of bark texture on fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生注意到樹皮以裂紋、纖維與皺褶記錄生長。作品探問，這種自然紋理如何轉化為清晰的線與層的構築邏輯。
captions: 以墨拓印於布上的樹皮紋理。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Bark was wrapped in fabric and inked to capture its pattern as a print. Timber sticks and holographic strips were then gathered and sorted by length and thickness.
captions: Strips merged into a colourful mass.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以布包覆樹皮並上墨，將紋理拓印下來。接著收集木條與全像紙條，依長度與粗細分類。
captions: 合併成彩色量體的條片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Hand drawings turned the bark into a vocabulary of line, bundle and layer. They also set the density and the break points for the linear construction.
captions: Drawing of line density and breaks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 手繪將樹皮轉為線、束與層的語彙。這些圖也訂定了線性構築的密度與斷裂點。
captions: 線條密度與斷裂的手繪。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final structure stacks varied stripes with slight offsets into tall, jungle-like clusters. Under coloured light the holographic strips shimmer and reveal the depth of each layer.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終構造以略微錯位的條片堆疊成高聳如叢林的群組。在彩色光線下，全像條片閃爍，顯現每一層的深度。

sections.heading: Bark Lattice - The Texture of Growth Turned into Line and Layer
sections.body: The student noticed how tree bark records growth in its cracks, fibres and folds, and the project asks how that natural texture could become a clear building logic of lines and layers. Bark was wrapped in fabric and inked so that its pattern could be lifted as a print. Timber sticks and holographic strips were then gathered and sorted by length and thickness. Hand drawings translated the bark into a vocabulary of line, bundle and layer, and also set the density and the break points for the linear construction. The final structure stacks varied stripes with slight offsets into tall clusters that recall a jungle. Under coloured light the holographic strips shimmer and reveal the depth of each layer. The memory held in a fragment of bark is enlarged into a forest of light one could almost walk through, and close looking at a humble surface becomes the foundation for a structure that is both disciplined and dreamlike.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹皮格構-把生長的紋理化為線與層
zh-Hant.body: 學生注意到，樹皮以裂紋、纖維與皺褶記錄著生長。作品追問：這種自然的紋理，能否成為一套清晰的、由線與層構成的建築邏輯？樹皮被包覆在布中並施以墨色，把紋理拓印下來；木棒與全像條帶隨後被蒐集，依長度與粗細分類。手繪圖把樹皮轉化為線、束與層的語彙，也設定了線性構築的密度與斷點。最終的結構把錯落的條紋稍加位移、層層堆疊，形成高聳如叢林般的群簇。在彩色燈光下，全像條帶閃爍微光，揭示每一層的深度，讓一片樹皮的記憶，被放大為可以穿越的光之林。

pins.title: The Growing Pattern
pins.description:
Roots and branches traced into lines, then woven from painted sticks and acrylic platforms into ordered chaos.

Spatial design | Model | Order and chaos | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生長紋理
zh-Hant.description:
將樹根與枝條描繪為線條，再以上色木條與壓克力平台編織成有序的混沌。

空間設計｜模型｜秩序與混沌｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final interwoven structure lit against black.
在黑色背景中打光的最終編織構造。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: On a field trip the student saw a hidden order beneath the apparent chaos of a jungle. The project asks how branching roots and vines can be read as a line, node and bundle logic.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在一次田野考察中，看見叢林表面混亂之下隱藏的秩序。作品探問，枝狀的樹根與藤蔓如何被解讀為線、節點與束的邏輯。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Growth patterns of roots and branches were traced to find their structural rhythm. The tracings were refined into simple two-dimensional line drawings that could guide the build.
captions: Tracing of root and branch patterns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪樹根與枝條的生長紋理，找出其結構節奏。描圖再被提煉為簡潔的二維線條圖，作為構築的依據。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks of many sizes were interwoven, and acrylic paint marked a hidden order within the chaos. Laser-cut acrylic plates were added as hexagonal platforms with open voids above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同尺寸的木條相互編織，並以壓克力顏料在混沌中標示隱藏的秩序。雷射切割的壓克力板被加入成為六角形平台，上方留有開放的空隙。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Different stick densities create places to move through and places to pause. Under light the transparent platforms and coloured sticks add layers of depth and a playful rhythm.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 不同的木條密度創造出可穿行與可停留的地方。在光線下，透明平台與彩色木條增添了層次深度與輕快的節奏。

sections.heading: The Growing Pattern - Reading Order in the Chaos of a Jungle
sections.body: On a field trip the student glimpsed a hidden order beneath the apparent chaos of a jungle, and the project asks whether branching roots and vines could be read through a logic of line, node and bundle. Growth patterns of roots and branches were traced to uncover their structural rhythm, and the tracings were refined into simple two-dimensional line drawings to guide construction. Sticks of many sizes were then interwoven, with acrylic paint marking the concealed order within the tangle, and laser-cut acrylic plates were added as hexagonal platforms with open voids above. Varying densities of sticks create places to move through and places to pause. Under light, the transparent platforms and coloured sticks add layers of depth and a playful rhythm. The jungle's seeming disorder is revealed as a language that can be learned, and the model becomes both a record of close observation and an invitation to inhabit complexity rather than fear it.

zh-Hant.heading: 生長的圖樣-在叢林的混沌中讀出秩序
zh-Hant.body: 一次野外考察中，學生在叢林看似混亂的表象之下，看見一種隱藏的秩序。作品追問：分枝的根系與藤蔓，能否被解讀為線、節點與束的邏輯？根與枝的生長圖樣被描摹下來，以找出它們的結構節奏；這些描摹再被提煉為簡單的平面線圖，作為建造的指引。粗細不一的木棒被交織在一起，壓克力顏料標記出混沌中隱藏的秩序；雷射切割的壓克力板則被加入，成為上方留有空隙的六角形平台。不同的木棒密度，形成可以穿行與可以停駐的地方；在燈光下，透明的平台與彩色的木棒增添層次與輕快的節奏。

pins.title: Growth Rings
pins.description:
Tree-ring patterns become stacked PVC rings that merge building, trees and ground into one landscape.

Spatial design | Landscape model | Growth pattern | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 年輪
zh-Hant.description:
將年輪紋理轉化為層疊的 PVC 環，使建築、樹木與地面融為一片地景。

空間設計｜地景模型｜生長紋理｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The ring landscape model with trees, lit at night.
種有樹木的年輪地景模型夜間打光。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project responds to a self-replicating urban concept but shifts it toward organic growth like tree rings. It asks how cold urban motifs can become a living system shared by people, space and nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品回應一個自我複製的城市構想，但將其轉向如年輪般的有機生長。它探問，冰冷的城市母題如何成為人、空間與自然共享的生命系統。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Circular pattern paintings and hand drawings explored how rings overlap and link. These studies set the ring and strip units that the model would be built from.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圓形紋理繪畫與手繪探討環與環之間如何重疊與連結。這些研究訂定了模型所用的環形與條狀單元。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Templates were used to cut PVC sheet into rings and linear strips. The units were layered into three-dimensional pieces and then combined into a larger whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以模板將 PVC 板切成圓環與線條。這些單元被疊合成立體構件，再組合成更大的整體。
captions: 手中的切割 PVC 環。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Trees and grass powder are embedded among the rings so building and site blur together. The result is a seamless landscape where the built form reads as an extension of the ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 樹木與草粉嵌入環形之間，使建築與基地的界線變得模糊。成果是一片連續的地景，建築形體如同地面的延伸。

sections.heading: Growth Rings - A Cold Urban Motif Grown into a Living Landscape
sections.body: The project responds to a self-replicating urban concept but turns it toward organic growth, like the rings of a tree, asking how cold urban motifs could become a living system shared by people, space and nature. Circular pattern paintings and hand drawings explored how rings overlap and link, and these studies established the ring and strip units from which the model would be built. Using templates, the student cut PVC sheet into rings and linear strips, then layered the units into three-dimensional pieces and combined them into a larger whole. Trees and grass powder were embedded among the rings so that building and site blend into each other. The result is a seamless landscape in which built form reads as an extension of the ground, much like the rings a tree quietly lays down over the years. A once mechanical idea of the city softens into something patient and alive, where growth is measured not in units but in seasons.

zh-Hant.heading: 年輪-讓冰冷的城市母題長成活的地景
zh-Hant.body: 作品回應一個自我複製的城市概念，卻把它轉向如年輪般的有機生長。它追問：冰冷的城市母題，如何成為人、空間與自然共享的生命系統？圓形圖樣的繪畫與手繪，探索環圈如何交疊、如何相連；這些研究確立了模型將由環形與條狀單元構成。學生以模板把PVC板切割為環圈與線性條帶，再把單元層疊成立體部件，組合成更大的整體。樹木與草粉被嵌入環圈之間，讓建築與基地彼此交融。最終呈現的是一片無縫的地景，建成的形體讀起來就像大地的延伸，如同一棵樹在時間裡默默長出的年輪。

pins.title: Kaleidoscopic Dreams
pins.description:
A simple block is twisted, mirrored and rotated in 3D software into a shimmering kaleidoscope form.

Digital design | 3D modelling | Form operations | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 萬花筒之夢
zh-Hant.description:
以 3D 軟體將簡單方塊扭轉、鏡射與旋轉，生成閃爍的萬花筒形體。

數位設計｜3D 建模｜形體操作｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final forms repeated into a kaleidoscope image.
最終形體重複構成的萬花筒影像。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After a digital workshop the student set out to design an interactive system inspired by the kaleidoscope. The project asks how shapes and colours in constant flux can make us question what we see.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 參加數位工作坊後，學生著手設計一個受萬花筒啟發的互動系統。作品探問，持續變化的形狀與色彩如何讓人質疑自己所見。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A single block was put through a chain of operations such as twist, mirror, rotate and scale. Each step was recorded so the logic of the form stayed readable.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生讓單一方塊經過扭轉、鏡射、旋轉與縮放等一連串操作。每一步都被記錄下來，讓形體的邏輯保持清晰可讀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Mirrored and rotated copies were combined, then split with a boolean step to open the form. This produced a flower-like object with folded petals and deep pockets.
captions: From copies and boolean split to the final work.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鏡射與旋轉的複本被組合，再以布林運算切開形體。如此產生一個花瓣摺疊、內有深陷凹處的花狀物件。
captions: 由複製、布林切割到最終作品。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final objects carry an iridescent finish that shifts with every view. Repeated into a kaleidoscope image, they invite open reflection on how stable perception really is.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終物件帶有隨視角變化的虹彩表面。重複構成萬花筒影像後，它們引人反思感知究竟有多穩定。

sections.heading: Kaleidoscopic Dreams - Form and Colour That Question What We See
sections.body: After a digital workshop, the student set out to design an interactive system inspired by the kaleidoscope, asking how shapes and colours in constant flux might lead us to question what we see. A single block was passed through a chain of operations, twist, mirror, rotate and scale, and each step was recorded so that the logic of the form remained legible throughout. Mirrored and rotated copies were then combined and cut open with a boolean operation, revealing an object like a flower, with folded petals and deep pockets. The final pieces carry an iridescent finish that changes with every angle of view. Repeated into a kaleidoscope image, they invite open reflection on how stable perception really is. Rigorous procedure and shimmering illusion turn out to be partners rather than opposites, and a sequence of precise digital steps ends in an experience that unsettles certainty and returns the viewer, gently, to the act of looking itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 萬花筒之夢-讓形與色質疑我們所見
zh-Hant.body: 一場數位工作坊之後，學生著手設計一套受萬花筒啟發的互動系統。作品追問：不斷流變的形狀與色彩，如何讓我們質疑自己所見？單一方塊被送入一連串操作：扭轉、鏡射、旋轉與縮放，每一步都被記錄下來，使形體的邏輯始終清晰可讀。鏡射與旋轉後的複本被結合起來，再以布林運算切開，使形體敞開；由此生成一個如花般的物件，帶著摺疊的花瓣與深邃的凹穴。最終的物件覆以隨視角變幻的虹彩表面；當它們被重複排列成萬花筒影像，便邀請觀者開放地反思：知覺究竟有多穩定？

pins.title: Entangled Realms
pins.description:
A tree-shaped tower of stacked wooden sticks is wrapped in hand-shaped clay and ringed by yellow paper paths.

Model making | Mixed-media tower | Coexistence study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 糾纏之境
zh-Hant.description:
以木棒堆疊成樹形塔體，外覆手塑黏土，並以黃色瓦楞紙環道環繞。

模型製作｜複合材料塔體｜共存研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished tower with its yellow ring paths.
完成的塔體與黃色環道。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted a single model to hold both human order and the unruly growth of nature. The project asks how built frames and wild habitat might share one body.
captions: Sketch diagrams of the stacked form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生希望以單一模型同時容納人類的秩序與自然的恣意生長。作品探問，人造框架與野性棲地如何共存於同一個形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A digital sketch first tested a stack of shrinking hexagonal layers shaped like a festive tree. The layers were then rebuilt as wooden sticks of graded lengths to make the frame.
captions: Making process from frame to clay.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以數位草圖測試逐層縮小、形如節慶樹的六角形堆疊。之後再以長度漸變的木棒重新構築這些層，形成框架。
captions: 從框架到黏土的製作過程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Clay was pressed between the sticks to form irregular pockets that stand for animal and plant habitat. The rigid frame and the soft clay begin to grip and depend on each other.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生將黏土壓入木棒之間，形成代表動植物棲地的不規則空間。剛硬的框架與柔軟的黏土開始彼此咬合、相互依存。
captions: 被黏土包覆的木棒框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Yellow corrugated paper rings now spiral around the tower as paths that link every level. The model reads as a shared home where people, animals and plants overlap.
captions: Front view of the finished model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 黃色瓦楞紙環道螺旋環繞塔體，串連每一層。模型呈現出人、動物與植物交疊共居的家園。

sections.heading: Entangled Realms - Order and Wildness Sharing One Body
sections.body: The student wanted a single model to hold both human order and the unruly growth of nature, and the project asks whether built frames and wild habitat might share one body. A digital sketch first tested a stack of shrinking hexagonal layers shaped like a festive tree, and those layers were then rebuilt as wooden sticks of graded lengths to form the frame. Clay was pressed between the sticks to create irregular pockets standing for animal and plant habitats. Gradually the rigid frame and the soft clay began to grip and depend on each other, neither complete without the other. Yellow corrugated paper rings now spiral around the tower as paths linking every level. The model reads as a shared home in which people, animals and plants overlap, a vision of coexistence where structure offers support and wildness offers life, and where the boundary between the two is less a wall than a meeting place.

zh-Hant.heading: 交纏之境-秩序與野性共享一個身體
zh-Hant.body: 學生希望以單一模型，同時容納人的秩序與自然的恣意生長。作品追問：人造框架與野生棲地，能否共享同一個身體？一張數位草圖首先測試層層縮小的六角形堆疊，形如一棵節慶之樹；這些層隨後以長度漸變的木棒重建，構成框架。陶土被壓入木棒之間，形成不規則的孔穴，象徵動植物的棲地；剛硬的框架與柔軟的陶土，開始彼此咬合、彼此依存。如今，黃色瓦楞紙環螺旋繞塔而上，成為串連每一層的路徑。模型讀起來像一個共享的家，人、動物與植物在其中相互重疊。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to tensile roofs where thin members carry wave-like skins. The project asks how stiff sticks alone can make surfaces that curve and cross.

Early tests with rods, foam and fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生受到以纖細構件撐起波浪表皮的張拉屋頂吸引。作品探問，僅靠硬直的棒材，能否做出彎曲並相互交錯的曲面。
captions: 啟發本案的張拉結構先例照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Early tests stretched fabric over rods set in foam, but the result stayed one solid form. Removing the fabric and keeping only sticks let separate parts start to connect.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 初期測試將布料撐在插入泡棉的棒材上，結果卻仍是單一實體。拿掉布料、只留棒材後，各個部分開始能彼此連結。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A sketch set out a wooden main frame with bamboo bent between its posts. Fixing the bamboo at regular but staggered points made the surfaces weave and meet.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以草圖規劃木構主框架，並在柱間彎繞竹棒。竹棒以規律而錯位的節點固定，使曲面交織相會。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a cluster of towers wrapped in fine bamboo curves. Its openings and crossings come straight from the logic of bending and fixing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以細密竹曲線包覆的塔群拔地而起。其開口與交錯，都直接來自彎曲與固定的邏輯。

sections.heading: Intertwining Surfaces - Towers Woven by Bending and Fixing
sections.body: Tensile roofs in which slender members carry wave-like skins fascinated the student, and the project asks whether stiff sticks alone could create surfaces that curve and cross. Early tests stretched fabric over rods set in foam, yet the result always remained one solid form. The turning point came through subtraction: once the fabric was removed and only the sticks were kept, separate parts began to connect with one another. A sketch then established a wooden main frame with bamboo bent between its posts, and fixing the bamboo at regular but staggered points allowed the surfaces to weave and meet. The final model rises as a cluster of towers wrapped in fine bamboo curves, with every opening and crossing arising directly from the logic of bending and fixing. Material behaviour, rather than imposed form, writes the architecture, and a simple rule patiently repeated yields a structure of surprising grace.

zh-Hant.heading: 交織的曲面-以彎折與固定編出塔群
zh-Hant.body: 細桿承托波浪般表皮的張力屋頂，深深吸引著學生。作品追問：只用堅硬的木棒，能否做出彎曲並相互交錯的曲面？早期的試驗把布料繃在插於泡棉中的桿件上，結果卻始終是一個實心的整體。轉折來自一次減法：拿掉布料，只留下木棒，分離的部件才開始彼此連結。一張草圖確立了木構主框架，竹片在柱子之間彎折；以規律卻錯開的點固定竹片，讓曲面得以交織、相遇。最終的模型升起為一群塔，被細緻的竹曲線包覆，它的開口與交會，全都直接來自彎折與固定的邏輯。

zh-Hant.heading: 問題

zh-Hant.heading: 研究

sections.body: The curves were set on cobblestones inside an acrylic box and planted with moss and small trees. A grid of red sticks was then added as roads and frames that hint at human use.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The two layers press against and absorb each other across the whole landscape. The model imagines a place where people have left and the line between built and natural blurs.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩個層次在整片地景中相互擠壓、彼此吸納。模型想像一處人已離去、人造與自然界線逐漸模糊的場所。

sections.heading: Fossilized Architecture - When Nature Slowly Reclaims the Built
sections.body: The student explored the tension between organic growth and human-made order, asking what a structure might look like once nature has slowly taken it back. Line studies drawn from ecological networks were turned into a parametric curve system, and the flowing pieces were printed in resin so that they read like the remains of a living body. These curves were set on cobblestones inside an acrylic box and planted with moss and small trees. A grid of red sticks was then added as roads and frames, hinting at a human presence now absent. Across the whole landscape the two layers press against and absorb one another. The model imagines a place people have left behind, where the boundary between built and natural grows faint and time itself becomes the final designer. It is at once elegy and promise, suggesting that what we construct may one day be gently folded back into the living ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 化石建築-當自然緩慢收回人造之物
zh-Hant.body: 學生探討有機生長與人造秩序之間的張力。作品追問：當自然緩慢收回一座結構，它會呈現什麼模樣？取自生態網絡的線條研究，被轉化為一套參數化的曲線系統；流動的構件以樹脂列印，讀起來宛如某個生命體的遺骸。曲線被安放在壓克力盒中的鵝卵石上，種上苔蘚與小樹；一組紅色木棒格網隨後被加入，作為道路與框架，暗示人曾經的使用。兩個層次在整片地景中相互擠壓、彼此吸收。模型想像一個人已離去的地方，在那裡，人造與自然的界線逐漸模糊，時間成為最終的設計者。

zh-Hant.heading: 推演

sections.heading: Cliffside Beach House - A Home Both Sheltered and Open to the View
sections.body: Memories of buildings seen while travelling led the student to imagine a house on a hill above a beach, and the project asks how a home could feel both sheltered and open to the view. A digital terrain study placed the house on the slope with a tower at its peak, and the ground was then built up from layered sheets, sand and painted water. Hand-drawn plans link rounded rooms through narrow corridors and a shared stair, while curved windows were 3D printed so that each room glows softly like a small lantern. The finished model scatters timber rooms on red stilts across the hillside. Geometric shapes cross one another freely, yet every space keeps a purpose of its own. Shelter and openness, enclosure and horizon, are held in gentle balance, and fragments of remembered journeys settle into a single imagined dwelling where the sea is always present but never overwhelming.

zh-Hant.heading: 懸崖海濱小屋-既受庇護又向景開放的家
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中見過的建築留下的記憶，引領學生想像一棟坐落於海灘上方山丘的房子。作品追問：一個家，如何同時讓人感到受庇護，又向景色敞開？一項數位地形研究，把房子安放在坡地上，並在頂端立起一座塔；地面隨後以層疊的板材、沙與彩繪的水建構而成。手繪平面以狹窄的廊道與共享的樓梯，串連起一個個圓潤的房間；弧形的窗以3D列印製成，讓房間如小燈籠般柔和地發光。完成的模型把架在紅色高腳柱上的木構房間散落在山坡上，幾何形體自由交錯，每個空間卻都有各自的用途。

zh-Hant.description:

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Creepers growing over the walls near the student's home showed how plants cling to buildings without falling. The project asks whether a structure can be designed so greenery grows into it from the start.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生家附近牆面上的爬藤，展現了植物如何攀附建築而不掉落。作品探問，能否從一開始就設計一座讓綠意自然長入的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Studies of vertical greening showed plants held in neat but varied frames. The student chose a language of straight lines and rectangles taken from abstract painting and turned it into 3D.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究垂直綠化，發現植物被安置在整齊卻多變的框架中。學生選用取自抽象繪畫的直線與矩形語彙，並將其轉為立體。
captions: 基座與框架的製作過程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A thick core stick was glued to a plastic base, then black sticks and plates were stacked around it. Wood rods and acrylic boxes added texture before plants were set into the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先將較粗的核心木棒黏在塑膠底座上，再於周圍堆疊黑色棒材與板材。木棒與壓克力盒增添質感，最後才把植物安置進框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Plants now spill over every level so the frame and the greenery read as one facade. A line drawing and a digital replica with more plants and animals extend the idea beyond the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果

sections.heading: Verdant Facade - A Structure Where Plants Belong from the Start
sections.body: Creepers growing over walls near the student's home revealed how plants can cling to buildings without falling, and the project asks whether a structure could be designed so that greenery grows into it from the very beginning. Studies of vertical greening showed plants held within neat yet varied frames. The student chose a language of straight lines and rectangles drawn from abstract painting and translated it into three dimensions. A thick core stick was glued to a plastic base, and black sticks and plates were stacked around it, with wood rods and acrylic boxes adding texture before plants were set into the frame. Today the plants spill over every level, so frame and foliage read as a single facade. A line drawing and a digital replica populated with more plants and animals carry the idea beyond the model, imagining a building that is less a container for life than a trellis on which life is invited to settle.

zh-Hant.heading: 翠綠立面-讓植物從一開始就住進結構
zh-Hant.body: 住家附近攀滿牆面的藤蔓，讓學生看見植物如何緊附建築而不墜落。作品因此追問：能否設計一種結構，讓綠意從一開始就生長其中？垂直綠化的研究顯示，植物常被安置在整齊卻富變化的框架裡。學生選擇了一種取自抽象繪畫的直線與矩形語言，並把它轉化為立體。一根粗壯的核心木棒先被黏在塑膠底座上，黑色木棒與板片再圍繞它層層堆疊；木桿與壓克力盒增添肌理，植物最後被安放進框架之中。如今，植物從每一層溢出，框架與綠意讀起來就是同一面立面；一張線圖與一個加入更多動植物的數位複本，則把構想延伸到模型之外。

pins.title: A Spatial Narrative of Escape

zh-Hant.title: 逃脫的空間敘事
zh-Hant.description:
一部越獄影集中的四種逃脫手法，化為環繞螺旋梯相連的四個空間，之後再重建成遊戲關卡。

模型製作｜空間敘事｜複合材料迷宮｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student admired how a TV prison drama solves escape through careful planning rather than force. The project asks how a sequence of clever escape moves can be told as one continuous space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題

Four escape scenes, one for each part of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究四個行動：鑿穿牆面、刺青地圖、腐蝕下水道鐵條與攀爬電梯井。每個行動都被轉譯為切割、層疊、溶解或攀爬等材料動作。

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 中央螺旋梯串連四個較小的空間，包含PVC窗洞、地圖化的表面與交錯的木棒網絡。手繪圖測試樓梯、拱與紋理如何在量體中盤繞。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model reads as a dense maze where every route ends in a breakthrough. The student then rebuilt it in a game engine as a playable final level of an escape game.
captions: Stick paths in the game level.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型成為一座密集的迷宮，每條路線都通往一次突破。學生之後在遊戲引擎中重建模型，成為逃脫遊戲中可遊玩的最終關卡。
captions: 遊戲關卡中的木棒路徑。

sections.heading: A Spatial Narrative of Escape - Every Route Ends in a Breakthrough
sections.body: The student admired how a television prison drama achieves escape through careful planning rather than force, and the project asks whether a sequence of clever escape moves could be told as one continuous space. Four moves were studied in turn: chiselling through a wall, a tattooed map, corroded sewer bars and a climb up an elevator shaft. Each was distilled into a material action such as cutting, layering, dissolving or climbing. A central spiral stair links four smaller spaces featuring PVC window openings, a mapped surface and a criss-cross network of sticks, while hand drawings tested how stairs, arches and textures wind through the volume. The completed model reads as a dense maze in which every route ends in a breakthrough. Going a step further, the student rebuilt it in a game engine as the playable final level of an escape game, so that a story first watched, then built, could finally be lived through by others.

zh-Hant.heading: 越獄的空間敘事-每條路都通向突破
zh-Hant.body: 學生欣賞一部監獄影集，以縝密的計畫而非蠻力完成越獄。作品追問：一連串巧妙的脫逃步驟，能否被述說為一個連續的空間？四個步驟被逐一研究：鑿穿牆面、刺青地圖、被腐蝕的下水道鐵條與攀爬電梯井；每一步都被提煉為一種材料動作，如切割、層疊、溶解或攀爬。一座中央旋梯串連四個較小的空間，包含PVC窗洞、繪有地圖的表面與交錯的木棒網絡；手繪圖則測試階梯、拱圈與肌理如何在量體中盤繞。完成的模型宛如一座密集的迷宮，每條路線都終於一次突破；學生其後更在遊戲引擎中重建它，成為一款脫逃遊戲可遊玩的最終關卡。

pins.title: Restyled Temple of Time
