A stepped temple from a favourite video game is rebuilt in bamboo strips and ringed with hanging sticks of many heights.

Model making | Game-inspired architecture | Bamboo stick model | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重塑時之神殿
zh-Hant.description:
學生把喜愛的電玩中一座階梯式神殿，以竹條重新搭建，並以高低不一的垂掛木棒環繞。

模型製作｜遊戲啟發建築｜竹木棒模型｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished temple wrapped in hanging sticks.
被垂掛木棒包覆的完成神殿。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loved a calm, monumental temple in a video game and wanted to build it without making a copy. The question was how to keep its stepped silhouette while making it feel open and light.
captions: Game screenshots of the temple that inspired the model.
Sketches of the front facade and the roof space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生喜愛電玩中一座沉靜而宏偉的神殿，想將它做成模型卻不只是複製。問題在於如何保留階梯式輪廓，同時讓它顯得開放輕盈。
captions: 啟發模型的神殿遊戲截圖。
正立面與屋頂空間草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches broke the facade and roof into stacked layers that could be built in strips. The overall form was then redrawn as dense vertical lines, a step that set the language of the model.
captions: Translating the exterior into vertical lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以草圖把立面與屋頂拆解為可用條材搭建的堆疊層次。整體造型再被重繪成密集的垂直線條，奠定模型的語彙。
captions: 將外觀轉譯為垂直線條。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin bamboo strips were laid layer by layer and glued into curved floors and frames. Vertical sticks of varied heights were then added around the edge to form a loose boundary.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以細竹條逐層鋪設，黏合成弧形樓板與框架。接著在外緣加上高低不一的垂直木棒，形成鬆散的邊界。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: When lit, the sticks cast moving shadows across the stepped floors and give the temple depth. Small red figures show how the open interior can be walked through.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在燈光下，木棒於階梯樓板上投下變化的光影，讓神殿更有深度。紅色小人偶顯示開放的室內如何被穿行。

sections.heading: Restyled Temple of Time - A Stepped Silhouette Woven Light in Bamboo
sections.body: The student loved a calm, monumental temple in a video game and wanted to build it without simply making a copy. The question was how to keep its stepped silhouette while making it feel open and light. Sketches broke the facade and roof into stacked layers that could be built in strips, and the whole form was then redrawn as dense vertical lines, a step that set the language of the entire model. Thin bamboo strips were laid layer by layer and glued into curved floors and frames, after which vertical sticks of varied heights were added around the edge to form a loose, permeable boundary. When lit, the sticks cast moving shadows across the stepped floors and give the temple depth, while small red figures show how its open interior can be walked through. A virtual monument is thus recast as a space of light and air, approachable rather than imposing, its grandeur carried by rhythm instead of mass.

zh-Hant.heading: 重塑時之神殿-以竹條織出輕盈的階梯輪廓
zh-Hant.body: 學生喜愛一款電玩中寧靜而宏偉的神殿，想把它建造出來，卻不願只是複製。問題是：如何保留它階梯般的輪廓，同時讓它顯得開放而輕盈？草圖把立面與屋頂拆解為可以條狀建造的堆疊層；整體形體隨後被重新描繪為密集的垂直線條，這一步確立了模型的語言。細竹條被逐層鋪設、黏合成弧形的樓板與框架，高低不一的垂直木棒再沿邊緣加入，形成一道疏朗的邊界。點亮之後，木棒在階梯狀的樓板上投下流動的影子，賦予神殿深度；小小的紅色人形，則顯示開放的內部可以如何被穿行。虛擬的宏偉，在此轉化為透光而可親的空間。

pins.title: Medieval Castle Isometric Studies
pins.description:
Gothic castle parts are modelled one by one and recombined into three coloured isometric castles.

Digital modelling | Isometric design | Gothic castle | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 中世紀城堡等角研究
zh-Hant.description:
哥德式城堡構件被逐一建模，再重組成三座上色的等角城堡。

數位建模｜等角設計｜哥德城堡｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A tall castle rendered in pink light.
以粉色光線渲染的高聳城堡。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A castle in a favourite animated series caught the student's eye with its bold gothic forms and colours. The aim was to rebuild that spirit as new castles rather than copy a single scene.
captions: A castle still from the series that inspired the studies.
Game screenshots of gothic castles used as references.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被一部喜愛的動畫中城堡大膽的哥德造型與配色吸引。目標是將那份精神重建為新的城堡，而不是複製單一場景。
captions: 啟發這些習作的影集城堡劇照。
作為參考的哥德式城堡遊戲截圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched typical parts such as towers, pointed windows, domes and spires. Each part was then modelled in Rhino as a reusable piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先描繪塔樓、尖拱窗、圓頂與尖塔等典型構件。再於Rhino中將每個構件建成可重複使用的元件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The parts were combined into different castles with stairs, terraces and bridges between towers. Isometric views were exported and coloured with simple settings around them.
captions: Castle with arcades in orange light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把構件組合成不同的城堡，以樓梯、平台與橋樑連接各塔。等角視圖匯出後加上色彩與簡單的環境布景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three castles show how one kit of parts can produce very different moods. Line elevations record the outlines of each design.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三座城堡顯示同一套構件能營造截然不同的氛圍。線稿立面記錄了每個設計的輪廓。

sections.heading: Medieval Castle Isometric Studies - Many Moods from One Kit of Parts
sections.body: A castle in a favourite animated series caught the student's eye with its bold gothic forms and colours, and the aim was to rebuild that spirit as new castles rather than copy any single scene. Typical components came first: towers, pointed windows, domes and spires were sketched and then modelled in Rhino as reusable pieces. These parts were combined into different castles, with stairs, terraces and bridges linking tower to tower, and isometric views were exported and coloured within simple surroundings. Three castles demonstrate how one kit of parts can produce strikingly different moods, from austere to playful, while line elevations record the outline of each design. Imitation is thus transformed into a generative design language, a system that can keep producing new variations, and admiration for an imagined world becomes a disciplined lesson in how architectural vocabulary, once broken into parts, can be recomposed into countless new wholes.

zh-Hant.heading: 中世紀城堡等角研究-以一套零件生成多種情緒
zh-Hant.body: 一部喜愛的動畫影集裡，一座城堡以大膽的哥德式形體與色彩吸引了學生的目光。目標不是複製某一個場景，而是把那份精神重建為新的城堡。學生先草繪典型的構件，如塔樓、尖拱窗、圓頂與尖塔，再把每一個構件以Rhino建模為可重複使用的零件。這些零件隨後被組合成不同的城堡，塔樓之間以階梯、露台與橋梁相連；等角視圖被輸出，並配上簡單的環境加以上色。三座城堡展示了同一套零件如何生成截然不同的情緒，線條立面則記錄下每個設計的輪廓。模仿，就此轉化為一套可以不斷衍生的設計語言。

pins.title: Vertical Terrains
pins.description:
Terrain data from places the student loves is stacked into layered landscapes held up by white columns, forming a vertical forest.

Model making | Parametric terrain | Layered landscape | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂直地景
zh-Hant.description:
學生把喜愛之地的地形資料堆疊成多層地景，由白色柱體支撐，形成一座垂直森林。

模型製作｜參數化地形｜層疊地景｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Trees and columns between two terrain layers.
兩層地形之間的樹木與柱體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Travel lets people feel landscapes and local culture in a way screens cannot. The project asks how landscapes from many places could be gathered into one compact, vertical forest.
captions: Height maps and landscape photos used as sources.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 旅行讓人以螢幕無法取代的方式感受地景與在地文化。作品探問，如何把多地的地景聚集成一座緊湊的垂直森林。
captions: 作為來源的高程圖與地景照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student collected elevation data of places visited or wished for and read it as height maps. A node script turned each map into a 3D terrain surface.
captions: Node script and generated terrain surfaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集曾造訪或嚮往之地的高程資料，並以高程圖讀取。透過節點程式，每張圖都被轉成立體地形曲面。
captions: 節點程式與生成的地形曲面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two terrains were stacked and propped apart by tapered white columns. Layers of PVC plate were cut to the contours and the columns were 3D-printed.
captions: Render of the space between the columns.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 兩層地形上下堆疊，由漸縮的白色柱體撐開。學生依等高線切割PVC板層層疊合，柱體則以3D列印製作。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Moss and small trees cover both levels so the model reads as a forest climbing upward. Between the layers, the columns frame a shaded valley.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 苔蘚與小樹覆蓋上下兩層，讓模型讀起來像一座向上攀升的森林。層與層之間，柱體框出一處陰涼的山谷。

sections.heading: Vertical Terrains - Distant Landscapes Stacked into a Forest
sections.body: Travel allows people to feel landscapes and local culture in a way no screen can, and the project asks whether landscapes from many places might be gathered into one compact, vertical forest. The student collected elevation data from places visited or longed for and read each as a height map, then used a node script to turn every map into a three-dimensional terrain surface. Two terrains were stacked one above the other and held apart by tapered white columns. Layers of PVC plate were cut along the contours, and the columns were 3D printed. Moss and small trees now cover both levels, so the model reads as a forest climbing upward, while between the layers the columns frame a shaded valley. Memories of distant places and the wish to reach others meet within a single small landscape, and data that began as numbers on a screen returns to the hand as soil, green and the cool hush of a hidden valley.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直地形-把遠方的山水疊成森林
zh-Hant.body: 旅行讓人以螢幕無法取代的方式，感受地景與在地文化。這個作品追問：來自許多地方的地景，能否被匯聚成一座緊湊而垂直的森林？學生蒐集曾經造訪或心之所嚮之地的高程資料，把它們讀作高度圖；節點腳本再把每張圖轉化為立體的地形曲面。兩片地形被上下疊起，以漸縮的白色柱子撐開距離；PVC板依等高線層層切割，柱子則以3D列印製成。苔蘚與小樹覆蓋上下兩層，讓模型讀起來像一座向上攀升的森林；在兩層之間，柱列框出一道幽蔭的山谷。遠方的記憶與嚮往，於是在同一座小小的地景中相遇。

pins.title: The Fusion Cafe
pins.description:
Favourite details from many neighbourhood coffee shops are combined into one composite cafe model.

Model making | Interior design | Composite cafe | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 融合咖啡館
zh-Hant.description:
把社區裡多間咖啡店最喜愛的細節，組合成一座複合式咖啡館模型。

模型製作｜室內設計｜複合式咖啡館｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 完成的複合式咖啡館模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student visited many coffee shops in the community, from cafes in office towers to an old house in the old town, and found that each had its own charm. The project asks how favourite elements from different cafes can be combined into one place for both rest and work.
captions: Ink and watercolour drawing of a cafe interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生走訪社區中許多咖啡店，從辦公大樓裡的咖啡館到老城區的老屋，發現每一間都有自己的魅力。作品探問，如何把不同咖啡館中喜愛的元素，組合成一個兼顧休息與工作的空間。
captions: 咖啡館室內的鋼筆淡彩圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Favourite elements such as bold greens, spacious tables, comfortable chairs and bright lighting were recorded in watercolour. Patterns, brick, tiles and chair forms were collected as a small library of details.
captions: Sketches of plants, tiles, brick, chairs and furniture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 鮮明的綠色、寬敞的桌子、舒適的椅子與明亮的燈光等喜愛元素，都以水彩記錄下來。花紋、磚牆、磁磚與椅子造型被整理成一個細節資料庫。
captions: 植物、磁磚、磚牆、椅子與家具的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The composite cafe was modelled digitally, then scaled and translated into PVC components. The parts were finished with wallpaper and paint and assembled with furniture, glass, plants and an acrylic block mosaic.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 複合式咖啡館先以數位模型建構，再依比例轉譯為PVC構件。構件貼上壁紙、上漆，並組裝家具、玻璃、植物與壓克力方塊馬賽克。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model joins a dark green cafe front, a tiled wall, a timber terrace and an open stair into one building. Seating, lighting and planting are arranged so visitors can both relax and work.
captions: Terrace and tiled facade of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型把深綠色的店面、磁磚牆、木露台與開放樓梯結合成一棟建築。座位、燈光與植栽的安排，讓來客既能放鬆也能工作。
captions: 模型的露台與磁磚立面。

sections.heading: The Fusion Cafe - Favourite Corners Assembled into One Place
sections.body: The student visited many coffee shops around the community, from cafes in office towers to an old house in the historic quarter, and found that each had a charm of its own. The project asks how favourite elements from different cafes could merge into one place suited to both rest and work. Observation began in watercolour: bold greens, generous tables, comfortable chairs and bright lighting were recorded one by one, and patterns, brick, tiles and chair forms were collected into a small library of details. The composite cafe was then modelled digitally, scaled and translated into PVC components, finished with wallpaper and paint, and assembled with furniture, glass, plants and an acrylic block mosaic. The final model joins a dark green shopfront, a tiled wall, a timber terrace and an open stair into a single building, with seating, lighting and planting arranged so that visitors can unwind or settle into focused work. Fragments of a neighbourhood are distilled into one welcoming room.

zh-Hant.heading: 融合咖啡館-把喜愛的角落拼成一個地方
zh-Hant.body: 學生走訪社區裡許多咖啡館，從辦公大樓裡的咖啡店到老城區的一棟老屋，發現每一間都有獨特的魅力。作品追問：如何把不同咖啡館裡最喜愛的元素，融合成一個既能休息又能工作的地方？觀察從水彩開始：濃烈的綠、寬敞的桌面、舒適的座椅與明亮的燈光被一一記錄；圖樣、磚、磁磚與椅子的形態，則被蒐集成一座小小的細部資料庫。融合的咖啡館先以數位建模，再經縮放轉譯為PVC構件，部件以壁紙與油漆修飾，並與家具、玻璃、植物及壓克力馬賽克組裝。最終模型把深綠色的店面、磁磚牆、木平台與開放樓梯結合為一棟建築，座位、燈光與植栽的安排，讓人既能放鬆，也能專注工作。

pins.title: Living and Farming
pins.description:
A stacked complex where purifying, farming and living share one green tower.

Model making | Vertical farming | Mixed-media complex | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生活與耕種
zh-Hant.description:
一座把淨化、耕種與居住疊在同一座綠色塔中的複合建築。

模型製作｜垂直農耕｜複合材料建築｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished living and farming complex.
完成的生活與耕種複合建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A classic study of rural society describes the deep attachment of Chinese people to the land. Many families still tend plants on balconies and rooftop gardens, so the project asks how farming and daily life can share one building.
captions: The book cover that inspired the living-and-farming complex.
Diagrams of plant, soil and roots, and the three layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部探討鄉土社會的經典著作，描述了華人與土地之間深厚的連結。許多家庭至今仍在陽台與屋頂花園種植，因此作品探問，耕種與日常生活如何共享一棟建築。
captions: 啟發居住與農耕綜合體的書籍封面。
植物、土壤與根系，以及三個層次的圖解。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Plant structure, soil and roots were studied in diagrams. The building was then organised in three parts from bottom to top: purifying, farming and living.
captions: Pencil sketch of the stacked model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以圖解研究植物構造、土壤與根系。建築由下而上分為三個部分：淨化、耕種與居住。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: White living boxes were tested above timber planting decks. Sticks, fabric, clay, straw, yarn and acrylic were combined for structure, shade and water.
captions: Details of homes and planting decks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色的居住量體被安排在木構種植平台之上反覆測試。木棒、布料、黏土、吸管、毛線與壓克力被組合成結構、遮陽與水路。
captions: 住居與種植平台的細部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model stacks a purifying base, planted terraces and white homes into one tower. Greenery spills over every level, making farming part of everyday life.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型把淨化基座、種植平台與白色住居堆疊成一座塔。綠意溢出每一層，讓耕種成為日常生活的一部分。

sections.heading: Living and Farming - Letting Fields Grow into a Building
sections.body: A classic study of rural society describes the deep attachment of Chinese people to the land, and many families still tend plants on balconies and rooftop gardens. The project therefore asks whether farming and daily life might share a single building. Plant structure, soil and roots were first studied in diagrams, and the building was then organised in three parts from bottom to top: purifying, farming and living. White living boxes were tested above timber planting decks, while sticks, fabric, clay, straw, yarn and acrylic were combined to handle structure, shade and water. The finished model stacks a purifying base, planted terraces and white homes into one tower, with greenery spilling over every level. Farming is no longer something that happens elsewhere; it becomes part of the everyday rhythm of the household, a quiet continuation of an old bond with the soil carried upward into the density of contemporary city life.

zh-Hant.heading: 生活與耕作-讓田地長進一棟樓
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於鄉土社會的經典研究，描述了華人對土地的深厚依戀。至今仍有許多家庭在陽台與屋頂花園照料植物，這個作品於是追問：耕作與日常生活，能否共享同一棟建築？植物的構造、土壤與根系先以圖解加以研究；建築隨後由下而上分為三個部分：淨化、耕作與居住。白色的居住盒子在木構種植平台上方被反覆測試，木棒、布料、陶土、稻草、毛線與壓克力被組合起來，承擔結構、遮陽與水的功能。最終的模型把淨化的基座、種滿植物的平台與白色住宅疊成一座塔；綠意從每一層溢出，讓耕作成為日常生活的一部分。

pins.title: A Plant Stand That Breathes
pins.description:
Coconut fibre from food waste strengthens cement pots for a plant stand that breathes.

Material research | Product design | Bio-based concrete | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 會呼吸的植物架
zh-Hant.description:
以廚餘中的椰子纖維強化水泥花盆，做成一座會呼吸的植物架。

材料研究｜產品設計｜生質混凝土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Flower pots made of coconut fibre at home led the student to experiment with food waste. The aim was a breathing plant stand that can really be used to grow plants.
captions: From fresh coconut to chunks, fibre, fertiliser and powder.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 家中的椰纖花盆，啟發學生以廚餘進行實驗。目標是做出一座真的能種植物、會呼吸的植物架。
captions: 從新鮮椰子到碎塊、纖維、肥料與粉末。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Coconut was chopped, shredded into fibre, fermented into fertiliser and ground into powder. Shrimp shells, eggshells and other wastes were mixed with concrete in different amounts and compared.
captions: Test discs of concrete mixed with different food wastes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 椰子被切塊、撕成纖維、發酵成肥料，並磨成粉末。蝦殼、蛋殼等廚餘以不同比例混入混凝土並加以比較。
captions: 混入不同廚餘的混凝土試片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Coconut fibre was chosen because it bridges micro-cracks in cement while its porous fibres carry water and air. Pots were cast and planted to test drainage, moisture and root health.
captions: A hanging pot in rope netting.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選擇椰纖，是因為它能橋接水泥中的微裂縫，多孔的纖維又能輸送水分與空氣。學生灌製花盆並種上植物，測試排水、保濕與根系健康。
captions: 種上植物的纖維混凝土花盆。
放置空氣鳳梨的小花盆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The stand combines timber shelves, branches and fibre-concrete pots, including a hanging pot. Leftover coconut shells can also be processed into nutrient-rich soil.
captions: Arranging plants on the finished stand.
Details of shelves and disc pots.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 植物架結合木層架、樹枝與纖維混凝土花盆，還有一只懸吊花盆。剩下的椰殼也能再處理成養分豐富的土壤。
captions: 在完成的花架上擺放植物。
層架與圓形花盆的細部。

sections.heading: A Plant Stand That Breathes - Coconut Fibre Letting Concrete Breathe
sections.body: Flower pots made of coconut fibre at home led the student to experiment with food waste, aiming for a breathing plant stand that could genuinely be used to grow plants. Coconut was chopped, shredded into fibre, fermented into fertiliser and ground into powder, while shrimp shells, eggshells and other wastes were mixed with concrete in different proportions and compared side by side. Out of this series of comparisons, coconut fibre stood out: it bridges micro-cracks in cement, and its porous strands carry water and air. Pots were cast and planted to test drainage, moisture and the health of roots over time. The finished stand brings together timber shelves, branches and fibre-concrete pots, including one that hangs, and leftover coconut shells can themselves be processed into nutrient-rich soil. Nothing in the cycle is wasted, and a household object becomes a small, careful demonstration of how material research can return what we discard to the life of the soil.

zh-Hant.heading: 會呼吸的植物架-以椰纖讓混凝土透氣
zh-Hant.body: 家中以椰子纖維製成的花盆，引領學生開始以食物廢料進行實驗，目標是一座真正能種植植物、會呼吸的植物架。椰子被剁碎、撕成纖維、發酵為肥料，再磨成粉末；蝦殼、蛋殼等廢棄物則以不同比例與混凝土混合並加以比較。在一連串的比較之後，椰纖脫穎而出：它能跨越水泥中的微小裂縫，多孔的纖維也能輸送水與空氣。花盆被澆鑄並種下植物，用以測試排水、濕度與根系的健康。完成的植物架結合木層板、枝條與纖維混凝土花盆，還包含一個吊盆；剩下的椰殼，也能被處理成富含養分的土壤，讓整個循環沒有浪費。

pins.title: Cinderella
pins.description:
A favourite fairy-tale film becomes a tower that grows from paper arches into glowing blue petals.

Model making | Film-inspired narrative | Mixed-media tower | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 灰姑娘
zh-Hant.description:
一部喜愛的童話電影，化為一座從紙拱長成發光藍色花瓣的塔。

模型製作｜電影敘事｜複合材料塔｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student's favourite film is a live-action version of a classic fairy tale, with harmonious colours and pastoral, intricate details. The project asks how the heroine's growth, gentle yet resilient, can become a physical model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生最喜愛的電影是一部經典童話的真人版，色彩和諧，田園氣息與精緻細節兼具。作品探問，女主角溫柔而堅韌的成長歷程，如何化為實體模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each stage of the story was mapped onto a part of a tower, from a closed white base to an open, blooming top. The signature blue, natural greenery and glowing details became the palette.
captions: Shaping plastic, cutting card and testing colour.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 故事的每個階段被對應到塔的不同部位，從封閉的白色基座到綻放的頂端。招牌藍色、自然綠意與發光細節構成材料色盤。
captions: 塑形塑膠片、切割卡紙與測試色彩。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Card arcades, bamboo weaving, organza, resin and heat-shaped plastic were tested layer by layer. An LED strip and UV light make the transparent pieces glow.
captions: The blue petals and the paper arcade.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 卡紙拱廊、竹編、歐根紗、樹脂與熱塑塑膠被逐層測試。LED燈條與紫外光讓透明構件發光。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower rises from paper arches into swirling blue petals, a bamboo ribbon and branches. Each layer stands for one stage of growth.
captions: Branches and petals over the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 塔從紙拱升起，轉為旋繞的藍色花瓣、竹帶與枝葉。每一層代表成長的一個階段。
captions: 基座上方的枝葉與花瓣。

sections.heading: Cinderella - From a Closed White Base to Blooming Blue Petals
sections.body: The student's favourite film is a live-action version of a classic fairy tale, rich in harmonious colour and intricate pastoral detail, and the project asks how the heroine's growth, gentle yet resilient, could become a physical model. Each stage of the story was mapped onto a part of a tower, rising from a closed white base to an open, blossoming crown, while the signature blue, natural greenery and glimmering details formed the palette. Card arcades, bamboo weaving, organza, resin and heat-shaped plastic were tested layer by layer, and an LED strip and UV light make the transparent pieces glow from within. The finished tower climbs from paper arches into swirling blue petals, a bamboo ribbon and reaching branches, with every layer standing for a single stage of growth. A fairy tale's tenderness is thus held in a luminous vertical form, where the slow unfolding of a character becomes something the eye can follow upward, tier by tier, toward the light.

zh-Hant.heading: 仙杜瑞拉-從封閉的白色基座綻放成藍色花瓣
zh-Hant.body: 學生最喜愛的電影，是一部經典童話的真人版，色彩和諧，田園般的細節細膩繁複。作品追問：女主角溫柔而堅韌的成長，如何化為一件實體模型？故事的每個階段被對應到一座塔的不同部位，從封閉的白色基座，一路走向開放而綻放的頂端；招牌的藍、自然的綠意與閃爍的細節，則構成了色盤。卡紙拱廊、竹編、歐根紗、樹脂與熱塑塑膠被逐層測試，LED燈條與紫外光讓透明的部件發出光芒。最終，高塔從紙拱升起，化為旋轉的藍色花瓣、一道竹編緞帶與枝條，每一層都代表一段成長，讓童話的溫柔被凝結為一座發光的塔。

pins.title: Spinning Motion
pins.description:
A paper volume and a personal spinning gesture merge into a wearable model of sticks and paper.

Model making | Motion study | Stick and paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 旋轉的動作
zh-Hant.description:
紙量體與個人旋轉的動作結合，成為以木棒與紙製作的可穿戴模型。

模型製作｜動作研究｜木棒與紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 木棒與紙的可穿戴模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from a three-dimensional paper model built from a painting. The student asks how that volume can be joined with a personal movement, spinning with arms outstretched.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品從一件依據畫作製作的立體紙模型出發。學生探問，這個量體如何與張開雙臂旋轉的個人動作結合。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The paper volume was photographed and rendered to read its rhythm of ribs and curves. Digital studies looked at it from several angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拍攝並渲染紙量體，閱讀肋片與曲線的節奏。數位研究從多個角度觀察它。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The spinning motion was captured and frozen in a large hatched drawing. Its form was then abstracted and rebuilt as a light frame of sticks.
captions: Drawing of the frozen spinning motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 旋轉的動作被捕捉並凝結在一張大幅排線手繪中。接著將其形體抽象化，重建為輕盈的木棒框架。
captions: 凝結旋轉動作的手繪圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A new wearable model was assembled piece by piece from wooden sticks and paper. The finished frame follows the sweeping path of the spin.
captions: Wearing the stick-and-paper frame on the arm.
Assembling the wearable frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木棒與紙逐件組裝出新的可穿戴模型。完成的框架順著旋轉時掃過的軌跡延伸。
captions: 將木棒與紙框戴在手臂上。

sections.heading: Spinning Motion - Freezing an Outstretched Spin into a Wearable Frame
sections.body: The project begins with a three-dimensional paper model derived from a painting, and the student asked how that volume could be joined with a personal movement: spinning with arms outstretched. The paper form was first photographed and rendered to read its rhythm of ribs and curves, and digital studies examined it from several angles. Then the spin itself was captured and frozen in a large hatched drawing. Its shape was abstracted and rebuilt as a light frame of sticks, translating a blur of motion into a clear structure. Finally, a new wearable model was assembled piece by piece from wooden sticks and paper. The finished frame follows the sweeping path of the spin, so that a fleeting gesture of the body is preserved as something one can touch and even wear. Painting, paper, movement and body are drawn into a single loop, each giving shape to the next, until the dance and the object become nearly indistinguishable.

zh-Hant.heading: 旋轉之舞-把張臂旋轉凝成可穿的框架
zh-Hant.body: 作品始於一件由繪畫衍生的立體紙模型。學生追問：這個量體，如何與一個屬於自己的動作結合？那個動作，是張開雙臂旋轉。紙的量體先被拍攝與渲染，以解讀肋條與曲線的節奏，數位研究則從多個角度加以觀察。接著，旋轉的動作被捕捉下來，凝結在一張大幅的排線繪圖中；它的形態隨後被抽象化，重建為一副輕盈的木棒框架。最後，一件新的可穿戴模型以木棒與紙逐片組裝而成。完成的框架追隨旋轉時橫掃而過的軌跡，讓一瞬間的身體姿態，被留存為可以觸摸的結構。

pins.title: A Scaffold of Growth
pins.description:
A cement-and-wire viewing tower grows a ligament of clay and wire around its spiral stair.

Model making | Bio-inspired structure | Cement and wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生長的支架
zh-Hant.description:
一座水泥與鐵絲的觀景塔，沿著螺旋梯長出黏土與鐵絲的韌帶。

模型製作｜仿生結構｜水泥與鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work is inspired by how a torn knee ligament can be rebuilt, with a braided graft fixed by absorbable pins becoming a new ligament. The project asks how this process of repair and growth can shape a structure.
captions: MRI scans of the knee that were traced for the structure studies.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品的靈感來自膝關節韌帶的重建：以編織的移植物搭配可吸收的固定釘，長成新的韌帶。作品探問，這種修復與生長的過程，如何塑造一個結構。
captions: 描繪結構習作所依據的膝關節核磁共振影像。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Knee structures were drawn with bones as support and muscles and ligaments as flexible protectors. Joint-like wire-and-cement pieces were then tested for strength and load-bearing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪膝關節結構，以骨骼為支撐，肌肉與韌帶為柔性的保護。接著測試類似關節的鐵絲與水泥構件的強度與承重。
captions: 水泥與鐵絲的關節測試。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Most joint tests succeeded, though one wood-like tensile form did not. Several moulds of the cement tower failed under their own weight before the structure was reinforced.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 多數關節測試成功，只有一個仿木的張力形體失敗。水泥塔的數個模具在自重下失敗，之後才補強成功。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A clay-and-wire ligament grows along the tower and wraps its spiral stair. Intentional cracks in the cement express damage, repair and growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 黏土與鐵絲的韌帶沿著塔身生長，包覆螺旋梯。水泥上刻意留下的裂痕，表達損傷、修復與生長。
captions: 包覆在纖維中的螺旋梯。

sections.heading: A Scaffold of Growth - A Tower Raised in the Posture of Repair
sections.body: A torn knee ligament can be rebuilt, with a braided graft fixed by absorbable pins gradually becoming a new ligament, and the project asks how this process of repair and growth might shape a structure. The student first drew the anatomy of the knee, with bone as support and muscles and ligaments as flexible protection, and then tested joint-like pieces of wire and cement for strength and load-bearing. Most of the joint trials succeeded, though one wood-like tensile form did not, and several moulds of the cement tower collapsed under their own weight before the structure was reinforced. Those failures became part of the story. In the end, a ligament of clay and wire grows along the tower and wraps around its spiral stair, while deliberate cracks in the cement speak of damage, mending and growth. The tower stands not as a flawless object but as a body that has been injured, held together and allowed to heal.

zh-Hant.heading: 生長的支架-以修復之姿撐起高塔
zh-Hant.body: 膝蓋韌帶撕裂後可以被重建：編織的移植物以可吸收的骨釘固定，最終長成新的韌帶。作品由此追問：這段修復與生長的過程，如何塑造一座結構？學生先描繪膝蓋的構造，以骨骼為支撐，肌肉與韌帶為柔韌的保護；接著，類似關節的鐵絲與水泥構件被測試其強度與承重。多數關節試驗成功，但一個類似木材的張力形體並未如願；水泥塔的數個模具也在自身重量下失敗，直到結構被補強。最終，一條陶土與鐵絲構成的韌帶沿著塔身生長，纏繞螺旋樓梯；水泥中刻意留下的裂縫，訴說著損傷、修復與成長。

pins.title: Oranges Pavilion
pins.description:
Mandarin pulp segments become the woven roofs of a bamboo pavilion in an orange grove.

Model making | Pavilion | Bamboo strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 橘子涼亭
zh-Hant.description:
橘子果肉的瓣形，化為果園中竹編涼亭的屋頂。

模型製作｜涼亭｜竹條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student studied the cross-sections of more than twenty fruits and chose the mandarin orange. The project explores how nature and architecture relate through a pavilion set inside an orange grove.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了二十多種水果的剖面，最後選擇橘子。作品透過一座位於橘子園中的涼亭，探索自然與建築的關係。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The pulp segments were drawn and then shaped digitally. The forms were scattered on a grid to test spacing and rhythm.
captions: Pulp segment forms on a grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪果肉瓣形，再以數位方式塑形。這些形體被散佈在網格上，測試間距與節奏。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The pulp forms were stretched into curved roofs over raised timber decks. A sketch placed the pavilion among the orange trees.
captions: Sketch of the pavilion in the grove.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 果肉形體被拉伸成架高木平台上方的曲面屋頂。一張草圖把涼亭放進橘子樹之間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The bamboo-strip model shows woven shells floating above a walkway. The organic shapes form a harmonious space that blends with the grove.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 竹條模型呈現漂浮在步道上方的編織殼體。有機的形體構成一個與果園融為一體的和諧空間。

sections.heading: Oranges Pavilion - Fruit Segments Woven in a Grove
sections.body: After studying the cross-sections of more than twenty fruits, the student chose the mandarin orange. Through a pavilion set within an orange grove, the project explores how nature and architecture relate. The segments of the fruit were drawn first and then shaped digitally, and these forms were scattered across a grid to test spacing and rhythm. Next, the segment shapes were stretched into curved roofs hovering over raised timber decks, and a sketch placed the pavilion among the orange trees. The final bamboo-strip model shows woven shells floating above a walkway. Their organic shapes create a harmonious space that blends into the grove, as if the pavilion had grown there alongside the trees. The quiet order hidden inside a single fruit is enlarged into a shelter that people can inhabit, and the act of peeling an orange becomes, in miniature, a method for reading structure, light and shade in the natural world.

zh-Hant.heading: 橘子涼亭-在果園中編出的果瓣
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了二十多種水果的剖面，最終選擇了橘子。作品藉一座置於橘園中的涼亭，探索自然與建築之間的關係。果瓣先被描繪，再以數位方式塑形；這些形體被散佈在格網上，測試間距與節奏。隨後，果瓣的形態被拉伸為弧形屋頂，覆蓋在架高的木平台上，一張草圖把涼亭安放在橘樹之間。最終的竹條模型，呈現編織的殼體漂浮於步道之上。有機的形狀圍塑出一處和諧的空間，與果園融為一體；一顆水果內部的秩序，就此被放大為人可以棲身的庇蔭。

pins.title: Redesigning a Civic Plaza
pins.description:
Angled terraces, pools and planters reshape a downtown plaza for rest and market stalls.

San Francisco | Digital model | Public plaza | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 市民廣場再設計
zh-Hant.description:
以傾斜平台、水池與植栽重塑市中心廣場，容納休憩與市集攤位。

舊金山｜數位模型｜公共廣場｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 再設計後的廣場透視圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A high school design competition asked students to reimagine a downtown plaza in San Francisco. The plaza is surrounded by office buildings and hosts events such as free lessons and markets, so it needs places to rest and room for stalls.
captions: The plaza site map and street-level photos.
Rock and shoreline forms that inspired the plaza edges.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一項高中設計競賽，邀請學生重新想像舊金山市中心的一座廣場。廣場被辦公大樓包圍，並舉辦免費課程與市集等活動，因此需要休憩空間與攤位位置。
captions: 廣場基地地圖與街道照片。
啟發廣場邊緣的岩石與海岸形態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site was studied through maps, photos and the directions people walk. Diagrams marked green zones and the main routes across the plaza.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生透過地圖、照片與行人方向研究基地。圖解標示出綠地分區與穿越廣場的主要動線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The design took cues from the plaza's fountain and was oriented along pedestrian movement. Faceted planters, pools and seats were modelled as one landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計從廣場的噴泉取得靈感，並順著行人移動的方向配置。多面體的植栽、水池與座椅被塑造成一整片地景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The digital model shows angled terraces wrapping pools and green islands. People can rest along the edges while open ground stays free for stalls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 數位模型呈現傾斜平台環抱水池與綠島。人們可以在邊緣休憩，開放的地面則留給攤位使用。

sections.heading: Redesigning a Civic Plaza - Letting Crowds and Markets Share Ground
sections.body: A high school design competition invited students to reimagine a downtown plaza in San Francisco. Surrounded by office buildings and hosting events such as free lessons and markets, the plaza needs both places to rest and room for stalls. Understanding the site came first: maps, photographs and the directions in which people walk were studied one by one, and diagrams marked green zones and the main routes across the square. Building on that analysis, the design took cues from the plaza's fountain and was oriented along the flow of pedestrians, with faceted planters, pools and seats shaped into a single continuous landscape. The digital model shows angled terraces wrapping around pools and green islands, so that people can rest along the edges while open ground remains free for stalls. Movement and pause, commerce and leisure, are balanced within one gesture, turning a space of transit into a place where the city can gather, linger and trade.

zh-Hant.heading: 市民廣場再設計-讓人潮與市集共存
zh-Hant.body: 一場高中設計競賽，邀請學生重新想像舊金山市中心的一座廣場。廣場被辦公大樓環繞，舉辦免費課程與市集等活動，因此既需要休憩之處，也需要攤位的空間。理解基地是第一步：地圖、照片與行人行走的方向被一一研究，圖解則標示出綠帶與穿越廣場的主要動線。在這樣的分析之上，設計從廣場的噴泉汲取線索，並順著人流的方向配置；多面的植栽、水池與座椅被塑造成一片完整的地景。數位模型呈現傾斜的平台環抱著水池與綠島，人們可以沿著邊緣休息，開闊的地面則保留給攤位。

pins.title: The Garden of Eternity
pins.description:
A mourning space that treats death as a milestone, with flower tombstones, roots and light.

Model making | Installation | Mourning space | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 永恆花園
zh-Hant.description:
一個把死亡視為里程碑的追思空間，以花朵墓碑、根系與光影構成。

模型製作｜裝置｜追思空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cemeteries hold people's thoughts about eternity, and every farewell shows how fleeting life is. The project designs a mourning space that treats death as a milestone in a continuing journey rather than an end.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 墓園承載人們對永恆的思索，每一次告別都讓人感受生命的短暫。作品設計一個追思空間，把死亡視為持續旅程中的里程碑，而非終點。
captions: 初期的框架與屋頂模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Natural materials, light and shadow were chosen to show the cycle of life. Tombstones were made from flowers set in glue, to capture each bloom and pass hope to the next generation.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生選用自然材料與光影，表現生命的循環。墓碑以花朵封入膠中製成，留住盛放的瞬間，並把希望傳給下一代。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A grassy roof, a bamboo frame and twisting roots shelter small figures, coils and stairs inside. Model views test how light falls through the slatted walls.
captions: Figures among coils and stairs inside.
Roots and stairs in the interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 草皮屋頂、竹構框架與蜿蜒的根系，庇護著室內的小人形、線圈與樓梯。模型視角測試光線如何穿過條狀牆面。
captions: 室內線圈與樓梯間的人形。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Two installations extend the garden: a rope bloom hung on a tree, and a corner of cyanotypes and netting about the threads that bind people together. Together they say that life continues in memory and that separation need not be feared.
captions: The outdoor rope installation hanging from a tree.
A rope bloom hung on a tree.
Looking up into the rope canopy.
Cyanotypes and netting on a red corner.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩件裝置延伸了花園：一朵懸掛在樹上的繩結花，以及一個以藍曬與網講述人與人之間牽絆的牆角。它們共同訴說生命延續在記憶裡，分離不必畏懼。
captions: 掛在樹上的戶外繩索裝置。
紅色牆角上的藍曬與網。

sections.heading: The Garden of Eternity - Farewell as a Milestone on a Journey
sections.body: Cemeteries hold human thoughts about eternity, and every farewell is a reminder of how fleeting life is. The project designs a mourning space that treats death as a milestone in a continuing journey rather than an end. Natural materials, light and shadow were chosen as the language of life's cycle, and tombstones were made from flowers set in glue, holding each bloom in place and passing hope on to the next generation. Over this, a grassy roof, a bamboo frame and twisting roots shelter small figures, coils and stairs within, while model views test how light falls through the slatted walls. Two installations extend the garden further: a rope bloom hung on a tree, and a corner of cyanotypes and netting about the threads that bind people together. Together they suggest that life continues in memory and that separation need not be feared, offering a place where grief can soften into something closer to gratitude.

zh-Hant.heading: 永恆之園-讓告別成為旅程的一站
zh-Hant.body: 墓園承載著人們對永恆的思索，而每一次告別，都提醒著生命的短暫。這個作品設計一處哀悼空間，把死亡視為持續旅程中的一座里程碑，而非終點。自然材料與光影被選為表達生命循環的語言；墓碑由封存於膠中的花朵製成，留住每一次綻放，也把希望傳給下一代。在此之上，草坡屋頂、竹構框架與盤繞的根系，庇護著內部的小人形、線圈與階梯，模型視角則測試光如何穿過條板牆面灑落。兩件裝置進一步延伸這座花園：一朵懸掛在樹上的繩編花，以及一角由藍曬與網材構成、講述人與人之間牽繫的空間。它們共同訴說：生命延續於記憶之中，分離無需畏懼。

pins.title: Passage in Planes
pins.description:
Folded and peeled paper planes turn a lakeside slope into a landscape of paths and shelters.

Model making | Landscape architecture | Paper and basswood | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 平面中的通道
zh-Hant.description:
折疊與剝離的紙平面，把湖畔坡地變成一片由路徑與遮蔽構成的地景。

模型製作｜地景建築｜紙與椴木｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project was made in a summer design studio, starting from a layered abstract painting chosen as a precedent. The student pulled out two actions from it, fragmentation and layering, to guide the design of a site on a lakeside slope.
captions: A composite line drawing of fragments.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品完成於一個暑期設計工作營，以一幅層疊的抽象畫作為先例。學生從中提取「碎片化」與「層疊」兩個動作，引導湖畔坡地基地的設計。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A language of cutting and folding surfaces was developed to express fragmentation. Basswood sticks were added to show movement and direction across the site.
captions: The digital model of the terrain.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生發展出一套切割與折疊表面的語彙，表達碎片化。椴木條則用來表現穿越基地的移動與方向。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Folded and peeled planes respond to the natural topography and guide visitors across, around and through the terrain. Walkable roofs rise to viewpoints while the ground peels down at the centre into a quiet zone near the lake.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 折疊與剝離的平面回應自然地形，引導訪客跨越、環繞並穿過地景。可行走的屋頂升向觀景點，中央的地面則向下剝離，形成靠近湖水的安靜區域。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model avoids fixed entries and set programs, so circulation unfolds through each visitor's own choices. Basswood sticks mark sightlines and pauses among the angular planes.
captions: Close views of planes and sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型避免固定的入口與既定機能，讓動線隨著每位訪客的選擇展開。椴木條在銳利的平面之間標示視線與停頓。

sections.heading: Passage in Planes - A Landscape Where Paths Choose Themselves
sections.body: Also from a summer design studio, this work takes a layered abstract painting as its precedent. From it the student drew out two actions, fragmentation and layering, to guide the design of a site on a lakeside slope. To express fragmentation, a language of cutting and folding surfaces was developed step by step, and basswood sticks were added to convey movement and direction across the land. Folded and peeled planes respond to the natural topography, guiding visitors across, around and through the terrain. Walkable roofs rise toward viewpoints, while at the centre the ground peels downward into a quiet zone near the water. The model deliberately avoids fixed entries and assigned programmes, so circulation unfolds through each visitor's own choices, and the sticks mark sightlines and pauses among the angular planes. A painting's restless energy is thus translated into a landscape of freedom, where wandering itself becomes the purpose of the place.

zh-Hant.heading: 平面中的通道-讓地景自行選擇路徑
zh-Hant.body: 同樣出自夏季設計工作營，作品以一幅層疊的抽象繪畫為先例。學生從中提煉出兩個動作：碎裂與層疊，用以引導湖畔坡地上的基地設計。為了表達碎裂，一套切割與摺疊表面的語言被逐步發展出來；椴木棒則被加入，呈現跨越基地的移動與方向。摺起與剝離的平面回應自然地形，引導訪客橫越、環繞並穿過地勢；可行走的屋頂升向觀景點，中央的地面則向下剝離，形成鄰近湖畔的靜謐區域。模型刻意避免固定的入口與既定機能，讓動線隨每位訪客的選擇而展開；椴木棒在稜角分明的平面之間，標示出視線與停頓。

pins.title: Continuum
pins.description:
Tori carved out of stacked cylinders form a tower wrapped by one continuous circular path.

Digital model | Rendering | Torque study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 連續體
zh-Hant.description:
以圓環體切削堆疊的圓柱，形成一座被連續環形路徑包覆的塔。

數位模型｜渲染｜扭轉研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project was made in a summer design studio and explores the verb torque. The question was how a twisting action can carve spaces out of simple cylinders.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品完成於一個暑期設計工作營，探索動詞「扭轉」。題目在問，扭轉的動作如何從簡單的圓柱中切削出空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Tori were used to cut into stacked cylinders, step by step. Each step was checked in plan and in section.
captions: Section through the tower and ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以圓環體逐步切入堆疊的圓柱。每一步都在平面與剖面中檢查。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Like a spiral gallery, the design replaces stairs with a continuous circular path that leads to the top. Openings were cut for views, and a carved ground plane connects to the main building.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 如同螺旋展廊，設計以一條通往頂部的連續環形路徑取代樓梯。牆上切出觀景開口，切削的地面則連接主建築。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model was rendered into composite, section and unrolled drawings and a short animation. The drawings show how one rotating move organises the whole tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型被渲染成複合圖、剖面圖、展開圖與一段短動畫。這些圖說明一個旋轉的動作如何組織整座塔。

sections.heading: Continuum - A Whole Tower Carved by a Single Twist
sections.body: Made in a summer design studio, this project explores the verb torque, asking how a twisting action can carve spaces out of simple cylinders. Tori were used to cut into stacked cylinders step by step, and each step was checked in plan and in section. Like a spiral gallery, the design replaces stairs with a continuous circular path that leads to the top. Openings were cut to frame views, and a carved ground plane connects the tower to the main building. Finally, the model was rendered into composite, section and unrolled drawings along with a short animation. Together these drawings reveal how one rotating move organises the entire tower, allowing a simple geometric operation to generate an unbroken spatial experience. The rigour of the method and the fluidity of the result reinforce each other, so that the visitor's ascent becomes a slow reading of the twist from which every room, view and threshold was born.

zh-Hant.heading: 連續體-以一次扭轉雕出整座塔
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品誕生於夏季設計工作營，探索的動詞是扭轉。問題在於：一個扭轉的動作，如何從簡單的圓柱中雕刻出空間？環面被用來逐步切入堆疊的圓柱，每一步都在平面與剖面中加以檢驗。設計如同一座螺旋藝廊，以連續的環形坡道取代樓梯，一路引向頂端；開口被切出以引入景觀，被雕刻的地面則與主建築相連。最終，模型被渲染為合成圖、剖面圖、展開圖與一段短動畫。這些圖面共同揭示，一個旋轉的動作如何組織起整座塔，讓單純的幾何操作，生成連綿不斷的空間經驗。

pins.title: Misery House
pins.description:
A suspended frame of basswood splints and folded PVC explores how confinement tightens space.

Model making | Spatial narrative | PVC and basswood | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 苦難之屋
zh-Hant.description:
以椴木夾板與折疊PVC構成的懸吊框架，探索禁錮如何收緊空間。

模型製作｜空間敘事｜PVC與椴木｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work is inspired by a psychological thriller in which an obsessive fan holds a writer captive in a remote house. The student explored how psychological constraint can shape the tightness of a space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品的靈感來自一部心理驚悚故事：一位偏執的書迷把作家囚禁在偏遠的房子裡。學生探索心理上的束縛如何塑造空間的緊迫感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A diagram of the tortures in the story was drawn and fed into a parametric script. The script turned the drawing into patterns of lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把故事中的折磨畫成圖解，輸入參數化腳本。腳本把圖面轉化為線條圖樣。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sections were cut from PVC board along the lines and folded. Basswood sticks joined the pieces like brittle splints, echoing the splints of a slow recovery.
captions: Cutting and folding the PVC pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生沿著線條從PVC板切出片段並折疊。椴木條像脆弱的夾板般連接構件，呼應緩慢復原時的夾板。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The pieces were connected and hung with fishing line from a metal frame. The suspended mass gives a feeling of containment similar to the house in the story.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 構件連接後以釣魚線懸吊在金屬框架上。懸浮的量體帶來與故事中那棟房子相似的禁錮感。

sections.heading: Misery House - Captivity Suspended in the Air
sections.body: The work draws on a psychological thriller in which an obsessive fan holds a writer captive in a remote house, and the student explored how psychological constraint can shape the tightness of a space. The tortures in the story were drawn as a diagram and fed into a parametric script, which turned the drawing into patterns of lines. Following those lines, sections were cut from PVC board and folded, and basswood sticks joined the pieces like brittle splints, echoing the splints of a slow recovery. Finally, all the parts were connected and hung with fishing line from a metal frame. The suspended mass creates a feeling of containment close to that of the house in the story, letting the viewer sense, in its stillness above the ground, a pressure that is hard to escape. Narrative dread is carried not by depiction but by tension, fragility and the unsettling calm of an object that cannot touch the floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 戰慄之屋-懸吊於空中的禁錮
zh-Hant.body: 作品的靈感來自一部心理驚悚片：一位偏執的書迷，把作家囚禁在偏遠的屋子裡。學生探討的是，心理的束縛如何塑造空間的緊迫感。故事中的種種折磨被繪成一張圖解，再輸入參數化腳本，轉化為線條構成的圖樣。沿著這些線條，PVC板被切出剖面並加以摺疊；椴木棒像脆弱的夾板般把各片接合，呼應緩慢復原時所用的夾板。最後，所有部件被連接起來，以釣魚線懸吊於金屬框架之下。懸浮的量體，營造出一種與故事中那棟屋子相似的禁錮感，讓觀者在空中的靜止裡，感受到難以掙脫的壓迫。

pins.title: Edge of Thaw
pins.description:
A gallery that collects glacier meltwater and purifies it in layered tanks people can watch.

Model making | Gallery | Resin and gypsum | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 融冰邊緣
zh-Hant.description:
一座收集冰川融水、以可觀看的層疊水槽淨化的展廊。

模型製作｜展廊｜樹脂與石膏｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student grew interested in glacier melting caused by global warming. The project asks how a space could reuse the water collected after glaciers melt.
captions: A glacier landscape that inspired the purification gallery.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生關注全球暖化造成的冰川融化。作品探問，一個空間如何再利用冰川融化後收集的水。
captions: 啟發淨化藝廊的冰川景觀。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The idea was sketched by hand and then built as a digital model. Ice forms were shaped to drip into the space below.
captions: Digital model of the ice form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先手繪構想，再建成數位模型。冰體形態被塑造成向下方空間滴落。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stone, sand and filter media were tested in each acrylic tank to refine the purifying layers. Resin and gypsum were cast for the hanging ice.
captions: Material tests with stone and gypsum.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生在每個壓克力水槽中測試石頭、沙與過濾材料，調整淨化層。懸吊的冰體則以樹脂與石膏澆鑄。
captions: 石頭與石膏的材料測試。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A transparent gallery lets visitors watch the water being purified and learn about the harm of glacier melting. A tube beneath the tanks delivers clean water directly to people.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 透明的展廊讓訪客看見水被淨化的過程，認識冰川融化的危害。水槽下方的管線把乾淨的水直接送到人們手中。

sections.heading: Edge of Thaw - Making Glacial Meltwater Drinkable Again
sections.body: Glacier melt caused by global warming drew the student's attention, and the project asks whether a space could reuse the water gathered after glaciers thaw. The idea was first sketched by hand and then built as a digital model, with forms of ice shaped to drip into the space below so that the flow of water itself takes the leading role. Testing followed. Stone, sand and filter media were placed in each acrylic tank and adjusted again and again to refine the purifying layers, while resin and gypsum were cast to form the hanging ice. In the end, a transparent gallery lets visitors watch the water being cleaned and learn about the harm of glacial loss, and a tube beneath the tanks delivers clean water directly to people. A climate crisis is thus turned into something tangible, a place of learning and of care, where the sight of each falling drop carries both a warning and a gift.

zh-Hant.heading: 融冰之境-讓冰川的淚水重新被飲用
zh-Hant.body: 全球暖化造成的冰川融化，引起學生的關注。作品追問：一個空間，能否再利用冰川融化後所收集的水？構想先以手繪草圖勾勒，再建構為數位模型；冰的形體被塑造成向下滴落的姿態，讓水流成為空間的主角。測試隨之展開：石塊、砂與濾材被放入每一座壓克力水槽，反覆調整淨化層的組合；樹脂與石膏則被澆鑄成懸吊的冰。最終，一座透明的展廳讓參觀者看見水被淨化的過程，並認識冰川消融的危害；水槽下方的管線，則把乾淨的水直接送到人們手中。一場氣候的危機，在此被轉化為可以觸及的教育與照護。

pins.title: The Inert World
pins.description:
A wire and found-object assemblage of a still central world circled by four rebellious planets.

Model making | Assemblage | Mixed media | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 惰性世界
zh-Hant.description:
以鐵絲與拾得物件組成的集合裝置：一個靜止的中心世界，被四顆反抗的星球環繞。

模型製作｜集合裝置｜複合媒材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work starts from an animated science-fiction series whose hero believes life is meaningless yet keeps living, exploring other universes. The student asked how a space can express this quiet resistance.
captions: Stills from the animated series studied.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品從一部動畫科幻影集出發，主角相信生命毫無意義，卻仍持續活著、探索其他宇宙。學生探問，空間如何表達這種安靜的反抗。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Episodes of the series were studied and sketched into a map of worlds. Each world was given its own attitude towards rules and systems.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究影集的各集內容，畫成一張世界地圖。每個世界都被賦予面對規則與體系的不同態度。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A central middle planet represents a regulated, restrained world where people often feel powerless. Four planets around it each show a way to resist, break or face the systems that confine them.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 中央的星球代表一個受規範、受約束、令人常感無力的世界。周圍四顆星球各自呈現抵抗、打破或面對束縛體系的方式。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The inert world at the centre is defined by apathy rather than laws, a chaos disguised as order. The assemblage shows the many ways beings struggle for agency in a universe that offers none.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 中心的惰性世界由冷漠而非法則定義，是偽裝成秩序的混亂。集合裝置呈現眾生在毫無回應的宇宙中爭取自主的多種方式。

sections.heading: The Inert World - Searching for Resistance Across a Multiverse
sections.body: The work starts from an animated science-fiction series whose hero believes life is meaningless yet keeps living, wandering through other universes, and the student asked how a space could express that quiet resistance. Episodes of the series were studied and sketched into a map of worlds, with each world given its own attitude toward rules and systems. At the centre of this map sits a middle planet, regulated and restrained, standing for a world where people often feel powerless. Four planets circle it, each showing a different way to resist, break or confront the systems that confine them. The inert world at the core is defined not by laws but by apathy, a chaos disguised as order. The assemblage thereby reveals the many ways beings struggle for agency in a universe that offers none, turning philosophical unease into an arrangement of wire and void that invites the viewer to choose a path of their own.

zh-Hant.heading: 惰性世界-在多重宇宙中尋找抵抗
zh-Hant.body: 一部動畫科幻影集的主角，相信生命毫無意義，卻依然活著、穿梭於不同宇宙。學生由此追問：空間如何表達這種安靜的抵抗？影集的各集被研究並草繪為一張世界地圖，每一個世界都被賦予面對規則與體制的獨特態度。在這張地圖的中心，一顆受到管控、克制的中間星球，象徵人們常感無力的世界；環繞它的四顆星球，各自呈現抵抗、打破或直面束縛體制的方式。位於核心的惰性世界，並非由法律界定，而是由冷漠所定義，是一種偽裝成秩序的混亂。這件組合作品，因此展現了萬物如何在一個不給予任何主體性的宇宙中，努力爭取自身的位置。

pins.title: CoHabit
pins.description:
A climbing framework of sticks and tubes gives cats high, hidden places above shared human space.

Model making | Multispecies design | Basswood and straws | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 共棲
zh-Hant.description:
由木條與管子構成的攀爬框架，在人類共享空間上方，為貓提供高處與隱蔽處。

模型製作｜跨物種設計｜椴木與吸管｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began with the student's experience of caring for stray cats that came and went as they wished. The student asked whether architecture, usually built for humans, could also serve other creatures without forcing them to adapt.
captions: Studies of cat postures and behaviour.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品始於學生照顧流浪貓的經驗，這些貓來去自如。學生思考，通常為人而建的建築，能否也服務其他生物，而不強迫牠們適應。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Feline behaviour was studied through a documentary and readings on animal ethics. The studies showed that cats love high places and secret, solitary spots.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生透過紀錄片與動物倫理的閱讀研究貓的行為。研究顯示貓喜歡高處與隱密、獨處的角落。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stick grids were tested as frames for climbing at different heights. Plastic straws became tubes that cats can use as hiding spots.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生測試木條網格作為不同高度的攀爬框架。塑膠吸管化為貓可以躲藏的管道。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The upper framework belongs to cats, while the ground level stays free for people to meet and relax. The aim is a shared space that does not force animals to fit human patterns.
captions: Close views of tubes and sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 上層框架屬於貓，地面層則留給人們相聚與休憩。目標是一個不強迫動物配合人類模式的共享空間。

sections.heading: CoHabit - A Framework Shared by Cats and People
sections.body: Caring for stray cats that came and went as they pleased lay at the source of this project. The student asked whether architecture, usually built for humans, could also serve other creatures without forcing them to adapt. Answering that question meant first understanding cats. Through a documentary and readings in animal ethics, the research found that cats love high places as well as secret, solitary corners. These findings were turned into concrete trials. Stick grids were tested as climbing frames at different heights, and plastic straws became tubes in which cats could hide. In the end, the upper framework belongs to the cats while the ground level stays open for people to meet and rest. The design pursues a genuinely shared space, one that does not ask animals to fit human patterns but lets two ways of living find their own place side by side, each respected rather than merely tolerated.

zh-Hant.heading: 共棲-為貓與人共享的框架
zh-Hant.body: 照顧來去自如的流浪貓的經驗，是這個作品的源頭。學生追問：通常為人而建的建築，能否也服務其他生命，而不強迫牠們適應？要回答這個問題，必須先理解貓。透過紀錄片與動物倫理的閱讀，研究發現貓偏愛高處，也喜歡隱密而獨處的角落。這些發現轉化為具體的試驗：木棒格網被測試為不同高度的攀爬框架，塑膠吸管則成為貓可以躲藏的管道。最終，上層的框架屬於貓，地面則留給人們相遇與休憩。這個設計追求一種共享的空間，不要求動物迎合人的模式，而讓兩種生活各得其所。

pins.title: Coffee-ground Brick
pins.description:
Bricks of used coffee grounds and mud lead to an underground coffee hub in a downtown block.

Material research | Architecture | Coffee grounds | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 咖啡渣磚
zh-Hant.description:
以咖啡渣與泥土製成的磚，延伸為市中心地下的咖啡社區據點。

材料研究｜建築｜咖啡渣｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The full-scale brick wall in its timber frame.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Having lived in a coffee-growing country where people built with corrugated sheets, the student wanted an ecofriendly, low-cost material for better construction. Used coffee grounds became the starting point.
captions: Photos of the downtown plaza site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生曾住在一個咖啡產地，當地人以浪板搭建房屋，因此希望找到環保、低成本的材料改善建造。用過的咖啡渣成為起點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Grounds collected from local coffee shops were dried for several days. They were then mixed with mud and water and pressed into moulds.
captions: Collecting used coffee grounds from a local café.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生向在地咖啡店收集咖啡渣，晾乾數天。接著與泥土和水混合，壓入模具。
captions: 向在地咖啡店收集咖啡渣。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The bricks were applied to a proposal for an underground coffee community in downtown San Francisco. Three levels hold a market tracing the bean-to-brew cycle, a gallery on coffee origins and a rooftop café with an open plaza.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 磚被應用在舊金山市中心地下咖啡社區的提案中。三個樓層分別容納呈現從咖啡豆到沖煮全過程的市集、介紹咖啡產地的展廊，以及附開放廣場的屋頂咖啡館。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Many bricks were stacked in a full-scale timber frame with an opening at the top that acts as a window. The wall shows that waste from daily coffee can become a real building material.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 大量磚塊被堆疊進足尺木框中，頂部留有一個作為窗戶的開口。這面牆證明日常咖啡的廢料可以成為真正的建材。

sections.heading: Coffee-ground Brick - Laying Daily Leftovers into a Wall
sections.body: Having lived in a coffee-growing country where people built with corrugated sheets, the student wanted an eco-friendly, low-cost material that could improve construction, and used coffee grounds became the starting point. Grounds collected from local coffee shops were dried over several days, then mixed with mud and water and pressed into moulds to form bricks. Those bricks were next applied to a proposal for an underground coffee community in downtown San Francisco. Its three levels hold a market tracing the journey from bean to cup, a gallery on coffee origins and a rooftop café opening onto a plaza. Finally, many bricks were stacked within a full-scale timber frame, with an opening at the top that serves as a window. The wall demonstrates that the leftovers of a daily ritual can become genuine building material, closing a loop between the places where coffee grows and the cities where it is consumed.

zh-Hant.heading: 咖啡渣磚-把每日的殘渣砌成牆
zh-Hant.body: 曾在咖啡產地生活的學生，看見人們以浪板搭建房屋，於是希望找到一種環保而低成本的材料，讓營造更好。用過的咖啡渣，成為一切的起點。從在地咖啡店收集來的咖啡渣被連續曬乾數日，再與泥土和水混合，壓入模具成磚。這些磚隨後被應用於一個提案：舊金山市中心的地下咖啡社區。三個樓層分別容納追溯從咖啡豆到一杯咖啡的市集、關於咖啡產地的藝廊，以及帶有開放廣場的屋頂咖啡館。最後，大量磚塊被堆疊在實尺寸的木框中，頂端留出開口作為窗。這面牆證明，每日咖啡的殘渣，也能成為真正的建材。

pins.title: Scraps to Soil
pins.description:
A kitchen-waste bin grows into a full composting system, first as a model and then as a working machine.

Model making | Product and system design | Concrete, wood and acrylic | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從廚餘到土壤
zh-Hant.description:
一個廚餘桶發展成完整的堆肥系統，先做成模型，再做成可運轉的機器。

模型製作｜產品與系統設計｜混凝土、木材與壓克力｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began with the student's daily routine of taking out kitchen waste at home. A bin that filters out liquid waste came first, but a single object could not make a lasting impact.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品起於學生在家倒廚餘的日常。最先設計的是能濾除液體的廚餘桶，但單一物件無法帶來長久的影響。
captions: 廚餘變土壤的循環草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The idea grew into a complete system in which a wheel feeds a grinder and turns waste into soil. Sketches mapped each step from kitchen to garden.
captions: Sketch of the wheel and grinder.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 構想發展成一套完整系統：水車帶動研磨機，把廚餘變成土壤。草圖標出從廚房到花園的每一步。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A concrete and wood model placed the grinder under an orange frame among garden beds. The student also sold the bins at an Earth Day sale.
captions: The orange frame over the grinder.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以混凝土與木材製作模型，把研磨機放在花圃之間的橘色框架下。學生也在一場地球日義賣中賣出了這些廚餘桶。
captions: 研磨機上方的橘色框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A full-size machine with acrylic boards, a metal frame and a pipe nozzle system was then built. With local support, it was introduced to a village to address organic waste in rivers.
captions: A drawer of the waste bin.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生接著以壓克力板、金屬框架與管嘴系統打造出實尺寸的機器。在地方支持下，機器被引入一個村落，處理河流中的有機廢棄物。

sections.heading: Scraps to Soil - Returning Daily Waste to the Earth
sections.body: The project grew out of the student's daily routine of taking out kitchen waste at home. A bin that filters out liquid came first, yet a single object could not make a lasting difference. The idea therefore expanded into a complete system in which a wheel feeds a grinder that turns waste into soil, with sketches mapping every step from kitchen to garden. A model in concrete and wood placed the grinder beneath an orange frame among garden beds, and the bins themselves were sold at an Earth Day sale. A full-size machine followed, built with acrylic boards, a metal frame and a pipe nozzle system, and with local support it was introduced to a village to address organic waste in rivers. What began as a small household chore thus travelled outward into real ground, proving that design can move from a passing thought to a working tool that changes how a community treats what it throws away.

zh-Hant.heading: 從廚餘到土壤-讓日常的垃圾回到大地
zh-Hant.body: 作品起於學生每天在家倒廚餘的日常。最初的構想是一個能濾出液體的垃圾桶，但單一物件難以帶來長久的影響。於是，想法逐漸擴展為一套完整的系統：一個轉輪餵入粉碎機，把廚餘轉化為土壤，草圖則描繪從廚房到花園的每一個步驟。混凝土與木材構成的模型，把粉碎機置於橘色框架之下，周圍環繞花圃；學生也在世界地球日義賣中售出這些垃圾桶。其後，一部由壓克力板、金屬框架與管嘴系統構成的實尺寸機器被建造出來，並在在地支持下引入一座村莊，回應河川中的有機廢棄物問題。設計就此從一個念頭，走進了真實的土地。

pins.title: The Daya Bay Boathouse
pins.description:
A sailing base rethought as a boathouse of light wooden rods and woven joints.

Model making | Architecture | Wooden rods and cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 大亞灣船屋
zh-Hant.description:
以輕巧木桿與交織接頭，重新構想一座帆船基地的船屋。

模型製作｜建築｜木桿與紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As a sailor, the student noticed many functional shortcomings in the infrastructure of a sailing base. The project responds directly to the needs found on site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 身為帆船手，學生注意到帆船基地設施的許多功能不足。作品直接回應在現場發現的需求。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Japanese and Hakka wooden joinery became the main references. The student studied how rods interlock without heavy connectors.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 日式與客家木構接合是主要參考。學生研究木桿如何不靠厚重五金而彼此咬合。
captions: 在基地觀察的木構接合。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sketches tested trusses, roofs and openings made of thin rods. Blue gel wax, cardboard and wire mesh were combined to show water, decks and walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 草圖測試以細桿構成的桁架、屋頂與開口。藍色凝膠蠟、紙板與鐵絲網組合起來，表現水面、甲板與牆面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model shows a system of rods that emphasises lightness, exposure and structural elegance. Boats sit under the decks, ready to slide into the water.
captions: Side view of the rod frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型呈現一套強調輕盈、外露與結構美感的木桿系統。船隻停在甲板下方，隨時可以滑入水中。

sections.heading: The Daya Bay Boathouse - Lightness Woven from Slender Rods
sections.body: As a sailor, the student noticed many functional shortcomings in the infrastructure of a sailing base, and the project responds directly to the needs found on site. Japanese and Hakka timber joinery became the main references, and the student studied how slender rods can interlock without heavy connectors. Sketches went on to test trusses, roofs and openings made entirely of thin members. Blue gel wax, cardboard and wire mesh were then combined to represent water, decks and walls. The finished model presents a system of rods that celebrates lightness, exposure and structural elegance, with boats resting beneath the decks, ready to slide into the water. Observation drawn from everyday practice is transformed into a waterfront building that is at once practical and refined, where the logic of craft traditions meets the rhythm of tides and the daily routine of those who sail.

zh-Hant.heading: 大亞灣船屋-以細桿編出輕盈的結構
zh-Hant.body: 作為帆船手，學生察覺帆船基地的設施存在許多功能上的不足，這個作品便直接回應現場所發現的需求。日式與客家的木構榫接成為主要參考，學生研究細桿如何在不依賴笨重接件的情況下彼此咬合。草圖接著測試由細桿構成的桁架、屋頂與開口；藍色凝膠蠟、紙板與鐵絲網被組合起來，分別表現水面、甲板與牆體。完成的模型呈現一套強調輕盈、外露與結構優雅的桿件系統，船隻停放在甲板之下，隨時準備滑入水中。來自日常的觀察，就此轉化為一座既實用又精巧的水岸建築。

pins.title: Hometown Memory
pins.description:
A section model of a traditional Hakka home, with 3D-printed roof tiles and hand-built joinery.

Model making | Vernacular architecture | Wood, cement and resin | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 故鄉記憶
zh-Hant.description:
一座傳統客家民居的剖面模型，結合3D列印屋瓦與手作木構接合。

模型製作｜傳統建築｜木材、水泥與樹脂｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The section model of the home.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Returning to the father's hometown, the student saw the mudbrick walls and green tiles of an old family house. Traditional Hakka building is fading with urbanisation, and the project sets out to study and record it.
captions: Perspective sketch of the roof frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 回到父親的故鄉，學生看見老家的泥磚牆與青瓦。客家傳統建築正隨著都市化逐漸消失，作品因此著手研究並記錄它。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Mortise and tenon joints from the ancestral home were photographed and studied closely. The student also researched how semi-cylindrical pan and cover tiles overlap in rows.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拍攝並仔細研究祖屋的榫卯接合。學生也研究半圓筒形的板瓦與筒瓦如何成排交疊。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Tile panels were modelled in Rhino, 3D printed at home and layered like the real roof. The base was cast in concrete after dirt proved too weak to support the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 屋瓦板在Rhino中建模，在家以3D列印製作，並像真實屋頂般層疊。由於泥土不足以支撐模型，底座改以混凝土澆鑄。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The section cut reveals the techniques used inside the home. Layered bricks in the courtyard show the flooring traditionally used in Hakka houses.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 剖切面揭示民居內部使用的工法。庭院中層疊的磚塊呈現客家民居傳統的地坪做法。

sections.heading: Hometown Memory - Cutting Open an Old Hakka House
sections.body: Returning to the family's ancestral hometown, the student saw the mudbrick walls and green tiles of an old house. Traditional Hakka building is fading with urbanisation, and the project took on the task of studying and recording it. Mortise-and-tenon joints in the ancestral home were photographed and examined closely, and the way semi-cylindrical pan and cover tiles overlap in rows became a subject of research in its own right. With that understanding in hand, tile panels were modelled in Rhino, 3D printed at home and layered just like the real roof. When dirt proved too weak to carry the model, the base was cast in concrete instead. The section cut reveals the techniques hidden inside the house, while layered bricks in the courtyard show the flooring traditionally used in Hakka homes. A model thus becomes a careful, affectionate act of preservation, keeping a family memory and a vanishing craft legible for those who come after.

zh-Hant.heading: 故鄉記憶-剖開一座客家老屋
zh-Hant.body: 回到父親的故鄉，學生看見老家土磚牆與青瓦的身影。傳統客家建築正隨都市化逐漸消逝，這個作品因此以研究與記錄為志業。祖厝中的榫卯接點被拍攝並仔細研究；半圓筒形的板瓦與筒瓦如何成排交疊，也成為探究的對象。在理解之後，瓦片面板以Rhino建模，在家中以3D列印製作，並如真實屋頂般層層鋪疊；當泥土被證明不足以承托模型，底座改以混凝土澆鑄。剖面切開之處，揭示屋內所運用的工法；中庭裡層疊的磚，則呈現客家民居傳統的鋪地方式。一座模型，就此成為對一段家族記憶溫柔而嚴謹的保存。

zh-Hant.title: 幽靈漁網
zh-Hant.description:
以水槽模型與潮汐實驗，呈現污染物如何聚集在海中的人造結構周圍。

模型製作｜環境研究｜木條、沙與壓克力｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As a sailing coach, the student saw abandoned fishing nets tangled with wood, plastic and dead fish. Artificial structures often trap this waste in tidal areas and harm local ecosystems.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 身為帆船教練，學生看見廢棄漁網與木頭、塑膠和死魚纏在一起。人造結構常在潮間帶困住這些垃圾，傷害在地生態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two tanks compared a shoreline with pillars against a natural one at low, normal and high tide. Debris stayed trapped around the pillars but washed away along the natural coast.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 兩個水槽在低潮、平潮與高潮下，比較有樁柱的海岸與自然海岸。垃圾困在樁柱周圍，在自然海岸則被沖散。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The results led to a tall model that layers plastic, fishing line, hooks and structures. Each pollutant was placed where it would gather in the sea.
captions: A wire cage on the seabed.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 實驗結果引出一座高聳的模型，層疊塑膠、釣魚線、魚鉤與結構。每種污染物都被放在海中會聚集的位置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model shows how pollutants intertwine and make marine contamination more complex. It makes the impact of human activity on the ocean visible at a glance.
captions: Stones and plants on the seabed.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型呈現污染物如何交織，讓海洋污染變得更複雜。它讓人類活動對海洋的影響一目了然。

sections.heading: The Ghost Net - Letting the Tide Reveal Trapped Pollution
sections.body: While coaching sailing, the student found abandoned fishing nets tangled with wood, plastic and dead fish, and noticed that artificial structures often trap such waste in tidal zones, harming local ecosystems. To test this, the inquiry turned experimental. Two tanks simulated a shoreline with pillars and a natural coast, compared at low, normal and high tide. The result was clear: debris lingered around the pillars but washed away along the natural shore. These findings shaped a tall model that layers plastic, fishing line, hooks and structures, with each pollutant placed where it would actually gather in the sea. The model shows how pollutants intertwine and make marine contamination ever more complex, and it lets the impact of human activity on the ocean be grasped at a glance. Evidence gathered in a tank becomes an image in space, turning observation into argument and argument into something both haunting and quietly precise.

zh-Hant.heading: 幽靈網-讓潮水揭露被困住的污染
zh-Hant.body: 擔任帆船教練時，學生看見被遺棄的漁網纏著木頭、塑膠與死魚；人造結構常在潮間帶困住這些垃圾，傷害當地生態。為了證明這一點，研究以實驗展開：兩座水槽分別模擬有樁柱的海岸與自然海岸，在低潮、正常與高潮之間比較。結果清楚呈現，碎屑在樁柱周圍滯留不去，在自然海岸則被沖走。這些發現引導出一座高聳的模型，層層疊合塑膠、釣線、魚鉤與結構，每一種污染物都被放在它在海中會聚集的位置。模型呈現污染如何彼此纏繞，使海洋污染更加複雜，也讓人類活動對海洋的衝擊一眼可見。

pins.title: Daya Bay Eco-model

zh-Hant.title: 大亞灣生態模型
zh-Hant.description:
以樹脂、貝殼與在地海灘的珊瑚碎片，呈現擁擠的海岸如何傷害海洋。

模型製作｜環境設計｜樹脂、貝殼與珊瑚｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Active in the bay, the student saw the local coral ecosystem decline at first hand. Oil and fertiliser spills have harmed the coral and the animals that depend on it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生長期在海灣活動，親眼看見在地珊瑚生態衰退。油污與肥料外洩傷害了珊瑚以及依賴它的生物。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Coral skeletons and shells washed up on a local beach were collected as materials. Their meaning was compared with AB resin as an artificial material.
captions: The resin block from an angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集沖上在地海灘的珊瑚骨骼與貝殼作為材料。學生把它們的意義與作為人工材料的AB膠對照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Shells and fragments were layered in resin, with 3D-printed buildings packed along the shore. Pebbles and clay shaped the edge between city and sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 貝殼與碎片層層封入樹脂，3D列印的建築密集排列在岸邊。卵石與黏土塑造出城市與海之間的邊界。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model shows how rapid urbanisation leads to algae blooms and oil pollution. It is a visual example of how the ocean has been harmed.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型呈現快速都市化如何導致藻華與油污。它直觀呈現海洋受到的傷害。

sections.heading: Daya Bay Eco-model - A Shoreline Sealed in Resin
sections.body: Active in the bay, the student saw the decline of the local coral ecosystem at first hand, as oil and fertiliser spills harmed the coral and the creatures that depend on it. The work began on the beach. Coral skeletons and shells washed ashore were gathered as materials and set against AB resin, an artificial substance, so that the meaning each carries could be weighed. Building on this, shells and fragments were layered within resin while 3D-printed buildings crowded along the shore, and pebbles and clay shaped the edge between city and sea. The finished model shows how rapid urbanisation leads to algae blooms and oil pollution, offering a visual testimony of how the ocean has been wounded. Natural remains and synthetic clarity meet in a single cross-section, speaking to each other in silence, and the beauty of the object makes its warning all the harder to ignore.

zh-Hant.heading: 大亞灣生態模型-封存在樹脂裡的海岸
zh-Hant.body: 常在海灣活動的學生，親眼看見當地珊瑚生態的衰退；油污與肥料外洩，傷害了珊瑚與依賴它的生物。作品從海灘開始：被沖上岸的珊瑚骨骼與貝殼被一一拾起，成為材料，並與AB樹脂這種人造物質並置比較，思考兩者各自承載的意義。在此之上，貝殼與碎片被層層封存於樹脂之中，3D列印的建築沿著海岸密集排列；卵石與陶土則塑造出城市與海之間的邊界。完成的模型呈現快速都市化如何引發藻華與油污，成為一則關於海洋如何受傷的視覺見證。自然的殘骸與人造的透明，在同一個切面裡無聲對話。

pins.title: Algorithmic Modelling: Artificial Coral Reefs
pins.description:
Coral forms generated by script and 3D printed as shelters for fish and marine life.

Parametric design | 3D printing | Marine ecology | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 演算法建模：人工珊瑚礁
zh-Hant.description:
以腳本生成珊瑚形態並3D列印，作為魚類與海洋生物的庇護所。

參數化設計｜3D列印｜海洋生態｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As a local sailor, the student watched coral reefs degrade after an oil leak. Global warming and industry keep shrinking reefs around the world.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 身為在地帆船手，學生目睹珊瑚礁在一次油污外洩後退化。全球暖化與工業活動也持續讓世界各地的珊瑚礁縮小。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Artificial coral ecosystems that protect fish like real reefs became the chosen solution. A parametric script generated porous forms inspired by coral species.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇以能像真實珊瑚礁般保護魚類的人工珊瑚生態系作為解方。參數化腳本生成受珊瑚物種啟發的多孔形態。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Print tests compared density and pore size. The pattern was then turned into modules that could be stacked.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 列印測試比較密度與孔洞大小。圖樣接著被轉化為可堆疊的模組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A 3D-printed tower shows the final reef form. Concept views imagine fish and coral living inside it.
captions: Concept view of fish in the reef.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 3D列印的塔呈現最終的礁體形態。概念圖想像魚群與珊瑚在其中生長。
captions: 魚群在礁體中的概念圖。

sections.heading: Algorithmic Modelling Artificial Coral Reef - Scripting a New Home for Fish
sections.body: A local sailor, the student watched coral reefs degrade after an oil leak, while global warming and industry continue to shrink reefs across the world. Facing this loss, the project chose a direction: artificial coral ecosystems that could shelter fish the way living reefs do. A parametric script, drawing on several coral species, generated porous forms, and print tests compared density and pore size to find the structure most hospitable to life. The resulting pattern was then translated into modules that can be stacked, allowing the reef to expand piece by piece. A 3D-printed tower presents the final reef form, and concept views imagine fish and coral living together within it. Here the algorithm is more than a drawing aid; it becomes a language of repair, a way of writing new shelter into damaged water, and a reminder that careful computation can serve something as fragile and essential as a reef.

zh-Hant.heading: 演算模型人工珊瑚礁-為魚群寫下新的家
zh-Hant.body: 身為在地的帆船手，學生親眼目睹一次漏油之後，珊瑚礁逐漸退化；全球暖化與工業發展，也讓世界各地的礁岩持續縮減。面對這樣的流失，作品選擇了一個方向：打造能像真實珊瑚般庇護魚群的人工生態系。參數化腳本以不同珊瑚物種為靈感，生成多孔的形體；列印測試則比較密度與孔徑的差異，尋找最適合生命棲居的結構。圖樣隨後被轉化為可以堆疊的模組，讓礁體得以逐步擴張。一座3D列印的塔，呈現最終的礁體形態；概念圖則想像魚與珊瑚在其中共生。演算法在此不只是工具，而成為一種修復海洋的語言。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project was made in a summer design studio and starts from the idea that patterns shape how we see the world. The question was how patterns could connect with the way people move through a space.
captions: Photo frames of the swinging movement over the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品完成於一個暑期設計工作營，起點是圖樣影響我們觀看世界的方式。題目在問，圖樣如何與人在空間中的移動連結。
captions: 擺盪動作的連續照片與模型疊合。
從藝術作品得出的圖樣研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Parts of a pattern in an artwork were marked and extruded into 3D. A sketch model was built both in Rhino and with physical materials.
captions: A second view of the digital model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在一件藝術作品的圖樣中標出局部並擠出為立體。草模同時在Rhino與實體材料中製作。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: An unconventional movement, swinging on monkey bars, was analysed frame by frame. Parts of the frames were removed so the model could follow the swing.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生逐格分析一個不尋常的動作：擺盪單槓。框架被局部移除，讓模型能跟隨擺盪。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model completes the swinging motion while keeping the look of the first pattern. It shows architecture as the design of human interaction with a set environment.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型完成擺盪的動作，同時保有最初圖樣的樣貌。它呈現建築作為人與既定環境互動的設計。

sections.heading: Summer Studio Movement Model - When a Swing Becomes Architecture
sections.body: Also made in a summer design studio, this project began from the idea that patterns shape the way we see the world, and asked how patterns might connect with the way people move through space. Parts of a pattern in an artwork were marked and extruded into three dimensions, and a sketch model was built both in Rhino and with physical materials. Then came an unconventional movement: swinging on monkey bars. The motion was analysed frame by frame, and some frames were deliberately removed so that the model could follow the arc of the swing. The final model completes the swinging gesture while still keeping the character of the original pattern. In doing so it reveals architecture as the design of how people interact with a given environment, rather than simply a still container. A playground habit, observed closely enough, turns into a lesson about rhythm, suspension and the way a body traces its own invisible geometry through the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 夏季工作營動態模型-讓擺盪成為建築
zh-Hant.body: 同樣出自夏季設計工作營，這個作品始於一個想法：圖樣形塑我們看待世界的方式。問題隨之而來：圖樣如何與人們穿越空間的方式相連？學生從一件藝術作品中標記出部分圖樣，向上擠出為立體，並同時以Rhino與實體材料建構草模。接著登場的，是一種非常規的動作：在單槓上擺盪。這個動作被逐格分析，部分格幀被刻意移除，使模型能夠追隨擺盪的軌跡。最終的模型完整呈現擺盪的動態，同時保留最初圖樣的樣貌。它讓人看見，建築也可以是對人在既定環境中如何互動的設計，而非只是一個靜止的容器。

zh-Hant.body: 學生以一個摺紙先例為起點，摺出對稱的紙模型。學生並測試每道摺痕如何讓光穿透。

captions: A paper model of the shell.

sections.heading: Summer Studio Folded Paper Pavilion - Sifting Light Through Folds
sections.body: This work was born in a summer design studio devoted to light in architecture. The site needed shade for the students and teachers moving in and out of a building, a place to pause for a moment. Beginning with an origami precedent, the student folded series of symmetrical paper models and examined each crease for the way it lets light pass through. The lightness of paper became a tool for thinking about light itself. Those folds were then rebuilt as paper shells and translated into a Rhino model, where openings were cut with care so that natural light would fall into the space below. The finished timber pavilion creates a social setting where people can feel at ease, and renders place it among the courtyard's columns and brick walls. A single folded sheet thus unfolds into a canopy of light and shadow, a shelter where the simple gesture of a crease becomes the measure of how a day is lived.

zh-Hant.heading: 夏季工作營摺紙涼亭-以摺痕篩落光線
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品誕生於一個夏季設計工作營，主題是建築中的光。基地需要一片遮蔭，讓進出建築的學生與老師得以稍作停歇。以一件摺紙先例為起點，學生摺出一組組對稱的紙模型，逐一檢驗每道摺痕如何讓光穿透。紙的輕盈，於是成為思考光的工具。這些摺痕隨後被重建為紙殼，再轉化為Rhino模型；開口被精準切出，讓自然光落入下方的空間。最終的木構涼亭，營造出一處令人自在的社交場所，渲染圖將它置於中庭的柱列與紅磚牆之間。一張紙的摺疊，就此延展為一片可以棲身的光影。
