模型製作｜都市設計｜3D列印與雷射切割｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The street was a passage between the back walls of large buildings, with few shops and little sunlight. People walked through it, but few chose to stay.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這條街夾在大型建築的背面之間，商店稀少，日照不足。人們只是穿過，很少有人願意停留。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied elevated parks and stepped pocket gardens as ways to layer a street. Sketches tested where people could pause, sit and find sunlight.
captions: Render of the stairs and planters.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究高架公園與階梯式口袋花園，作為讓街道分層的方法。草圖測試人們可以在哪裡停留、坐下並曬到太陽。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The ground level gained wider sidewalks, planted edges and street furniture, while cars moved to a driveway below. AI renders helped picture the mood of each layer.
captions: Sketch of the new ground level.
AI render of the driveway entrance.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 地面層加寬人行道、加入植栽邊帶與街道家具，車輛則移到下方車道。AI渲染圖幫助想像每一層的氛圍。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model was made with 3D printing and laser cutting at a length of 900 mm. A white walkway zigzags above the street and links its two ends.
captions: Stairs and a tree on the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以3D列印與雷射切割製成，長900毫米。白色步道在街道上方曲折延伸，連接街道兩端。

sections.heading: The Layered Street - Turning a Passage into a Place to Stay
sections.body: The street ran between the back walls of large buildings, with few shops and little sunlight; people walked through it, but few chose to stay. Turning a passage back into a true street was the task at hand. Research began with elevated parks and stepped pocket gardens as ways of layering a street, while sketches tested where people might pause, sit and find the sun. The ground level then gained wider sidewalks, planted edges and street furniture, and cars were moved to a driveway below. AI renders helped picture the mood of each layer before anything was fixed. The final model, made through 3D printing and laser cutting, stretches to 900 mm, and a white walkway zigzags above the street to link its two ends. What had been a cold gap between buildings grows into a sequence of levels where lingering becomes natural, and the simple act of crossing turns into an invitation to remain a little longer.

zh-Hant.heading: 層疊街道-讓穿行之路成為停留之處
zh-Hant.body: 這條街夾在大型建築的背牆之間，店鋪稀少，陽光難以照入；人們穿行而過，卻少有人願意停留。如何讓一條通道重新成為街道，是學生面對的課題。研究從高架公園與階梯式口袋花園展開，探討如何讓街道分層；草圖則測試人們可以在哪裡停頓、坐下、找到陽光。地面層隨之拓寬人行道，加入植栽邊緣與街道家具，車輛則移至下方的車道；AI渲染幫助想像每一層的氛圍。最終模型以3D列印與雷射切割製成，長達九百毫米，一道白色步道在街道上方曲折前行，串起兩端。原本冷清的縫隙，由此長出可以駐足的層次。

pins.title: The Gaze Chamber
pins.description:

zh-Hant.title: 凝視之室
zh-Hant.description:
一座廳室與一座漂浮舞台，把繁忙的城市廣場變成看與被看的場所。

模型製作｜公共空間設計｜3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The plaza sits between transit, theatres and civic buildings, yet people mostly pass through it. The project asks how it could hold markets, shows and everyday meetings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座廣場位於交通、劇院與市政建築之間，人們卻大多只是路過。作品探問它如何容納市集、演出與日常相遇。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how vision and power are linked, and how sightlines can divide a space. Red lines in the plans extend the gaze between the chamber and the stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究視線與權力的關係，以及視線如何劃分空間。平面圖中的紅線延伸了廳室與舞台之間的凝視。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chamber was carved into the plaza as a broken but continuous sequence of arches. Pauses, turns and framed views slow people down as they move through.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 廳室以一連串斷開卻連續的拱形嵌入廣場。停頓、轉折與框景讓穿越的人放慢腳步。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A stage floats over a shallow pool and works as seating, a platform or a backdrop. The design does not try to be a landmark, but a frame where different people meet.
captions: Render of the chamber and stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 舞台漂浮在淺水池上，可作為座位、平台或布景。設計不求成為地標，而是成為不同人群相遇的框架。

sections.heading: The Gaze Chamber - Turning a Passing Plaza into a Place of Meeting
sections.body: The plaza sits between transit, theatres and civic buildings, yet most people simply pass through it, and the project asks how it might hold markets, performances and everyday encounters. Thinking began with sightlines. The student studied how looking and power are entangled and how lines of sight can divide a space, and red lines in the plans carry the gaze from the chamber out to the stage. The chamber itself was carved into the plaza as a broken yet continuous sequence of arches, where pauses, turns and framed views slow people down as they move. A stage floats over a shallow pool and can serve as seating, a platform or a backdrop. Rather than reaching for the status of a landmark, the design accepts a humbler role as a frame, a setting in which different people can meet, linger and see one another, and in which the act of looking becomes shared rather than one-sided.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝視之室-讓穿越的廣場成為相遇之地
zh-Hant.body: 這座廣場位於交通、劇院與市政建築之間，人們卻大多只是匆匆穿越。作品追問：它如何容納市集、演出與日常的相遇？思考的起點是視線。學生研究觀看與權力如何彼此牽連，視線又如何分割空間；平面圖中的紅線，把凝視從室內延伸到舞台。凝視之室被刻入廣場之中，成為一串斷裂卻連續的拱圈；停頓、轉折與被框住的景致，讓行經的人放慢腳步。一座舞台漂浮在淺池之上，可以是座椅、平台或背景。這個設計無意成為地標，而是甘願成為一個框架，讓不同的人在此相遇、駐足與彼此看見。

pins.title: House of Lines and Colour
pins.description:
Grid paintings are traced and turned into the planes, voids and colours of a house.

Model making | Architecture | Foam board, acrylic and laser cutting | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 線與色之屋
zh-Hant.description:
臨摹格狀繪畫，並把它們轉化為一棟房屋的平面、虛空與色彩。

模型製作｜建築｜泡棉板、壓克力與雷射切割｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to grid paintings with layered depth and shifting lines and colours. The question was how such a flat composition could become a house.
captions: The grid paintings that were traced for the house.
Traced drafts of lines and points.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被層次豐富、線條與色彩不斷位移的格狀繪畫吸引。問題是如此平面的構圖如何成為一棟房屋。
captions: 學生臨摹、作為房屋依據的格狀繪畫。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The paintings were traced to pull out proportions, solids and voids, lines and flows. These drafts became plans and sections of a house.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生臨摹這些畫作，萃取比例、實與虛、線條與流動。這些草稿成為房屋的平面與剖面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Clear and coloured acrylic, perforated metal mesh, laser-cut wood and 3D-printed parts were layered. Each part was cut and assembled following CAD models.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生層疊透明與彩色壓克力、沖孔金屬網、雷射切割木材與3D列印零件。每個零件都依照CAD模型切割並組裝。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The house reads as a reinterpreted painting in three dimensions. Windows, slats and coloured panels shift as the viewer walks around it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這棟房屋就像一幅被立體重新詮釋的畫作。觀者繞行時，窗、條板與彩色面板隨之變化。

sections.heading: House of Lines and Colour - Walking into a Painting in Three Dimensions
sections.body: Grid paintings with layered depth and shifting lines and colours captured the student's attention, raising a question: could such a flat composition become a house? Translation began with tracing. Following the paintings closely, the student drew out their proportions, solids and voids, lines and flows, and these drafts gradually developed into plans and sections of a dwelling. Materials were then layered one upon another: clear and coloured acrylic, perforated metal mesh, laser-cut wood and 3D-printed parts, each cut and assembled according to CAD models. The finished house reads as a painting reinterpreted in three dimensions. As the viewer walks around it, windows, slats and coloured panels slide past one another and recombine, so that an image once fixed on a canvas begins to move again with every step, its rhythm now measured not by the eye alone but by the body travelling through space.

zh-Hant.heading: 線與色之屋-走進一幅立體的畫
zh-Hant.body: 格狀繪畫中層疊的深度與游移的線條、色彩，深深吸引著學生。問題隨之而來：如此平面的構圖，能否成為一棟房子？轉譯從描摹開始。學生沿著畫作抽取比例、實與虛、線條與流動，再讓這些草稿逐步發展為住宅的平面與剖面。材料隨後層層疊合：透明與彩色壓克力、穿孔金屬網、雷射切割木材與3D列印零件，每一個部件都依循CAD模型切割與組裝。最終的房子，讀起來像一幅被重新詮釋的立體畫作。當觀者繞行其間，窗、條板與彩色面板不斷位移、重組，讓一張靜止的畫，在行走之中重新流動起來。

pins.title: Lunar Nexus

zh-Hant.title: 月球樞紐
zh-Hant.description:
一座位於月球坑洞內的棲地，有玻璃穹頂、發光高塔與六個地下艙。

模型製作｜思辨建築｜水泥、壓克力與3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Lunar craters and underground caves could shelter people from extreme heat, cold and radiation. The project imagines a self-sufficient base built from what the Moon offers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 月球坑洞與地下洞穴可以讓人避開極端溫差與輻射。作品想像一座以月球自身資源建造的自給基地。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how lunar soil could make bricks, water and glass. Plan sketches linked homes, labs, energy rooms and gardens around a central core.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究月壤如何製成磚、水與玻璃。平面草圖把住宅、實驗室、能源室與花園連結在中央核心周圍。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The crater was cast in cement and fitted with six pods for living, farming, water, repair, storage and computing. Each pod was built and lit as its own small world.
captions: A pod on the crater edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 坑洞以水泥鑄造，並配置六個分別用於居住、農業、水循環、維修、儲存與運算的艙體。每個艙體都被製作並打光成一個小世界。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A glowing acrylic tower rises from the crater under a faceted glass dome. The model shows how a community could live and grow in a hostile place.
captions: The tower against the crater wall.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 發光的壓克力高塔在多面玻璃穹頂下自坑洞升起。模型呈現一個社群如何在嚴酷之地生活與成長。

sections.heading: Lunar Nexus - A Settlement Lit Within a Crater
sections.body: Lunar craters and underground caves might shelter people from extreme heat, cold and radiation, and the project imagines a self-sufficient base built from what the Moon itself can offer. Working from that premise, the student studied how lunar soil could be turned into bricks, water and glass, while plan sketches linked homes, laboratories, energy rooms and gardens around a central core. The crater was cast in cement and fitted with six pods, one each for living, farming, water, repair, storage and computing. Every pod was built and lit on its own, like a small world with its own inner life. From the centre a glowing acrylic tower rises beneath a faceted glass dome. The model sketches a possibility as much as a building: that even in the harshest place, a community could find a way to live, work and grow, its light held carefully against the surrounding dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 月球樞紐-在隕石坑中點亮的聚落
zh-Hant.body: 月球的隕石坑與地下洞穴，或許能讓人免於極端的冷熱與輻射。這個作品想像一座自給自足的基地，以月球本身所能提供的資源建造而成。在這個前提下，學生研究月壤如何製成磚、水與玻璃；平面草圖則把住所、實驗室、能源室與花園，環繞中央核心串連起來。隕石坑以水泥澆鑄，嵌入六個艙體，分別承擔居住、耕作、供水、維修、儲存與運算；每個艙體都被獨立製作並點亮，如同一個個小世界。一座發光的壓克力塔自坑中升起，覆以多面的玻璃穹頂。模型因此描繪出一種可能：即使在嚴酷之地，一個社群仍能生活、成長。

pins.title: Auspicious Clouds

Model making | Architecture | 3D print | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 祥雲
zh-Hant.description:
傳統祥雲紋樣發展成一座高聳、摺疊的光與虛空之塔。

模型製作｜建築｜3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cloud patterns carry hopes of rising, harmony and shared memory, and they appear on screens and windows. The student remembered carved screens and paper-cut windows at a grandmother's house.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 祥雲紋樣承載著步步高升、和諧與共同記憶的寓意，常見於屏風與窗花。學生想起外婆家的雕花屏風與剪紙窗花。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Digital studies turned flat cloud curls into stacked walls and voids. Each version tested how light and shadow pass between them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 數位研究把平面的雲紋捲曲轉化為堆疊的牆與虛空。每個版本都測試光影如何在其間穿行。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The forms were drawn and printed as thin, folded shells that open and close. Small figures show the scale of the spaces inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把形體繪製並列印成可開可合的薄摺殼。小人模型標示出內部空間的尺度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower looks like clouds drifting overhead and forms small sanctuaries of light. Each visitor finds a personal view, while the whole stays one continuous memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 塔體宛如飄過頭頂的雲，形成一處處光的小聖所。每位訪客都能找到自己的視角，而整體仍是一段連續的記憶。

sections.heading: Auspicious Clouds - Remembered Cloud Patterns Stacked into a Tower
sections.body: Cloud patterns carry wishes for rising, harmony and shared memory, and they often appear on screens and windows. The student remembered the carved screens and paper-cut windows in a grandmother's house, and that memory became the gentle starting point of the work. Digital studies turned flat cloud curls into stacked walls and voids, with each version testing how light and shadow might pass between them. The forms were then drawn and printed as thin, folded shells that open and close, while small figures mark the scale of the spaces inside. The finished tower resembles clouds drifting overhead and gathers small sanctuaries of light within its folds. Every visitor can find a personal view, yet the whole remains one continuous memory. A traditional motif is thus allowed to breathe again through contemporary tools, carrying something of a childhood home into a structure that belongs to the present.

zh-Hant.heading: 祥雲-把記憶中的雲紋堆成高塔
zh-Hant.body: 雲紋承載著升騰、和諧與共同記憶的祝願，常見於屏風與窗花之上。學生記起外婆家裡那些雕花屏風與剪紙窗。這份記憶，成為作品溫柔的起點。數位研究把平面的雲卷轉化為層層堆疊的牆與空隙，每一個版本都在測試光與影如何在其間穿行。形體隨後被繪製並列印為薄而摺疊的殼，時開時合；小小的人形標示出內部空間的尺度。完成的塔宛如頭頂飄過的雲，圍塑出一處處光的小聖所。每位來訪者都能找到屬於自己的視角，而整體仍是一段連續不斷的記憶，讓傳統的紋樣在當代的工具裡重新呼吸。

pins.title: Traversing the Fifth Dimension
pins.description:
A film scene of an endless bookshelf in time becomes a grid of wooden sticks and mirrors.

Model making | Spatial design | Wooden sticks and mirrors | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 穿越第五維度
zh-Hant.description:
一個時間中無盡書架的電影場景，化為木條與鏡子構成的格網。

模型製作｜空間設計｜木條與鏡子｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In a science-fiction film, a space outside time lets a traveller look into a room at many moments. The student chose this bookshelf scene for its rich spatial quality.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在一部科幻電影中，一個時間之外的空間讓旅人能在許多時刻窺看同一個房間。學生因這個書架場景豐富的空間感而選擇它。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Scenes were sketched and then reduced to points, lines and planes. The grid became a way to show past, present and future at once.
captions: Lines and planes from the scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先速寫場景，再把它簡化為點、線與面。格網成為同時呈現過去、現在與未來的方法。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were glued into a regular frame, with each crossing marking a moment. Small figures were placed to show a parent and child across dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把木條黏成規則的框架，每個交點代表一個時刻。小人物被放在不同維度中，代表一對親子。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Mirrors repeat the grid endlessly, and threads hint at the pull of gravity. The centre of the maze stands for the point where space and time begin and end.
captions: Drawing of a figure in the grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鏡子讓格網無限重複，細線暗示重力的牽引。迷宮的中心象徵時空的起點與終點。

sections.heading: Traversing the Fifth Dimension - Time Woven into a Grid
sections.body: In a science-fiction film, a space outside time lets a traveller look into one room at many different moments, and the student chose this bookshelf scene for its rich spatial quality. Scenes were sketched and then pared down to points, lines and planes, and through that reduction the grid became a way to show past, present and future at once. Wooden sticks were glued into a regular frame in which every crossing marks a moment, and small figures were placed within it to suggest a parent and child reaching toward each other across dimensions. Mirrors repeat the grid without end, while threads hint at the pull of gravity. At the heart of the maze lies the point where space and time begin and end. An abstract idea from physics is thus translated into a structure that can be held in the gaze, and a bond that stretches across time is given a form one can walk around and slowly read.

zh-Hant.heading: 穿越第五維度-時間被編成格網
zh-Hant.body: 一部科幻電影裡，有一個時間之外的空間，讓旅人得以望進同一個房間的許多時刻。學生被這場書架場景豐富的空間質感所吸引，選擇以它為題。場景先被草繪，再被簡化為點、線與面；格網由此成為同時呈現過去、現在與未來的方法。木棒被黏合成規則的框架，每一個交點都標記一個時刻，小小的人形則被安放其間，暗示一對親子跨越維度的相望。鏡面讓格網無盡重複，絲線隱約透露重力的牽引。迷宮的中心，象徵時間與空間的起點與終點。在這裡，抽象的物理想像被轉譯為可以凝視的結構，也讓一份跨越時空的牽掛有了形狀。

pins.title: Infinite Loop: Memory Paths
pins.description:
Looping paper stairs inside a wooden frame show branching choices held in one structure.

Model making | Spatial design | PVC board and wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無限迴圈：記憶路徑
zh-Hant.description:
木框中迴繞的紙階梯，呈現收束在同一結構中的分岔選擇。

模型製作｜空間設計｜PVC板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to stories where different choices unfold as parallel paths. Each stair in the model stands for a possible memory or decision.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生著迷於不同選擇展開成平行路徑的故事。模型中的每段階梯都代表一段可能的記憶或抉擇。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A stair unit was designed and repeated to test how paths can branch and loop. Stacked units began to form a tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生設計一個階梯單元並重複使用，測試路徑如何分岔與迴繞。堆疊的單元逐漸形成一座塔。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A wooden frame was built first, and the looping stairs were attached to it. The frame stands for one self, while the stairs inside show unstable paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先搭建木框，再把迴繞的階梯固定上去。木框代表一個完整的自我，內部階梯則呈現不穩定的路徑。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Stairs grow outward step by step like branching storylines. However far the paths go, they stay inside one frame, a picture of freedom within limits.
captions: The final model from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 階梯一步步向外生長，宛如分岔的故事線。無論路徑延伸多遠，都仍在同一框架內，象徵限制中的自由。

sections.heading: Infinite Loop - A Stair Tower of Branching Memories
sections.body: Stories in which different choices unfold as parallel paths had long drawn the student in, and in this model every stair stands for a possible memory or decision. The design grew from a single unit. A stair module was repeated to test how paths can branch and loop, and as the units stacked, a tower quietly took shape. In construction, a wooden frame was raised first and the looping stairs were then attached to it one by one. The frame stands for a single self, while the stairs within it trace unstable, wandering routes. Step by step they grow outward like branching storylines, yet however far they travel, they never leave the frame that holds them. The tower thus becomes an image of freedom within limits, a reminder that even inside fixed boundaries there remain countless ways to climb, turn back and begin again, each path as real as the one actually taken.

zh-Hant.heading: 無限迴圈-記憶岔路的階梯之塔
zh-Hant.body: 不同的選擇如何展開為平行的道路，一直吸引著學生。在這件模型裡，每一道階梯都代表一段可能的記憶或一個決定。設計從一個單元開始：階梯單元被重複排列，測試路徑如何分岔、如何迴繞；當單元逐漸堆疊，一座塔便悄然成形。建造時，木框架先被立起，迴旋的階梯再一一附著其上。框架象徵一個自我，內部的階梯則呈現那些不穩定的路徑。階梯一步步向外生長，宛如不斷分岔的故事線；然而，無論走得多遠，它們始終留在同一個框架之內。這座塔因此成為一幅關於自由的圖像：在限制之中，仍有無數條路可以選擇。

pins.title: Living Cavities: Symbiotic Habitat
pins.description:
Coral skeletons and neural networks inspire a porous habitat of linked living spaces.

Digital modelling | Speculative architecture | Rhino and 3D print | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生命孔洞：共生棲地
zh-Hant.description:
珊瑚骨骼與神經網絡啟發一座由相連生活空間構成的多孔棲地。

數位建模｜思辨建築｜Rhino與3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Coral skeletons lose their link to the outside world, and the student saw them as frames for new life. Neural networks added the idea of connected flows.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 珊瑚骨骼失去了與外界的連結，學生把它們視為新生命的框架。神經網絡則帶來相互連結流動的概念。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Random points in a cube were turned into cells and then into a branching network. Contour lines cut the form into floor plates.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在立方體中產生隨機點，轉成細胞，再轉成分枝網絡。等高線把形體切出樓板。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A sectional cut showed each cavity as a node for living, working or gathering. Studies marked which voids could hold rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 剖切面把每個孔洞呈現為居住、工作或聚會的節點。研究圖標出哪些虛空可以容納房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The porous habitat joins private rooms and public space in one network. It suggests a way for people and the environment to live together.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 多孔棲地把私人房間與公共空間結合在同一個網絡中。它提出人與環境共存的一種方式。

sections.heading: Living Cavities - A Coral Network for Symbiotic Habitat
sections.body: Coral skeletons, once cut off from the world outside, appeared to the student as frames ready to carry new life, while neural networks added the idea of connected flows. Where the two met, the project found its central image. The computational steps began with a cube. Random points inside it were turned into cells and then into a branching network, and contour lines sliced the resulting form into floor plates. A sectional cut revealed that each cavity could act as a node for living, working or gathering, and further studies marked which voids were generous enough to hold rooms. The finished porous habitat joins private rooms and public space within one continuous network. It proposes a way for people and their environment to live together, in which a building is no longer a sealed box but something closer to a reef, a structure that breathes, branches and grows around the lives it shelters.

zh-Hant.heading: 活的孔洞-共生棲地的珊瑚網絡
zh-Hant.body: 珊瑚的骨骼在失去與外界的聯繫之後，在學生眼中卻成為承載新生命的骨架；神經網絡則補上了連結與流動的概念。兩者的交會，構成了作品的核心想像。演算的步驟從一個立方體開始：其中的隨機點被轉化為細胞，再被轉化為分枝狀的網絡；等高線隨後把形體切成一層層樓板。一道剖切揭示了每一個孔洞，都能成為居住、工作或聚會的節點，研究圖則標出哪些空隙足以容納房間。最終的多孔棲地，把私人房間與公共空間連成同一張網絡，暗示一種人與環境共同生活的方式：建築不再是封閉的盒子，而是一片可以呼吸、可以生長的礁石。

pins.title: Ski Trail
pins.description:
A spiral ski training base brings slopes, simulators and viewing halls into the city all year.

Model making | Architecture | PVC board and wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 滑雪道
zh-Hant.description:
一座螺旋形滑雪訓練基地，把雪道、模擬器與觀賞廳全年帶進城市。

模型製作｜建築｜PVC板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student skis competitively and found it hard to keep training in the off season. The city has no proper place for year-round practice.
captions: Ski racing photos and diagrams of skiing technique.
Drafts of spiral and floor plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生參加滑雪競賽，發現淡季很難持續訓練。城市裡沒有適合全年練習的場所。
captions: 滑雪競賽照片與滑雪技術圖解。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drafts tested spirals and rings for slopes, rental rooms, viewing halls and changing rooms. The spiral kept every part open to view.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草稿測試以螺旋與環形安排雪道、租借室、觀賞廳與更衣室。螺旋讓每個部分都保持可見。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second model wrapped the floors in rings with an artificial slope on the roof and outer edges. Simulators inside allow technical training in any season.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二個模型以環形包覆樓層，並在屋頂與外緣設置人工雪道。內部的模擬器讓任何季節都能進行技術訓練。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Coaches and parents can watch training from many points around the base. Skiing becomes both practice and a show for the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 教練與家長可以從基地周圍許多位置觀看訓練。滑雪同時成為練習與城市的風景。

sections.heading: Ski Trail - Giving the City a Slope for Every Season
sections.body: A competitive skier, the student found it hard to keep training in the off season, and the city offered no proper place to practise all year round. That personal difficulty became the starting point of the design. Drafts moved back and forth between spirals and rings to arrange slopes, rental rooms, viewing halls and changing rooms, and the spiral emerged as the form that kept every part in view of every other. A second model went further, wrapping the floors in rings and laying an artificial slope across the roof and outer edges, while simulators inside make technical training possible in any season. Coaches and parents can watch from many points around the base, following each run as it unfolds. Skiing thus becomes more than private practice; it turns into a performance woven into the everyday life of the city, where speed and skill are seen, shared and celebrated rather than hidden away until the snow returns.

zh-Hant.heading: 滑雪步道-讓城市擁有四季的雪坡
zh-Hant.body: 身為競技滑雪選手，學生在非雪季時難以維持訓練，而城市裡也沒有一處適合全年練習的場所。這份切身的困境，成為設計的出發點。草案在螺旋與環圈之間反覆測試，安排滑道、租借室、觀賞廳與更衣室，並發現螺旋能讓每個部分都保持彼此可見。第二個模型進一步以環圈包覆樓層，在屋頂與外緣鋪設人工雪坡，內部則置入模擬器，讓技術訓練不再受季節限制。教練與家長可以從基地四周的許多角度觀看訓練。滑雪因此不只是一項私人的鍛鍊，也成為城市日常裡的一場演出，讓速度與技巧被看見、被分享。

pins.title: Cage of a Broken Friendship
pins.description:
A stage model of sticks, corroded blocks and wire tells how a friendship on a quiet island falls apart.

Model making | Stage design | Card paper and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 破碎友誼之籠
zh-Hant.description:
以木棒、侵蝕方塊與金屬線構成的舞台模型，講述寧靜島嶼上一段友誼的崩解。

模型製作｜舞台設計｜卡紙與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to turn a story about two friends who drift apart on an island into space. The model had to show isolation, rupture and a final act of revenge.
captions: The film poster that inspired the stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把一段發生在島上、兩位朋友逐漸疏遠的故事轉化為空間。模型必須呈現孤立、斷裂與最後的報復。
captions: 啟發這座舞台的電影海報。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The story was broken into six moments, from a quiet life to a last farewell by the sea. Each moment was linked to a material, such as sticks for the cage of daily life.
captions: A storyline of six scenes with film stills and sketches.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 故事被拆成六個時刻，從平靜生活到海邊的最後告別。每個時刻都對應一種材料，例如以木棒代表日常生活的牢籠。
captions: 以電影劇照與草圖構成的六幕故事線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Corroded paper blocks show a friendship worn down over time, while tangled curves show an obsession. Aluminium wire shaped like flowing water marks a sister leaving the island.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 侵蝕的紙方塊表現隨時間磨損的友誼，糾結的曲線則表現執念。像流水般的鋁線代表離開島嶼的妹妹。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Part of the model was burned on purpose, and the burn marks were kept. The final cage reads as a ruin of a relationship standing on the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型的一部分被刻意燒灼，並保留燒痕。最終的籠體就像一段關係的廢墟立在水面上。

sections.heading: Cage of a Broken Friendship - A Relationship Burning on the Water
sections.body: A story about two friends who drift apart on an island became the material the student wanted to transform, and the model had to convey isolation, rupture and a final act of revenge. The story was first broken into six moments, from a quiet life to a last farewell by the sea, and each was assigned a material, with sticks forming the cage of daily routine. As the narrative advances, corroded paper blocks speak of a friendship worn down by time, tangled curves trace an obsession, and aluminium wire shaped like flowing water marks a sister leaving the island. The decisive step was to burn part of the model on purpose and keep the scorch marks rather than hide them. Standing on the water, the finished cage reads as the ruin of a relationship, a reminder that once a fracture forms it does not disappear but becomes part of memory itself, as present in the structure as any beam or joint.

zh-Hant.heading: 破碎友誼之籠-在水面上燃燒的關係
zh-Hant.body: 一個關於島上兩位朋友漸行漸遠的故事，成為學生想要轉化的對象。模型必須呈現孤立、斷裂，以及最後的復仇。故事首先被拆為六個時刻，從平靜的生活一路走到海邊最後的告別；每個時刻都對應一種材料，例如以木棒構成日常生活的牢籠。隨著敘事推進，被侵蝕的紙塊訴說友誼如何被時間磨損，糾纏的曲線描繪執念，形如流水的鋁線則標記一位妹妹離開島嶼。最關鍵的一步，是刻意焚燒模型的一部分，並保留燒痕。最終的籠子佇立在水面上，像一段關係的廢墟，提醒觀者：裂痕一旦形成，便會成為記憶本身的一部分。

pins.title: Four Detectives in Paper
pins.description:
Four characters from a mystery game are turned into patterns and then into four paper models.

Model making | Spatial narrative | PVC board, card paper and wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 紙中的四位偵探
zh-Hant.description:
把推理遊戲中的四個角色轉化為圖案，再轉化為四座紙模型。

模型製作｜空間敘事｜PVC板、卡紙與金屬線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves story-driven role-playing games where four officers solve a series of crimes. The question was how a personality could become a space.
captions: The four detective characters from the game.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛由劇情推動的角色扮演遊戲，故事中四位警員偵辦一連串案件。問題是一種性格如何成為一個空間。
captions: 遊戲中的四位偵探角色。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Keywords were pulled from each officer's personality and behaviour, such as nervous, rigorous or talkative. These words were drawn as flat black and white patterns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從每位警員的性格與行為中萃取關鍵字，例如緊張、嚴謹或健談。這些詞被畫成黑白的平面圖案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each pattern was folded, cut and stacked into a model on a square base. Curves, slats, rings and coloured film gave each character its own spatial language.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每個圖案被摺疊、切割並堆疊成方形底座上的模型。曲線、條板、圓環與彩色薄膜賦予每個角色自己的空間語言。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Four models now retell the story through space instead of words. Seen side by side, they show how different minds work on the same case.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 四座模型以空間而非文字重述故事。並排觀看時，它們呈現不同的思維如何面對同一個案件。

sections.heading: Four Detectives in Paper - Letting Personality Grow into Space
sections.body: The student loves a story-driven role-playing game in which four officers solve a series of crimes together, and from it came a question: could a personality become a space? The process began with language. Keywords were drawn from each officer's character and behaviour, such as nervous, rigorous or talkative, and then rendered as flat black-and-white patterns, giving abstract traits a visible shape before anything was built. Those patterns were next folded, cut and stacked into models on square bases, where curves, slats, rings and coloured film lent every character a spatial vocabulary of its own. Placed side by side, the four models retell the story through space instead of words. The viewer can see how different minds approach the same case in strikingly different ways, one tightly ordered, another restless, another open and generous, so that the game's narrative survives not as plot but as atmosphere, texture and the quiet logic of form.

zh-Hant.heading: 紙上的四位警探-讓性格長成空間
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛一款以故事驅動的角色扮演遊戲，四位警探在其中聯手偵破一連串案件。問題由此浮現：一種性格，能否成為一個空間？過程從語言開始。每位警探的個性與行為被提煉為關鍵字，如緊張、嚴謹或健談，再被畫成平面的黑白圖樣，讓抽象的特質先擁有可見的形狀。圖樣隨後被摺疊、切割並堆疊在方形基座上，弧線、條板、環圈與彩色膠片，賦予每個角色各自的空間語彙。四件模型並排之時，故事不再透過文字，而是透過空間被重新述說；觀者得以看見，面對同一樁案件，不同的心靈如何以截然不同的方式運轉。

pins.title: A Settlement Growing from Ruins
pins.description:
Broken walls become the base of a settlement that keeps growing with scaffolds, ladders and bridges.

Model making | Speculative architecture | PVC board and sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從廢墟生長的聚落
zh-Hant.description:
斷牆成為聚落的基座，鷹架、梯子與橋不斷向外生長。

模型製作｜思辨建築｜PVC板與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The settlement model lit at night.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project imagines a people forced to keep living before their wounds have healed. Instead of rebuilding a perfect building, it keeps the sense of fragments and temporary repair.
captions: Key art from the game that inspired the settlement.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品想像一群在傷口尚未癒合前就必須繼續生活的人。它不重建完美的建築，而是保留碎片與臨時修補的感覺。
captions: 啟發這座聚落的遊戲主視覺。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student first tested broken forms with stacked hollow PVC blocks. Tilting and leaning the blocks showed how ruins could still carry weight.
captions: A collage of game scenes with ruins and scaffolds.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以堆疊的中空PVC方塊測試破碎形體。傾斜與倚靠的方塊顯示廢墟仍能承重。
captions: 由廢墟與鷹架遊戲場景構成的拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Collapsed walls became the base, and scaffolds, platforms and bridges were added layer by layer. Mesh, ladders and tiny figures made the settlement feel lived in.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 倒塌的牆成為基座，鷹架、平台與橋被一層層加上。網片、梯子與小人物讓聚落顯得有人居住。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The lit model shows a settlement that is repairing, living and defending at the same time. Red light and warm windows make the ruin feel both fragile and alive.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 打光後的模型呈現一座同時在修補、居住與防禦的聚落。紅光與溫暖的窗讓廢墟既脆弱又充滿生命。

sections.heading: A Settlement Growing from Ruins - Living On Among Fragments
sections.body: The project imagines a people forced to keep living before their wounds have healed. Rather than rebuilding a perfect building, it deliberately keeps the sense of fragments and temporary repair. Exploration started with broken forms: the student stacked hollow PVC blocks, tilting and leaning them to see how ruins might still carry weight. Once those tests had shown what a damaged structure could bear, collapsed walls became the base, and scaffolds, platforms and bridges were added layer by layer. Mesh, ladders and tiny figures gradually gave the settlement the feel of daily life. When lit, the model shows a place that is repairing, living and defending all at once, and its red light and warm windows make the ruin appear both fragile and alive. The work becomes a quiet statement about resilience, suggesting that a home does not have to come from wholeness and is often born from what has been broken.

zh-Hant.heading: 廢墟中生長的聚落-在碎片裡繼續生活
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品想像一群人在傷口尚未癒合之前，就被迫繼續生活。它不追求重建一座完美的建築，而是刻意保留碎片與臨時修補的痕跡。探索從破碎的形體開始：學生以中空的PVC塊堆疊、傾斜與倚靠，觀察廢墟如何仍能承受重量。在這樣的測試之後，倒塌的牆成為基座，鷹架、平台與橋梁被一層層加上；網材、梯子與小小的人形，讓聚落逐漸有了生活的氣息。點亮之後，模型同時呈現修復、居住與防禦三種狀態；紅色的光與溫暖的窗，讓廢墟顯得既脆弱又鮮活。作品因此成為一則關於韌性的低語：家，未必來自完整，而常常誕生於破碎之中。

pins.title: Chromatic Narratives
pins.description:
Three small rooms in blue, red and warm white follow a girl from loneliness to fantasy and back.

Model making | Stage design | Plywood, clay and plastic tile | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 色彩敘事
zh-Hant.description:
藍、紅與暖白三個小房間，跟隨一個女孩從孤獨走入幻想再回到現實。

模型製作｜舞台設計｜夾板、黏土與塑膠磁磚｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began with a drama the student created and performed at school. The story follows a girl who loses a close friend, escapes into fantasy and then returns to reality.
captions: The drama teacher's painting that inspired the performance.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品源自學生在學校創作並演出的戲劇。故事跟隨一個女孩失去好友、逃入幻想，最後回到現實。
captions: 啟發這場演出的戲劇老師畫作。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Key moments of the play were collaged into three scenes: a classroom, a bedroom and a hospital. Each scene was given its own colour of light.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 戲中的關鍵時刻被拼貼成三個場景：教室、臥室與醫院。每個場景都被賦予自己的光色。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The classroom uses brick walls and square tiles to show rigid rules. The bedroom is wrapped in grey clay, like concrete closing in on a dream.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 教室以磚牆與方形磁磚表現僵硬的規範。臥室被灰色黏土包覆，像混凝土包圍著一場夢。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The hospital is finished in bright white clay to suggest letting go and starting again. Together the three rooms tell the whole story through colour and material.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 醫院以明亮的白色黏土完成，暗示放下與重新開始。三個房間一起以色彩與材料講完整個故事。

sections.heading: Chromatic Narratives - Three Rooms That Tell a Farewell
sections.body: The project began with a play the student wrote and performed at school, in which a girl loses a close friend, escapes into fantasy and finally returns to reality. The challenge was to turn that inner journey into spaces one could step into. Key moments of the play were first collaged into three scenes, a classroom, a bedroom and a hospital, and each was given its own colour of light. From there, materials took over the storytelling. The classroom uses brick walls and square tiles to convey rigid rules. The bedroom is wrapped in grey clay, like concrete slowly closing in on a dream. The hospital is finished in bright white clay, suggesting release and a fresh start. Set side by side, the three rooms tell the whole story without a single word, carried only by shifts of colour and texture, so that loss, escape and acceptance each acquire a temperature that can be seen and almost felt.

zh-Hant.heading: 色彩敘事-三個房間說完一段告別
zh-Hant.body: 作品的起點，是學生在校內創作並演出的一齣戲：一個女孩失去摯友，逃入幻想，最終回到現實。如何讓這段內在的旅程化為可以走入的空間？劇中的關鍵時刻首先被拼貼為三個場景，教室、臥室與醫院，並各自被賦予一種光色。接下來，材料承擔起敘事。教室以磚牆與方形磁磚表現僵硬的規則；臥室被灰色陶土包覆，宛如混凝土逐漸逼近一場夢；醫院則以明亮的白色陶土完成，暗示放手與重新開始。三個房間並置時，整個故事無需言語，便在色彩與材質的轉換之間被完整說出，讓失落、逃避與釋懷，各自擁有可以被看見的溫度。

pins.title: A Triptych Set for a Lakeside Drama
pins.description:
A stage split into three rooms, with a painted bird at the centre standing for lost dreams.

Model making | Stage design | Foam board, balsa and acrylic paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 湖畔戲劇的三聯舞台
zh-Hant.description:
一座分成三個房間的舞台，中央手繪的飛鳥象徵失落的夢想。

模型製作｜舞台設計｜泡棉板、輕木與壓克力顏料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The play is about the clash between a stifling home and a restless wish to make art. The student wanted the set itself to split the characters' worlds apart.
captions: Photos of stage productions of the play.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這齣戲講述窒息的家庭與不安的藝術渴望之間的衝突。學生希望舞台本身就把角色們的世界分開。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Diagrams mapped a domestic zone on each side and a symbolic void in the middle. A material palette of wood, brick and white surfaces was set for each room.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圖解在兩側配置家庭區，中央則是象徵性的虛空。學生為每個房間設定木、磚與白色表面的材料配置。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The living room uses vertical wooden slats like a cage, while the bedroom uses heavy exposed brick. The centre is not a literal lake but a highly textured painting of a bird.
captions: The painted bird at the centre.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 客廳以垂直木條營造籠子般的感覺，臥室則用厚重的裸磚。中央不是真實的湖，而是一幅肌理豐富的飛鳥畫作。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The audience looks at both homes through the painted void at the centre. The set turns the play's emotional fracture into three separate rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 觀眾透過中央的繪畫虛空觀看兩側的家。舞台把戲中的情感裂痕轉化為三個分離的房間。

sections.heading: A Triptych Set for a Lakeside Drama - An Emotional Fracture Made into Three Rooms
sections.body: The play turns on a clash between a stifling home and a restless wish to make art, and the student wanted the set itself to pull the characters' worlds apart. To that end, diagrams first mapped a domestic zone on each side and a symbolic void in the middle, and a material palette of wood, brick and white surfaces was assigned to each room. Within this framework the living room is enclosed by vertical wooden slats that read like a cage, while the bedroom is wrapped in heavy exposed brick. The centre is not a literal lake but a richly textured painting of a bird. The audience must look through this painted void to see either home. The set therefore stops being a backdrop and becomes part of the drama, translating an emotional fracture into three separate rooms that stand apart yet keep gazing at one another, each holding a different answer to the question of where a life should be lived.

zh-Hant.heading: 湖畔劇場三聯舞台-讓情感的裂痕成為三個房間
zh-Hant.body: 這齣劇講述令人窒息的家庭與躁動的創作渴望之間的衝突。學生希望舞台本身，就能把角色的世界一分為二。為此，圖解先把空間劃定為兩側的居家區域與中央的象徵性空白，並為每個房間設定木材、磚與白色表面組成的材料色盤。在這套框架之下，客廳以垂直木條圍出牢籠般的格柵，臥室則以厚重的裸露紅磚包覆；中央並非寫實的湖泊，而是一幅肌理濃厚的飛鳥繪畫。觀眾必須穿過這片被描繪的空白，才能望見兩邊的家。舞台於是不只是背景，而成為情節的一部分，把劇中的情感裂痕，轉譯為三個彼此分離、卻又彼此凝望的房間。

pins.title: The Water Prison Stage
pins.description:
Curved stairs and arches rise around a round water prison inside a curtain of glowing acrylic.

Model making | Stage design | PVC board, acrylic and LED light | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 水牢舞台
zh-Hant.description:
弧形階梯與拱圈環繞圓形水牢，外圍是一圈發光的壓克力簾幕。

模型製作｜舞台設計｜PVC板、壓克力與LED燈｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The stage model in coloured light.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student set out to design a semicircular stage for a tragic drama of desire. At its heart stands a round water prison, a symbol of confinement.
captions: A stage production that inspired the design.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生為一齣關於慾望的悲劇設計半圓形舞台。舞台中心是一座圓形水牢，象徵禁錮。
captions: 啟發本設計的舞台演出。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Curved stairs and arches were drawn to create a flowing route of entrances, escapes and gazes. The ground and the prison were shaped in clay in muted yellow-grey tones.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生繪製弧形階梯與拱圈，營造入口、逃離與凝視交織的流動路徑。地面與水牢以黏土塑形，呈現低調的黃灰色調。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Clear acrylic panels were set around the stage like a curtain. LED strips behind them refract changing colours across the panels.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 透明壓克力板像簾幕一樣圍繞舞台。後方的LED燈條讓變換的色彩折射在板面上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: As the light shifts from red to blue, the same stage moves between moods. Simple geometric forms carry the tension of the story.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 當燈光從紅轉藍，同一個舞台在不同情緒之間轉換。簡單的幾何形體承載故事的張力。

sections.heading: The Water Prison Stage - Light and Colour Steering a Tragedy
sections.body: The student set out to design a semicircular stage for a tragic drama of desire, with a round water prison at its heart as a symbol of confinement. How the space itself could carry the tension of the play was the thread running through the whole process. Curved stairs and arches were drawn again and again, weaving a flowing route of entrances, escapes and gazes. The ground and the prison were shaped in clay and held to muted yellow-grey tones, leaving room for light to take the leading role. Clear acrylic panels were placed around the stage like a curtain, and LED strips behind them refract shifting colours across their surfaces. As the light moves from red to blue, the same stage drifts from one mood to another. Simple geometric forms thus stop being silent and begin to carry the weight of the story, letting the audience feel, through changes of colour alone, the pull between longing and captivity that drives the drama.

zh-Hant.heading: 水牢舞台-以光色牽動悲劇的情緒
zh-Hant.body: 學生著手為一齣關於慾望的悲劇設計一座半圓形舞台，舞台中央立著一座圓形水牢，象徵禁錮。如何讓空間本身承載戲劇的張力，是整個過程的核心。弧形階梯與拱圈被反覆繪製，編織出一條關於入場、逃離與凝視的流動路徑；地面與水牢則以陶土塑形，色調壓在沉靜的黃灰之間，讓光線成為真正的主角。透明壓克力板環繞舞台，宛如一道帷幕，背後的LED燈條把變幻的色彩折射到板面上。當光由紅轉藍，同一座舞台便在不同的情緒之間游移。簡單的幾何形體因此不再沉默，而是靜靜承擔起故事的重量，讓觀者在光影的轉變裡，感受到慾望與禁錮之間的拉扯。

pins.title: A Twisted Bond in Two Castles
pins.description:
A hanging tower of paper castles and a twirling stair turns a film about two rival friends into space.

Model making | Spatial narrative | PVC board, window film, wire and mirror paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 雙城之間的糾結情誼
zh-Hant.description:
以紙城堡與迴旋階梯構成的懸吊塔，把一部關於兩位對立好友的電影轉化為空間。

模型製作｜空間敘事｜PVC板、窗膜、金屬線與鏡面紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to turn the changing bond between two young women in a fantasy film into architecture. One is labelled a witch and the other a good girl, yet they stay friends.
captions: The film that inspired the work.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把一部奇幻電影中兩位年輕女性不斷變化的情誼轉化為建築。一人被貼上女巫的標籤，另一人被視為好女孩，但她們仍是朋友。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The story was split into four moments, from being loved by everyone to escaping the world. Each moment was linked to a bright castle, a dark castle or a prison.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 故事被拆成四個時刻，從受眾人喜愛到逃離世界。每個時刻都對應明亮的城堡、黑暗的城堡或牢籠。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The outer paper castles were built first, then the inside was filled with wire, mesh and coloured film. The structure stays the same from top to bottom while colours and materials change.
captions: Building the castles, from paper walls to the final assembly.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先建造外層的紙城堡，再以金屬線、網片與彩色薄膜填滿內部。結構由上到下保持一致，色彩與材料則不斷變化。
captions: 從紙牆到最終組裝的城堡製作過程。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A twirling stair runs through the tower, tracing a journey from enemies to friends and apart again. Mirror paper against wire and gloss against grit show two personalities side by side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 迴旋階梯貫穿整座塔，描繪從敵人到朋友再到分離的旅程。鏡面紙對比金屬線、光滑對比粗糙，呈現兩種並存的性格。

sections.heading: A Twisted Bond in Two Castles - Spiralling Between Light and Dark
sections.body: In a fantasy film, two young women stay friends even though one is labelled a witch and the other a good girl, and the student set out to turn that shifting bond into architecture. The story was divided into four moments, from being loved by everyone to escaping the world, and each moment was tied to a bright castle, a dark castle or a prison. Construction moved from the outside in. Paper castles were built first, then filled with wire, mesh and coloured film. The structure stays constant from top to bottom while its colours and materials keep changing, much as moods keep changing within a single relationship. A twirling stair runs through the tower, tracing a journey from enemies to friends and apart again. Mirror paper set against wire, gloss set against grit, lets two personalities stand side by side within one body, so that the tower reads less as a monument than as a portrait of attachment, tension and distance held in balance.

zh-Hant.heading: 兩座城堡的糾纏情誼-在明暗之間盤旋
zh-Hant.body: 一部奇幻電影裡，兩位年輕女子一人被稱為女巫，一人被視為好女孩，卻始終維繫著友誼。學生想做的，是把這段起伏不定的情誼轉化為建築。故事被拆為四個時刻，從受眾人喜愛到逃離世界，每一刻各自對應一座明亮的城堡、一座幽暗的城堡或一座牢籠。建造的順序由外而內：先以紙板完成外部的城堡，再把鐵絲、網材與彩色膠片填入其中。結構從上到下保持一致，色彩與材質卻不斷轉換，恰如同一段關係裡反覆變化的心境。一道旋梯貫穿高塔，描出從敵人到朋友、再到分離的旅程；鏡面紙與鐵絲、光滑與粗糙並置，讓兩種性格在同一座塔中並肩而立。

pins.title: Looms
pins.description:
The frames and rhythm of old weaving machines are taken apart and rebuilt as a tower of wooden sticks.

Model making | Structural form | Wooden sticks and string | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 織機
zh-Hant.description:
把古老織布機的框架與節奏拆解，再重組為一座木棒之塔。

模型製作｜結構造型｜木棒與棉線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project draws on old weaving looms and sewing machines. The question was how the rhythm of a machine could become an architectural form.
captions: Notes on how a loom works.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品取材自古老的織布機與縫紉機。問題是機械的節奏如何成為建築形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how the treadles, beams and beater of a loom work together. Digital models and part drawings helped break the machine into frames and joints.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究織機的踏板、經軸與筘如何協同運作。數位模型與構件圖幫助把機械拆解成框架與接頭。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A first tower was built from straight sticks that spread out like threads from a central core. Square frames were then twisted around it to show motion.
captions: Sticks fanning out at the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一座塔以直木棒構成，像絲線一樣從中央核心向外展開。接著在周圍扭轉方形框架以表現運動。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final tower, red string is woven between the sticks to tie the frames together. It merges the precision of a machine with the fluid feel of weaving.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終的塔中，紅線穿梭於木棒之間，把框架連成一體。它融合了機械的精準與編織的流動感。

sections.heading: Looms - Weaving the Rhythm of a Machine into a Tower
sections.body: Old weaving looms and sewing machines lie at the root of this project, and the question was how the rhythm of a machine might become an architectural form. Answering it meant understanding the machine itself. The student studied how the treadles, beams and beater of a loom pull on one another, while digital models and part drawings broke the whole apparatus into frames and joints until its logic became legible. A first tower was then built from straight sticks spreading out from a central core like threads drawn apart. Around that core, square frames were twisted layer by layer, so that a still structure began to hint at motion. In the final tower, red string is woven back and forth between the sticks, binding every frame to the next. Here the precision of a machine and the softness of weaving no longer stand in opposition; they are braided into a single, quietly turning rhythm that the eye can follow from base to crown.

zh-Hant.heading: 織機-把機械的節奏編成高塔
zh-Hant.body: 古老的織布機與縫紉機，是這個作品的源頭。問題在於：一部機器的節奏，如何轉化為建築的形體？要回答它，學生必須先理解機器本身。踏板、經軸與打緯筘如何彼此牽動，被一一研究；數位模型與零件圖則把整部織機拆解為框架與接點，讓機械的邏輯變得清晰可讀。第一座塔以筆直的木棒構成，從中央核心向外散開，如同被拉開的絲線；接著，方形框架環繞核心逐層扭轉，讓靜止的結構透露出運動的暗示。最終的塔中，紅色細繩在木棒之間來回編織，把每一層框架緊緊相繫。機械的精準與編織的柔軟，在此不再對立，而是交纏成同一種韻律。

pins.title: Cycles of Nature
pins.description:
Branches, bark and resin build a layered model of how fallen trees slowly turn into soil.

Model making | Natural systems | Branches, bark, fibre optics and 3D resin | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然循環
zh-Hant.description:
以樹枝、樹皮與樹脂構成層疊模型，呈現倒下的樹木如何慢慢化為土壤。

模型製作｜自然系統｜樹枝、樹皮、光纖與3D樹脂｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The layered tree and soil model.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project looks at how fallen bark and leaves slowly become soil that feeds new trees. It treats decay and rebirth as one continuous cycle.
captions: Inspiration photos of tree bark and ink.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品探討落下的樹皮與葉子如何慢慢化為滋養新樹的土壤。它把腐朽與重生視為一個連續的循環。
captions: 樹皮與墨跡的靈感照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student collected bark and made ink drawings that merge water flow with bark texture. Six material tests mixed branches, bark, powder and resin.
captions: Ink studies of bark and water.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集樹皮，並以墨跡畫融合水流與樹皮紋理。六組材料實驗混合了樹枝、樹皮、粉末與樹脂。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Layers of stone, mesh and soil were stacked inside a frame of branches. A pencil drawing tested how roots could pass through each layer.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石頭、網片與土壤被層層堆疊在樹枝框架中。一張鉛筆畫測試根系如何穿過每一層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model shows a tree rising from layers of soil and bedrock. Fibre optics make it glow green in the dark, like life returning.
captions: The model glowing in the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型呈現一棵從土層與岩床中升起的樹。光纖讓它在黑暗中發出綠光，彷彿生命回歸。

sections.heading: Cycles of Nature - Between Decay and Rebirth
sections.body: Fallen bark and leaves slowly turn into soil that feeds new trees. The project treats this decay and rebirth as one continuous cycle and asks how such slow, invisible time might be made visible. Collecting bark was the first gesture; the student then made ink drawings in which the flow of water and the grain of bark merge into a single texture. Six material tests followed, mixing branches, bark, powder and resin to find how far natural matter could be recombined while keeping its character. On that ground, layers of stone, mesh and soil were stacked inside a frame of branches, and a pencil drawing tested how roots might push through each stratum. In the finished model a tree rises from soil and bedrock, and fibre optics glow green in the dark, as though life were quietly returning. The work becomes a meditation on time, suggesting that an ending and a beginning are simply two points on the same ring of growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 自然循環-在腐朽與重生之間
zh-Hant.body: 落下的樹皮與葉片，緩慢地化為土壤，再滋養新的樹木。這個作品把腐朽與重生視為同一個不間斷的循環，並追問如何讓這段看不見的時間被看見。學生先蒐集樹皮，以墨線繪圖把水流與樹皮紋理融為一體，再進行六組材料實驗，混合枝條、樹皮、粉末與樹脂，摸索自然材料能被重組到什麼程度。在此基礎上，石塊、網材與土壤被層層堆疊於枝條構成的框架之中，一張鉛筆圖則測試根系如何穿越每一層。完成的模型裡，一棵樹自土層與岩盤之中升起；光纖在黑暗中透出綠光，宛如生命正悄悄回返。作品因此成為一則關於時間的沉思：結束與開始，原來只是同一圈年輪的兩端。

pins.title: Kinetics of Space
pins.description:
Speed, timing, angle and division in a squash game become four small studies and one large installation.

Model making | Installation | Mirror, foil, acrylic, springs and plywood | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間動力學
zh-Hant.description:
壁球比賽中的速度、時機、角度與分割，成為四件小研究與一座大型裝置。

模型製作｜裝置｜鏡面、錫箔、壓克力、彈簧與夾板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student plays squash and finds it striking that the ball always returns from the wall. In a way, the court works as if it were twice its real size.
captions: Players moving on a squash court.
Sketches of time, space and angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生打壁球，並著迷於球總會從牆面反彈回來。某種程度上，球場的運作就像是實際大小的兩倍。
captions: 時間、空間與角度的草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Four ideas were drawn from the game: speed, timing, angle and division. Each became a small study model in a different material.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從比賽中提取四個概念：速度、時機、角度與分割。每個概念都成為一件不同材料的小研究模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The four studies were joined into one large model with a frame of chicken wire and wooden boards. Foil-wrapped foam balls and stretched fabric show the speed of the ball.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 四件研究被組合成一座以雞籠網與木板為框架的大型模型。錫箔包覆的泡棉球與拉伸的布料表現球速。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Mirrors extend the space, while threads and plates capture direction and velocity. The installation turns the game into a system of geometry, time and movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鏡面延伸了空間，細線與板片捕捉方向與速度。裝置把比賽轉化為幾何、時間與運動的系統。

sections.heading: Kinetics of Space - The Rebound of a Squash Ball Turned into Geometry
sections.body: As a squash player, the student was fascinated by one simple fact: the ball always comes back from the wall, so the court behaves as if it were twice its real size. That bodily intuition became the seed of the whole project. From the game itself the student distilled four ideas, speed, timing, angle and division, and gave each its own small study model in a different material, testing how each concept might take physical shape. The harder task was to stitch these four studies into one body. A large frame of chicken wire and wooden boards holds them together, while foil-wrapped foam balls and stretched fabric capture the rush of the ball. Mirrors push the space outward, and threads and plates record direction and velocity. In the end the installation is no longer a picture of a sport but a system woven from geometry, time and movement, where a fleeting rally leaves behind a trace that can be studied, walked around and held in the eye.

zh-Hant.heading: 空間動力學-讓壁球的反彈成為幾何
zh-Hant.body: 身為壁球選手，學生總為一件事著迷：球永遠會從牆面彈回，球場因此彷彿擁有兩倍於實際的尺寸。這份來自身體的直覺，成為整個作品的起點。從比賽之中，學生提煉出四個概念：速度、時機、角度與分割，並讓每一個概念各自化為一件小型研究模型，以不同材料試探它的性格。隨後的挑戰，是把四件研究縫合為一個整體。雞籠網與木板構成大型骨架，以鋁箔包覆的泡棉球與繃緊的布料，捕捉球的飛速；鏡面讓空間向外延伸，絲線與板片則記錄方向與速度。最終的裝置不再只是對運動的描繪，而是一套由幾何、時間與移動交織而成的系統，讓一場短暫的對打，在空間中留下可以凝視的軌跡。

pins.title: Soap City
pins.description:
A soap mountain melts through a forest of sticks into a city of staples below.

Model making | Urban narrative | Soap, steel, acrylic, staples and wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 肥皂城市
zh-Hant.description:
一座肥皂山穿過木棒森林，融化成下方以釘書針構成的城市。

模型製作｜城市敘事｜肥皂、鋼材、壓克力、釘書針與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The soap city in its acrylic frame.
壓克力框中的肥皂城市。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The idea came while the student was using soap in the shower. Soap making changed from natural herbs to industrial chemicals as rural land turned into cities.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個想法來自學生淋浴時使用肥皂。隨著鄉村變成城市，肥皂製作也從天然草本轉為工業化學品。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches set out three layers: nature at the top, industry in the middle and the city at the bottom. Soap was melted, cast and cut to test how it could flow and harden.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖安排了三層：上方是自然、中間是工業、下方是城市。學生熔化、澆鑄並切割肥皂，測試它如何流動與凝固。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A snowy soap mountain sits at the top, and melted soap drips through a dense grid of wooden sticks. At the bottom, piles of staples form towers and streets.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 雪白的肥皂山位於頂端，融化的肥皂沿著密集的木棒格網滴落。底部則以成堆的釘書針形成高樓與街道。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model hangs between two acrylic sheets held by steel rods. It reads as a story of natural land slowly becoming an urban grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型懸掛在以鋼桿固定的兩片壓克力板之間。它講述自然土地逐漸變成城市網格的故事。

sections.heading: Soap City - A Melting Peak Dripping into a City
sections.body: The idea arrived in the shower, with a bar of soap in hand. The student noticed that soap making had moved from natural herbs to industrial chemicals just as rural land had turned into cities, and the question became whether an everyday material could tell the story of a changing landscape. Sketches came first, dividing the narrative into three layers: nature above, industry in the middle, the city below. Soap was then melted, cast and cut again and again, so that the student could test with bare hands how it flows and how it hardens. Through these trials the character of the material became a language of its own. A snowy soap mountain melts quietly at the top, its liquid dripping through a dense grid of wooden sticks, while at the bottom piles of staples rise into towers and streets. Suspended between two acrylic sheets on steel rods, the finished model reads like a frozen fable, letting the viewer watch natural ground give way, drop by drop, to the urban grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 肥皂之城-從融化的山峰滴落成城市
zh-Hant.body: 靈感起於淋浴時手中的一塊肥皂。學生察覺，製皂從天然草本走向工業化學，恰與鄉野轉為城市的歷程相互映照。於是，追問落在一個看似微小卻深遠的問題：一種日常材料，能否講述土地的變遷？草圖首先把敘事分為三層：自然居上，工業居中，城市在下；接著，肥皂被反覆融化、澆鑄與切割，讓學生親手測試它如何流動、如何凝固。在這樣的試驗裡，材料的性格逐漸成為語言：雪白的皂山在頂端靜靜融化，皂液穿過密集的木棒格網緩緩滴落，最底層則以釘書針堆疊成高樓與街道。最終，模型懸吊於兩片壓克力之間，由鋼桿固定，像一則被凝結的寓言，讓人看見自然的土地如何一點一滴，被城市的格網取代。

pins.title: The Recycled City
pins.description:
Handmade paper from waste fabric, leaves and branches floats in layers on steel rods.

Model making | Material study | Recycled paper and steel rods | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 再生之城
zh-Hant.description:
以廢棄布料、落葉與樹枝製成的手工紙，層層漂浮在鋼桿上。

模型製作｜材料研究｜再生紙與鋼桿｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student saw paper as thin, easily torn and always keeping traces of what happened to it. The project asks how marks of damage can become signs of strength.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生認為紙很薄、容易撕破，並總會留下經歷的痕跡。作品探問損傷的痕跡如何成為堅韌的象徵。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Old garments, rotting leaves and branches were collected and crushed in a blender. A step-by-step guide set out how fibre becomes pulp, then sheets.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集舊衣、腐葉與樹枝，並用果汁機打碎。一份逐步圖解說明纖維如何變成紙漿，再成為紙張。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two or three sheets were stitched together with red thread and hardened with glue. The stitches were left visible as marks that resist being erased.
captions: Stitching the handmade paper sheets with red thread.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 兩到三張紙以紅線縫合，再以膠固化。縫線被刻意保留，成為抗拒被抹去的痕跡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each sheet was drilled and stacked on steel rods, with the gaps measured again and again. The floating layers read as a quiet city built from what others threw away.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每張紙都被鑽孔並疊上鋼桿，間距經過反覆測量。漂浮的紙層像一座由他人丟棄之物築成的安靜城市。

sections.heading: Recycled City - A Floating City Stacked from Handmade Paper
sections.body: The student saw paper as thin, easily torn and always keeping traces of what has happened to it, and the project asked how marks of damage could become signs of strength. The guidance first led the student to collect old garments, rotting leaves and branches and crush them in a blender, then to write a step-by-step guide recording how fibre becomes pulp and then sheets, so that discarded things first gained a new identity through transformation. In development, two or three sheets were stitched together with red thread and hardened with glue, the stitches deliberately left visible as marks that resist being erased. Finally, each sheet was drilled and stacked on steel rods, the gaps measured and adjusted again and again, and the floating layers read as a quiet city built from what others threw away, so that fragility itself becomes the most resolute of languages.

zh-Hant.heading: 再生之城-以手抄紙堆疊出的漂浮城市
zh-Hant.body: 在學生眼中，紙輕薄、易破，總是留下曾經發生之事的痕跡。這個作品追問：損傷的印記，如何成為力量的象徵？指導過程先引導學生蒐集舊衣、腐葉與枝條，以果汁機打碎，再寫下一份步驟說明，記錄纖維如何成為紙漿、再成為紙張，讓廢棄之物先在轉化中獲得新的身分。進入推演，兩三張紙以紅線縫合，再以膠水使其硬化，縫線被刻意保留，成為抗拒被抹去的痕跡。最後，每張紙被鑽孔，堆疊在鋼棒上，間距一次次量測調整，漂浮的層次讀來如一座安靜的城市，由別人丟棄的東西築成，讓脆弱本身，成為最堅定的語言。

pins.title: A Field Chapel in Plaster and Burnt Timber
pins.description:
A plaster shell cast around burnt wooden strips studies a small chapel standing alone in a field.

Model making | Precedent study | Plaster and wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 石膏與燒木的田野小教堂
zh-Hant.description:
以石膏包覆燒過的木條，研究一座獨立於田野中的小教堂。

模型製作｜案例研究｜石膏與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student studied a small concrete chapel that stands alone in farm fields. Its outer shell was poured in thin layers, and its inner walls carry the marks of burnt wood.
captions: Photos of the original chapel that the model studies.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一座獨立於農田中的混凝土小教堂。它的外殼以薄層澆灌，內牆則留有燒木的痕跡。
captions: 模型所研究的原教堂照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The question was how to rebuild that process at a small scale with simple materials. A core of wooden strips stood in for the timber frame used on site.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 問題是如何以簡單材料在小尺度上重現這個過程。木條核心代替了現場使用的木構架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plaster was poured around the core in layers inside a sloped mould. After it set, the inner wood was burnt and cleaned to leave a dark, ribbed surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石膏在斜面模具中分層澆灌於核心周圍。凝固後，內部的木材被燒灼並清理，留下深色的肋紋表面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model shows a pale, heavy shell around a dark, narrow void. Light falls through the opening at the top, much like the real chapel.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型呈現淺色厚重的外殼包圍著深色狹長的空腔。光從頂部開口灑落，正如真實的小教堂。

sections.heading: Burnt Timber Field Chapel - Recreating Light and Char at Small Scale
sections.body: The student studied a small concrete chapel standing alone among farm fields, its outer shell poured in thin layers and its inner walls carrying the marks of burnt wood, and the question was how to rebuild that process at small scale with simple materials. The guidance first led the student to use a core of wooden strips in place of the timber frame used on site, so that the logic of construction was first understood and then simulated by hand. In development, plaster was poured in layers around the core inside a sloped mould, and once it set the inner wood was burnt and cleaned away to leave a dark, ribbed surface, the process itself becoming the most honest reading of the original. Finally, the model shows a pale, heavy shell around a dark, narrow void, with light falling through the opening at the top much like the real chapel, so that the traces of fire and time glow quietly in the hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 焚木田野小教堂-以小尺度重現光與焦痕
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一座獨自矗立於農田之間的小型混凝土教堂，它的外殼以薄層逐次澆灌，內牆則留著焚燒木材的痕跡。問題是：如何以簡單的材料，在小尺度上重建這個過程？指導過程先引導學生以木條組成的核心，代替現場使用的木構架，讓建造的邏輯先被理解，再被親手模擬。進入推演，石膏在傾斜的模具中，分層澆灌於核心四周，凝固之後，內部的木材被焚燒、清理，留下深色而帶肋紋的表面，過程本身成為對原作最誠實的閱讀。最後，模型呈現一道淺色而厚重的外殼，包圍著深色狹窄的空腔，光從頂部的開口落下，一如真實的教堂，讓火與時間留下的痕跡，在掌中靜靜發光。

pins.title: Hive Commons
pins.description:
Hexagonal modules in three sizes turn a quiet city plaza into a lively, flexible public space.

Urban design | Public space | Laser cutting and 3D printing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 蜂巢共享廣場
zh-Hant.description:
三種尺寸的六角形模組，把冷清的城市廣場變成熱鬧而靈活的公共空間。

城市設計｜公共空間｜雷射切割與3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site is a quiet, underused plaza in San Francisco that feels unsafe at night. The aim was to make it welcoming for skaters, visitors, locals and families.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地是舊金山一處冷清、少被使用、夜間令人不安的廣場。目標是讓它對滑板族、遊客、居民與家庭都更友善。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Site maps traced where people gather and the main routes across the plaza. These showed large empty areas that could take new activities.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地圖追蹤人群聚集之處與穿越廣場的主要動線。結果顯示有大片空地可以容納新活動。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Inspired by honeycombs, the student designed hexagon units in three sizes for benches, food trucks and small galleries. Coloured blocks on study models tested many ways to group them.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 受蜂巢啟發，學生設計了三種尺寸的六角單元，用作座椅、餐車與小型展廊。研究模型上的彩色方塊測試了多種組合方式。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The units can be added or removed as events change, so the plaza keeps evolving. The final view shows a friendly space for both busy lunches and calm evening walks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 單元可隨活動增減，讓廣場持續變化。最終的透視呈現一個適合忙碌午餐與寧靜晚間散步的友善空間。

sections.heading: Hive Commons - A Public Plaza of Hexagons That Grows and Shrinks
sections.body: The site is a quiet, underused plaza in San Francisco that feels unsafe at night, and the aim was to make it welcoming for skaters, visitors, locals and families. The guidance first led the student to trace in site maps where people gather and the main routes across the plaza, revealing large empty areas that could take new activities, so that observation first pointed to the opportunity for design. In development, inspired by honeycombs, the student designed hexagonal units in three sizes for benches, food trucks and small galleries, and coloured blocks on study models tested many ways to group them. Finally, the units can be added or removed as events change so that the plaza keeps evolving, and the final view shows a friendly space for both busy lunches and calm evening walks, so that a forgotten plaza regains the warmth of people.

zh-Hant.heading: 蜂巢共享廣場-可增減的六角形公共空間
zh-Hant.body: 基地是舊金山一座安靜而少人使用的廣場，夜裡令人感到不安。目標是讓它對滑板族、遊客、在地居民與家庭都友善。指導過程先引導學生以基地圖描繪人們聚集之處與穿越廣場的主要動線，從中發現大片可以容納新活動的空地，讓觀察先指出設計的機會。進入推演，學生從蜂巢獲得靈感，設計三種尺寸的六角形單元，作為長椅、餐車與小型展廊，並在研究模型上以彩色方塊測試多種組合方式。最後，單元可隨活動的變化增減，讓廣場持續演變，最終的畫面呈現一處既適合熱鬧午餐、也適合寧靜夜間散步的親切空間，讓一座被遺忘的廣場，重新有了人的溫度。

pins.title: A Tower of Two Cities
pins.description:
A cardboard and wire tower turns an animated series about two divided cities and two sisters into space.

Model making | Spatial narrative | Pencil, card paper and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 雙城之塔
zh-Hant.description:
以紙板與金屬線構成的塔，把一部關於兩座分裂城市與一對姊妹的動畫影集轉化為空間。

模型製作｜空間敘事｜鉛筆、卡紙與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student chose an animated series about two divided cities and the broken bond between two sisters. The aim was to show how inequality and conflict can shape a person's path.
captions: The full series poster that inspired the tower.
Stills of the story, part one.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇了一部關於兩座分裂城市與一對姊妹破裂情誼的動畫影集。目標是呈現不平等與衝突如何塑造一個人的道路。
captions: 啟發這座塔的影集完整海報。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Key scenes were collected and lined up as a storyline from the crowded lower city to the final flare. Each scene was then given a layer in a sketch of the tower.
captions: Stills of the story, part two.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集關鍵場景，從擁擠的下城到最後的信號火光排成一條故事線。每個場景都在塔的草圖中對應一個層次。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cardboard houses form the base and a bar sits at the centre, with silver cards and blue wire for an explosion. Above them, black sticks form a prison and wire wrapped in mesh shows a restless mind.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙板房屋構成底座，中央是一間酒館，銀色卡片與藍色金屬線代表爆炸。上方的黑色木棒形成牢籠，包覆網布的金屬線呈現不安的心境。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower reads from bottom to top as one journey through the story. Blue straws at the very top stand for a flare, a promise to find each other again.
captions: Wire and straws at the top.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔由下而上讀起來就是穿越故事的一段旅程。最頂端的藍色吸管象徵信號火光，也是再次找到彼此的承諾。

sections.heading: Two Cities Tower - From an Animated Story into Space
sections.body: The student chose an animated series about two divided cities and the broken bond between two sisters, aiming to show how inequality and conflict can shape a person's path. The guidance first led the student to collect key scenes and line them up as a storyline from the crowded lower city to the final flare, then to give each scene a layer in a sketch of the tower, so that the narrative first became a vertical structure. In development, cardboard houses form the base with a bar at the centre, silver cards and blue wire express an explosion, and above them black sticks form a prison while wire wrapped in mesh shows a restless mind. Finally, the tower reads from bottom to top as one journey through the story, and blue straws at the very top stand for a flare, a promise to find each other again, so that a separation waits on high for reunion.

zh-Hant.heading: 雙城之塔-從動畫故事走進空間
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇一部關於兩座分裂城市、以及一對姊妹斷裂情誼的動畫影集，目標是呈現不平等與衝突如何塑造一個人的道路。指導過程先引導學生蒐集關鍵場景，把它們排成一條從擁擠的下城到最後信號彈的故事線，再在高塔草圖中為每個場景分配一層，讓敘事先成為垂直的結構。進入推演，紙板小屋構成底部，中央是一間酒館，銀色卡片與藍色鐵絲表現爆炸，上方的黑色木棒形成牢籠，包覆網布的鐵絲則呈現一顆不安的心。最後，高塔由下而上讀來如一段穿越故事的旅程，頂端的藍色吸管象徵一枚信號彈，一個要再次找到彼此的承諾，讓一段分離，在高處等待重逢。

pins.title: Shade Pavilion for a Seaside Plaza
pins.description:
A light wooden pavilion gives shade, seats and a place for events on a windy, sunny plaza by the sea.

Model making | Public space | Pencil, card paper and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 海濱廣場遮陽亭
zh-Hant.description:
一座輕巧的木構亭為海邊多風、日曬強烈的廣場提供遮陽、座位與活動空間。

模型製作｜公共空間｜鉛筆、卡紙與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The plaza by the sea has few obstructions, so summer sun is strong and winter wind is harsh. Outdoor seats are also scarce, and the space stays empty when no events are held.
captions: Photos of the seaside plaza site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座海邊廣場幾乎沒有遮蔽，夏天日曬強烈，冬天風勢猛烈。戶外座位也很少，沒有活動時空間便閒置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student mapped the park, food places, offices and the ferry terminal around the plaza. Simple sketches then tested three needs: shade, rest and activity.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生繪出廣場周邊的公園、餐飲、辦公與渡輪碼頭。接著以簡單草圖測試三種需求：遮陽、休憩與活動。
captions: 遮陽、休憩與活動的構想。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A ring of wooden sticks holds a fabric roof that dips between the posts. Double seats along the edge let people face in or out.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一圈木棒撐起在柱間下垂的布質屋頂。邊緣的雙向座椅讓人可以面向內或外。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Renders place the temporary pavilion on the plaza as a spot for meals, rest and small events. It brings life to an empty space while keeping people out of the strong sun.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 渲染圖將這座臨時亭子置於廣場上，作為用餐、休息與小型活動的場所。它為閒置空間帶來活力，也讓人避開強烈日曬。

sections.heading: Seaside Plaza Shade Pavilion - Bringing Life to an Open Ground
sections.body: The plaza by the sea has few obstructions, so summer sun is strong and winter wind is harsh, outdoor seats are scarce, and the space stays empty whenever no events are held. The guidance first led the student to map the park, food places, offices and ferry terminal around the plaza, then to test three needs in simple sketches, shade, rest and activity, so that the problem of emptiness was first broken down into concrete needs. In development, a ring of wooden sticks holds a fabric roof that dips between the posts, and double seats along the edge let people face inward or outward, a simple structure answering many uses. Finally, renders place the temporary pavilion on the plaza as a spot for meals, rest and small events, bringing life to an empty space while sheltering people from the strong sun, so that a wind-swept plaza at last offers a reason to stay.

zh-Hant.heading: 海濱廣場遮蔭亭-為空曠之地帶來生氣
zh-Hant.body: 海邊的廣場少有遮擋，夏日陽光強烈，冬季寒風刺骨，戶外座位稀少，沒有活動時便空無一人。指導過程先引導學生繪製廣場周邊的公園、餐飲、辦公室與渡輪碼頭，再以簡單的草圖測試三種需求：遮蔭、休息與活動，讓空曠的問題先被拆解為具體的需要。進入推演，一圈木棒撐起在柱間下垂的布質屋頂，沿邊配置的雙向座椅讓人可以朝內或朝外而坐，簡單的構造回應多樣的使用。最後，渲染圖把這座臨時涼亭放在廣場上，成為用餐、休憩與小型活動的去處，為空曠之地帶來生氣，也替人們擋住烈日，讓海風吹拂的廣場，終於有了停留的理由。

pins.title: Tree-Architecture Symbiosis
pins.description:
Thousands of wooden strips grow like a tree around metal platforms, so nature and building become one.

Model making | Nature and structure | Wooden sticks, wooden board, paint and steel frames | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹與建築的共生
zh-Hant.description:
成千上萬的木條像樹一樣圍繞金屬平台生長，讓自然與建築合而為一。

模型製作｜自然與結構｜木棒、木板、顏料與鋼框｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Much building begins by clearing forests, and modern buildings often feel cold and over-refined. The student asked how a building could grow with a tree instead of replacing it.
captions: A treehouse precedent that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多建造始於砍伐森林，現代建築也常顯得冰冷、過度精緻。學生思考建築如何能與樹一起生長，而不是取代它。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Tree houses seen on trips abroad showed how small rooms can sit high in branches. Sketches tested posts, roofs and ladders that lean on a trunk.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 在國外旅行看到的樹屋，展示了小房間如何高掛在枝幹間。草圖測試了倚靠樹幹的支柱、屋頂與梯子。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden strips were graded from thick to thin to follow the taper of a real tree. Silver-painted frames and platforms were then tied in with ladders and weathered with acrylic.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條由粗到細分級，以呼應真實樹木的漸細形態。接著以梯子連接漆成銀色的框架與平台，並用壓克力顏料做出風化效果。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model, branches and rusted steel frames merge into one form linked by free paths. It suggests a future where people, trees and buildings live as partners.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，枝幹與生鏽鋼框融為一體，並以自由的路徑串連。它描繪出人、樹與建築成為夥伴的未來。

sections.heading: Tree and Architecture in Symbiosis - A Home That Grows with a Tree
sections.body: Much building begins by clearing forests, and modern buildings often feel cold and over-refined, so the student asked how a building could grow with a tree instead of replacing it. The guidance first led the student to recall tree houses seen on trips abroad and understand how small rooms can sit high among branches, then to test in sketches posts, roofs and ladders that lean on a trunk, so that a way of living with nature first took shape on paper. In development, wooden strips were graded from thick to thin to follow the taper of a real tree, and silver-painted frames and platforms were tied in with ladders and weathered with acrylic paint. Finally, branches and rusted steel frames merge into one form linked by free paths, picturing a future in which people, trees and buildings live as partners, so that dwelling becomes once more a gentle way of sharing the world.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹與建築的共生-與樹一同生長的家
zh-Hant.body: 許多建造始於砍伐森林，現代建築也常顯得冰冷而過度精緻。學生追問：建築如何與一棵樹一同生長，而非取代它？指導過程先引導學生回想旅途中見過的樹屋，理解小小的房間如何高踞枝間，再以草圖測試倚靠樹幹的柱子、屋頂與梯子，讓與自然相處的方式先在紙上成形。進入推演，木條由粗到細分級，順著真實樹木的漸收，銀色塗裝的框架與平台再以梯子串連，並以壓克力顏料做出風化的痕跡。最後，枝幹與鏽蝕的鋼框融為一體，以自由的路徑相連，描繪一個人、樹與建築彼此為伴的未來，讓棲居，重新成為一種與萬物共處的溫柔。

pins.title: Tokyo Light Topography
pins.description:
A night satellite image of Tokyo Bay becomes a mountain of wooden triangles, taller where the city glows brighter.

Model making | Data to form | Pencil, card paper and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 東京光之地形
zh-Hant.description:
一張東京灣夜間衛星影像化為木棒三角形構成的山，城市越亮的地方就越高。

模型製作｜數據轉化造型｜鉛筆、卡紙與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to turn abstract city data into a physical form. A night satellite image of Tokyo Bay shows where people live and work most densely.
captions: Night satellite image of the bay.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把抽象的城市數據轉化為實體造型。東京灣的夜間衛星影像顯示人們居住與工作最密集的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The image was split into a grid and each cell was given a grey value. Each value became a height, so brightness turns directly into elevation.
captions: Two precedent buildings studied for geometric form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 影像被切成網格，每一格都給予灰階值。每個數值轉為高度，讓亮度直接變成海拔。
captions: 為幾何形式研究的兩個建築案例。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangles of wooden sticks were joined into a frame that rises over the brightest areas. Coloured and shiny films were tested to catch light inside the frame.
captions: Turning the satellite image into the stick model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒三角形接合成框架，在最亮的區域升起。學生也測試了彩色與亮面薄膜，讓框架內部捕捉光線。
captions: 將衛星影像轉化為木棒模型的過程。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model reads as an urban mountain range made of light. It is a study in data, material logic and the shape of a city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讀起來像一座由光構成的城市山脈。它是一項關於數據、材料邏輯與城市形態的研究。

sections.heading: Tokyo Light Topography - Night Lights Piled into Mountains
sections.body: The student wanted to turn abstract city data into physical form, and a night satellite image of Tokyo Bay revealed where people live and work most densely. The guidance first led the student to divide the image into a grid and give each cell a grey value, then to let each value become a height so that brightness turns directly into elevation, so that the distribution of light first became a rigorous rule. In development, triangles of wooden sticks were joined into a frame rising over the brightest areas, and coloured and reflective films were tested one by one to catch light inside the frame, the data gaining texture through material. Finally, the model reads as an urban mountain range made of light, a study in data, material logic and the shape of a city, so that the countless lights of a night sky settle into a terrain one can walk around.

zh-Hant.heading: 東京光地形-把夜間燈火堆成山脈
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把抽象的城市數據轉化為實體的形態。一張東京灣的夜間衛星影像，顯示出人們生活與工作最密集的地方。指導過程先引導學生把影像切分為網格，為每一格賦予灰階數值，再讓每個數值成為一個高度，使亮度直接轉化為高程，讓光的分布先成為一套嚴謹的規則。進入推演，木棒組成的三角形接合為框架，在最明亮的區域上方升起，彩色與反光的薄膜被逐一測試，在框架內捕捉光線，數據在材料中獲得質感。最後，模型讀來如一片由光構成的城市山脈，是一次關於數據、材料邏輯與城市形狀的研究，讓夜空中的萬家燈火，凝結為可以環繞觀看的地形。

pins.title: Night Market and Housing
pins.description:
An empty parking lot becomes a night market with homes, wrapped in a facade of hundreds of thin wooden strips.

Model making | Housing | Wooden board, wooden strips and PLA | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 夜市與住宅
zh-Hant.description:
一塊閒置停車場化為結合住宅的夜市，外牆包覆數百根細木條。

模型製作｜住宅設計｜木板、木條與PLA｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The house with its strip facade.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site is a wasteful parking lot in a busy city district. The student proposed turning it into a night market and public community, keeping a free parking section.
captions: Satellite map and street photos of the parking-lot site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地是繁忙城區中一塊浪費的停車場。學生提議將其改造為夜市與公共社區，並保留一區免費停車。
captions: 停車場基地的衛星地圖與街景照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: To get sizes right, the student studied how human figures scale against furniture and rooms. Each drawn figure became a gauge for real bodies and movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 為了掌握尺寸，學生研究人體與家具、房間之間的比例。每個繪製的人形都成為衡量真實身體與動作的尺規。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In a later step, one corner became homes for couples, singles and families. All parts were drawn to scale, laser-cut from wood and joined, with window frames painted black.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在後續階段，一角被規劃為情侶、單身者與家庭的住宅。所有構件依比例繪製、以雷射切割木材並接合，窗框漆成黑色。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The frame is wrapped in hundreds of hand-cut basswood strips that give a rhythmic, tactile facade. White 3D-printed furniture shows how the rooms are lived in.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 框架外包覆數百根手工切割的椴木條，形成富有節奏與觸感的外牆。白色3D列印家具呈現房間的使用方式。

sections.heading: Night Market Housing - Wooden Strips Weaving Rhythm into the City
sections.body: The site is a wasteful parking lot in a busy city district, and the student proposed turning it into a night market and public community while keeping a section of free parking. The guidance first led the student to study how human figures scale against furniture and rooms, so that each drawn figure became a gauge for real bodies and movement, the body serving as the origin of every dimension. In development, one corner was developed into homes for couples, singles and families, with every part drawn to scale, laser cut from wood and joined, the window frames painted black, precision of detail supporting an imagined way of life. Finally, the frame is wrapped in hundreds of hand-cut basswood strips that give a rhythmic, tactile facade, while white 3D-printed furniture shows how the rooms are lived in, so that an idle plot of land lights up the city's nights once more.

zh-Hant.heading: 夜市住宅-以木條為城市編出節奏
zh-Hant.body: 基地是繁忙城區裡一座浪費土地的停車場。學生提議把它轉化為夜市與公共社區，同時保留一區免費停車。指導過程先引導學生研究人體尺度如何對應家具與房間，讓每一個畫出的人形，都成為衡量真實身體與移動的量尺，以身體作為一切尺寸的起點。進入推演，其中一角被發展為供伴侶、單身者與家庭居住的住宅，所有部分依比例繪製，以木材雷射切割並接合，窗框漆成黑色，細節的精確撐起生活的想像。最後，框架包覆著數百根手工裁切的椴木條，形成富有節奏與觸感的立面，白色3D列印家具則展示房間如何被居住，讓一塊閒置的土地，重新點亮城市的夜晚。

pins.title: Frozen Harbour
pins.description:
