A snowy harbour map from a video game is broken into flat shapes, then rebuilt with straws, sticks and shiny paper.

Model making | Game space | Wood sticks, plastic, straws, corrugated paper and laser paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 冰封港灣
zh-Hant.description:
把電子遊戲中的雪地港灣地圖拆成平面造型，再以吸管、木棒與亮面紙重建。

模型製作｜遊戲空間｜木棒、塑膠片、吸管、瓦楞紙與雷射紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student took a snowy harbour map from a video game as the starting point. The aim was to take its spaces apart and rebuild them by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生以一款電子遊戲中的雪地港灣地圖作為起點。目標是拆解它的空間，再親手重建。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Elements such as the curved dome, lanes, cranes and containers were sketched one by one. They were then arranged into a composition of pure flat shapes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圓頂、通道、吊車與貨櫃等元素被逐一描繪。接著它們被排列成純粹的平面幾何構成。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The flat design was translated into 3D through a careful choice of materials. White and blue straws stand for water, and silver and brown strips frame the crane.
captions: Building the model from sticks, straws and corrugated paper.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 平面設計透過精選的材料轉化為立體。白色與藍色吸管代表水，銀色與棕色木條構成吊車的骨架。
captions: 以木棒、吸管與瓦楞紙製作模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Icebergs became white sticks and holographic paper that catch cold light. Orange and green cubes clad in corrugated card recall the harbour's metal containers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 冰山化為白色木棒與雷射紙，捕捉冷冽光線。包覆瓦楞紙的橘色與綠色方塊讓人想起港灣的金屬貨櫃。

sections.heading: Frozen Harbour - Taking a Game Map Apart and Rebuilding It by Hand
sections.body: The student took a snowy harbour map from a video game as a starting point, aiming to take its spaces apart and rebuild them by hand. The guidance first led the student to sketch elements such as the curved dome, lanes, cranes and containers one by one, then to arrange them into a composition of pure flat shapes, so that a virtual world was first reduced to its most basic geometry. In development, the flat design was translated into three dimensions through a careful choice of materials, with white and blue straws standing for water and silver and brown strips framing the crane, each material carrying a meaning. Finally, icebergs became white sticks and holographic paper catching cold light, while orange and green cubes clad in corrugated card recall the harbour's metal containers, so that a frozen landscape on a screen gains warmth in the hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 冰封港口-把遊戲地圖拆解再親手重建
zh-Hant.body: 學生以電子遊戲中的一張雪地港口地圖作為起點，目標是把其中的空間拆開，再親手重建。指導過程先引導學生把弧形穹頂、巷道、起重機與貨櫃等元素逐一草繪，再把它們安排成一幅純粹由平面形狀構成的構圖，讓虛擬的世界先被還原為最基本的幾何。進入推演，平面設計透過審慎的材料選擇轉譯為三維，白色與藍色吸管代表水面，銀色與棕色條板框出起重機，每一種材料都承擔一種意義。最後，冰山化為白色木棒與捕捉冷光的全息紙，覆上瓦楞紙板的橘色與綠色方塊，令人想起港口的金屬貨櫃，讓螢幕裡的冰封風景，在手中有了溫度。

pins.title: Parametric Morphogenesis
pins.description:
One free curve is copied, scaled and rotated in a script until it grows into a flowing tower.

Digital design | Parametric form | 3D modelling and visual scripting | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 參數化形態生成
zh-Hant.description:
一條自由曲線經程式複製、縮放與旋轉，逐步長成流動的塔。

數位設計｜參數化造型｜3D建模與視覺化程式｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how a single simple line can grow into a complex 3D structure. It is a first step into designing with rules instead of drawing every shape by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專案探討一條簡單的線如何長成複雜的立體結構。這是以規則設計、而非手繪每個造型的第一步。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student tested three basic moves on the curve: array, scale and rotate. Each move changed how the copies stacked into layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在曲線上測試三種基本操作：陣列、縮放與旋轉。每種操作都改變了複本堆疊成層的方式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A visual script links the steps, so changing one value updates the whole form. Loft, extrude and contour with pipe turned the layers into surfaces and lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 視覺化程式串連各個步驟，改動一個數值就能更新整個造型。放樣、擠出與等高線加管線把層次轉為曲面與線條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower flares at the base and splits into two peaks at the top. Its contour lines show form, structure and visual complexity under one set of rules.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔在底部展開，頂端分成兩座峰。它的等高線在同一組規則下呈現造型、結構與視覺的複雜度。

sections.heading: Parametric Morphogenesis - From a Single Line to a Tower
sections.body: The project asks how a single simple line can grow into a complex three-dimensional structure, a first step toward designing with rules instead of drawing every shape by hand. The guidance first led the student to test three basic moves on the curve, array, scale and rotate, observing how each changed the way the copies stacked into layers, so that the effect of every rule was first seen clearly. In development, a visual script linked the steps so that changing one value updates the whole form, and loft, extrude and contour with pipe turned the layers into surfaces and lines, the form growing freely among the parameters. Finally, the tower flares at its base and splits into two peaks at the top, its contour lines showing form, structure and visual complexity under one set of rules, so that a thin line climbs into a tower that seems alive.

zh-Hant.heading: 參數化形態生成-從一條線長成一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品追問：一條簡單的線，如何生長為複雜的立體結構？它是以規則設計、而非逐一手繪每個形狀的第一步。指導過程先引導學生在曲線上測試陣列、縮放與旋轉三種基本操作，觀察每一種如何改變複本堆疊成層的方式，讓規則的效果先被一一看清。進入推演，視覺化程式串連各個步驟，改變一個數值便能更新整個形體，放樣、擠出與等高線加管線，把層次轉化為曲面與線條，形態在參數之間自由生長。最後，高塔在底部擴張，頂端分裂為兩座峰，等高線在同一套規則之下呈現形態、結構與視覺的複雜，讓一條細線，攀升為一座有生命的塔。

pins.title: Stones & Habitats
pins.description:
Beach stones are studied one by one, then rebuilt into a coastal landscape where people and nature share the shore.

Model making | Landscape and ecology | Wax, wooden sticks, stones, plaster cloth, clay and plants | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 石與棲地
zh-Hant.description:
逐一研究海灘上的石頭，再重組成人與自然共享海岸的濱海地景。

模型製作｜地景與生態｜蠟、木棒、石頭、石膏布、黏土與植物｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student asked how stones on a beach could become new natural habitats. The aim was to design a shore that supports both people and wildlife.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生思考海灘上的石頭如何成為新的自然棲地。目標是設計一處同時支持人與野生生物的海岸。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Stones were collected and logged by size, hardness, roughness and porosity. Sketches then explored how stones, terrain and waves move and trade materials along the coast.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集石頭，並記錄其大小、硬度、粗糙度與孔隙。草圖接著探討石頭、地形與海浪如何沿著海岸移動與交換物質。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: 3D studies combined stones with water, plants, paths and structures. The terrain was then shaped with clay and plaster cloth, and stones, wire and boards were arranged on top.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 立體研究把石頭與水、植物、步道與構造物結合。接著以黏土與石膏布塑造地形，並在上方安排石頭、金屬線與木板。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model mixes rock caves, planted terraces and steps that lead down to the water. Small figures show how people can rest and walk while the stones keep giving shelter to life.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型融合岩洞、植栽平台與通往水邊的階梯。小人偶呈現人們如何休憩與散步，而石頭持續為生物提供庇護。

sections.heading: Stones and Habitats - Letting Shore Stones Become New Homes
sections.body: The student asked how stones on a beach could become new natural habitats, aiming for a shore that supports both people and wildlife. The guidance first led the student to collect stones and log each by size, hardness, roughness and porosity, then to explore in sketches how stones, terrain and waves move and exchange material along the coast, so that a handful of stones first became a field of study. In development, three-dimensional studies combined stones with water, plants, paths and structures, and the terrain was then shaped with clay and plaster cloth, with stones, wire and boards arranged on top in turn. Finally, the model mixes rock caves, planted terraces and steps leading down to the water, and small figures show people resting and walking while the stones keep sheltering life, so that a single shoreline becomes a home for people and creatures alike.

zh-Hant.heading: 石與棲地-讓海岸的石頭成為新的家
zh-Hant.body: 學生追問：海灘上的石頭，如何成為新的自然棲地？目標是設計一道同時支持人與野生生物的海岸。指導過程先引導學生蒐集石頭，依大小、硬度、粗糙度與孔隙逐一記錄，再以草圖探索石頭、地形與海浪如何沿著海岸移動、交換物質，讓一塊塊石頭先成為一門學問。進入推演，立體研究把石頭與水、植物、步道與構造物結合，地形再以黏土與石膏布塑形，石頭、鐵絲與板材依序安放其上。最後，模型混合了岩洞、植栽的階地與通往水邊的台階，小人偶顯示人們如何在此休息、漫步，石頭則持續為生命提供庇護，讓一道海岸，同時成為人與萬物的居所。

pins.title: Geometry in Flux
pins.description:
Pure concrete geometry meets free-flowing metal curves in one model joined by corridors.

Model making | Form and structure | Plywood, steel wire, concrete, iron mesh and metal-effect film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動中的幾何
zh-Hant.description:
純粹的混凝土幾何與自由流動的金屬曲線，在一座以廊道相連的模型中相遇。

模型製作｜造型與結構｜夾板、鋼線、混凝土、鐵網與金屬質感膜｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished concrete and metal model.
完成的混凝土與金屬模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wondered what happens when strict concrete geometry and free metal curves meet. The aim was to merge two opposite design languages without simply placing them side by side.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生好奇嚴謹的混凝土幾何與自由的金屬曲線相遇時會發生什麼。目標是融合兩種對立的設計語言，而非只是把它們並置。
captions: 從實體幾何中提取的形狀。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two precedents were studied, one for its solid cut-out forms and one for its flowing metal skins. Sketches pulled out basic shapes and simplified the curves into layers.
captions: The two precedent buildings: a concrete parliament and a metal-clad concert hall.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究兩個先例，一個著重實體挖孔造型，一個著重流動的金屬表皮。草圖提取基本形狀，並把曲線簡化成層次。
captions: 兩個參考建築：混凝土國會建築與金屬外覆的音樂廳。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A watercolour tested how corridors could tie the solid pieces to the flowing parts. Concrete rings were then cast and joined with plywood, wire and metal film.
captions: Casting the concrete rings by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 水彩畫測試廊道如何把實體部分與流動部分串連。接著澆鑄混凝土環，並以夾板、金屬線與金屬膜結合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets a pierced concrete drum on timber stilts beside a ring-topped tower. Corridors and curved metal roofs link them into one walkable piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把穿孔的混凝土圓筒架在木支柱上，旁邊是頂部有圓環的塔。廊道與彎曲的金屬屋頂把它們連成一個可穿行的整體。

sections.heading: Geometry in Flux - Where Concrete Meets Metal
sections.body: The student wondered what happens when strict concrete geometry meets free metal curves, aiming to merge two opposite design languages rather than simply placing them side by side. The guidance first led the student to study two precedents, one known for solid cut-out forms and one for flowing metal skins, then to pull basic shapes from them in sketches and simplify the curves into layers, so that opposing vocabularies first found a common unit. In development, a watercolour tested how corridors could tie the solid pieces to the flowing parts, and concrete rings were then cast and joined with plywood, wire and metal film. Finally, the model sets a pierced concrete drum on timber stilts beside a ring-topped tower, with corridors and curved metal roofs linking them into one walkable piece, so that hardness and softness shake hands in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 流動的幾何-混凝土與金屬的相遇
zh-Hant.body: 學生好奇，當嚴謹的混凝土幾何與自由的金屬曲線相遇，會發生什麼？目標是融合兩種相反的設計語言，而非只是把它們並置。指導過程先引導學生研究兩個先例，一個以厚實的挖空形體著稱，一個以流動的金屬表皮聞名，再以草圖提取基本形狀，把曲線簡化為層次，讓對立的語彙先找到共同的單位。進入推演，一幅水彩測試廊道如何把實體的部分與流動的部分繫在一起，接著澆鑄混凝土環，並以合板、鐵絲與金屬膜相互接合。最後，模型讓一座穿孔的混凝土圓筒立於木樁之上，旁邊是一座環形頂的高塔，廊道與彎曲的金屬屋頂把它們串成一件可以行走的作品，讓剛與柔，在空間中握手。

pins.title: Movement & Form
pins.description:
The paths of two dancers become a tower of wooden strips and red and blue rods.

Model making | Movement and space | Wooden sticks and plastic rods | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 動態與形體
zh-Hant.description:
兩位舞者的軌跡，化為一座由木條與紅藍塑膠棒構成的塔。

模型製作｜動態與空間｜木棒與塑膠棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student asked how the movement of dancing bodies could become a 3D space. The goal was a sculptural model that feels like a fluid dance space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生思考舞動身體的動作如何成為立體空間。目標是一座讓人感受到流動舞蹈空間的雕塑模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Figure sketches marked joints and turns as dots and arcs. One path was then pulled out on its own to study its shape.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 人物草圖把關節與轉身標記成點與弧線。接著單獨抽出一條軌跡，研究它的形狀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Single trajectories were built in 3D software, then combined, rotated and stretched into one drawing. Wooden strips set the frame and red and blue rods traced the two dancers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 單一軌跡先在3D軟體中建立，再組合、旋轉與拉伸成一張圖。木條定出框架，紅藍棒材描繪兩位舞者。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model merges structure and motion into one expressive form with foil nodes at the joints. The fabric base records the dancers' shadows and extended paths.
captions: Shadows drawn on the fabric base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以關節處的鋁箔節點，把結構與動態融為一個有表現力的形體。布面底座記錄舞者的影子與延伸的軌跡。
captions: 畫在布面底座上的影子。

sections.heading: Movement and Form - The Paths of a Duet Turned into Space
sections.body: The student asked how dancing bodies in motion could become a three-dimensional space, aiming for a sculptural model that feels like a fluid space for dance. The guidance first led the student to mark joints and turns as dots and arcs in figure sketches, then to pull one path out on its own to study its shape, so that intricate movement was first distilled into clear lines. In development, single trajectories were built in 3D software and then combined, rotated and stretched into one drawing, wooden strips set the frame, and red and blue rods traced the two dancers, structure and motion winding around each other. Finally, the model merges structure and movement into one expressive form with foil nodes at the joints, while its fabric base records the dancers' shadows and extended paths, so that a vanished duet leaves behind a shape one can touch.

zh-Hant.heading: 動態與形體-雙人舞的軌跡化為空間
zh-Hant.body: 學生追問：舞動的身體，如何成為三維的空間？目標是一件讓人感覺像流動舞蹈空間的雕塑模型。指導過程先引導學生以人體速寫，把關節與轉身標記為點與弧線，再單獨抽出其中一條路徑研究它的形狀，讓繁複的舞姿先被提煉為清晰的線。進入推演，單一軌跡在3D軟體中建立，再組合、旋轉與拉伸為一幅圖，木條定出框架，紅色與藍色細桿分別描出兩位舞者，結構與動作在此相互纏繞。最後，模型把結構與動作融為一個富表現力的形體，關節處以鋁箔節點標示，布質底座記錄舞者的影子與延伸的路徑，讓一段消逝的雙人舞，留下了可以觸摸的形狀。

pins.title: Dog Hill
pins.description:
A soft hill with caves and holes gives dogs and people a shared place to play.

Model making | Landscape and habitat | Clay, pebbles, grass powder and artificial plants | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 狗狗山丘
zh-Hant.description:
一座有洞穴與孔洞的柔和山丘，讓狗與人有共享的遊憩場所。

模型製作｜地景與棲地｜黏土、卵石、草粉與人造植物｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Close-up of the hill with a figure and dog.
人偶與狗在山丘旁的近景。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted a landscape where dogs and their owners can share space. The question was how terrain itself could invite play, rest and hiding.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想打造一處讓狗與飼主共享的地景。問題是地形本身如何引發遊戲、休息與躲藏。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student mapped how dogs move, sniff and stop along a route. These notes became a plan of paths and resting spots.
captions: Inspiration board with notes, dog-treat shapes and cave references.
Map of dog routes and stops.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪狗沿路移動、嗅聞與停留的方式。這些筆記成為步道與休息點的平面。
captions: 包含筆記、狗零食造型與洞穴參考的靈感板。
狗狗路線與停留點的地圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Soft mounds were modelled in 3D to test sizes and openings. The forms were then built as hollow clay shells and given a rough stone texture.
captions: The shell with a rough texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以3D建立柔和的土丘，測試尺度與開口。接著把造型做成中空黏土殼，並加上粗糙的石材質感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final hill is full of caves and holes framed by grass, flowers and trees. Small figures of a person and a dog show how the hill is shared.
captions: Top view of the whole site.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的山丘布滿洞穴與孔洞，四周是草地、花與樹。人與狗的小人偶呈現山丘如何被共享。

sections.heading: Dog Hill - Terrain That Invites Play and Hiding
sections.body: The student wanted a landscape where dogs and their owners could share space, and the question was how terrain itself could invite play, rest and hiding. The guidance first led the student to record how dogs move, sniff and stop along a route, then to turn these notes into a plan of paths and resting spots, so that animal behaviour first became the basis of the design. In development, soft mounds were modelled in 3D to test sizes and openings, then built as hollow clay shells and given a rough stone texture, the form realised step by step between the digital and the handmade. Finally, the hill is full of caves and holes framed by grass, flowers and trees, and small figures of a person and a dog show how it is shared, so that a piece of terrain becomes a playground where people and dogs run together.

zh-Hant.heading: 狗狗山丘-讓地形邀請嬉戲與躲藏
zh-Hant.body: 學生想設計一片讓狗與主人共享的地景。問題是：地形本身，如何邀請嬉戲、休息與躲藏？指導過程先引導學生記錄狗沿著路線如何移動、嗅聞與停留，再把這些筆記轉化為一張路徑與休憩點的平面，讓動物的行為先成為設計的依據。進入推演，柔和的土丘以3D建模測試大小與開口，再以中空的黏土殼體建構，並賦予粗糙的石材質感，形態在數位與手作之間逐步落實。最後，山丘布滿洞穴與孔洞，四周環繞青草、花朵與樹木，一個人與一隻狗的小人偶顯示這座山丘如何被共享，讓一片地形，成為人與狗一起奔跑的樂園。

pins.title: Silk Road
pins.description:
The lightness of silk is turned into a floating frame of woven curves.

Model making | Culture and material | PLA, acrylic, hot-melt glue and silk | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 絲路
zh-Hant.description:
把絲的輕盈轉化為一座由編織曲線構成的漂浮框架。

模型製作｜文化與材料｜PLA、壓克力、熱熔膠與絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was moved by the ancient trade route and the silk carried along it. The question was how the lightness and weave of silk could become architecture.
captions: A collage of Silk Road travellers and trade scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被古老的貿易路線與沿途運送的絲綢所觸動。問題是絲的輕盈與編織如何成為建築。
captions: 絲路旅人與貿易場景的拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Crumpled silk was photographed to study folds and light. Line sketches then traced how threads loop and overlap.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拍攝揉皺的絲，研究皺褶與光線。線條草圖接著描繪絲線如何環繞與重疊。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Printed frames were tested with silk fibres and hot-melt glue. A sequence of digital steps grew a single loop into a layered curve frame.
captions: Steps from loop to layered form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以絲纖維與熱熔膠測試列印框架。一連串數位步驟把單一環形發展成層狀曲線框架。
captions: 從環形到層狀造型的步驟。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final work is a flowing curve frame that seems to float like a silk thread. It links craft, material and space as a dialogue between cultures.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終作品是一座彷彿絲線般漂浮的流動曲線框架。它把工藝、材料與空間連結成一場文化之間的對話。

sections.heading: Silk Road - Weaving a Dialogue Between Cultures from a Single Thread
sections.body: The ancient trade route and the silk carried along it moved the student deeply, and the question was how the lightness and weave of silk could become architecture. The guidance first led the student to photograph crumpled silk to study its folds and light, then to trace in line sketches how threads loop and overlap, so that a sense of touch was first translated into a form that could be read. In development, printed frames were tested with silk fibres and hot-melt glue, and a sequence of digital steps grew a single loop into a layered curved frame, craft and computation extending each other. Finally, the work becomes a flowing curved frame that seems to float like a silk thread, linking craft, material and space as a dialogue between cultures, so that a road of many centuries is travelled again through gentle lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 絲路-以一縷絲線編織文化的對話
zh-Hant.body: 古老的貿易之路與沿途運送的絲綢，深深觸動了學生。問題是：絲的輕盈與編織，如何成為建築？指導過程先引導學生拍攝揉皺的絲綢，研究褶皺與光線，再以線條草圖描繪絲線如何繞圈、交疊，讓一種觸感先被轉譯為可以閱讀的形態。進入推演，列印的框架與絲纖維、熱熔膠一同測試，一連串數位步驟讓單一的線圈，生長為層層疊合的曲線框架，手工與數位在此彼此延伸。最後，作品成為一道流動的曲線框架，彷彿一縷絲線般漂浮，把工藝、材料與空間串連為文化之間的對話，讓一條千年的道路，在輕柔的線條中重新被走過。

pins.title: Civic Stage: Performing Arts Complex
pins.description:
A parking lot becomes an arts complex of stacked blocks and a spherical theatre.

Digital design | Urban architecture | 3D modelling, rendering and watercolour | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市舞台：表演藝術綜合體
zh-Hant.description:
一座停車場化身為由堆疊量體與球形劇場組成的藝術綜合體。

數位設計｜城市建築｜3D建模、算圖與水彩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project turns a city parking lot into a complex for the arts, culture and learning. It asks how one building can bring students, artists and the public together.
captions: Site photos and movement maps of the parking-lot site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專案把城市停車場改造成藝術、文化與學習的綜合體。它探討一座建築如何讓學生、藝術家與大眾聚在一起。
captions: 停車場基地的照片與動線地圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied land use, routes and street life around the site. Simple block moves such as shifting, lifting and cutting were then tested.
captions: Massing steps from block to cluster.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究基地周邊的土地使用、動線與街道生活。接著測試平移、抬升與切割等簡單的量體操作。
captions: 從方塊到群組的量體步驟。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Four programmes were given their own blocks and colours: an academy, a civic hall, an innovation hub and a theatre. They were stacked so their edges overlap and open onto shared spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 四種機能各自分配量體與顏色：學院、市民空間、創新中心與劇場。它們互相堆疊，讓邊緣重疊並通往共享空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Renders show a raised performance deck and a spherical theatre forming a strong public landmark. A watercolour adds daylight and people to show an open, walkable arts campus.
captions: Front view of the arrival deck.
Street view with the theatre sphere.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 算圖呈現抬高的表演平台與球形劇場構成鮮明的公共地標。水彩畫加入日光與人群，表現開放、適合步行的藝術園區。

sections.heading: Civic Stage - Turning a Parking Lot into a Gathering of the Arts
sections.body: The project turns a city parking lot into a complex for the arts, culture and learning, asking how one building can bring students, artists and the public together. The guidance first led the student to study land use, routes and street life around the site, then to test simple massing moves such as shifting, lifting and cutting, so that the context of the city first set the starting point of the form. In development, four programmes each received their own block and colour, an academy, a civic hall, an innovation hub and a theatre, stacked so that their edges overlap and open onto shared spaces. Finally, renders show a raised performance deck and a spherical theatre forming a strong public landmark, while a watercolour adds daylight and people to picture an open, walkable arts campus, so that an empty lot in the city becomes a stage on which everyone may appear.

zh-Hant.heading: 市民舞台-把停車場變成藝術的聚落
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品把城市裡的一座停車場，轉化為一座結合藝術、文化與學習的綜合體。它追問：一棟建築如何把學生、藝術家與大眾聚在一起？指導過程先引導學生研究基地周邊的土地使用、動線與街道生活，再測試錯動、抬升與切割等簡單的量體操作，讓城市的脈絡先決定形體的起點。進入推演，四種機能各自獲得量體與色彩，學院、市民廳、創新中心與劇場相互堆疊，邊緣彼此重疊，向共享的空間敞開。最後，渲染圖呈現抬升的表演平台與球形劇場，構成鮮明的公共地標，一幅水彩則加入日光與人群，描繪一座開放、可漫步的藝術校園，讓城市的空地，成為眾人登場的舞台。

pins.title: Emerging Eco-Architecture
pins.description:
Square wooden frames climb a rocky slope like a structure growing out of the land.

Model making | Architecture and nature | Wooden strips, white board and gravel | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 浮現的生態建築
zh-Hant.description:
方形木框沿著岩坡攀升，彷彿從大地長出的結構。

模型製作｜建築與自然｜木條、白板與碎石｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished frame structure on gravel.
碎石上完成的框架結構。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was struck by recent natural disasters and saw them as a sign of nature under stress. The question was whether architecture could help restore balance between people and land.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被近年的天然災害所觸動，視之為自然承受壓力的訊號。問題是建築能否幫助恢復人與土地之間的平衡。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two precedents were studied for how they blend with landscape and use repeated modules. Sketches turned these ideas into crossing frames.
captions: Two architects studied for buildings that blend with nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究兩個先例如何融入地景並運用重複模組。草圖把這些概念轉化為交錯的框架。
captions: 為與自然融合的建築而研究的兩位建築師。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small cube frames were made as concept modules. They were then stacked along a slope so the structure seems to rise from the rock.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生製作小型立方框架作為概念模組。接著沿坡堆疊，使結構彷彿從岩石中升起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model uses square frames as structure and slopes to create porosity. Flat platforms woven between them act as public spaces that grow from the rocky ground.
captions: Side view on the white base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以方形框架為結構，並以坡度創造孔隙。穿插其間的平台成為從岩地長出的公共空間。

sections.heading: Emerging Eco-Architecture - Frames Rising from a Rocky Slope
sections.body: Recent natural disasters struck the student as a sign of nature under stress, and the question was whether architecture could help restore balance between people and land. The guidance first led the student to study two precedents for how they blend with landscape and use repeated modules, then to turn these ideas into crossing frames through sketching, so that concern for nature first found a structural language that could touch the ground. In development, the student made small cube frames as concept modules and stacked them along a slope so that the structure seems to rise from the rock, the repetition of units becoming a way of speaking with the terrain. Finally, the model uses square frames as structure and slopes to create porosity, with flat platforms woven between them as public spaces growing from the rocky ground, so that architecture no longer presses upon the land but grows along with it.

zh-Hant.heading: 新生生態建築-從岩坡長出的框架
zh-Hant.body: 近年的天然災害觸動了學生，視之為自然承受壓力的訊號。問題是：建築能否幫助恢復人與土地之間的平衡？指導過程先引導學生研究兩個先例，觀察它們如何融入地景、運用重複的模組，再以草圖把這些概念轉化為交錯的框架，讓一份對自然的關懷，先找到可以落地的結構語言。進入推演，學生製作小型立方框架作為概念模組，再沿著坡地堆疊，讓結構彷彿從岩石中升起，單元的重複成為與地形對話的方式。最後，模型以方形框架為結構，以坡度創造孔隙，穿插其間的平台化為從岩地長出的公共空間，讓建築不再壓在土地之上，而是與它一同生長。

pins.title: Streamlined High-rise
pins.description:
A stack of distorted ellipses grows into a porous, layered tower through a visual script.

Digital design | Parametric tower | Visual scripting and 3D modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流線高層建築
zh-Hant.description:
一疊變形的橢圓透過視覺化程式長成多孔、層疊的塔。

數位設計｜參數化高塔｜視覺化程式與3D建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explores how rules can shape a high-rise instead of drawing it by hand. It asks whether simple geometry can produce an organic, flowing tower skin.
captions: Ellipse array, mapping and random scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專案探討如何以規則而非手繪來塑造高樓。它思考簡單的幾何能否產生有機、流動的塔樓表皮。
captions: 橢圓陣列、映射與隨機縮放。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A single ellipse was arrayed upward, then distorted with mapping and random scaling. Surfaces and colours were added to preview the stack.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 單一橢圓向上陣列，再以映射與隨機縮放加以變形。學生加上曲面與顏色來預覽堆疊效果。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A visual script links every step so one change updates the whole tower. The curves were rebuilt, lofted, subdivided into a mesh and merged into two layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 視覺化程式串連每個步驟，改動一處就更新整座塔。曲線經過重建、放樣、細分成網格，再合併成兩層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower reads like layers of rock built up over time. It shows how a clear digital workflow can lead to expressive yet buildable facades.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔看起來像長年堆積的岩層。它展示清楚的數位流程如何帶來有表現力又可建造的立面。

sections.heading: Streamlined High-Rise - A Skin Grown by Rules like Layers of Rock
sections.body: The project explores how rules, rather than hand drawing, can shape a high-rise, asking whether simple geometry can produce an organic, flowing tower skin. The guidance first led the student to array a single ellipse upward and distort it through mapping and random scaling, then to add surfaces and colours to preview the stack, so that one curve first grew layers within a set of rules. In development, a visual script linked every step so that a single change updates the whole tower, and the curves were rebuilt, lofted, subdivided into a mesh and merged into two layers, the clarity of the logic setting the form free. Finally, the tower reads like layers of rock built up over time, showing how a clear digital workflow can lead to facades that are both expressive and buildable, so that rational steps arrive at an almost natural elegance.

zh-Hant.heading: 流線高樓-以規則長出岩層般的表皮
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品探索如何以規則塑造一棟高樓，而非逐筆手繪。它追問：簡單的幾何，能否生成有機而流動的塔樓表皮？指導過程先引導學生把單一橢圓向上陣列，再以映射與隨機縮放加以扭曲，並加上曲面與色彩預覽堆疊的效果，讓一條曲線先在規則中長出層次。進入推演，視覺化程式串連每一個步驟，一處改變便能更新整座高塔，曲線經過重建、放樣，細分為網格，再合併成兩層表皮，邏輯的清晰讓形態得以自由。最後，高塔讀來如同隨時間堆積而成的岩層，顯示清楚的數位流程如何引向既富表現力又可建造的立面，讓理性的步驟，成就一份近乎自然的優雅。

pins.title: Material Regeneration
pins.description:
Plastic bags, bamboo chopsticks and old mesh are knotted into a new woven surface.

Model making | Material reuse | Plastic bags, bamboo chopsticks, iron mesh and hemp rope | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 材料再生
zh-Hant.description:
塑膠袋、竹筷與舊網片被打結編織成全新的表面。

模型製作｜材料再利用｜塑膠袋、竹筷、鐵網與麻繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Everyday waste such as plastic bags and old mesh is usually thrown away after one use. The project asks how these overlooked materials could gain a second life as a new building surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠袋與舊網片等日常廢棄物通常用過一次就被丟棄。這個專案思考這些被忽略的材料，如何以新的建築表面重獲第二次生命。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student collected common household waste and tested how it could be tied, wrapped and woven. Bamboo chopsticks became a light frame that could hold softer materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集常見的家庭廢棄物，測試如何綁、包與編織它們。竹筷成為能承載柔軟材料的輕巧框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plastic bags were stretched and knotted across the chopstick grid in several layers. Mesh strips and rope were woven in to add strength and texture.
captions: Plastic bags stretched over the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠袋被拉開並分層綁在竹筷格網上。網條與麻繩被編入其中，增加強度與質感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final panel is a light, translucent skin that shows waste in a new form. It also works as a teaching piece that invites neighbours to rethink what they throw away.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的板材是輕盈、半透明的表皮，以新形式呈現廢棄物。它也是一件教材，邀請鄰里重新思考自己丟掉的東西。

sections.heading: Material Regeneration - Weaving Waste into a New Skin
sections.body: Everyday waste such as plastic bags and old mesh is usually thrown away after a single use, and the project asked how these overlooked materials could gain a second life as a new building surface. The guidance first led the student to collect common household waste and test how it could be tied, wrapped and woven, then to discover that bamboo chopsticks could form a light frame able to hold softer materials, so that ordinary things first revealed their potential through experiment. In development, plastic bags were stretched and knotted across the chopstick grid in several layers, and mesh strips and rope were woven in to add strength and texture. Finally, the panel becomes a light, translucent skin that shows waste in a new form, and also a teaching piece inviting neighbours to rethink what they throw away, so that forgotten materials are seen once more.

zh-Hant.heading: 材料再生-讓廢棄物織成新的表皮
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠袋與舊網布等日常廢棄物，往往用過一次就被丟棄。這個作品追問：這些被忽略的材料，能否以新的建築表皮獲得第二次生命？指導過程先引導學生蒐集常見的家庭廢棄物，測試它們如何被綁、纏繞與編織，再發現竹筷可以成為輕巧的框架，承托較柔軟的材料，讓尋常之物先在實驗中顯露潛能。進入推演，塑膠袋被拉伸、打結，層層橫跨竹筷格網，網布條與繩索再被編入，增添強度與質感。最後，作品成為一片輕盈半透明的表皮，以新的形態呈現廢棄物，也成為一件教學作品，邀請鄰里重新思考自己丟掉的東西，讓被遺忘的材料，重新被看見。

pins.title: Urban Rain Garden
pins.description:
A terrain model shows rainwater cleaned in four steps as it flows to a pond.

Model making | Landscape and water | Foam, clay, sand, stone, wax and model plants | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市雨水花園
zh-Hant.description:
一座地形模型呈現雨水流向水池時經過的四道淨化步驟。

模型製作｜地景與水｜泡棉、黏土、沙、石頭、蠟與模型植物｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cities face heavier storms and flooding as the climate changes. The student asked how a garden could hold, clean and reuse rainwater while staying pleasant for people.
captions: Photos of the rain garden that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷讓城市面對更強的暴雨與淹水。學生思考一座花園如何留住、淨化並再利用雨水，同時讓人感到舒適。
captions: 啟發本案的雨水花園照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A site visit to a terraced park wetland showed how stepped pools slow water down. The student sketched the flow from street runoff through filters to a retention pool.
captions: Hand sketch of the water path.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 實地走訪一座階梯式公園濕地，看見層層水池如何減緩水流。學生畫出雨水從街道逕流、經過過濾到滯留池的路徑。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The landform was carved from foam, then covered with clay and sand for texture. Stones of different sizes, wax water and white tubes showed each cleaning stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 地形以泡棉雕出，再覆上黏土與沙增加質感。不同大小的石頭、蠟製水面與白色管線呈現每一道淨化階段。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model reads as a section of sedimentation, plant filter, gravel filter and pond. It shows how a park can work like a sponge while also offering a green place to rest.
captions: Detail of the gravel and pond.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型以剖面呈現沉澱、植物過濾、礫石過濾與水池。它展示公園如何像海綿一樣運作，同時提供可休憩的綠地。

sections.heading: Urban Rain Garden - A Park That Breathes like a Sponge
sections.body: Cities face heavier storms and flooding as the climate changes, and the student asked how a garden could hold, clean and reuse rainwater while remaining pleasant for people. The guidance first led the student to visit a terraced park wetland and observe how stepped pools slow the water, then to sketch its path from street runoff through filters into a retention pool, so that an invisible water cycle first became a clear drawing. In development, the landform was carved from foam and covered with clay and sand for texture, while stones of different sizes, wax water and white tubes showed each stage of cleaning. Finally, the model reads as a section unfolding through sedimentation, plant filter, gravel filter and pond, showing how a park can work like a sponge while offering a green place to rest, so that every rainfall is received gently.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市雨水花園-讓公園像海綿一樣呼吸
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷，讓城市面對更猛烈的暴雨與淹水。學生追問：一座花園如何蓄留、淨化並再利用雨水，同時仍讓人感到愉悅？指導過程先引導學生走訪一座梯田式公園濕地，觀察階梯狀的水池如何減緩水流，再草繪雨水從街道逕流、經過過濾、流入滯留池的路徑，讓看不見的水循環先成為一張清晰的圖。進入推演，地形以泡棉雕刻，覆上黏土與沙增加質感，大小不一的石頭、蠟製的水與白色管子，分別呈現每一道淨化的階段。最後，模型讀來如一幅剖面，依序展開沉澱、植物過濾、礫石過濾與水塘，顯示公園如何像海綿般運作，又提供一處綠意的休憩之所，讓每一場雨，都被溫柔地收下。

pins.title: Shared Kitchen
pins.description:
Stackable kitchen modules grow from a single dining unit into a community hub.

Model making | Community space | PLA frames, wooden sticks, resin prints and laser cutting | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 共享廚房
zh-Hant.description:
可堆疊的廚房模組，從單一用餐單元長成社區據點。

模型製作｜社區空間｜PLA框架、木棒、樹脂列印與雷射切割｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cooking and eating together is one of the easiest ways for neighbours to meet. The project asks how a kitchen could become a flexible social space for communities of any size.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一起煮飯吃飯是鄰居相遇最自然的方式之一。這個專案思考廚房如何成為適合不同規模社區的彈性社交空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student treated everyday activities as social moments and studied how dining, teaching and workshops could share one space. A single module was sized for a small neighbourhood meal.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把日常活動視為社交時刻，研究用餐、教學與工作坊如何共用空間。單一模組的尺度適合小型鄰里聚餐。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Black frames were printed and filled with timber floors, slatted screens and white furniture. Modules were stacked and shifted to test larger kitchens and movable units.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生列印黑色框架，再放入木地板、格柵屏風與白色家具。模組被堆疊與錯位，測試更大的廚房與可移動單元。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stacks modules into a stepped community kitchen with stairs and terraces. It shows a building that can grow or shrink with the people who use it.
captions: Stairs and screens in a module.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把模組堆成有樓梯與平台的階梯式社區廚房。它展示一座能隨使用者增減而成長或縮小的建築。

sections.heading: Shared Kitchen - Modules That Gather Neighbours Around a Meal
sections.body: Cooking and eating together is one of the easiest ways for neighbours to meet, and the project asked how a kitchen could become a flexible social space for communities of any size. The guidance first led the student to treat everyday activities as social moments and study how dining, teaching and workshops could share one space, then to size a single module for a small neighbourhood meal, so that the gathering of people first set the scale of the space. In development, black frames were printed and filled with timber floors, slatted screens and white furniture, and modules were stacked and shifted to test larger kitchens and movable units. Finally, the model stacks modules into a stepped community kitchen with stairs and terraces, showing a building that can grow or shrink with the people who use it, so that a shared table becomes the heart of a community.

zh-Hant.heading: 共享廚房-以一頓飯連結鄰里的模組
zh-Hant.body: 一起煮飯、一起吃飯，是鄰居相識最容易的方式之一。這個作品追問：廚房如何成為一個可伸縮、適合任何規模社群的社交空間？指導過程先引導學生把日常活動視為社交的時刻，研究用餐、教學與工作坊如何共享同一個空間，再把單一模組的尺寸設定為一場小型鄰里聚餐，讓人的聚集先決定空間的大小。進入推演，黑色框架以列印製作，填入木地板、格柵屏風與白色家具，模組被堆疊、錯動，測試更大的廚房與可移動的單元。最後，模型把模組堆成一座階梯狀的社區廚房，配有樓梯與露台，展示一棟能隨使用者增減而生長或收縮的建築，讓一桌飯菜，成為社區的中心。

pins.title: Living Layers, Watching Streets
pins.description:
Shifting floor plates let residents on every level keep an eye on the street.

Model making | Housing and safety | PVC sheets and red figures | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 層層生活，守望街道
zh-Hant.description:
錯動的樓板讓每一層的住戶都能看顧街道。

模型製作｜住宅與安全｜PVC板與紅色人偶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Streets feel safer when people living nearby can see them. The project asks how a housing block could keep that link to the street across several floors.
captions: The book and author behind the idea of eyes on the street.
Front view of the floor plates.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 當附近居民看得見街道時，街道會更讓人安心。這個專案思考一棟住宅如何在好幾層樓之間維持與街道的連結。
captions: 「街道之眼」概念背後的書與作者。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student started from a well-known urban idea that residents watching from home keep streets safe. That effect fades above a few storeys, so height and openness became the key questions.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從一個知名的城市觀念出發：居民在家中看著街道，就能讓街道更安全。這種效果在幾層樓以上會減弱，所以高度與開放性成為關鍵。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin PVC plates were staggered and held by short vertical partitions. Red figures were placed at edges and terraces to test where people could look out.
captions: A figure at the floor edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 薄PVC樓板被錯開排列，以短隔牆支撐。紅色人偶放在邊緣與平台上，測試人們能從哪裡往外看。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final towers turn every level into a lookout while keeping private corners. They show how small choices in floor layout can shape a sense of safety.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔樓讓每一層都成為瞭望點，同時保留私密角落。它們展示樓層配置上的小選擇如何影響安全感。

sections.heading: Living Layers - Letting Every Floor Keep Watch over the Street
sections.body: Streets feel safer when people living nearby can see them, and the project asked how a housing block could keep that link to the street across several floors. The guidance first led the student to start from a well-known urban idea that residents watching from home keep streets safe, and then to find that this effect fades above a few storeys, so that height and openness became the key questions. In development, thin PVC plates were staggered and held by short vertical partitions, and red figures were placed at edges and terraces to test where people could look out, sightlines becoming the measure of the design. Finally, the towers turn every level into a lookout while keeping private corners, showing how small choices in floor layout can shape a sense of safety, so that the watchfulness of a city reaches higher than before.

zh-Hant.heading: 層層而居-讓每一層樓都看得見街道
zh-Hant.body: 當附近的居民看得見街道，街道便感覺更安全。這個作品追問：一棟住宅如何在好幾層樓之間，維持與街道的連結？指導過程先引導學生從一個著名的城市理念出發，即居民在家中的守望讓街道安全，再發現這種效果在數層樓以上便會消退，讓高度與開放成為關鍵的問題。進入推演，細薄的PVC板錯落堆疊，以短短的垂直隔牆支撐，紅色人偶被放在邊緣與露台上，測試人們能從哪裡向外眺望，視線成為設計的度量。最後，高塔讓每一層都成為瞭望之處，同時保留私密的角落，顯示樓層配置上的小小選擇，如何塑造一份安全感，讓城市的守望，延伸到更高的地方。

pins.title: Passive Facade
pins.description:
Layered timber strips shade, cool and quiet the rooms behind them.

Model making | Facade and climate | Wooden sticks and laser-cut panels | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 被動式立面
zh-Hant.description:
層疊的木條為後方的房間遮陽、降溫並隔音。

模型製作｜立面與氣候｜木棒與雷射切割板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Large glass walls let in too much sun and noise, so buildings rely on air conditioning. The project asks whether a facade itself could control light, heat and sound.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 大面玻璃牆引入過多陽光與噪音，使建築依賴空調。這個專案思考立面本身能否調節光線、熱與聲音。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how layered surfaces filter sunlight and scatter sound waves. Cutting diagrams were drawn in software for every floor and strip.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究層疊表面如何過濾陽光並分散聲波。每一層樓與每根木條都以軟體繪製切割圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin strips were laser-cut, assembled in a staggered sequence and lightly sanded. Light tests showed soft patterns falling across the floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 細木條經雷射切割，依錯落順序組裝並輕輕打磨。光線測試呈現灑落在樓板上的柔和圖案。
captions: 灑在地板上的過濾光線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model shows a rough, deep facade that shades rooms and breaks up noise. It treats beauty and comfort as one goal rather than two.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型呈現粗糙而有深度的立面，為室內遮陽並打散噪音。它把美感與舒適視為同一個目標。

sections.heading: Passive Facade - A Skin That Tempers Light and Sound on Its Own
sections.body: Large glass walls let in too much sun and noise, leaving buildings dependent on air conditioning, and the project asked whether a facade itself could control light, heat and sound. The guidance first led the student to study how layered surfaces filter sunlight and scatter sound waves, and then to draw cutting diagrams in software for every floor and every strip, so that environmental principles first became precise components. In development, thin strips were laser cut, assembled in a staggered sequence and lightly sanded, and light tests showed soft patterns falling across the floors, performance and beauty emerging together through experiment. Finally, the model shows a rough, deep facade that shades rooms and breaks up noise, treating beauty and comfort as one goal rather than two, so that the skin of a building learns to breathe quietly.

zh-Hant.heading: 被動式立面-讓表皮自己調節光與聲
zh-Hant.body: 大片玻璃牆引入過多的陽光與噪音，讓建築依賴空調。這個作品追問：立面本身，能否控制光、熱與聲音？指導過程先引導學生研究層疊的表面如何過濾陽光、散射聲波，再以軟體為每一層樓、每一根木條繪製切割圖，讓環境的原理先轉化為精確的構件。進入推演，細木條經雷射切割，以錯落的順序組裝並輕輕打磨，光線測試則顯示柔和的圖案落在各層樓板上，性能與美感在實驗中同時浮現。最後，模型呈現一道粗糙而深邃的立面，為房間遮陽並打散噪音，把美與舒適視為同一個目標而非兩件事，讓建築的表皮，學會安靜地呼吸。

pins.title: Big Bang Constellation
pins.description:
Star patterns become stick-and-plaster forms that merge into one expanding cluster.

Model making | Form from data | Wooden sticks, plaster mix, hot glue and board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 大爆炸星座
zh-Hant.description:
星座圖形化為木棒與石膏造型，再融合成一個不斷擴張的星團。

模型製作｜從資料到造型｜木棒、石膏、熱熔膠與板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Star signs look flat in the sky, but the stars are really far apart in space. The student asked what these patterns would look like as real 3D forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 星座在天空中看起來是平的，但星星在宇宙中其實相距遙遠。學生思考這些圖形若成為真實的立體造型會是什麼樣子。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The twelve star signs were mapped and each one was modelled digitally. The forms were then placed back on the chart to check their links.
captions: A chart of the star signs.
Digital forms placed on the chart.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生整理十二星座，並逐一以數位方式建模。接著把造型放回星圖上，檢查它們之間的關係。
captions: 放在星圖上的數位造型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Signs were combined in groups to invent new constellations built from sticks and plaster panels. The stages were then merged, with card used to suggest the shielding of an expanding universe.
captions: Merging the stages step by step.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 星座被分組組合，以木棒與石膏板創造新的星座。各階段再被融合，並用紙板暗示不斷擴張的宇宙所產生的遮蔽。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final cluster grows outward like a living structure of triangles and struts. Its regular geometry means it could keep extending in any direction.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的星團像一座由三角形與支桿組成的生命體向外生長。規則的幾何讓它能朝任何方向持續延伸。

sections.heading: Big Bang - Constellations Stepping from the Night Sky into Three Dimensions
sections.body: Star signs look flat in the sky, yet their stars lie far apart in space, and the student asked what these patterns would look like as real three-dimensional forms. The guidance first led the student to map the twelve star signs and model each one digitally, then to place the forms back on the chart to check how they link, so that a distant sky was first brought within working reach. In development, signs were combined in groups to invent new constellations built from sticks and plaster panels, and the stages were then merged, with card suggesting the shielding of an expanding universe, imagination and geometry weaving together. Finally, the cluster grows outward like a living structure of triangles and struts, its regular geometry allowing it to keep extending in any direction, so that the story of a night sky goes on expanding in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 大爆炸-讓星座從夜空走進三維
zh-Hant.body: 星座在天空中看似平面，星星之間其實相隔遙遠。學生追問：這些圖案若成為真實的立體形態，會是什麼模樣？指導過程先引導學生繪出十二星座，並逐一以數位方式建模，再把這些形體放回星圖上，檢驗彼此的關聯，讓遙遠的星空先被拉回到可以操作的距離。進入推演，星座被分組組合，創造出以木棒與石膏板構成的新星座，各個階段再被合併，並以卡紙暗示一個膨脹中宇宙的屏障，想像與幾何在此交織。最後，星團如一個有生命的三角與支桿結構向外生長，規律的幾何讓它可以朝任何方向持續延伸，讓一片夜空的故事，在空間裡繼續膨脹。

pins.title: Wonders of the World Stacks
pins.description:
Memories of three trips are stacked into one tower of brick, coloured houses and a white facade.

Model making | Travel and culture | Gypsum, tiny shells, bricks, wooden sticks, acrylic rods, PVC and cellophane | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 世界奇觀堆疊
zh-Hant.description:
三段旅行的記憶堆疊成一座由磚、彩色小屋與白色立面組成的塔。

模型製作｜旅行與文化｜石膏、小貝殼、磚、木棒、壓克力棒、PVC與玻璃紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Travel leaves strong memories of places, food and buildings. The student asked how three very different trips could live together in one structure.
captions: The full concept sketch with notes on each landmark and material.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 旅行留下對地方、食物與建築的深刻記憶。學生思考三段截然不同的旅行如何共存於一個結構中。
captions: 附有各地標與材料註記的完整概念草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Thailand, Macau and Hokkaido were each reduced to a few strong symbols. A watercolour tested how temples, a church facade and snowy hills could stack.
captions: An impression collage of street scenes, temples and towers from the trips.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 泰國、澳門與北海道各自被濃縮成幾個鮮明的符號。水彩畫測試寺廟、教堂立面與雪山如何堆疊。
captions: 旅途中街景、寺廟與高樓的印象拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The base was formed from gypsum and tiny shells, then ringed with miniature brick walls. Coloured houses on wooden sticks and a cut PVC facade were added above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 底座以石膏與小貝殼塑成，再圍上迷你磚牆。上方加入以木棒支撐的彩色小屋與切割的PVC立面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower reads from calm stone at the bottom to busy streets and a white facade at the top. Each layer uses materials that match the mood of each place.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔由底部沉穩的石材，往上到熱鬧的街道與白色立面。每一層都使用符合當地氛圍的材料。

sections.heading: Wonders of the World - Stacking Three Journeys into One Tower
sections.body: Travel leaves vivid memories of places, food and buildings, and the student asked how three very different journeys could live together in one structure. The guidance first led the student to reduce Thailand, Macau and Hokkaido each to a few strong symbols, and then to test in a watercolour how temples, a church facade and snowy hills might stack, so that crowded recollections were first distilled into clear images. In development, the base was formed from gypsum and tiny shells and ringed with miniature brick walls, while coloured houses on wooden sticks and a cut PVC facade were added above, each material matched to the air of a place. Finally, the tower reads from calm stone at the bottom through busy streets to a white facade at the top, each layer using materials that echo the mood of its place, so that distant memories live side by side within one tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 世界奇觀-把三段旅程疊成一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 旅行在記憶中留下鮮明的地方、食物與建築。學生思考，三段截然不同的旅程，能否共存於同一座結構之中？指導過程先引導學生把泰國、澳門與北海道各自提煉為幾個鮮明的象徵，再以一幅水彩測試寺廟、教堂立面與雪丘如何相互堆疊，讓紛繁的回憶先被濃縮為清晰的意象。進入推演，底座以石膏與細小貝殼塑成，周圍環繞迷你磚牆，上方再加入立在木棒上的彩色小屋與切割而成的PVC立面，每一種材料都對應一處地方的氣息。最後，高塔從底部沉靜的石材，讀到熱鬧的街道，再到頂端白色的立面，每一層的材料都呼應各地的氛圍，讓遠方的記憶，在一座塔裡比鄰而居。

pins.title: Tiny Forest
pins.description:
Rice terraces inspire stepped hexagon platforms where plants and city can share space.

Model making | Landscape and planting | Straws, PVC boards, model trees and glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 微型森林
zh-Hant.description:
以梯田為靈感，讓植物與城市共享空間的階梯式六角平台。

模型製作｜地景與植栽｜吸管、PVC板、模型樹與膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Dense cities leave little room for plants, yet greenery helps both people and wildlife. The student asked how buildings could make space for nature in layers.
captions: The Longji rice terraces that inspired the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 高密度城市留給植物的空間很少，但綠意對人與野生動物都有益。學生思考建築如何分層為自然騰出空間。
captions: 啟發本模型的龍脊梯田。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A hike through mountain rice terraces showed how stepped fields hold water and soil. The student also collected and painted rooftop-garden plants to see which could live at each height.
captions: Plant species collected from rooftop gardens, with a garden watercolour.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一次梯田健行讓學生看見階梯式田地如何保住水與土壤。學生也收集並描繪屋頂花園的植物，觀察哪些能在不同高度生長。
captions: 從屋頂花園蒐集的植物種類，附庭園水彩。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: PVC boards were cut into hexagons so their edges could interlock without bending. Straw columns lifted each layer and a terrace sketch guided the overall shape.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: PVC板被切成六角形，讓邊緣能互相咬合而不必彎折。吸管柱撐起每一層，梯田速寫則引導整體造型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stacks green platforms like terraces, each planted with different model trees. It suggests a city where buildings and plants grow together.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型像梯田般堆疊綠色平台，每一層種上不同的模型樹。它描繪一座建築與植物共同生長的城市。

sections.heading: Tiny Forest - Buildings Growing Green like Terraced Fields
sections.body: Dense cities leave little room for plants, yet greenery sustains both people and wildlife, and the student asked how buildings could make space for nature in layers. The guidance first led the student to observe, on a hike through mountain rice terraces, how stepped fields hold water and soil, and then to collect and paint rooftop-garden plants to learn which could live at each height, so that knowledge of landscape and planting together became the roots of the design. In development, PVC board was cut into hexagons so that their edges could interlock without bending, straw columns lifted each layer, and a sketch of terraces guided the overall shape. Finally, the model stacks green platforms like terraced fields, each planted with different model trees, picturing a city where buildings and plants grow together, so that a small forest rises again between the concrete.

zh-Hant.heading: 微型森林-讓建築像梯田般長出綠意
zh-Hant.body: 密集的城市少有植物的空間，綠意卻同時滋養人與野生動物。學生思考建築如何以層層堆疊的方式，為自然留出位置。指導過程先引導學生在山間梯田的健行中，觀察階梯狀的田地如何保住水與土，再蒐集並描繪屋頂花園的植物，了解哪些能在不同高度生長，讓地景與植栽的知識一同成為設計的根基。進入推演，PVC板被切成六角形，讓邊緣不需彎折便能互相扣合，吸管柱撐起每一層，一張梯田草圖則引導整體的形態。最後，模型如梯田般堆疊綠色平台，每層種上不同的模型樹，描繪出一座建築與植物共同生長的城市，讓水泥之間，重新長出一片小小的森林。

pins.title: Rhythms in Structure
pins.description:
A lively piano piece becomes a burst of black sticks, coloured film and cotton balls.

Model making | Music and form | Sticks, spray paint, cellophane, cotton balls and iridescent board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 結構中的節奏
zh-Hant.description:
一首輕快的鋼琴曲化為黑色木棒、彩色玻璃紙與棉球的迸發。

模型製作｜音樂與造型｜木棒、噴漆、玻璃紙、棉球與炫彩板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student had composed a short piano piece in a lively style for a music class. The question was how to turn rhythm and melody into a space you can see.
captions: The piano score sheets for the bass and melody parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在音樂課上創作了一段輕快風格的鋼琴曲。問題在於如何把節奏與旋律變成看得見的空間。
captions: 低音與旋律部分的鋼琴樂譜。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The steady left-hand bass and the playful right-hand melody were drawn as two kinds of lines. Bold arcs showed the bass, while loose curves and dots showed the melody.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 穩定的左手低音與俏皮的右手旋律被畫成兩種線條。粗弧線代表低音，鬆散的曲線與圓點代表旋律。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Black-sprayed sticks were tied in a tent shape to hold the bass, and white sticks twisted around them for the melody. Cellophane strips and cotton balls added colour and drum-like beats.
captions: Weaving the cellophane strips into the sticks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 噴黑的木棒被綁成帳篷形狀代表低音，白色木棒環繞其間代表旋律。玻璃紙條與棉球加入色彩與鼓點般的節拍。
captions: 親手將玻璃紙條編入木棒之間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final sculpture glows under light and reflects off an iridescent base. It turns a three-minute tune into one bright, frozen moment.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的雕塑在光線下發亮，並映照在炫彩底座上。它把三分鐘的樂曲凝結成一個明亮的瞬間。

sections.heading: Rhythms in Structure - Holding a Piano Piece Still as Light
sections.body: The student had composed a short, lively piano piece for a music class, and the question was how to turn its rhythm and melody into a space that could be seen. The guidance first led the student to draw the steady left-hand bass and the playful right-hand melody as two kinds of line, bold arcs for the bass and loose curves and dots for the melody, so that the dialogue of two hands first separated into layers on paper. In development, black-sprayed sticks were tied into a tent shape to hold the bass while white sticks twisted around them as the melody, and cellophane strips and cotton balls added colour and drum-like beats, each material taking its own voice. Finally, the sculpture glows under light and reflects off an iridescent base, turning a three-minute tune into one bright, frozen moment, so that music which fades once heard can be gazed upon at length.

zh-Hant.heading: 結構中的節奏-把一首鋼琴曲凝成光
zh-Hant.body: 學生曾為音樂課創作一首風格輕快的鋼琴短曲。問題是：如何把節奏與旋律，化為一個看得見的空間？指導過程先引導學生把穩定的左手低音與俏皮的右手旋律畫成兩種線條，粗重的弧線代表低音，鬆散的曲線與點代表旋律，讓兩隻手的對話先在紙上分出層次。進入推演，噴黑的木棒綁成帳篷般的形狀承載低音，白色木棒環繞其間化為旋律，玻璃紙條與棉球再添上色彩與如鼓點般的節拍，材料各自擔任聲部。最後，雕塑在燈光下發光，倒映在虹彩的底座上，把一首三分鐘的曲子，凝成一個明亮而靜止的瞬間，讓聽過即逝的音樂，得以被長久凝視。

pins.title: Visualization of Personality
pins.description:
Drawings of four personality types grow into one model of clay, sticks and white boards.

Model making | Psychology and form | Wooden sticks, plastic clay, wire and PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 個性的視覺化
zh-Hant.description:
四種個性類型的繪畫，發展成一座由黏土、木棒與白板構成的模型。

模型製作｜心理與造型｜木棒、塑形黏土、鐵線與PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Every person has a different mix of traits, but these are hard to see. The project asks how colour, shape and space could express a personality.
captions: Warm circles for an open type.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 每個人都有不同的特質組合，卻很難被看見。這個專案思考色彩、形狀與空間如何表達個性。
captions: 代表開朗類型的暖色圓。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied personality theories and drew one composition for each of four types. Warm circles, sharp blocks, closed forms and mixed patterns each told a different story.
captions: Four compositions, each for one personality type.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究個性理論，並為四種類型各畫一幅構圖。暖色圓、銳利方塊、封閉形與混合圖案各自訴說不同的故事。
captions: 四幅構圖，各自對應一種人格類型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two hand drawings were picked and turned into 3D studies. Clay, wooden sticks, wire and PVC boards were then combined into one piece.
captions: Shaping the clay and sticks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生挑選兩幅手繪轉化成立體研究。接著把黏土、木棒、鐵線與PVC板組合成一件作品。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model mixes open grids with closed boxes to show the many sides of one person. Light and shadow make each angle feel like a different mood.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型混合開放的格網與封閉的盒體，呈現一個人的多重面向。光影讓每個角度都像不同的情緒。

sections.heading: Visualization of Personality Traits - Drawing a Person in Colour and Form
sections.body: Every person carries a different mix of traits, yet these are hard to see, and the project asked how colour, shape and space could express a personality. The guidance first led the student to study theories of personality and draw one composition for each of four types, warm circles, sharp blocks, closed forms and mixed patterns each telling a different story, so that inner character first took on an appearance on paper. In development, two hand drawings were chosen and turned into three-dimensional studies, and clay, wooden sticks, wire and PVC board were combined into a single piece, each material carrying a different temperament. Finally, the model mixes open grids with closed boxes to show the many sides of one person, and light and shadow make each angle feel like a different mood, so that an invisible self unfolds gently in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 人格特質的視覺化-以色彩與形體描繪一個人
zh-Hant.body: 每個人都有不同的特質組合，卻難以被看見。這個作品追問：色彩、形體與空間，能否表達一種人格？指導過程先引導學生研究人格理論，為四種類型各畫一幅構成，溫暖的圓、銳利的方塊、封閉的形體與混合的圖案，各自訴說不同的故事，讓內在的性格先在平面上有了樣貌。進入推演，從中挑選兩幅手繪轉化為立體研究，再把黏土、木棒、鐵絲與PVC板結合為一件作品，不同材料承載不同的心性。最後，模型以開放的格柵混合封閉的盒子，呈現一個人的多重面向，光影讓每個角度都像一種不同的心情，讓看不見的自我，在空間中被溫柔地展開。

pins.title: Chilling Refuge: Penguin Habitat
pins.description:
A ring of stacked stones and a light acrylic frame form a shared home for penguins.

Model making | Animal habitat | Stone, wood strips, jelly wax, acrylic strips and foamboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 寒冷避風港：企鵝棲地
zh-Hant.description:
堆疊的石塊與輕巧的壓克力框架，圍成企鵝共享的家。

模型製作｜動物棲地｜石塊、木條、果凍蠟、壓克力條與珍珠板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Penguins kept on hard concrete can fall ill because the ground does not suit them. The student asked how a man-made habitat could feel natural and still support their social life.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 企鵝若住在堅硬的混凝土上容易生病，因為地面不適合牠們。學生思考人工棲地如何既自然又能支持牠們的群居生活。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Some penguins build nests from stones, so stacked rock became the main material. A round, inward-facing house type was studied because it lets neighbours meet in a shared centre.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 有些企鵝會用石頭築巢，因此堆疊的石塊成為主要材料。學生也研究一種向內圍合的圓形住屋，因為它讓鄰居能在共享的中心相遇。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stones were glued into a ring of nests around a pool made from jelly wax. A thin acrylic frame was then raised over the ring to suggest shelter without blocking light.
captions: Building the ring and stone nests.
Drawing of the frame over the stones.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把石塊黏成一圈巢穴，圍繞著以果凍蠟做成的水池。接著在環上架起細壓克力框架，暗示遮蔽又不擋住光線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model joins rough natural stone with a light, regular frame. Small penguin figures show how the ring creates a shared, protected home.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型結合粗糙的天然石塊與輕巧規則的框架。小企鵝模型顯示環形如何創造一個共享且受保護的家。

sections.heading: Chilling Refuge - A Penguin Home Ringed with Stone Nests
sections.body: Penguins kept on hard concrete can fall ill because the ground does not suit them, and the student asked how a man-made habitat could feel natural while still supporting their social life. The guidance first led the student to learn that some penguins build nests from stones, making stacked rock the main material, and then to study a round, inward-facing house type that lets neighbours meet in a shared centre, so that animal habit and human dwelling wisdom met. In development, stones were glued into a ring of nests around a pool made from jelly wax, and a thin acrylic frame was raised over the ring to suggest shelter without blocking the light. Finally, the model joins rough natural stone with a light, regular frame, and small penguin figures show how the ring creates a shared and protected home, so that a cold need is met with warmth.

zh-Hant.heading: 冰涼的避難所-以石巢圍出企鵝的家
zh-Hant.body: 被飼養在堅硬水泥地上的企鵝，可能因地面不適而生病。學生思考人造的棲地如何既感覺自然，又能支持牠們的群居生活。指導過程先引導學生發現有些企鵝以石頭築巢，於是以堆疊的岩石作為主要材料，再研究一種圓形、向內圍合的住宅類型，讓鄰里在共享的中心相遇，物種的習性與人的居住智慧就此交會。進入推演，石頭被黏成一圈巢穴，環繞著以果凍蠟製成的水池，一道纖細的壓克力框架再升起於環形之上，暗示庇護卻不遮擋光線。最後，模型結合粗糙的天然石材與輕盈規整的框架，小小的企鵝人偶顯示環形如何形成一個共享而受保護的家，讓冰冷的需求，被溫柔地接住。

pins.title: Spatial Deconstruction of Chinese Gardens
pins.description:
Fragments of classical garden plans are reassembled into a new winding water garden.

Model making | Garden space | PVC board, stone clay, wooden sticks and landscape materials | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 中國園林的空間解構
zh-Hant.description:
古典園林平面的片段被重新組合成一座蜿蜒的新水景園。

模型製作｜園林空間｜PVC板、石粉黏土、木棒與造景材料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished water garden from above.
從上方看完成的水景園。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Classical gardens hide and reveal views as people walk, which makes them feel larger than they are. The project asks how this effect could be taken apart and rebuilt in a new layout.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 古典園林隨著行走藏景與露景，讓空間感覺比實際更大。這個專案思考如何拆解這種效果，再在新的配置中重建。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied gardens from Yangzhou and Suzhou and the idea that scenery changes with every step. Pieces of their plans were cut out and reassembled into one new plan.
captions: Two watercolour impression sketches of the garden.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究揚州與蘇州的園林，以及「移步換景」的概念。接著把它們的平面片段剪下，重新組合成一張新的平面。
captions: 兩幅庭園印象水彩速寫。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The new plan was refined in pencil and then built with PVC board, stone clay and wooden sticks. Halls were framed in sticks so their outlines stay light against the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 新平面先以鉛筆修整，再用PVC板、石粉黏土與木棒製作。廳堂以木棒搭出框架，使輪廓在水面前保持輕盈。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model winds paths and bridges around a bright blue pond. Each turn opens a new view, just as in the gardens that inspired it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓小徑與橋繞著亮藍色的水池蜿蜒。每一次轉折都開啟新的景色，正如啟發它的園林。

sections.heading: Spatial Deconstruction of a Classical Garden - Taking Apart and Rebuilding Shifting Views
sections.body: Classical gardens hide and reveal views as people walk, which makes them feel larger than they are, and the project asked how this effect could be taken apart and rebuilt in a new layout. The guidance first led the student to study gardens of Yangzhou and Suzhou and the idea that scenery changes with every step, then to cut pieces from their plans and reassemble them into one new plan, so that analysis itself became an act of design. In development, the new plan was refined again and again in pencil and then built with PVC board, stone clay and wooden sticks, the halls framed in sticks so their outlines stay light against the water. Finally, paths and bridges wind around a bright blue pond, each turn opening a new view just as in the gardens that inspired it, so that an old wisdom, once rearranged, still invites one to wander.

zh-Hant.heading: 古典園林的空間解構-拆解步移景異再重組
zh-Hant.body: 古典園林在人行走時隱藏又揭示景致，讓它感覺比實際更大。這個作品追問：這種效果能否被拆解，並在新的格局中重建？指導過程先引導學生研究揚州與蘇州的園林，以及步移景異的造園理念，再把它們的平面裁切成片段，重新組合為一個新的平面，讓分析本身就成為一次設計。進入推演，新平面先以鉛筆反覆修整，再以PVC板、石粉黏土與木棒建構，廳堂以木棒框出輪廓，讓它們在水面前保持輕盈。最後，模型讓小徑與橋蜿蜒環繞一池明亮的藍水，每一次轉折都展開新的景致，一如啟發它的那些園林，讓古老的智慧，在重組之後依然引人漫步。

pins.title: Flowing Sleeves: Dance to Space Design
pins.description:
Silk hung in lattice frames captures the soft lines of a traditional sleeve dance.

Model making | Movement to space | Wood strips, cloth, yarn, fishing line and a wooden doll | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動水袖：從舞蹈到空間設計
zh-Hant.description:
懸掛在格柵框架中的絲布，捕捉傳統水袖舞的柔和線條。

模型製作｜從動作到空間｜木條、布料、紗線、釣魚線與木偶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A sleeve dance creates soft lines in the air that vanish a moment later. The student asked how those passing movements could be turned into lasting space.
captions: Stills of a sleeve dance from a period drama.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 水袖舞在空中畫出柔和的線條，轉瞬即逝。學生思考如何把這些短暫的動作轉化為持久的空間。
captions: 古裝劇中的水袖舞劇照。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Scenes from a period drama were studied and the sleeve paths were traced as coloured lines. Traditional cracked-ice window patterns gave a frame for holding these lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究古裝劇中的片段，把水袖的軌跡描成彩色線條。傳統冰裂紋窗格則提供承載這些線條的框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Three wooden frames of different sizes were filled with thin strips and fishing line. Silk was then hung and pulled in different ways, and each change was photographed frame by frame.
captions: Making the frames and hanging the fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木條製作三個不同大小的框架，並加入細條與釣魚線。接著以不同方式懸掛與拉動絲布，逐格拍攝每一次變化。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final frames hold layers of pink and white fabric like a dancer frozen mid-turn. Together they show one movement unfolding through space and time.
captions: Frame-by-frame record of pulling the fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的框架容納層層粉白布料，像舞者在旋轉中定格。它們一起呈現一個動作在時空中展開。

sections.heading: Flowing Sleeves - Turning a Moment of Dance into Space
sections.body: A sleeve dance draws soft lines in the air that vanish a moment later, and the student asked how those passing movements could become lasting space. The guidance first led the student to study dance scenes from a period drama and trace the paths of the sleeves as coloured lines, then to use traditional cracked-ice window patterns as a frame to hold them, so that a flowing dance first found a resting place within an ancient order. In development, three wooden frames of different sizes were filled with thin strips and fishing line, silk was hung and pulled in different ways, and each change was photographed frame by frame, the softness of the fabric unfolding within the restraint of the frame. Finally, the frames hold layers of pink and white fabric like a dancer caught mid-turn, together showing one movement unfolding through space and time, so that a single glance back lingers in the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 水袖流轉-把舞動的瞬間化為空間
zh-Hant.body: 水袖舞在空中劃出柔軟的線條，轉瞬便消失無蹤。學生追問：這些短暫的動作，能否化為持久的空間？指導過程先引導學生研究一部古裝劇中的舞蹈場景，把袖子的軌跡描成彩色線條，再以傳統冰裂紋花窗作為承載這些線條的框架，讓流動的舞姿先在古老的秩序中找到停靠。進入推演，三個大小不同的木框填入細木條與釣魚線，絲綢懸掛其上，以不同方式拉扯，每一次變化都被逐格拍攝，材料的柔軟在框架的節制中展開。最後，木框承載著層層粉色與白色的布料，如同舞者在旋轉中被定格，三者共同呈現一個動作在時間與空間中的展開，讓一次回眸，長久地留在空中。

pins.title: Tranquil Retreat House
pins.description:
A small timber house keeps only the essentials and frames the forest through one low window.

Model making | Small house | Wooden board, laser cutting, PVC board and clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 寧靜隱居小屋
zh-Hant.description:
一座小木屋只保留必需品，並以一扇與視線同高的窗框住森林。

模型製作｜小住宅｜木板、雷射切割、PVC板與黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Stress and conflict can make city life feel overwhelming. The student wanted a small place in the forest that helps a person slow down and think.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 壓力與衝突會讓城市生活令人喘不過氣。學生想要一個森林中的小地方，幫助人放慢腳步思考。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The house was kept small, with only essential furniture and functions. A window set at eye height became the key idea, turning the view outside into a calm daily ritual.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 小屋保持小巧，只有必要的家具與功能。與視線同高的窗成為關鍵概念，讓看向窗外成為平靜的日常儀式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The form was modelled digitally, turned into flat drawings and laser cut from wood. Walls, furniture and framed clear windows were then glued together piece by piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 造型先以數位建模，再轉成平面圖並以雷射切割木板。接著逐片黏合牆面、家具與嵌有透明片的窗框。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model shows a quiet timber shelter that glows warmly at night. Its simple rooms keep the focus on light, wood and the view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型呈現一座在夜裡透出暖光的安靜木屋。簡單的房間讓焦點留在光、木材與景色上。

sections.heading: Tranquil Retreat - Learning to Slow Down in the Forest
sections.body: Stress and conflict can make city life overwhelming, and the student wanted a small place in the forest to help a person slow down and think. The guidance first led the student to keep the house small, with only essential furniture and functions, and then to make a window set at eye height the key idea, turning the view outside into a calm daily ritual, so that subtraction became the attitude of the design. In development, the form was modelled digitally, turned into flat drawings and laser cut from wood, and the walls, furniture and framed clear windows were glued together piece by piece, simple parts gaining weight through careful assembly. Finally, the model shows a quiet timber shelter that glows warmly at night, its simple rooms keeping attention on light, wood and the view, so that a tired person can find again the time to be with oneself.

zh-Hant.heading: 寧靜居所-在森林裡學會慢下來
zh-Hant.body: 壓力與衝突，讓城市生活令人喘不過氣。學生想在森林裡設計一個小小的地方，幫助人放慢腳步、靜心思考。指導過程先引導學生讓房子保持小巧，只留下必要的家具與機能，再把一扇設在視線高度的窗戶作為核心概念，讓窗外的風景化為每日平靜的儀式，減法因此成為設計的態度。進入推演，形體先以數位建模，轉成平面圖後以木材雷射切割，牆面、家具與框起的透明窗再一片片黏合，簡單的構件在細心的組裝中顯出分量。最後，模型呈現一座安靜的木構小屋，在夜裡溫暖地發光，簡潔的房間讓注意力回到光、木與風景，讓一個疲憊的人，重新找回與自己相處的時間。

pins.title: Volleyball Motion Trajectory
pins.description:
Frames of a volleyball swing become rows of paper fins under a triangulated stick canopy.

Model making | Motion to form | PVC board, paper and wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 排球動作軌跡視覺化
zh-Hant.description:
排球揮擊的連續畫格化為一排排紙鰭，上方覆蓋三角化的木棒棚架。

模型製作｜從動作到造型｜PVC板、紙與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A volleyball move lasts only a second, so its shape is hard to see. The student asked how the student's own playing motion could be turned into a lasting space.
captions: The motion traced as a 3D band.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個排球動作只持續一秒，形狀很難被看見。學生思考如何把自己打球的動作轉化成持久的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A video of one strong move was split into single frames to find the key angles. These were traced as a band and rebuilt digitally as rows of thin fins.
captions: Digital model of the fin field.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把一段動作最清楚的影片拆成單格，找出關鍵角度。這些角度被描成帶狀，再以數位方式重建為一排排薄鰭片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper fins were cut, folded and tested under side light to read the motion. A canopy of triangles was then drawn and built in sticks to sit above them.
captions: Fin studies lit from the side.
First stick frame over the fins.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙鰭片經過切割、摺疊，並在側光下測試動作的表現。接著繪製三角形棚架，以木棒搭建在鰭片上方。
captions: 鰭片上方的第一版木棒框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets a wave of white fins under a varied stick canopy. Each strut length changes with the motion, so the roof reads like a frozen swing.
captions: Canopy and fins from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓一波白色鰭片位於變化豐富的木棒棚架下。每根支桿的長度隨動作改變，使屋頂像一次定格的揮擊。

sections.heading: Volleyball Motion Trajectory - Freezing a Single Second of a Swing
sections.body: A volleyball move lasts only a second, so its shape is hard to see, and the student asked how a movement from the student's own play could become a lasting space. The guidance first led the student to split a video of one strong move into single frames to find the key angles, then to trace them as a band and rebuild it digitally as rows of thin fins, so that a moment of force was first broken down into a sequence that could be read. In development, paper fins were cut, folded and tested under side light to read the motion, and a canopy of triangles was then drawn and built in sticks to sit above them, motion and stillness speaking to each other from below and above. Finally, the model sets a wave of white fins beneath a varied stick canopy whose strut lengths change with the motion, so that the roof reads like a swing frozen in time.

zh-Hant.heading: 排球的軌跡-凝固一秒鐘的揮擊
zh-Hant.body: 一個排球動作只持續一秒，形狀難以看清。學生追問：自己擊球的動作，能否轉化為一個持久的空間？指導過程先引導學生把一次有力動作的影片拆成單格，找出關鍵的角度，再把它們描成一條帶狀，並以數位方式重建為一排排細薄的鰭片，讓瞬間的力量先被拆解為可以閱讀的序列。進入推演，紙鰭片經過裁切、折疊，在側光下測試，以讀出動作的痕跡，接著繪出三角形的頂棚，以木棒搭建於其上，動與靜在上下之間對話。最後，模型以一道白色鰭片的波浪，安放在變化多端的木棒頂棚之下，每根支桿的長度隨動作而變，讓屋頂讀來如同一次被凝固的揮擊。

pins.title: The Fragile Arctic: Revolving Ice
pins.description:
Clear and black layers stack into a tower that shows sea ice thinning as it warms.

Model making | Climate change | Paper, vegetation, wood sticks and transparent bars | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 脆弱的北極：旋轉的冰
zh-Hant.description:
透明與黑色層板堆疊成塔，呈現海冰在暖化中變薄。

模型製作｜氣候變遷｜紙、植栽、木棒與透明條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Rising temperatures are melting Arctic sea ice faster every year. Many animals lose the ice they need for resting, hunting and raising their young.
captions: Animals that rely on sea ice.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 氣溫上升使北極海冰逐年加速融化。許多動物因此失去休息、覓食與繁殖所需的冰面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student ran a test comparing how fast ice melts in room-temperature and heated water. The results showed how a small rise in heat speeds up the loss of ice.
captions: Ice blocks for the melting test.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生進行實驗，比較冰在室溫水與加熱水中的融化速度。結果顯示熱度的小幅上升就會加快冰的流失。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A tall tower was sketched with clear planks and white platforms to stand for ice and human space. Black parts were added at the base to show the warming creeping upward.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出一座高塔，以透明板與白色平台代表冰與人的空間。底部加入黑色構件，表現暖化逐漸向上蔓延。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower grows thinner and darker toward the bottom, like ice melting away. It turns test results into a clear image that invites people to learn and act.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔越往下越細、越暗，像冰正在融化。它把實驗結果轉化成清楚的畫面，邀請人們了解並採取行動。

sections.heading: Fragile Arctic - A Tower of Ice Melting from Below
sections.body: Rising temperatures are melting Arctic sea ice faster every year, and many animals are losing the ice they need for resting, hunting and raising their young. The guidance first led the student to run an experiment comparing how fast ice melts in room-temperature and heated water, and the results showed that even a small rise in heat speeds the loss of ice, so that a distant crisis was first witnessed on a tabletop. In development, the student sketched a tall tower with clear planks and white platforms standing for ice and human space, then added black parts at the base to show warming creeping upward, the data translated into a language of form. Finally, the tower grows thinner and darker toward the bottom like ice melting away, turning experimental results into a clear image that invites people to learn and act, so that fragility is seen gently and firmly.

zh-Hant.heading: 脆弱的北極-一座向下融化的冰之塔
zh-Hant.body: 氣溫上升，北極海冰一年比一年融化得更快，許多動物因此失去休息、狩獵與育幼所需的冰面。指導過程先引導學生進行一項實驗，比較冰在室溫水與加熱水中融化的速度，結果顯示，熱度的小小上升，就會加速冰的消失，讓遙遠的危機先在桌面上被親眼看見。進入推演，學生草繪一座高塔，以透明板與白色平台代表冰層與人的空間，再在底部加入黑色構件，表現暖化正一步步向上蔓延，數據就此轉化為形體的語言。最後，高塔越往下越細、越暗，如同正在融化的冰，作品把實驗結果化為清晰的意象，邀請人們學習並採取行動，讓一份脆弱，被溫柔而堅定地看見。

pins.title: Interpretation of Music as a Sculpture
pins.description:
Two trials turn the calm of playing the flute into waves of cut straws.

Model making | Music to space | Plastic straws, hot glue, plastic board and spray paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 音樂的雕塑詮釋
zh-Hant.description:
兩次嘗試把吹奏長笛的平靜轉化為由剪裁吸管組成的波浪。

模型製作｜從音樂到空間｜塑膠吸管、熱熔膠、塑膠板與噴漆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Playing the flute gives the student a calm, familiar feeling. The project asks how that feeling could be shown as a sculpture and a space.
captions: Drawing of a flute and birds.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 吹奏長笛給學生平靜而熟悉的感受。這個專案思考如何把這種感受呈現為雕塑與空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A first trial used tubes, arches and coloured flags around a flute form. It looked more like a busy playground than calm music, so the student chose to start again.
captions: The first trial with arches and flags.
Close views of the first trial.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 第一次嘗試在長笛造型周圍使用管子、拱與彩色旗子。它看起來更像熱鬧的遊樂場而非平靜的音樂，因此學生決定重新開始。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The second trial went abstract, using hundreds of cut paper and plastic straws. Flowing lines were sketched and then built as separate waves that were pieced together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二次嘗試轉向抽象，使用數百根剪裁的紙吸管與塑膠吸管。學生先描繪流動線條，再做成一段段波浪拼合起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final sculpture rises in grey and black waves like notes in the air. Small figures turn it into an urban space shaped by music.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的雕塑以灰黑色的波浪升起，像空中的音符。小人偶讓它成為由音樂塑造的城市空間。

sections.heading: Music as Sculpture - Turning the Calm of the Flute into Waves
sections.body: Playing the flute gives the student a calm and familiar feeling, and the project asked how that feeling could be shown as a sculpture and a space. The guidance began with a first trial in which tubes, arches and coloured flags surrounded a flute form, yet it looked more like a busy playground than quiet music, so the guidance encouraged the student to let it go bravely and start again. In development, the second trial turned abstract, using hundreds of cut paper and plastic straws; flowing lines were sketched first and then built as separate waves that were pieced together into one whole. Finally, the sculpture rises in grey and black waves like notes drifting in the air, and small figures turn it into an urban space shaped by music, so that a private calm opens itself to everyone.

zh-Hant.heading: 音樂即雕塑-讓長笛的平靜化為波浪
zh-Hant.body: 吹奏長笛，給學生一種平靜而熟悉的感受。這個作品追問：這份感受，能否被呈現為一件雕塑與一個空間？指導過程從第一次嘗試開始，管子、拱形與彩色旗幟環繞著長笛的形體，看起來卻更像熱鬧的遊樂場而非沉靜的音樂，指導便引導學生勇敢放下，重新出發。進入推演，第二次嘗試走向抽象，使用數百根剪開的紙吸管與塑膠吸管，先草繪流動的線條，再把它們建構成一道道獨立的波浪，拼合為一體。最後，雕塑以灰與黑的波浪升起，如同飄在空中的音符，小小的人偶把它轉化為由音樂塑造的城市空間，讓一份私密的平靜，向眾人敞開。

pins.title: Three-Dimensional Modular System Study
pins.description:
A precedent study of stacked modular boxes grows into an open cardboard tower.

Model making | Precedent model study | Wood sticks, white cardboard and glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 立體模組系統研究
zh-Hant.description:
一項堆疊模組盒體的先例研究，長成一座開放的紙板塔。

模型製作｜先例模型研究｜木棒、白紙板與膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A famous 1960s housing idea stacked boxes in three dimensions to solve crowded space. The student wanted to test how far such a modular system could grow.
captions: Cardboard and sticks ready to build.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個著名的1960年代住宅構想，以立體堆疊盒體解決擁擠的空間。學生想測試這樣的模組系統能長到多遠。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several small modular models were made first to understand how the units link. They were then combined and extended upward and sideways.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先做幾個小型模組模型，了解單元如何相連。接著把它們組合，並向上與向旁延伸。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: As the model grew, continuous voids appeared that let light in from many angles. Some spaces were then enclosed to add a sense of boundary, and stick frames marked open rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 模型長大時出現連續的虛空間，讓光從多個角度進入。學生接著封閉部分空間以增加邊界感，並用木棒框架標示開放房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
