sections.body: The final tower mixes closed white boxes, open frames and platforms of many sizes. A detailed hand drawing was used to study its light, shadow and connections.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔混合封閉的白色盒體、開放框架與各種尺度的平台。學生以細緻的手繪研究它的光影與連結。

sections.heading: Three-Dimensional Modular System - Testing How Far Stacked Boxes Can Grow
sections.body: A famous housing idea of the 1960s stacked boxes in three dimensions to answer crowded space, and the student wanted to test how far such a modular system could grow. The guidance first led the student to make several small modular models to understand how the units link, then to combine and extend them upward and sideways, so that the rules of the system became clear through making. In development, as the model grew, continuous voids appeared that let light in from many angles, some spaces were enclosed to add a sense of boundary, and stick frames marked the open rooms, solid and void finding balance as the structure grew. Finally, the tower mixes closed white boxes, open frames and platforms of many sizes, and a detailed hand drawing was used to study its light, shadow and connections, so that a rational system grows into an unexpected richness.

zh-Hant.heading: 三維模組系統-測試堆疊盒子的生長極限
zh-Hant.body: 一九六〇年代一個著名的住宅構想，以三維堆疊的盒子回應擁擠的空間。學生想測試這樣的模組系統能夠生長到什麼程度。指導過程先引導學生製作數個小型模組模型，理解單元之間如何相互扣連，再把它們組合起來，向上與向兩側延伸，讓系統的規則在實作中逐漸清晰。進入推演，隨著模型長大，連續的空隙自然出現，讓光從多個角度進入，部分空間再被圍合以增加邊界感，木棒框架則標示開放的房間，虛與實在生長中找到平衡。最後，高塔混合了封閉的白色盒子、開放的框架與大小不一的平台，一張細緻的手繪圖用來研究光影與連接，讓一套理性的系統，長出出乎意料的豐富。

pins.title: City in Window
pins.description:
Broken reflections in city windows are rebuilt as a tower of stick frames and planes.

Model making | City impressions | PVC board and wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 窗中城市
zh-Hant.description:
城市窗戶中破碎的倒影，被重建成一座木棒框架與平面組成的塔。

模型製作｜城市印象｜PVC板與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Windows in the city reflect buildings in bent and broken pieces. The student found these reflections more interesting than the city seen directly.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 城市中的窗戶以彎曲破碎的片段映照建築。學生發現這些倒影比直接看到的城市更有趣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Photos of windows were traced, cut and collaged into new patterns. The lines were then simplified into points, lines and surfaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描下窗戶的照片，再剪裁拼貼成新的圖案。接著把線條簡化為點、線與面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The patterns were imagined in 3D and built with wood strips and PVC boards. Three phases moved from single fragments to overlapping layers and then to tower forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些圖案被想像成立體，以木條與PVC板製作。三個階段從單一碎片走向重疊層次，再發展成塔的造型。
captions: 早期的木棒與板材模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stacks striped frames and pale planes into an irregular tower. Its overlapping shadows rebuild the broken city seen in a window.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把條紋框架與淺色平面堆疊成不規則的塔。重疊的陰影重建了窗中那座破碎的城市。

sections.heading: City in Window - Rebuilding the City from Broken Reflections
sections.body: City windows reflect buildings in bent and broken pieces, and the student found these reflections more intriguing than the city seen directly. The guidance first led the student to photograph windows and trace, cut and collage the images into new patterns, then to simplify their lines into points, lines and surfaces, so that a confusion of reflections first became a vocabulary that could be worked. In development, the patterns were imagined in three dimensions and built with wood strips and PVC board through three phases, moving from single fragments to overlapping layers and then to tower forms, each step growing from the fragments of the last. Finally, the model stacks striped frames and pale planes into an irregular tower whose overlapping shadows rebuild the broken city seen in a window, so that an illusion glimpsed for an instant becomes a landscape to be contemplated at length.

zh-Hant.heading: 窗中之城-在破碎的倒影裡重建城市
zh-Hant.body: 城市的窗戶，把建築映成彎折而破碎的片段。學生發現，這些倒影比直接看見的城市更加耐人尋味。指導過程先引導學生拍攝窗戶，將照片描繪、剪裁並拼貼成新的圖案，再把線條簡化為點、線與面，讓紛亂的倒影先被整理成可以操作的語彙。進入推演，圖案在想像中被立體化，以木條與PVC板建構，分三個階段推進，從單一碎片到層層疊合，再發展為塔的形態，每一步都在前一步的碎片上生長。最後，模型以條紋框架與淺色平面堆疊成不規則的高塔，交疊的陰影重建了窗中那座破碎的城市，讓一瞥之間的錯覺，成為可以久久凝視的風景。

pins.title: The Sharpness of Language
pins.description:
Clay mouths sit in a mirror cube surrounded by sharp paper shards of words.

Model making | Concept installation | Mirrors, clay, plastic sticks, magazine paper and plastic sheets | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 語言的鋒利
zh-Hant.description:
黏土嘴巴坐在鏡面立方中，四周環繞著尖銳的文字紙片。

模型製作｜概念裝置｜鏡子、黏土、塑膠棒、雜誌紙與塑膠片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Online, a few harsh words can hurt more than a physical weapon. The student wanted to show how one person cannot escape the pressure of public opinion.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在網路上，少數尖銳的言語可能比實體武器更傷人。學生想表現一個人如何難以逃離輿論的壓力。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The idea grew into a person wishing for many mouths to answer words coming from every side. A mouth was chosen as the main form and sculpted in clay with careful colour and texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 概念發展成一個人渴望擁有許多張嘴，回應來自四面八方的言語。學生選擇嘴巴作為主要造型，以黏土細緻塑造顏色與質感。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Headlines in many languages were cut into sharp triangles and fixed on clear sheets and rods. Three mirrors were then joined into a cube to multiply the mouths and shards.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 多種語言的標題被剪成尖銳的三角形，固定在透明片與塑膠棒上。接著把三面鏡子組成立方，讓嘴巴與紙片不斷倍增。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Inside the cube, the mouths seem endless and the shards point in from all sides. The small piece makes an invisible pressure feel physical and close.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在立方內，嘴巴彷彿無窮無盡，紙片從四面指向中心。這件小作品讓看不見的壓力變得具體而貼近。

sections.heading: Sharpness of Language - Endless Mouths and Shards in a Mirror
sections.body: Online, a few harsh words can wound more deeply than a physical weapon, and the student wanted to show how one person cannot escape the pressure of public opinion. The guidance first led the student to grow the idea into a person wishing for many mouths to answer words arriving from every side, then to choose the mouth as the main form and sculpt it in clay with careful colour and texture, so that an abstract pain first gained a body. In development, headlines in many languages were cut into sharp triangles and fixed on clear sheets and rods, and three mirrors were joined into a cube so that mouths and shards multiply endlessly in reflection. Finally, inside the cube the mouths seem without end and the shards point inward from all sides, and the small piece makes an invisible pressure feel physical and close, letting the viewer see in the mirror the weight that words carry.

zh-Hant.heading: 語言的鋒利-鏡中無盡的嘴與碎片
zh-Hant.body: 在網路上，幾句刻薄的話，可能比實體的武器更傷人。學生想呈現一個人如何無法逃離輿論的壓力。指導過程先引導學生把構想發展為一個渴望擁有許多張嘴、以回應四面八方言語的人，再選定嘴作為主要形體，以黏土細心塑造色彩與質感，讓抽象的痛楚先有了身體。進入推演，多種語言的新聞標題被剪成銳利的三角形，固定在透明片與細桿上，三面鏡子再組成立方體，讓嘴與碎片在反射中不斷增殖。最後，立方體內的嘴彷彿無窮無盡，碎片從各個方向指向中心，這件小小的作品，讓一種看不見的壓力變得具體而貼近，也讓觀者在鏡中，看見言語的重量。

pins.title: Harmonic Home
pins.description:
A house shaped by the treble clef wraps a sloping roof garden for a musical family.

Model making | House design | 3D print (PLA), wooden board, clay and Rhino | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 和諧之家
zh-Hant.description:
一座以高音譜號為形的住宅，包覆著為音樂家庭設計的傾斜屋頂花園。

模型製作｜住宅設計｜3D列印（PLA）、木板、黏土與Rhino｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished house and roof garden.
完成的住宅與屋頂花園。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A home can be more than rooms; it can connect the people who live in it. The student wanted a house that expresses music and the bond between family members.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 家不只是房間，也能連結住在其中的人。學生希望設計一座表現音樂與家人情感連結的住宅。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The treble clef gave the flowing plan, and a note shape gave the triangular structure. A lush garden was added to stand for the growth of the family.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 高音譜號帶來流動的平面，音符的形狀則形成三角形結構。學生加入茂盛的花園，象徵家庭的成長。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The design was modelled and tested digitally, then the complex roof was 3D printed. Walls and clear windows were laser cut, and furniture and planting were added by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計先以數位建模與模擬，再以3D列印製作複雜的屋頂。牆面與透明窗經雷射切割，家具與植栽則以手工加入。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises from a glass frame to a green roof walk. Its open plan and shared garden invite the family to meet and talk.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型從玻璃框架升起，延伸到綠色的屋頂步道。開放平面與共享花園邀請家人相聚交流。

sections.heading: Harmonic Home - Composing a Family's Togetherness with a Treble Clef
sections.body: A home can be more than a set of rooms; it can connect the people who live in it, and the student wanted a house that expresses music and the bond between family members. The guidance first led the student to take a flowing plan from the treble clef and a triangular structure from the shape of a note, then to add a lush garden standing for the growth of the family, so that symbol and feeling first played together in the concept. In development, the design was modelled and tested digitally, the complex roof was 3D printed, walls and clear windows were laser cut, and furniture and planting were added by hand, precision and warmth living side by side in one model. Finally, the model rises from a glass frame to a green roof walk, its open plan and shared garden inviting the family to meet and talk, so that a melody becomes the harmony of everyday life.

zh-Hant.heading: 和諧之家-以高音譜號譜寫家人的相聚
zh-Hant.body: 家可以不只是房間的組合，也能把住在裡面的人連繫起來。學生想設計一座表達音樂與家人情感的住宅。指導過程先引導學生從高音譜號取得流動的平面，從音符的形狀取得三角形的結構，再加入一座繁茂的花園，象徵家庭的成長，讓符號與情感先在構想中合奏。進入推演，設計先以數位建模反覆測試，複雜的屋頂以3D列印製作，牆面與透明窗以雷射切割，家具與植栽則以手工逐一加入，精密與溫度在同一座模型裡並存。最後，模型從玻璃框架升至綠色的屋頂步道，開放的平面與共享的花園邀請家人相遇、交談，讓一段旋律，成為日常生活的和聲。

pins.title: House of Wishes
pins.description:
A two-storey timber house by the sea gives children calm rooms for learning and rest.

Model making | Care-centred housing | Wooden board and spray paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 願望之家
zh-Hant.description:
一座海邊的雙層木構住宅，為孩子提供安靜的學習與休息空間。

模型製作｜以照護為核心的住宅｜木板與噴漆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished house cut open in section.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Children who need a quiet setting often learn in crowded, worn-out rooms. The student asked what a calm, purpose-built house for them could look like.
captions: A satellite photo of the beach site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 需要安靜環境的孩子，常在擁擠老舊的房間裡學習。學生思考一座為他們量身打造的安靜住宅會是什麼樣子。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A seaside site was chosen because the steady sound of waves helps focus. The rooms were sorted into learning, sleeping and relaxing zones on two floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇海邊基地，因為規律的海浪聲有助專注。房間被分為學習、睡眠與放鬆三區，配置在兩層樓中。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The layout was modelled digitally at 1:50 and cut from wooden board. Walls were glued cleanly and small furniture was made to test the scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 平面以 1:50 比例數位建模，再從木板切割。牆面以乾淨的膠合方式組裝，並製作小家具來檢驗尺度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model opens in section to show a tall stair hall and bright rooms. Large glass walls and a deep roof keep the house light but sheltered.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以剖面打開，展現高聳的樓梯廳與明亮的房間。大片玻璃牆與深遠的屋簷，使住宅明亮又有遮蔽。

sections.heading: House of Wishes - A Seaside Learning House Accompanied by Waves
sections.body: Children who need a quiet setting often learn in crowded, worn-out rooms, and the student asked what a calm house built for them could look like. The guidance first led the student to choose a seaside site, because the steady sound of waves helps concentration, and then to sort the rooms into learning, sleeping and relaxing zones across two floors, so that needs first became a clear spatial order. In development, the layout was modelled digitally at one to fifty and cut from wooden board, the walls were glued cleanly, and small pieces of furniture were made to test the scale, every room checked against the body of a child. Finally, the model opens in section to reveal a tall stair hall and bright rooms, its large glass walls and deep roof keeping the house both light and sheltered, so that a wish finds a steady home in the sea breeze.

zh-Hant.heading: 願望之屋-浪聲陪伴的海邊學習之家
zh-Hant.body: 需要安靜環境的孩子，常常在擁擠而破舊的教室裡學習。學生追問：一座專為孩子而建、平靜的房子，可以是什麼模樣？指導過程先引導學生選擇海邊的基地，因為規律的浪聲有助專注，再把房間整理為學習、睡眠與放鬆三個區域，分布於上下兩層，讓需求先成為清晰的空間秩序。進入推演，平面以一比五十數位建模，再以木板切割，牆面乾淨地黏合，並製作小家具測試尺度，讓每個房間都回到孩子的身體來檢驗。最後，模型以剖面打開，展示挑高的樓梯廳與明亮的房間，大片玻璃牆與深遠的屋簷讓住宅既通透又受庇護，讓一個願望，在海風中有了安穩的居所。

admitted_schools.zh-Hant: 康乃爾大學建築本科 ED

pins.title: Extension of Motions
pins.description:
Violin bowing paths become clay caves wrapped in a net of wooden sticks.

Model making | Motion to form | Air-dry clay, wood sticks and wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 動作的延伸
zh-Hant.description:
拉小提琴的運弓軌跡化為黏土洞穴，外覆木棒網架。

模型製作｜從動作到造型｜風乾黏土、木棒與鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished clay and stick model.
完成的黏土與木棒模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Playing the violin is a chain of quick arm movements that leave no trace. The student wanted to see the space created by the student's own bowing motions.
captions: Video frames of playing the violin, used to trace the motions.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 拉小提琴是一連串快速、不留痕跡的手臂動作。學生想看見自己的運弓動作所創造出的空間。
captions: 拉小提琴的影片截圖，用來追蹤動作。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A video of the student playing was broken down frame by frame to study each angle. The paths were layered in sketches to find where they meet.
captions: Clay shaped over the wire paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把自己演奏的影片逐格拆解，研究每個角度。這些路徑在草圖中層層疊合，找出彼此交會之處。
captions: 黏土包覆鐵絲路徑成形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wires twisted into a foam base were wrapped in clay to form half-closed caves. Wooden sticks then stretched the hollows outward like a skeleton.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 插在泡棉底座上的鐵絲被黏土包覆，形成半封閉的洞穴。接著以木棒把空洞向外延伸，如同骨架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model joins solid white caves with an open stick net. Light falling through the net casts shadows that echo the moving bow.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型結合白色實心洞穴與開放的木棒網架。穿過網架的光影，呼應移動中的琴弓。

sections.heading: Extension of Motions - Letting the Path of the Bow Leave a Space Behind
sections.body: Playing the violin is a chain of quick arm movements that leave no trace, and the student wanted to see the space created by the motions of the bow. The guidance first led the student to break down a video of the performance frame by frame to study each angle, then to layer these paths in sketches to find where they meet, so that fleeting movement was first fixed as lines that could be read. In development, wires set into a foam base were wrapped in clay to form half-closed caves, and wooden sticks then stretched the hollows outward like a skeleton, solid and void pulling against each other within one form. Finally, the model joins solid white caves with an open net of sticks, and light falling through the net casts shadows that echo the moving bow, so that a performance dissolved into the air leaves behind a shape where it can linger.

zh-Hant.heading: 動作的延伸-讓運弓的軌跡留下空間
zh-Hant.body: 拉小提琴是一連串快速而不留痕跡的手臂動作。學生想看見自己的運弓所創造出的空間。指導過程先引導學生把演奏的影片逐格拆解，研究每一個角度，再把這些路徑在草圖中層層疊合，找出彼此交會之處，讓轉瞬即逝的動作先被凝固為可以閱讀的線。進入推演，插在泡棉底座上的鐵絲被黏土包覆，形成半封閉的洞穴，再以木棒把空洞向外延伸，如同骨架，實與虛在同一個形體中相互拉扯。最後，模型結合白色的實心洞穴與開放的木棒網架，穿過網架的光影呼應著移動中的琴弓，讓一段消散於空氣的演奏，留下了可以停留的形狀。

admitted_schools.zh-Hant: 康乃爾大學建築本科 ED

pins.title: Three-Dimensional Violin Sound Waves
pins.description:
Sketched sound waves from a violin piece are rebuilt as triangles of sticks and board.

Model making | Sound to form | Wood sticks and PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 小提琴聲波的立體呈現
zh-Hant.description:
把小提琴樂曲的聲波草圖，重建為木棒與板材的三角形結構。

模型製作｜從聲音到造型｜木棒與PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sound waves from an instrument are invisible, yet they have shape and rhythm. The student wondered whether the waves of the violin the student plays were curved or sharp.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 樂器的聲波看不見，卻有形狀與節奏。學生好奇自己小提琴的聲波是彎曲的還是尖銳的。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student recorded a favourite piece and sketched its waves, linking their key points. The waves repeated with small changes, which suggested a triangular system.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生錄下喜愛的曲子並描繪聲波，把關鍵點連接起來。聲波重複中帶有細微變化，啟發了三角形的系統。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: PVC board was cut into triangles of many sizes to stand for each wave form. Sticks were glued into a frame, then added where the music grew more complex.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: PVC板被切成大小不一的三角形，代表各種波形。木棒先黏成框架，再在樂曲更複雜之處加密。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises in sharp peaks of sticks over white panels. Denser areas mark the busiest moments of the piece.
captions: The whole model on its base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以尖銳的木棒峰頂聳立在白色板面上。較密集的區域標示出曲中最繁複的時刻。
captions: 密集木棒呈現繁複的樂段。

sections.heading: Three-Dimensional Violin Sound Waves - Melody Rising into Sharp Peaks
sections.body: The sound waves of an instrument are invisible, yet they have shape and rhythm, and the student wondered whether the waves of a beloved violin were curved or sharp. The guidance first led the student to record a favourite piece and sketch its waves, linking their key points, and then to draw a triangular system from the way the waves repeat with small variations, so that music heard first became geometry that could be built. In development, PVC board was cut into triangles of many sizes to stand for each wave form, and sticks were glued into a frame and then added more densely where the music grew more complex, the density of the structure faithfully following the rise and fall of the piece. Finally, the model rises in sharp peaks of sticks over white panels, its denser areas marking the busiest moments of the music, so that a melody is held in space as a range of mountains.

zh-Hant.heading: 小提琴聲波的立體呈現-讓旋律長出尖峰
zh-Hant.body: 樂器的聲波看不見，卻有形狀與節奏。學生好奇，自己小提琴的聲波究竟是彎曲的，還是尖銳的？指導過程先引導學生錄下喜愛的曲子並描繪聲波，把關鍵點連接起來，再從聲波在重複中帶有細微變化的特性，找到三角形的系統，讓聽見的音樂先轉化為可以建構的幾何。進入推演，PVC板被切成大小不一的三角形，代表各種波形，木棒先黏成框架，再在樂曲更複雜之處加密，結構的疏密忠實跟隨音樂的起伏。最後，模型以尖銳的木棒峰頂聳立在白色板面之上，較密集的區域標示出曲中最繁複的時刻，讓一段旋律，在空間裡被凝成山脈。

pins.title: Blooming with the Bamboo
pins.description:
Layered petals of a chrysanthemum become arching bamboo strips around an open centre.

Model making | Nature to structure | Bamboo strips and wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 與竹共綻
zh-Hant.description:
菊花層層的花瓣化為環繞開放中心的拱形竹條。

模型製作｜從自然到結構｜竹條與木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A chrysanthemum packs many layers of petals into a small, ordered space. The student asked how that hidden complexity could be built at a larger scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 菊花在小小空間裡容納了層層有序的花瓣。學生思考如何以更大尺度建構這種隱藏的複雜性。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew the flower's main shape, structure and petal directions step by step. Bamboo strips alone were chosen to show its curves clearly.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生逐步描繪花的主要形狀、結構與花瓣方向。只選用竹條，以清楚呈現花的曲線。
captions: 第一版放射狀木棒框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A radiating stick frame was built first and repeated for the centre. Bamboo strips were then bent into arching petals in an oval outer ring.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 先搭建放射狀木棒框架，並在中心重複這套結構。接著把竹條彎成拱形花瓣，形成橢圓外環。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model blooms in layers of curved strips that viewers can look through. Repetition in the centre and outer ring keeps the flower's order.
captions: A low view through the petals.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以層層彎曲竹條綻放，觀者可穿透觀看內部。中心與外環的重複保留了花的秩序。

sections.heading: Blooming with the Bamboo - Enlarging the Order of a Chrysanthemum
sections.body: A chrysanthemum packs layer upon layer of ordered petals into a small space, and the student asked how that hidden complexity could be built at a larger scale. The guidance first led the student to draw the flower's main shape, structure and petal directions step by step, and then to choose bamboo strips alone so that its curves could be shown clearly, trading restraint in material for clarity of form. In development, a radiating stick frame was built first and its structure repeated at the centre, then bamboo strips were bent into arching petals forming an oval outer ring, the order unfolding ring by ring from the inside out. Finally, the model blooms in layers of curved strips that viewers can look through into its heart, and the repetition at the centre and outer ring keeps the flower's order, so that the precision of a single bloom still opens with ease once enlarged.

zh-Hant.heading: 與竹共綻-放大一朵菊花的秩序
zh-Hant.body: 一朵菊花，在小小的空間裡容納層層有序的花瓣。學生思考如何以更大的尺度，建構這份隱藏的複雜。指導過程先引導學生逐步描繪花的主要形狀、結構與花瓣方向，再刻意只選用竹條，讓曲線得以清楚呈現，以材料的克制換取形態的明晰。進入推演，先搭建放射狀的木棒框架，並在中心重複同一套結構，接著把竹條彎成拱形花瓣，形成橢圓的外環，秩序由內而外一圈圈展開。最後，模型以層層彎曲的竹條綻放，觀者可以穿透觀看內部，中心與外環的重複保留了花的秩序，讓一朵花的精密，在放大之後依然從容地盛開。

pins.title: Exploring Chinese Calligraphy
pins.description:
Free-flowing cursive strokes are rebuilt as curling bands of woven bamboo.

Model making | Calligraphy to space | Bamboo, wire and hot glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 探索中國書法
zh-Hant.description:
草書流動的筆畫，被重建為捲曲的編織竹帶。

模型製作｜從書法到空間｜竹、鐵絲與熱熔膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished woven bamboo model, lit at night.
夜間點燈的完成竹編模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cursive script moves freely and uses empty space boldly, but it lives flat on paper. The student asked what space its strokes would hold in three dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 草書自由流動、大膽運用留白，卻只存在於平面紙上。學生思考這些筆畫在三維中會包覆出怎樣的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied a classic cursive work and traced its strokes as abstract sketches. The sketches were turned into a 2D design that reads like layered terraces.
captions: Historic cursive calligraphy studied for its strokes.
Strokes turned into a layered terrace design.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一件經典草書作品，把筆畫描成抽象草圖。草圖再轉化為宛如層疊梯田的平面設計。
captions: 研究其筆畫的歷代草書書法。
筆畫轉化為層疊梯田的平面設計。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bamboo was chosen for its flexibility and sharp edges, which match the speed of the brush. Strips were woven into a hexagonal mesh and bent into twisting bands.
captions: Weaving the bamboo strips by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選用竹子，是因為它的柔韌與銳利呼應筆勢的速度。竹條被編成六角網格，再彎成扭轉的竹帶。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model curls and crosses like a line of cursive written in the air. Small lights inside cast the woven pattern across the space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型捲曲交錯，如同寫在空中的一行草書。內部的小燈把編織紋理投射到四周。

sections.heading: Exploring Chinese Calligraphy - Cursive Script Woven in Bamboo upon the Air
sections.body: Cursive script flows freely and uses empty space boldly, yet it lives only on flat paper, and the student asked what space its strokes would enclose in three dimensions. The guidance first led the student to study a classic work of cursive calligraphy and trace its strokes as abstract sketches, then to turn them into a two-dimensional design like layered terraces, so that the rhythm of the brush first found a structure on the plane. In development, bamboo was chosen because its flexibility and sharp edges match the speed of the brush, and strips were woven into a hexagonal mesh and bent into twisting bands, the character of the material and the spirit of the writing completing each other. Finally, the model curls and crosses like a line of cursive written in the air, and small lights inside cast the woven pattern across the surroundings, so that the breath of ink becomes light and shadow moving through space.

zh-Hant.heading: 探索中國書法-在空中書寫的竹編草書
zh-Hant.body: 草書自由流動，大膽運用留白，卻只存在於平面的紙上。學生思考這些筆畫在三維之中，會包覆出怎樣的空間。指導過程先引導學生研究一件經典草書作品，把筆畫描成抽象的草圖，再轉化為宛如層疊梯田的平面設計，讓筆勢的節奏先在二維中找到結構。進入推演，選用竹子，是因為它的柔韌與銳利恰好呼應運筆的速度，竹條被編成六角網格，再彎成扭轉的竹帶，材料的性格與書寫的氣韻彼此成全。最後，模型捲曲交錯，如同寫在空中的一行草書，內部的小燈把編織的紋理投射到四周，讓墨跡的呼吸，化為光影在空間裡流轉。

pins.title: Harmony in Nature
pins.description:
A classical garden model joins pavilions, rockery, water and planting in one balanced scene.

Model making | Classical garden design | Paper, wood sticks, model trees and stone | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然的和諧
zh-Hant.description:
一座古典園林模型，把亭台、假山、水景與植栽融為和諧的一景。

模型製作｜古典園林設計｜紙、木棒、模型樹與石材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Pavilion and arched bridge over the water.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Classical gardens now sit among high-rise towers, almost as borrowed scenery for the city. The student asked whether their techniques can still live in modern design.
captions: A classical garden among high-rise towers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 古典園林如今座落在高樓之間，幾乎成為城市的借景。學生思考這些造園手法能否在現代設計中延續。
captions: 高樓環繞中的古典庭園。
古典園林元素的分析圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched windows, pavilions and plans to study framing, borrowing and screening views. The student also looked at how plants change with water depth and humidity.
captions: The front elevation of the garden.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪花窗、亭台與平面，研究框景、借景與障景等手法。學生也觀察植物如何隨水深與濕度變化。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper and wood sticks formed walls, roofs and a bridge, while stone built up the rockery. Model trees were placed by height and density around the water.
captions: Building the garden model by hand.
Rockery and pavilion from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以紙與木棒製作牆垣、屋頂與橋，石材堆疊出假山。模型樹依高度與密度環繞水景配置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final garden balances solid rockery against open water and light planting. Each view through a gate or over the bridge reveals a new framed scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終園林以厚重假山對比開闊水面與輕盈植栽。穿過門洞或越過橋時，每一處都展開新的框景。

sections.heading: Harmony in Nature - Carrying the Art of the Garden Among Towers
sections.body: Classical gardens now sit among high-rise towers, almost as borrowed scenery for the city, and the student asked whether their techniques could still live in modern design. The guidance first led the student to sketch windows, pavilions and plans to study the framing, borrowing and screening of views, and then to observe how plants change with water depth and humidity, so that the craft of the gaze and the order of ecology were understood together. In development, paper and wood sticks formed walls, roofs and a bridge, stone built up the rockery, and model trees were placed by height and density around the water, each element finding its place within scale. Finally, the garden balances solid rockery against open water and light planting, and each passage through a gate or over the bridge opens a new framed scene, so that the old art of views changing with each step still has a place today.

zh-Hant.heading: 自然的和諧-在高樓之間延續造園之道
zh-Hant.body: 古典園林如今座落在高樓之間，幾乎成了城市的借景。學生思考這些造園手法能否在現代設計中延續。指導過程先引導學生描繪花窗、亭台與平面，研究框景、借景與障景等手法，再觀察植物如何隨水深與濕度變化，讓視線的經營與生態的秩序一同被理解。進入推演，以紙與木棒製作牆垣、屋頂與橋，石材堆疊出假山，模型樹依高度與密度環繞水景配置，每一個元素都在比例中找到位置。最後，園林以厚重的假山對比開闊的水面與輕盈的植栽，穿過門洞或越過橋時，每一處都展開新的框景，讓古老的步移景異，在今日仍有安放之處。

pins.title: The Echo of Lights
pins.description:
Clear coloured acrylic panels catch a spotlight and scatter it into moving colour.

Model making | Light and reflection | Acrylic board, PVC board and spotlight | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光的回響
zh-Hant.description:
透明彩色壓克力板承接聚光燈，把光散射成流動的色彩。

模型製作｜光與反射｜壓克力板、PVC板與聚光燈｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Panels spread out from the light source.
從光源向外擴散的壓克力板。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Coloured glass windows turn sunlight into a painting made of light. The student asked how a simple panel could guide light into a moving visual effect.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 彩色玻璃窗把陽光化為一幅由光構成的畫。學生思考簡單的板片如何引導光線，產生流動的視覺效果。
captions: 壓克力板折射出的彩色光線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student held acrylic panels under a spotlight to test angles, heights and combinations. Each setup bent and scattered the light in a different way.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把壓克力板置於聚光燈下，測試角度、高度與組合。每種配置都以不同方式折射與散射光線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Laser-cut panels were glued to the wall, densest near the light for rich reflections. Further out they spread apart so their shadows stretched longer.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 雷射切割的板片黏在牆上，靠近光源處最密集，反射最豐富。越往外越分散，陰影也越拉越長。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final piece fans out from the light like a spray of colour. To the student's surprise, the panels cast two sets of shadows across the wall.
captions: Watching the light pass through the panels.
Long double shadows on the wall.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終作品如一道彩色噴泉從光源展開。出乎學生意料，板片在牆上投下了兩組陰影。

sections.heading: The Echo of Lights - Guiding Light into Motion with Simple Panels
sections.body: Coloured glass windows turn sunlight into a painting made of light, and the student asked how a simple panel could guide light into a flowing visual effect. The guidance first led the student to hold acrylic panels under a spotlight and test angles, heights and combinations again and again, observing how each arrangement bent and scattered the light in its own way, so that the character of light was gradually revealed through experiment. In development, laser-cut panels were glued to the wall, densest near the light for the richest reflections and spreading apart further out so that their shadows stretched longer, density becoming a language for controlling light. Finally, the piece fans out from the light like a fountain of colour, and the panels unexpectedly cast two sets of shadows across the wall, so that a careful arrangement is answered by a surprise the light brings on its own.

zh-Hant.heading: 光的回響-以板片引導光的流動
zh-Hant.body: 彩色玻璃窗把陽光化為一幅由光構成的畫。學生思考簡單的板片如何引導光線，產生流動的視覺效果。指導過程先引導學生把壓克力板置於聚光燈下，反覆測試角度、高度與組合，觀察每種配置如何以不同方式折射與散射光線，讓光的性格在實驗中逐漸顯露。進入推演，雷射切割的板片黏在牆上，靠近光源處最密集，換取最豐富的反射，越往外越分散，讓陰影越拉越長，密度成為控制光的語言。最後，作品如一道彩色噴泉從光源展開，板片更出乎意料地在牆上投下兩組陰影，讓一次細心的安排，迎來一份光自己帶來的驚喜。

pins.title: Tower of Descending Feasts
pins.description:
A three-part clay tower, inspired by a film, shows food and greed flowing from the top down.

Model making | Film to form | Clay, wire, wood sticks and acrylic paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 層層下降的盛宴之塔
zh-Hant.description:
受一部電影啟發的三段式黏土高塔，呈現食物與貪婪由上而下流動。

模型製作｜從電影到造型｜黏土、鐵絲、木棒與壓克力顏料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished tower with its domed top.
頂部為圓頂的完成高塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A film about a vertical prison uses a descending food platform as a metaphor for inequality. The student wanted to turn its message about greed and survival into a model.
captions: Annotated sketch of the three levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於垂直監獄的電影，以下降的食物平台比喻不平等。學生想把它關於貪婪與生存的訊息轉化為模型。
captions: 標註三個階層的概念草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student rewatched the film and picked out greed, waste and revolt as its key themes. Stills of feasts and leftovers guided the mood of each level.
captions: The title card of the film that inspired the tower.
Film still of a crowded feast.
Film still of the food platform.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生重看電影，歸納出貪婪、浪費與反抗三個主題。盛宴與殘羹的畫面引導了各層的氛圍。
captions: 啟發這座塔的電影片名畫面。
電影中擁擠盛宴的畫面。
電影中散落殘餘的畫面。
電影中食物平台的畫面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The tower was split into three sections for three social classes. Clay over wire formed spikes, warped outlines and hanging strips around the frame.
captions: Shaping the clay and wire by hand.
Spikes and strands at the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 高塔分為三段，代表三個社會階層。鐵絲外包黏土，在框架周圍形成尖刺、扭曲輪廓與垂掛條帶。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The white tower rises from a ruined base to a calm dome at the top. Bright clay food stands out at first glance and thins out further down.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色高塔從殘破的底部升至頂端寧靜的圓頂。鮮豔的黏土食物一眼可見，越往下越稀少。

sections.heading: Tower of Descending Feasts - Sculpting Greed and Survival into a Vertical Fable
sections.body: A film about a vertical prison uses a slowly descending food platform as a metaphor for inequality, and the student wanted to turn its message about greed and survival into a model. The guidance first led the student to rewatch the film and draw out greed, waste and revolt as its key themes, then to set the mood of each level through stills of feasts and leftovers, so that the narrative first became the emotion of space. In development, the tower was divided into three sections for three social classes, and clay wrapped over wire formed spikes, warped outlines and hanging strips around the frame, the form itself carrying the pressure of class. Finally, the white tower rises from a ruined base to a calm dome at the top, its bright clay food striking at first glance and thinning further down, so that the height of a tower becomes a silent fable about who receives what.

zh-Hant.heading: 層層下降的盛宴之塔-把貪婪與生存塑成垂直寓言
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於垂直監獄的電影，以緩緩下降的食物平台比喻不平等。學生想把其中關於貪婪與生存的訊息轉化為模型。指導過程先引導學生重看電影，歸納出貪婪、浪費與反抗三個主題，再以盛宴與殘羹的畫面定下各層的氛圍，讓敘事先化為空間的情緒。進入推演，高塔分為三段，代表三個社會階層，鐵絲外包黏土，在框架周圍形成尖刺、扭曲的輪廓與垂掛的條帶，形體本身承載了階級的壓力。最後，白色高塔從殘破的底部升至頂端寧靜的圓頂，鮮豔的黏土食物一眼可見，越往下越稀少，讓一座塔的高度，成為一則關於分配的沉默寓言。

pins.title: Observation Deck: Haven
pins.description:
A hillside observation deck rebuilds the stacked timber joinery of an ancient pagoda with sticks.

Model making | Traditional structure | Wood sticks, popsicle sticks and clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 觀景台：避風港
zh-Hant.description:
一座山坡觀景台，以木棒重建古塔層層堆疊的木構榫卯。

模型製作｜傳統結構｜木棒、冰棒棍與黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished deck on its clay hill.
黏土山丘上的完成觀景台。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Traditional timber structures are admired but rarely used in new buildings. The student asked how an ancient wooden frame could serve a modern hillside deck.
captions: Drawing of the layered timber frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 傳統木構備受讚賞，卻很少用在新建築中。學生思考古老的木構架如何服務一座現代山坡觀景台。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied a historic wooden pagoda and found that each level nests a smaller ring inside a larger one. This socket-like layering explains its great stability.
captions: Digital model of the ring frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一座歷史木塔，發現每一層都在大環中嵌入小環。這種如套筒般的層疊，正是它穩固的原因。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stick joints that imitate mortise and tenon form the base, and sticks pave the floors. A two-layer platform came first, then a roof of popsicle-stick rafters.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 模仿榫卯的木棒節點構成基座，地板則以木棒鋪成。先完成雙層平台，再加上冰棒棍椽條的屋頂。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The deck sits on a clay hill with corridors and small platforms on both sides. Plain, straight rafters blend old craft with modern simplicity.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 觀景台座落在黏土山丘上，兩側有廊道與小平台。簡潔筆直的椽條，融合傳統工藝與現代簡約。

sections.heading: Observation Deck - An Ancient Timber Frame Sheltering a Hillside
sections.body: Traditional timber structures are widely admired yet rarely used in new buildings, and the student asked how an ancient wooden frame could serve a modern hillside observation deck. The guidance first led the student to study a historic wooden pagoda and discover that each level nests a smaller ring inside a larger one, a socket-like layering that is the secret of its stability, so that the intelligence of the structure was understood first. In development, stick joints imitating mortise and tenon formed the base and sticks paved the floors, a two-level platform came first and then a roof of popsicle-stick rafters, the construction rising step by step from the ground. Finally, the deck sits on a clay hill with corridors and small platforms reaching out on both sides, its plain straight rafters blending old craft with modern simplicity, turning a centuries-old skill into a haven for looking out in the mountain wind.

zh-Hant.heading: 觀景台-讓古老木構守護山坡
zh-Hant.body: 傳統木構備受讚賞，卻很少用於新的建築。學生思考古老的木構架如何服務一座現代的山坡觀景台。指導過程先引導學生研究一座歷史木塔，發現每一層都在大環之中嵌入小環，這種如套筒般的層疊，正是它穩固的祕密，讓結構的智慧先被看懂。進入推演，模仿榫卯的木棒節點構成基座，木棒鋪成地板，先完成雙層平台，再加上冰棒棍椽條的屋頂，構造按部就班地從地面升起。最後，觀景台座落在黏土山丘上，兩側延伸出廊道與小平台，簡潔筆直的椽條融合傳統工藝與現代簡約，讓一份千年的手藝，在山風之中，成為眺望的避風港。

pins.title: Sounds of Nature
pins.description:
Nets of shredded paper recall the sound of leaves and form a light resting shelter.

Model making | Sound and memory | Recycled paper and straws | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然之聲
zh-Hant.description:
碎紙編成的網，喚起樹葉的聲音，形成輕盈的休憩棚架。

模型製作｜聲音與記憶｜回收紙與吸管｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished shelter and its shadows.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Familiar sounds can bring back a place long after we have left it. The student asked whether a space could be built from the sound of a memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 熟悉的聲音能在多年後喚回一個地方。學生思考能否以一段記憶中的聲音建構空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The rustle of shredded paper reminded the student of wind in the trees of a childhood garden. The student first tried pairing the shreds with straws to suggest trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 碎紙的沙沙聲讓學生想起童年庭園裡風吹過樹葉。學生先嘗試把碎紙與吸管結合，暗示樹木。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The straws did not capture the mood, so the shreds were joined in pairs to form nets. The nets were pressed into the base like trunks meeting the ground.
captions: The low profile of the nets.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 吸管無法傳達氛圍，於是改把碎紙兩兩相連成網。網被壓入底座，如同樹幹扎入地面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The nets were kept apart so their shadows overlap in a staggered pattern. The result is a light public shelter whose shadows sway like leaves.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 網片彼此分開，使陰影錯落交疊。最終成為一座輕盈的公共棚架，陰影如樹葉般搖曳。

sections.heading: Sounds of Nature - Rebuilding a Childhood Garden from the Rustle of Paper
sections.body: Familiar sounds can bring a place back long after it has been left, and the student asked whether a space could be built from the sound of a memory. The guidance began with the rustle of shredded paper, which recalled wind through the trees of a childhood garden; a first attempt paired the shreds with straws to suggest trees but failed to carry the mood, so the guidance led the student back to the sound itself to begin again. In development, the shreds were joined in pairs to form nets that were pressed into the base like trunks meeting the ground, the lightness of the material answering the softness of the memory. Finally, the nets were deliberately kept apart so that their shadows overlap in a staggered pattern, and a light public shelter took shape whose shadows sway like leaves, letting a wind long gone blow once more through the light.

zh-Hant.heading: 自然之聲-以碎紙的沙沙聲重建童年庭園
zh-Hant.body: 熟悉的聲音，能在多年後喚回一個地方。學生思考能否以一段記憶中的聲音建構空間。指導過程從碎紙的沙沙聲開始，那聲響讓學生想起童年庭園裡風吹過樹葉，第一次嘗試把碎紙與吸管結合來暗示樹木，卻無法傳達那份氛圍，指導便引導學生回到聲音本身重新出發。進入推演，碎紙被兩兩相連成網，壓入底座，如同樹幹扎入地面，材料的輕盈與記憶的柔軟彼此呼應。最後，網片刻意彼此分開，讓陰影錯落交疊，一座輕盈的公共棚架就此成形，陰影如樹葉般搖曳，讓一陣早已遠去的風，在光裡重新吹過。

pins.title: Puzzle of Liminal Space
pins.description:
Five overlooked in-between spaces, from a pool to a long hallway, are stacked into one puzzle.

Model making | Liminal space | Wood board, resin, 3D print and LED | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 過渡空間的拼圖
zh-Hant.description:
五種常被忽略的過渡空間，從泳池到長廊，被堆疊成一個拼圖。

模型製作｜過渡空間｜木板、樹脂、3D列印與LED｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Hallways and stairwells are passed every day yet hardly noticed. The student wanted to bring these quiet, uncanny in-between spaces into focus.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 走廊與樓梯間每天經過，卻很少被注意。學生想讓這些安靜又詭異的過渡空間成為焦點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student gathered images of empty halls and drew from places that felt oddly familiar. Collages and sketches set out five spaces to connect.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生蒐集空曠大廳的影像，並從似曾相識的場所取材。拼貼與草圖定出五個要連接的空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The structure was modelled digitally, unrolled for laser cutting and 3D printed where curved. A tapered hallway with a warm light at the end exaggerates its length.
captions: Assembling the laser-cut parts by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 結構先數位建模，展開後雷射切割，曲面部分則以3D列印製作。漸縮的走廊盡頭點上暖光，誇大了它的深度。
captions: 親手組裝雷射切割零件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A pool with a spiral stair, a grey window block, a hallway, shelves and a playground lock together. Stairs and slides join them into one puzzle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 有旋轉樓梯的泳池、灰色窗格量體、長廊、書架與遊樂場相互咬合。樓梯與滑梯把它們串成一個拼圖。

sections.heading: Puzzle of Liminal Space - Bringing Forgotten Hallways into Focus
sections.body: Hallways and stairwells are passed every day yet hardly noticed, and the student wanted to bring these quiet, faintly uncanny in-between spaces into focus. The guidance first led the student to gather images of empty halls and draw from places that felt oddly familiar, then to set out five spaces to connect through collage and sketch, so that a vague feeling first gained a concrete outline. In development, the structure was modelled digitally, unrolled for laser cutting and 3D printed where curved, and a tapered hallway lit warmly at its end exaggerated its depth along with its uneasy familiarity. Finally, a pool with a spiral stair, a grey window block, a hallway, shelves and a playground lock together, stairs and slides joining them into a single puzzle, so that places once only passed through are at last paused before and seen.

zh-Hant.heading: 過渡空間的拼圖-讓被忽略的走廊成為主角
zh-Hant.body: 走廊與樓梯間每天經過，卻很少被注意。學生想讓這些安靜而略帶詭異的過渡空間成為焦點。指導過程先引導學生蒐集空曠大廳的影像，從那些似曾相識的場所取材，再以拼貼與草圖定出五個要相互連接的空間，讓模糊的感受先有了具體的輪廓。進入推演，結構先數位建模，展開後雷射切割，曲面部分以3D列印製作，一條漸縮的走廊在盡頭點上暖光，誇大了深度，也放大了那份不安的熟悉。最後，有旋轉樓梯的泳池、灰色窗格量體、長廊、書架與遊樂場彼此咬合，樓梯與滑梯把它們串成一幅拼圖，讓那些只是路過的地方，終於被停下來凝視。

pins.title: Tower Pointing Towards Brutalism
pins.description:
Bold concrete forms are recombined into a grey tower that rises with spikes pointing upward.

Model making | Retro-futurism | 3D print and grey plaster | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 指向粗獷主義之塔
zh-Hant.description:
厚重的混凝土造型被重組為一座向上尖刺聳立的灰色高塔。

模型製作｜復古未來主義｜3D列印與灰色石膏｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Retro-futurist art shows huge, hopeful towers, but real buildings in that heavy style are rarely tall. The student set out to build the tower those images promise.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 復古未來主義藝術描繪巨大而充滿希望的高塔，但這種厚重風格的真實建築很少是高樓。學生決定建造那些影像所許諾的高塔。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied dozens of heavy concrete buildings known for raw surfaces and one colour. Single modules were taken from them and reshaped.
captions: Five brutalist buildings whose forms became the tower's modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究數十棟以粗糙表面與單一色調著稱的混凝土建築。從中擷取單一模組並重新塑形。
captions: 五座粗獷主義建築，其形體成為塔的模組。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A first collage spread the parts outward to express strength but missed the idea of hope. The parts were regrouped so that they all climb and point upward.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一版拼貼讓構件向外擴張以表達力量，卻缺少希望的意涵。構件因此重組，全部向上攀升並指向天空。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 3D-printed tower was coated in grey plaster to mimic raw concrete. Sanded sharp edges keep both its strength and its fine details.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 3D列印的高塔塗上灰色石膏，模仿清水混凝土。打磨後的銳利邊角同時保留力量感與細節。

sections.heading: Tower Pointing Towards Brutalism - Fulfilling a Retro-Futurist Promise
sections.body: Retro-futurist art pictures huge, hopeful towers, yet real buildings in that heavy style are rarely tall, and the student set out to build the tower those images promise. The guidance first led the student to study dozens of concrete buildings known for raw surfaces and a single colour, taking individual modules from them and reshaping them, so that the vocabulary of a style first became units that could be worked. In development, a first collage spread the parts outward to express strength but missed the idea of hope, so the parts were regrouped to climb and point upward together, the correction itself becoming part of the understanding. Finally, the 3D-printed tower was coated in grey plaster to mimic raw concrete, its sanded sharp edges keeping both strength and fine detail, so that a heavy tower at last learns to look up.

zh-Hant.heading: 指向粗獷主義之塔-兌現復古未來的許諾
zh-Hant.body: 復古未來主義的藝術描繪巨大而充滿希望的高塔，但這種厚重風格的真實建築卻很少是高樓。學生決定建造那些影像所許諾的塔。指導過程先引導學生研究數十棟以粗糙表面與單一色調著稱的混凝土建築，從中擷取單一模組並重新塑形，讓風格的語彙先成為可操作的單元。進入推演，第一版拼貼讓構件向外擴張以表達力量，卻遺漏了希望的意涵，於是構件重新組合，全部向上攀升、指向天空，修正本身成為理解的一部分。最後，3D列印的高塔塗上灰色石膏，模仿清水混凝土，打磨後的銳利邊角同時保留力量與細節，讓一座沉重的塔，終於學會仰望。

pins.title: Boundless Spatial Memory
pins.description:
A familiar route through a home becomes a stick model with enlarged memory anchors.

Model making | Memory and space | Wood sticks, 3D print, resin and cotton | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無邊的空間記憶
zh-Hant.description:
一條熟悉的居家路線，化為放大記憶錨點的木棒模型。

模型製作｜記憶與空間｜木棒、3D列印、樹脂與棉花｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A memory technique stores ideas along a familiar route of rooms. The student asked how the spaces we pass every day shape the way we think.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 有一種記憶法把知識存放在熟悉的房間路線上。學生思考每天經過的空間如何塑造我們的思考方式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student chose four areas along a route at home that the student used to memorise study notes. The features the student relied on were enlarged and exaggerated.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生選了家中一條路線上的四個區域，那是學生用來記憶課業的地方。學生依賴的空間特徵被放大並誇張化。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks were glued along the plan, with stairs dropping below it to vary the levels. 3D-printed objects, gears, resin and cotton became anchors for each memory.
captions: The route with its memory anchors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒依平面黏合，樓梯向下延伸以改變高程。3D列印物件、齒輪、樹脂與棉花，成為每段記憶的錨點。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model reads as a journey from room to room, each marked by a strange object. Together they tell the story of how memory lives in space.
captions: A room filled with cotton clouds.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讀起來像一段穿越房間的旅程，每處都有奇特物件標記。它們共同講述記憶如何寄存在空間中。

sections.heading: Boundless Spatial Memory - Walking Through the Rooms Where Memory Lives
sections.body: One memory technique stores knowledge along a familiar route of rooms, and from it the student asked how the spaces passed every day shape the way we think. The guidance first led the student to choose four areas along a route at home, the very places used to memorise study notes, and then to enlarge and exaggerate the spatial features relied upon, so that hidden cues of memory rose to the surface. In development, sticks were glued along the plan with stairs dropping below to vary the levels, and 3D-printed objects, gears, resin and cotton became anchors for each memory, space and recollection recognising each other through differences of material. Finally, the model reads as a journey from room to room, each marked by a strange object, together telling how memory lives inside space, so that a path once walked becomes a map of thought.

zh-Hant.heading: 無邊的空間記憶-走進記憶寄居的房間
zh-Hant.body: 有一種記憶法，把知識存放在熟悉的房間路線上。學生由此追問：每天經過的空間，如何塑造我們思考的方式？指導過程先引導學生選出家中一條路線上的四個區域，那正是平日用來記憶課業的地方，再把所依賴的空間特徵放大並誇張化，讓隱而不顯的記憶線索浮上表面。進入推演，木棒沿著平面黏合，樓梯向下延伸改變高程，3D列印物件、齒輪、樹脂與棉花，成為每段記憶的錨點，空間與記憶在材料的差異中互相指認。最後，模型讀來像一段穿越房間的旅程，每處都有一件奇特的物件標記，共同講述記憶如何寄居在空間之中，讓走過的路，成為思想的地圖。

pins.title: Vase of the City
pins.description:
A 3D-printed planter borrows the lattice facades of city towers to help newcomers feel at home.

Model making | Parametric product | 3D print (PLA) | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市之瓶
zh-Hant.description:
一個3D列印花器借用城市高樓的格柵立面，讓新移居者感到歸屬。

模型製作｜參數化產品｜3D列印（PLA）｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many people who move to a fast-growing city struggle to feel they belong there. The student wanted an everyday object that ties them to the city around them.
captions: A glass tower photographed on the city walk.
A lattice facade in the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多移居快速發展城市的人，難以產生歸屬感。學生想做一件日常物品，把他們與周遭的城市連結起來。
captions: 城市漫步中拍攝的玻璃高樓。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student toured the city photographing building exteriors and traced their patterns on paper. The patterns were compared to find the best one for a vase.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生走訪城市拍攝建築外觀，並把圖案描在紙上。比較各種圖案，找出最適合花瓶的一種。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Because many identical vases were needed, the student fully adopted 3D modelling and printing. A parametric script generated the lattice shell, and square pillars like rebar hold the inner pot.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 因為需要大量相同的花瓶，學生全面採用3D建模與列印。參數化程式生成格柵外殼，如鋼筋般的方柱支撐內盆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The white lattice vase holds plants while echoing the towers outside. Planting it turns a reminder of the city into a small act of care.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色格柵花瓶容納植物，同時呼應窗外的高樓。種植它，讓城市的印記成為一份小小的照顧。

sections.heading: Vase of the City - Planting the Texture of Towers into Everyday Life
sections.body: Many people who move to a fast-growing city struggle to feel they belong, and the student wanted an everyday object that could tie them to the city around them. The guidance first led the student to walk the city photographing building exteriors and tracing their patterns on paper, then to compare them one by one to find the best for a vase, so that the face of the city was first looked at closely. In development, because many identical vases were needed, the student fully adopted 3D modelling and printing, with a parametric script generating the lattice shell and square pillars like rebar holding the inner pot, the structural logic of the city shrunk into an object for the hand. Finally, the white lattice vase holds plants while echoing the towers outside, and the act of planting turns a trace of the city into a small gesture of care, letting an unfamiliar place slowly become home through daily watering.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市之瓶-把高樓的紋理種進日常
zh-Hant.body: 許多移居快速發展城市的人，難以生出歸屬感。學生想做一件日常的物品，把人與周遭的城市連結起來。指導過程先引導學生走訪城市，拍攝建築的外觀，把圖案描在紙上，再逐一比較，找出最適合花瓶的一種，讓城市的面貌先被細細看見。進入推演，由於需要大量相同的花瓶，學生全面採用3D建模與列印，參數化程式生成格柵外殼，如鋼筋般的方柱支撐內盆，城市的構造邏輯被縮小為手中的器物。最後，白色格柵花瓶容納植物，同時呼應窗外的高樓，種植它的動作，讓城市的印記化為一份小小的照顧，也讓異鄉，在日日澆灌中慢慢成為家。

pins.title: Cats and Humans: A Vertical Apartment
pins.description:
An apartment where cats climb a tangle of jump paths while people live in a simple timber frame.

Model making | Animal movement | PVC board, wood and hot melt glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 貓與人：垂直公寓
zh-Hant.description:
一座公寓裡，貓在交錯的跳躍路徑間攀爬，人則住在簡潔的木構框架中。

模型製作｜動物行為｜PVC板、木材與熱熔膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Homes are stacked in flat floors joined by stairs, but cats move by climbing and leaping. The student asked whether one apartment could suit both ways of moving.
captions: Video frames of a cat jumping.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 住宅以樓梯連接一層層平坦樓板，但貓靠攀爬與跳躍移動。學生思考一間公寓能否同時適合兩種移動方式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student filmed a cat hunting and traced each jump and landing frame by frame. Each pose was simplified into straight lines that suggest a path.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拍攝貓捕獵的影片，逐格描繪每次跳躍與落地。每個姿態被簡化為暗示路徑的直線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each path was modelled as a small space sized to a cat and the pieces were combined. The human part was kept to a plain square timber frame.
captions: Assembling the apartment and packing the parts.
The timber frame with cat paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每條路徑都被建模成符合貓尺寸的小空間，再組合在一起。人的部分則保持為簡單方正的木構框架。
captions: 組裝公寓模型並打包零件。
帶有貓路徑的木構框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Cat paths weave through the frame above a calm living floor for people. A pencil drawing and photos look up through the busy vertical world.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 貓的路徑穿梭在框架中，下方是安靜的人居樓層。鉛筆圖與照片向上望穿這個熱鬧的垂直世界。

sections.heading: Cats and Humans - A Vertical Apartment for Leaping and Walking
sections.body: Homes stack flat floors joined by stairs, but cats move by climbing and leaping, and the student asked whether one apartment could hold both ways of moving. The guidance first led the student to film a cat hunting and trace each jump and landing frame by frame, then to simplify every pose into straight lines suggesting a path, so that the rhythm of an animal's body first became a drawing that could be read. In development, each path was modelled as a small space sized to a cat and the pieces were combined, while the human part was deliberately kept to a plain square timber frame, the two scales each made clear through contrast. Finally, cat paths weave through the frame above a calm living floor for people, and a pencil drawing and photographs look up through this busy vertical world, giving two kinds of life under one roof each a sky of their own.

zh-Hant.heading: 貓與人-跳躍與步行共居的垂直公寓
zh-Hant.body: 住宅以樓梯連接一層層平坦的樓板，貓卻靠攀爬與跳躍移動。學生追問：一間公寓能否同時容納兩種移動方式？指導過程先引導學生拍攝貓捕獵的影片，逐格描繪每一次跳躍與落地，再把每個姿態簡化為暗示路徑的直線，讓動物的身體節奏先成為可被閱讀的圖。進入推演，每條路徑被建模成符合貓尺寸的小空間並組合在一起，人的部分則刻意保持為簡單方正的木構框架，兩種尺度在對比中各自清晰。最後，貓的路徑穿梭於框架之上，下方是安靜的人居樓層，鉛筆圖與照片向上望穿這個熱鬧的垂直世界，讓兩種生命在同一屋簷下，各有各的天空。

pins.title: Coconut for Arch
pins.description:
Coconut fibre bound with glue is cast into a light, cave-like arch.

Material study | Natural fibre | Coconut fibre, white glue and water | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 椰子之拱
zh-Hant.description:
以膠水黏合的椰子纖維，鑄成輕盈如洞穴的拱。

材料研究｜天然纖維｜椰子纖維、白膠與水｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A coconut can drift across an ocean, yet its hard shell alone sinks. The student wanted to know what makes it float and whether that could become a building material.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 椰子能漂洋過海，但單獨的硬殼卻會下沉。學生想知道它浮起的原因，以及能否成為建築材料。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student found that the outer fibre layer is full of tiny air pockets that give buoyancy. Fibre, tea leaf residue and coconut jelly were tested as mixes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生發現外層纖維充滿細小氣室，提供浮力。學生測試了纖維、茶渣與椰果等混合配方。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Fibre coated with glue and water was dried on round objects to copy the husk. Tunnels carved into foam made a mould like an ant nest.
captions: Gluing the coconut fibre into the mould.
Tunnels carved into a foam mould.
Fibre sheets dried on round forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塗上膠水的纖維在圓形物上乾燥，模仿椰殼外層。在泡棉中刻出的通道則形成如蟻巢般的模具。
captions: 在泡棉模具中刻出的通道。
在圓形模上乾燥的纖維片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The cast is strong yet light, with arches and hollows like a cave. Scale figures show how natural material can shape a sheltering space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鑄件堅固而輕盈，拱與空洞宛如洞穴。比例人偶展示天然材料如何塑造庇護空間。

sections.heading: Coconut for Arch - A Cave Grown from a Drifting Fruit
sections.body: A coconut can drift across an ocean, yet its hard shell alone will sink, and the student wanted to know what keeps it afloat and whether that strength could become a building material. The guidance first led the student to discover that the outer fibre layer is full of tiny air pockets, the true source of buoyancy, and then to test mixes of fibre, tea leaf residue and coconut jelly, so that a natural structure came to be understood through experiment. In development, fibre coated with glue was dried over round objects to imitate the husk, and tunnels carved into foam formed a mould like an ant nest, material and space meeting in a single cast. Finally, the cast is strong yet light, its arches and hollows like a cave, and scale figures show how a natural material can shape a sheltering space, letting a fruit carried by the waves leave behind a curve one can dwell in.

zh-Hant.heading: 椰子之拱-從漂流的果實長出洞穴
zh-Hant.body: 椰子能漂洋過海，單獨的硬殼卻會下沉。學生想知道它浮起的原因，以及這份力量能否成為建築材料。指導過程先引導學生發現外層纖維充滿細小氣室，正是浮力的來源，再測試纖維、茶渣與椰果等混合配方，讓自然的構造在實驗中逐步被理解。進入推演，塗上膠水的纖維在圓形物上乾燥，模仿椰殼的外層，泡棉中刻出的通道則形成如蟻巢般的模具，材料與空間在同一次鑄造中相遇。最後，鑄件堅固而輕盈，拱與空洞宛如洞穴，比例人偶顯示天然材料如何塑造庇護的空間，讓一顆隨浪漂流的果實，留下可以棲身的弧形。

pins.title: Cat Shelter
pins.description:
A resin tree shelter copies a cat's pupil and ear to shade, listen and glow.

Model making | Biomimicry | Resin, steel bars, optical fibre and wood | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 貓的庇護所
zh-Hant.description:
一座樹脂樹形庇護所，模仿貓的瞳孔與耳朵來遮陽、聆聽與發光。

模型製作｜仿生設計｜樹脂、鋼條、光纖與木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The shelter glowing in the dark.
在黑暗中發光的庇護所。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cats like hidden spots where they can still watch the world. The student designed a shelter that answers a cat's sharp senses.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 貓喜歡隱蔽又能觀察外界的地方。學生設計一座回應貓敏銳感官的庇護所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A cat's pupil widens and narrows with light, and its ears gather faint sounds. These two senses became the rules for the roof and the lights.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 貓的瞳孔隨光線放大縮小，耳朵能收集細微聲音。這兩種感官成為屋頂與燈光的設計規則。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A light sensor and filtered rainwater on the roof shade the inside in strong sun and drain away in dim light. Branches of steel and optical fibre grow inside a clear resin shell.
captions: Wiring the fibres and shaping the resin shell.
The water roof and a cat figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂的光感測器與過濾雨水，在強光時遮蔭，光線不足時排走。鋼條與光纖的枝幹在透明樹脂殼內生長。
captions: 佈設光纖並塑造樹脂外殼。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Cats can rest on the branches while sound sensors change the light colour to warn of danger. The shelter glows like a tree at night.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 貓可在枝幹上休息，聲音感測器會改變燈光顏色以提示危險。庇護所在夜裡如一棵發光的樹。

sections.heading: Cat Shelter - A Tree of Light Designed by Pupil and Ear
sections.body: Cats love hidden corners from which they can still watch the world, and the student designed a shelter that answers a cat's sharp senses. The guidance first led the student to observe how a cat's pupil widens and narrows with light and how its ears gather faint sounds, then to turn these two senses into rules for the roof and the lighting, so that the animal's body became the brief for the building. In development, a light sensor and filtered rainwater on the roof shade the interior in strong sun and drain away in dim light, while branches of steel and optical fibre grow inside a clear resin shell, the logic of the senses realised piece by piece as construction. Finally, cats can rest on the branches while sound sensors shift the colour of the light to warn of danger, and the shelter glows at night like a tree, gently guarding eyes that stay awake in the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 貓的庇護所-以瞳孔與耳朵設計的光之樹
zh-Hant.body: 貓喜歡隱蔽的角落，卻又想看著外面的世界。學生設計一座回應貓敏銳感官的庇護所。指導過程先引導學生觀察貓的瞳孔如何隨光線放大縮小，耳朵如何收集細微的聲音，再把這兩種感官轉化為屋頂與燈光的設計規則，讓動物的身體成為建築的說明書。進入推演，屋頂的光感測器與過濾雨水，在強光時遮蔭、光線不足時排走，鋼條與光纖的枝幹在透明樹脂殼內生長，感官的邏輯逐一落實為構造。最後，貓可在枝幹上休憩，聲音感測器則以燈光顏色的變化提示危險，庇護所在夜裡如一棵發光的樹，溫柔地守護著一雙在黑暗中仍然清醒的眼睛。

pins.title: Reinventing a Family House
pins.description:
An old family house is redesigned around a shared courtyard learned from round earthen houses.

Model making | Vernacular housing | Laser-cut wood board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重塑家族老屋
zh-Hant.description:
一座家族老屋以圓形土樓的共享中庭為靈感重新設計。

模型製作｜傳統民居｜雷射切割木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was asked to rebuild an old family villa in a historic town. The student wanted to bring back the joy of the old house with a modern layout.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生受託重建歷史小鎮中的一棟家族老宅。學生想以現代格局找回老屋的歡樂。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied the town's round earthen houses, where many families share a central courtyard behind thick walls. Their flexible routes and shared ground became key ideas.
captions: Study of a round earthen house.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究鎮上的圓形土樓，許多家庭在厚牆後共享中央庭院。靈活的動線與共享地面成為關鍵概念。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many tracing-paper sketches over the old plans were merged into one design and modelled digitally. Walls were laser cut and assembled piece by piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在舊平面上以描圖紙畫下大量草圖，合併為一個設計並數位建模。牆面以雷射切割，再逐片組裝。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Curved wings wrap a patterned courtyard with stairs and open frames. The house blends a shared vernacular layout with a light modern structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 弧形翼樓環抱帶有圖案的中庭，配有樓梯與開放框架。住宅融合了共享的傳統格局與輕盈的現代結構。

sections.heading: Reinventing a Family House - Recovering Gathering Through the Memory of Round Houses
sections.body: The student was asked to rebuild an old family villa in a historic town, hoping to bring back the joy the old house once held through a modern layout. The guidance first led the student to study the town's round earthen houses, observing how many families share a central courtyard behind thick walls, so that flexible routes and shared ground became the key ideas of the design. In development, many tracing-paper sketches were drawn over the old plans, compared layer by layer and merged into one design that was modelled digitally, and the walls were laser cut and assembled piece by piece, the traditional layout slowly surfacing within a new structure. Finally, curved wings wrap a patterned courtyard threaded with stairs and open frames, and the house blends a shared vernacular layout with a light modern structure, giving a family's gatherings a place to return to once more.

zh-Hant.heading: 重塑家族老屋-在圓樓的記憶裡重拾歡聚
zh-Hant.body: 學生受託重建歷史小鎮中的一棟家族老宅，希望以現代的格局，找回老屋曾有的歡樂。指導過程先引導學生研究鎮上的圓形土樓，觀察許多家庭如何在厚牆之後共享一座中央庭院，讓靈活的動線與共享的地面，成為設計的關鍵概念。進入推演，學生在舊平面上以描圖紙畫下大量草圖，層層比對後合併為一個設計並數位建模，牆面再以雷射切割，一片片組裝成形，傳統的格局在新的結構中慢慢顯影。最後，弧形翼樓環抱著帶有圖案的中庭，樓梯與開放框架穿插其間，住宅融合共享的在地格局與輕盈的現代結構，讓一個家族的團聚，重新有了可以回去的地方。

pins.title: Different Tone: Rich and Varied Space
pins.description:
The rising and falling tones of a recited poem are turned into blocks that stack into a tower.

Model making | Sound and language | Wood, clear acrylic and PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 不同的聲調：豐富多變的空間
zh-Hant.description:
朗誦詩句時起伏的聲調，被轉化為層層堆疊成塔的量體。

模型製作｜聲音與語言｜木材、透明壓克力與PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Two Chinese dialects share the same characters yet sound very different, one with four tones and one with nine. The student wanted to make that difference visible as space.
captions: A painting of the classic poem chosen as the case study.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 兩種漢語方言共用同樣的文字，聽起來卻差異很大，一種有四個聲調，另一種有九個。學生想把這種差異化為可見的空間。
captions: 作為案例的經典詩作之畫作。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student recorded a classical poem read in both dialects and studied the spectrograms. Each syllable's tone was traced as a simple line symbol.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生錄下以兩種方言朗誦的一首古詩，並研究聲譜圖。每個音節的聲調都被描成簡單的線條符號。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The tone lines were drawn digitally and given thickness to become blocks. Following the order of the poem, the blocks were combined and stretched where the reading is most emphatic.
captions: Stacking the tone blocks into the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 聲調線條以數位方式繪製並賦予厚度成為量體。依照詩句的順序組合量體，並在朗誦最強調之處加以拉伸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Wood and acrylic panels rise into a dense tower full of narrow gaps and platforms. Scale figures show how the rhythm of speech becomes a varied, climbable space.
captions: Side view of the stacked panels.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 木板與壓克力板升起成為一座密集的塔，充滿窄縫與平台。比例人偶顯示說話的節奏如何成為豐富可攀的空間。

sections.heading: Different Tone - Stacking the Rise and Fall of Dialect into a Tower
sections.body: Two Chinese dialects share the same characters yet sound worlds apart, one with four tones and the other with nine, and the student wanted to make that difference visible as space. The guidance first led the student to record a classical poem read in both dialects and study its spectrograms, then to trace each syllable's tone as a simple line symbol, so that the rise and fall of hearing first settled as strokes on paper. In development, the tone lines were drawn digitally and given thickness to become blocks, combined in the order of the poem and stretched where the reading is most emphatic. Finally, wood and acrylic panels rise into a dense tower full of narrow gaps and platforms, and scale figures show how the rhythm of speech becomes a varied, climbable space, letting the voice of a poem settle into architecture layer by layer.

zh-Hant.heading: 不同的聲調-把方言的起伏堆成高塔
zh-Hant.body: 兩種漢語方言共用同樣的文字，聽起來卻相去甚遠，一種有四個聲調，另一種有九個。學生想讓這份差異成為看得見的空間。指導過程先引導學生錄下以兩種方言朗誦的一首古詩，研究其聲譜圖，再把每個音節的聲調描成簡單的線條符號，讓聽覺的起伏先落為紙上的筆畫。進入推演，聲調線條以數位方式繪製並賦予厚度成為量體，依照詩句的順序組合，並在朗誦最強調之處加以拉伸。最後，木板與壓克力板升起成一座充滿窄縫與平台的密集高塔，比例人偶顯示說話的節奏如何成為豐富可攀的空間，讓一首詩的聲音，被一層層住進建築裡。

pins.title: Hive in the Sand
pins.description:
Folding honeycomb paper grows into a sphere, shelters and towers imagined for the desert.

Material study | Honeycomb structure | Honeycomb paper and marker sketches | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沙中蜂巢
zh-Hant.description:
可伸縮的蜂巢紙長成球體、庇護所與塔，構想於沙漠之中。

材料研究｜蜂巢結構｜蜂巢紙與麥克筆草圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Honeycomb paper is used as packing, yet it can stretch, fold and stand on its own. The student asked whether this humble material could suggest new structures for harsh places.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 蜂巢紙常用於包裝，卻能伸展、折疊並自行站立。學生思考這種平凡材料能否為嚴酷環境帶來新的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how geometric patterns are fitted to different shapes in traditional ornament. The same method guided how cones and fans were spread across a sphere.
captions: Geometric relief works studied for their texture and form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究傳統紋樣如何將幾何圖案配合不同形狀。同樣的方法引導學生把錐體與扇形分布在球面上。
captions: 研究其紋理與形體的幾何浮雕作品。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wrapping the paper around sticks made small towers of hexagon cells. Sketches imagined prefabricated units that people could combine into homes in the dunes.
captions: Stretching the honeycomb paper by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 把紙纏繞在棍上，形成由六角格構成的小塔。草圖構想人們可組合成沙丘住宅的預製單元。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The sphere, animal shelter and curved wall show one material taking many forms. Marker drawings picture a city that grows with the desert rather than against it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 球體、動物庇護所與弧牆展現一種材料的多種形態。麥克筆圖描繪一座與沙漠共生而非對抗的城市。

sections.heading: Hive in the Sand - A Desert City Folded from Humble Paper
sections.body: Honeycomb paper is made for packing, yet it can stretch, fold and stand on its own, and the student asked whether such a humble material could bring new structures to harsh places. The guidance first led the student to study how traditional ornament fits geometric patterns to different shapes, and then to use the same method to spread cones and fans across a sphere, so that the wisdom of decoration became the logic of structure. In development, the paper was wrapped around sticks into small towers of hexagonal cells, and sketches imagined prefabricated units that people could combine into homes among the dunes. Finally, a sphere, an animal shelter and a curved wall show one material taking many forms, and marker drawings picture a city that grows with the desert rather than against it, letting thin paper stand as a home amid wind and sand.

zh-Hant.heading: 沙中蜂巢-平凡紙材裡的沙漠城市
zh-Hant.body: 蜂巢紙原是包裝材料，卻能伸展、折疊並自行站立。學生追問：這種平凡的材料，能否為嚴酷的環境帶來新的結構？指導過程先引導學生研究傳統紋樣如何把幾何圖案貼合於不同形狀，再以同樣的方法，把錐體與扇形分布在球面上，讓裝飾的智慧轉化為結構的邏輯。進入推演，紙被纏繞在木棒上，形成由六角格構成的小塔，草圖進一步構想可被人們組合成沙丘住宅的預製單元。最後，球體、動物庇護所與弧牆展現一種材料的多種形態，麥克筆圖描繪出一座與沙漠共生而非對抗的城市，讓輕薄的紙，在風沙之中站成家園。

pins.title: Flowing Reed Pavilion
pins.description:
A summer group workshop bends steel wire and reeds into a flowing outdoor pavilion.

Group workshop | Pavilion build | Steel wire, reeds and digital modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動蘆葦亭
zh-Hant.description:
一場暑期團體工作坊，將鋼絲與蘆葦彎折成流動的戶外涼亭。

團體工作坊｜涼亭搭建｜鋼絲、蘆葦與數位建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The workshop asked how a light pavilion could be made from simple, sustainable materials. The form had to come from what wire and reeds can naturally do.
captions: Sketches of bending and twisting wire.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 工作坊探討如何以簡單、永續的材料做出輕盈的涼亭。形態必須來自鋼絲與蘆葦本身能做到的事。
captions: 鋼絲彎折與扭轉的草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student first sketched ways a wire can bend and twist into loops. Small models tested these curves with reed covering on the ground.
captions: A small wire and reed model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先草繪鋼絲彎折、扭轉成環的方式。小模型則在地面上測試這些曲線與蘆葦覆面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chosen form was refined digitally and then built as a team on site. Scaffolding, welding, lighting and reed weaving were done step by step.
captions: Building the reed frame on site.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選定的形態以數位方式修整，再由團隊在現場搭建。鷹架、焊接、燈光與蘆葦編織逐步完成。
captions: 現場以蘆葦包覆的柱子。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A long woven ribbon sweeps over curved legs and seats on the lawn. The build taught form, structure and construction as one connected process.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條長長的編織帶越過草地上的弧形支腳與座椅。這次搭建把形態、結構與施工當作一個相連的過程來學習。

sections.heading: Flowing Reed Pavilion - Letting Material Speak Its Own Form
sections.body: Could a light pavilion be made from nothing more than simple, sustainable materials? The workshop's answer was to let form grow out of what wire and reeds can naturally do. The guidance first led the student to sketch how wire bends and twists into loops, then to test those curves with reed covering in small models on the ground, so that the temperament of the material spoke before any idea. In development, the chosen form was refined digitally and then built as a team on site, with scaffolding, welding, lighting and reed weaving completed step by step, each stage another confirmation of the form. Finally, a long woven ribbon sweeps over curved legs and seats on the lawn, and the build turns form, structure and construction into one connected process, leaving on the grass a breeze that has been woven into shape.

zh-Hant.heading: 流動蘆葦亭-讓材料自己說出形態
zh-Hant.body: 一座輕盈的涼亭，能否只以簡單而永續的材料做成？工作坊給出的答案，是讓形態從鋼絲與蘆葦本身的能力中長出來。指導過程先引導學生草繪鋼絲如何彎折、扭轉成環，再以小模型在地面上測試這些曲線與蘆葦覆面，讓材料的脾性先於構想發言。進入推演，選定的形態以數位方式修整，再由團隊在現場一同搭建，鷹架、焊接、燈光與蘆葦編織逐步完成，每一道工序都是對形態的再一次確認。最後，一條長長的編織帶越過草地上的弧形支腳與座椅，這次搭建讓形態、結構與施工成為一個相連的過程，也讓一片草地上，多了一陣被編織起來的風。

pins.title: Wilderness & Urbanization
pins.description:
Sounds recorded on a hike from city to forest become a landscape where towers meet wild growth.

Model making | Sound and landscape | Paper, glue and digital modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 荒野與城市化
zh-Hant.description:
從城市走向山林的健行錄音，化為高樓與野生植物交會的地景。

模型製作｜聲音與地景｜紙、膠與數位建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished city and wilderness model.
完成的城市與荒野模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As cities expand, wild land is pushed further away. The student asked how natural landscape could be kept alive inside a growing city.
captions: Hiking route traced over a map.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 城市擴張時，荒野被推得越來越遠。學生思考如何在成長中的城市裡保留自然地景。
captions: 描在地圖上的健行路線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: On a hike away from the city the student recorded both traffic and forest sounds. The two recordings were turned into wave patterns with clear contrast.
captions: City and nature sounds as waves.
Paper layers set in a frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 在離開城市的健行中，學生錄下車流與森林的聲音。兩段錄音被轉成對比鮮明的波形圖案。
captions: 城市與自然聲音的波形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The waves were cut into paper strips and layered as rolling ground. Towers were modelled digitally to rise from the loud city parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 波形被裁成紙條，層疊成起伏的地面。高樓以數位方式建模，從聲音嘈雜的城市段落升起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: White towers and wild trees share one contoured ground. The model asks the viewer to hear the tension between city and nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色高樓與野生樹木共享同一片等高地面。模型邀請觀者聽見城市與自然之間的張力。

sections.heading: Wilderness and Urbanization - Hearing the Tension in Sound Waves
sections.body: As cities expand, wild land is pushed ever further away, and the student asked how natural landscape could be kept alive within a growing city. The guidance first led the student, on a hike away from the city, to record both traffic and forest sounds, then to turn the two recordings into strongly contrasting wave patterns, so that a difference heard by the ear first became a shape the eye could read. In development, the waves were cut into paper strips and layered into rolling ground, and towers were modelled digitally to rise from the loudest, most urban passages, the intensity of sound deciding where landscape and building would fall. Finally, white towers and wild trees share one contoured ground, and the model invites the viewer to hear the tension between city and nature, turning the sound memory of a hike into a question about living together.

zh-Hant.heading: 荒野與城市化-聽見聲波裡的張力
zh-Hant.body: 城市擴張時，荒野被推得越來越遠，學生思考如何在成長中的城市裡保留自然地景。指導過程先引導學生在一次離開城市的健行中，錄下車流與森林的聲音，再把兩段錄音轉成對比鮮明的波形圖案，讓耳朵聽見的差異先成為眼睛可讀的形狀。進入推演，波形被裁成紙條，層層疊成起伏的地面，高樓則以數位方式建模，從聲音嘈雜的城市段落升起，聲音的強弱於是決定了地景與建築的分布。最後，白色高樓與野生樹木共享同一片等高地面，模型邀請觀者聽見城市與自然之間的張力，讓一段健行的聲音記憶，成為關於共存的提問。

pins.title: Growing Spires
pins.description:
A tree is broken into lines, curves and spheres, then rebuilt as a dense timber stick tower hung with chains.

Model making | Composition | Wood sticks, timber frame and chains | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生長的尖塔
zh-Hant.description:
把一棵樹拆解為線、曲線與球體，再以密集的木條重建成垂掛鐵鍊的塔。

模型製作｜構成｜木條、木框與鐵鍊｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A famous basilica has been growing spire by spire for over a century. The student wondered whether a tower could grow in the same impulsive yet harmonious way.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座著名的大教堂一百多年來一座座尖塔地生長。學生思考一座塔能否以同樣隨性卻和諧的方式生長。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Inspired by abstract painting, the student broke a tree into vertical trunk lines, horizontal branches, curved canopy and round fruit. These simple parts became the building rules.
captions: The stick city in its frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 受抽象繪畫啟發，學生把樹拆解為垂直樹幹、水平枝條、弧形樹冠與圓形果實。這些簡單元素成為建構規則。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Curves for the canopy were placed first and extended upward into a volume. A central trunk then grew freely while spheres balanced the straight lines.
captions: An early stage of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 代表樹冠的曲線先被放置，再向上延伸成量體。接著中央樹幹自由生長，球體則平衡直線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Thousands of sticks rise like spires inside a timber frame. Hanging chains add a soft canopy over the hard, upright city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 上千根木條如尖塔般在木框中升起。垂掛的鐵鍊為堅硬直立的城市加上柔軟的頂蓋。

sections.heading: Growing Spires - Building by the Rules of a Tree
sections.body: A famous basilica has been growing spire by spire for over a century, and the student wondered whether a tower could grow in the same impulsive yet harmonious way. The guidance first drew inspiration from abstract painting, breaking a tree into vertical trunk lines, horizontal branches, a curving canopy and round fruit, so that these simple elements became the rules of construction. In development, curves for the canopy were placed first and extended upward into a volume, then a central trunk grew freely while spheres balanced the straight lines, rule and improvisation finding harmony together. Finally, thousands of sticks rise like spires inside a timber frame, and hanging chains lay a soft canopy over the hard, upright city, so that the logic by which a tree grows becomes a building that seems still to be growing.

zh-Hant.heading: 生長的尖塔-以一棵樹的規則構築
zh-Hant.body: 一座著名的大教堂一百多年來一座座尖塔地生長，學生思考一座塔能否以同樣隨性卻和諧的方式生長。指導過程先從抽象繪畫汲取啟發，把一棵樹拆解為垂直的樹幹、水平的枝條、弧形的樹冠與圓形的果實，讓這些簡單元素成為構築的規則。進入推演，代表樹冠的曲線先被放置，再向上延伸成量體，接著中央樹幹自由生長，球體則平衡著直線，規則與即興在其中取得和諧。最後，上千根木條如尖塔般在木框中升起，垂掛的鐵鍊為堅硬直立的城市加上一片柔軟的頂蓋，讓一棵樹的生長邏輯，長成一座仍在延續的建築。

pins.title: Exploring a New Architectural Language Through Facade and Form
pins.description:
Sketches of favourite facades become unit blocks that stack into an expressive timber tower.

Model making | Facade study | Wood boards, wood sticks, paper and PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 以立面與形體探索新建築語言
zh-Hant.description:
喜愛的立面草圖化為單元量體，堆疊成富表現力的木構塔。

模型製作｜立面研究｜木板、木條、紙與PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Walking through the city, the student saw each building as a piece in a huge exhibition. The student wanted to invent a new language by mixing their forms and facade materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 走在城市中，學生把每棟建築看成巨大展覽中的一件作品。學生想混合它們的形體與立面材料，創造新的語言。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student collected six favourite facades and summarised each in pencil. Each sketch then became a unit block built with a different method.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集六個喜愛的立面，以鉛筆提煉其特徵。每張草圖再以不同手法做成一個單元量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The blocks were stacked and tested in several combinations. White legs lift the tower while sticks and boards build up its layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 量體以多種組合堆疊測試。白色支腳托起塔身，木條與木板則堆出層次。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower mixes slats, frames and solid panels into one rich surface. A crown of sticks reaches upward like scaffolding.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 塔身把格柵、框架與實板混合為豐富的表面。木條頂冠像鷹架般向上伸展。

sections.heading: A New Architectural Language - A Hybrid Tower from the City's Exhibition
sections.body: Walking through the city, the student saw each building as a piece in a vast exhibition and wanted to invent a new language by mixing their forms and facade materials. The guidance first led the student to collect six favourite facades and distil each in pencil, then to turn every sketch into a unit block made by a different method, so that admiration was first transformed into research with a method. In development, the blocks were stacked and tested in several combinations, white legs lifting the tower while sticks and boards built up its layers one upon another. Finally, the tower mixes slats, frames and solid panels into one rich surface, crowned with sticks that reach upward like scaffolding, so that the vocabulary scattered through a city is rewritten into a sentence of architecture that belongs to the student alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 以立面與形體探索新建築語言-城市展覽裡的混種之塔
zh-Hant.body: 走在城市裡，學生把每一棟建築看作巨大展覽中的一件作品，想混合它們的形體與立面材料，創造一種新的語言。指導過程先引導學生收集六個喜愛的立面，以鉛筆提煉各自的特徵，再把每一張草圖以不同的手法做成一個單元量體，讓欣賞先轉化為有方法的研究。進入推演，量體以多種組合堆疊測試，白色支腳托起塔身，木條與木板則一層層堆出層次。最後，塔身把格柵、框架與實板混合為豐富的表面，一頂木條冠冕像鷹架般向上伸展，讓城市裡散落的語彙，被重新編寫成一句屬於自己的建築語言。

pins.title: Curled Shell Pavilion
pins.description:
A summer workshop project grows curling digital shells into a sculptural pavilion.

Summer workshop | Digital form | Digital modelling and rendering | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 捲曲殼體涼亭
zh-Hant.description:
一個暑期工作坊作品，把捲曲的數位殼體發展成雕塑般的涼亭。

暑期工作坊｜數位形體｜數位建模與渲染｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Render of the curled shell pavilion.
捲曲殼體涼亭的渲染圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The workshop asked students to make a space from a single continuous digital form. The student wanted a shell that curls into rooms rather than walls.
captions: Plan lines of the first form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 工作坊要求學生以單一連續的數位形體創造空間。學生想做出捲曲成房間而非牆面的殼體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student started from simple crossing tubes drawn in plan. Bending and twisting them in the software revealed many curling surfaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
