zh-Hant.body: 學生從平面上簡單交叉的管狀體開始。在軟體中彎曲扭轉後，出現許多捲曲的曲面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A section with a human figure checked the height and openings. Three render studies compared different curls and densities.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 帶有人物的剖面檢查了高度與開口。三個渲染研究比較了不同的捲曲與密度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final shells overlap into a cave-like pavilion lit from above. The project shows how one digital gesture can become a complex space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終殼體交疊成一座由上方採光的洞穴般涼亭。作品展示一個數位手勢如何成為複雜空間。

sections.heading: Curled Shell Pavilion - A Cave Curled from One Digital Gesture
sections.body: The workshop asked students to make a space from a single continuous digital form, and the student wanted a shell that curls into rooms rather than standing up as walls. The guidance began from simple crossing tubes drawn in plan, bent and twisted in the software until many curling surfaces gradually appeared, so that a modest starting point opened onto rich possibilities. In development, a section with a human figure checked height and openings, and three rendered studies compared different degrees of curl and density, testing the beauty of the form against the scale of the body. Finally, the shells overlap into a cave-like pavilion lit from above, and the work shows how one digital gesture can grow into a complex space, so that a single curve on a screen becomes a shelter one can walk into.

zh-Hant.heading: 捲曲殼體涼亭-一個數位手勢捲成的洞穴
zh-Hant.body: 工作坊要求以單一連續的數位形體創造空間，學生想做出一個捲曲成房間、而非立成牆面的殼體。指導過程先從平面上簡單交叉的管狀體出發，在軟體中彎曲、扭轉，讓許多捲曲的曲面逐漸浮現，使一個簡單的起點展開豐富的可能。進入推演，一張帶有人物的剖面檢查了高度與開口，三組渲染研究比較不同的捲曲程度與密度，讓形體的美感接受身體尺度的檢驗。最後，殼體彼此交疊，成為一座由上方採光的洞穴般涼亭，作品展示一個數位手勢如何長成複雜的空間，讓螢幕上的一次彎曲，化為可以走入的庇護。

pins.title: Between Solid and Void
pins.description:
The eight trigrams of an ancient classic are built as stick frames filled with plaster blocks.

Model making | Traditional cosmology | Plaster, wood sticks and cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 虛實之間
zh-Hant.description:
把古代經典中的八卦，以木條框架填入石膏塊建構出來。

模型製作｜傳統宇宙觀｜石膏、木條與紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In traditional thought, solid and void suggest how people relate to their surroundings. The student wanted to give this idea a physical form at different scales.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統思想中，虛與實暗示人與環境的關係。學生想在不同尺度上把這個概念化為實體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how the eight trigrams each describe a relationship between people and environment. Lines of the trigrams were read as solid and broken bars.
captions: A frame with one plaster block.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究八卦如何各自描述人與環境的關係。卦象中的線被解讀為實線與斷線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stick frames like building parts first made empty spaces without clear edges. Solid plaster blocks were added to give each trigram its form and field.
captions: Plaster pieces added to a frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 像建築構件的木條框架最初只形成沒有清楚邊界的空間。加入實心石膏塊後，每一卦才有了形與場。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Eight small models were combined into one arrangement of frames and blocks. Together they show solid and void working as a pair.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 八個小模型組合成框架與石塊的整體配置。它們共同展現虛與實相互依存。

sections.heading: Between Solid and Void - Form and Field in the Eight Trigrams
sections.body: In traditional thought, solid and void suggest how people relate to their surroundings, and the student wanted to give this idea physical form at different scales. The guidance first led the student to study how each of the eight trigrams describes a relationship between people and environment, reading the lines of the trigrams as solid and broken bars, so that ancient symbols first became a grammar of space. In development, stick frames resembling building parts at first enclosed only spaces without clear edges; once solid plaster blocks were added, each trigram gained its own form and field, solid and void defining one another through the act of making. Finally, eight small models were combined into a single arrangement of frames and blocks, showing together how solid and void depend on each other, so that a philosophy thousands of years old grows into an order one can touch.

zh-Hant.heading: 虛實之間-八卦裡的形與場
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統思想中，虛與實暗示著人與環境的關係，學生想在不同尺度上，把這個概念化為實體。指導過程先引導學生研究八卦如何各自描述人與環境的關係，把卦象中的線讀為實線與斷線，讓古老的符號先成為空間的語法。進入推演，像建築構件般的木條框架最初只圍出邊界模糊的空間，加入實心的石膏塊之後，每一卦才有了自己的形與場，虛與實在操作中彼此定義。最後，八個小模型組合成框架與石塊的整體配置，共同展現虛與實相互依存，讓一套千年的哲學，在手中長成可以觸摸的秩序。

pins.title: Floating Mangrove Pavilion
pins.description:
A curving, translucent building floats on wire legs above a mangrove forest.

Model making | Building and nature | Wire, frosted plastic sheet, bamboo strip and sand | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮紅樹林涼亭
zh-Hant.description:
一座彎曲半透明的建築，以鋼絲支柱漂浮在紅樹林之上。

模型製作｜建築與自然｜鋼絲、霧面塑膠片、竹條與沙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished pavilion over the mangroves.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A mangrove forest stands on soft mud, floods with seawater and shelters rare birds. The student asked how a building could sit there without harming it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 紅樹林生長在軟泥上，會被海水淹沒，也是稀有鳥類的棲地。學生思考建築如何在此存在而不造成傷害。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student decided to lift the building so its main structure never touches the forest floor. Digital studies tested curved slats that stay open to birds.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生決定把建築抬高，讓主結構不接觸林地。數位研究測試了對鳥類保持開放的弧形格柵。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin wire pillars rise like roots to hold a light canopy. Frosted sheets were tested so sunlight can still reach the trees.
captions: The wire frame in dark light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 細鋼絲柱如根系般升起，托住輕盈的頂蓋。霧面片材經過測試，讓陽光仍能照到樹木。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Curving translucent sheets float above model trees and sand. The open roof lets birds fly through while light falls on the forest.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 彎曲的半透明片材漂浮在模型樹與沙地之上。開放的屋頂讓鳥自由穿越，光線灑落林間。

sections.heading: Floating Mangrove Pavilion - A Canopy That Barely Touches the Forest
sections.body: A mangrove forest stands on soft mud, floods with the tide and shelters rare birds, and the student asked how a building might exist there without harm. The guidance first led the student to lift the building so that its main structure never touches the forest floor, then to test in digital studies curved slats that stay open to birds, so that respect for the ecosystem became the premise of the design. In development, thin wire pillars rise like roots to hold a light canopy, and frosted sheets were tested to make sure sunlight could still reach the trees. Finally, curving translucent sheets float above model trees and sand, and the open roof lets birds fly freely through as light falls among the branches, so that architecture, in its lightest possible gesture, becomes a quiet visitor to the wetland.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂浮紅樹林涼亭-輕觸林地的頂蓋
zh-Hant.body: 紅樹林生長在柔軟的泥地上，隨海水漲落，也是稀有鳥類的棲地，學生思考建築如何在此存在而不造成傷害。指導過程先引導學生決定把建築抬高，讓主結構不觸及林地，再以數位研究測試對鳥類保持開放的弧形格柵，讓尊重生態先成為設計的前提。進入推演，細鋼絲柱如根系般升起，托住輕盈的頂蓋，霧面片材經過測試，確保陽光仍能照進林間。最後，彎曲的半透明片材漂浮在模型樹與沙地之上，開放的屋頂讓鳥群自由穿越，光線灑落林間，讓建築以最輕的姿態，成為濕地的一位安靜訪客。

admitted_schools.zh-Hant: 加州大學聖地牙哥分校

pins.title: Site of Solid and Steel
pins.description:
Columns that vanish into a building's foundation inspire a cantilevered plaster form pierced by steel rods.

Model making | Structure and material | Whiteform, PVC board, metal rods, plaster and clear plastic | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 實體與鋼筋之境
zh-Hant.description:
終將隱沒於建築基礎中的柱子，啟發了一個被鋼條穿透的懸挑石膏形體。

模型製作｜結構與材料｜白色泡綿板、PVC板、金屬條、石膏與透明塑膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The cantilevered plaster and steel model.
懸挑的石膏與鋼條模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Foundation columns are built and then hidden for ever inside a building. The student wanted to make this unseen rebar moment visible as architecture.
captions: A round form bound with wire.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基礎柱子在建造後便永遠隱沒於建築之中。學生想把這段看不見的鋼筋時刻轉化為可見的建築。
captions: 以鐵絲綁紮的圓形量體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student first sculpted solid forms on a grid and found them heavy and bound by gravity. Wire and rods were tried as ways to loosen the mass.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先在格網上雕塑實體量體，發現它們沉重且受制於重力。接著嘗試以鐵絲與鋼條鬆動量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin sheets were pierced with rods to test how steel can hold a surface. Clear plastic molds then helped turn heavy plaster into a curved cantilever.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以鋼條穿透薄片，測試鋼材如何撐起表面。透明塑膠模具則幫助把厚重石膏轉化為彎曲的懸挑。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A white plaster wave floats over its base while a cloud of rods rises above it. Solid and steel finally share one light structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色石膏波浪漂浮在基座上方，一片鋼條之雲在其上升起。實體與鋼材終於共構成一個輕盈的結構。

sections.heading: Site of Solid and Steel - Bringing Hidden Rebar to Light
sections.body: Foundation columns are built and then hidden for ever inside a building, and the student wanted to turn this unseen moment of rebar into visible architecture. The guidance first had the student sculpt solid forms on a grid and notice how heavy they felt, bound by gravity, then try wire and rods as ways of loosening the mass, so that the tension within the materials was first felt by hand. In development, thin sheets were pierced with rods to test how steel can hold a surface, and clear plastic moulds helped turn heavy plaster into a curving cantilever. Finally, a white plaster wave floats above its base while a cloud of rods rises over it, solid and steel at last sharing one light structure, so that the most silent bones inside a building are seen for the first time.

zh-Hant.heading: 實體與鋼筋之境-讓看不見的鋼筋浮現
zh-Hant.body: 基礎的柱子在建造之後，便永遠隱沒於建築之中，學生想把這段看不見的鋼筋時刻，轉化為可見的建築。指導過程先讓學生在格網上雕塑實體量體，察覺它們沉重而受制於重力，再嘗試以鐵絲與鋼條鬆動量體，讓材料的矛盾先被親手感受。進入推演，以鋼條穿透薄片，測試鋼材如何撐起表面，透明塑膠模具則幫助把厚重的石膏轉化為彎曲的懸挑。最後，白色的石膏波浪漂浮在基座之上，一片鋼條之雲在其上升起，實體與鋼材終於共構成一個輕盈的結構，讓建築內部最沉默的骨骼，第一次被看見。

pins.title: Ascending Realms
pins.description:
A layered sandbox game world becomes a vertical tower of white blocks, timber stairs and decks.

Model making | Vertical space | Wood slices, wood battens and 3D printing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 攀升之境
zh-Hant.description:
層層堆疊的沙盒遊戲世界，化為由白色量塊、木梯與平台組成的垂直塔樓。

模型製作｜垂直空間｜木片、木條與3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sandbox games let players build freely across many stacked layers. The student asked how that playful, layered world could become a real piece of architecture.
captions: A collage of game world scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 沙盒遊戲讓玩家在多層堆疊的世界中自由建造。學生思考這個充滿玩心的分層世界如何成為真實的建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student made a collage of game scenes to study their vertical and modular spaces. The collage was then rebuilt as a precise digital block model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拼貼遊戲場景，研究其垂直與模組化的空間。拼貼再被重建為精確的數位量塊模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The blocks were 3D printed and assembled into a stack. Wood battens and stairs were added to brace the tower and link its levels like tunnels.
captions: An angled view of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 量塊經3D列印後組裝成堆疊。再加入木條與樓梯，強化塔身，並像隧道般串連各層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: White masses and timber decks climb together into a busy vertical town. Viewers are invited to trace routes from level to level.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色量體與木平台一同攀升，成為熱鬧的垂直小鎮。觀者被邀請追尋一層又一層的路徑。

sections.heading: Ascending Realms - A Sandbox World Grown into a Vertical Town
sections.body: Sandbox games let players build freely across many stacked layers, and the student asked whether that playful, layered world could become a real piece of architecture. The guidance first led the student to collage scenes from the game and study their vertical and modular spaces, then rebuild the collage as a precise digital block model, so that virtual freedom first found an order that could be constructed. In development, the blocks were 3D printed and assembled into a stack, and wooden battens and stairs were added to brace the tower and link its levels like tunnels, structure and exploration growing together. Finally, white masses and timber decks climb side by side into a busy vertical town, and viewers are invited to trace routes from level to level, so that the joy of building in a game becomes an adventure through real space.

zh-Hant.heading: 攀升之境-沙盒世界長成垂直小鎮
zh-Hant.body: 沙盒遊戲讓玩家在層層堆疊的世界裡自由建造，學生思考這個充滿玩心的分層世界，能否成為真實的建築。指導過程先引導學生拼貼遊戲場景，研究其中垂直與模組化的空間，再把拼貼重建為精確的數位量塊模型，讓虛擬的自由先找到可以構築的秩序。進入推演，量塊經3D列印後組裝成堆疊，再加入木條與樓梯，強化塔身，並像隧道般串連各層，讓結構與探索一同成長。最後，白色量體與木平台一起攀升，成為熱鬧的垂直小鎮，觀者被邀請追尋一層又一層的路徑，讓遊戲中的建造樂趣，化為真實空間裡的探險。

pins.title: Ethereal Bamboo Pavilion
pins.description:
Woven bamboo and wood strips form a hollow two-level pavilion that lets light and air pass through.

Model making | Bamboo structure | Bamboo weaving and wood strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 輕盈竹亭
zh-Hant.description:
編織的竹材與木條構成中空的雙層涼亭，讓光與空氣自由穿透。

模型製作｜竹構造｜竹編與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Bamboo is light, flexible and deeply tied to Asian building traditions. The student wanted a pavilion that feels open and at one with nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 竹材輕盈、柔韌，並與亞洲建築傳統緊密相連。學生想做一座開放、與自然融為一體的涼亭。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied traditional pagoda forms and many bamboo weaving patterns. Small star-shaped units tested how thin poles can lock together.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究傳統塔樓形式與多種竹編圖樣。小型星形單元測試細竹如何相互扣合。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Poles of different thickness were woven and braided into the outer walls. Two floors were linked by an open triangular stair and braced with wood strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同粗細的竹竿被編織成外牆。兩層樓以開放的三角樓梯相連，並以木條斜撐加固。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The hollow pavilion curls upward like a woven cloud. Light passes through its rhythmic net and casts soft patterns below.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 中空的涼亭如編織的雲般向上捲起。光線穿過富節奏的網格，在下方投出柔和的圖案。

sections.heading: Ethereal Bamboo Pavilion - A Woven Cloud Curling Upward
sections.body: Bamboo is light, flexible and deeply bound to Asian building traditions, and the student wanted a pavilion that feels open and at one with nature. The guidance first led the student to study traditional pagoda forms and many patterns of bamboo weaving, then to test with small star-shaped units how thin poles can lock together, so that the wisdom of craft was first understood at the scale of a single joint. In development, poles of different thickness were woven and braided into the outer walls, and the two floors were linked by an open triangular stair and braced with strips of wood, structure and weaving taking shape together. Finally, the hollow pavilion curls upward like a woven cloud, and light passes through its rhythmic net to cast soft patterns below, so that an ancient material breathes again in a gesture of lightness.

zh-Hant.heading: 輕盈竹亭-如編織之雲向上捲起
zh-Hant.body: 竹材輕盈、柔韌，並與亞洲的建築傳統緊密相連，學生想做一座開放、與自然融為一體的涼亭。指導過程先引導學生研究傳統塔樓的形式與多種竹編圖樣，再以小型星形單元測試細竹如何相互扣合，讓傳統的工藝智慧先在最小的接點上被理解。進入推演，粗細不同的竹竿被編織成外牆，兩層樓以開放的三角樓梯相連，並以木條斜撐加固，結構與編織同時成形。最後，中空的涼亭如一朵編織的雲向上捲起，光線穿過富有節奏的網格，在下方投出柔和的圖案，讓一種古老的材料，以輕盈的姿態重新呼吸。

pins.title: Modern Serenity
pins.description:
A detached house in wood plank and strip balances shared living spaces with quiet private rooms.

Model making | House design | Wood plank and wood strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 現代寧靜
zh-Hant.description:
以木板與木條製作的獨棟住宅，在共享起居空間與安靜的私密房間之間取得平衡。

模型製作｜住宅設計｜木板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A home should bring people together while still giving each person a quiet place. The student set out to design a detached house with that balance.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 住宅應讓人們相聚，也要給每個人安靜的角落。學生著手設計一棟兼顧這種平衡的獨棟住宅。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Foam block models tested several room arrangements. Plan sketches then fixed an open living and kitchen space with a guest room downstairs.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 泡綿量塊模型測試多種房間配置。平面草圖再確定開放的客廳與廚房，以及一樓的客房。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second concept model framed the rooms in timber. Large clear windows were added to bring natural light deep inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二個概念模型以木構框出房間。加入大面透明窗戶，把自然光引入深處。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final house uses wood boards and battens for warm, textured walls. A central stair leads up to a private floor of bedrooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終住宅以木板與木條構成溫暖而有質感的牆面。中央樓梯通往私密的臥室樓層。

sections.heading: Modern Serenity - A Home between Gathering and Solitude
sections.body: A home should bring people together while still giving each person a quiet place, and the student set out to design a detached house that holds this balance. The guidance first used foam block models to test several arrangements of rooms, then plan sketches to fix an open living and kitchen space with a guest room on the ground floor, so that the order of daily life was first clearly arranged among the volumes. In development, a second concept model framed the rooms in timber, and large clear windows were added to draw natural light deep into the house. Finally, the house uses wood boards and battens for warm, textured walls, and a central stair leads up to a private floor of bedrooms, so that shared and private life separate naturally along a single stair, and one house makes room for both the warmth of gathering and the calm of solitude.

zh-Hant.heading: 現代寧靜-相聚與獨處之間的家
zh-Hant.body: 一個家應讓人們相聚，也要給每個人安靜的角落，學生著手設計一棟兼顧這種平衡的獨棟住宅。指導過程先以泡綿量塊模型測試多種房間配置，再以平面草圖確定開放的客廳與廚房，以及一樓的客房，讓生活的秩序先在體量之間被安排清楚。進入推演，第二個概念模型以木構框出房間，加入大面透明的窗戶，把自然光引入住宅深處。最後，住宅以木板與木條構成溫暖而有質感的牆面，中央樓梯通往私密的臥室樓層，讓公共與私密沿著一道階梯自然分層，一棟房子因此同時容得下團聚的溫度與獨處的寧靜。

pins.title: Shaped by Time
pins.description:
A plaster sea cliff with projected future scenes shows how coastlines erode into stacks and new habitats.

Model making | Landscape and time | Foam, plants, stones, glue, plaster cloth and sand | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 時間之形
zh-Hant.description:
一座投影未來場景的石膏海崖，呈現海岸如何侵蝕成岩柱並形成新的棲地。

模型製作｜地景與時間｜泡綿、植物、石頭、膠、石膏布與沙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Weathering is slow and almost invisible, yet it reshapes every coast. The student wanted a model that makes this passing of time visible.
captions: A sketch of the cliff receding.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 風化緩慢而幾乎不可見，卻重塑每一片海岸。學生想做一個讓時間流逝變得可見的模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied a famous coastal rock formation and how waves cut cliffs into stacks. Sketches traced the edge moving back over thousands of years.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一處著名的海岸岩層，以及海浪如何把海崖切成岩柱。草圖描繪了數千年間崖邊的後退。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Foam, plaster cloth, stones and sand built up the layered cliff. A projector then cast rising seas and new stacks onto its surface.
captions: Future scenes projected on the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 泡綿、石膏布、石頭與沙堆出層狀海崖。再以投影機把上升的海面與新的岩柱投射在表面上。
captions: 投影在模型上的未來場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model is not static but changes with each projected scene. Worn rocks become homes for sea life as the beach slips under water.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型不是靜態的，而是隨每段投影改變。當沙灘沒入水中，被磨蝕的岩石成為海洋生物的家。

sections.heading: Shaped by Time - Projected Light Revealing Erosion
sections.body: Weathering is slow and almost invisible, yet it reshapes every coast, and the student wanted a model that makes the passing of time visible. The guidance first led the student to study a famous coastal rock formation and how waves cut cliffs into stacks, then to sketch the cliff edge retreating over thousands of years, so that vast geological time was first compressed into a sequence one could read. In development, foam, plaster cloth, stones and sand were built up into a layered cliff, and a projector then cast rising seas and newly formed stacks across its surface. Finally, the model is no longer still but shifts with each projected scene; as the beach slips beneath the water, worn rocks become homes for sea life, so that the loss carried by erosion is also the beginning of new life.

zh-Hant.heading: 時間之形-以光投影讓風化顯現
zh-Hant.body: 風化緩慢而幾乎不可見，卻重塑著每一片海岸，學生想做一個讓時間的流逝變得可見的模型。指導過程先引導學生研究一處著名的海岸岩層，理解海浪如何把海崖切成岩柱，再以草圖描繪數千年間崖邊的後退，讓漫長的地質時間先被壓縮成可以閱讀的序列。進入推演，泡綿、石膏布、石頭與沙堆疊出層狀的海崖，投影機再把上升的海面與新生的岩柱投射在表面上。最後，模型不再靜止，而隨每一段投影改變，當沙灘沒入水中，被磨蝕的岩石成為海洋生物的家，讓侵蝕的失去，同時成為新生命的開端。

pins.title: Kingdom's Legacy
pins.description:
Ancient ruins from a fantasy video game are reinterpreted as a 3D printed temple tower.

Model making | Game-inspired form | 3D printing (PLA) and plaster | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 王國遺產
zh-Hant.description:
奇幻電玩中的古老遺跡，被重新詮釋為一座3D列印的神殿塔樓。

模型製作｜遊戲啟發的形體｜3D列印（PLA）與石膏｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Video game worlds often hold ruins that feel as sacred as real temples. The student asked how these imagined forms could be read again in a modern context.
captions: A still of the game's ruins.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 電玩世界中常有如真實神殿般神聖的遺跡。學生思考這些想像的形體如何在當代語境中被重新閱讀。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Screenshots of the ruins were compared with ancient temple geometry. Their arches and heavy columns were redrawn as plans and elevations.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 遺跡截圖被拿來與古代神殿的幾何比較。拱與厚重的柱子被重新繪成平面與立面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The screenshots were turned into a detailed digital model. Ten columns were 3D printed and coated in plaster to match the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 截圖被轉化為精細的數位模型。十根柱子以3D列印製作，再塗上石膏與基座一致。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The white tower blends sacred temple geometry with game-world fantasy. Scale figures show it as a space between real and imagined landscapes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色塔樓融合神殿的神聖幾何與遊戲世界的奇想。比例人顯示它是介於真實與想像地景之間的空間。

sections.heading: Kingdom's Legacy - Rereading Ruins between Temple and Game
sections.body: Video game worlds often hold ruins that feel as sacred as real temples, and the student asked how these imagined forms might be read again within a contemporary context. The guidance first set screenshots of the ruins beside the geometry of ancient temples, then redrew their arches and heavy columns as plans and elevations, so that a fictional scene was first tested by the discipline of architectural drawing. In development, the screenshots were turned into a detailed digital model, and ten columns were 3D printed and coated in plaster to match the texture of the base. Finally, the white tower blends the sacred geometry of temples with the fantasy of a game world, and scale figures reveal it as a space between real and imagined landscapes, so that an adventure on a screen settles into a quiet legacy.

zh-Hant.heading: 王國遺產-在神殿與遊戲之間重讀遺跡
zh-Hant.body: 電玩世界中常有一些遺跡，莊嚴得宛如真實的神殿，學生思考這些想像的形體能否在當代的語境中被重新閱讀。指導過程先把遺跡的截圖與古代神殿的幾何並置比較，再把拱與厚重的柱子重新繪成平面與立面，讓虛構的場景先接受建築圖學的檢驗。進入推演，截圖被轉化為精細的數位模型，十根柱子以3D列印製作，再塗上石膏，與基座的質地一致。最後，白色塔樓融合神殿的神聖幾何與遊戲世界的奇想，比例人顯示它是一處介於真實與想像地景之間的空間，讓一段螢幕裡的冒險，沉澱為一座安靜的遺產。

pins.title: Tactical Pathways
pins.description:
Maps from a team shooter game are mixed into one white board tower full of routes to the top.

Model making | Game-inspired space | PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 戰術路徑
zh-Hant.description:
把團隊射擊遊戲中的多張地圖混合成一座白色板材塔，布滿通往頂端的路徑。

模型製作｜遊戲啟發的空間｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Game maps are designed around routes, cover and a final goal. The student wondered how those rules could shape a piece of architecture.
captions: Game scenes and the map layout that inspired the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 遊戲地圖圍繞路線、掩體與最終目標而設計。學生思考這些規則能如何塑造建築。
captions: 啟發這座塔的遊戲場景與地圖配置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied several maps, from a control tower to a big garage door. Each element was sketched as a wall, roof, stair or window.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究數張地圖，從控制塔到巨大的車庫門。每個元素都被草繪為牆、屋頂、樓梯或窗。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Boards were cut and glued into open rooms linked by many pathways. Every space was left open so light could pass right through.
captions: Cutting and joining the boards by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 板材被裁切黏合成開放的房間，以多條路徑相連。每個空間都保持開放，讓光可以穿透。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Visitors can climb from the bottom to the top by many different routes. Ink drawings show the tower as a dense, playful maze.
captions: An ink drawing of the levels.
A hatched drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 訪客可沿多條不同路線從底部攀到頂端。墨線圖呈現這座塔如密集而充滿趣味的迷宮。

sections.heading: Tactical Pathways - A Maze Tower Grown from Game Maps
sections.body: Game maps are designed around routes, cover and a final goal, and the student wondered whether those rules could shape a work of architecture. The guidance first led the student through several maps, from a control tower to a vast garage door, sketching each element as a wall, roof, stair or window, so that the strategy of a virtual world was first translated into an architectural vocabulary. In development, boards were cut and glued into open rooms linked by many pathways, every space left open so that light could pass straight through. Finally, visitors can climb from bottom to top along many different routes, and ink drawings present the tower as a dense and playful maze, so that the choices and adventures of a game continue within real space, each ascent a new strategy to be discovered.

zh-Hant.heading: 戰術路徑-遊戲地圖長成的迷宮之塔
zh-Hant.body: 遊戲地圖圍繞路線、掩體與最終目標而設計，學生思考這些規則能否塑造一件建築。指導過程先引導學生研究數張地圖，從控制塔到巨大的車庫門，把每一個元素草繪為牆、屋頂、樓梯或窗，讓虛擬世界的策略先被翻譯成建築的語彙。進入推演，板材被裁切、黏合成開放的房間，以多條路徑彼此相連，每個空間都保持開放，讓光能夠一路穿透。最後，訪客可以沿著許多不同的路線，從底部攀上頂端，墨線圖呈現這座塔如一座密集而充滿趣味的迷宮，讓遊戲中的選擇與冒險，在真實的空間裡延續。

pins.title: Squash Sport
pins.description:
The sharp angles of a squash ball's bounce become a cluster of folded board pyramids and sticks.

Model making | Movement study | PVC boards, paper board and wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 壁球運動
zh-Hant.description:
壁球反彈的銳利角度，化為一簇摺板角錐與木條。

模型製作｜運動研究｜PVC板、紙板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In squash, a ball hit with skill bounces at only a few sharp angles. The student asked whether that path could be turned into a shape.
captions: A squash match, where the rebound angles were observed.
Bounce paths drawn in small boxes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在壁球中，有技巧的擊球只會以少數幾種銳角反彈。學生思考這條路徑能否轉化為一個形體。
captions: 觀察反彈角度的壁球比賽。
在小盒中繪出的反彈路徑。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student traced the ball's path inside small model courts. The strong first bounce and the weak second one gave the student a set of angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在小型球場模型中描繪球的路徑。強勁的第一次反彈與微弱的第二次反彈給了學生一組角度。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The angles were folded into board pyramids and joined with wood sticks. More pyramids were added until the cluster felt like a moving ball.
captions: A striped version of the form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些角度被摺成板材角錐，以木條相連。學生持續加入角錐，直到群組有如運動中的球。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final piece bursts outward with sharp points and long sticks. Drawings and a planted collage test it as a future structure.
captions: A low view of the cluster.
An ink drawing of the angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終作品以尖角與長木條向外迸發。墨線圖與植栽拼貼測試它成為未來構築物的可能。

sections.heading: Squash Sport - Folding the Angles of a Rebound into Form
sections.body: In squash, a skilful shot rebounds at only a few sharp angles, and from this the student asked whether that path could become a form. The guidance first had the student trace the ball's flight inside small model courts, drawing a set of angles from the strong first bounce and the weaker second one, so that speed and force were first converted into precise geometry. In development, the angles were folded into board pyramids joined by wooden sticks, and pyramid after pyramid was added until the cluster felt like a ball in motion. Finally, the piece bursts outward in sharp points and long sticks, while ink drawings and a planted collage test its potential as a future structure, so that the instant of a single stroke becomes a construction that still seems to vibrate with the impact.

zh-Hant.heading: 壁球運動-把反彈的角度摺成形體
zh-Hant.body: 在壁球裡，一記有技巧的擊球只會以少數幾種銳角反彈，學生由此發問：這條路徑能否成為一個形體？指導過程先讓學生在小型球場模型中描繪球的軌跡，從強勁的第一次反彈與微弱的第二次反彈裡，整理出一組角度，讓速度與力量先被轉換為精確的幾何。進入推演，這些角度被摺成板材角錐，以木條彼此相連，角錐一個個加入，直到整個群組宛如一顆正在運動的球。最後，作品以尖角與長木條向外迸發，墨線圖與植栽拼貼進一步測試它成為未來構築物的可能，讓一次擊球的瞬間，化為一座仍在震動的結構。

pins.title: Walled Street Dream
pins.description:
Dense old shopfronts seen on a trip are stacked into a glowing walled-city model with two light paths.

Model making | Street memory | PVC boards, paper, wire and small lights | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 圍城街道之夢
zh-Hant.description:
旅途中看到的密集老店面，被堆疊成一座發光的圍城模型，並有兩條燈光路徑。

模型製作｜街道記憶｜PVC板、紙、電線與小燈｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Walking down a narrow street, the student saw old structures stacked tightly on each other. The scene later came back in a dream of being chased through a walled city.
captions: Dense old shopfronts and night streets that inspired the dream.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 走在狹窄的街道上，學生看見老建築緊密地互相堆疊。這個場景後來出現在學生被追逐穿越圍城的夢中。
captions: 啟發這場夢的密集老店面與夜街。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched shopfronts from reference photos onto paper. Each sketch was stuck to a board as a small facade.
captions: An ink drawing of the stack.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生依參考照片在紙上草繪店面。每張草圖都貼在板材上，成為一個小立面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The facades were glued together at different heights to build a walled-city feeling. Two paths were outlined with tiny lights and wire.
captions: Drawing and folding the shopfront panels.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 立面以不同高度黏合，營造圍城的感覺。兩條路徑以小燈與電線勾勒。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: One light path is the dreamer and the other is the chaser climbing behind. The model turns a street memory into a glowing vertical story.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條燈光路徑是做夢者，另一條是在後方攀爬的追逐者。模型把街道記憶化為發光的垂直故事。

sections.heading: Walled Street Dream - A Chase through Glowing Facades
sections.body: Walking down a narrow street, the student saw old structures stacked tightly upon one another, a scene that later returned as a dream of being chased through a walled city. The work asked how memory and dream might be layered into space. The guidance first led the student to sketch shopfronts from reference photographs and mount each drawing on board as a small facade, so that fragments of the street first became units that could be combined. In development, the facades were glued together at different heights to build the density of a walled city, and two paths were outlined with tiny lights and wire. Finally, one path of light is the dreamer and the other the pursuer climbing behind, and the model turns a memory of a street into a vertical story glowing in the dark, letting the tension of the dream and the layering of the city entwine.

zh-Hant.heading: 圍城街道之夢-在發光的立面間追逐
zh-Hant.body: 走在狹窄的街道上，學生看見老建築緊緊相疊，這幅景象後來化為一場夢：在一座圍城裡被追逐。作品要問的，是如何把記憶與夢境疊成空間。指導過程先引導學生依參考照片在紙上草繪店面，再把每一張草圖貼在板材上，成為一個個小立面，讓街道的片段先成為可以組合的單元。進入推演，立面以不同高度黏合，營造出圍城般的密度，兩條路徑以細小的燈與電線勾勒出來。最後，一條燈光是做夢的人，另一條是在後方攀爬的追逐者，模型把一段街道的記憶，化為一則在黑暗中發光的垂直故事，讓夢的緊張與城市的層疊彼此交纏。

pins.title: Rooted Lattice Tower
pins.description:
A summer workshop project grows vines and tree roots into an organic 3D printed lattice tower.

Summer workshop | Organic structure | Foam board, museum board and 3D printing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 根系晶格塔
zh-Hant.description:
一個暑期工作坊作品，把藤蔓與樹根發展成有機的3D列印晶格塔。

暑期工作坊｜有機結構｜泡綿板、博物館板與3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A steel frame under a bench made the student imagine a more organic and random structure. The student wanted to stand inside a building that feels like vines.
captions: Basic forms used as a start.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 長椅下的鋼構讓學生想像一種更有機、更隨機的結構。學生想站在一棟宛如藤蔓的建築之中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Vines, tree roots and a twisting lattice tower all fed the idea. Basic shapes were tested in a parametric script inside a rectangular limit.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 藤蔓、樹根與扭轉的晶格塔都啟發了學生。基本形體在矩形限制內以參數化腳本測試。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The digital lattice was refined until it felt both irregular and stable. Ink drawings tested stairs and decks threading through it.
captions: Cutting the boards and assembling the printed lattice.
An ink drawing of the tower.
A sketch of the root form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 數位晶格被不斷調整，直到既不規則又穩定。墨線圖測試穿越其中的樓梯與平台。
captions: 裁切板材並組裝列印的格構。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The printed tower rises like a cluster of white roots with stairs wrapping round it. Red figures show how people could move through its hollows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 列印出的塔如一簇白色根系升起，樓梯環繞其外。紅色人偶顯示人們如何穿行於孔洞之間。

sections.heading: Rooted Lattice Tower - Stepping into a Building Like Vines
sections.body: A steel frame beneath a bench led the student to imagine a more organic, more random structure, and to long for standing inside a building that feels like vines. The guidance first drew on vines, tree roots and a twisting lattice tower for inspiration, then tested basic shapes with a parametric script inside a rectangular limit, so that natural growth was first translated into rules that could be adjusted. In development, the digital lattice was refined again and again until it felt both irregular and stable, while ink drawings tested how stairs and decks might thread through it, bringing human movement into an organic skeleton. Finally, the printed tower rises like a cluster of white roots with stairs wrapping around it, small red figures showing how people could pass through its hollows, so that a long look at an everyday piece of steel grows into a forest one could inhabit.

zh-Hant.heading: 根系晶格塔-走進一棟藤蔓般的建築
zh-Hant.body: 長椅下的一副鋼構，讓學生想像一種更有機、更隨機的結構，渴望站進一棟宛如藤蔓的建築之中。指導過程先從藤蔓、樹根與扭轉的晶格塔汲取靈感，再於矩形的限制內，以參數化腳本測試基本形體，讓自然的生長先被轉譯為可以調整的規則。進入推演，數位晶格被反覆修正，直到既不規則又足夠穩定，墨線圖則測試樓梯與平台如何穿梭其中，讓人的動線進入有機的骨架。最後，列印出的塔如一簇白色根系向上生長，樓梯環繞其外，紅色人偶顯示人們如何在孔洞之間穿行，讓一次對日常構件的凝視，長成一座可以棲居的森林。

pins.title: Silent Canopy
pins.description:
Tank experiments and a concrete-and-wire model show mangroves buried beneath a growing city.

Model making | Ecology study | Wood sticks, wire, cement, rocks and plants | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 寂靜樹冠
zh-Hant.description:
以水箱實驗與混凝土鐵絲模型，呈現被擴張城市掩埋的紅樹林。

模型製作｜生態研究｜木條、鐵絲、水泥、石頭與植物｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Fast city growth and land reclamation have destroyed large areas of coastal mangroves. The student wanted to show this hidden loss.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 快速的城市擴張與填海工程摧毀了大片海岸紅樹林。學生想呈現這種隱藏的失落。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew mangrove species, their food chain and how they sit across tidal zones. Tank tests with plants, sand and salt water showed roots acting as a natural sea wall.
captions: Tank experiments simulating tides, wind and wave erosion.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪紅樹林物種、食物鏈及其在潮間帶的分布。以植物、沙與鹽水進行的水箱實驗，顯示根系如天然海堤。
captions: 模擬潮汐、風與波浪侵蝕的水槽實驗。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A sketch split the scene into reclaimed land above and living habitat below. A first model used withered red saplings to show the damage.
captions: Wiring, casting and painting the model.
A first model with red sap.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一張草圖把場景分為上方的填海土地與下方的棲地。第一個模型以枯萎的紅色幼苗表現破壞。
captions: 帶紅色汁液的第一個模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model buries plants and rocks under cement slabs, pillars and wire. Small figures walk above, unaware of the roots below.
captions: The buried level from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把植物與石頭埋在水泥板、柱子與鐵絲之下。小人偶在上方行走，對下方的根系渾然不覺。

sections.heading: Beneath the Roots - The Tides the City Forgot
sections.body: Mangroves are the quietest border between city and sea; they do not speak, they simply remember every tide in their roots. This work did not begin with form but with a question: when land reclamation pushes the shore away, what exactly is buried? The guidance first asked the student to become an observer, building an ecological way of reading through species, food chains and the tidal zone, then stepped into the water tank, letting sand, salt water and roots prove for themselves how they hold back the waves. Knowledge here was not citation but a phenomenon verified by hand. In development, the question was translated into a section: above, a hard, level, measurable city; below, a wet, tangled, vanishing habitat. The rupture between the two became the grammar of the work. Finally, cold cement and wire press down on real plants and stones, while small figures walk above, unaware. The work does not accuse; it quietly draws the gaze downward and lets viewers discover for themselves that what we call development is sometimes built upon losses no one can see.

zh-Hant.heading: 根系之下-被城市遺忘的潮汐
zh-Hant.body: 紅樹林是城市與海之間最沉默的邊界，它們不說話，只用根系記住每一次潮汐。這件作品沒有從造型開始，而是從一個問題出發：當填海造地把海岸推遠，被掩埋的究竟是什麼？指導過程先讓學生成為一名觀察者，在物種、食物鏈與潮間帶之間建立生態的閱讀方式，再走進水箱，讓沙、鹽水與根系自己證明它們如何抵擋海浪。知識在這裡不是引用，而是親手驗證過的現象。進入推演，問題被翻譯成剖面：上層是堅硬、平整、可被丈量的城市，下層是潮濕、糾纏、正在消失的棲地。兩者的斷裂成為作品的語法。最後，冰冷的水泥與鐵絲壓在真實的植物與石頭之上，小人偶在上方行走，渾然不覺。作品不控訴，只是安靜地把視線往下拉，讓觀者自己發現：所謂發展，有時正建立在看不見的失去之上。

pins.title: Light, Shadow, Colour
pins.description:
Twisting stick cubes filled with nylon line, colour film and small lights become a large lightbox.

Model making | Light study | Wood sticks, nylon line, laser paper and mini spotlights | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光、影、色
zh-Hant.description:
填滿尼龍線、彩色膠片與小燈的扭轉木條立方體，組成一座大型燈箱。

模型製作｜光線研究｜木條、尼龍線、鐳射紙與迷你聚光燈｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Light, shadow and colour change how a space feels. The student wanted to show that lighting can build space, not just brighten it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 光、影與色彩改變空間的感受。學生想證明照明能構築空間，而不只是讓它變亮。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student built square stick frames and tested wire mesh, colour film and mirror paper inside them. Small spotlights were wired in series for better control.
captions: A cube with mesh and film.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生製作方形木條框架，並在其中測試鐵絲網、彩色膠片與鏡面紙。小聚光燈以串聯方式接線，以便控制。
captions: 加入網片與膠片的立方體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The cubes were rotated and stacked, with nylon lines forming curved surfaces between them. Each layer was tested for the shadows it cast.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 立方體被旋轉並堆疊，尼龍線在其間形成曲面。每一層都測試它投下的影子。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Inside a paper box, the lights throw red and blue lines across every surface. The lightbox shows how light alone can reshape a room.
captions: The stack in red and blue.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在紙盒中，燈光把紅藍線條投射到每個表面。燈箱展現光本身如何重塑一個空間。

sections.heading: Light, Shadow, Colour - Building a Room out of Light
sections.body: Light, shadow and colour change how a space feels, and the student wanted to show that lighting can build space rather than simply brighten it. The guidance first had the student make square stick frames and test wire mesh, colour film and mirror paper inside them, wiring small spotlights in series for precise control, so that each effect of light was first examined unit by unit. In development, the cubes were rotated and stacked, nylon lines drawing curved surfaces between them, and each layer was tested for the shadows it cast, structure and light being worked out together. Finally, inside a paper box, the lights throw red and blue lines across every surface, and the lightbox shows how light alone can reshape a room, so that illumination, invisible in itself, becomes the lightest of building materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 光、影、色-以光構築一個房間
zh-Hant.body: 光、影與色彩改變著空間的感受，學生想證明照明能構築空間，而不只是讓它變亮。指導過程先讓學生製作方形木條框架，在其中測試鐵絲網、彩色膠片與鏡面紙，並把小聚光燈以串聯方式接線，以便精確控制，讓光的效果先在小小的單元裡被逐一檢驗。進入推演，立方體被旋轉、堆疊，尼龍線在其間牽出曲面，每一層都測試它投下的影子，結構與光影一同被推敲。最後，在紙盒之中，燈光把紅與藍的線條投射到每一個表面，這只燈箱展現光本身如何重塑一個房間，讓看不見的照明，成為最輕盈的建築材料。

pins.title: Sonic Refraction
pins.description:
Threads stretched between pins trace how sound bounces around a shoebox-shaped hall.

Model making | Acoustic study | Cotton thread, 3D print, PVC board, pins and wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聲音折射
zh-Hant.description:
在釘子之間拉緊的線，描繪聲音如何在鞋盒形大廳中反彈。

模型製作｜聲學研究｜棉線、3D列印、PVC板、釘子與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The hall model with its roof grid.
帶屋頂格柵的大廳模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student plays guitar and wondered how music could shape architecture. Sound moves through a room in paths we cannot see.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生彈吉他，思考音樂如何塑造建築。聲音以我們看不見的路徑在房間中移動。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied a famous shoebox-shaped concert hall, where walls and ceilings spread sound evenly. Sketches traced how sound bends and reflects.
captions: The shoebox concert hall studied as a precedent.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一座著名的鞋盒形音樂廳，其牆與天花板讓聲音均勻擴散。草圖描繪聲音如何彎折與反射。
captions: 作為案例研究的鞋盒式音樂廳。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A hall was modelled digitally and printed in parts. Pins marked reflection points, and threads joined them to show each sound path.
captions: Assembling the hall model and threading the pins.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 大廳以數位建模並分件列印。釘子標示反射點，線把它們連接以呈現每條聲音路徑。
captions: 組裝音樂廳模型並穿線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under strong light, the threads and roof grid cast a web of shadows. The model makes the movement of sound visible.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在強光下，線與屋頂格柵投下一片影子網。模型讓聲音的移動變得可見。

sections.heading: Sonic Refraction - Threads Drawing the Invisible Paths of Sound
sections.body: The student loves playing a stringed instrument and wondered how music might shape architecture: sound travels through a room along paths no one can see, so could they be made visible? The guidance first led the student to study a famous shoebox-shaped concert hall, understanding how its walls and ceilings spread sound evenly, and then to sketch how sound bends and reflects, so that the experience of listening first became a set of geometric relations. In development, the hall was modelled digitally and printed in parts, pins marked each point of reflection, and threads joined them one by one to reveal every path of sound. Finally, under strong light, the threads and the roof grid cast an interwoven web of shadows, and the model makes the movement of sound visible, tracing with fine lines the route a melody takes as it passes through space.

zh-Hant.heading: 聲音折射-以絲線畫出看不見的聲路
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛彈奏弦樂，思索音樂如何塑造建築：聲音在房間裡沿著看不見的路徑移動，能否被看見？指導過程先引導學生研究一座著名的鞋盒形音樂廳，理解牆面與天花板如何讓聲音均勻擴散，再以草圖描繪聲音的彎折與反射，讓聽覺的經驗先成為幾何的關係。進入推演，大廳以數位建模並分件列印，釘子標出每一個反射點，絲線把它們一一連起，呈現每一條聲音的路徑。最後，在強光之下，絲線與屋頂格柵投下一片交織的影子網，模型讓聲音的移動變得可見，讓一段旋律在空間中走過的路，被細細描繪出來。

pins.title: Rhythm of the Court
pins.description:
Sticks, shoelaces and a hanging chain net turn the rhythm of a basketball game into a model.

Model making | Sport study | Wood sticks, spray paint, shoelaces and iron chain | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 球場的節奏
zh-Hant.description:
木條、鞋帶與懸掛的鐵鍊網，把籃球比賽的節奏化為一座模型。

模型製作｜運動研究｜木條、噴漆、鞋帶與鐵鍊｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The chain net over the court.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Basketball is full of rhythm: passes, jumps and shots. The student wanted to turn that rhythm into a space.
captions: Mind maps of the game's rhythm, players and space.
A sketch of movement on court.
A sketch of the rising form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 籃球充滿節奏：傳球、跳躍與投籃。學生想把這種節奏轉化為空間。
captions: 關於比賽節奏、球員與空間的心智圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches mapped the elements of the game and how players move. Loose drawings tested a form that rises from the floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖整理比賽的元素與球員的移動方式。隨意的線稿測試一個從地面升起的形體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Painted sticks became the court floor. Upright sticks wrapped in yellow, blue and grey laces stood for two teams and the referees, and cantilevered sticks traced passes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 上漆的木條成為球場地板。纏上黃、藍、灰鞋帶的直立木條代表兩隊與裁判，懸挑木條則描繪傳球軌跡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A chain from a street hoop was split and draped over the top, with a ball hung in the middle. The model captures the energy of a game in motion.
captions: The ball caught in the chains.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 取自街頭籃框的鐵鍊被拆開並披掛在頂部，中央懸掛一顆球。模型捕捉比賽進行中的能量。

sections.heading: Rhythm of the Court - A Game Held Still as Space
sections.body: Basketball is full of rhythm, passes, jumps and shots rising and falling into the breath of a game, and the student wanted to turn that rhythm into space. The guidance first used sketches to map the elements of play and the ways players move, then loose line drawings to test a form rising from the floor, so that motion first left its traces on paper. In development, painted sticks became the court floor, upright sticks wrapped in yellow, blue and grey laces stood for the two teams and the referees, and cantilevered sticks traced the paths of passes, material and colour together carrying the roles of the game. Finally, a chain taken from a street hoop was split and draped over the top with a ball hung at the centre, and the model captures the energy of a game in motion, so that a fleeting rhythm keeps echoing through space.

zh-Hant.heading: 球場的節奏-把一場比賽凝成空間
zh-Hant.body: 籃球充滿節奏：傳球、跳躍、投籃，一次次起落交織成比賽的呼吸。學生想把這種節奏轉化為空間。指導過程先以草圖整理比賽的元素與球員的移動方式，再以隨意的線稿測試一個從地面升起的形體，讓動態先在紙上留下軌跡。進入推演，上漆的木條鋪成球場地板，纏上黃、藍、灰鞋帶的直立木條分別代表兩隊與裁判，懸挑的木條則描繪傳球的路徑，材料與色彩共同承載比賽的角色。最後，一條取自街頭籃框的鐵鍊被拆開，披掛在頂部，中央懸著一顆球，模型捕捉到比賽進行中的能量，讓轉瞬即逝的節奏，在空間裡持續迴盪。

pins.title: Cube Rotate
pins.description:
A summer workshop project rotates, stacks and splits boxes into a carved white volume.

Summer workshop | Form study | 3D modelling and 3D printed model | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 旋轉立方
zh-Hant.description:
一個暑期工作坊作品，把方塊旋轉、堆疊並切分成一個雕刻般的白色量體。

暑期工作坊｜形體研究｜3D建模與3D列印模型｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The printed model with a figure.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The workshop asked students to pick a volume and a verb that would shape it. The student chose a cube and the verb rotate.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 工作坊要求學生選擇一個量體與一個塑造它的動詞。學生選了立方體與「旋轉」。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A rectangle was copied, rotated and stacked again and again. The steps were tested in a series of animation frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一個矩形被反覆複製、旋轉與堆疊。各步驟以一系列動畫畫格測試。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A boolean cut split the stacked boxes into halves, and the same commands were repeated with small changes. Drawings explained the rotation and the surfaces.
captions: A render of the whole form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以布林運算把堆疊的方塊切成兩半，並以細微調整重複相同指令。圖面說明旋轉與表面。
captions: 以線條表現的表面邏輯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The printed model is a carved white mass with stairs and terraces inside. An unrolled elevation and a section show how it works as a space.
captions: A close view of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 列印模型是一個內含樓梯與平台的白色雕刻量體。展開立面與剖面呈現它如何成為空間。

sections.heading: Cube Rotate - A Volume Carved by a Single Verb
sections.body: A workshop asked students to choose a volume and a verb that would shape it, and the student chose the cube and the verb rotate. The guidance first had the student copy, rotate and stack a rectangle again and again, testing each step through a series of animation frames, so that the verb first became a set of operations that could be repeated. In development, a boolean cut split the stacked boxes into halves, and the same commands were run once more with small variations, while drawings clearly explained the logic of the rotation and the surfaces it produced. Finally, the printed model is a carved white mass with stairs and terraces inside, and an unrolled elevation and a section show how it works as an inhabitable space, so that a simple action, through rule and patience, sculpts a piece of architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 旋轉立方-一個動詞雕出的量體
zh-Hant.body: 工作坊要求學生選擇一個量體與一個塑造它的動詞，學生選了立方體與「旋轉」。指導過程先讓學生把一個矩形反覆複製、旋轉與堆疊，並以一系列動畫畫格測試每一個步驟，讓動詞先成為一套可以重複的操作規則。進入推演，以布林運算把堆疊的方塊切成兩半，再以細微的調整重複相同的指令，圖面則清楚說明旋轉的邏輯與生成的表面。最後，列印出的模型是一個內含樓梯與平台的白色雕刻量體，展開立面與剖面呈現它如何成為可以居處的空間，讓一個簡單的動作，經由規則與耐心，雕刻出一座建築。

pins.title: Music Reflection Space
pins.description:
A guitar is taken apart and rebuilt with mirror paper and white balls into a tall reflective box.

Model making | Music and space | Guitar parts, paper, fishing line and white balls | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 音樂反射空間
zh-Hant.description:
一把吉他被拆解，並以鏡面紙與白球重組成一座高大的反射盒。

模型製作｜音樂與空間｜吉他零件、紙、釣魚線與白球｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The guitar inside the reflective box.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to show music as a space, not only a sound. A guitar became the starting point.
captions: A drawing of a guitar and music.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把音樂呈現為空間，而不只是聲音。一把吉他成為起點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The guitar was taken apart piece by piece, and every stage was recorded. The neck, pegs and joints were studied closely.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 吉他被逐件拆解，每個階段都被記錄。琴頸、弦鈕與接合處都被仔細研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The parts were put back together with mirror paper and white balls hung on fishing line. The reflections stand for the echo of music.
captions: Reassembling the guitar parts into the new model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 零件與鏡面紙、以釣魚線懸掛的白球重新組合。反射代表音樂的回響。
captions: 將吉他零件重新組裝成新模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tall box holds the broken guitar among bright shards and floating balls. It reads like a song frozen in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 高大的盒子把拆開的吉他置於明亮碎片與漂浮白球之間。它如同凝結在空間中的一首歌。

sections.heading: Music Reflection Space - Echoes of a Guitar Taken Apart
sections.body: The student wanted to present music as a space rather than only a sound, and a guitar became the starting point. The guidance first led the student to take the guitar apart piece by piece, recording every stage and studying the neck, the pegs and the joints closely, so that a familiar instrument came to be known anew through its undoing. In development, the parts were reassembled together with mirror paper and white balls suspended on fishing line, the reflections standing for the echo of music, so that the lingering of sound took on an optical form. Finally, a tall box holds the dismantled guitar among bright shards and floating balls, and the work reads like a song frozen in space, letting an invisible melody become visible between reflection and suspension, its last notes still seeming to ring off every mirrored surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 音樂反射空間-拆開吉他後的回響
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把音樂呈現為空間，而不只是聲音，一把六弦琴成為起點。指導過程先引導學生把琴逐件拆解，記錄每一個階段，仔細研究琴頸、弦鈕與接合處，讓熟悉的樂器在拆解中重新被認識。進入推演，零件與鏡面紙、以釣魚線懸掛的白球重新組合，鏡面的反射代表音樂的回響，聲音的延續於是有了光學的形式。最後，高大的盒子把拆開的琴安放在明亮的碎片與漂浮的白球之間，作品宛如一首凝結在空間中的歌，讓看不見的旋律，在反光與懸浮之間被看見。

pins.title: Dissipating Forms of Time
pins.description:
Bent iron and steel wire, hung in a wooden frame, capture a passing moment as a hovering form.

Model making | Installation | Wooden frame, iron wire, clay, steel wire and fishing line | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 消散的時間形態
zh-Hant.description:
彎折的鐵絲與鋼絲懸掛於木框中，以懸浮的形體捕捉流逝的瞬間。

模型製作｜裝置｜木框、鐵絲、黏土、鋼絲與釣魚線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wire form in light and shadow.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Paintings record moments, but they felt too flat to hold changing emotions. The student wanted a three-dimensional piece that could hold a feeling.
captions: The self-portrait line drawing behind the piece.
The face the wire form was shaped from.
The first wire in the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 繪畫能記錄瞬間，但對承載變化的情緒來說太平面。學生想做一件能承載感受的立體作品。
captions: 作品背後的自畫像線描。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A wooden frame was sized to fit a face. Thin black wire was woven into a flat plane fixed at both ends.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 木框依臉部尺寸製作。細黑鐵絲被編成固定兩端的平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The wire was pressed into shape with a little clay, and curly steel wire was added on top. The piece was then hung from the frame with fishing line.
captions: The form hung by fishing line.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲被壓塑成形並加入少量黏土，頂部加上捲曲的鋼絲。作品再以釣魚線懸掛於框中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under a single light, loose strands seem to blow away from the form. The installation shows a moment slowly fading.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在單一光源下，鬆散的線條彷彿從形體飄散。裝置呈現一個逐漸消逝的瞬間。

sections.heading: Dissipating Forms of Time - Wire Holding a Moment as It Fades
sections.body: Paintings record moments, yet they felt too flat to hold emotions in motion, so the student set out to make a three-dimensional piece that could contain a feeling. The guidance first had the student build a wooden frame sized to fit a face and weave thin black wire into a plane fixed at both ends, so that the scale of the body became the starting point of the work. In development, the wire was pressed into shape with a little clay, curling steel wire was added on top, and the piece was hung within the frame on fishing line, the form balanced between the fixed and the loose. Finally, under a single light, the loose strands seem to drift away from the form, and the installation shows a moment slowly fading, letting time itself become a material one can look at and giving an emotion hard to name a light and fragile outline.

zh-Hant.heading: 消散的時間形態-以鐵絲留住正在消逝的瞬間
zh-Hant.body: 繪畫能記錄瞬間，卻平得無法承載變動的情緒，學生於是想做一件能盛住感受的立體作品。指導過程先讓學生依臉部的尺寸製作木框，再把細黑鐵絲編成固定兩端的平面，讓身體的尺度成為作品的起點。進入推演，鐵絲被壓塑成形，加入少量黏土，頂部再添上捲曲的鋼絲，最後以釣魚線懸掛於框中，形體在固定與鬆散之間取得平衡。最後，在單一光源下，鬆散的線條彷彿正從形體飄散，裝置呈現一個緩緩消逝的瞬間，讓時間本身成為可被觀看的材料，也讓一種難以言說的情緒，有了輕盈而脆弱的輪廓。

pins.title: Bagua
pins.description:
Eight plaster walls carved with the eight trigrams form an octagon crossed by a web of sticks.

Model making | Traditional culture | PVC board, plaster, wooden sticks, wooden board and spray paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 八卦
zh-Hant.description:
刻有八卦卦象的八面石膏牆圍成八角形，再由交錯的木條網貫穿。

模型製作｜傳統文化｜PVC板、石膏、木條、木板與噴漆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to an old classic of Chinese culture that reads fortune through eight trigrams. The aim was to turn the flat bagua diagram into a space.
captions: The eight trigrams in two diagrams.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生對一部以八個卦象推演吉凶的中國古典著作深感興趣。目標是把平面的八卦圖轉化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each trigram was linked to a meaning such as sky, soil, mountain, water or wind. These notes guided the pattern on every wall.
captions: Notes on what each trigram means.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個卦象都對應一種意義，例如天、地、山、水或風。這些筆記決定了每面牆的圖樣。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The trigrams were cut into boards and filled with plaster, then eight walls were stood up as an octagon. Sticks were driven through the open parts of the walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 卦象被切割於板材上並灌入石膏，八面牆再立成八角形。木條穿過牆面的開口處。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model is a dense web of sticks inside eight patterned walls. Small figures and strong shadows show how the space would feel.
captions: Figures among the sticks and walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型是在八面圖樣牆內的密集木條網。小人偶與強烈的陰影呈現空間的感受。

sections.heading: Bagua - Eight Trigrams Raised into Walls
sections.body: The student was drawn to an ancient Chinese classic that reads fortune through eight trigrams, and the aim was to turn the flat bagua diagram into a space. The guidance first led the student to find a meaning for each trigram, sky, soil, mountain, water, wind, and to let those notes become the pattern on each wall, so that ancient symbols first turned into a language one could design with. In development, the trigrams were cut into boards and filled with plaster, the eight walls were stood up as an octagon, and sticks were driven through their open parts, symbol and structure piercing one another. Finally, the model is a dense web of sticks enclosed by eight patterned walls, small figures and strong shadows conveying the atmosphere of the space, so that a diagram thousands of years old becomes a place one can enter and feel the shifting of light.

zh-Hant.heading: 八卦-把卦象立成八面牆
zh-Hant.body: 學生對一部以八個卦象推演吉凶的中國古典深感興趣，目標是把平面的八卦圖轉化為空間。指導過程先引導學生為每個卦象找出對應的意義，天、地、山、水、風，並把這些筆記化為每一面牆的圖樣，讓古老的符號先成為可以設計的語言。進入推演，卦象被切割在板材上並灌入石膏，八面牆立成八角形，木條則穿過牆面的開口，符號與結構彼此貫穿。最後，完成的模型是一張被八面圖樣牆包圍的密集木條網，小人偶與強烈的陰影呈現空間的氛圍，讓一張千年的圖，成為可以走入其中、感受光影變幻的場所。

pins.title: Parallel Worlds in a Box
pins.description:
3D-pen lines, mirror and laser acrylic sheets turn three wooden boxes into glowing parallel worlds.

Model making | Film and space | Wooden sticks, PLA, 3D printing pen and laser acrylic sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 盒中的平行世界
zh-Hant.description:
3D筆線條、鏡面與雷射壓克力板，讓三個木盒化為發光的平行世界。

模型製作｜電影與空間｜木條、PLA、3D列印筆與雷射壓克力板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to show parallel universes as a real object. An animated superhero film about many worlds became the starting point.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把平行宇宙呈現為真實的物件。一部描寫多重世界的動畫英雄電影成為起點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Wire and plastic thread were tested first, but they were too soft or too stiff. A 3D printing pen gave lines that were both free and strong.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 最先測試了鐵絲與塑膠線，但它們不是太軟就是太硬。3D列印筆畫出的線條既自由又堅韌。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Curved lines filled the inside of wooden boxes. Laser acrylic sheets on four sides and a mirror below reflect the colours of the lines.
captions: Drawing the lines with the 3D pen inside the boxes.
A simple web inside a cube.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 曲線填滿木盒內部。四面的雷射壓克力板與底部的鏡子反射出線條的色彩。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three boxes tell the story: one bright, one red and black, and one large box for the hero's whole journey. Small cut-out pictures of the characters sit inside.
captions: The bright green and yellow box.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三個盒子講述故事：一個明亮、一個紅黑，以及一個代表主角完整旅程的大盒子。盒內放有角色的小剪影圖片。

sections.heading: Parallel Worlds in a Box - Many Universes Drawn in Light
sections.body: The student wanted to make parallel universes visible as a real object, and an animated superhero film about many worlds became the starting point. The guidance first had the student test materials: wire and plastic thread proved either too soft or too stiff, until a 3D printing pen gave lines both free and strong, so that the choice of material itself became a piece of research. In development, curving lines filled the inside of wooden boxes, with laser-cut acrylic sheets on four sides and a mirror beneath that reflects the colours of the lines, letting a finite box open onto endless layers. Finally, three boxes tell the whole story, one bright, one red and black, and one large box holding the hero's entire journey, with small cut-out silhouettes of the characters set inside, so that many universes stretch without end within a space no larger than the hands.

zh-Hant.heading: 盒中的平行世界-以光筆畫出多重宇宙
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把平行宇宙呈現為真實可見的物件，一部描寫多重世界的動畫英雄電影成為起點。指導過程先引導學生測試材料：鐵絲與塑膠線不是太軟就是太硬，最後由3D列印筆畫出既自由又堅韌的線條，讓材料的選擇本身成為一次研究。進入推演，曲線填滿木盒的內部，四面裝上雷射壓克力板，底部鋪上鏡子，反射出線條的色彩，有限的盒子因此映出無盡的層次。最後，三個盒子講述整個故事：一個明亮、一個紅黑，以及一個承載主角完整旅程的大盒子，盒內放著角色的小剪影，讓多重宇宙在掌心大小的空間裡無限延伸。

pins.title: Vertical Ascent
pins.description:
A tall tower wrapped in DNA spirals and ramps tells a film story of reaching for space against the odds.

Model making | Film and space | Plastic, AB glue, wooden sticks, wire, spray paint, PLA and PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂直攀升
zh-Hant.description:
一座纏繞DNA螺旋與坡道的高塔，講述一個逆境中追尋太空夢的電影故事。

模型製作｜電影與空間｜塑膠、AB膠、木條、鐵絲、噴漆、PLA與PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The model is based on a science-fiction film where genes decide a person's job. Its hero, born with weaker genes, still works his way to space, and the student wanted to build that persistence.
captions: A collage of the film's characters and objects that inspired the tower.
A drawing of the tower idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 模型取材自一部由基因決定職業的科幻電影。主角天生基因較弱，仍努力走向太空，學生想把這份堅持建構出來。
captions: 啟發這座塔的電影角色與物件拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The sketches set out four levels: a race, a workplace, a climb through challenges and the final launch. Each level marks a key moment of the story.
captions: Level sketches beside the film stills they draw on.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖規劃四個層次：一場競賽、一個工作場所、穿越挑戰的攀爬，以及最終的升空。每一層代表故事的關鍵時刻。
captions: 各層草圖與其所依據的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A green base was cast with tinted AB glue, and a 3D-printed pillar and platform held wooden sticks. Silver-painted plastic, wire and red forms added the upward movement.
captions: Printing, gluing and assembling the tower by hand.
The top level for higher goals.
A DNA spiral beside the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以調色AB膠澆鑄綠色基座，3D列印的柱子與平台固定木條。銀色噴漆的塑膠、鐵絲與紅色形體加強向上的動勢。
captions: 親手列印、上膠與組裝塔體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower rises through DNA spirals, ramps and stairs to a sharp tip. It reads as a vertical path toward a dream.
captions: The spiral stairs at the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 高塔穿過DNA螺旋、坡道與樓梯，直升至尖頂。它如同一條通往夢想的垂直路徑。
captions: 代表遺傳物質的紅色形體。

sections.heading: Vertical Ascent - A Tower of Genes Written in Persistence
sections.body: The model draws on a science fiction film in which genes decide a person's job; its hero, born with weaker genes, still works step by step toward space, and the student wanted to build that persistence. The guidance first used sketches to set out four levels, a race, a workplace, a climb through trials and the final launch, so that the key moments of the story were first ordered along a vertical line. In development, a green base was cast in tinted AB glue, a 3D-printed pillar and platform held wooden sticks in place, and silver-painted plastic, wire and red forms were added to strengthen the upward surge. Finally, the tower rises through DNA spirals, ramps and stairs to a sharp tip, reading as a vertical path toward a dream, so that the pull between fate and will becomes a tower that never stops climbing.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直攀升-以堅持寫成的基因之塔
zh-Hant.body: 這件模型取材自一部由基因決定職業的科幻電影，主角天生基因較弱，卻仍一步步走向太空，學生想把這份堅持建構出來。指導過程先以草圖規劃四個層次：一場競賽、一處工作場所、一段穿越挑戰的攀爬，以及最終的升空，讓故事的關鍵時刻先在垂直方向上排好秩序。進入推演，學生以調色AB膠澆鑄綠色基座，以3D列印的柱子與平台固定木條，再以銀色噴漆的塑膠、鐵絲與紅色形體加強向上的動勢。最後，高塔穿過DNA螺旋、坡道與樓梯，直升至銳利的尖頂，讀來如同一條通往夢想的垂直路徑，讓宿命與意志的拉扯，化為一座不斷上升的塔。

pins.title: Transcoding Traditional Chinese Architecture
pins.description:
Mortise and tenon logic is rebuilt in wooden sticks and bamboo weaving as a new courtyard pavilion.

Model making | Traditional architecture | Wooden sticks and bamboo weaving | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 轉譯中國傳統建築
zh-Hant.description:
以木條與竹編重構榫卯邏輯，形成一座新的庭院亭子。

模型製作｜傳統建築｜木條與竹編｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to bring traditional Chinese timber building into a modern design. The goal was a courtyard that honours the past and fits today's life.
captions: Reference drawings of the historic pavilion's joinery and elevation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把中國傳統木構建築帶入現代設計。目標是一座既尊重傳統又適合當代生活的庭院。
captions: 歷史樓閣的榫卯構造與立面參考圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A historic pavilion was studied through a digital model and books. Its double eaves, carved beams and mortise and tenon joints were the key lessons.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生透過數位模型與書籍研究一座歷史亭閣。重簷、雕樑與榫卯接合是主要的學習重點。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Simple joints were made from combined wooden sticks, then built up into a full frame. The logic of the joints shaped a new pavilion.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以組合木條做出簡單接頭，再逐步建成完整框架。接頭的邏輯塑造出一座新的亭子。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Bamboo weaving finished the sweeping roof. Light falls through the layered sticks onto the courtyard below.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 竹編完成了舒展的屋頂。光線穿過層疊的木條灑落在下方庭院。

sections.heading: Transcoding Traditional Chinese Architecture - A New Pavilion from Joinery
sections.body: The student wanted to carry traditional Chinese timber building into contemporary design, aiming for a courtyard that honours the past while suiting present-day life. The guidance first led the student to study a historic pavilion through a digital model and books, learning from its double eaves, carved beams and mortise and tenon joints, so that an ancient way of building was first read closely and understood. In development, simple joints were made from combined wooden sticks and then built up step by step into a complete frame, the logic of the joint growing from small to large until it shaped a new pavilion. Finally, bamboo weaving completed the sweeping roof, and light falls through the layered sticks onto the courtyard below, so that the language of traditional craft begins to speak again in the light and shadow of today.

zh-Hant.heading: 轉譯中國傳統建築-榫卯邏輯長出新亭
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把中國傳統木構建築帶入現代設計，目標是一座既尊重過去、又適合當代生活的庭院。指導過程先引導學生透過數位模型與書籍研究一座歷史亭閣，從重簷、雕樑與榫卯接合中學習傳統的智慧，讓古老的構造先被細細讀懂。進入推演，學生以組合木條做出簡單的接頭，再逐步建成完整的框架，接頭的邏輯由小而大，塑造出一座新的亭子。最後，竹編完成了舒展的屋頂，光線穿過層疊的木條灑落在下方庭院，讓傳統的工藝語言，在今日的光影中重新開口說話。

pins.title: Hexagonal Corridor Structure
pins.description:
Mirror paper and PVC hexagons stack along a model riverbank into walkways and waterfront platforms.

Model making | Landscape and structure | Mirror paper, PVC board, stone clay, AB glue and grass powder | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 六角形廊道結構
zh-Hant.description:
鏡面紙與PVC六角形沿著模型河岸堆疊，形成步道與親水平台。

模型製作｜地景與結構｜鏡面紙、PVC板、石粉黏土、AB膠與草粉｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began with a test of how materials bend. Mirror paper curved easily, while PVC board stayed firm, and the student wanted to use both.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品起於一次材料彎曲的測試。鏡面紙容易彎曲，PVC板則保持堅挺，學生想同時運用兩者。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: After many trials, a hexagon was chosen for its regular shape and easy joins. Sketches showed how units could link into walkways and supports.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 經過多次嘗試，六角形因規則的形狀與易於接合而被選用。草圖呈現單元如何連成步道與支撐。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A riverbank was modelled with stone clay, grass powder and stones, and the river was poured with tinted AB glue. Hexagon units were stacked on both banks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以石粉黏土、草粉與石頭塑造河岸，並以調色AB膠澆灌河道。六角形單元堆疊於兩岸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The stacked units form corridors and platforms for rest and meeting by the water. The model shows a structure that grows with the landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 堆疊的單元形成可在水邊休憩與相聚的廊道與平台。模型呈現一個隨地景生長的結構。

sections.heading: Hexagonal Corridor Structure - Units That Grow along the River
sections.body: The work began with a test of how materials bend: mirror paper curved easily while PVC board stayed firm, and the student wanted to use both characters at once. The guidance first moved through many trials before settling on the hexagon, regular in shape and easy to join, and then used sketches to work out how units could link into walkways and supports, so that the nature of the materials first became a unit of structure. In development, a riverbank was modelled from stone clay, grass powder and stones, the river poured in tinted AB glue, and hexagon units were stacked along both banks, structure and landscape forming together. Finally, the stacked units make corridors and platforms for resting and meeting by the water, and the model shows a structure that grows with its terrain, extending a simple material experiment into a stretch of public life beside a river.

zh-Hant.heading: 六角形廊道結構-隨河岸生長的單元
zh-Hant.body: 作品起於一次材料彎曲的測試：鏡面紙容易彎曲，PVC板則保持堅挺，學生想同時運用兩者的性格。指導過程先經過多次嘗試，選定規則而易於接合的六角形，再以草圖推演單元如何連成步道與支撐，讓材料的特性先轉化為結構的單位。進入推演，學生以石粉黏土、草粉與石頭塑造河岸，以調色AB膠澆灌出河道，六角形單元則在兩岸層層堆疊，結構與地景同時生成。最後，堆疊的單元形成可在水邊休憩與相聚的廊道與平台，模型呈現一個隨地景生長的結構，讓一次簡單的材料實驗，延伸成河畔的一段公共生活。

pins.title: Pineapple Bio-geometry
pins.description:
The fibres inside a pineapple cake inspire a growing web of wood sticks that casts patterned shadows.

Model making | Bio-inspired structure | Tracing paper, wood sticks, pencil, hot glue and cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鳳梨生物幾何
zh-Hant.description:
鳳梨酥內部的纖維啟發一張不斷生長的木條網，投下帶有圖案的陰影。

模型製作｜仿生結構｜描圖紙、木條、鉛筆、熱熔膠與紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The canopy under a low light.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Breaking open a pineapple cake, the student saw a web of fibres inside. The aim was to turn that inner structure into a space.
captions: The pastry shop building and the pineapple cakes that inspired the canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 剝開一塊鳳梨酥時，學生看見內部交織的纖維。目標是把這種內部結構轉化為空間。
captions: 啟發這座頂棚的糕餅店建築與鳳梨酥。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches studied the fibres, and thin wood strips were cut to copy them. The pieces were stacked into a first concept model.
captions: A drawing of the stick web.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖研究纖維，並切割細木條模仿它們。這些木條被堆疊成第一個概念模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: As the model grew, the gaps between sticks became spaces to explore, so corridor-like paths were added. The form spread into a cantilevered umbrella shape.
captions: Testing the sticks by hand and drawing the shadow traces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 隨著模型生長，木條間的縫隙成為可探索的空間，於是加入如廊道般的路徑。形體延展成懸挑的傘狀。
captions: 親手測試木條並描繪陰影軌跡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under light, the web casts rich patterns, which were traced in pencil on the base. The model reads as an organism that can keep on growing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在光線下，木條網投下豐富的圖案，並以鉛筆描繪在底座上。模型如同一個可以持續生長的有機體。

sections.heading: Pineapple Bio-geometry - Fibres of a Pastry Grown into a Canopy
sections.body: Breaking open a pineapple cake, the student noticed a web of fibres inside, and the work asked whether such a delicate inner structure could become space. The guidance first had the student study the direction of the fibres in sketches, then cut thin wood strips to imitate them and stack them into a first concept model, so that the order hidden in an everyday pastry was first enlarged for close looking. In development, as the model kept growing, the gaps between the sticks became spaces worth exploring, and corridor-like paths were added while the form spread outward into a cantilevered umbrella. Finally, under light, the web casts rich patterns that were traced in pencil onto the base, and the model reads as an organism still able to grow, turning a small discovery inside a sweet into a canopy that seems to breathe.

zh-Hant.heading: 鳳梨生物幾何-酥餅裡的纖維長成傘
zh-Hant.body: 剝開一塊鳳梨酥時，學生看見內部交織的纖維，作品於是問：這種細微的內部結構，能否成為空間？指導過程先以草圖研究纖維的走向，再切割細木條模仿它們，堆疊成第一個概念模型，讓日常點心裡的秩序先被放大觀察。進入推演，隨著模型不斷生長，木條之間的縫隙成為可以探索的空間，於是加入如廊道般的路徑，形體也延展成懸挑的傘狀。最後，在光線下，木條網投下豐富的圖案，學生以鉛筆把這些影子描在底座上，模型如同一個仍可持續生長的有機體，讓一口甜點的發現，化為一片會呼吸的頂蓋。

pins.title: House
pins.description:
Two crossing rectangles and a round core create a house with a sense of horizontal movement.

Model making | House design | Cardboard, hot glue and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 住宅
zh-Hant.description:
兩個交錯的矩形與一個圓形核心，構成一座帶有水平移動感的住宅。

模型製作｜住宅設計｜紙板、熱熔膠與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted a house that gives a sense of moving sideways. The question was how a plan could show that motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想設計一座帶有橫向移動感的住宅。問題在於平面如何表現這種動態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Reference houses led to one idea: two rectangles crossing each other to make a space in the middle. Plans tested a round core at the crossing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 參考案例引出一個想法：兩個矩形彼此交錯，在中間創造空間。平面圖在交錯處測試一個圓形核心。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Card panels and sticks were cut and glued to test the crossing walls and roofs. The pieces slid past each other like moving plates.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 切割並黏合紙板與木條，測試交錯的牆與屋頂。各部件像移動的板片般彼此錯開。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets long white volumes across each other around a round core. Open frames let the space flow from end to end.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓長形白色量體圍繞圓形核心交錯。開放的框架讓空間由一端流向另一端。

sections.heading: House - Movement Born of Two Crossing Rectangles
sections.body: The student wanted to design a house that carries a sense of sideways movement, and the question was how a plan could express that motion. The guidance first led the student through reference houses, distilling a single idea from them: two rectangles crossing one another to open a space between, with plans testing a round core at the point of intersection, so that movement first became a clear geometric relationship. In development, card panels and sticks were cut and glued to test the crossing walls and roofs again and again, the pieces slipping past each other like shifting plates, the model itself becoming a tool for thinking. Finally, long white volumes cross one another around the round core, and open frames let space flow from one end to the other, so that a house standing still seems, even so, to be gently sliding.

zh-Hant.heading: 住宅-兩道矩形交錯出的流動
zh-Hant.body: 學生想設計一座帶有橫向移動感的住宅，問題在於：平面如何表現這種動態？指導過程先引導學生研究參考案例，從中提煉出一個想法：兩個矩形彼此交錯，在中間創造空間，並在平面上測試交錯處的圓形核心，讓動感先成為一個清楚的幾何關係。進入推演，學生切割並黏合紙板與木條，反覆測試交錯的牆與屋頂，各部件像移動的板片般彼此錯開，模型成為思考的工具。最後，長形的白色量體圍繞圓形核心交錯，開放的框架讓空間由一端流向另一端，讓一棟靜止的房子，彷彿仍在緩緩滑動。

pins.title: Drowned Legacy: The Inevitable Tide
pins.description:
A coastal model shows houses from different eras slowly taken by rising seas until only stone shelters remain.

Model making | Climate and architecture | Wooden sticks, steel, stones, sand, cement, plants and acrylic rods | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 淹沒的遺產：無法避免的潮水
zh-Hant.description:
一座海岸模型呈現不同時代的房屋被上升的海水逐步吞沒，最後只剩石造庇護所。

模型製作｜氣候與建築｜木條、鋼材、石頭、沙、水泥、植物與壓克力棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Frames and walls in the water.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Rising sea levels threaten homes along every coast. The student asked what would be left of our buildings if the water kept coming.
captions: A news photo of houses hit by a flood.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 上升的海平面威脅著每一段海岸上的家。學生思考，若海水持續上漲，我們的建築會留下什麼。
captions: 房屋遭洪水侵襲的新聞照片。
同一海岸上的四個時代。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A drawing set four houses from different eras side by side, each built of glass, cement, steel, wood or stone. Only the stone house stays above the water.
captions: Casting and testing the stone and cement layers by hand.
The stone shelter above the sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張圖面將不同時代的四座房屋並排，分別以玻璃、水泥、鋼材、木材或石頭建成。只有石屋留在水面之上。
captions: 親手灌製並測試石材與水泥層。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The model was built in layers of sand, stone and cement with clear rods as water. It was shot in three stages as the tide rises.
captions: Three stages of the rising tide.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 模型以沙、石頭與水泥分層建造，並以透明棒表現水。它依海水上升分三個階段拍攝。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Sunken walls and frames turn into reefs where sea life can settle. The work suggests a future where people and the ocean share the same structures.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 沉沒的牆與框架轉變為海洋生物可棲息的礁體。作品提出人與海洋共享同一結構的未來。

sections.heading: Drowned Legacy - The Reef That Remains after the Tide
sections.body: Rising seas threaten homes along every coast, and the student asked what would remain of human buildings if the water kept coming. The guidance first used a drawing that set houses from different eras side by side, built of glass, cement, steel, wood or stone, revealing that only the stone house stays above the water, so that the fate of materials was first compared with a calm eye. In development, the model was built in layers of sand, stone and cement, with clear rods standing for the sea, and photographed in three stages as the tide rises, holding time still within a sequence of images. Finally, sunken walls and frames become reefs where marine life can settle, and the work proposes a future in which people and the ocean share the same structures, turning a meditation on loss into a fable of living together.

zh-Hant.heading: 淹沒的遺產-潮水之後留下的礁石
zh-Hant.body: 上升的海平面威脅著每一段海岸上的家，學生思考：若海水持續上漲，人類的建築會留下什麼？指導過程先以一張圖面將不同時代的房屋並排，分別以玻璃、水泥、鋼材、木材或石頭建成，觀察到只有石屋仍留在水面之上，讓材料的命運先被冷靜地比較。進入推演，模型以沙、石頭與水泥分層建造，以透明棒表現海水，並依潮水上升分三個階段拍攝，時間因此被凝結在影像的序列裡。最後，沉沒的牆與框架轉變為海洋生物可以棲息的礁體，作品提出人與海洋共享同一結構的未來，讓一份關於失去的憂思，翻轉為一則共生的寓言。

pins.title: Green Charging Park
pins.description:
An old fuel station becomes a car charging park under a terraced garden whose plants help make power.

Architectural design | Adaptive reuse | Hand sketches and 3D modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 綠色充電公園
zh-Hant.description:
一座舊加油站轉變為充電公園，上方的階梯花園以植物協助發電。

建築設計｜再利用｜手繪草圖與3D建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Fuel stations are being left empty as more people drive electric cars. Nearby residents also lack parking and easy access for seniors and wheelchair users.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 隨著更多人駕駛電動車，加油站逐漸閒置。附近居民也缺少停車位，長者與輪椅使用者出入不便。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how bacteria around plant roots release a small electric current. Sketches tested a stepped garden that could sit above a charging floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究植物根部周圍的細菌如何釋放微小電流。草圖測試一座可架在充電層上方的階梯花園。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Tree-shaped columns hold round planters over the parking and charging level. Ramps and a side elevator give everyone a way up to the garden.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 樹狀柱在停車與充電層上方撐起圓形種植台。坡道與側邊電梯讓每個人都能登上花園。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The roof becomes a green public park while the ground floor charges cars. Power from the plants lights the garden at night.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂成為綠色公共公園，地面層則為車輛充電。植物產生的電力在夜間點亮花園。

sections.heading: Green Charging Park - A Rooftop Lit by Plants at Night
sections.body: As more people drive electric cars, fuel stations are being left empty, while nearby residents lack parking and older people and wheelchair users struggle with access. The work asked whether such an abandoned site could serve its community again. The guidance first led the student to study how bacteria around plant roots release a tiny electric current, then to sketch a stepped garden set above a charging floor, so that a scientific discovery first became a spatial idea. In development, tree-shaped columns hold round planters over the parking and charging level, and ramps with a side elevator give everyone a way up into the garden. Finally, the roof becomes a green public park while the ground floor charges cars, and power drawn from the plants lights the garden at night, so that energy, access and nature come to live together on a single roof.

zh-Hant.heading: 綠色充電公園-讓植物點亮夜晚的屋頂
zh-Hant.body: 隨著更多人駕駛電動車，加油站逐漸閒置，而附近的居民缺少停車位，長者與輪椅使用者也出入不便。作品要問的是，一處被遺留的站點能否重新服務社區。指導過程先引導學生研究植物根部周圍的細菌如何釋放微小電流，再以草圖測試一座架在充電層上方的階梯花園，讓科學的發現先成為空間的構想。進入推演，樹狀柱在停車與充電層上方撐起圓形的種植台，坡道與側邊電梯讓每一個人都能登上花園。最後，屋頂成為綠色的公共公園，地面層為車輛充電，植物產生的電力在夜裡點亮花園，讓能源、無障礙與自然，在同一處屋頂上和諧共生。

pins.title: Puzzle-piece Calm Space
pins.description:
