Eight rooms shaped like puzzle pieces connect by ramps into a calm, semi-open place for autistic children.

Model making | Space for children | Wooden board, PVC board, laser cutting and 3D modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 拼圖形的安心空間
zh-Hant.description:
八個拼圖形的房間以坡道相連，為自閉症兒童打造一處安心的半開放空間。

模型製作｜兒童空間｜木板、PVC板、雷射切割與3D建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Autistic children often feel anxious in places that are crowded or new. The student wanted a space where they could move and rest safely.
captions: A chart of common traits of autism used as the brief.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 自閉症兒童在擁擠或陌生的環境中常感到焦慮。學生想打造一個讓他們能安心活動與休息的空間。
captions: 作為設計依據的自閉症常見特徵圖表。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Mind maps listed the activities and feelings the space should hold. The puzzle piece became the idea, as each piece looks incomplete alone but fits into a whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 心智圖列出空間應容納的活動與感受。拼圖成為核心概念，因為每一片單獨看似不完整，卻能拼成整體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Eight boxes of different sizes hold rooms for rest, play and meals. The form was modelled in 3D and then laser cut from board.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 八個大小不同的盒子容納休息、遊戲與用餐的房間。形體先以3D建模，再以板材雷射切割。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Ramps and balconies let children move freely between floors at their own pace. The model shows a calm place built with care and patience.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 坡道與陽台讓孩子能依自己的步調在樓層間自由移動。模型呈現一個以關懷與耐心打造的安心場所。

sections.heading: Puzzle-piece Calm Space - Where Every Piece Finds Its Place
sections.body: Autistic children often feel anxious in places that are crowded or unfamiliar, and the student wanted to create a space where such children could move and rest in safety. The guidance began with mind maps listing the activities and feelings the space should hold, from which the idea of the puzzle piece emerged: each piece looks incomplete alone yet belongs to a whole, so that care first became a clear and gentle design position. In development, eight boxes of different sizes were arranged to hold rooms for rest, play and meals, the form refined first in a 3D model and then laser cut from board. Finally, ramps and balconies allow children to move freely between floors at their own pace, and the model presents a calm place built with patience and attention, so that architecture becomes a pair of hands ready to hold unease.

zh-Hant.heading: 拼圖形的安心空間-讓每一片都找到位置
zh-Hant.body: 自閉症兒童在擁擠或陌生的環境中常感到焦慮，學生想打造一個讓孩子能安心活動與休息的空間。指導過程先以心智圖列出空間應容納的活動與感受，再提煉出拼圖的概念：每一片單獨看似不完整，卻能拼成整體，讓關懷先成為一個清楚而溫柔的設計立場。進入推演，八個大小不同的盒子容納休息、遊戲與用餐的房間，形體先以3D建模推敲，再以板材雷射切割成形。最後，坡道與陽台讓孩子能依自己的步調在樓層間自由移動，模型呈現一個以關懷與耐心打造的安心場所，讓建築成為接住不安的一雙手。

pins.title: The Illusion of Choices
pins.description:
A wooden box wrapped in coloured yarn hides mirror shards, so looking inside shows only the viewer's own reflection.

Installation | Thought and perception | Pencil, card paper, wooden sticks, wool and glass | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 選擇的錯覺
zh-Hant.description:
一個纏繞彩色毛線的木箱內藏鏡面碎片，往內看時只會看見觀者自己的倒影。

裝置｜思想與感知｜鉛筆、卡紙、木條、毛線與玻璃｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wondered how people tell the real from the unreal. A box became the test, looking solid outside but holding a different world inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生思考人們如何分辨真實與虛幻。一個木箱成為實驗，外表看似實在，內部卻藏著另一個世界。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each of the four faces was matched to a different school of thought about truth. Sketches tried patterns of yarn, from order to tangle.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 四個面各自對應一種關於真理的思想流派。草圖嘗試從有序到糾結的不同毛線圖案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A painted wooden frame was wrapped in blue, black, natural and green yarn. Strands run from the inside to each face and never fold back.
captions: Looking out through blue yarn and clouds.
A head inside the black yarn network.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塗色的木框纏上藍色、黑色、原色與綠色毛線。線束由內部連向各個面，且不會折返。
captions: 透過藍色毛線與雲朵向外望。
置身黑色毛線網絡中的頭部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Mirror shards inside the box show viewers only themselves. The work suggests that every choice is a path with no way back.
captions: Vertical natural yarn around a viewer.
A viewer inside the tree of glass fragments.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 箱內的鏡面碎片只讓觀者看見自己。作品暗示每個選擇都是一條無法回頭的路。
captions: 圍繞觀者的垂直自然色毛線。
置身玻璃碎片之樹中的觀者。

sections.heading: The Illusion of Choices - A Box That Reflects Only Oneself
sections.body: The student wondered how people tell the real from the unreal, and a wooden box became the experiment: solid on the outside, yet holding another world within. The guidance first had the student match each of the box's four faces to a different school of thought about truth, then sketch yarn patterns ranging from strict order to tangle, so that abstract philosophy first settled into an order one could see. In development, a painted wooden frame was wrapped in blue, black, natural and green yarn, the strands running from the interior out to each face and never folding back, so that the rule of making itself became a metaphor for thought. Finally, mirror shards inside the box show viewers only themselves, and the work suggests that every choice is a path with no return, letting a question about truth quietly turn back toward whoever is looking.

zh-Hant.heading: 選擇的錯覺-一只只照見自己的箱子
zh-Hant.body: 學生思索人們如何分辨真實與虛幻，一只木箱成為實驗：外表看似實在，內部卻藏著另一個世界。指導過程先讓學生把箱子的四個面，各自對應一種關於真理的思想流派，再以草圖嘗試從有序到糾結的不同毛線圖案，讓抽象的哲學先落在可以觀看的秩序上。進入推演，塗色的木框纏上藍、黑、原色與綠色的毛線，線束由內部連向每一個面，且從不折返，製作的規則本身就成為思想的隱喻。最後，箱內的鏡面碎片只讓觀者看見自己，作品暗示每一個選擇都是一條無法回頭的路，讓一個關於真實的提問，安靜地回到凝視者身上。

pins.title: The Source of Purity
pins.description:
Three clay and foam cubes move from a pure blue block to a polluted, broken one and then to signs of rebirth.

Model making | Ocean and environment | Ultra-light clay, foam adhesive, foam board, acrylic, cotton, stone, leaves, sand and hay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 純淨之源
zh-Hant.description:
三個黏土與泡沫方塊，從純淨的藍色方塊走向受污染的破碎方塊，再到重生的跡象。

模型製作｜海洋與環境｜超輕黏土、泡沫膠、泡沫板、壓克力、棉花、碎石、落葉、沙與乾草｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Plastic and oil keep harming the ocean. The student wanted a simple form to show how clean water is lost and might return.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠與油污持續傷害海洋。學生想用一個簡單的形體，表現乾淨的水如何失去又可能回來。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A perfect blue cube was chosen to stand for clean sea and sky. Each later cube would be more scrambled, like a puzzle cube being turned.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以完美的藍色方塊代表乾淨的海洋與天空。之後的每個方塊都更加打亂，如同被轉動的方塊玩具。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Ultra-light clay and blue foam adhesive formed the cubes, and foam board built the polluted zone. Stones, leaves, sand and hay were added as details.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以超輕黏土與藍色泡沫膠塑造方塊，並以泡沫板建構污染區。碎石、落葉、沙與乾草作為細節加入。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The last cube is fully scrambled yet full of life, with foam waves and driftwood. The series shows that nature can heal if people act.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最後的方塊完全打亂卻充滿生機，帶有泡沫浪花與漂流木。這個系列表現只要人們行動，自然就能修復。

sections.heading: The Source of Purity - An Ocean Cube Scrambled and Restored
sections.body: Plastic and oil keep wounding the ocean, and the student wanted one simple form to tell how clean water is lost and how it might return. The guidance first settled on a perfect blue cube to stand for clear sea and sky, imagining each later cube more scrambled than the last, like a puzzle cube being turned, so that the story of pollution first became the clear logic of a series. In development, the cubes were shaped from ultra-light clay and blue foam adhesive, foam board built the polluted zone, and stones, leaves, sand and hay were added as details. Finally, the last cube, though fully scrambled, teems with life through foam waves and driftwood, and the series as a whole suggests that nature can heal when people act, turning worry into a hope that is gentle and steady at once.

zh-Hant.heading: 純淨之源-被打亂又復原的海洋方塊
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠與油污持續傷害著海洋，學生想用一個簡單的形體，說出乾淨的水如何失去、又如何可能回來。指導過程先選定一個完美的藍色方塊，代表潔淨的海洋與天空，並設想之後的每一個方塊都更加打亂，如同被轉動的方塊玩具，讓污染的過程先成為一個清晰的系列邏輯。進入推演，學生以超輕黏土與藍色泡沫膠塑造方塊，以泡沫板建構污染區，再加入碎石、落葉、沙與乾草作為細節。最後，最後一個方塊雖然完全打亂，卻因泡沫浪花與漂流木而充滿生機，整個系列訴說只要人們行動，自然便能修復，讓一份憂慮轉為溫柔而堅定的盼望。

pins.title: Two Sides Tower
pins.description:
A tall mixed-material model grows in six parts, each one telling a stage of a story about two rivals.

Model making | Narrative structure | PVC board, wooden and bamboo sticks, tin foil, clay, iron wire, foam and acrylic strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 雙面之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一座高聳的複合材料模型分六個部分生長，每個部分講述兩個對手故事中的一個階段。

模型製作｜敘事結構｜PVC板、木條與竹籤、錫箔、黏土、鐵絲、泡沫塊與壓克力條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to turn the plot of a crime film into a building. Two rivals, one on each side of the law, had to share one structure.
captions: Film stills arranged around the story sketch in five parts.
A colour sketch of the six parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把一部犯罪電影的情節轉化為建築。分處法律兩端的兩個對手，必須共享同一個結構。
captions: 圍繞五段故事草圖排列的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A colour sketch divided the story into six stages from bottom to top. Each stage was given its own material and form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張彩色草圖將故事由下而上分成六個階段。每個階段都被賦予各自的材料與形態。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stick platforms and stairs form the base, with a crumpled foil mass beside them. Above them rise folded paper, foam supports, clay and a cage of wire houses.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條平台與樓梯構成基座，旁邊是揉皺的錫箔量體。其上依序升起摺紙、泡沫支撐、黏土與鐵絲房屋組成的籠子。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower reads as one climb through the whole story. A detailed pen drawing records every part of it.
captions: A pen drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座塔讀起來就像一次貫穿整個故事的攀升。一張細膩的鋼筆畫記錄了它的每個部分。

sections.heading: Two Sides Tower - One Building Shared across the Law
sections.body: The student wanted to turn the plot of a crime film into a building, where two rivals standing on opposite sides of the law must share a single structure. The guidance first used a colour sketch to divide the story into six stages from bottom to top, and then assigned each stage its own material and form, so that every turn of the narrative became first a change of matter. In development, stick platforms and stairs formed the base beside a mass of crumpled foil, and above them rose folded paper, foam supports, clay and finally a cage of small wire houses, each layer holding a different kind of tension. In the end, the tower reads as one continuous climb through the whole story, and a detailed pen drawing records every part of it, so that the standoff between light and shadow is stacked, level by level, into a single tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 雙面之塔-法律兩端共享的一座建築
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把一部犯罪電影的情節轉化為建築：分處法律兩端的兩個對手，必須共享同一個結構。指導過程先以一張彩色草圖把故事由下而上分成六個階段，再為每個階段指定各自的材料與形態，讓敘事的轉折先成為材質的轉換。進入推演，木條平台與樓梯構成基座，旁邊是一團揉皺的錫箔量體，其上依序升起摺紙、泡沫支撐、黏土，以及由鐵絲房屋組成的籠子，每一層都是一種不同的張力。最後，這座塔讀起來就像一次貫穿整個故事的攀升，一張細膩的鋼筆畫記錄下它的每一個部分，讓光明與陰影的對峙，在同一座高塔中層層堆疊。

pins.title: Tower of Echoes
pins.description:
Roofs, door frames and a spire from familiar buildings are echoed in a white card tower wrapped by red paths.

Model making | Tower design | PVC board, wooden sticks and cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 回聲之塔
zh-Hant.description:
熟悉建築中的屋頂、門框與尖塔，在一座被紅色路徑環繞的白色紙板塔中迴響。

模型製作｜塔樓設計｜PVC板、木條與紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student took photos of the old brick buildings around them every day. The aim was to sample their parts and build a new tower from them.
captions: Photos of the old brick buildings and bell tower that the spire samples.
A stipple drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生每天拍攝身邊的老磚造建築。目標是取樣它們的構件，建造一座新的塔。
captions: 塔體取樣自的老磚造建築與鐘塔照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Triangular roofs, square door frames and window frames were picked out from the photos. A tall spire with doors on four sides became the top.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從照片中挑出三角形屋頂、方形門框與窗框。一座四面開門的高聳尖塔成為頂部。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Card walls were cut and glued with great care, since each cut decided whether the parts above could stand. Red strips wind through the levels as paths.
captions: Cutting and assembling the card tower and red paths by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙板牆面經過仔細切割與黏合，因為每一刀都決定上方構件能否站穩。紅色紙條作為路徑在各層間蜿蜒。
captions: 親手裁切並組裝卡紙塔體與紅色路徑。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The white tower climbs past arches, gables and ramps to a pointed spire. Small red figures show how people would move through it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色的塔經過拱門、山牆與坡道，升至尖頂。紅色小人偶呈現人們如何在其中移動。

sections.heading: Tower of Echoes - A Spire Sampled from Old Brick Buildings
sections.body: Every day the student photographed the old brick buildings nearby, and the work asked whether those everyday presences could be sampled to build a new tower. The guidance first led the student to pick out triangular roofs, square door frames and window frames from the photographs, crowning them with a tall spire that opens on all four sides, so that a familiar streetscape was first broken into a vocabulary that could be recombined. In development, card walls were cut and glued with great care, since every cut decided whether the parts above could stand, while red strips wound between the levels as paths, structure and circulation taking shape together. Finally, the white tower climbs past arches, gables and ramps to its pointed spire, small red figures showing how people would move within it, so that a daily gaze echoes upward into a vertical memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 回聲之塔-老磚樓取樣而成的尖塔
zh-Hant.body: 學生每天拍攝身邊的老磚造建築，作品要問的是：能否從這些日常的身影中取樣，建造一座新的塔？指導過程先引導學生從照片裡挑出三角形屋頂、方形門框與窗框，並以一座四面開門的高聳尖塔作為頂部，讓熟悉的街景先被拆解成可以重組的字彙。進入推演，紙板牆面經過細心的切割與黏合，因為每一刀都決定上方構件能否站穩，紅色紙條則作為路徑，在各層之間蜿蜒穿梭，結構與動線同時成形。最後，白色的塔經過拱門、山牆與坡道，一路升至尖頂，紅色小人偶示範人們如何在其中移動，讓日復一日的凝視，迴響成一座垂直的記憶。

pins.title: Steel Unity
pins.description:
Triangles of card braced by wooden sticks form an angular structure that can also be worn on the shoulder.

Model making | Wearable structure | PVC board and wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鋼之聯結
zh-Hant.description:
以木條支撐的紙板三角形，組成一個稜角分明、也能披在肩上的結構。

模型製作｜可穿戴結構｜PVC板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The steel frame of a tall tower caught the student's eye with its intricate yet orderly pattern. The question was how to turn that frame into a small object.
captions: The television tower whose steel frame inspired the structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座高塔的鋼構框架以其複雜卻有序的圖案吸引了學生。問題在於如何把這個框架轉化為小型物件。
captions: 啟發此結構的電視塔鋼構照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings traced how the frame repeats in triangles. Single card triangles were tested with sticks as braces.
captions: Reference images of faces wrapped in linear frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圖面描繪框架如何以三角形重複。以木條作為支撐，測試單一的紙板三角形。
captions: 以線性框架包覆臉部的參考圖像。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many triangles of different shapes were cut and joined into one angular form. Line and shaded drawings helped keep the whole piece cohesive.
captions: A line drawing of the form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 切割許多不同形狀的三角形，並接合成一個稜角分明的形體。線稿與明暗素描幫助整件作品保持一致。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished structure sits on a table or rests on the shoulder like armour. Its sticks and triangles echo the tower frame at a human scale.
captions: The structure worn on the shoulder like a knight's armour.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的結構可放在桌上，也能像盔甲般披在肩上。它的木條與三角形以人的尺度呼應塔的框架。
captions: 如騎士盔甲般戴在肩上的結構。

sections.heading: Steel Unity - A Tower's Frame Worn on the Shoulder
sections.body: The steel frame of a tall tower caught the student's eye with its intricate yet orderly pattern, and the work asked how that vast skeleton could become a small object. The guidance first used drawings to trace how the frame repeats itself in triangles, then tested a single card triangle braced with sticks, so that the logic of the structure was first understood in its smallest unit. In development, many triangles of differing shapes were cut and joined into one angular form, while line drawings and shaded studies helped the whole piece keep a single, coherent language. Finally, the finished structure can stand on a table or rest on the shoulder like armour, its sticks and triangles answering the tower's frame at the scale of a human body, so that the strength of a city's skyline is brought close to the skin.

zh-Hant.heading: 鋼之聯結-把高塔骨架披上肩頭
zh-Hant.body: 一座高塔的鋼構，以複雜而有序的圖案吸引了學生。作品要問的是，這副巨大的骨架如何轉化為一件小小的物件。指導過程先以圖面追索框架如何以三角形不斷重複，再以紙板做出單一三角形，用木條作為支撐加以測試，讓結構的邏輯先在最小的單元裡被理解。進入推演，許多形狀各異的三角形被切割、接合成一個稜角分明的形體，線稿與明暗素描則幫助整件作品維持一致的語言。最後，完成的結構既能立在桌上，也能像盔甲般披在肩頭，木條與三角形以人的尺度回應高塔的框架，讓城市天際線的力量，貼近了身體。

pins.title: Open Windows Community
pins.description:
Houses with oversized openings are cut into cross sections and grown into a small open community of white walls and wooden frames.

Model making | Housing and community | PVC board, wooden strips and cubes, cotton, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 開窗社區
zh-Hant.description:
帶有超大開口的住宅被切成剖面，並生長為一個由白牆與木框組成的小型開放社區。

模型製作｜住宅與社區｜PVC板、木條與木塊、棉花、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was struck by a house whose doors and windows blur into large openings. Such openness pushes against old ideas that kept women inside the home, and the student wrote a poem about their hidden feelings.
captions: House N by Sou Fujimoto Architects, the precedent for the project.
A study of light through the openings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被一棟門與窗模糊成大型開口的住宅所震撼。這種開放性對抗了將女性束縛於家中的舊觀念，學生為她們隱藏的情感寫了一首詩。
captions: 本案的先例：藤本壯介建築設計事務所的 House N。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Eight sketches turned the house into cross sections with openings of different sizes. From them the student made up four house types.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 八張草圖把住宅轉化為開口大小不一的剖面。學生從中發展出四種住宅類型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each type was built in white board and photographed from three sides. Public facilities in wooden frames and blocks were then added, following the pattern of the sections.
captions: One house type from three sides.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每種類型都以白色板材製作，並從三個面拍攝。接著依循剖面的圖案，加入以木框與木塊構成的公共設施。
captions: 一種住宅類型的三個面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The houses open onto stairs, frames and cotton trees shared by everyone. The community turns private homes outward.
captions: A cotton tree in a courtyard.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 住宅向所有人共享的樓梯、木框與棉花樹敞開。這個社區讓私人住宅轉向外部。

sections.heading: Open Windows Community - Private Homes Turned Outward
sections.body: A house whose doors and windows blur into broad openings moved the student deeply. Such openness pushes back against old ideas that kept women inside the home, and the student wrote a poem for the feelings once hidden there, so the work asked whether a dwelling could open outward. The guidance first led the student through eight sketches that turned the house into cross sections with openings of varied size, and from these four house types were distilled, so that a poetic feeling first found an architectural grammar. In development, each type was built in white board and photographed from three sides, then public facilities of wooden frames and blocks were added, following the patterns of the sections. Finally, the houses open onto stairs, frames and cotton trees shared by all, private homes turning to face the community, so that the cry within a poem becomes a landscape of windows looking toward one another.

zh-Hant.heading: 開窗社區-讓私宅向彼此敞開
zh-Hant.body: 一棟門與窗模糊成大型開口的住宅，深深觸動了學生。這種開放，抵抗著將女性留在家中的舊觀念，學生為那些被隱藏的情感寫下一首詩，作品於是問：住宅能否向外打開？指導過程先引導學生以八張草圖把住宅轉化為剖面，開口大小各不相同，再從中整理出四種住宅類型，讓詩意的感受先找到建築的語法。進入推演，每種類型以白色板材製作，從三個面拍攝檢視，再依循剖面的圖案，加入以木框與木塊構成的公共設施。最後，住宅向眾人共享的樓梯、框架與棉花樹敞開，私人的家轉身面向社區，讓一首詩裡的呼喊，化為一片彼此相望的開窗風景。

pins.title: Hidden Fears of a Night Street
pins.description:
Fears felt on a dark walk are mapped and built into thirteen wire-tangled stick frames hidden behind calm walls.

Model making | Urban perception | PVC board, wooden strips and cubes, cotton, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 夜街裡隱藏的恐懼
zh-Hant.description:
一次黑暗步行中感受到的恐懼被繪製成圖，並建造成十三個纏滿鐵絲、藏在平靜牆面後的木條框架。

模型製作｜城市感知｜PVC板、木條與木塊、棉花、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Three buildings from the final model.
最終模型中的三棟建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: On a trip, the student had to walk alone through a rough district at night with a dead phone. Darkness, laughter and noise leaked from the buildings, and the question became how a building can hide its chaos.
captions: A map of the district walked at night.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中，學生在手機沒電的情況下，必須在夜裡獨自穿越一個混亂的街區。黑暗、笑聲與噪音從建築中滲出，問題於是成為：建築如何隱藏它的混亂。
captions: 夜間步行經過的街區地圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew the route and marked what was frightening: passing trains, lines of sight, areas of darkness and levels of sound. Each factor became its own map.
captions: A mind map of the factors that made the street frightening.
Street photos with the hidden chaos traced over them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出走過的路線，並標出令人恐懼的事物：經過的列車、視線方向、黑暗區域與聲音大小。每個因素都成為一張獨立的地圖。
captions: 讓街道令人不安之因素的心智圖。
疊繪隱藏混亂的街道照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wires and pillars were stuck to thirteen stick structures and left messy on purpose. Small wire patterns stand for incidents, and pillars show how the events connect.
captions: Sticking the wires and pillars together by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲與柱子被黏在十三個木條結構上，並刻意保持凌亂。小型鐵絲圖案代表事件，柱子則呈現事件之間的關聯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The structures were joined into buildings that are messy inside but calm outside. Pale walls cover the tangle, just as the street hid its danger.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些結構被組合成內部雜亂、外部平靜的建築。淺色牆面掩蓋了糾結，正如那條街隱藏了它的危險。

sections.heading: Hidden Fears of a Night Street - A Tangle behind Calm Walls
sections.body: On a journey, with a dead phone, the student had to walk alone at night through a rough district, darkness, laughter and noise seeping from the gaps between buildings. The work asked how a building can hide its own chaos. The guidance first had the student draw the route taken and mark what had been frightening, passing trains, lines of sight, pockets of darkness, levels of sound, each factor becoming its own map, so that fear was first measured with a calm hand. In development, wires and pillars were fixed to thirteen stick structures and left deliberately messy, small wire patterns standing for incidents and pillars tracing how those events connect. Finally, the structures were joined into buildings that are tangled inside yet composed outside, pale walls drawn over the disorder just as the street once concealed its danger, so that the unease of a night walk is held within a silent form.

zh-Hant.heading: 夜街裡隱藏的恐懼-平靜牆面下的糾結
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中，學生在手機沒電的夜裡，獨自穿越一個混亂的街區，黑暗、笑聲與噪音從建築縫隙中滲出。作品由此發問：建築如何把混亂藏起來？指導過程先請學生畫出走過的路線，標出令人害怕的事物，經過的列車、視線的方向、黑暗的區域、聲音的大小，每個因素各成一張地圖，讓恐懼先被冷靜地測量。進入推演，鐵絲與柱子被黏上十三個木條結構，刻意保留凌亂，小小的鐵絲圖案代表一次次事件，柱子則說明事件之間如何牽連。最後，這些結構組合成內部糾結、外表平靜的建築，淺色牆面覆蓋住紛亂，正如那條街曾經隱藏它的危險，讓一段夜行的不安，被收進一座沉默的形體。

pins.title: Scenery along the Road
pins.description:
Layered wooden strips rise from a carved board like a canyon that changes shape with every angle.

Model making | Landscape form | Wooden board and wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沿途風景
zh-Hant.description:
層層木條從雕刻的木板上升起，宛如一座隨每個角度改變形態的峽谷。

模型製作｜地景形態｜木板與木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A canyon seen on a trip looked different from every angle. The student wanted a hand-made model that keeps this change and ties it to human life.
captions: The travel photo and the triangle mesh drawn over it.
A triangulated drawing of the scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中看到的峽谷從每個角度看都不一樣。學生想做一個保留這種變化、並連結人類生活的手工模型。
captions: 旅途照片與疊繪其上的三角網格。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photo was traced into a triangulated mesh. The mesh showed where surfaces fold and where they open.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張照片被描繪成三角網格。網格呈現出表面在哪裡折起、在哪裡打開。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin wooden strips were layered on a board to make the ground. Bundles of strips were then set at angles to rise above it.
captions: Cutting and gluing the wooden strips by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 細木條層層鋪在木板上構成地面。接著將成束的木條以不同角度架設，升起於其上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model looks like a canyon from one side and a tangle of paths from another. Light through the strips casts changing shadows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型從一側看像峽谷，從另一側看則是交錯的路徑。穿過木條的光線投下變化的陰影。

sections.heading: Scenery along the Road - Holding a Canyon's Change in Wooden Strips
sections.body: A canyon seen on a journey looked different from every angle, and the student wanted a hand-made model that keeps this change and ties it to human life. The guidance first led the student to trace a photograph into a triangulated mesh, reading from it where surfaces fold and where they open, so that natural form was first translated into geometry that could be worked with. In development, thin wooden strips were laid in layers across a board to make the ground, and bundles of strips were then set at varying angles to rise above it, the direction of the material carrying the swell of the terrain. Finally, the model reads as a canyon from one side and as a tangle of crossing paths from another, while light passing through the strips casts ever-changing shadows, so that scenery glimpsed along the road keeps turning with the viewer's eye on the tabletop.

zh-Hant.heading: 沿途風景-以木條留住峽谷的變化
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中看見的峽谷，從每個角度看都不一樣。學生想做一個手工模型，保留這種變化，並把它與人的生活連結起來。指導過程先引導學生把一張照片描繪成三角網格，從網格中讀出表面在哪裡折起、在哪裡打開，讓自然的形態先被轉譯為可以操作的幾何。進入推演，細木條層層鋪在木板上構成地面，接著將成束的木條以不同角度架起，升起於地面之上，材料的方向承接了地形的起伏。最後，完成的模型從一側看像峽谷，從另一側看卻是交錯的路徑，穿過木條的光投下不斷變化的陰影，讓一段沿途的風景，在桌面上繼續隨視角流轉。

pins.title: Optical Exploration
pins.description:
A hand-made cardboard camera is paired with a stick tower built to be seen through its lens.

Model making | Optics and architecture | Cardboard, wood, tape, optical lens | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光學探索
zh-Hant.description:
一台手工紙板相機，搭配一座為了透過其鏡頭觀看而建造的木條塔。

模型製作｜光學與建築｜紙板、木材、膠帶、光學鏡頭｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to learn how a camera forms an image. The plan was to build both a simple camera and a building for it to capture.
captions: A historic engraving explaining how a camera forms an image.
A concept drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想了解相機如何成像。計畫是同時建造一台簡易相機，以及一棟供它拍攝的建築。
captions: 說明相機成像原理的歷史版畫。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Cardboard formed the frame, and tape sealed off all light except at the lens. Wax paper was tested as the screen and gave the clearest image.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 紙板構成框架，膠帶封住鏡頭以外的所有光線。蠟紙被測試作為成像屏，呈現出最清晰的影像。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The tower was built only from wooden strips. The size of the box set the focal length, and the lens position set where the image lands.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塔僅以木條建造。盒子的尺寸決定焦距，鏡頭的位置決定影像落在何處。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Looking into the camera, one sees the tower appear on the wax paper. The project taught the student about lenses, focal length and building by hand.
captions: Testing the camera with people looking through it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從相機看進去，可以看到塔出現在蠟紙上。這個專案讓學生學到鏡頭、焦距與手工建造。
captions: 有人透過相機觀看的測試照片。

sections.heading: Optical Exploration - A Camera and the Tower It Gazes At
sections.body: The student wanted to understand how a camera forms an image, and so set out to build two things at once: a simple camera, and a building for it to capture. The guidance began with a cardboard frame for the camera, sealed with tape against every ray except those entering through the lens, followed by tests of different materials as a screen, until wax paper gave the clearest image, so that abstract optics were first proven between the hands. In development, the tower was built entirely of wooden strips, while the size of the box set the focal length and the position of the lens decided where the image would land, the seer and the seen shaping each other within the design. Finally, looking into the camera, one watches the tower appear on the wax paper, and the student learned about lenses, focal length and making by hand, turning a curious question into a work where light and architecture gaze at each other.

zh-Hant.heading: 光學探索-一台相機與它凝視的塔
zh-Hant.body: 學生想了解相機如何成像，於是決定同時建造兩件東西：一台簡易相機，以及一棟供它拍攝的建築。指導過程先以紙板構成相機的框架，用膠帶封住鏡頭以外的所有光線，再測試不同材料作為成像屏，最後由蠟紙呈現出最清晰的影像，讓抽象的光學原理先在雙手之間被證實。進入推演，塔僅以木條建造，盒子的尺寸決定焦距，鏡頭的位置決定影像落在何處，觀看者與被觀看者在設計中彼此牽動。最後，從相機看進去，塔便浮現在蠟紙之上，學生也從中學到鏡頭、焦距與手工建造，讓一次好奇的探問，成為光與建築相互凝望的作品。

pins.title: Fragments of Hope
pins.description:
Wavy lines drawn by many young hands are joined into one painting, then cut into a wooden puzzle given back as a gift.

Painting and puzzle design | Volunteer-inspired | Tracing paper, wooden board, marker | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 希望的碎片
zh-Hant.description:
許多孩子畫下的波浪線條被組合成一幅畫，再切割成一副木製拼圖，作為禮物送回給他們。

繪畫與拼圖設計｜志工經驗啟發｜描圖紙、木板、麥克筆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: While volunteering in weekend art classes, the student saw that many children found it hard to hold a brush steadily. Their drawings were mostly curved, wavy lines, and few could finish a picture alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在週末美術課擔任志工時，學生發現許多孩子難以穩定地握筆。他們的畫多半是彎曲的波浪線，很少有人能獨自完成一幅畫。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student collected the colourful lines drawn by ten children and looked for links between them. The lines met and formed small shapes, which the children then filled with colour.
captions: A small face on a piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生收集了十個孩子畫下的彩色線條，並尋找它們之間的關聯。線條相交形成小形狀，孩子們再為它們填上顏色。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The painting was scanned and set into a 3D puzzle model. Each piece was given its own small face, then cut from wood with a laser.
captions: The cut pieces in a box.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 畫作經掃描後放入3D拼圖模型。每一片都被賦予一張獨特的小臉，再以雷射從木板切出。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The puzzle went back to the children as a gift to put together. Each piece stands for one child, and the whole picture appears only when they join.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這副拼圖作為禮物送回孩子手中，讓他們一起拼。每一片代表一個孩子，只有拼在一起時，完整的畫面才會出現。

sections.heading: Fragments of Hope - Children's Lines Joined into One Picture
sections.body: While volunteering in weekend art classes, the student noticed that many children struggled to hold a brush steadily; their drawings were mostly curving, wavy lines, and few could finish a picture alone. The guidance first led the student to gather the colourful lines of ten children and look for the links between them, the places where lines crossed forming small shapes that the children then filled with colour by hand, so that difficulty itself became the starting point of creation. In development, the shared painting was scanned and set into a 3D puzzle model, each piece given its own small face and then cut from wood with a laser, digital and handmade processes woven together. Finally, the puzzle returned to the children as a gift to assemble: each piece stands for one child, and the full picture appears only when they are joined, turning an act of kindness into hope that holds together.

zh-Hant.heading: 希望的碎片-把孩子們的線條拼成一幅畫
zh-Hant.body: 在週末美術課擔任志工時，學生發現許多孩子難以穩穩握筆，畫下的多是彎曲的波浪線，很少有人能獨自完成一幅畫。指導過程先引導學生收集十個孩子的彩色線條，尋找它們之間的關聯，線條相交處形成小小的形狀，再由孩子們親手填上顏色，讓困難本身成為創作的起點。進入推演，這幅共同的畫被掃描、放入3D拼圖模型，每一片都被賦予一張獨特的小臉，再以雷射從木板切出，數位與手工在此交織。最後，拼圖作為禮物回到孩子們手中，每一片代表一個孩子，唯有拼在一起，完整的畫面才會浮現，讓一份善意，化為彼此相連的希望。

pins.title: Twisted Chessboard
pins.description:
A ceramic chessboard warps like cloth, and glazed pieces of very different shapes stand on its coloured squares.

Ceramics | Object design | Ceramic clay, underglaze, transparent glaze, glass glaze | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 扭曲的棋盤
zh-Hant.description:
一個陶瓷棋盤如布料般扭曲，形態迥異的上釉棋子立於彩色方格之上。

陶藝｜物件設計｜陶土、釉下彩、透明釉、玻璃釉｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to make a chessboard where the board itself is part of the play. A twisted surface would make every square feel uneven.
captions: A colour study of the warped grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想做一個讓棋盤本身也參與遊戲的棋盤。扭曲的表面會讓每個方格都顯得不平均。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings tested how a square grid bends and how many colours it could hold. Two kinds of pieces were planned: one large sculpted figure and many simple, formless ones.
captions: A sketch of the board and pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圖面測試了方格網如何彎曲、能容納多少色彩。規劃了兩種棋子：一個大型雕塑人物，以及許多簡單、無具體形態的棋子。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A relief board was carved in ceramic clay, then the pieces were shaped. After air-drying, underglaze added layered colour.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以陶土雕出浮雕棋盤，再塑造棋子。風乾後以釉下彩加上層次豐富的色彩。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Glass glaze makes the sculpted piece shine, and a clear glaze seals the whole set. The contrast between the pieces makes the game feel uneven from the start.
captions: The set before the final glaze.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 玻璃釉讓雕塑棋子閃閃發亮，透明釉則封住整組作品。棋子之間的對比，讓遊戲從一開始就顯得不平等。
captions: 上最後一層釉之前的棋組。

sections.heading: Twisted Chessboard - When the Board Joins the Game
sections.body: The student wanted a chessboard in which the board itself takes part in the play, its twisted surface making every square unequal. The guidance first used drawings to test how a square grid bends and how many colours it can hold, and to plan two kinds of pieces, one large sculpted figure and many simple, formless ones, so that the unevenness of the rules was thought through in design before any making. In development, the student carved a relief board in ceramic clay and then shaped the pieces, adding layered colour with underglaze once they had dried in the air, the handling of material becoming a continuation of thought. Finally, glass glaze makes the sculpted piece gleam and a clear glaze seals the whole set, while the stark contrast between the pieces makes the game feel unequal from the very first move, so that a chessboard quietly raises a question about fairness.

zh-Hant.heading: 扭曲的棋盤-讓棋盤也加入對弈
zh-Hant.body: 學生想做一個讓棋盤本身也參與遊戲的棋盤，扭曲的表面會讓每一格都不再平均。指導過程先以圖面測試方格網如何彎曲、能容納多少色彩，並規劃兩種棋子：一個大型的雕塑人物，與許多簡單、無具體形態的棋子，讓規則的不平等先在設計上被想清楚。進入推演，學生以陶土雕出浮雕棋盤，再塑造棋子，風乾之後以釉下彩一層層加上色彩，材料的處理成為思考的延續。最後，玻璃釉讓雕塑棋子閃閃發亮，透明釉封住整組作品，棋子之間的強烈對比讓遊戲從一開始就顯得不平等，讓一副棋盤，安靜地提出關於公平的提問。

pins.title: A Garden for an Individual
pins.description:
A photo collage of a window turns into striped walls and terrain, shaping a quiet garden walked in sequence.

Summer architecture studio | Garden design | Rhino model, picture collage | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 一個人的花園
zh-Hant.description:
一張窗戶的照片拼貼轉化為條紋牆與地形，塑造出一座依序漫步的寧靜花園。

暑期建築工作營｜花園設計｜Rhino模型、圖像拼貼｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The task was to design a garden for one person from a single image. The student began with a photo grid of the window beside the study desk.
captions: The first collage from window photos.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 題目是從一張圖像出發，為一個人設計花園。學生從書桌旁窗戶的照片格網開始。
captions: 由窗戶照片做成的第一張拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A perspective collage of the photos was redrawn to stress the contrast of bright and dark. The white and dark lines kept strict right angles to each other.
captions: Light and dark lines in the collage.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 照片的透視拼貼被重新繪製，以強調明暗對比。白色與深色線條彼此保持嚴格的直角關係。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many versions of wall and terrain led to the idea of striations across the landscape. Bands carved from the wall tops let sunlight fall into the spaces below.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 多次牆與地形的版本，發展出橫越地景的條紋概念。從牆頂刻出的帶狀開口，讓陽光灑入下方空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: After the final review, some strips were raised or lowered to form stairs. A visitor now moves through the garden in a clear order of light and shade.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 期末評圖後，部分條帶被升高或降低以形成階梯。訪客如今能依明暗的清楚順序穿越花園。

sections.heading: A Garden for an Individual - Walking through Striations of Light
sections.body: The brief was to design a garden for one person, beginning from a single image. The student chose the window beside the study desk and started from a photo grid of it. The guidance first led the student to redraw a perspective collage of the photographs so that the contrast of bright and dark came forward, white and dark lines holding strict right angles to one another, so that an everyday window first became an order of light. In development, many versions of wall and terrain gradually produced the idea of striations sweeping across the landscape, with bands carved from the tops of the walls letting sunlight fall into the spaces beneath. Finally, after the closing review, some strips were raised or lowered into stairs, and a visitor now moves through the garden in a clear sequence of light and shade, so that the view from one person's desk unfolds into a quiet, rhythmic walk.

zh-Hant.heading: 一個人的花園-在條紋間行走明與暗
zh-Hant.body: 題目是從一張圖像出發，為一個人設計一座花園。學生選擇了書桌旁的窗，從它的照片格網開始。指導過程先引導學生把照片的透視拼貼重新繪製，強調明與暗的對比，白色與深色線條彼此維持嚴格的直角，讓日常的一扇窗先成為一種光的秩序。進入推演，牆與地形經過多次版本的嘗試，逐漸發展出橫越地景的條紋概念，牆頂刻出的帶狀開口，讓陽光灑入下方空間。最後，在期末評圖之後，部分條帶被升高或降低，化為階梯，訪客得以依明暗清晰的順序穿越花園，讓一個人的書桌視野，延展成一段安靜而有節奏的漫步。

pins.title: Golf Motion in Space
pins.description:
The turning body of a golf swing is traced, frozen into a solid form and cut from stacked acrylic sheets.

Motion study | Sculpture | Rhino model, physical model, acrylic board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間中的高爾夫揮桿
zh-Hant.description:
高爾夫揮桿中轉動的身體被描繪下來，凝固成實體形態，再以層疊的壓克力板切割而成。

動作研究｜雕塑｜Rhino模型、實體模型、壓克力板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The acrylic model stands on its own.
壓克力模型能自行站立。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A golf swing turns the shoulders, waist and hips and folds the arms one after another. The student wanted to show how these linked motions could describe space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 高爾夫揮桿依序轉動肩、腰、髖，並彎曲手臂。學生想呈現這些連續動作如何描述空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Tracing the swing showed that the triangle between head, shoulder and wrist stays almost fixed while the body spins. Those points were taken out and reduced to simple diagrams.
captions: Points of the swing in order.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 描繪揮桿後發現，身體旋轉時頭、肩與手腕之間的三角關係幾乎不變。這些點被抽取出來，簡化為簡單的圖解。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In Rhino the diagrams grew from points to lines and then to a solid body. The body was sliced into contours and each slice was cut from acrylic.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在Rhino中，圖解從點發展為線，再成為實體。實體被切成等高輪廓，每一片都以壓克力切出。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model can stand on the ground by itself, like a statue or even a chair. Changing light throws striped shadows that move across it.
captions: Stripes of light through the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型能自行立於地面，像一座雕像，甚至像一張椅子。變化的光線投下在其上移動的條紋陰影。

sections.heading: Golf Motion in Space - One Swing Frozen into Sculpture
sections.body: A golf swing turns the shoulders, waist and hips in sequence while the arms fold after them, and the student wanted to know whether these linked motions could describe space. The guidance first had the student trace the path of the swing, discovering that the triangle between head, shoulder and wrist stays almost fixed while the body spins, and then extract those points into simple diagrams, so that movement first became geometry open to analysis. In development, the diagrams grew in Rhino from points into lines and then into a solid body, which was sliced into contours and cut piece by piece from acrylic, giving the motion a thickness. Finally, the model stands on the ground by itself, like a statue or even a chair, while shifting light throws striped shadows that travel across it, so that a fleeting swing is held still as a moment one can stay with.

zh-Hant.heading: 空間中的高爾夫揮桿-把一次揮動凝成雕塑
zh-Hant.body: 一次高爾夫揮桿，依序轉動肩、腰與髖，手臂隨之彎折。學生想知道，這些相連的動作能否描繪出空間。指導過程先讓學生描摹揮桿的軌跡，發現在身體旋轉時，頭、肩與手腕之間的三角關係幾乎不變，再把這些點抽取出來，簡化成清楚的圖解，讓運動先成為可被分析的幾何。進入推演，學生在Rhino中讓圖解從點長成線、再長成實體，接著把實體切成等高輪廓，每一片都以壓克力切出，動作因此有了厚度。最後，完成的模型能自行立於地面，像一座雕像，甚至像一張椅子，變化的光線在其上投下移動的條紋陰影，讓轉瞬即逝的一揮，被凝成一段可以停留的時間。

pins.title: Spiral of Choices
pins.description:
Five turning points of a story about chasing dreams become platforms on a spiral tower that climbs from bottom to top.

Model making | Narrative space | Plastic board, coloured aluminium wire, acrylic, reflective sheets | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 選擇的螺旋
zh-Hant.description:
一個追夢故事的五個轉折點，化為一座由下而上攀升的螺旋塔上的平台。

模型製作｜敘事空間｜塑膠板、彩色鋁線、壓克力、反光片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The spiral stair in blue light.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A favourite musical film made the student think about growth, choices and chasing dreams. The project asks how those themes could be read in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部喜愛的音樂電影讓學生思考成長、選擇與追夢。這個專題探問這些主題如何在空間中被閱讀。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Five key moments were picked, from a hopeful start to a final parting on separate paths. For each one, a body motion or a turn of the plot was drawn as a spatial part.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生挑選了五個關鍵時刻，從充滿希望的開始到各自走上不同道路的分別。每一個時刻的肢體動作或情節轉折，都被畫成一個空間構件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The parts were stacked from bottom to top in the order of the story. Each was built on its own and then joined into one tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些構件依故事順序由下往上堆疊。每一個先單獨製作，再組合成一座塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Stairs, rings and round platforms climb through blue light toward the top. The tower shows that each choice brings some loss, yet every step adds to growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 階梯、圓環與圓形平台在藍光中向上攀升。這座塔表達每個選擇都伴隨失去，但每一步都促成成長。

sections.heading: Spiral of Choices - Growth Climbing through Blue Light
sections.body: A favourite musical film set the student thinking about growing up, making choices and chasing dreams, and the work asked how such themes could be read in space. The guidance first invited the student to pick five key moments, from a hopeful beginning to a final parting on separate paths, and to draw the gesture or plot turn of each moment as a spatial part, so that the story was first broken into pieces one could hold. In development, the parts were stacked from bottom to top in the order of the narrative, each built on its own and then joined into one tower, giving time a vertical direction. Finally, stairs, rings and round platforms climb through blue light toward the summit, and the tower tells that every choice carries some loss while every step still adds to growth, turning the feeling left by a film into a spiral to look up at.

zh-Hant.heading: 選擇的螺旋-在藍光中攀升的成長
zh-Hant.body: 一部喜愛的音樂電影，讓學生思索成長、選擇與追夢，作品於是問：這些主題如何在空間中被閱讀？指導過程先請學生挑出五個關鍵時刻，從充滿希望的開端，到最終各自走上不同道路的分別，並把每一刻的肢體動作或情節轉折畫成一個空間構件，讓敘事先被拆成可以觸摸的片段。進入推演，構件依故事的順序由下而上堆疊，每一個先單獨製作，再組合成一座塔，時間因此有了垂直的方向。最後，階梯、圓環與圓形平台在藍光中向上攀升，這座塔訴說每個選擇都伴隨失去，而每一步仍促成成長，讓一段觀影的感動，化為一道可以仰望的螺旋。

pins.title: Imaginary Space
pins.description:
Traced pieces of curved, circular and flat buildings are collaged into one drawing and then built as a bursting white model.

Model making | Collage and form | PVC board, wooden sticks, wooden plate | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 想像的空間
zh-Hant.description:
描下的曲面、圓形與平面建築片段被拼貼成一張圖，再建成一座迸發的白色模型。

模型製作｜拼貼與形態｜PVC板、木棒、木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to buildings known for curved fronts, round forms and calm flat walls. The aim was to join these very different languages in one imaginary space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生被以曲面立面、圓形量體與平靜平牆聞名的建築所吸引。目標是把這些迥異的語彙結合在一個想像的空間中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Pictures of the buildings were traced on tracing paper and cut into pieces. The pieces were stretched and collaged into one composite drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 建築的圖片被描在描圖紙上並剪成碎片。這些碎片被延展、拼貼成一張組合圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Elements were lifted from the drawing to make the model. The work focused on fusing curved, circular and flat surfaces together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生從圖中提取元素來製作模型。重點在於把曲面、圓形與平面融合在一起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: White walls curl around round rooms while sticks burst out on every side. The model reads as a single new place built from many borrowed parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白牆環繞圓形空間捲曲，木棒向四面八方迸出。模型看起來是由許多借來的片段組成的一個全新場所。

sections.heading: Imaginary Space - Fusing Curve, Circle and Flat Wall
sections.body: The student was drawn to several architectural languages: curving facades, round volumes and calm flat walls. The work asked whether such different vocabularies could live together within one imaginary space. The guidance first had the student trace pictures of these buildings onto tracing paper, cut them into pieces, then stretch and collage them into a single composite drawing, so the borrowed fragments could converse on paper before anything was built. In development, elements were lifted from that drawing to make the model, with attention fixed on how curved, circular and flat surfaces might fuse into one, turning the tension of the collage into a question of construction. Finally, white walls curl around round rooms while sticks burst outward on every side, and the model reads as a wholly new place assembled from many borrowed parts, so that admiring the work of others becomes the beginning of a language of one's own.

zh-Hant.heading: 想像的空間-曲面圓形與平牆的融合
zh-Hant.body: 學生被幾種建築語彙所吸引：曲面的立面、圓形的量體、平靜的平牆。作品要問的是，這些迥異的語言能否在同一個想像的空間裡共處。指導過程先讓學生把建築圖片描在描圖紙上，剪成碎片，再延展、拼貼成一張組合圖，讓借來的片段在紙上先彼此對話。進入推演，學生從這張圖中提取元素製作模型，重點放在曲面、圓形與平面如何融為一體，讓拼貼的張力轉化為構造的問題。最後，白牆環繞圓形空間捲曲，木棒向四面八方迸出，模型讀起來是一個由許多借來的片段構成的全新場所，讓欣賞他人的作品，成為長出自己語言的開始。

pins.title: The Ground I Run Upon
pins.description:
Ground textures noticed on daily runs are drawn as patterns and rebuilt as small models of foam, cotton, sand and sticks.

Model making | Material study | Foam board, cotton, plaster, sand, pebbles, wooden sticks, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 我奔跑的地面
zh-Hant.description:
日常跑步時注意到的地面紋理被畫成圖案，再以泡棉、棉花、沙與木棒重建為小模型。

模型製作｜材料研究｜泡棉板、棉花、石膏、沙、卵石、木棒、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student runs around the neighbourhood and slows down when a view catches the eye. At that pace, the texture of the ground beneath becomes very clear.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生常在住家附近跑步，看到吸引目光的景色就會放慢腳步。在這樣的速度下，腳下地面的紋理變得格外清晰。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Some ground was hard and some was soft, and each was made of different materials. The student photographed the ground and traced a pattern from each texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 有些地面堅硬、有些柔軟，各自由不同材料組成。學生拍下地面，並從每種紋理描出圖案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Materials that felt close to each texture were chosen, though not the same as on the ground. Each model was also lifted upward so it could be read as a space.
captions: A stick frame over the ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇感覺接近各種紋理的材料，雖然與地面上的並不相同。每個模型也被向上發展，讓它能被讀成一個空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The pieces turn ordinary ground into shelters, sails and gardens. Working with so many materials broadened the student's sense of texture and making.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些作品把平凡的地面變成棚架、帆與花園。運用這麼多材料，拓展了學生對紋理與製作的感受。

sections.heading: The Ground I Run Upon - Reading Space Beneath the Feet
sections.body: The student often runs around the neighbourhood, slowing down whenever a view catches the eye, and at that pace the texture of the ground underfoot becomes vivid. The work asked whether these surfaces, so often stepped on, could become space. The guidance first helped the student notice that some ground is hard and some soft, each made of different materials, and to photograph them and trace a pattern from every texture, so that sensations glimpsed in passing were first held still. In development, the student chose materials that felt close to each texture without copying it, and lifted every model upward so that it could be read as a space. Finally, the pieces turn ordinary ground into shelters, sails and gardens, and working with so many materials widened the student's sense of texture and making, so that an everyday route became a notebook of space one can touch.

zh-Hant.heading: 我奔跑的地面-在腳下讀出空間
zh-Hant.body: 學生常在住家附近跑步，每當景色吸引目光便放慢腳步，而在那樣的速度裡，腳下地面的紋理變得格外清晰。作品要問的，是這些被踩過的質地能否成為空間。指導過程先讓學生察覺地面有硬有軟、材料各異，拍下它們並從每種紋理描出圖案，讓奔跑時一閃而過的感受先被定格。進入推演，學生選擇感覺相近卻不相同的材料來詮釋每一種紋理，並讓每個模型向上生長，使它能被讀成一個空間。最後，這些作品把平凡的地面變成棚架、帆與花園，大量材料的嘗試也拓展了學生對質感與製作的體會，讓日常的路徑成為一本可以觸摸的空間筆記。

pins.title: Fragments House
pins.description:
Drawings of one given image are broken into fragments and rebuilt, step by step, into a long house by a lake.

Summer architecture studio | House design | Foam board, museum board, Photoshop, Rhino, Illustrator | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 碎片之屋
zh-Hant.description:
一張指定圖像的多次繪製被拆解成碎片，再一步步重組成一座湖畔的長形住宅。

暑期建築工作營｜住宅設計｜泡棉板、博物館紙板、Photoshop、Rhino、Illustrator｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Every student received the same image and had six weeks to turn it into architecture. The student set out to find forms and line weights hidden in that one picture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 每位學生都拿到同一張圖像，並有六週把它轉化為建築。學生著手尋找藏在這張圖中的形態與線條粗細。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many drawings of the image were made by hand and then layered digitally. The work kept moving from flat drawings to models and back again.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先手繪多張圖像研究，再以數位方式層疊。過程不斷在平面圖與模型之間來回轉換。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small fragments from the scale models were joined into one overall form. The form became a house by a hillside lake for two scientists.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 比例模型中的小碎片被組合成一個整體形態。這個形態成為山坡湖畔一座供兩位科學家居住的住宅。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Long slabs and walls slide past each other and reach out over the water. The course also taught the student to cut cleaner and manage time better.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 長形樓板與牆體彼此錯動，向水面伸出。這門課也讓學生學會切得更俐落、更善於管理時間。

sections.heading: Fragments House - A Lakeside Home Grown from One Image
sections.body: Every student received the same image and six weeks to turn it into architecture, and the student set out to find the forms and line weights hidden inside that single picture. The guidance first had the student study the image through many hand drawings and then layer them digitally, moving back and forth between flat drawings and models, so that the latent space of the picture was revealed little by little. In development, small fragments from the scale models were joined into one overall form, and that form gradually became a house by a hillside lake for two scientists, giving abstract research someone to live in it. Finally, long slabs and walls slide past one another and reach out over the water, and beyond the work itself the student learned to cut more cleanly and manage time better, so that six weeks of translation were also a training of hand and mind.

zh-Hant.heading: 碎片之屋-從一張圖長出湖畔住宅
zh-Hant.body: 每位學生都拿到同一張圖像，有六週把它轉化為建築。學生著手尋找藏在這張圖裡的形態與線條粗細。指導過程先讓學生以手繪反覆研究圖像，再以數位方式層層疊合，並在平面與模型之間不斷往返，讓一張圖的潛在空間一點一點被揭露。進入推演，比例模型中的小碎片被組合成一個整體形態，這個形態逐漸成為一座山坡湖畔的住宅，供兩位科學家居住，抽象的研究於是有了生活的對象。最後，長形樓板與牆體彼此錯動，向水面伸出，作品之外，學生也學會切得更俐落、更善於管理時間，讓六週的轉譯同時成為一段手與心的磨練。

pins.title: Cell Bridge
pins.description:
A frame of cell-like openings rises over a small sunken stage, letting light fall onto the performers below.

Summer architecture studio | Performance space | Polystyrene foam board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 細胞之橋
zh-Hant.description:
一座由細胞狀開口組成的框架升起於小型下沉舞台之上，讓光線灑落在下方的表演者身上。

暑期建築工作營｜表演空間｜聚苯乙烯泡棉板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The earlier course project turned a parking space under an elevated park into a stage for a small band. Rows of benches circled a round platform sunk below the pavement.
captions: The elevated park site above the parking space.
A section of the sunken stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 先前的課程專題把高架公園下方的一個停車位改造成小型樂團的舞台。一排排長椅環繞著一個低於路面的圓形平台。
captions: 停車空間上方的高架公園基地。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: For the next step, the student looked at how living cells move and change shape. The idea was a frame that could feel alive and also bring in daylight.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 下一步，學生研究活細胞如何移動與變形。構想是一個看起來有生命、同時能引入日光的框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cells with rounded openings were cut from foam board and joined at their edges. Layers of cells were stacked into a long, bridge-like frame over the stage.
captions: Cutting and assembling the cells on the cutting mat.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 帶有圓角開口的細胞單元以泡棉板切出，並在邊緣相接。一層層細胞單元被堆疊成跨越舞台的長形橋狀框架。
captions: 在切割墊上裁切並組裝單元。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Light passes through the openings and moves across the stage below. The frame gives the small performance space a lively, organic roof.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 光線穿過開口，在下方舞台上移動。這個框架為小小的表演空間撐起一片生動而有機的屋頂。

sections.heading: Cell Bridge - Organic Light over a Sunken Stage
sections.body: An earlier course project had turned a single parking space beneath an elevated park into a stage for a small band, with rows of benches circling a round platform sunk below the pavement. This time the work asked how that stage might gain a roof that seems to breathe. The guidance led the student to observe how living cells move and change shape, imagining a frame that could feel alive while drawing daylight in, so that biological form became the starting point of structure. In development, cells with rounded openings were cut from foam board and joined at their edges, then stacked layer upon layer into a long, bridge-like frame spanning the stage. In the end, light passes through the openings and drifts slowly across the stage below, and the frame gives the small performance space a lively, organic roof, adding a rhythm of light and life to a design carried forward.

zh-Hant.heading: 細胞之橋-為下沉舞台撐起有機的光
zh-Hant.body: 先前的課程專題，把高架公園下方的一格停車位改造成小型樂團的舞台，一排排長椅環繞著低於路面的圓形平台。這一次，作品要問的是如何為這個舞台加上一片會呼吸的頂。指導過程引導學生觀察活細胞如何移動與變形，構想一個看似有生命、又能引入日光的框架，讓生物的形態成為結構的起點。進入推演，帶圓角開口的細胞單元以泡棉板切出，沿邊緣彼此相接，再一層層堆疊成跨越舞台的長形橋狀框架。最後，光線穿過開口，在下方舞台上緩緩移動，這個框架為小小的表演空間撐起一片生動而有機的屋頂，讓延續的設計多了一層光與生命的節奏。

pins.title: Rhythm of Notes
pins.description:
Notes, clefs and beats of a piano piece are turned into shapes, laid out as a diagram and built up in thin sticks and blue sheets.

Model making | Music and form | Coloured plastic sheets, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 音符的節奏
zh-Hant.description:
一首鋼琴曲中的音符、譜號與節拍被轉化為形狀，排成圖解，再以細木棒與藍色片材堆疊而成。

模型製作｜音樂與形態｜彩色塑膠片、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Every piece of music is built from meter, dynamics, rhythm, harmony and scales. The student wanted to show the movement and energy these parts create together.
captions: The printed piano score whose notes, clefs and beats were translated into forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 每一首樂曲都由拍子、力度、節奏、和聲與音階構成。學生想呈現這些部分共同創造的動態與活力。
captions: 被轉化為形狀的鋼琴樂譜，包含音符、譜號與節拍。
轉化為形態的音樂符號。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each element, from single notes to clefs, was given its own shape. The shapes were then placed along a chosen piano piece to show how they move and meet.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從單一音符到譜號，每個元素都被賦予專屬的形狀。這些形狀再依一首選定的鋼琴曲排列，呈現它們如何移動與交會。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The flat diagram was raised into a model with thin wooden sticks. Open common areas sit beside smaller, more closed and private corners.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 平面圖解被以細木棒提升為立體模型。開放的公共區域旁，是較小、較封閉而私密的角落。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Small triangles stand for movement in the music and cast lively shadows. Light slips through the gaps into the empty spaces between the sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 小三角形代表音樂中的律動，並投下生動的陰影。光線從縫隙滲入木棒之間的空隙。

sections.heading: Rhythm of Notes - Listening to a Piano Piece in Sticks
sections.body: Every piece of music is built from meter, dynamics, rhythm, harmony and scale, and the student wanted to show the movement and energy these elements stir up together. The guidance first asked the student to give each element its own shape, from single notes to clefs, and then to lay those shapes along a chosen piano piece to watch how they travel and meet, so that a score first became a spatial diagram. In development, the flat diagram was raised into a model of thin wooden sticks, with open common areas set beside smaller, more enclosed and private corners, the rise and fall of sound translated into the opening and closing of space. Finally, small triangles stand for the pulse of the music and cast lively shadows, while light slips through the gaps between the sticks, so the piece is no longer only heard but becomes a rhythm one can stand inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 音符的節奏-以木棒聆聽一首鋼琴曲
zh-Hant.body: 每一首樂曲都由拍子、力度、節奏、和聲與音階構成。學生想呈現的，是這些元素共同激起的動態與能量。指導過程先讓學生為每個元素賦予專屬的形狀，從單一音符到譜號，再沿著一首選定的鋼琴曲排列，觀察它們如何移動、如何交會，讓樂譜先成為一張空間的圖解。進入推演，平面圖解以細木棒被提升為立體模型，開放的公共區域旁，安排了較小、較封閉的私密角落，聲音的強弱於是轉譯成空間的開闔。最後，小三角形代表音樂中的律動，投下生動的陰影，光線從縫隙滲入木棒之間的空隙，讓一首曲子不再只是被聽見，而是可以在其中駐足的節奏。

pins.title: Piano Key Tower
pins.description:
Notes from piano scores are drawn as black and white boxes, then stacked into an uneven tower of white layers.

Model making | Music and vertical city | Foam board, museum board, Photoshop, Rhino, Illustrator | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 琴鍵之塔
zh-Hant.description:
鋼琴樂譜中的音符被畫成黑白方塊，再堆疊成一座參差不齊的白色層疊高塔。

模型製作｜音樂與垂直城市｜泡棉板、博物館紙板、Photoshop、Rhino、Illustrator｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower set into a skyline.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student has played piano since early childhood and loves classical pieces. The project asks how the black and white keys could become a building.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生從小就彈鋼琴，熱愛古典樂曲。這個專題探問黑白琴鍵如何成為一棟建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Short passages of favourite pieces were chosen and each note was redrawn as a box. Filled boxes stand for the black keys.
captions: Notes filled as boxes on the score.
The notes as a 3D block diagram.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生挑選喜愛樂曲中的短樂段，把每個音符重畫成方塊。填黑的方塊代表黑鍵。
captions: 在樂譜上填成方塊的音符。
音符化成的立體方塊圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The idea of building upward instead of outward guided the next step. Board layers, each with its own uneven design, were built one by one and stacked.
captions: Cutting and stacking the foam and board blocks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 向上而非向外發展的概念引導了下一步。每一層都有獨特而不規則設計的板材層被逐一製作並堆疊起來。
captions: 親手裁切並堆疊泡沫與板材量體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each block could hold homes, sports, dining, balconies or green rooms. The tower can change or grow taller as needs change.
captions: A sketch looking up the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個方塊都能容納住宅、運動、餐飲、陽台或綠色空間。這座塔可以隨需求改變或繼續長高。

sections.heading: Piano Key Tower - Notes Stacked into a Skyscraper
sections.body: The student has played piano since early childhood and loves classical music, so the work asked whether black and white keys could become a building. The guidance first invited the student to choose short passages from favourite pieces and redraw every note as a box, the filled boxes standing for black keys, so that sound first became a form that could be seen on paper. In development, the idea of growing upward rather than outward guided the next step: board layers, each with its own uneven design, were made one by one and stacked, giving the melody a height. Finally, every block can hold homes, sport, dining, balconies or green rooms, and the tower can change or keep growing as needs shift, turning a familiar phrase of music into a vertical score for a city that is still growing, still being played.

zh-Hant.heading: 琴鍵之塔-把音符疊成摩天樓
zh-Hant.body: 學生從小彈鋼琴，熱愛古典樂曲，於是作品問：黑白琴鍵能否成為一棟建築？指導過程先請學生從喜愛的樂曲中挑出短短的樂段，把每一個音符重畫成方塊，填黑的方塊代表黑鍵，讓聲音先在紙上變成可以被觀看的形體。進入推演，向上而非向外發展的概念引導了下一步，每一層板材都有各自不規則的設計，被逐一製作、層層疊起，旋律因此有了高度。最後，每個方塊都能容納住宅、運動、餐飲、陽台或綠色空間，這座塔還能隨需求改變或繼續長高，讓一段熟悉的樂句，成為一座仍在生長、仍在演奏的城市垂直樂譜。

pins.title: Trombone Metropolis
pins.description:
A trombone is taken apart into tubes on paper, and the parts become an industrial city built from recycled nails and bike parts.

Model making | Industrial city | Recycled nails, screws, bicycle parts | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 長號都市
zh-Hant.description:
一把長號在紙上被拆解成管件，這些部件化為一座以回收螺絲與單車零件建成的工業城市。

模型製作｜工業城市｜回收鐵釘、螺絲、單車零件｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The trombone, a long-time interest of the student, is made of many linked tubes. The project asks whether those parts could become blocks for building a city.
captions: A product photo of the brass instrument that was taken apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 長號是學生長久以來的興趣，由許多相連的管子組成。這個專題探問這些部件能否成為建造城市的積木。
captions: 被拆解的銅管樂器產品照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched the whole instrument and then focused on the slide braces and mouthpiece. In Photoshop the drawings were cut into small pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先畫下整把樂器，再聚焦於滑管支架與吹嘴。這些圖在Photoshop中被切成小片段。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Only the broken-down parts were used to draw new buildings and structures. The scale model then swapped tubes for recycled nails and bicycle parts.
captions: Sorting and joining the metal parts by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生只用拆解後的部件來繪製新的建築與結構。比例模型再以回收鐵釘與單車零件取代管件。
captions: 親手分類並接合金屬零件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Long parts act as pipes and thick nails act as beams, like the inside of a factory. Small figures show that people can still live and meet in this metal skyline.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 長形零件像管線，粗鐵釘像樑，宛如工廠內部。小人偶表示人們仍能在這片金屬天際線中生活與相遇。

sections.heading: Trombone Metropolis - An Instrument Taken Apart into City Blocks
sections.body: The trombone, a long-held passion of the student, is made of many linked tubes, and the work asked whether those parts could become building blocks for a city. The guidance first had the student draw the whole instrument, then narrow the focus to the slide braces and the mouthpiece, cutting the drawings into small fragments in Photoshop, so that a familiar instrument was first dismantled into unfamiliar components. In development, only these broken-down parts were used to draw new buildings and structures, and the scale model swapped tubes for recycled nails and bicycle parts, letting the materials carry the same mechanical character. Finally, long pieces act as pipes and thick nails as beams, like the interior of a factory, while small figures show that people can still live and meet within this metal skyline, so that the sound of one trombone echoes outward into a city.

zh-Hant.heading: 長號都市-把樂器拆成城市的積木
zh-Hant.body: 長號是學生長久以來的興趣，由許多相連的管子組成。作品要問的是，這些部件能否成為建造城市的積木。指導過程先讓學生完整畫下整把樂器，再把目光收斂到滑管支架與吹嘴，並在Photoshop中把圖切成細小的片段，讓熟悉的樂器先被拆解成陌生的構件。進入推演，學生只用這些拆解後的部件繪製新的建築與結構，比例模型再以回收鐵釘與單車零件替代管件，讓材料也承接了機械的氣質。最後，長形零件化為管線，粗鐵釘成為樑柱，宛如工廠的內部，小人偶則說明人們仍能在這片金屬天際線中生活與相遇，讓一把長號的聲音，迴盪成一座城市。

pins.title: Crossing Lines
pins.description:
A collage of a busy street crossing and line drawings of film scenes are folded together into one layered paper city.

Model making | Collage city | Photoshop, Illustrator, Procreate, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 交錯之線
zh-Hant.description:
繁忙路口的拼貼與電影場景的線稿被摺疊結合，成為一座層層疊疊的紙上城市。

模型製作｜拼貼城市｜Photoshop、Illustrator、Procreate、紙材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to join a favourite street scene and a favourite science fiction film in one work. The question was how two very different worlds could share one city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把最喜愛的街景與最喜愛的科幻電影結合在同一件作品中。問題在於兩個截然不同的世界如何共享一座城市。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Buildings were cut from photos of a busy crossing and rebuilt as a noisy collage. Scenes from the film were sketched only as line segments on a black ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從繁忙路口的照片中剪下建築，重組成一幅喧鬧的拼貼。電影場景則只以線段的形式畫在黑色底上。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The two layers were printed and folded into standing frames. Early studies tested how the frames could lean and lock together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 兩個圖層被列印出來並摺成立起的框架。早期研究測試這些框架如何傾斜並互相扣合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model reads like a dragon of buildings winding across the table. Photo surfaces and white line frames sit side by side, so both worlds stay visible.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型宛如一條由建築組成、蜿蜒於桌面的巨龍。照片表面與白色線框並置，讓兩個世界都清晰可見。

sections.heading: Crossing Lines - A Street and a Science Fiction Share One City
sections.body: The student wanted to bring a favourite street scene and a favourite science fiction film into a single work, and the question was how two utterly different worlds could share one city. The guidance first let each world find its own language: buildings were cut from photographs of a busy crossing and rebuilt as a noisy collage, while scenes from the film were drawn only as line segments on a black ground, one dense and one spectral, each answering the other. In development, the two layers were printed and folded into standing frames, and early studies tested again and again how they might lean and lock together, letting a flat dialogue grow into structure. In the end, the model winds across the table like a dragon made of buildings, photographic surfaces and white line frames standing side by side, so that the real and the imagined meet on the same street.

zh-Hant.heading: 交錯之線-街景與科幻共享一座城
zh-Hant.body: 學生想把最喜愛的街景與最喜愛的科幻電影放進同一件作品，問題在於：兩個截然不同的世界，如何共享一座城市？指導過程先讓兩個世界各自找到語言：從繁忙路口的照片中剪下建築，重組為一幅喧鬧的拼貼；電影場景則只以線段描在黑色底上，一實一虛，彼此對照。進入推演，兩個圖層被列印並摺成立起的框架，早期的研究反覆測試它們如何傾斜、如何互相扣合，讓平面的對話長出結構。最後，模型宛如一條由建築組成的巨龍蜿蜒於桌面，照片的表面與白色線框並肩而立，兩個世界都清晰可見，讓真實與虛構在同一條街上交會。

pins.title: Independent Ecosystem Research
pins.description:
A woven bamboo tower carries plants from four climates, from tropical at the base to boreal at the top.

Model making | Ecosystem and climate | Bamboo, wood, mosses, plants, branches | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 獨立生態系統研究
zh-Hant.description:
一座竹編塔承載四種氣候的植物，從底部的熱帶到頂端的寒帶。

模型製作｜生態與氣候｜竹、木、苔蘚、植物、樹枝｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The woven tower with moss and branches.
覆滿苔蘚與樹枝的編織塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Climate change and fast-growing cities are putting pressure on many plants and animals. The student asked what a stable home for living things might look like in a changing world.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷與快速擴張的城市正對許多動植物造成壓力。學生思考在變動的世界裡，生物穩定的家園會是什麼模樣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Plants were grouped into four climate types, from tropical to subtropical, temperate and boreal. A sketch placed them in layers from bottom to top.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把植物分為熱帶、亞熱帶、溫帶與寒帶四種氣候類型。一張草圖將它們由下而上分層排列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bamboo weaving was chosen as the main structure because it is gentle on the environment and strong enough. Woven shells were shaped to hold soil, moss and branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生選擇竹編作為主要結構，因為它對環境友善且足夠堅韌。編織外殼被塑造成能承載土壤、苔蘚與樹枝的形狀。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower changes its plants as it rises, like a small climate map. It expresses a calm and stable world where living things can stay.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔隨高度變換植物，就像一張小型氣候地圖。它表達出一個讓生物得以安居的平靜而穩定的世界。

sections.heading: Independent Ecosystem Research - A Woven Bamboo Climate Tower
sections.body: Climate change and swiftly spreading cities are pressing hard on many plants and animals, and from this the student asked what a stable home for living things might look like in a shifting world. The guidance first led the student to sort plants into four climates, tropical, subtropical, temperate and boreal, and to sketch them in layers from bottom to top, so that the planet's climates were first gathered into a single vertical order. In development, bamboo weaving was chosen as the main structure, gentle on the environment yet strong enough, and the woven shells were shaped into vessels able to hold soil, moss and branches. Finally, the finished tower changes its vegetation as it rises, like a small map of climates, expressing a calm world where life can stay, and turning concern about a crisis into an act of carefully woven care.

zh-Hant.heading: 獨立生態系統研究-一座竹編的氣候之塔
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷與快速擴張的城市，正壓迫著許多動植物的生存。學生由此發問：在變動的世界裡，生物穩定的家園會是什麼模樣？指導過程先引導學生把植物分為熱帶、亞熱帶、溫帶與寒帶四種氣候，並以草圖由下而上分層排列，讓抽象的地球氣候先被收進一個垂直的秩序。進入推演，學生選擇竹編作為主要結構，因為它對環境溫和又足夠堅韌，編織的外殼被塑形成能盛載土壤、苔蘚與樹枝的容器。最後，完成的塔隨高度變換植被，宛如一張小小的氣候地圖，表達出一個讓生命得以安居的平靜世界，也讓對危機的憂慮，轉化為一種細心編織的守護。

pins.title: Library Renovation
pins.description:
A web of wooden sticks holds coloured translucent panes, testing a new ceiling that paints the floor with light.

Model making | Ceiling renovation | Coloured plastic sheets, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 圖書館改造
zh-Hant.description:
木棒編成的網架承托彩色半透明板，試驗一片能以光彩繪地面的新天花板。

模型製作｜天花板改造｜彩色塑膠片、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student set out to rethink the ceiling of a library at school. The aim was a ceiling that changes how light enters and colours the room.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生著手重新構想學校圖書館的天花板。目標是讓天花板改變光線進入的方式，並為空間染上色彩。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Coloured glass windows in old churches were the main inspiration. The student studied how tinted glass turns plain daylight into patches of colour.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 古老教堂中的彩色玻璃窗是主要靈感來源。學生研究有色玻璃如何把平凡的日光化為一片片色彩。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A spider-web structure of wooden sticks was built to hold translucent coloured sheets as panes. Each pane was set at a different angle to test the shadows it casts.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木棒建構蜘蛛網般的結構，承托作為窗板的半透明彩色片。每片彩板以不同角度安裝，以測試它投下的陰影。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under a strong light, the model throws coloured shapes across the floor and walls. Small figures show how a reader would sit and walk within the shifting colour.
captions: A figure in the coloured shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在強光下，模型把彩色形狀投射到地面與牆上。小人形呈現讀者如何在變幻的色彩中坐下與走動。

sections.heading: Library Renovation - Dyeing Daylight for Reading
sections.body: The student set out to reimagine the ceiling of the school library, hoping to change how light enters and to tint the room where reading happens. The guidance first turned attention to the coloured glass windows of old churches, asking the student to study how tinted panes transform plain daylight into patches of colour, finding a grammar of light in history. In development, wooden sticks were woven into a spider-web structure that holds translucent coloured sheets as panes, each set at a different angle and tested one by one for the shadow it casts, so that structure and colour were examined together. Finally, under a strong light, the model scatters coloured shapes across floor and walls, while small figures show how a reader might sit and wander through the drifting hues, giving an everyday space among the shelves a quiet, luminous canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 圖書館改造-把日光染成閱讀的顏色
zh-Hant.body: 學生著手重新構想學校圖書館的天花板，希望它改變光線進入的方式，為閱讀的空間染上色彩。指導過程先把目光引向古老教堂的彩色玻璃窗，讓學生研究有色玻璃如何把平凡的日光化為一片片色塊，從歷史中找到光的語法。進入推演，學生以木棒編出蜘蛛網般的結構，承托半透明的彩色片作為窗板，每一片都以不同角度安裝，逐一測試它投下的陰影，讓結構與色彩一起被檢驗。最後，在強光之下，模型把彩色的形狀灑落在地面與牆上，小人形示範讀者如何在流動的色彩中坐下、走動，讓一處日常的書架之間，多了一層安靜而明亮的光之頂蓋。

pins.title: Machinery City
pins.description:
Toy bricks, gears and a small programmed controller come together as a moving city of arms, bridges and lifts.

Model making | Programming design | Toy bricks, gears, sensors, controller board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 機械城市
zh-Hant.description:
玩具積木、齒輪與小型程式控制器組合成一座擁有手臂、橋梁與升降機的會動城市。

模型製作｜程式設計｜玩具積木、齒輪、感測器、控制板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how a city could move like a machine. The student imagined parts that lift, swing and connect on their own.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問城市能否像機器一樣運作。學生想像能自行抬升、擺動與連接的部件。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A hand sketch mapped out arms, shafts and gears before building began. Each motion was broken down into a simple mechanism.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 動手搭建前，學生先以手繪草圖規劃手臂、轉軸與齒輪。每個動作都被拆解成簡單的機構。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The mechanisms were built from toy bricks and linked to a controller board and sensors. The student then wrote programs to set each part in motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些機構以玩具積木搭建，並連接控制板與感測器。學生接著編寫程式讓每個部件動起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model behaves like a small working city with a lifting bridge of beams. It joins design, mechanics and coding in one piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型像一座小型運轉中的城市，擁有一道由樑組成的升降橋。它在同一件作品中結合了設計、機械與程式。

sections.heading: Machinery City - A City That Moves on Its Own
sections.body: The work began with a bold question: could a city run the way a machine does? The student imagined parts that lift, swing and connect by themselves. The guidance first asked for hand sketches made before any building began, mapping arms, shafts and gears and breaking each motion into the simplest possible mechanism, so that imagination gained a skeleton that could be understood. In development, the mechanisms were assembled one by one from toy bricks and wired to a controller board and sensors, and the student then wrote the programs that woke each part in turn. In the end, the model behaves like a small working city, a lifting bridge of beams rising and falling at its heart, where design, mechanics and code meet in a single piece. The city becomes not only a shape to be seen but a motion that has been written.

zh-Hant.heading: 機械城市-讓城市自己動起來
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品從一個大膽的提問出發：城市能否像一部機器那樣運轉？學生想像著會自行抬升、擺動與連接的部件。指導過程先讓學生在動手之前以手繪草圖鋪排手臂、轉軸與齒輪，把每一個動作拆解成最簡單的機構，讓想像先有了可以被理解的骨架。進入推演，這些機構以玩具積木一一搭建，接上控制板與感測器，學生再親自編寫程式，讓每個部件依序甦醒。最後，模型像一座小小的、正在運轉的城市，一道由樑組成的升降橋在其中起落，設計、機械與程式在同一件作品裡相遇，讓城市不只是被看見的形狀，更是一種被寫出來的動作。

pins.title: The Multiverse
pins.description:
A five-layer tower of stairs, small worlds and coloured glass turns the feelings of a film story into space.

Model making | Story and space | Salt, acrylics, cotton, spray paint, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 多重宇宙
zh-Hant.description:
一座由樓梯、小世界與彩色玻璃組成的五層塔，把電影故事中的情感轉化為空間。

模型製作｜故事與空間｜鹽、壓克力、棉花、噴漆、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower crowned with coloured glass.
頂端覆著彩色玻璃的塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A film about travelling through many universes inspired the student to look at the feelings inside the story. These include facing the dark side of oneself, a mother's strong hold on her child and the spirit of a team.
captions: A labelled sketch of the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於穿越多重宇宙的電影，啟發學生審視故事中的情感。其中包括面對自我的黑暗面、母親對孩子的強烈執著，以及團隊精神。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each feeling was given its own layer, so the model grew into a five-layer body. Sketches set out how stairs would link one layer to the next.
captions: A sketch of the stair layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每一種情感都有自己的一層，使模型發展成五層的實體。草圖規劃了樓梯如何連接各層。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A foundation floor with stairs came first, then a prism frame of wooden strips on the second floor. Five small spaces on the third floor stand for different times and places, filled with clay and bionic trees.
captions: Small worlds on the third floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先做出帶樓梯的基礎樓層，再在二樓以木條搭建稜柱框架。三樓的五個小空間代表不同的時間與空間，並填入黏土與仿生樹。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A grand staircase climbs to a stained glass building set on a turning wheel at the top. Small figures give the scale of a real person against the tower.
captions: The full model from the front.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一道大樓梯通往頂端轉輪上的彩繪玻璃建築。小人偶標示出真人與塔之間的尺度。

sections.heading: The Multiverse - A Tower of Five Stacked Feelings
sections.body: A film about leaping across many universes led the student to the feelings beneath its plot: facing one's own darker side, a mother's fierce hold on a beloved child, the spirit of a team. The work asked whether such invisible emotions could become a space one climbs. The guidance first had the student give each feeling its own level, so the model grew into a five-layer body, with sketches deciding how stairs would carry one level to the next. In development, a foundation floor and its stairs came first, then a prism frame of wooden strips on the second floor, while five small rooms on the third stood for different times and places, filled with clay and bionic trees. Finally, a grand staircase rises to a stained glass building set on a turning wheel at the top, small figures fixing the human scale, so a film's emotional strata are stacked into a tower to look up at.

zh-Hant.heading: 多重宇宙-五層情感疊成的塔
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於穿越多重宇宙的電影，讓學生看見故事底下的情感：直面自我的黑暗、母親對孩子的執著、團隊並肩的精神。作品要問的是，這些看不見的情緒能否成為可以攀登的空間。指導過程先引導學生為每一種情感各給一層，讓模型長成五層的身體，並以草圖安排樓梯如何把一層接往下一層。進入推演，基礎樓層與階梯先落地，二樓以木條架起稜柱框架，三樓的五個小空間各自代表不同的時間與地點，填入黏土與仿生樹。最後，一道大階梯通往頂端轉輪上的彩繪玻璃建築，小人偶標出真實的尺度，讓一部電影的情感地層，被疊成一座可以仰望的塔。

pins.title: Bionic Canyon
pins.description:
The curving layers of a sandstone canyon are rebuilt twice, once in spliced sticks and once in folded paper hung on thread.

Model making | Landscape and form | Bamboo sticks, wooden sticks, paper, thread | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 仿生峽谷
zh-Hant.description:
砂岩峽谷的彎曲層理被重建兩次，一次以拼接木棒，一次以懸掛於細線上的摺紙。

模型製作｜地景與形態｜竹棒、木棒、紙、細線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Folded paper walls like a canyon.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: On a trip the student photographed a sandstone canyon whose shape changed with every viewing angle. The project asks how that shifting form could be combined with a human-scale model.
captions: Canyon walls that inspired the work.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在旅途中拍下一座砂岩峽谷，它的形狀隨觀看角度不斷改變。這個專題探問如何把這種變化的形態結合到人的尺度模型中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student traced the flowing lines of the rock into hand drawings. The drawings show how the layers bend, split and meet.
captions: Flowing lines drawn from the rock.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把岩石的流動線條描成手繪圖。這些圖呈現層理如何彎曲、分開與交會。
captions: 從岩石描出的流動線條。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first model splices sticks of different lengths into curling waves, then adds small figures. The second folds cardboard into the same pattern and hangs it on fishing line inside a frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個模型把不同長度的木棒拼接成捲曲的波浪，再加入小人偶。第二個模型把紙板摺成相同的紋理，並以釣魚線懸掛於框架中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The two models give two readings of the same landscape, one rough and one smooth. Small red figures show how people might walk through these canyon spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩個模型為同一片地景提供兩種詮釋，一個粗獷、一個柔順。紅色小人偶呈現人們如何在這些峽谷空間中穿行。
