sections.heading: Bionic Canyon - One Rock Written in Two Textures
sections.body: On a journey, the student photographed a sandstone canyon whose outline shifted with every turn of the body. The work asked how such flowing form might be brought down to human scale. The guidance began with hand drawings that traced the rock's streaming lines, so the eye first learned to read how strata bend, part and meet again, the slow rhythm of geology made legible. In development, the same pattern was translated twice: once in sticks of uneven length spliced into curling waves, and once in cardboard folded along the identical grain and suspended on fishing line inside a frame. In the end, the two models offer two readings of a single landscape, one rough and one smooth, with small red figures walking through them, so that a passing gaze from a trip becomes a canyon one can enter.

zh-Hant.heading: 仿生峽谷-兩種質地寫下同一片岩層
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中，學生拍下一座砂岩峽谷，它的輪廓隨每一次轉身而改變。作品要問的是：這種流動的形態，如何被帶進人的尺度。指導過程先讓學生以手繪追索岩石的流線，看清層理如何彎曲、分開又交會，讓目光先學會閱讀地質的節奏。進入推演，同一組紋理被翻譯兩次：一次以長短不一的木棒拼接成捲曲的波浪，一次以摺疊的紙板沿相同紋路成形，再用釣魚線懸於框架之中。最後，兩個模型為同一片地景給出兩種讀法，一個粗獷、一個柔順，紅色小人偶穿行其間，讓一段旅途中的凝視，化為可以走進去的峽谷空間。

pins.title: The Arch
pins.description:
Arches noticed along a shopping street are sorted, drawn and rebuilt as layered units of acrylic and wood.

Model making | Form study | Acrylic sheets, boards, Rhino, laser cutting | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 拱
zh-Hant.description:
在購物街上注意到的拱被分類、繪製，再重建為壓克力與木板層疊的單元。

模型製作｜形態研究｜壓克力板、板材、Rhino、雷射切割｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Walking down a shopping street, the student noticed that the arches of the shops were all quite different. It was something that had never caught the student's eye before.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 走在購物街上，學生注意到店面的拱形各不相同。這是學生過去從未留意過的現象。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied many arches, adding arches seen on earlier travels, and sorted them by type. Hand drawings and quick paper tests explored their curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了許多拱，也加入過去旅途中見過的拱，並依類型分類。手繪圖與快速的紙模測試探索了它們的曲線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A single model was built in Rhino and sliced into layers, with the size of each layer set step by step. Acrylic and wood pieces were laser cut, glued and repeated to make many identical units.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生在Rhino中建立單一模型並切成多層，逐層決定每層的尺寸。壓克力與木板經雷射切割、黏合後，重複製作成許多相同的單元。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The units were put together into one model of mixed arches. Light passing through the thin layers makes each arch look soft and shifting.
captions: A drawing of the arch city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些單元被組合成一個混合多種拱形的模型。穿過薄層的光線讓每個拱看起來柔和而多變。

sections.heading: The Arch - Overlooked Curves Along the Street
sections.body: Walking down a shopping street, the student noticed that the shops' arches were all quite different, something that had never caught the student's eye before. Starting from this belated discovery, the work brings overlooked everyday curves into view. The guidance first led the student to study many arches, adding those seen on earlier travels and sorting them by type, then to explore their curves through hand drawings and quick paper tests, so that observation built up into a personal vocabulary of arches. In development, the student built a single model in Rhino and sliced it into layers, setting the size of each layer step by step; acrylic and wood pieces were laser cut, glued and repeated into many identical units. Finally, the units were assembled into one model of mixed arches, and light passing through the thin layers makes each arch look soft and shifting, suggesting that beauty often hides on the street corners we pass every day.

zh-Hant.heading: 拱-街道上被忽略的曲線
zh-Hant.body: 走在購物街上，學生注意到店面的拱形各不相同，這是過去從未留意過的現象。這件作品從這份遲來的發現出發，把日常中被忽略的曲線帶到眼前。指導過程先引導學生研究許多拱，加入過去旅途中見過的拱並依類型分類，再以手繪圖與快速的紙模測試探索它們的曲線，讓觀察先累積成一套自己的拱形詞彙。進入推演，學生在Rhino中建立單一模型並切成多層，逐層決定尺寸，壓克力與木板經雷射切割、黏合後，重複製作成許多相同的單元。最後，這些單元被組合成一個混合多種拱形的模型，光線穿過薄層，讓每個拱顯得柔和而多變，提示美往往就藏在每天經過的街角。

pins.title: An Intricate Symmetry
pins.description:
Ideas from science fiction films are sorted into a symmetrical stick megastructure wrapped in clouds of light clay.

Model making | Future architecture | Wooden sticks, light clay, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 繁複的對稱
zh-Hant.description:
科幻電影中的構想被整理成一座對稱的木棒巨構，外覆輕黏土雲團。

模型製作｜未來建築｜木棒、輕黏土、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves science fiction films, which often show brand-new forms of architecture. The project asks what these imagined buildings have in common.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛科幻電影，這些電影常呈現全新的建築形式。這個專題探問這些想像中的建築有何共通之處。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several well-known science fiction films, old and new, were studied as references. Shared features included megastructures, symmetry, glowing curtain walls and irregular elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了數部新舊知名科幻電影作為參考。共同特徵包括巨型結構、對稱、發光的帷幕元素與不規則元素。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: These features were sorted and combined into one design. Stick frames form the symmetrical body, while light clay adds soft and irregular clouds.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把這些特徵分類並整合成一個設計。木棒框架構成對稱的主體，輕黏土則加上柔軟而不規則的雲團。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model sets strict frames against loose white forms. It reads as a building from a future film set on the table.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型讓嚴謹的框架與鬆散的白色形體相互對照。它就像一棟從未來電影中搬到桌上的建築。

sections.heading: An Intricate Symmetry - The Shared Traits of Science-Fiction Architecture
sections.body: Science-fiction films often show buildings never seen before, as if the future had arrived early. Starting from the student's love of such films, the work asked what these imagined buildings have in common. The guidance first led the student to study several well-known science-fiction films, old and new, as references, distilling shared features such as megastructures, symmetry, glowing curtain walls and irregular elements, so that on-screen fantasy was first analysed with a cool eye. In development, the student sorted and combined these features into a single design: stick frames form the symmetrical body, while light clay adds soft, irregular clouds. Finally, the model sets strict frames against loose white forms, reading like a building lifted from a future film and set upon a table, letting research and imagination stand side by side in one work.

zh-Hant.heading: 繁複的對稱-科幻電影中的建築共性
zh-Hant.body: 科幻電影常呈現前所未見的建築，彷彿未來已提前抵達。這件作品從學生對科幻電影的熱愛出發，問的是這些想像中的建築有何共通之處。指導過程先引導學生研究數部新舊知名科幻電影作為參考，從中歸納出巨型結構、對稱、發光的帷幕與不規則元素等共同特徵，讓銀幕上的幻想先被冷靜地分析。進入推演，學生把這些特徵分類並整合成一個設計，木棒框架構成對稱的主體，輕黏土則添上柔軟而不規則的雲團。最後，完成的模型讓嚴謹的框架與鬆散的白色形體相互對照，像一棟從未來電影中搬到桌上的建築，讓研究與想像在同一件作品中並肩。

pins.title: Emergent Architecture
pins.description:
Elements pulled from drawings become foam objects, then a habitat stepping down a hillside between water and land.

Summer architecture studio | Habitat on a hillside | Polystyrene foam, museum board, Rhino, Photoshop, Illustrator | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 浮現的建築
zh-Hant.description:
從繪圖中萃取的元素化為泡棉物件，再發展成一座沿山坡層疊、介於水陸之間的棲居。

暑期建築工作營｜山坡棲居｜聚苯乙烯泡棉、博物館紙板、Rhino、Photoshop、Illustrator｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In this summer studio, nine possible elements were pulled out of existing drawings. The aim was to show these elements as built solid models.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在這個暑期工作營中，學生從既有繪圖中萃取出九個可能的元素。目標是以實體模型呈現這些元素。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each element was made into a small foam object and photographed. The objects were then cut and dug into to find new spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個元素都被做成小型泡棉物件並拍攝記錄。接著學生切割並挖掘這些物件，以尋找新的空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The excavated pieces grew into an emergent building, tested in drawings and elevations. Renderings checked how the spaces might feel from inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 挖掘後的構件發展成一座浮現的建築，並以繪圖與立面加以測試。渲染圖檢驗了從內部體驗這些空間的感受。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A habitat at human scale was built on a hillside where water and land meet, so people can enjoy nature and watch wildlife. It tests how people might live, meet and move in such a place.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生在水陸交會的山坡上建構了一座人的尺度的棲居，讓人們能親近自然、觀察水陸生物。它測試了人們如何在這樣的地方生活、交流與移動。

sections.heading: Emergent Architecture - A Habitat Excavated from Drawings
sections.body: Architecture is sometimes not designed so much as slowly emerging from existing traces. Coming from a summer studio, the work began with nine possible elements the student drew out of existing drawings, aiming to present them as solid models. The guidance first led the student to make each element into a small foam object and photograph it, then cut and dig into these objects in search of new spaces, letting possibilities reveal themselves through subtraction. In development, the excavated pieces grew into an emergent building, tested through drawings and elevations, while renderings examined how the spaces might feel from within. Finally, a habitat at human scale was built on a hillside where water and land meet, letting people come close to nature and watch the life of both water and land, and testing how people might live, meet and move in such a place.

zh-Hant.heading: 浮現的建築-從繪圖中挖掘出的棲居
zh-Hant.body: 建築有時不是被設計出來，而是從既有的痕跡中慢慢浮現。這件作品來自一個暑期工作營，學生從既有繪圖中萃取出九個可能的元素，目標是以實體模型呈現它們。指導過程先引導學生把每個元素做成小型泡棉物件並拍攝記錄，再切割並挖掘這些物件，以尋找新的空間，讓形體在減法中顯露可能。進入推演，挖掘後的構件發展成一座浮現的建築，並以繪圖與立面測試，渲染圖則檢驗從內部體驗這些空間的感受。最後，一座人的尺度的棲居被建構在水陸交會的山坡上，讓人們能親近自然、觀察水陸生物，也測試了人們如何在這樣的地方生活、交流與移動。

pins.title: Black Mesh Canopy
pins.description:
Stockings stretched over a stick frame form a black mesh canopy, later refined into flowing digital shells.

Model making | Tensile canopy | Wooden sticks, light clay, stockings, parametric modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 黑網天幕
zh-Hant.description:
絲襪撐在木棒框架上，形成一片黑色網狀天幕，之後再發展成流動的數位殼體。

模型製作｜張拉天幕｜木棒、輕黏土、絲襪、參數化建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project aims to bring people and nature closer together. It also challenges how living spaces might be made on a hillside.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題旨在讓人與自然更加貼近。它也挑戰人們如何在山坡上創造生活空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Soft natural forms were sketched as stretched surfaces held by a few points. The sketches tested where the canopy should rise and fall.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把柔和的自然形態畫成由少數支點撐起的張拉曲面。這些草圖測試天幕該在哪裡升起與落下。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stockings were stretched over a frame of wooden sticks, with light clay figures added below. The form was then rebuilt in a parametric model as a fine mesh shell.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把絲襪撐在木棒框架上，並在下方加入輕黏土人物。接著以參數化模型把形態重建為細緻的網格殼體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The canopy creates shaded rooms where people could live, meet and move around. Renderings show light filtering through the mesh onto the ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 天幕形成有遮蔭的空間，讓人們能在其中生活、交流與走動。渲染圖呈現光線穿過網格灑落地面的效果。

sections.heading: Black Mesh Canopy - A Tensile Dwelling on the Hillside
sections.body: The distance between people and nature can be closed by a soft canopy. The work aimed to bring people and nature closer together while challenging how living spaces might be made on a hillside. The guidance first led the student to sketch soft natural forms as stretched surfaces held by a few points, testing where the canopy should rise and where it should fall, so that terrain and structure first found an understanding on paper. In development, the student stretched stockings over a frame of wooden sticks with light clay figures below, then rebuilt the form in a parametric model as a fine mesh shell. Finally, the canopy creates shaded spaces where people could live, meet and move about, and renderings show light filtering through the mesh onto the ground, making the architecture as light as a breath upon the hillside.

zh-Hant.heading: 黑網天幕-山坡上的張拉之居
zh-Hant.body: 人與自然之間的距離，可以被一片柔軟的天幕拉近。這件作品旨在讓人與自然更加貼近，同時挑戰人們如何在山坡上創造生活空間。指導過程先引導學生把柔和的自然形態畫成由少數支點撐起的張拉曲面，以草圖測試天幕該在哪裡升起、在哪裡落下，讓地形與結構先在紙上找到默契。進入推演，學生把絲襪撐在木棒框架上，並在下方加入輕黏土人物，再以參數化模型把形態重建為細緻的網格殼體。最後，天幕形成有遮蔭的空間，讓人們能在其中生活、交流與走動，渲染圖呈現光線穿過網格灑落地面，讓建築輕得像山坡上的一層呼吸。

pins.title: Volumes of Transitional Edges
pins.description:
Nested cube frames in black and white wooden strips explore how the edges of shapes pass into one another.

Model making | Geometric frame study | Wooden strips, white glue, super glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 過渡邊界的體量
zh-Hant.description:
以黑白木條製成的層疊立方框架，探索形體邊界如何彼此過渡。

模型製作｜幾何框架研究｜木條、白膠、瞬間膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how the boundaries of simple shapes relate to each other. It looks for the moments where one edge turns into the next.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問簡單形體的邊界之間如何互相關聯。它尋找一條邊轉變為另一條邊的瞬間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Cubes were rotated, shifted and combined in a series of line drawings. Each drawing tested a different way for frames to overlap.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在一系列線稿中把立方體旋轉、位移並組合。每張圖都測試框架重疊的不同方式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chosen combinations were built from thin wooden strips in black and white. Smaller frames were set inside larger ones at changing angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以黑白細木條搭建選定的組合。較小的框架以不同角度置入較大的框架之中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model reads as one volume made of many transitional edges. Seen from each side, the frames line up and break apart in new ways.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型看起來是由許多過渡邊界構成的單一體量。從不同側面觀看，框架會以新的方式對齊又分離。

sections.heading: Volumes of Transitional Edges - The Moment One Edge Becomes Another
sections.body: Simple shapes seem independent, yet their boundaries are always quietly in conversation. The work asked how the edges of simple shapes relate to one another, searching for the moment when one edge turns into the next. The guidance first led the student to rotate, shift and combine cubes in a series of line drawings, each testing a different way for frames to overlap, so that the relationships between edges were carefully weighed on paper first. In development, the student built the chosen combinations from thin black and white wooden strips, setting smaller frames inside larger ones at changing angles, nesting layer within layer into a shifting rhythm. Finally, the model reads as a single volume made of many transitional edges; seen from each side, the frames align and break apart in new ways, letting viewers, as they move, discover the liveliness of geometry itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 過渡邊界的體量-一條邊轉為另一條邊的瞬間
zh-Hant.body: 簡單的形體看似獨立，它們的邊界卻總在悄悄對話。這件作品問的是，簡單形體的邊界之間如何互相關聯，並尋找一條邊轉變為另一條邊的瞬間。指導過程先引導學生在一系列線稿中把立方體旋轉、位移並組合，每張圖都測試框架重疊的不同方式，讓邊界的關係先在紙上被細細推敲。進入推演，學生以黑白細木條搭建選定的組合，較小的框架以不同角度置入較大的框架之中，層層嵌套出變化的節奏。最後，模型看起來是由許多過渡邊界構成的單一體量，從不同側面觀看，框架會以新的方式對齊又分離，讓觀者在移動之間，看見幾何本身的靈動。

pins.title: Hiking
pins.description:
Quick marker sketches of hiking views are cut up, recombined and built into a curving model of PVC board and sticks.

Model making | Landscape abstraction | PVC boards, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 健行
zh-Hant.description:
把健行風景的快速麥克筆速寫剪開、重組，再搭建成由 PVC 板與木棒構成的曲線模型。

模型製作｜風景抽象化｜PVC 板、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The curving PVC and stick model.
PVC 板與木棒的曲線模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how everyday views can be abstracted into elements and rebuilt as space. The student wanted building blocks that were not shaped by too much thinking.
captions: Fast marker sketches of the views.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問日常風景如何被抽象成元素，再重建為空間。學生希望得到不被過度思考左右的造形元素。
captions: 風景的快速麥克筆速寫。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Views from a hiking trip were traced with markers as quickly and randomly as possible. The tracing paper was then cut into pieces and reassembled into a new pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以麥克筆盡可能快速而隨機地描繪健行時的風景。接著把描圖紙剪成碎片，重新拼組成新的圖案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The flat pattern was imagined as a spatial one using PVC boards, sticks and glue. Curves became the key element, giving motion and rhythm while linking the parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以 PVC 板、木棒與膠，把平面圖案想像成立體空間。曲線成為關鍵元素，在連接各部分的同時帶出動感與節奏。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sweeps ribs, spirals and triangles around a loose centre. Its shadows add another layer of moving lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓肋片、螺旋與三角形環繞一個鬆散的中心展開。它的陰影又增添了一層流動的線條。

sections.heading: Hiking - Landscape Elements Free of Overthinking
sections.body: Everyday landscapes pass before our eyes daily yet are rarely taken apart with care. The work asked how such views could be abstracted into elements and rebuilt as space, and the student wanted forms not shaped by too much thinking. The guidance first led the student to trace views from a hiking trip with markers as quickly and randomly as possible, then cut the tracing paper into pieces and reassemble them into a new pattern, letting intuition speak before reason. In development, the student used PVC boards, sticks and glue to imagine the flat pattern as a spatial one, and curves became the key element, linking the parts while bringing motion and rhythm. Finally, the model sweeps ribs, spirals and triangles around a loose centre, and its shadows add another layer of moving lines, turning the memory of a hike into a brisk spatial rhythm.

zh-Hant.heading: 健行-不經思索的風景元素
zh-Hant.body: 日常的風景每天從眼前掠過，很少被認真拆解。這件作品問的是，這些風景如何被抽象成元素，再重建為空間，而學生希望得到的，是不被過度思考左右的造形。指導過程先引導學生以麥克筆盡可能快速而隨機地描繪健行時的風景，再把描圖紙剪成碎片、重新拼組成新的圖案，讓直覺先於理性發聲。進入推演，學生以PVC板、木棒與膠把平面圖案想像成立體空間，曲線成為關鍵元素，在連接各部分的同時帶出動感與節奏。最後，模型讓肋片、螺旋與三角形環繞一個鬆散的中心展開，它的陰影又增添一層流動的線條，讓一段健行的記憶化為輕快的空間節拍。

pins.title: Unearth
pins.description:
Folding studies of insect wings lead to laser-cut PVC slices, a cast plaster relief and a field of sticks.

Model making | Folding and layering study | PVC boards, plaster, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 出土
zh-Hant.description:
從昆蟲翅膀的摺疊研究出發，發展出雷射切割 PVC 切片、石膏翻模浮雕與一片木棒林。

模型製作｜摺疊與層疊研究｜PVC 板、石膏、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A field of sticks on a plaster base.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began as an experiment with the folding wings of insects. It then asked how a flat image of light and dark could become depth.
captions: Folded panels based on wing creases.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題從昆蟲翅膀的摺疊實驗開始。接著探問一張明暗平面影像如何轉化為深度。
captions: 依翅膀摺痕製作的摺板。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The key fold of beetle wings was studied and stretched upward into a three-dimensional form. The form was then split into faces and cut from PVC boards.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究甲蟲翅膀的關鍵摺疊，並把它向上拉伸成立體形態。接著把形態拆成面，再從 PVC 板上切出。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The darkness of an image was read as depth in a digital model, then sliced and laser cut from PVC. Plaster poured over the slices made a negative relief that kept the burnt layer lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把影像的暗度解讀為數位模型中的深度，再切片並以雷射切割 PVC。把石膏灌在切片上，得到保留燒痕層線的負形浮雕。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A dense field of sticks rises from the plaster base like a buried landscape breaking through. Small red figures show narrow paths and rooms between the sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 密集的木棒林從石膏基座升起，像被埋藏的地景破土而出。小小的紅色人偶顯示木棒之間狹窄的通道與空間。

sections.heading: Unearth - A Buried Landscape Breaking Through
sections.body: An insect's wing hides intricate folds, and an image's light and dark hide depth. Beginning as an experiment with the folding wings of insects, the work went on to ask how a flat image of light and dark could become depth. The guidance first led the student to study the key fold of beetle wings, stretch it upward into a three-dimensional form, then split it into faces cut from PVC boards, so that a biological structure first became buildable geometry. In development, the student read the darkness of an image as depth in a digital model, sliced it and laser cut the slices from PVC, then poured plaster over them to make a negative relief that keeps the burnt layer lines. Finally, a dense field of sticks rises from the plaster base like a buried landscape breaking through, and small red figures reveal narrow paths and rooms between the sticks, letting a memory of light and shadow grow into a forest one can pass through.

zh-Hant.heading: 出土-破土而出的埋藏地景
zh-Hant.body: 昆蟲的翅膀藏著精巧的摺疊，一張影像的明暗也藏著深度。這件作品從昆蟲翅膀的摺疊實驗開始，進而問一張明暗平面影像如何轉化為深度。指導過程先引導學生研究甲蟲翅膀的關鍵摺疊，把它向上拉伸成立體形態，再拆成面並從PVC板上切出，讓生物的結構先成為可以建造的幾何。進入推演，學生把影像的暗度讀作數位模型中的深度，切片後以雷射切割PVC，再灌上石膏，得到保留燒痕層線的負形浮雕。最後，密集的木棒林從石膏基座升起，像被埋藏的地景破土而出，小小的紅色人偶顯示木棒之間狹窄的通道與空間，讓光影的記憶長成一片可以穿行的森林。

pins.title: Pitch Trajectories
pins.description:
Movement lines traced over a football pitch become wires, bent sheets and finally a model of curved PVC walls.

Model making | Movement trace study | PVC boards, wooden sticks, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 球場軌跡
zh-Hant.description:
描在足球場平面上的移動軌跡，轉化為線材、彎折薄片，最後成為由彎曲 PVC 牆構成的模型。

模型製作｜移動軌跡研究｜PVC 板、木棒、線材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Curved PVC walls on the pitch plan.
球場平面上的彎曲 PVC 牆。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how the movement of players on a pitch could be turned into space. Lines of motion are treated as the raw material for form.
captions: Movement lines drawn on pitch plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問球員在球場上的移動如何轉化為空間。移動的線條被視為形態的原始材料。
captions: 畫在球場平面上的移動線條。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Paths were traced in colour over plans of a football pitch. The traced lines were then lifted into three-dimensional sketches.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在足球場平面上以彩色線條描出移動路徑。接著把這些描線提升為立體草模。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The lines were tested as bent paper sheets and as curved rows of sticks. Each test made the flow of movement more solid.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把線條分別以彎折紙片與彎曲的木棒列來測試。每一次測試都讓移動的流動更加具體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets curved PVC walls and stick fences directly on the pitch plan. The walls follow the traced paths and form open rooms between them.
captions: Walls and fences along the paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把彎曲的 PVC 牆與木棒圍欄直接立在球場平面上。牆體沿著描出的路徑展開，在其間形成開放的空間。
captions: 沿路徑展開的牆與圍欄。

sections.heading: Pitch Trajectories - Running Lines Turned into Space
sections.body: Players running across a pitch leave behind trails that vanish in an instant. The work asked how such movement could be turned into space, treating lines of motion as the raw material of form. The guidance first led the student to trace paths in colour over plans of a football pitch and then lift those traced lines into three-dimensional sketch models, so that the dynamics of a match first became visible on paper. In development, the student tested the lines as bent paper sheets and as curved rows of sticks, each trial making the flow of movement more concrete. Finally, the model sets curved PVC walls and stick fences directly on the pitch plan; the walls unfold along the traced paths and form open spaces between them, freezing the rhythm of a match into architecture one can walk through and pause within.

zh-Hant.heading: 球場軌跡-奔跑的線條化為空間
zh-Hant.body: 球員在球場上奔跑，留下一道道轉瞬即逝的軌跡。這件作品問的是，這些移動如何轉化為空間，並把移動的線條視為形態的原始材料。指導過程先引導學生在足球場平面上以彩色線條描出移動路徑，再把這些描線提升為立體草模，讓比賽的動態先在紙上被看見。進入推演，學生把線條分別以彎折紙片與彎曲的木棒列來測試，每一次測試都讓流動的移動更加具體。最後，模型把彎曲的PVC牆與木棒圍欄直接立在球場平面上，牆體沿著描出的路徑展開，在其間形成開放的空間，讓一場比賽的節奏凝固為可以行走與停留的建築。

pins.title: Floating
pins.description:
A tree is broken down into lines, curves and spheres, then rebuilt as a large hanging installation of bamboo, wood and string.

Installation | Abstract composition in space | Bamboo, wood, branches, hemp string | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮
zh-Hant.description:
把一棵樹拆解為直線、曲線與球體，再以竹、木與麻繩重建成一座大型懸吊裝置。

裝置｜空間中的抽象構成｜竹、木、樹枝、麻繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks whether harmony can come from a seemingly impulsive spread of simple elements. It takes an idea from abstract painting and tries it as a volume.
captions: Curves that stand for the canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問和諧能否來自看似隨性分布的簡單元素。它借用抽象繪畫的概念，嘗試以體量來實踐。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A tree was broken into vertical lines for the trunk, horizontal lines for branches, curves for the canopy and spheres for fruit. These four kinds of element became the full vocabulary of the piece.
captions: A low view of the elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把樹拆解為代表樹幹的垂直線、代表枝條的水平線、代表樹冠的曲線與代表果實的球體。這四類元素構成整件作品的全部語彙。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The canopy curves were placed first and stretched downward into a volume. A trunk was added in the middle and allowed to grow, with spheres added to balance the straight lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先放置樹冠曲線，再向下延伸成一個體量。接著在中央加入樹幹讓它自由生長，並加入球體來平衡直線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished piece hangs at about the size of a person, dense yet light. Dry segmented branches were finally added to test more natural elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的作品懸吊著，尺度約與人相當，密集而輕盈。最後學生加入分段的乾樹枝，測試更接近自然的元素。

sections.heading: Floating - Harmony Born from Impulse
sections.body: Harmony need not come from strict calculation; it can also emerge from a seemingly impulsive spread. Borrowing an idea from abstract painting, the work asked whether a free scattering of simple elements could produce harmony, and tried it out as a volume. The guidance first led the student to break a tree into four kinds of element—vertical lines for the trunk, horizontal lines for the branches, curves for the canopy and spheres for the fruit—which together became the entire vocabulary of the piece. In development, the student placed the canopy curves first and stretched them downward into a volume, then added a trunk in the middle and let it grow freely, with spheres balancing the straight lines. Finally, the piece hangs at about the size of a person, dense yet light, and dry segmented branches were added to test more natural elements, letting a tree become an abstract and lively poem suspended in the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂浮-隨性之中生成的和諧
zh-Hant.body: 和諧未必來自嚴密的計算，也可能從看似隨性的分布中浮現。這件作品借用抽象繪畫的概念，問的是簡單元素的自由散布能否產生和諧，並嘗試以體量來實踐。指導過程先引導學生把一棵樹拆解為四類元素：代表樹幹的垂直線、代表枝條的水平線、代表樹冠的曲線與代表果實的球體，讓它們構成整件作品的全部語彙。進入推演，學生先放置樹冠曲線並向下延伸成體量，再於中央加入樹幹讓它自由生長，並以球體平衡直線。最後，完成的作品懸吊著，尺度約與人相當，密集而輕盈，分段的乾樹枝又被加入以測試更自然的元素，讓一棵樹在空中化為一首抽象而靈動的詩。

pins.title: Stages of Freedom
pins.description:
A stick tower rises from a closed frame of crystal cubes to folded paper wings, telling a journey from restriction to freedom.

Model making | Narrative tower | Wooden sticks, PVC boards, iridescent sheets, string | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自由的階段
zh-Hant.description:
木棒高塔從封閉框架中的晶體方塊升起，延伸到摺紙翅膀，講述從受限到自由的旅程。

模型製作｜敘事高塔｜木棒、PVC 板、虹彩片、細線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower rising out of its frame.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how a story of escape could be told as a vertical space. Each level of the tower stands for one stage of the journey.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問一段逃離的故事如何以垂直空間來講述。高塔的每一層代表旅程的一個階段。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches set out three stages: being bound by restrictions, confronting the rules and finally being free. Cubes, triangles and loose loops were tried as symbols for each stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以草圖設定三個階段：受限制所束縛、挑戰規則，最後獲得自由。方塊、三角形與鬆散的迴圈被試作為各階段的象徵。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The lowest stage was built as a closed stick frame holding iridescent crystal cubes. Above it, a twisting stick structure and an orange ribbon climb toward folded paper wings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 最低的階段以封閉的木棒框架承載虹彩晶體方塊。其上，扭轉的木棒結構與橘色緞帶一路攀升至摺紙翅膀。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower reads from bottom to top as a path from confinement to open sky. Small figures climb its stairs and stand among the wings.
captions: The full height of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的高塔由下而上，讀起來像一條從禁錮走向開闊天空的路徑。小人偶沿著樓梯攀爬，站在翅膀之間。

sections.heading: Stages of Freedom - A Vertical Journey from Cage to Sky
sections.body: An escape is a journey that takes time, and each step carries a different weight. The work asked how a story of escape could be told as a vertical space, with each level of the tower standing for one stage of the journey. The guidance first led the student to set out three stages in sketches—being bound by restrictions, confronting the rules, and finally being free—and to try cubes, triangles and loose loops as symbols for each, so that the plot first became shape. In development, the lowest stage was built as a closed stick frame holding iridescent crystal cubes, and above it a twisting stick structure and an orange ribbon climb toward folded paper wings. Finally, the finished tower reads from bottom to top as a path from confinement to open sky, with small figures climbing its stairs and standing among the wings, making freedom a height that can be reached step by step.

zh-Hant.heading: 自由的階段-從禁錮走向天空的垂直旅程
zh-Hant.body: 逃離是一段需要時間的旅程，每一步都有不同的重量。這件作品問的是，一段逃離的故事如何以垂直空間來講述，讓高塔的每一層代表旅程的一個階段。指導過程先引導學生以草圖設定三個階段：受限制所束縛、挑戰規則，最後獲得自由，並以方塊、三角形與鬆散的迴圈試作各階段的象徵，讓情節先轉為形狀。進入推演，最低的階段以封閉的木棒框架承載虹彩晶體方塊，其上，扭轉的木棒結構與橘色緞帶一路攀升至摺紙翅膀。最後，完成的高塔由下而上，讀起來像一條從禁錮走向開闊天空的路徑，小人偶沿著樓梯攀爬、站在翅膀之間，讓自由成為可以一步步抵達的高度。

pins.title: Sonic Spectrum
pins.description:
Curves drawn from the way sound and force travel grow into a layered tower of bent PVC strips and sticks.

Model making | Sound and structure study | PVC boards, wooden sticks, ABS sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聲音光譜
zh-Hant.description:
從聲音與力的傳遞方式畫出曲線，再發展成由彎曲 PVC 條與木棒構成的層疊高塔。

模型製作｜聲音與結構研究｜PVC 板、木棒、ABS 棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The layered tower of bent strips.
由彎曲板條層疊而成的高塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began with the inner structure of headphones. The student noticed that the way sound travels looks like the way force travels through a bridge, and asked whether that shared shape could become space.
captions: Product photos of the headphones and their internal parts that started the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題從耳機的內部結構出發。學生發現聲音傳遞的方式與力在橋梁中傳遞的方式相似，於是探問這種共通的形態能否轉化為空間。
captions: 啟發本案的耳機及其內部零件產品照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Wave patterns of sound were laid over bridge structures, and the points of force were drawn and then lifted into three dimensions. In the shadows the energy read as softer curves.
captions: The travel photo used as a test subject, with sound curves drawn over it.
Wire curves over the drawn lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把聲波的圖形疊在橋梁結構上，畫出受力點，再把它們立體化。在陰影中，能量呈現為更柔和的曲線。
captions: 作為實驗對象、疊繪聲音曲線的旅途照片。
覆在線稿上的線材曲線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A quiet scene from a trip was used as a test. The parts that felt like sound were turned into curves, and each kind of sound became its own layer, growing more blurred toward the top.
captions: Fixing the curved paper strips by hand.
A first relief of curved paper.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以旅途中一處安靜的場景作為實驗對象。畫面中帶有聲音感的部分被轉為曲線，每一種聲音成為一層，越往上越模糊。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower stacks these sound layers like the inside of a headphone. A contrasting upper section uses regular geometry and a helix to stand for the sound changed by the earphone.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終高塔把這些聲音層疊起來，如同耳機的內部。上段以規則幾何與螺旋結構作為對比，代表經過耳機改變後的聲音。

sections.heading: Sonic Spectrum - The Shared Shape of Sound and Bridges
sections.body: Sound cannot be seen, yet it has paths along which it travels. Starting from the inner structure of headphones, the student noticed that the way sound travels resembles the way force travels through a bridge, and asked whether that shared shape could become space. The guidance first led the student to lay wave patterns of sound over bridge structures, drawing the points of force and lifting them into three dimensions; in the shadows, the energy read as softer curves. In development, a quiet scene from a trip served as a test: the parts that felt like sound became curves, and each kind of sound became its own layer, growing more blurred toward the top. Finally, the tower stacks these sound layers like the inside of a headphone, while a contrasting upper section of regular geometry and a helix stands for sound changed by the earphone, turning listening itself into architecture one can see.

zh-Hant.heading: 聲音光譜-聲波與橋梁共通的形態
zh-Hant.body: 聲音看不見，卻有它傳遞的路徑。這件作品從耳機的內部結構出發，學生發現聲音傳遞的方式與力在橋梁中傳遞的方式相似，於是問這種共通的形態能否轉化為空間。指導過程先引導學生把聲波的圖形疊在橋梁結構上，畫出受力點再將其立體化，在陰影中，能量呈現為更柔和的曲線。進入推演，學生以旅途中一處安靜的場景作為實驗，把畫面中帶有聲音感的部分轉為曲線，每一種聲音成為一層，越往上越模糊。最後，高塔把這些聲音層疊起來，如同耳機的內部，上段則以規則幾何與螺旋作為對比，代表經過耳機改變後的聲音，讓聆聽本身成為可以觀看的建築。

pins.title: Return to the Renaissance
pins.description:
Domes, arches and columns are collaged into a white citadel that climbs a mountain of stacked stick triangles.

Model making | Collage and deconstruction | Wooden sticks, paperboard, model trees | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 回到文藝復興
zh-Hant.description:
把穹頂、拱與柱拼貼成一座白色城堡，攀附在由木棒三角堆疊而成的山上。

模型製作｜拼貼與解構｜木棒、紙板、模型樹｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The white citadel with its dome and arches.
帶有穹頂與拱的白色城堡。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project started from an interest in Renaissance European architecture. It asks how a style known for order and symmetry could be taken apart and rebuilt as a new story.
captions: Photos of the Renaissance basilica and cathedrals that inspired the citadel.
A collage drawing of domes and facades.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源於學生對歐洲文藝復興建築的興趣。它探問一種以秩序與對稱著稱的風格，如何被拆解後重建成新的故事。
captions: 啟發這座城堡的文藝復興大教堂照片。
穹頂與立面的拼貼線稿。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings of Renaissance buildings were cut and collaged into one deconstructed scene. A second drawing tested how the building could sit on a rough, mountain-like base.
captions: Line drawings of single landmark buildings.
A hatched study of the citadel on its hill.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把文藝復興建築的線稿剪開，拼貼成一個解構的場景。第二張圖則測試建築如何坐落在粗糙如山的基座上。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were used to build mountains for the buildings to stand on. Arches and rows of columns carry the sense of grandeur, and the empty areas were filled with stacked triangles.
captions: Building the stick frame and card arches by hand.
The dome above a curving stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木棒搭出讓建築立足的山體。拱與成排的柱子帶出宏偉感，空隙則以堆疊的三角形填滿。
captions: 親手搭建木棒框架與卡紙拱。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Winding paper strips link the parts into one piece. Model trees and tiny figures turn it into a scene with a story.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 蜿蜒的紙條把各部分連成一體。模型樹與小人偶則讓它成為一個有故事的場景。

sections.heading: Return to the Renaissance - A New Story from Dismantled Order
sections.body: Renaissance architecture is known for order and symmetry, as if nothing could be allowed to disturb it. Starting from the student's interest in this style, the work asked how it could be taken apart and rebuilt as a new story. The guidance first led the student to cut drawings of Renaissance buildings and collage them into a single deconstructed scene, then use a second drawing to test how the buildings could sit on a rough, mountain-like base, letting a rigorous classical vocabulary first meet irregular terrain. In development, the student built mountains of wooden sticks for the buildings to stand on; arches and rows of columns carry a sense of grandeur, while empty areas were filled with stacked triangles. Finally, winding paper strips link the parts into one piece, and model trees and tiny figures turn it into a scene with a story, giving classical dignity new life through recomposition.

zh-Hant.heading: 回到文藝復興-拆解秩序後的新故事
zh-Hant.body: 文藝復興建築以秩序與對稱著稱，彷彿不容任何打擾。這件作品從學生對這種風格的興趣出發，問的是它如何被拆解後重建成新的故事。指導過程先引導學生把文藝復興建築的線稿剪開，拼貼成一個解構的場景，再以第二張圖測試建築如何坐落在粗糙如山的基座上，讓嚴謹的古典語彙先與不規則的地形相遇。進入推演，學生以木棒搭出讓建築立足的山體，拱與成排的柱子帶出宏偉感，空隙則以堆疊的三角形填滿。最後，蜿蜒的紙條把各部分連成一體，模型樹與小人偶讓它成為一個有故事的場景，讓古典的莊嚴在重組之中獲得新的生命。

pins.title: Wave-Fold Pavilion

Folded paper waves of small irregular triangles are modelled digitally and enlarged into an arching pavilion.

Paper folding and digital modelling | Pavilion | Paper, Rhino | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.description:
以不規則小三角形摺出的紙浪，經數位建模後放大成一座拱形亭。

摺紙與數位建模｜涼亭｜紙、Rhino｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The folded arch placed in a courtyard.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work grew from a love of paper folding and of nature. It asks how the motion of a rough sea could be caught in a folded surface.
captions: Photos of breaking waves that inspired the folds.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品源於學生對摺紙與自然的喜愛。它探問洶湧海面的動態如何被捕捉在摺疊的表面中。
captions: 啟發摺紙形態的浪花照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied folding techniques and copied known folded works. Then a new folding device was designed, using irregular small triangles to imitate turbulent water.
captions: The wave stretched into a loop.
The fold on a dark ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究摺紙技法並臨摹既有作品。接著設計出新的摺紙裝置，以不規則的小三角形模仿翻騰的水面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The paper model was first redrawn by hand. It was then rebuilt in Rhino, where control points were used to shape and render the surface.
captions: A drawing of the folded surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙模型先以手繪重新描繪。接著於 Rhino 中重建，並以控制點塑形與算圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model was enlarged into a pavilion that could stand in the centre of a teaching building. Images placed it in a courtyard to show its size.
captions: The full pavilion montage with visitors walking beneath the arch.
An illustration of the pavilion by a building.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型被放大為一座可置於教學大樓中央的涼亭。學生並以影像合成放入庭院中呈現尺度。
captions: 完整的展亭合成圖，訪客從拱下走過。

sections.heading: Wave-Fold Pavilion - A Rough Sea Folded into Paper
sections.body: Can the instant a sea surges be kept within a sheet of paper? Growing from the student's love of paper folding and of nature, the work asked how the motion of a rough sea could be caught in a folded surface. The guidance first led the student to study folding techniques and copy known folded works, and once the rules were familiar, to design a new folding device that uses irregular small triangles to imitate turbulent water. In development, the paper model was first redrawn by hand and then rebuilt in Rhino, where control points were used to shape and render the surface, letting the intuition of the hand and the precision of the digital calibrate one another. Finally, the model was enlarged into a pavilion that could stand at the centre of a teaching building, with images placing it in a courtyard to show its scale, so that a wave on paper becomes architecture people can shelter beneath.

zh-Hant.heading: 浪摺亭-摺進紙面的洶湧海潮
zh-Hant.body: 海面翻騰的瞬間，能否被一張紙收藏起來？這件作品源於學生對摺紙與自然的喜愛，問的是洶湧海面的動態如何被捕捉在摺疊的表面中。指導過程先引導學生研究摺紙技法並臨摹既有作品，在熟悉規則之後，再設計出新的摺紙裝置，以不規則的小三角形模仿翻騰的水面。進入推演，紙模型先以手繪重新描繪，再於Rhino中重建，並以控制點塑形與算圖，讓手的直覺與數位的精確彼此校準。最後，模型被放大為一座可置於教學大樓中央的涼亭，影像合成將它放入庭院以呈現尺度，讓一片紙上的浪潮成為人們可以棲身其下的建築。

pins.title: Stacked Circles
pins.description:
A digital study of stacked rings is drawn, animated and then built as a laser-cut table of layered boards.

Digital modelling to furniture | Stacking study | Rhino, laser-cut boards, clear board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 疊環
zh-Hant.description:
一個疊環的數位研究經過繪圖與動畫，最後以雷射切割層板做成一張桌子。

從數位建模到家具｜堆疊研究｜Rhino、雷射切割板、透明板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The laser-cut table with two model figures.
雷射切割桌與兩個模型人偶。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Made in a summer programme, the project is an expression of stacking circles. It then asks how a purely digital form could become a real object.
captions: A rendered view of the rings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題完成於一個暑期課程，是對疊環的表現。接著它探問一個純數位的形態如何成為真實的物件。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The rings were modelled in Rhino. They were shown through rotation drawings and an alternate surface made only of lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在 Rhino 中建立疊環模型。接著以旋轉圖與僅由線條構成的替代表面來呈現。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Animation frames show the rings gathering into a cluster. A zoomed-in render and a section drawing read the form from the inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 動畫影格呈現疊環逐步聚合。放大算圖與剖面圖則從內部解讀這個形態。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Research showed the model had much in common with furniture. It was laser cut in layers and topped with clear board to give a sense of science fiction.
captions: The stacked layers of the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 研究後學生發現模型與家具有許多相似之處。於是以雷射切割分層製作，並以透明板為桌面，營造科幻感。

sections.heading: Stacked Circles - From Digital Form to Real Object
sections.body: A set of stacked rings can exist only on a screen, or it can become an object within reach. Made in a summer programme, the work began as an expression of stacking circles and went on to ask how a purely digital form could become a real object. The guidance first led the student to model the rings in Rhino and present them through rotation drawings and an alternate surface made only of lines, so that the form was viewed again and again through different modes of expression. In development, animation frames show the rings gathering into a cluster, while a zoomed-in render and a section drawing read the form from the inside. Finally, research revealed to the student how much the model had in common with furniture, so it was laser cut in layers and topped with clear board for a sense of science fiction, letting virtual geometry land steadily as a table for everyday use.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊環-從數位形態到真實物件
zh-Hant.body: 一組疊起的圓環，可以只存在於螢幕之中，也可以成為觸手可及的物件。這件作品完成於一個暑期課程，從疊環的表現出發，進一步問一個純數位的形態如何成為真實的物件。指導過程先引導學生在Rhino中建立疊環模型，再以旋轉圖與僅由線條構成的替代表面來呈現，讓形體在不同的表達方式中被反覆觀看。進入推演，動畫影格呈現疊環逐步聚合，放大算圖與剖面圖則從內部解讀這個形態。最後，研究讓學生發現模型與家具有許多相似之處，於是以雷射切割分層製作，並以透明板為桌面，營造科幻感，讓虛擬的幾何安穩地落地為日常可用的桌子。

pins.title: Tree, Nest and Root
pins.description:
Tree houses, nests and ladders climb a root-wood tree while cast ant tunnels show what happens underground.

Model making | Spaces between people, species and trees | Wood, rope, plaster, stone, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹、巢與根
zh-Hant.description:
樹屋、鳥巢與梯子攀上一棵樹根木，翻模的蟻道則呈現地底下發生的事。

模型製作｜人、物種與樹之間的空間｜木、繩、石膏、石、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tree model on its root base.
立於根部基座上的樹木模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explores the spaces shared by people, other species and trees. Inspired by bird nests, it asks how lively spaces could be made in the crown, branches, trunk and roots.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探索人、其他物種與樹之間共享的空間。學生從鳥巢得到啟發，探問如何在樹冠、樹枝、樹幹與樹根中創造生動的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: To study the space beneath, ants were placed in a gel medium and their tunnels observed. Plaster was then poured in to capture the tunnels as a solid form.
captions: Placing ants, roots and gel in the tanks by hand and watching the tunnels form.
Roots set in the gel tank.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 為了研究地下空間，學生把螞蟻放入凝膠介質中觀察牠們挖出的通道。接著灌入石膏，把通道凝固成實體。
captions: 親手將螞蟻、樹根與凝膠放入水箱，觀察蟻道成形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Eaves, windows, tree holes and nests were built into the branches. Ladders and small decks link them together.
captions: Nests and decks among the branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把屋簷、窗、樹洞與鳥巢做進樹枝之間。梯子與小平台把它們串連起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model the ants have undermined the base and the tree is toppling. It is a reminder to step in with care and keep the balance of nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型中，螞蟻掏空了基座，樹正在傾倒。它提醒人們適度介入，守護自然的平衡。

sections.heading: Tree, Nest and Root - Keeping Balance in a Shared Home
sections.body: From canopy to root, a tree is a home shared by many lives. Exploring the spaces shared by people, other species and trees, and inspired by bird nests, the work asked how lively spaces could be made in the crown, branches, trunk and roots. The guidance first led the student to study the world below ground, placing ants in a gel medium to observe the tunnels they dig, then pouring plaster to set those tunnels into solid form, so that invisible space became something that could be studied. In development, eaves, windows, tree holes and nests were built in among the branches, linked by ladders and small decks. Finally, in the model the ants have undermined the base and the tree is toppling, an ending that gently yet soberly reminds people that stepping into nature calls for restraint, and that a shared home needs a balance kept in common.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹、巢與根-在共享之中守護平衡
zh-Hant.body: 一棵樹從樹冠到樹根，是許多生命共享的家。這件作品探索人、其他物種與樹之間的共享空間，並從鳥巢得到啟發，問的是如何在樹冠、樹枝、樹幹與樹根中創造生動的空間。指導過程先引導學生研究地下的世界，把螞蟻放入凝膠介質中觀察牠們挖出的通道，再灌入石膏把通道凝固成實體，讓看不見的空間成為可以研究的形體。進入推演，屋簷、窗、樹洞與鳥巢被做進樹枝之間，梯子與小平台把它們串連起來。最後，模型中的螞蟻掏空了基座，樹正在傾倒，這個結局溫和而清醒地提醒人們，介入自然需要分寸，共享的家也需要共同守護的平衡。

pins.title: Sandy Adobe
pins.description:
Branching tunnels of paper clay, inspired by crab burrows, are knotted together and coated in sand.

Sculpture | Organic structure study | Sand, paper clay, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沙之巢
zh-Hant.description:
受蟹洞啟發，以紙黏土塑出分岔通道，彼此纏結後再覆上沙。

雕塑｜有機結構研究｜沙、紙黏土、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work comes from watching crabs by the sea. Their nests are made of many linked tunnels, and the project asks how that hidden structure could be made visible.
captions: The crab and its burrow pellets on the beach that inspired the sculpture.
A drawing of the tunnel form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品來自學生在海邊觀察螃蟹的經驗。蟹巢由許多相連的通道構成，這個專題探問如何讓這個隱藏的結構被看見。
captions: 啟發這件雕塑的海灘螃蟹與洞穴沙球。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Long strips of paper clay were moulded one by one to stand for the inner tunnels. Each piece was given enough branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以紙黏土逐一塑出長條，代表內部通道。學生並確保每一段都有足夠的分岔。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The strips were joined into one knotted form. It was then covered in sand to bring back the look of the original burrow.
captions: Rolling, joining and sanding the clay tubes by hand.
The form being coated in sand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把這些長條接合成一個纏結的整體。接著覆上沙，還原蟹洞原本的質感。
captions: 親手搓製、接合黏土管並覆上沙。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished sculpture is an organic device of looping tunnels. It is rough and porous like the ground it came from.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的雕塑是一個由迴繞通道構成的有機裝置。它粗糙而多孔，如同它所來自的土地。

sections.heading: Sandy Adobe - Bringing Hidden Tunnels to the Surface
sections.body: Crabs by the sea dig linked tunnels in the sand, forming an invisible underground city. Drawn from the student's experience of watching crabs on the shore, the work asked how this hidden structure could be made visible. The guidance first led the student to mould long strips of paper clay one by one to stand for the inner tunnels, making sure each piece had enough branches, so that the burrow network was first understood as a spatial system. In development, the student joined the strips into one knotted whole and covered it in sand to restore the texture of the original burrow, returning the made form to the language of the ground. Finally, the finished sculpture is an organic device of looping tunnels, rough and porous like the earth it came from, allowing viewers to gaze upon a home that once belonged only to crabs.

zh-Hant.heading: 沙之巢-讓地下的通道浮出地表
zh-Hant.body: 海邊的螃蟹在沙中挖出相連的通道，構成一座看不見的地下城市。這件作品來自學生在海邊觀察螃蟹的經驗，問的是如何讓這個隱藏的結構被看見。指導過程先引導學生以紙黏土逐一塑出長條，代表巢穴內部的通道，並確保每一段都有足夠的分岔，讓蟹巢的網絡先被理解為一套空間系統。進入推演，學生把這些長條接合成一個纏結的整體，再覆上沙，還原蟹洞原本的質感，讓人工的形體重新回到土地的語言。最後，完成的雕塑是一個由迴繞通道構成的有機裝置，粗糙而多孔，如同它所來自的土地，讓觀者得以凝視一座原本只屬於螃蟹的家。

pins.title: Accessible Recreation Campus

Model and drawings | Accessibility study | PVC board, wooden sticks, tracing paper, laser-cut wood | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無障礙休閒園區
zh-Hant.description:
紅色坡道在木條框架間迂迴穿行，串起長者也能抵達的小型休閒空間。

模型與繪圖｜無障礙研究｜PVC板、木條、描圖紙、雷射切割木料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Red ramps winding through the model.
紅色坡道在模型中迂迴。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student saw that older neighbours struggled with stairs and that the rooms they met in were too small. The project asks how a campus could make every recreation space easy to reach.
captions: Reference photos of a ramp model and a raised window cabin.
A section sketch of ramps and rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生觀察到年長鄰居上下樓梯很吃力，聚會的房間也太小。這個專題探問，園區如何讓每個休閒空間都容易抵達。
captions: 坡道模型與高架窗屋的參考照片。
坡道與房間的剖面草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The design was first built in 3D software. Painted PVC ramps were chosen for gentle slopes, with laser-cut wooden frames as support.
captions: A stick screen beside the ramp.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 設計先在3D軟體中建立。學生選用上漆的PVC板做出平緩坡道，並以雷射切割的木框架支撐。
captions: 沿黑色框架爬升的坡道。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wheat-straw walls proved too weak, so tracing paper on zig-zag sticks was used instead. Light through the paper casts shadows that show the structure.
captions: A paper-and-stick room above the ramps.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 麥稈牆太脆弱，學生改用鋸齒木條撐起描圖紙。光線穿透紙面投下陰影，顯出結構。
captions: 坡道上方的紙與木條房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 500 mm model ties twisting ramps to rooms hung from the top. Two hand-drawn views show people moving through the planted courtyards.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個500公釐的模型以迂迴坡道連接從頂部懸掛的房間。兩張手繪透視表現人們穿行於植栽庭院之中。

sections.heading: Accessible Recreation Campus - Making Every Space Within Reach
sections.body: Older neighbours struggling with stairs, and the cramped rooms where they gathered, were difficulties the student noticed in daily life. Starting from this observation, the work asked how a campus could make every recreation space easy to reach. The guidance first led the student to build the design in 3D software, choosing painted PVC boards for gentle ramps supported by laser-cut wooden frames, so that accessibility became the core of the structure. In development, wheat-straw walls proved too weak, and the student turned instead to tracing paper stretched on zig-zag sticks; light passing through the paper casts shadows that reveal the structure. Finally, the 500 mm model ties twisting ramps to rooms hung from the top, while two hand-drawn views show people moving through planted courtyards, turning care into gentle slopes and the play of light and shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 無障礙休閒園區-讓每一處都容易抵達
zh-Hant.body: 年長鄰居上下樓梯的吃力，以及聚會房間的狹小，是學生在日常中看見的困境。這件作品從這份觀察出發，問的是一座園區如何讓每個休閒空間都容易抵達。指導過程先引導學生在三維軟體中建立設計，選用上漆的PVC板做出平緩的坡道，並以雷射切割的木框架支撐，讓可及性成為結構的核心。進入推演，麥稈牆被證明太過脆弱，學生改以鋸齒木條撐起描圖紙，光線穿透紙面投下陰影，結構因此清晰可見。最後，這個五百公釐的模型以迂迴的坡道連接從頂部懸掛的房間，兩張手繪透視描繪人們穿行於植栽庭院，讓關懷化為溫和的坡度與光影。

pins.title: Stick-Frame Japanese House
pins.description:
A traditional Japanese house is rebuilt from wooden sticks alone, with a roof that lifts off to show the rooms inside.

Model and drawings | Timber structure study | Wooden sticks, hot glue, plaster | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 木條日式民居
zh-Hant.description:
以木條重建一棟傳統日式民居，屋頂可以掀起，露出內部房間。

模型與繪圖｜木構研究｜木條、熱熔膠、石膏｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to understand the craft behind Japanese timber houses. The project asks whether sticks alone can show how such a house is put together.
captions: Photos of traditional Japanese houses and gardens that inspired the model.
A study sketch of the house and its parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想了解日式木屋背後的工藝。這個專題探問，只用木條能否呈現這類房屋如何組構。
captions: 啟發本模型的日本傳統民居與庭園照片。
房屋與構件的研究草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied a bird's-eye view, an interior layout and an exterior sketch. Hand drawings marked the roof, foundation stones and paper screens.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了鳥瞰圖、室內配置與外觀草圖。手繪圖標出屋頂、基礎石與紙拉門。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A scaled plan was printed and the base built on it. Sticks were cut and glued one by one, thin sticks split the rooms, and plaster levelled the base.
captions: Lifting off the roof frame by hand to show the rooms inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生印出等比例平面，在上面搭建基座。木條逐根裁切黏合，細木條分隔房間，並以石膏整平基座。
captions: 親手掀起屋頂結構，展示內部空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The roof is fixed with tape so it can be lifted off. Small errors were sanded down, and the finished model shows the full frame.
captions: The roof frame seen from above.
The model with its roof in place.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂以雙面膠固定，可以掀起。小誤差經砂磨修整，完成的模型完整呈現整個框架。

sections.heading: Stick-Frame Japanese House - Reading a House Through Sticks
sections.body: The beauty of a Japanese timber house lies in how it is assembled piece by piece. Starting from the student's curiosity about this craft, the work asked whether sticks alone could show how such a house is put together. The guidance first led the student to study a bird's-eye view, an interior layout and an exterior sketch, marking the roof, foundation stones and paper screens in hand drawings, so that the house's construction was first understood on paper. In development, the student printed a scaled plan and built the base on it; sticks were cut and glued one by one, thin sticks divided the rooms, and plaster levelled the base, with patience as the main tool. Finally, the roof was fixed with double-sided tape so it can be lifted off, small errors were sanded down, and the finished model shows the full frame, so that viewers who lift the roof can see the inner logic of a house.

zh-Hant.heading: 木條日式民居-以木條讀懂一棟房子
zh-Hant.body: 一棟日式木屋的美，藏在它如何被一根根構件組起來。這件作品從學生想了解這份工藝的好奇出發，問的是只用木條能否呈現這類房屋的組構方式。指導過程先引導學生研究鳥瞰圖、室內配置與外觀草圖，以手繪標出屋頂、基礎石與紙拉門，讓房屋的構造先在紙上被讀懂。進入推演，學生印出等比例平面並在上面搭建基座，木條逐根裁切黏合，細木條分隔房間，石膏則整平基座，耐心成為最主要的工具。最後，屋頂以雙面膠固定，可以掀起，小誤差經砂磨修整，完成的模型完整呈現整個框架，讓觀者掀開屋頂，便能看見一棟房子的內在邏輯。

pins.title: Nine Garden Scenes
pins.description:
Nine small models capture nine spots in a traditional Chinese garden and the senses each one speaks to.

Models | Garden and senses study | Wooden sticks, PVC board, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 園林九景
zh-Hant.description:
九個小模型捕捉傳統中式園林中的九個場景，以及各自觸動的感官。

模型｜園林與感官研究｜木條、PVC板、紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Chinese gardens feel calm because each part speaks to a different sense. The project asks how that strategy could be shown in models.
captions: A bird's-eye sketch of the scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 中式園林讓人平靜，是因為各處觸動不同的感官。這個專題探問如何以模型呈現這套策略。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied one garden in depth and marked nine places on its plan. Routes through the garden were traced to see how views change.
captions: Nine spots marked on a garden plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生深入研究一座園林，並在平面上標出九個地點。學生也描出園中路線，觀察視野如何變化。
captions: 園林平面上標出的九個地點。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each spot became a small model of card walls and stick frames. Different materials stand for sound, smell, touch and sight.
captions: Cutting sticks and card and assembling the models by hand.
Models in progress on the desk.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每個地點都化為一個紙板牆與木條框架的小模型。不同材料代表聲音、氣味、觸感與視覺。
captions: 親手裁切木條與紙板並組裝模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The nine models are joined into one cluster, like walking a route through the garden. They keep the fine detail of traditional craft.
captions: The joined models from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 九個模型組合成一體，彷彿沿著路線走過園林。它們保留了傳統工藝的細膩。

sections.heading: Nine Garden Scenes - A Wandering Path of the Senses
sections.body: A Chinese garden feels calm because each of its parts speaks to a different sense. Starting from this spatial strategy, the work asked how it could be shown through models. The guidance first led the student to study one garden in depth, marking nine places on its plan and tracing routes through it to see how views change with each step, so that the experience of wandering was carefully taken apart. In development, each spot became a small model of card walls and stick frames, with different materials standing for sound, smell, touch and sight, giving abstract sensations a concrete form. Finally, the nine models were joined into a single cluster, as if walking a route through the whole garden, while keeping the fine detail of traditional craft, letting viewers rediscover within a small compass the quiet poetry of scenery that shifts with every step.

zh-Hant.heading: 園林九景-五感交織的漫遊路徑
zh-Hant.body: 中式園林令人平靜，是因為每一處都觸動著不同的感官。這件作品從這套空間策略出發，問的是如何以模型把它呈現出來。指導過程先引導學生深入研究一座園林，在平面上標出九個地點，並描出園中的路線，觀察視野如何隨步移而變化，讓漫遊的經驗先被細細拆解。進入推演，每個地點都化為一個紙板牆與木條框架的小模型，不同的材料分別代表聲音、氣味、觸感與視覺，抽象的感受因此有了具體的形體。最後，九個模型組合成一體，彷彿沿著路線走過整座園林，同時保留傳統工藝的細膩，讓觀者在方寸之間重新體會步移景異的靜謐詩意。

pins.title: Flower Tower
pins.description:
Petal shapes become card reliefs, then stacked flower blocks joined by sticks rise into a tower.

Model and digital painting | Form study | Hard cardboard, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 花之塔
zh-Hant.description:
花瓣形狀化為紙板浮雕，再把花形量體以木條串接，堆疊成塔。

模型與數位繪畫｜形態研究｜硬紙板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The flower tower in the garden.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: While watering flowers, the student knocked off some petals and tried to put them back. The project asks how a flower's structure could become a space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在澆花時不小心碰落花瓣，試著把它們黏回去。這個專題探問花的結構如何化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The flower was drawn as a 2D pattern of circles. Card strips were then bent along those circles to make reliefs.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把花畫成由圓形組成的平面圖案。接著沿著圓弧彎折紙條，做成浮雕。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The reliefs were extended upward into 3D flower blocks. Several blocks were stacked and linked with sticks to show the direction of growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把浮雕向上延伸成立體花形量體。多個量體以木條串接疊起，表現生長方向。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 520 mm tower was given as a gift to make up for the damaged flowers. A digital painting lays real blooms over the tower lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座520公釐的塔作為禮物，彌補被碰壞的花。一幅數位繪畫把花朵疊在塔的線稿上。

sections.heading: Flower Tower - A Tower Built for Fallen Petals
sections.body: During an accident while watering flowers, the student knocked off some petals and tried to glue them back. Starting from this tender little episode, the work asked how a flower's structure could become space. The guidance first led the student to draw the flower as a flat pattern of circles and then bend card strips along those circles into reliefs, so that the order of the petals was first understood anew on a flat surface. In development, the reliefs were extended upward into three-dimensional flower blocks, and several were stacked and linked with sticks to show the direction of growth, the form of the flower gradually becoming an architectural frame. Finally, the 520 mm tower was given as a gift to make up for the damaged flowers, and a digital painting lays real blooms over the tower's lines, turning a slip of the hand into an apology and a tribute written in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 花之塔-為碰落的花瓣建一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 一次澆花時的意外，學生碰落了幾片花瓣，並試著把它們黏回去。這件作品從這個溫柔的小插曲出發，問的是花的結構如何化為空間。指導過程先引導學生把花畫成由圓形組成的平面圖案，再沿著圓弧彎折紙條做成浮雕，讓花瓣的秩序先在平面上被重新理解。進入推演，浮雕向上延伸成立體的花形量體，多個量體以木條串接疊起，表現出生長的方向，花的形態逐漸長成建築的骨架。最後，這座五百二十公釐的塔作為禮物，彌補那些被碰壞的花，一幅數位繪畫又把真實的花朵疊在塔的線稿上，讓一次失手轉化為一份以空間寫成的歉意與致意。

pins.title: The Cliffhouse
pins.description:
Slotted paper squares lock together, with little glue, into a house that leans out over a cliff edge.

zh-Hant.title: 崖邊之屋
zh-Hant.description:
以插接的紙方塊互相扣合，幾乎不用膠，做成一座探出崖邊的房屋。

模型｜接合研究｜紙板、熱熔膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In a summer course the brief was a paper model in a 12-inch box, with as little glue as possible. The student imagined a house by a waterfall, reaching over a cliff.
captions: Photos of stairwells and steel structures observed in New York.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在一門暑期課程中，題目是在12英寸的空間內做紙模型，並盡量少用膠。學生構想一座瀑布旁、伸出崖邊的房屋。
captions: 在紐約觀察到的樓梯間與鋼構照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Inspired by Japanese carpentry, the student drew how paper pieces could slide into each other. A wall pattern from an earlier project was reused.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生受日式木工啟發，畫出紙片如何互相插接。牆面圖案則沿用自先前的作品。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper squares were slotted together into stacked diamonds. The joints hold without glue, and the work focused on the front view.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙方塊互相插接，疊成菱形。節點不需膠就能固定，製作重點放在正立面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished house sits on a cliff edge, with part of it hanging out over the drop. Small test versions show how the same joint scales.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的房屋坐落崖邊，一部分懸出崖外。小型試作版本顯示同一種接合如何縮放。

sections.heading: The Cliffhouse - A Paper House Held Without Glue
sections.body: Constraints are often the best starting point for imagination. The work came from a summer course whose brief was a paper model within a 12-inch space, using as little glue as possible, and from it the student imagined a house beside a waterfall, reaching out over a cliff. The guidance first led the student to draw inspiration from Japanese carpentry, sketching how paper pieces could slide into one another, and to reuse a wall pattern from an earlier project, carrying past exploration into a new brief. In development, paper squares were slotted together into stacked diamonds, the joints holding without glue, with the making focused on the front view. Finally, the finished house sits on a cliff edge with part of it hanging out over the drop, while small test versions show how the same joint scales, letting the intelligence of a sheet of paper hold up a dwelling suspended in air.

zh-Hant.heading: 崖邊之屋-不用膠的紙之接合
zh-Hant.body: 限制往往是想像最好的起點。這件作品來自一門暑期課程，題目是在十二英寸的空間內做紙模型，並盡量少用膠，學生由此構想一座位於瀑布旁、伸出崖邊的房屋。指導過程先引導學生從日式木工汲取啟發，畫出紙片如何互相插接，並沿用先前作品中的牆面圖案，讓過去的探索延續到新的題目。進入推演，紙方塊互相插接、疊成菱形，節點不需膠就能固定，製作的重點放在正立面的表現。最後，完成的房屋坐落崖邊，一部分懸出崖外，小型試作版本則顯示同一種接合如何縮放，讓一張紙的智慧支撐起凌空的居所。

pins.title: Rain Tower
pins.description:
A 1 m tower stacks four story layers, from a grey city at the base to a swirl of blue paper rain at the top.

Model | Story-to-space study | Wooden sticks, PVC board, paper, mirrored paper, cotton | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 雨之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一座1公尺高的塔疊起四層故事，從底部灰色城市到頂部藍紙旋成的雨。

模型｜故事轉空間研究｜木條、PVC板、紙、鏡面紙、棉花｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work is based on an animated film about a rain-soaked city. The project asks how themes such as loneliness, power, family and sacrifice could become layers of a tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品以一部描寫雨中城市的動畫電影為本。這個專題探問，孤獨、力量、家庭與犧牲等主題如何化為塔的各層。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student rewatched the film and listed its main themes. Each theme was given its own layer in a tall stacked design.
captions: The story sketch of the tower, annotated with the film stills behind each layer.
Stepped walls for the city layer.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生重看電影並列出主要主題。每個主題都在高聳的疊層設計中擁有一層。
captions: 塔的故事草圖，標註各層所依據的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A grey city silhouette forms the bottom and third layers. A mirrored ball core stands for warmth, and blue paper squares on a bent rod make the rain.
captions: Holding the mirrored geometric core in hand.
Blue paper rain on a rod.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 灰色城市剪影構成底層與第三層。鏡面球體核心代表溫暖，彎曲金屬桿上的藍紙片則化為雨。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Cotton clouds top the 1 m tower. Read from bottom to top, the layers tell the story as a space.
captions: Clouds and rain at the top.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 棉花雲覆蓋在1公尺高的塔頂。由下往上讀，各層把故事化為空間。

sections.heading: Rain Tower - A Story Read from Bottom to Top
sections.body: A city soaked in rain carries loneliness, power, family and sacrifice. Based on an animated film about such a city, the work asked how these themes could become the layers of a tower. The guidance first led the student to rewatch the film and list its main themes, then give each theme its own layer in a tall stacked design, so that the structure of the narrative became a vertical structure. In development, a grey city silhouette forms the bottom and third layers, a mirrored ball core stands for warmth, and blue paper squares on a bent rod become the falling rain. Finally, cotton clouds crown the 1 m tower, and read from bottom to top the layers turn the story into space, letting viewers, as they look upward, travel from the gloomy city all the way to the sky.

zh-Hant.heading: 雨之塔-由下而上讀出的故事
zh-Hant.body: 一座被雨浸透的城市，承載著孤獨、力量、家庭與犧牲。這件作品以一部描寫雨中城市的動畫電影為本，問的是這些主題如何化為一座塔的各層。指導過程先引導學生重看電影並列出主要主題，再讓每個主題在高聳的疊層設計中擁有自己的一層，使敘事的結構轉為垂直的結構。進入推演，灰色的城市剪影構成底層與第三層，鏡面球體核心代表溫暖，彎曲金屬桿上的藍紙片則化為落下的雨。最後，棉花雲覆蓋在一公尺高的塔頂，由下往上閱讀，各層把故事化為空間，讓觀者在仰望之間，從陰鬱的城市一路走向天空。

pins.title: Clay Through the Frame
pins.description:
Soft clay flows through, wraps and slowly covers a rigid lattice of wooden sticks.

Model and drawing | Material contrast study | Wooden sticks, light clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 穿流框架的黏土
zh-Hant.description:
柔軟的黏土在剛硬的木條格架間流動、纏繞，並逐漸將它覆蓋。

模型與繪圖｜材料對比研究｜木條、輕黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The stick lattice wrapped in clay.
被黏土包覆的木條格架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A frame of sticks is sturdy and complex, but hard to change. The project asks how a soft material could slowly take over such a structure without breaking it.
captions: The architects and flowing buildings that inspired the clay forms, with a pencil curve study.
A pencil study of flowing curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 木條框架堅固而複雜，卻難以改變。這個專題探問，柔軟的材料如何在不破壞結構的情況下，慢慢接管它。
captions: 啟發黏土形態的建築師與流線建築，附鉛筆曲線研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Straight sticks stand for order and clay for softness. Small tests joined the two to see where they clash and where they fit.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 直木條代表秩序，黏土代表柔軟。學生以小型試作結合兩者，觀察它們何處衝突、何處契合。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The lattice was cut into curved outlines. Clay was then laid in so it twines round the sticks like fish among waterweeds.
captions: Cutting the stick frame and laying the clay by hand.
A pen drawing of the inner space.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把格架裁成弧形輪廓。接著填入黏土，讓它像水草間的魚一樣纏繞木條。
captions: 親手裁切木條框架並鋪上黏土。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the 420 mm model the clay becomes the new body of the frame. Light inside reveals cave-like passages.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在這個420公釐的模型中，黏土成為框架新的主體。內部光線顯出如洞穴般的通道。

sections.heading: Clay Through the Frame - Softness Taking Over Order
sections.body: A frame of sticks is sturdy and complex, yet hard to change. Starting from that rigidity, the work asked how a soft material could slowly take over such a structure without breaking it. The guidance first led the student to read the straight sticks as order and the clay as softness, then to join the two in small tests to see where they clash and where they fit, so that the dialogue between materials was heard first. In development, the student cut the lattice into curved outlines and then laid clay into it so that it twines around the sticks like fish among waterweeds, the rigid grid beginning to breathe with movement. Finally, in the 420 mm model the clay becomes the new body of the frame, and light inside reveals cave-like passages, suggesting that order and softness are not opposites but can transform one another over time.

zh-Hant.heading: 穿流框架的黏土-柔軟接管秩序
zh-Hant.body: 木條框架堅固而複雜，卻難以改變。這件作品從這份僵硬出發，問的是柔軟的材料如何在不破壞結構的情況下，慢慢接管它。指導過程先引導學生把直木條讀作秩序，把黏土讀作柔軟，再以小型試作結合兩者，觀察它們在何處衝突、在何處契合，讓材料的對話先被聽見。進入推演，學生把格架裁成弧形輪廓，接著填入黏土，讓它像水草間的魚一樣纏繞木條，剛硬的格子開始有了流動的呼吸。最後，在這個四百二十公釐的模型中，黏土成為框架新的主體，內部光線顯出如洞穴般的通道，提示秩序與柔軟並非對立，而能在時間中彼此轉化。

pins.title: Growing Up in Four Models
pins.description:
Four small mixed-media models trace growing up: plants, a red net, cotton clouds and a tangle of wire.

Models and drawings | Narrative series | Mixed media | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 成長四部曲
zh-Hant.description:
四個混合媒材小模型描繪成長：植物、紅網、棉花雲與纏繞的線材。

模型與繪圖｜敘事系列｜混合媒材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The series asks how four stages of growing up could each become a small space. Each stage gets its own material and mood.
captions: A pen drawing of a plant playground.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個系列探問，成長的四個階段如何各自化為一個小空間。每個階段都有自己的材料與氛圍。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Childhood is a green playground of leaves, rocks and branches. Real plant cuttings were set up with tiny figures to test the scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 童年是由樹葉、岩石與枝條構成的綠色遊樂場。學生以真實植物枝葉配上小人偶，測試尺度。
captions: 配上小人偶的植物枝葉。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The teenage years of exams became stairs inside a red net. The net is shown slowly closing in around the climb.
captions: A sketch of the net tower.
A sketch of the net and cloud.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以考試為主的青春期化為紅網中的階梯。紅網環繞著攀爬的路徑逐漸收緊。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Bright clay and cotton show a dreamy, then shattered, feeling. A tangle of wire, mesh and colour stands for an uncertain future.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鮮豔的黏土與棉花表現先如夢、後破碎的感受。線材、網布與色彩的纏結則代表不確定的未來。

sections.heading: Growing Up in Four Models - Life Stages Written in Materials
sections.body: Growing up is not a smooth line but a sequence of stages, each with its own atmosphere. The series asked how four stages of growing up could each become a small space with its own material and mood. The guidance first led the student to imagine childhood as a green playground of leaves, rocks and branches, testing the scale with real plant cuttings and tiny figures, so that memory first found a form one could touch. In development, the exam-filled teenage years became stairs inside a red net that slowly tightens around the climb, making pressure visible in space. Finally, bright clay and cotton express a feeling that is first dreamy and then shattered, while a tangle of wire, mesh and colour stands for an uncertain future, so that the four models together form a silent narrative about growing up.

zh-Hant.heading: 成長四部曲-以材料寫成的生命階段
zh-Hant.body: 成長不是一條平滑的線，而是由不同氛圍的階段接連而成。這個系列問的是，成長的四個階段如何各自化為一個小空間，各有自己的材料與情緒。指導過程先引導學生把童年想像成由樹葉、岩石與枝條構成的綠色遊樂場，並以真實植物枝葉配上小人偶測試尺度，讓記憶先找到可觸摸的形體。進入推演，以考試為主的青春期化為紅網中的階梯，紅網環繞著攀爬的路徑逐漸收緊，壓力在空間中具體可見。最後，鮮豔的黏土與棉花表現先如夢、後破碎的感受，線材、網布與色彩的纏結則代表不確定的未來，讓四個模型合成一部關於長大的無聲敘事。

pins.title: Within the Light Cone
pins.description:
Paper fragments fan out inside an acrylic frame in the shape of a light cone, bouncing light off mirrors.

Model and sketches | Physics-to-space study | Acrylic strips, paper, mirror | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光錐之內
zh-Hant.description:
紙片在壓克力框架中以光錐形狀展開，在鏡面間反射光線。

模型與素描｜物理轉空間研究｜壓克力條、紙、鏡面｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In physics, an event spreads through spacetime as a cone of light. The project asks how that idea could be made into a space you can look into.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在物理學中，事件以光錐的形式在時空中擴散。這個專題探問，如何把這個概念做成可以望入的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Like a stone thrown into water, light spreads out until it forms a 3D cone. A far event has no effect until its cone arrives.
captions: Time Record: a pencil sketch of cameras and newspaper fragments.
A pencil sketch of warped time.
A colour sketch of a world in a cone.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 如同石頭投入水中，光向外擴散，形成立體的錐形。遠方的事件在光錐抵達之前不會產生影響。
captions: 《時間紀錄》：相機與報紙碎片的鉛筆素描。
光錐中世界的彩色素描。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper fragments were hung in a cone within a grid of acrylic strips. Mirrors repeat them so the light seems to race away.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把紙片以錐形懸掛在壓克力條網格中。鏡面不斷複製它們，使光彷彿向遠方奔去。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 850 mm tall model looks endless from every side. The past reads like a shot already fired, racing to its end.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個850公釐高的模型從各面看都無止盡。過去就像已射出的子彈，奔向它的終點。

sections.heading: Within the Light Cone - A Spacetime One Can Look Into
sections.body: In physics, an event spreads through spacetime as a cone of light. Starting from this idea, the work asked how it could be made into a space one can look into. The guidance first led the student to understand the spread of light through the image of a stone thrown into water: light pushes outward until it forms a three-dimensional cone, and a distant event has no effect until its cone arrives, so that abstract theory first became a picture one could imagine. In development, the student hung paper fragments in a cone within a grid of acrylic strips, and mirrors repeat them endlessly so the light seems to race away. Finally, the 850 mm tall model appears endless from every side, the past reading like a shot already fired racing toward its end, letting viewers touch, in a single gaze, the calm grandeur of time flowing in one direction.

zh-Hant.heading: 光錐之內-可以望入的時空
zh-Hant.body: 在物理學中，事件以光錐的形式在時空中擴散。這件作品從這個概念出發，問的是如何把它做成一個可以望入的空間。指導過程先引導學生以石頭投入水中的意象理解光的擴散，光向外推展，形成立體的錐形，而遠方的事件在光錐抵達之前不會產生影響，讓抽象的理論先成為可以想像的畫面。進入推演，學生把紙片以錐形懸掛在壓克力條網格中，鏡面不斷複製它們，使光彷彿向遠方奔去。最後，這個八百五十公釐高的模型從各面看都無止無盡，過去就像已射出的子彈奔向它的終點，讓觀者在凝視之間，觸及時間單向流逝的冷靜與壯闊。

pins.title: Möbius Tower
pins.description:
Twisted Möbius rings of clear and white acrylic stack into a tower crowned with clay spheres and dry branches.

Model and drawings | Loop structure study | Modelling clay, PVC card, acrylic, dry branches | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 莫比烏斯之塔
zh-Hant.description:
透明與白色壓克力扭成的莫比烏斯環堆疊成塔，頂部以黏土球與枯枝收尾。

模型與繪圖｜迴圈結構研究｜造型黏土、PVC卡、壓克力、枯枝｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A Möbius strip is a loop with only one side. The project asks how such an endless loop could become a tower that hides and shows parts of itself.
captions: The concept collage and reference images behind the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 莫比烏斯帶是只有一面的迴圈。這個專題探問，這樣無盡的迴圈如何化為一座時隱時現的塔。
captions: 塔的概念拼貼與參考圖像。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew and rendered many twisted rings to test how they could stack. Each form was checked for how it might be built.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生繪製並渲染許多扭轉的環，測試它們如何堆疊。每種形態都檢查了建造的可能。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Ring pieces were cast and tested in white before the final build. Clear acrylic makes the curved structure lighter and harder to read.
captions: Casting, sanding and fitting the rings by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以白色材料翻製並測試環片，再做最終模型。透明壓克力讓彎曲結構更輕，也更難一眼看透。
captions: 親手翻模、打磨並組裝圓環。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Cracks were filled with stone clay and dry sticks pushed into it. The 405 mm tower is meant to suggest rebirth.
captions: A pen drawing of the tower.
Clay spheres and branches on top.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 裂縫以石粉黏土填補，並插入枯枝。這座405公釐的塔意在傳達重生之感。

sections.heading: Möbius Tower - Rebirth Within an Endless Loop
sections.body: A Möbius strip is a loop with only one side, where inside and outside can no longer be told apart. Starting from this mathematical form, the work asked how an endless loop could become a tower that hides and reveals parts of itself. The guidance first led the student to draw and render many twisted rings, testing how they might stack and checking each form for how it could be built, so that an abstract topology was first grounded in feasible construction. In development, the student cast and tested the ring pieces in white before making the final model, and clear acrylic makes the curved structure lighter and harder to read at a glance, the tower drifting between appearing and vanishing. Finally, cracks were filled with stone clay and dry sticks pushed into it, and the 405 mm tower is meant to suggest rebirth, letting rupture and continuity meet within the same loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 莫比烏斯之塔-無盡迴圈中的重生
zh-Hant.body: 莫比烏斯帶是只有一面的迴圈，內外在其中無從區分。這件作品從這個數學形體出發，問的是無盡的迴圈如何化為一座時隱時現的塔。指導過程先引導學生繪製並渲染許多扭轉的環，測試它們如何堆疊，並逐一檢查每種形態建造的可能，讓抽象的拓撲先落實為可行的構造。進入推演，學生先以白色材料翻製並測試環片，再做最終模型，透明壓克力讓彎曲結構更輕，也更難一眼看透，塔在顯現與隱沒之間游移。最後，裂縫以石粉黏土填補，並插入枯枝，這座四百零五公釐的塔意在傳達重生之感，讓破裂與延續在同一個迴圈裡相遇。

pins.title: House of Tree
pins.description:
Cut waste branches stack up like a growing trunk that slowly climbs over small white houses.

Model and sketches | Reuse and nature study | Tree branches, PVC card, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹之屋
zh-Hant.description:
裁切的廢棄枝條如生長的樹幹般層層堆疊，慢慢爬過白色小屋。

模型與草圖｜再利用與自然研究｜樹枝、PVC卡、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The branch tower with its small houses.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Building in nature can harm the place it sits in. The project asks how waste wood could give people shelter and still let nature lead.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在自然中建造可能傷害所在之地。這個專題探問，廢棄木材如何為人提供庇護，同時讓自然居於主導。
captions: 關於庇護的關鍵字圖解。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Old wrecks on a shore can serve as rough resting places. Dead wood also has pores that hold water and let tiny life grow.
captions: A section sketch of the idea.
A sketch of the trunk form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 海岸上的殘骸可以充當簡陋的休憩處。枯木也有能保存水分、讓微生物生長的孔隙。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Branches were cut into short pieces and stacked from the edge of a frame. At a set height they close in to carry the houses.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把樹枝裁成短段，從框架邊緣開始堆疊。到一定高度時枝段向內收合，承托小屋。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the 300 mm model the branches keep climbing over the houses. In time the homes would be wrapped and become part of the tree.
captions: A house resting on the branches.
A house half covered by branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在這個300公釐的模型中，枝條持續爬過小屋。隨著時間，住所會被包覆，成為樹的一部分。

sections.heading: House of Tree - A Shelter Where Nature Leads
sections.body: Building in nature often harms the very place it sits in. Starting from this contradiction, the work asked how waste wood could give people shelter while still letting nature lead. The guidance first led the student to observe how old wrecks on a shore serve as rough resting places, and to learn that the pores of dead wood hold water and let tiny life grow, so that discarded material was first understood anew as a resource. In development, the student cut branches into short pieces and stacked them from the edge of a frame; at a set height the pieces close inward to carry the small houses. Finally, in the 300 mm model the branches keep climbing over the houses, and in time the dwellings would be wrapped and become part of the tree, so that architecture no longer stands against nature but slowly returns to it over time.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹之屋-讓自然居於主導的庇護
zh-Hant.body: 在自然中建造，往往會傷害所在之地。這件作品從這份矛盾出發，問的是廢棄木材如何為人提供庇護，同時讓自然居於主導。指導過程先引導學生觀察海岸上的殘骸如何充當簡陋的休憩處，並認識枯木的孔隙能保存水分、讓微小生命生長，讓廢棄之物先被重新理解為資源。進入推演，學生把樹枝裁成短段，從框架邊緣開始堆疊，到一定高度時枝段向內收合，承托起小屋。最後，在這個三百公釐的模型中，枝條持續爬過小屋，隨著時間，住所將被包覆而成為樹的一部分，讓建築不再與自然對立，而是在時間中慢慢歸還於它。

pins.title: A Playground for Magpies
pins.description:
A white clay landscape of arches, holes and mushroom platforms is shaped for birds that hop before they fly.

Model and sketches | Animal habitat study | Modelling clay, wire, foam board, mat board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 喜鵲的遊樂場
zh-Hant.description:
由拱、孔洞與蘑菇狀平台構成的白色黏土地景，為起飛前會跳躍的鳥而塑造。

模型與草圖｜動物棲地研究｜造型黏土、線材、珍珠板、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The clay playground under coloured light.
