彩色光下的黏土遊樂場。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project puts birds, not people, at the centre. It asks what a space would look like if it were made for magpies first.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題把鳥而非人放在中心。它探問，如果空間首先為喜鵲而建，會是什麼模樣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Magpies hop before they take off and like sun and shade. The student drew their feathers and traced their jumps frame by frame.
captions: A traced hop and flight sequence.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 喜鵲起飛前會跳躍，也喜歡陽光與陰影。學生描繪牠們的羽毛，並逐格描摹跳躍動作。
captions: 描摹的跳躍與飛行序列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plan and side sketches set out walls, closed nooks and sunning spots. A bent wire frame then fixed the curves before the clay.
captions: A side sketch of the shelter.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 平面與側面草圖安排了牆、封閉角落與曬太陽的位置。接著以彎折的線材框架定下曲線，再敷上黏土。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 395 mm clay model has smooth edges, hidden gaps and raised platforms. Tiny figures show how small people are next to it.
captions: The model on a dark stage.
A low view of the forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個395公釐的黏土模型有平滑邊緣、隱密縫隙與高起的平台。小人偶顯示人在它旁邊有多渺小。

sections.heading: A Playground for Magpies - A Space Made for Birds First
sections.body: Most spaces are designed around people, but this work places magpies at the centre. It asked what a space would look like if it were built for birds first. The guidance first led the student to observe the habits of magpies, how they hop before taking off and how they like both sun and shade; the student drew their feathers and traced their jumps frame by frame, letting the bird's body set the scale of the design. In development, plan and side sketches set out walls, closed nooks and sunning spots, and a bent wire frame then fixed the curves before clay was applied, so the form follows the bird's behaviour. Finally, the 395 mm clay model has smooth edges, hidden gaps and raised platforms, while tiny figures show how small people are beside it, gently reminding viewers that design can also begin from the viewpoint of another life.

zh-Hant.heading: 喜鵲的遊樂場-以鳥為先的空間
zh-Hant.body: 多數空間以人為中心而設計，這件作品卻把喜鵲放在中心。它問的是，如果空間首先為鳥而建，會是什麼模樣。指導過程先引導學生觀察喜鵲的習性：起飛前的跳躍、對陽光與陰影的偏好，學生描繪牠們的羽毛，並逐格描摹跳躍動作，讓鳥的身體成為設計的尺度。進入推演，平面與側面草圖安排了牆、封閉角落與曬太陽的位置，接著以彎折的線材框架定下曲線，再敷上黏土，讓形體貼合鳥的行為。最後，這個三百九十五公釐的黏土模型有平滑的邊緣、隱密的縫隙與高起的平台，小人偶顯示人在它旁邊有多渺小，溫柔地提醒觀者，設計也可以從另一種生命的視角開始。

pins.title: Lighthouse in the Void
pins.description:
Two wooden-frame spaces imagine a long space voyage: a lonely lighthouse of stocking sails, then a bursting core of colour.

Models and sketches | Story-to-space study | Wood, stockings, thread, wire, straws, film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 虛空中的燈塔
zh-Hant.description:
兩個木框空間想像一段漫長的太空航程：由絲襪帆構成的孤獨燈塔，以及爆裂的彩色核心。

模型與草圖｜故事轉空間研究｜木材、絲襪、線、金屬線、吸管、薄膜｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The lighthouse space in its frame.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work starts from a story of people on a long, lonely trip through space. It asks how their feelings could be built as two spaces.
captions: A sketch of the lighthouse inside a pyramid.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品源自一則人們在太空中漫長孤獨旅行的故事。它探問，如何把他們的情緒建構成兩個空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A lighthouse stands for a clear goal and for being alone. A yellow ladder in the core stands for a troubled mind.
captions: The yellow ladder in cotton cloud.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 燈塔象徵明確的目標，也象徵孤獨。核心中的黃色梯子代表不安的心靈。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In the second space a wire ball wrapped in straws is the heart of a blast. Hanging weights show the paths people choose.
captions: A sketch of the blast lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在第二個空間中，以吸管包覆的線球是爆炸的核心。懸掛的重物代表人們選擇的道路。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Shards of clear film spin out from the core. The two frames together read as hope, chaos and the long way home.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 透明薄膜碎片從核心向外旋出。兩個框架合起來，讀作希望、混亂與漫長的歸途。

sections.heading: Lighthouse in the Void - Two Spaces of Solitude and Hope
sections.body: On a long and lonely journey through space, purpose and being lost are often separated by a single thread. Drawn from a story of people on a long trip through space, the work asked how the travellers' feelings could be built as two spaces. The guidance first led the student to find symbols for those feelings: a lighthouse for a clear goal and for solitude, and a yellow ladder in its core for a troubled mind. In development, the second space takes a wire ball wrapped in straws as the heart of a blast, while hanging weights stand for the paths people choose, making the weight of decision visible in the air. Finally, shards of clear film spin outward from the core, and the two frames together read as hope, chaos and the long way home, turning a story set among the stars into an inner landscape viewers can contemplate.

zh-Hant.heading: 虛空中的燈塔-孤獨與希望的兩個空間
zh-Hant.body: 在漫長而孤獨的太空旅程中，目標與迷失往往只有一線之隔。這件作品源自一則人們在太空中漫長旅行的故事，問的是如何把旅人的情緒建構成兩個空間。指導過程先引導學生為情緒找到象徵：燈塔代表明確的目標，也代表孤獨，核心中的黃色梯子則代表不安的心靈。進入推演，第二個空間以吸管包覆的線球作為爆炸的核心，懸掛的重物代表人們選擇的道路，讓抉擇的重量在空中被看見。最後，透明薄膜碎片從核心向外旋出，兩個框架合起來讀作希望、混亂與漫長的歸途，讓一則宇宙中的故事化為觀者可以凝視的內心風景。

pins.title: Tired Objects
pins.description:
A greenhouse, a washer, a cabinet, a sink and a bed are built as worn, messy models of a tired mind.

Model series | Everyday objects and mood | Wood, fabric, wire mesh, paper, clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 疲憊的物件
zh-Hant.description:
溫室、洗衣機、櫃子、水槽與床，被做成破舊凌亂的模型，表現疲憊的心。

模型系列｜日常物件與情緒｜木材、布料、鐵絲網、紙、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Fatigue is hard to show. The series asks how everyday things could carry the strain of a tired person.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 疲憊很難表現。這個系列探問，日常物件如何承載一個疲憊之人的壓力。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each object stands for a part of daily life. Plastic stands in for broken glass and crumpled paper for dirt.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個物件代表日常生活的一部分。塑膠代替碎玻璃，揉皺的紙代替泥土。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A shelf is lined with printed paper and tape shapes to show too many products. A mesh sink is full of holes and clay dishes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 櫃子貼滿印刷紙與膠帶形體，表現過多的商品。鐵絲網水槽滿是破洞與黏土碗盤。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The series ends with a bed of torn fabric and a cotton cloud. Its worn state shows the worries carried into sleep.
captions: The loft bed of torn fabric.
The bed with its cotton cloud.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 系列以撕裂布料與棉花雲構成的床作結。它破舊的樣子，表現被帶入睡眠的憂慮。

sections.heading: Tired Objects - The Weariness Carried by Everyday Things
sections.body: Fatigue is a feeling hard to show; it makes no noise, yet it seeps into every corner of life. Starting from this invisible weight, the series asked how everyday objects could carry the strain of a tired person. The guidance first led the student to let each object stand for a part of daily life and to translate feeling through substitute materials: plastic in place of broken glass, crumpled paper in place of dirt. In development, a shelf is lined with printed paper and tape shapes to show an excess of products, and a mesh sink is full of holes and clay dishes, the small chores of daily life piling up in material form as a burden. Finally, the series closes with a bed of torn fabric and a cotton cloud whose worn state shows the worries carried into sleep, letting viewers recognise in familiar objects a weariness they have known themselves.

zh-Hant.heading: 疲憊的物件-日常之物承載的倦意
zh-Hant.body: 疲憊是一種難以表現的感受，它不喧嘩，卻滲入生活的每個角落。這個系列從這種無形的重量出發，問的是日常物件如何承載一個疲憊之人的壓力。指導過程先引導學生讓每個物件代表日常生活的一部分，並以替代材料轉譯感受：塑膠代替碎玻璃，揉皺的紙代替泥土。進入推演，櫃子貼滿印刷紙與膠帶形體，表現過多的商品，鐵絲網水槽滿是破洞與黏土碗盤，日常的瑣碎在材料中逐漸堆積成負擔。最後，系列以撕裂布料與棉花雲構成的床作結，它破舊的樣子表現被帶入睡眠的憂慮，讓觀者在熟悉的物件裡，認出自己也曾有過的倦意。

pins.title: Flowing Winged Jungle
pins.description:
Waste branches trace the loop of a flapping wing, then grow into a silver tower threaded with balsa paths.

Model | Motion-to-form study | Waste sticks and branches, hot glue, foam base, balsa wood, silver spray paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動的羽翼叢林
zh-Hant.description:
廢棄枝條描出拍翅的迴圈，再長成一座穿插輕木步道的銀色塔。

模型｜動作轉形態研究｜廢棄木條與樹枝、熱熔膠、泡綿底座、輕木、銀色噴漆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A bird's wing traces a loop each time it flaps. The project asks how that loop could become a space people move through.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 鳥每次拍翅都會畫出一個迴圈。這個專題探問，這個迴圈如何成為人可以穿行的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student watched birds from a window and the broken twigs they use for nests. Each wing stroke was cut into segments.
captions: The hummingbird flight diagram, wing-shaped pavilion photos and bird silhouettes that inspired the loops.
The sprayed tower from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從窗口觀察鳥，以及牠們用來築巢的斷枝。每一次振翅都被切分成片段。
captions: 啟發迴圈造型的蜂鳥飛行圖、翅膀形展亭照片與鳥類剪影。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Twigs from the street were glued into wing segments and stacked into a tower. Balsa paths of different widths run in and around it.
captions: Bending and arranging the branches by hand into a wingbeat loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把街上撿來的枝條黏成羽翼片段，再堆疊成塔。不同寬度的輕木步道在塔內外穿行。
captions: 親手彎折並排列樹枝，形成振翅的迴圈。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 850 mm model was sprayed silver. Tiny figures show a tower of linked paths and flowing spaces.
captions: A close view of the paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個850公釐的模型噴上銀漆。小人偶顯示出一座由相連路徑與流動空間構成的塔。

sections.heading: Flowing Winged Jungle - A Tower of Paths Born from Wingbeats
sections.body: Each time a bird flaps, its wing traces a loop in the air. Starting from this motion, the work asked how such a loop could become a space people move through. The guidance first led the student to watch birds from a window, along with the broken twigs they use for nests, and then to cut each wing stroke into segments, breaking a fleeting motion into units that could be built. In development, the student glued twigs gathered from the street into wing segments and stacked them into a tower, while balsa paths of different widths run in and around it, turning the rhythm of flight into the rhythm of walking. Finally, the 850 mm model was sprayed silver, and tiny figures reveal a tower of linked paths and flowing spaces, giving the twigs left behind in the city a new pair of wings.

zh-Hant.heading: 流動的羽翼叢林-振翅迴圈化成的路徑之塔
zh-Hant.body: 鳥每一次拍翅，都在空中畫出一個迴圈。這件作品從這個動作出發，問的是迴圈如何成為人可以穿行的空間。指導過程先引導學生從窗口觀察鳥，以及牠們用來築巢的斷枝，再把每一次振翅切分成片段，讓轉瞬即逝的動作被拆解成可以建造的單元。進入推演，學生把街上撿來的枝條黏成羽翼片段，再堆疊成塔，不同寬度的輕木步道在塔內外穿行，讓飛行的節奏化為行走的節奏。最後，這個八百五十公釐的模型噴上銀漆，小人偶顯示出一座由相連路徑與流動空間構成的塔，讓城市中被遺落的枝條重新長出翅膀。

pins.title: Ring of Wings
pins.description:
Woven bamboo rings stack and sweep like the arcs of birds in flight, hung among real trees.

Installation | Flight path study | Bamboo, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 羽翼之環
zh-Hant.description:
編織竹環如飛鳥的弧線般堆疊、掠過，懸掛在真實的樹林間。

裝置｜飛行軌跡研究｜竹、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Bamboo rings hanging in the dark.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Each kind of bird flies along its own arc. The project asks how many such arcs could combine into one light structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 每種鳥都沿著自己的弧線飛行。這個專題探問，許多弧線如何結合成一個輕盈的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Bamboo strips were woven in several patterns. The tests showed bamboo is tough, light and kind to the environment.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以數種圖樣編織竹條。試驗顯示竹材強韌、輕巧，也對環境友善。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Flight arcs were woven as open baskets and joined at their tips. Paper sails were added to catch the light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把飛行弧線編成開口的籃形，並在末端相接。再加入紙帆來捕捉光線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 1350 mm piece was hung in a forest. Among the leaves it reads as wings that belong to the place.
captions: Posing beneath the hanging bamboo rings to show their scale.
A closer view in the forest.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這件1350公釐的作品懸掛在樹林中。在枝葉間，它像是屬於這個地方的羽翼。
captions: 站在懸吊的竹環下方，呈現作品尺度。

sections.heading: Ring of Wings - Flight Arcs Woven in Bamboo
sections.body: Each kind of bird flies along its own arc, leaving invisible traces across the sky. Starting from these arcs, the work asked how they might combine into one light structure. The guidance first led the student to weave bamboo strips in several patterns, and the tests revealed bamboo to be tough, light and kind to the environment, so that the character of the material became the basis of the design. In development, the student wove the flight arcs as open baskets joined at their tips, then added paper sails to catch the light, giving the structure both the density of weaving and the openness of flight. Finally, the 1350 mm piece was hung in a forest, where among the leaves it reads as wings that belong to the place, freezing a moment of flight into a form one can linger beside and contemplate.

zh-Hant.heading: 羽翼之環-編織飛行弧線的竹之結構
zh-Hant.body: 每種鳥都沿著自己的弧線飛行，在天空中留下看不見的軌跡。這件作品從這些弧線出發，問的是它們如何結合成一個輕盈的結構。指導過程先引導學生以數種圖樣編織竹條，在試驗中發現竹材強韌、輕巧，也對環境友善，讓材料的性格成為設計的依據。進入推演，學生把飛行弧線編成開口的籃形，並在末端相接，再加入紙帆來捕捉光線，使結構既有編織的密度，也有飛翔的通透。最後，這件一千三百五十公釐的作品懸掛在樹林中，在枝葉之間，它像是屬於這個地方的羽翼，讓飛行的瞬間被凝結成可以停留與凝視的形體。

pins.title: From Timber to Clear Rods
pins.description:
A tower of interlocking wooden joints turns into clear acrylic rods as it rises, as if the old structure is fading away.

Model and drawing | Traditional joinery study | Wooden strips, acrylic strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從木構到透明
zh-Hant.description:
一座以木構榫接組成的塔，越往上越變成透明壓克力桿，彷彿舊結構逐漸消逝。

模型與繪圖｜傳統榫卯研究｜木條、壓克力條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many old timber buildings are being rebuilt or lost. The project asks how a model could show that slow loss.
captions: A pen drawing of timber eaves.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多老木構建築正被改建或消失。這個專題探問，模型如何呈現這種緩慢的流失。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched joints in old buildings and studied how hidden parts carry an all-wood frame. Small stick joints tested each type.
captions: A reference drawing of traditional bracket parts with its legend.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生速寫老建築中的接頭，研究隱藏的構件如何支撐全木構架。小型木條接頭測試了每一種類型。
captions: 傳統斗栱構件的參考圖與圖例。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The joints were made so they could repeat and lock with as little glue as possible. They were then stacked into roof layers.
captions: Testing mortise-and-tenon joints and gluing sticks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生讓接頭可以重複、並盡量少用膠而互相咬合。接著把它們堆疊成一層層屋頂。
captions: 親手測試榫卯接合並黏合木條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 600 mm tower is solid wood at its base and clear acrylic at the top. The clear part reads as a past that is being lost.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座600公釐的塔底部是實木，頂部是透明壓克力。透明的部分象徵正在消逝的過去。

sections.heading: From Timber to Clear Rods - The Fading Memory of Joints
sections.body: Many old timber buildings are being rebuilt or are quietly disappearing. Starting from this slow loss, the work asked how a model could make disappearance itself visible. The guidance first led the student to sketch the joints of old buildings and study how hidden parts carry an all-wood frame, then to test each type with small stick joints, so that the intelligence of the craft was first understood by hand. In development, the student made the joints repeatable and able to lock together with as little glue as possible, then stacked them into layer upon layer of roof, the logic of the structure growing clearer through repetition. Finally, the 600 mm tower is solid wood at its base and turns to clear acrylic at its top, the transparent part standing for a past that is fading, so that one tower becomes both a memorial to tradition and a witness to its loss.

zh-Hant.heading: 從木構到透明-正在消逝的榫接記憶
zh-Hant.body: 許多老木構建築正被改建或悄然消失。這件作品從這種緩慢的流失出發，問的是模型如何讓消逝本身被看見。指導過程先引導學生速寫老建築中的接頭，研究隱藏的構件如何支撐全木構架，再以小型木條接頭逐一測試每種類型，讓工藝的智慧先在手中被理解。進入推演，學生讓接頭可以重複、並盡量少用膠而互相咬合，再把它們堆疊成一層層屋頂，結構的邏輯在重複中變得清晰。最後，這座六百公釐的塔底部是實木，頂部漸成透明壓克力，透明的部分象徵正在消逝的過去，讓一座塔同時成為傳統的紀念與失落的見證。

pins.title: Tower on a Mountain of Debris
pins.description:
Rings of arched walls rise from a heap of clay debris, hung with pearls and fragile plaster skin.

Model and drawing | Story-to-space study | Concrete, wooden sticks, pearls, PVC board, stone clay, gauze | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 廢墟山上的塔
zh-Hant.description:
一圈圈拱牆從黏土碎屑堆中升起，掛著珍珠與脆弱的石膏表皮。

模型與繪圖｜故事轉空間研究｜混凝土、木條、珍珠、PVC板、石粉黏土、紗布｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower on its debris base.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The work starts from a novel about glamour, memory and loss. It asks how bright parties and hidden decay could share one tower.
captions: A pen drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 作品源自一部關於浮華、記憶與失落的小說。它探問，耀眼的派對與隱藏的衰敗如何共存於一座塔。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Rings of arches stand for grand parties at the top. A heap of rocks and bones below stands for what lies behind the show.
captions: Film stills of luxury and decay that inspired the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 頂部的拱圈代表盛大的派對。下方的岩石與骨骼堆，代表浮華背後的真相。
captions: 啟發這座塔的奢華與衰敗電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stone clay was shaped into a mound of waste. Pearls and building scraps hang down from the rings like falling time.
captions: Gluing the sticks and rings together by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以石粉黏土塑出廢棄物堆。珍珠與建築碎片從環圈垂下，如流逝的時間。
captions: 親手黏合木條與環形構件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A thin plaster skin makes the tower look fragile. The 750 mm model shows layers from the bright top to the heavy base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 薄薄的石膏表皮讓塔顯得脆弱。這個750公釐的模型呈現出從明亮頂部到沉重底座的層次。

sections.heading: Tower on a Mountain of Debris - A Vertical Tale of Glamour and Decay
sections.body: Behind every dazzling party there is often a decay no one sees. Drawn from a novel about glamour, memory and loss, the work asked how brilliance and ruin could share a single tower. The guidance first led the student to find an image for each state: rings of arches at the top for the grand parties, and a heap of rocks and bones below for the truth behind the show, so that the story's contrast became a vertical structure. In development, the student shaped a mound of waste from stone clay, while pearls and building scraps hang from the rings like falling time, suspending the weight of memory in the air. Finally, a thin plaster skin makes the tower look fragile, and the 750 mm model presents layers from the bright top to the heavy base, letting viewers read from top to bottom how splendour is built upon loss.

zh-Hant.heading: 廢墟山上的塔-浮華與衰敗的垂直敘事
zh-Hant.body: 耀眼的派對背後，往往藏著不被看見的衰敗。這件作品源自一部關於浮華、記憶與失落的小說，問的是光鮮與腐朽如何共存於一座塔。指導過程先引導學生為兩種狀態找到形象：頂部的拱圈代表盛大的派對，下方的岩石與骨骼堆代表浮華背後的真相，讓故事的對比先成為垂直的結構。進入推演，學生以石粉黏土塑出廢棄物堆，珍珠與建築碎片從環圈垂下，如同流逝的時間，把記憶的重量懸在空中。最後，薄薄的石膏表皮讓塔顯得脆弱，這個七百五十公釐的模型呈現出從明亮頂部到沉重底座的層次，讓觀者由上而下讀出繁華如何建立在失落之上。

pins.title: Treehouse Dorm
pins.description:
A slatted plywood dorm stands on stilts so the trees around it can stay.

Model and drawings | Housing among trees | Plywood board, laser cut | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹屋宿舍
zh-Hant.description:
一棟板條夾板宿舍架高於支柱上，讓周圍的樹木得以保留。

模型與繪圖｜林間住宅｜夾板、雷射切割｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A planned dorm would mean cutting down a wood. The project asks how the dorm could be built without moving the site or losing the trees.
captions: A sketch of a room among trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座規劃中的宿舍將需要砍伐一片樹林。這個專題探問，如何在不改變基地、也不失去樹木的情況下建造宿舍。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student asked other students what they want from a dorm. Their views shaped a small house for a few people.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生詢問其他同學對宿舍的期待。他們的意見形塑出一棟供少數人居住的小屋。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A spiral stair links a living room below to two bedrooms above. The design was drawn in 3D and laser cut.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 螺旋梯連接下方的客廳與上方的兩間臥室。設計以3D繪製並雷射切割。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Thin slats let light and views pass through. The 200 mm model shows a house that sits lightly among trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 細板條讓光線與視線穿透。這個200公釐的模型呈現出一棟輕輕立於樹間的房子。

sections.heading: Treehouse Dorm - A Home Resting Lightly Among Trees
sections.body: A planned dormitory meant that a wood would be cut down. Starting from this dilemma, the work asked how a dorm could be built without moving the site or losing the trees. The guidance first led the student to ask fellow students what they wanted from a dorm, letting the voices of future users become the starting point; their views gradually shaped a small house for a few people. In development, a spiral stair links a living room below to two bedrooms above, and the design was drawn in 3D and laser cut, allowing the layers of daily life to unfold vertically. Finally, thin slats let light and views pass through, and the 200 mm model presents a house resting lightly among the trees, suggesting that architecture need not conquer its site but can coexist with a forest in humility.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹屋宿舍-輕輕立於樹間的家
zh-Hant.body: 一座規劃中的宿舍，意味著一片樹林將被砍伐。這件作品從這個兩難出發，問的是如何在不改變基地、也不失去樹木的情況下建造宿舍。指導過程先引導學生詢問其他同學對宿舍的期待，讓使用者的聲音成為設計的起點，這些意見逐漸形塑出一棟供少數人居住的小屋。進入推演，螺旋梯連接下方的客廳與上方的兩間臥室，設計以三維繪製並雷射切割，讓生活的層次沿著垂直方向展開。最後，細板條讓光線與視線穿透，這個兩百公釐的模型呈現出一棟輕輕立於樹間的房子，提示建築不必征服基地，也可以謙遜地與樹林共存。

pins.title: Bamboo and Taichi
pins.description:
A flat pattern becomes cube models, a wearable piece and finally a double spiral of panels in a bamboo forest.

Models and render | Pattern-to-space study | Card, paint, digital render | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 竹與太極
zh-Hant.description:
一個平面圖樣化為立方體模型、可穿戴作品，最終成為竹林中的雙層螺旋板片裝置。

模型與渲染｜圖樣轉空間研究｜卡紙、顏料、數位渲染｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The spiral installation in a bamboo forest.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how a flat pattern could grow into a space. It also links the pattern to the slow, firm and soft moves of taichi.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，平面圖樣如何長成空間。它也把圖樣與太極緩慢、剛柔並濟的動作相連。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The pattern was broken into black and white blocks. Each part was studied for rhythm and overlap.
captions: Famous paintings used as references for the installation scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把圖樣拆解成黑白方塊。每個部分都分析了節奏與重疊。
captions: 作為裝置場景參考的名畫。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Three test models and a 6-unit cube turned the blocks into space. Diagrams traced how the parts overlap.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三個試作模型與一個6單位立方體把方塊轉為空間。圖解追蹤了構件如何重疊。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Colours and turns from the models became a double-layer spiral in a bamboo forest. It mixes firm and soft, light and dark.
captions: Wearing the model and testing it with body movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型中的色彩與轉折化為竹林中的雙層螺旋。它融合剛與柔、明與暗。
captions: 穿戴模型並以身體動作測試。

sections.heading: Bamboo and Taichi - A Double Spiral Grown from a Pattern
sections.body: The movements of taichi are slow and firm, balancing strength with softness. Starting from a flat pattern, the work asked how it might grow into space and how it could connect to the rhythm of taichi. The guidance first led the student to break the pattern into black and white blocks and analyse the rhythm and overlap of each part, so that the order of the surface was understood before anything was built. In development, three test models and a six-unit cube turned the blocks into space, while diagrams traced how the parts overlap, the flat pattern gradually gaining depth through repeated trials. Finally, the colours and turns from the models became a double-layer spiral set in a bamboo forest, where firm and soft, light and dark blend together, extending the breath of a pattern into a field one can circle and pass through, a place where the rhythm of the body finds its echo.

zh-Hant.heading: 竹與太極-從平面圖樣長出的雙層螺旋
zh-Hant.body: 太極的動作緩慢而堅定，剛柔並濟。這件作品從一幅平面圖樣出發，問的是它如何長成空間，又如何與太極的節奏相連。指導過程先引導學生把圖樣拆解成黑白方塊，逐一分析每個部分的節奏與重疊，讓平面的秩序先被看清。進入推演，三個試作模型與一個六單位立方體把方塊轉為空間，圖解則追蹤構件如何彼此重疊，平面在反覆的試驗中逐漸獲得深度。最後，模型中的色彩與轉折化為竹林中的雙層螺旋，剛與柔、明與暗在其中交融，讓一幅圖樣的呼吸延展成可以環繞與穿行的場域，也讓身體的韻律在空間裡找到回聲。

pins.title: Forms and Language
pins.description:
Brush strokes become white plastic strips, then word groups, then a whole field of spaces with gaps and shadows.

Model | Writing-to-form study | PVC boards, ABS plastic sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 形態與語言
zh-Hant.description:
筆觸化為白色塑膠條，再組成詞組，最終成為一片帶有空隙與陰影的空間群。

模型｜書寫轉形態研究｜PVC板、ABS塑膠條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A film about learning an alien language sparked the work. The student asked how shapes could be read like words.
captions: The film poster, brush sketches and desert-architecture photo that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於學習外星語言的電影啟發了這件作品。學生探問，形狀如何能像文字一樣被閱讀。
captions: 啟發本案的電影海報、筆觸草圖與沙漠建築照片。
由筆觸而來的線條研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: In running script, solid lines show where the brush touches down and dashed lines where it lifts. Old wall-like forms seen on a trip added white lines.
captions: Copies of running-script calligraphy studied for brush touch-down and lift.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 在行書中，實線代表筆觸落下，虛線代表筆鋒提起。旅途中看到的古老牆體形態也加入成白色線條。
captions: 臨摹行書書法，研究落筆與提筆。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Lines 1 mm apart were drawn on card, then traced with 1 mm plastic strips. Units were joined into word groups, then into passages.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生在卡紙上畫出間距1公釐的線，再以1公釐塑膠條描出。單元組成詞組，再組成段落。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 590 mm model leaves blank spaces and shadows. They stand for what is unspoken, for metaphor and for guesswork.
captions: A low view of the field.
The field from the other side.
A close view of the upper strips.
A close view of the lower strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個590公釐的模型留下了空白與陰影。它們代表未說出口的話、隱喻與推測。

sections.heading: Forms and Language - The Blank Between Brush and Lift
sections.body: A film about learning an alien language led the student to wonder whether shapes could be read like words. Starting from that question, the work searched for a grammar shared by writing and space. The guidance first led the student to study running script, marking with solid lines where the brush touches down and with dashed lines where it lifts, and then to add, as white lines, the ancient wall-like forms seen on a trip, weaving the breath of calligraphy with the memory of walls. In development, lines 1 mm apart were drawn on card and patiently traced with 1 mm plastic strips; units joined into word groups and word groups into passages, so the form grew step by step into a readable text. Finally, the 590 mm model leaves blank spaces and shadows that stand for the unspoken, for metaphor and for guesswork, letting silence itself become part of the language.

zh-Hant.heading: 形態與語言-筆鋒起落之間的空白
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於學習外星語言的電影，讓學生開始思考形狀能否像文字一樣被閱讀。這件作品從這個問題出發，在書寫與空間之間尋找共通的文法。指導過程先引導學生研究行書，以實線標示筆觸落下之處，以虛線標示筆鋒提起之處，再把旅途中看到的古老牆體形態加入成白色線條，讓書法的呼吸與牆的記憶交織。進入推演，學生在卡紙上畫出間距一公釐的線，再以一公釐塑膠條細細描出，單元組成詞組，詞組再組成段落，形體逐步長成一篇可讀的文字。最後，這個五百九十公釐的模型留下了空白與陰影，代表未說出口的話、隱喻與推測，讓沉默本身也成為語言的一部分。

pins.title: Space of Hidden Clues
pins.description:
Wire grid cages, shiny film shards and a heap of sticks build one mystery space full of hidden clues.

Model | Story-to-space study | PVC boards, wooden sticks, colour-shift window film, wire, card, clay, mesh | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 藏著線索的空間
zh-Hant.description:
鐵絲網格籠、閃亮的薄膜碎片與一堆木條，構成一個藏滿線索的神秘空間。

模型｜故事轉空間研究｜PVC板、木條、變色窗膜、鐵絲、卡紙、黏土、網布｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wire grid and stick tower.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves making up detective stories. The project asks how a space could hold clues and feelings like a story does.
captions: A sketch of the parts of the story.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生喜歡自己編偵探故事。這個專題探問，空間如何能像故事一樣藏著線索與情感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each character got a material. Clear film stood for hope, clay for a struggle and wood for chaos at the base.
captions: The detective story collage of characters and clues behind each space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個角色都對應一種材料。透明薄膜代表希望，黏土代表掙扎，底部的木條代表混亂。
captions: 每個空間背後的偵探故事角色與線索拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Grid cages hold the shards above a heap of sticks. Clues are hidden in corners for the viewer to find.
captions: Building the wire cages and stick base by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 網格籠把碎片托在木條堆上方。線索藏在角落，等待觀者發現。
captions: 親手製作鐵絲網籠與木棒基座。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 550 mm model mixes fear, warmth and sadness in one space. It reads as a puzzle to be solved.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個550公釐的模型在同一空間中混合了恐懼、溫暖與悲傷。它像一道待解的謎題。

sections.heading: Space of Hidden Clues - A Detective Story Written in Materials
sections.body: The charm of a detective story lies in clues hidden in unnoticed corners. Starting from the student's love of inventing detective stories, the work asked whether a space could hold clues and feelings the way a story does. The guidance first led the student to give each character a matching material: clear film for hope, clay for struggle, and the sticks at the base for chaos, so that the narrative was first translated into a language of materials. In development, grid cages hold the shards above a heap of sticks, and clues are placed in corners for viewers to find on their own, turning the act of reading the model into the act of solving a case. Finally, the 550 mm model mixes fear, warmth and sadness in a single space and reads as a puzzle waiting to be solved, suggesting that space can be not only looked at but reasoned through and decoded.

zh-Hant.heading: 藏著線索的空間-以材料書寫的偵探故事
zh-Hant.body: 偵探故事的魅力，在於線索總是藏在不經意的角落。這件作品從學生自己編寫偵探故事的喜好出發，問的是空間能否像故事一樣藏著線索與情感。指導過程先引導學生為每個角色找到對應的材料：透明薄膜代表希望，黏土代表掙扎，底部的木條代表混亂，讓敘事先轉為材質的語言。進入推演，網格籠把碎片托在木條堆上方，線索被安放在角落，等待觀者自己發現，閱讀模型的過程也就成了破案的過程。最後，這個五百五十公釐的模型在同一空間中混合了恐懼、溫暖與悲傷，像一道待解的謎題，提示空間不只被觀看，也可以被推理與解讀。

pins.title: Fragmented Mirror
pins.description:
Like a twisting mirror puzzle cube, a daily living space is broken into mirror panels and then into a knot of upside-down stairs.

Models and drawing | Order-in-chaos study | PVC boards, reflective paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 破碎的鏡子
zh-Hant.description:
如同轉動的鏡面魔術方塊，日常生活空間被打碎成鏡面板片，再化為一團上下顛倒的樓梯。

模型與繪圖｜混亂中的秩序研究｜PVC板、反光紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A mirror puzzle cube looks wild after every turn, yet it follows clear rules. The project asks if a home could be broken up the same way.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 鏡面魔術方塊每轉一次都顯得雜亂，卻遵循清楚的規則。這個專題探問，住家能否以同樣的方式被打散。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student took phone photos of rooms used every day. They were cut and pieced into odd shapes.
captions: An artist's impossible-stair print and film poster that inspired the maze.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生用手機拍下每天使用的房間。照片被剪開，再拼成不規則形狀。
captions: 啟發這座迷宮的藝術家不可能階梯版畫與電影海報。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Part 1 built the fragments as mirror panels that reflect one another. Part 2 turned them into rooms and stairs facing every way.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一部分把碎片做成彼此反射的鏡面板片。第二部分再把它們化為朝向各方的房間與樓梯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 350 mm model is an upside-down knot of stairs. It shows a hidden order inside chaos.
captions: Holding the inverted stair model in both hands.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個350公釐的模型是一團上下顛倒的樓梯。它呈現出混亂之中的隱藏秩序。
captions: 雙手捧著倒置階梯模型。

sections.heading: Fragmented Mirror - The Hidden Order Within Chaos
sections.body: A mirror puzzle cube looks wild after every turn, yet it always follows clear rules. Starting from this order disguised as disorder, the work asked whether a home could be broken apart and reassembled in the same way. The guidance first led the student to photograph the rooms used every day with a phone, then cut the photos and piece them into irregular shapes, letting the familiar fracture first on a flat surface. In development, the first part built the fragments as mirror panels reflecting one another, and the second turned them into rooms and stairs facing every direction, so that up and down dissolve between reflection and inversion. Finally, the 350 mm model becomes an upside-down knot of stairs; it looks like a maze, yet it lets viewers recognise a hidden order inside the chaos and see another way a home might be composed.

zh-Hant.heading: 破碎的鏡子-混亂中的隱藏秩序
zh-Hant.body: 鏡面魔術方塊每轉一次都顯得雜亂，卻始終遵循清楚的規則。這件作品從這種看似失序的秩序出發，問的是住家能否以同樣的方式被打散再重組。指導過程先引導學生用手機拍下每天使用的房間，再把照片剪開、拼成不規則的形狀，讓熟悉的日常先在平面上碎裂。進入推演，第一部分把碎片做成彼此反射的鏡面板片，第二部分再把它們化為朝向各方的房間與樓梯，空間在反射與翻轉之間失去了上下之分。最後，這個三百五十公釐的模型成為一團上下顛倒的樓梯，看似迷宮，卻讓觀者在混亂之中辨認出隱藏的秩序，也重新看見家的另一種組成方式。

pins.title: The Trajectories of the Cosmos
pins.description:
Planet orbits drawn on paper are stacked into a turning tower of rings, stairs and stick walls.

Model and drawings | Orbit-to-form study | PVC boards, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 宇宙的軌跡
zh-Hant.description:
畫在紙上的行星軌道被疊成一座由圓環、樓梯與木條牆組成的旋轉塔。

模型與繪圖｜軌道轉形態研究｜PVC板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wants to imagine homes beyond the Earth. The project asks what a place to live in outer space could look like.
captions: A first sketch of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想像地球之外的家。這個專題探問，外太空的居所會是什麼樣子。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each planet moves at its own speed, so their places change every moment. The orbit curves were drawn and laid over one another.
captions: Solar-system orbit charts used as the starting point for the rings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每顆行星以自己的速度運行，位置時時改變。學生畫出軌道曲線並互相疊合。
captions: 作為環形起點的太陽系軌道圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stick walls follow the outer orbits. Rings and stairs rise inside them and turn as they climb.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條牆沿著外圈軌道排列。圓環與樓梯在其中升起，一邊攀升一邊旋轉。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 450 mm tower feels like an ancient tower that reaches for the sky. It joins science and art.
captions: A pen drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座450公釐的塔，像一座伸向天空的古老高塔。它結合了科學與藝術。

sections.heading: Trajectories of the Cosmos - An Orbital Tower Climbing Skyward
sections.body: A home beyond the Earth is one of humanity's oldest and most distant dreams. Starting from the student's curiosity about dwelling in outer space, the work asked what a home might look like once it is no longer fixed to a single planet. The guidance first led the student to observe planetary motion: each planet travels at its own speed, its position changing every moment, so the student drew the orbit curves and laid them over one another, turning celestial rhythm into a readable drawing. In development, stick walls follow the outer orbits while rings and stairs rise within them, turning as they climb, so that an orbit becomes not just a line but a path one can walk. Finally, the 450 mm tower stands like an ancient tower reaching for the sky, a single form in which the precision of science meets the imagination of art.

zh-Hant.heading: 宇宙的軌跡-向天空攀升的軌道之塔
zh-Hant.body: 地球之外的家，是人類最古老也最遙遠的想像之一。這件作品從學生對外太空居所的好奇出發，問的是當家不再固定於一顆星球，它會是什麼樣子。指導過程先引導學生觀察行星的運行，每顆行星以自己的速度前進，位置時時改變，於是學生畫出軌道曲線並讓它們彼此疊合，把天體的節奏轉為可以閱讀的圖。進入推演，木條牆沿著外圈軌道排列，圓環與樓梯在其中升起，一邊攀升一邊旋轉，軌道不再只是線，而成為可以行走的路徑。最後，這座四百五十公釐的塔像一座伸向天空的古老高塔，讓科學的精確與藝術的想像在同一個形體中相遇。

pins.title: Marine Habitat
pins.description:
A woven bamboo frame grows moss and vines and holds woven pods, as a habitat unit for a future at sea.

Model | Ecological habitat study | Bamboo weaving, moss, vines, tissue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 海洋棲地
zh-Hant.description:
一個竹編框架長著苔蘚與藤蔓，並托著編織的球體，作為未來海上生活的棲地單元。

模型｜生態棲地研究｜竹編、苔蘚、藤蔓、紙巾｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Land is scarce and sea levels are rising. The project asks if homes could move out onto the ocean.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 土地稀少，海平面不斷上升。這個專題探問，家園能否移到海上。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student imagined platforms made of separate living units. Each one would grow, spread and decay like a living thing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生想像由獨立生態單元組成的平台。每個單元都會像生物一樣生長、繁衍與衰敗。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bamboo was chosen as the frame for its strength and low impact. Moss and plants grow on it.
captions: Placing the bamboo pods and moss into the frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生選用竹子作為框架，因為它強韌且對環境影響小。苔蘚與植物生長其上。
captions: 親手將竹編球與苔蘚放入框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 650 mm model has a ground level for land life. Above it, poles give birds a place to rest.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個650公釐的模型底層供陸地生物棲息。上方的竹桿則提供鳥類停歇之處。

sections.heading: A Home Drifting Seaward - Bamboo Platforms That Grow
sections.body: When land grows scarce and sea levels keep rising, dwelling is no longer only a matter of architecture but of how we imagine survival. Starting from that reality, the work asked whether homes could move out onto the ocean. The guidance first led the student to imagine architecture as a living thing, proposing platforms made of separate living units that would each grow, spread and decay like an organism, so that time and change became premises of the design. In development, bamboo was chosen as the frame for its strength and low impact, with moss and plants growing upon it. Finally, the 650 mm model offers a ground level for land life, while poles above give birds a place to rest. What the work describes is not a city owned by humans alone, but a floating ecology shared with other species, gently redrawing the boundary of what a home can be.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂向海洋的家-會生長的竹之平台
zh-Hant.body: 當土地日漸稀少、海平面不斷上升，居住的問題便不再只是建築，而是生存的想像。這件作品從這樣的現實出發，問的是家園能否移到海上。指導過程先引導學生把建築想像為生命，構思由獨立生態單元組成的平台，每個單元都會像生物一樣生長、繁衍與衰敗，讓時間與變化成為設計的前提。進入推演，學生選用竹子作為框架，看重它的強韌與低環境影響，苔蘚與植物則生長其上。最後，六百五十公釐的模型以底層供陸地生物棲息，上方的竹桿提供鳥類停歇之處。作品描繪的不是一座人類獨佔的城市，而是一個與其他物種共享的漂浮生態，溫和地重新定義了家的邊界。

pins.title: Butterfly-Wing Shade Pavilion
pins.description:
Wing-like panels of colour-shift film on a frame of sticks give shade and coloured light in a sunny garden.

Model and digital study | Pavilion design | PVC boards, wooden sticks, colour-shift window film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 蝶翼遮蔭亭
zh-Hant.description:
以木條為骨架、覆以變色窗膜的翼狀板片，為陽光強烈的花園帶來遮蔭與彩色光影。

模型與數位研究｜涼亭設計｜PVC板、木條、變色窗膜｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In a community garden the student visited, strong sun hit the ground and there was no shade. The project asks for a place to rest and play.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生造訪的一座社區花園裡，烈日直射地面，沒有任何遮蔭。這個專題要提供一個休息與遊玩的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Butterfly wings gave the forms. Early digital and site models tested folded wing shapes among trees.
captions: Photos of the garden site and surrounding buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 蝴蝶的翅膀提供了形態。早期的數位與基地模型在樹間測試折疊的翼形。
captions: 花園基地與周邊建築的照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks form light arches. Colour-shift film fills the triangles so the light changes as you move.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條構成輕盈的拱。變色窗膜填滿三角形，讓光線隨人移動而變化。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 450 mm model casts strong light and shadow. It makes a cooler, lively place for people to stay.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個450公釐的模型投下強烈的光影。它創造出一個更涼爽、更有活力的停留空間。

sections.heading: Borrowed Wings - A Patch of Shade Under the Sun
sections.body: In a garden under direct sun, a patch of shade is a kind of generosity. Starting from the student's visit to a community garden with no shade at all, the work asked how to offer a place to rest and play. The guidance first led the student to borrow form from nature, taking butterfly wings as the source and testing folded wing shapes among the trees through early digital and site models, so that the design answered to a real place. In development, sticks formed light arches and colour-shift film filled the triangles, making the light change as people move, so that shade also became an experience. Finally, the 450 mm model casts strong light and shadow, creating a cooler and livelier place to stay. The work turns an everyday discomfort into a public gift, letting architecture rest lightly over people like a pair of wings.

zh-Hant.heading: 借來的翅膀-烈日下的一片蔭
zh-Hant.body: 在烈日直射的花園裡，一片陰影就是一種慷慨。這件作品從學生造訪一座社區花園的觀察出發，那裡沒有任何遮蔭，問的是如何提供一個休息與遊玩的地方。指導過程先引導學生向自然借形，以蝴蝶的翅膀作為形態來源，並透過早期的數位與基地模型在樹間測試折疊的翼形，讓設計回應真實的場地。進入推演，木條構成輕盈的拱，變色窗膜填滿三角形，光線因此隨人移動而變化，遮蔭也成為一種體驗。最後，四百五十公釐的模型投下強烈的光影，創造出更涼爽、更有活力的停留空間。作品把一個日常的不便轉化為公共的禮物，讓建築像翅膀一樣，輕輕覆在人們頭上。

pins.title: Sword Paths
pins.description:
Short plastic strips glued into twisting stairs trace the path of a sword through a match.

Model | Movement-to-form study | Plastic sticks, cardboard, foam board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 劍的軌跡
zh-Hant.description:
短塑膠條黏成扭轉的階梯，描出比賽中劍的軌跡。

模型｜動作轉形態研究｜塑膠條、卡紙、泡棉板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student does sabre fencing as a hobby. The project asks how the moves and plans of a match could be shown in 3D.
captions: Motion frames of a sword swing.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生的嗜好是軍刀擊劍。這個專題探問，比賽中的動作與策略如何以立體方式呈現。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Motion frames showed how the blade sweeps in arcs. Early loops tested how a strip could follow that sweep.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 分格影像顯示劍身如何以弧線掃過。早期的環形試驗測試塑膠條如何跟隨這道軌跡。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Strips were cut to set lengths and glued into stair shapes, the cross pieces standing for the sword and the long sides for its path. Each stair was then twisted to match a move.
captions: The tower on a strip base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠條被裁成固定長度，黏成階梯形狀，短橫條代表劍，兩側長條代表它的軌跡。每段階梯再依動作扭轉。
captions: 立在塑膠條底座上的塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 30-inch model is a light web of arcs and shadows. It reads like a frozen match.
captions: A close view of the strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這件30英寸長的模型是一張由弧線與陰影組成的輕盈網。它就像一場被凍結的比賽。

sections.heading: Arcs of the Blade - A Match Held Still
sections.body: A moment in fencing is too fast to see; all that remains is the arc a blade traces through the air. Starting from the student's hobby of sabre fencing, the work asked whether the moves and plans of a match could be shown in three dimensions. The guidance first led the student to analyse motion frames of the blade's sweep, then to test with early loops whether a strip could follow that path, so that speed was taken apart into shapes that could be studied. In development, strips were cut to set lengths and glued into stair shapes, the cross pieces standing for the sword and the long sides for its path, and each stair was twisted to match a move, writing tactics into structure. Finally, the 30-inch model becomes a light web of arcs and shadows, like a match held still. The work lets viewers see speed again within stillness, along with the thinking behind every strike.

zh-Hant.heading: 劍的弧線-凍結的一場比賽
zh-Hant.body: 擊劍的一瞬間快得看不見，留下的只有空氣中劍身劃過的弧。這件作品從學生的軍刀擊劍嗜好出發，問的是比賽中的動作與策略能否以立體方式呈現。指導過程先引導學生以分格影像分析劍身如何掃過，再以早期的環形試驗測試塑膠條能否跟隨這道軌跡，讓速度被拆解為可以研究的形狀。進入推演，塑膠條被裁成固定長度，黏成階梯形狀，短橫條代表劍，兩側長條代表軌跡，每段階梯再依動作扭轉，戰術因此被寫入結構。最後，三十英寸長的模型成為一張由弧線與陰影組成的輕盈網，像一場被凍結的比賽。作品讓觀者在靜止中重新看見速度，也看見每一次出劍背後的思考。

pins.title: Time-Loop Tower
pins.description:
Coloured cubes, clay forms and wire cages climb a spiral tower, each level holding one key moment of a looping story.

Model | Story-to-space study | Wooden sticks, PVC board, foam, clay, metal strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 時間迴圈之塔
zh-Hant.description:
彩色方塊、黏土形體與鐵絲籠沿著螺旋塔攀升，每一層承載一段迴圈故事中的關鍵時刻。

模型｜故事轉空間研究｜木條、PVC板、泡棉、黏土、金屬條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student turned a favourite animated story about time loops into space. The project asks how a plot can become a model.
captions: An annotated sketch of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生把一部喜愛的時間迴圈動畫故事轉化為空間。這個專題探問，情節如何變成模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Key events were sorted into five groups. Each group got its own mood, theme and material.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 關鍵事件被分成五組。每一組都有自己的情緒、主題與材料。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wire spirals and black cages link the levels. Bright foam cubes break apart near the top as the loop collapses.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲螺旋與黑色籠子串起各層。鮮豔的泡棉方塊在頂部散開，象徵迴圈崩解。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 31.5-inch tower ends in paper birds that fly off the top. It shows lost time being won back.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座31.5英寸高的塔，頂端以飛離的紙鳥作結。它呈現失去的時間被重新奪回。

sections.heading: The Loop Collapses - Winning Back Lost Time
sections.body: A time loop is both a predicament and a structure: the same days return again and again until a crack appears. Starting from an animated story about time loops that the student loves, the work asked how a plot could become a model. The guidance first led the student to sort the key events into five groups and give each its own mood, theme and material, so that narrative was translated into layers that could be stacked. In development, wire spirals and black cages link the levels, while bright foam cubes break apart near the top, standing for the collapse of the loop. Finally, the 31.5-inch tower ends in paper birds flying off its summit, showing lost time being won back. The work lets the vertical become the direction of time; reading from bottom to top, viewers follow the story as it breaks free of repetition and finally arrives at freedom.

zh-Hant.heading: 迴圈的崩解-奪回失去的時間
zh-Hant.body: 時間迴圈是一種困境，也是一種結構：同樣的日子不斷重來，直到某個裂縫出現。這件作品從學生喜愛的一部時間迴圈動畫故事出發，問的是情節如何成為模型。指導過程先引導學生把關鍵事件分成五組，為每一組設定情緒、主題與材料，讓敘事被轉譯為可以堆疊的層次。進入推演，鐵絲螺旋與黑色籠子串起各層，鮮豔的泡棉方塊在頂部散開，象徵迴圈的崩解。最後，三十一點五英寸的塔以飛離頂端的紙鳥作結，呈現失去的時間被重新奪回。作品讓垂直成為時間的方向，觀者由下而上閱讀，就像跟隨故事一路掙脫重複，最終抵達自由。

pins.title: Engawa House
pins.description:
White board rooms joined by a wooden veranda rebuild the open, linked layout of a traditional Japanese house.

Model and drawings | House study | Wooden sticks, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 緣側之家
zh-Hant.description:
以木製緣側串連的白色板材房間，重建傳統日式住宅開放而相連的格局。

模型與繪圖｜住宅研究｜木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves the structure of traditional Japanese houses. The project asks how their open, linked rooms could be rebuilt in a model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生喜愛傳統日式住宅的結構。這個專題探問，如何在模型中重建它們開放而相連的房間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The engawa is a veranda that links all the rooms. By day it opens to the outside; at night panels close it in.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 緣側是一條串起所有房間的廊道。白天它向外敞開，夜晚則以板門圍入室內。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: PVC boards of many sizes make the rooms. Wooden slats form the veranda, stairs and screens.
captions: A pen sketch of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同尺寸的PVC板構成房間。木條則形成緣側、樓梯與格柵。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 30-inch model is a semi-open cluster of rooms. Light falls through it as in a real house.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這件30英寸長的模型是一組半開放的房間群。光線如同在真實住宅中一般穿透其間。

sections.heading: The Time of the Engawa - A Veranda That Opens by Day
sections.body: The beauty of a Japanese house lies not in its walls but in the fact that the walls can open. Starting from the student's love for the structure of traditional Japanese houses, the work asked how their open, linked rooms could be rebuilt in a model. The guidance first led the student to study the engawa, the veranda that joins every room, understanding its double character of opening to the outside by day and closing behind panels at night, so that time became part of the space. In development, PVC boards of many sizes formed the rooms while wooden slats made the veranda, stairs and screens, clearly dividing the solid from the open. Finally, the 30-inch model becomes a semi-open cluster of rooms, light passing through it as in a real house. The work restates a philosophy of dwelling: a boundary is not a separation but a relationship that breathes with day and night.

zh-Hant.heading: 緣側的時間-晝開夜合的廊
zh-Hant.body: 日式住宅的美，不在於牆，而在於牆可以被打開。這件作品從學生對傳統日式住宅結構的喜愛出發，問的是那些開放而相連的房間如何在模型中重建。指導過程先引導學生研究緣側這條串起所有房間的廊道，理解它白天向外敞開、夜晚以板門圍入室內的雙重性格，讓時間成為空間的一部分。進入推演，不同尺寸的PVC板構成房間，木條形成緣側、樓梯與格柵，實與虛被清楚分配。最後，三十英寸長的模型成為一組半開放的房間群，光線如同在真實住宅中一般穿透其間。作品重新闡述了一種居住哲學：邊界不是隔絕，而是可以隨日夜呼吸的關係。

pins.title: Branch and Cage Tower
pins.description:
A dense field of sticks holds up a tangle of open cubes, bent bamboo and branches, a tower about what we forget in daily life.

Model and drawings | Film-to-form study | Wooden sticks, branches, bamboo | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 枝條與籠之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一片密集的木條撐起一團開放方框、彎曲竹片與枝條，這座塔關於我們在日常中遺忘的事物。

模型與繪圖｜影像轉形態研究｜木條、枝條、竹子｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The model grew from a short surreal film the student made. It asks how people get trapped chasing money and forget simple joys.
captions: A line drawing of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件模型源自學生拍攝的一部超現實短片。它探問人們如何在追逐金錢中受困，並遺忘簡單的快樂。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A round cage stands for being trapped. A ring around it stands for the parts of life people overlook.
captions: A line drawing of the cage and ring.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圓形的籠子代表受困。環繞它的圓環代表人們忽略的生活面向。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks were bundled, then packed into a dense field. Open cubes and bent strips rise from it, mixed with real branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條先被綁成束，再密集排列成一片。開放的方框與彎曲條片由此升起，並混入真實枝條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 31.5-inch tower joins man-made and natural parts. It mixes the real and the surreal.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座31.5英寸高的塔結合了人造與自然的構件。它融合了真實與超現實。

sections.heading: Cage and Branch - The Simple Joys We Forget
sections.body: In chasing money, people often fail to notice that they are walking into a cage. Growing out of a short surreal film the student made, the work asked how people become trapped in that pursuit and forget simple joys. The guidance first led the student to find symbols for the concept: a round cage for being trapped, and a ring around it for the parts of life people overlook, so that narrative was turned into spatial relationship. In development, sticks were bundled and then packed into a dense field, from which open cubes and bent strips rise, mixed with real branches, so that the made and the natural begin to interweave. Finally, the 31.5-inch tower joins man-made and natural parts, blending the real and the surreal. The work reads like a fable in three dimensions, letting viewers glimpse branches within a dense order and recall the things still growing outside the cage.

zh-Hant.heading: 籠與枝-被遺忘的簡單快樂
zh-Hant.body: 人們追逐金錢時，常常沒有察覺自己正走進一座籠子。這件作品源自學生拍攝的一部超現實短片，問的是人如何在追逐中受困，並遺忘簡單的快樂。指導過程先引導學生為概念尋找符號：圓形的籠子代表受困，環繞它的圓環則代表被忽略的生活面向，敘事因此轉為空間的關係。進入推演，木條先被綁成束，再密集排列成一片，開放的方框與彎曲條片由此升起，真實的枝條混入其中，人工與自然開始交錯。最後，三十一點五英寸的塔結合人造與自然的構件，融合真實與超現實。作品像一則立體的寓言，讓觀者在密集的秩序中瞥見枝條，想起那些仍在籠外生長的事物。

pins.title: Pulled Threads
pins.description:
A black frame box is filled with a dense web of pulled threads and sharp shards, a space about feeling trapped and tense.

Model and drawings | Feeling-to-space study | Wood, nylon rope, panes, rice paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 緊繃的線
zh-Hant.description:
黑色框架盒內布滿拉緊的細線與尖銳碎片，構成一個關於受困與緊繃感的空間。

模型與繪圖｜情感轉空間研究｜木材、尼龍繩、薄片、宣紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted to give form to a feeling of being trapped. The project asks how a space can make people feel how hard it is to break free.
captions: A drawing of trapped paper planes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生想為受困的感受賦予形體。這個專題探問，空間如何讓人感受到掙脫有多困難。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Pencil drawings explored a core caught in the middle. Other sketches showed forms pulled by many lines.
captions: A drawing of a framed core.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 鉛筆素描探索被困在中央的核心。其他草圖則描繪被許多線拉扯的形體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Threads were stretched across a frame in all directions. A small bound space sits inside the web.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 細線從各個方向拉過框架。一個被綁住的小空間位於網的中央。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 21.6-inch box is a maze of lines. Sharp shards point inward and the threads are pulled until they snap.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個21.6英寸的盒子是一座線的迷宮。尖銳碎片指向內部，細線被拉緊直到斷裂。

sections.heading: The Tension of Escape - A Core Bound by Threads
sections.body: Being trapped is not a state but a force that keeps pulling. Starting from the student's wish to give form to the feeling of being trapped, the work asked how a space could make people sense how hard it is to break free. The guidance first led the student to explore, in pencil, a core caught in the middle, and then forms pulled by many lines, so that an abstract emotion gradually gained direction and strength. In development, threads were stretched across a frame from every direction, with a small bound space at the centre of the web, and tension itself became the structure. Finally, the 21.6-inch box becomes a maze of lines, sharp shards pointing inward and threads drawn tight until they snap. The work offers no exit; it simply lets viewers gaze at lines stretched to their limit and feel, between strain and rupture, the longest moment before escape.

zh-Hant.heading: 掙脫的張力-被線綁住的核心
zh-Hant.body: 受困不是一個狀態，而是一種持續被拉扯的力。這件作品從學生想為受困感受賦予形體出發，問的是空間如何讓人體會掙脫有多困難。指導過程先引導學生以鉛筆素描探索被困在中央的核心，再描繪被許多線拉扯的形體，讓抽象的情緒逐步獲得方向與力度。進入推演，細線從各個方向拉過框架，一個被綁住的小空間位於網的中央，張力因此成為結構本身。最後，二十一點六英寸的盒子成為一座線的迷宮，尖銳碎片指向內部，細線被拉緊直到斷裂。作品不提供出口，只讓觀者凝視那些繃到極限的線，在緊張與斷裂之間，感受掙脫之前最漫長的一刻。

pins.title: Knotted Cylinders
pins.description:
One cylinder is bent, knotted and stacked step by step in 3D software into a soft white knot.

Digital model | Object-and-action study | 3D modelling, rendering | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 打結的圓柱
zh-Hant.description:
一根圓柱在3D軟體中一步步彎曲、打結與堆疊，成為柔和的白色繩結。

數位模型｜物件與動作研究｜3D建模、算圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In a summer online course, the student learned 3D modelling, animation and rendering. The task joins one object with one action.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在一門暑期線上課程中，學生學習了3D建模、動畫與算圖。題目是把一個物件與一個動作結合。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The object is a cylinder and the action is stacking. Each step bends and loops it further.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 物件是圓柱，動作是堆疊。每一步都讓它進一步彎曲與繞圈。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rotation drawings turn the knot around its axes. Section drawings cut through it to show the tubes inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 旋轉圖讓繩結繞著軸線轉動。剖面圖則切開它，呈現內部的管狀結構。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final 10-inch knot is shown in close renders. A line view maps the logic of its surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終10英寸的繩結以近距離算圖呈現。線框圖則描繪出它表面的邏輯。

sections.heading: The Making of an Action - How a Cylinder Learns to Knot
sections.body: Form is often not designed so much as generated by an action applied again and again. Arising from a summer online course in which the task was to join one object with one action, the work took a cylinder as the object and stacking as the action. The guidance first led the student to break the action into steps, each one bending and looping the cylinder further, so that the rules of operation stayed clear while the result remained hard to predict. In development, rotation drawings turned the knot around its axes and section drawings cut through it to reveal the tubes inside, allowing outside and inside to be read together. Finally, the 10-inch knot is presented in close renders, and a line view maps the logic of its surface. The work condenses the learning of modelling, animation and rendering into one proposition about process: complexity is often simple rules, patiently repeated.

zh-Hant.heading: 一個動作的生成-圓柱如何打結
zh-Hant.body: 形式往往不是被設計出來的，而是由一個動作反覆施加後生成的。這件作品來自一門暑期線上課程，題目是把一個物件與一個動作結合：物件是圓柱，動作是堆疊。指導過程先引導學生把動作拆解為步驟，每一步都讓圓柱進一步彎曲與繞圈，讓操作的規則清楚可循，結果卻難以預料。進入推演，旋轉圖讓繩結繞著軸線轉動，剖面圖則切開它，呈現內部的管狀結構，外與內被同時閱讀。最後，十英寸的繩結以近距離算圖呈現，線框圖描繪出它表面的邏輯。作品把建模、動畫與算圖的學習，凝縮為一個關於過程的命題：複雜，常常只是簡單規則被耐心重複後的樣子。

pins.title: Castle of White Gables
pins.description:
Small card houses with steep gables, arched windows and a cone spire are stacked into one dream castle.

Model | Castle study | Card paper, PVC board, clay, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 白色山牆城堡
zh-Hant.description:
帶有陡峭山牆、拱窗與圓錐尖塔的小卡紙房屋，層層堆疊成一座夢想城堡。

模型｜城堡研究｜卡紙、PVC板、黏土、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Since childhood the student has dreamed of living in a magic castle from the films. The project asks how that dream could be built by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生從小就夢想住進電影中的魔法城堡。這個專題探問，如何親手把這個夢想蓋出來。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Old European towns and castles gave the steep roofs, arched windows and towers. The student picked parts that share one look.
captions: The film-castle collage that inspired the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 歐洲古城與城堡提供了陡峭屋頂、拱窗與塔樓。學生挑選出風格一致的構件。
captions: 啟發這座模型的電影城堡拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each building was cut from board as its own piece. The pieces were then stacked and layered to form the castle.
captions: Cutting and assembling the card houses by hand.
Interior scenes furnished with themed toy figures and wallpaper.
A hall with a cone spire.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每棟建築都以板材單獨裁出。這些構件再層層堆疊，組成城堡。
captions: 親手裁切並組裝卡紙小屋。
以主題玩偶與壁紙佈置的室內場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 19.6-inch castle mixes many styles into one whole. Inside, small rooms catch light through tall arched windows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座19.6英寸的城堡把多種風格融為一體。內部的小房間透過高大的拱窗引入光線。

sections.heading: A Childhood Castle - A Dream Stacked by Hand
sections.body: Everyone carries a castle inside, built from childhood imagination and rarely given the chance to be made real. Starting from the magic castle the student has dreamed of living in since childhood, the work asked how that dream could be built by hand. The guidance first led the student to read an architectural vocabulary from old European towns and castles, identifying steep roofs, arched windows and towers one by one, and then to select parts that share a single look, giving fantasy an order to follow. In development, each building was cut from board as its own piece and the pieces were stacked and layered, so that the castle took shape through assembly. Finally, the 19.6-inch castle blends many styles into one whole, and small rooms inside catch light through tall arched windows. The work shows that a dream is not an escape from reality, but a construction that asks for research, choice and patient layering.

zh-Hant.heading: 童年的城堡-親手堆疊的夢
zh-Hant.body: 每個人心中都有一座城堡，它由童年的想像建成，卻很少有機會被真正建造。這件作品從學生自小夢想住進的魔法城堡出發，問的是如何親手把這個夢蓋出來。指導過程先引導學生從歐洲古城與城堡中閱讀建築語彙，陡峭屋頂、拱窗與塔樓被逐一辨認，再挑選出風格一致的構件，讓幻想有了可以依循的秩序。進入推演，每棟建築以板材單獨裁出，再層層堆疊，城堡在組合中逐漸成形。最後，十九點六英寸的城堡把多種風格融為一體，內部的小房間透過高大的拱窗引入光線。作品說明夢想並非遠離現實的逃逸，而是一種需要研究、選擇與耐心堆疊的建造。

pins.title: Hanging Blocks
pins.description:
Dozens of small dark blocks hang on threads inside a tall wooden frame above a broken mirror floor.

Model and drawings | Words-and-feelings study | Polyethylene, wood, mirror | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 懸吊的方塊
zh-Hant.description:
數十個深色小方塊以細線懸吊在高大的木框中，下方是碎裂的鏡面地板。

模型與繪圖｜言語與情緒研究｜聚乙烯、木材、鏡子｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Online, people speak to one another in many tones. The project asks how words can pull on our feelings like gravity.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在網路上，人們以各種語氣彼此交談。這個專題探問，言語如何像重力一樣牽動我們的情緒。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings showed faces with many moods and cubes drifting in space. A net catching falling blocks became the key image.
captions: Concept sketch of falling figures above a headstone.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 素描描繪了帶著各種情緒的面孔，以及漂浮在空中的方塊。一張接住下落方塊的網成為關鍵意象。
captions: 墓碑上方墜落人形的概念素描。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Blocks were hung on threads at different heights. They thin out as they fall towards a cracked mirror.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 方塊以細線懸吊在不同高度。它們越往下越稀疏，落向碎裂的鏡面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 21.6-inch frame casts shifting shadows on the wall. The broken mirror doubles the falling blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個21.6英寸的框架在牆上投下變動的陰影。碎裂的鏡面讓下落的方塊加倍。

sections.heading: The Gravity of Words - Falling Blocks and a Broken Mirror
sections.body: A sentence online weighs nothing, yet it can pull feelings downward like gravity. Starting from the many tones in which people speak to one another online, the work asked how words tug at our emotions. The guidance first led the student to explore faces carrying different moods and cubes drifting in space through drawing, and from these to recognise a key image: a net catching falling blocks. In development, blocks were hung on threads at different heights, thinning out as they descend toward a cracked mirror, so that the fall acquired rhythm and direction. Finally, the 21.6-inch frame casts shifting shadows on the wall, and the broken mirror doubles the falling blocks. The work turns an invisible psychological impact into a visible physical state, letting viewers realise, within the fractured reflection, that every word may land on someone.

zh-Hant.heading: 言語的重力-下墜的方塊與碎鏡
zh-Hant.body: 網路上的一句話沒有重量，卻能像重力一樣把情緒往下拉。這件作品從人們在線上以各種語氣交談的現象出發，問的是言語如何牽動我們的感受。指導過程先引導學生以素描探索帶著不同情緒的面孔與漂浮的方塊，並從中辨認出關鍵意象：一張接住下落方塊的網。進入推演，方塊以細線懸吊在不同高度，越往下越稀疏，落向一面碎裂的鏡子，墜落因此有了節奏與方向。最後，二十一點六英寸的框架在牆上投下變動的陰影，碎鏡讓下落的方塊加倍。作品把看不見的心理衝擊轉為可見的物理狀態，讓觀者在破碎的倒影中，意識到每一句話都可能落在某個人身上。

pins.title: Remixed Terrain
pins.description:
Card terrain pieces traced from favourite game maps are joined into one landscape under a web of stick roofs.

Model and drawings | Map remix study | Card paper, wooden sticks, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重組的地形
zh-Hant.description:
從喜愛的遊戲地圖描出的卡紙地形塊，被拼合成一片覆著木條屋頂網的地景。

模型與繪圖｜地圖重組研究｜卡紙、木條、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student has played one game for years and loves its maps. The project asks how favourite spots from different maps could form one new place.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生玩一款遊戲多年，深愛它的地圖。這個專題探問，不同地圖中喜愛的角落如何組成一個新地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two favourite spots were picked from each of three maps. Their plans were traced inside a set rectangle.
captions: Title art of the shooter game whose maps were remixed.
A painting of a game map scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從三張地圖中各挑出兩個喜愛的角落。它們的平面被描繪在一個固定的矩形內。
captions: 被重組地圖的射擊遊戲標題圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The terrain was cut from card and joined into a new layout. Raised walls and stick frames add depth.
captions: Holding a cut terrain piece during testing.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 地形以卡紙裁出，拼合成新的配置。加高的牆與木條框架增添了深度。
captions: 測試時手持裁切好的地形構件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 23.6-inch model is a maze of walls under faceted roofs. A pen drawing shows how it feels to stand inside.
captions: A sniper scene staged in the model with a toy figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個23.6英寸的模型是一座覆著多面屋頂的牆體迷宮。一張鋼筆畫呈現站在其中的感受。
captions: 在模型中以玩偶佈置的狙擊場景。

sections.heading: Collage of Maps - A New Place Made of Game Memories
sections.body: A map played for years stops being a virtual setting and becomes a series of places the body remembers. Starting from a game the student has loved for a long time, the work asked whether favourite spots from different maps could come together as one new place. The guidance first led the student to make choices, picking two spots from each of three maps and tracing their plans inside a set rectangle, so that a constraint became the rule of recombination. In development, the terrain was cut from card and joined into a new layout, while raised walls and stick frames allowed the flat plan to grow depth. Finally, the 23.6-inch model becomes a maze of walls beneath faceted roofs, and a pen drawing conveys how it feels to stand inside. The work edits private memory into shared space, showing that a sense of place can be remixed and inhabited again within a new order.

zh-Hant.heading: 地圖的拼貼-遊戲記憶的新地方
zh-Hant.body: 一張地圖玩過多年，便不再只是虛擬的場景，而是一段段被身體記住的地方。這件作品從學生長年喜愛的一款遊戲出發，問的是不同地圖中的心愛角落能否組成一個新地方。指導過程先引導學生做出選擇，從三張地圖中各挑兩個角落，並把它們的平面描進一個固定的矩形，讓限制成為重組的規則。進入推演，地形以卡紙裁出，拼合成新的配置，加高的牆與木條框架則讓平面長出深度。最後，二十三點六英寸的模型成為一座覆著多面屋頂的牆體迷宮，一張鋼筆畫呈現站在其中的感受。作品把私人的記憶編輯成公共的空間，證明場所感可以被重新混合，並在新的秩序中再次被居住。

pins.title: In Silence
pins.description:
Layers of gauze catch projected light in a dark box, built from close study of light and shadow in a quiet room.

Installation and drawings | Light-and-shadow study | Projector, wood, gauze | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 靜默之中
zh-Hant.description:
數層紗布在暗箱中承接投影光線，源自對安靜房間中光影的細心觀察。

裝置與繪圖｜光影研究｜投影機、木材、紗布｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student wanted others to feel what a dim, quiet inner world is like. The project asks how light and space can share that feeling.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生希望讓別人感受到一個昏暗而安靜的內心世界。這個專題探問，光與空間如何傳達這種感受。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew the light and shadow in one room over time. Curtains, plants and a chair were recorded in pencil.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生長時間描繪同一個房間裡的光影。窗簾、植物與椅子都以鉛筆記錄下來。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Window shadows became the key pattern. Layers of gauze on wooden frames were set up to catch a projection.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 窗影成為關鍵圖樣。木框上的數層紗布被架起，用來承接投影。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 21.6-inch box glows with soft, blurred light. Each layer of gauze makes the image hazier.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個21.6英寸的箱體散發柔和而模糊的光。每一層紗布都讓影像更加朦朧。

sections.heading: A Dim Interior - Whispers of Gauze and Light
sections.body: Some feelings cannot be spoken; they can only be revealed by light. Starting from the student's wish to let others sense a dim and quiet inner world, the work asked whether light and space could carry such a feeling. The guidance first led the student to look at one room for a long time, recording in pencil how light and shadow shifted over curtains, plants and a chair, so that observation itself became a practice of stillness. In development, the shadow of the window was recognised as the key pattern, and layers of gauze were set on wooden frames to catch a projection, giving the space depth as well as distance. Finally, the 21.6-inch box glows with soft, blurred light, each layer of gauze making the image hazier. The work does not explain an emotion; it lets clarity recede layer by layer, so that viewers experience, within the blur, a quietness that turns inward.

zh-Hant.heading: 昏暗的內在-紗與光的低語
zh-Hant.body: 有些感受無法被說出，只能被光照見。這件作品從學生想讓他者理解一個昏暗而安靜的內心世界出發，問的是光與空間能否承載這種感受。指導過程先引導學生長時間凝視同一個房間，以鉛筆記錄窗簾、植物與椅子上光影的變化，讓觀察本身成為一種沉靜的練習。進入推演，窗影被辨認為關鍵圖樣，數層紗布被架在木框上承接投影，空間因此有了深度，也有了距離。最後，二十一點六英寸的箱體散發柔和而模糊的光，每一層紗布都讓影像更加朦朧。作品不解釋情緒，而是讓清晰逐層退去，使觀者在模糊之中，親身經歷一種向內收斂的安靜。

pins.title: Snooker Museum
pins.description:
The paths of snooker balls in one match are drawn in 2D, then raised into a landscape of straws, sticks and folded planes.

Model | Movement-to-space study | Card paper, foam, tracing paper, wooden sticks, recycled straws | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 司諾克博物館
zh-Hant.description:
一場比賽中司諾克球的路徑先以平面繪出，再升起成一片由吸管、木條與折板構成的地景。

模型｜動作轉空間研究｜卡紙、泡棉、描圖紙、木條、回收吸管｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Snooker is a sport the student plays well. Spin makes the white ball take varied, creative routes, and the project turns them into space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 司諾克是學生擅長的運動。旋轉讓母球走出多變而富創意的路線，這個專題把它們轉化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student traced every ball path in a classic match. Small tests tried different materials on the same paths.
captions: Photo of the two players from the classic match whose ball paths were traced.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描出一場經典比賽中每顆球的路徑。小型試驗在相同路徑上測試不同材料。
captions: 被描繪球路的經典賽事中兩位球員的照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Card, sticks and straws were built up along the paths. Recycled straws were used to cut plastic waste.
captions: A stick frame with blue cubes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 卡紙、木條與吸管沿著路徑堆起。學生使用回收吸管以減少塑膠垃圾。
captions: 帶藍色方塊的木條框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 31.5-inch model is a hazy field of straws under stick peaks. Light through the straws makes soft round shadows.
captions: Folded planes with a scale figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個31.5英寸的模型是一片位於木條尖峰下的朦朧吸管群。穿過吸管的光投下柔和的圓形陰影。

sections.heading: Paths of Spin - A Landscape Written by the Cue Ball
sections.body: On the green cloth of a snooker table, spin sends the white ball along countless unexpected routes, and every shot is a small invention of space. Starting from a sport the student plays well, the work asked whether those trajectories could become architecture. The guidance first led the student to trace every ball path in a classic match, then to run small tests of different materials along the same paths, so that a single trajectory revealed a different character in each substance. In development, card, sticks and straws were built up layer by layer along the paths, and the choice of recycled straws also answered a concern for cutting plastic waste. Finally, the 31.5-inch model becomes a hazy field of straws beneath stick peaks, and light passing through the straws casts soft round shadows. The work translates the calculation and intuition of a match into a landscape of light one could wander through.

zh-Hant.heading: 旋轉的路徑-母球寫下的地景
zh-Hant.body: 在司諾克的綠色檯面上，旋轉讓一顆白球走出無數條意料之外的路線，每一桿都是一次空間的發明。這件作品從學生擅長的這項運動出發，問的是那些軌跡能否成為建築。指導過程先引導學生描出一場經典比賽中每顆球的路徑，再以小型試驗在相同路徑上測試不同材料，讓同一條軌跡在不同物質中顯現不同性格。進入推演，卡紙、木條與吸管沿路徑層層堆起，回收吸管的選擇同時回應了減少塑膠垃圾的意識。最後，三十一點五英寸的模型成為一片位於木條尖峰下的朦朧吸管群，穿過吸管的光投下柔和的圓形陰影。作品把一場比賽的計算與直覺，轉譯為可以漫步其中的光之地景。

pins.title: House of Reptiles
pins.description:
A twisted wire frame with stick platforms is covered in moss and plants as a rainforest home for lizards.

Model and render | Habitat study | Metal strips, wooden sticks, plants, coconut soil | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 爬蟲之家
zh-Hant.description:
扭轉的鐵絲框架加上木條平台，覆上苔蘚與植物，成為蜥蜴的雨林之家。

模型與算圖｜棲地研究｜金屬條、木條、植物、椰土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A gecko on a moss platform.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student keeps many lizards at home. The project asks how to build a rainforest home that suits them.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生在家養了許多蜥蜴。這個專題探問，如何打造適合牠們的雨林之家。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A branching frame like fungus threads was tested in a digital model. It gives many paths for climbing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一個如菌絲般分枝的框架先在數位模型中測試。它提供許多攀爬路徑。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Twisted wire forms the frame in the tank. Sticks fixed into triangles make platforms on it.
captions: The wire frame in the tank.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 扭轉的鐵絲在缸中構成框架。固定成三角形的木條在其上形成平台。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 19.6-inch frame is covered in moss over coconut soil that keeps it damp. The platforms look like natural leaves.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個19.6英寸的框架覆滿苔蘚，下方的椰土保持濕潤。平台看起來就像天然的葉片。

sections.heading: Designing for Another Life - A Damp Forest for Climbing
sections.body: Architecture is usually designed for people, but this work hands the role of user to lizards. Starting from the reptiles the student keeps at home, it asked how to build a rainforest home that truly suits them. The guidance first led the student to think at the scale of the animal, testing a branching frame like fungus threads in a digital model, so that routes for climbing became the core of the design rather than decoration. In development, twisted wire formed the frame inside the tank and sticks fixed into triangles made platforms upon it, letting structure answer directly to the habits of the animals. Finally, the 19.6-inch frame is covered in moss over coconut soil that keeps it damp, and the platforms look like natural leaves. The work gently widens the meaning of dwelling, suggesting that empathy in design can cross the boundary between species and reach the daily life of another creature.

zh-Hant.heading: 為另一種生命設計-濕潤的攀爬之森
zh-Hant.body: 建築往往只為人而設計，但這件作品把使用者換成了蜥蜴。它從學生在家飼養的爬蟲出發，問的是如何打造一座適合牠們的雨林之家。指導過程先引導學生站在動物的尺度思考，以如菌絲般分枝的框架在數位模型中測試，讓攀爬的路徑成為設計的核心，而非裝飾。進入推演，扭轉的鐵絲在缸中構成骨架，固定成三角形的木條在其上形成平台，結構與棲息行為彼此對應。最後，十九點六英寸的框架覆滿苔蘚，下方的椰土保持濕潤，平台看起來就像天然的葉片。作品溫柔地擴大了「居住」的定義，提示設計的同理心可以越過物種的邊界，抵達另一種生命的日常。

pins.title: The Experience of a Fracture
pins.description:
Plaster cast around clay leaves hollows like broken bone, and a web of wooden sticks stitches the pieces back together.

Model | Fracture study | Wooden sticks, plaster, clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 骨折的經驗
zh-Hant.description:
以黏土翻模灌注石膏，留下如斷骨般的空腔，再以木條網絡把碎片縫合起來。

模型｜骨折研究｜木條、石膏、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student studied how bones break and heal. The project asks how the feeling of a fracture can become space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了骨頭如何斷裂與癒合。這個專題探問，骨折的感受如何轉化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches compared linear, oblique, spiral and crushed breaks. Each pattern was then pressed into clay as a 2D image.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 素描比較了線狀、斜向、螺旋與粉碎性骨折。每種圖樣再以平面形式壓進黏土。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plaster was poured over the clay, and the clay was removed to leave a cavity. These hollows stand for the missing broken bone.
captions: Pressing the clay by hand to mould the fracture cavities.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石膏灌注在黏土上，移除黏土後留下空腔。這些空洞代表斷裂缺失的骨頭。
captions: 親手按壓黏土，塑造骨折空腔的模具。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 16.5-inch model sets a forest of sticks over the plaster ground. The sticks join the pieces like stitches.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個16.5英寸的模型在石膏地面上立起一片木條林。木條像縫線般把碎片連接起來。

sections.heading: Terrain of a Break - Stitching the Missing Bone
sections.body: A fracture is a landscape inside the body: linear, oblique, spiral or crushed, each crack records the direction in which force passed through. Starting from how bones break and heal, the work asked whether the feeling of a fracture could become space. The guidance first led the student to compare types of breaks through sketches and then press each pattern into clay, turning medical categories into a surface one can touch. In development, plaster was poured over the clay, and once the clay was removed a cavity remained; absence became form, each hollow standing for the bone that broke away. Finally, the 16.5-inch model raises a forest of sticks over the plaster ground, the sticks joining the pieces like stitches. The work reads the wound as terrain and the healing as construction, letting viewers see that repair is itself a way of making space.

zh-Hant.heading: 斷裂的地形-縫合缺席的骨
zh-Hant.body: 骨折是一種身體內部的地景：線狀、斜向、螺旋或粉碎，每一道裂痕都記錄著力量經過的方向。這件作品從骨頭如何斷裂與癒合出發，問的是疼痛的感受能否成為空間。指導過程先引導學生以素描比較各種斷裂型態，再把圖樣壓進黏土，讓醫學的分類轉為可觸摸的平面。進入推演，石膏灌注其上，黏土被移除後留下空腔，缺席反而成為形體，空洞代表那段斷裂而失去的骨。最後，十六點五英寸的模型在石膏地面上立起一片木條林，木條像縫線般把碎片連接起來。作品把傷口讀成地形，把癒合讀成建造，讓觀者看見修復本身也是一種空間的生成。

pins.title: Deconstructing Basketball
pins.description:
The lines on a moving basketball are traced and rebuilt as a field of wire, sticks and coloured see-through card.

Model and drawings | Movement study | Wire, wooden sticks, coloured transparent card | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 解構籃球
zh-Hant.description:
籃球運動中表面的線條被描出，再重建成一片由鐵絲、木條與彩色透明卡構成的場域。

模型與繪圖｜運動研究｜鐵絲、木條、彩色透明卡｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wire and colour card model.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student knows and loves basketball well. The project asks how the motion of a ball over time can become space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生熟悉並熱愛籃球。這個專題探問，球隨時間的運動如何轉化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The ball was rebuilt as a digital model and turned to many angles. Lines on its surface were drawn from each view.
captions: A historic patent-style drawing of basketball panel patterns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 籃球被重建成數位模型，並轉到各種角度。學生從每個視角描出球面上的線條。
captions: 早期專利式的籃球表面分片圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wire loops traced the curves first, and sticks were added along them. Coloured card was then set between the sticks.
captions: Building the stick and wire model by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲圈先描出曲線，再沿著曲線加上木條。接著在木條之間嵌入彩色卡片。
captions: 親手搭建竹籤與鐵絲模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 16.5-inch model is a field of curving sticks and bright card. Light through the card throws pink and orange shadows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個16.5英寸的模型是一片彎曲木條與鮮豔卡片的場域。穿過卡片的光投下粉紅與橙色的陰影。

sections.heading: Trajectories of a Ball - A Field Unfolding in Time
sections.body: Every moment a ball spends in flight is a space that vanishes almost as soon as it appears. Starting from basketball, a game the student knows and loves, the work asked whether the motion of a ball over time could become space. The guidance first led the student to rebuild the ball as a digital model, turn it to many angles and draw the lines on its surface from each view, so that a familiar object was understood anew through multiple ways of looking. In development, wire loops first traced the curves, sticks were added along them, and coloured card was set between the sticks, building order layer by layer through line, plane and colour. Finally, the 16.5-inch model becomes a field of curving sticks and bright card, and light passing through the card throws pink and orange shadows. The work spreads a fleeting motion into a landscape one can linger in, letting viewers see the shape of time among light and shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 球的軌跡學-在時間裡展開的場域
zh-Hant.body: 一顆球在空中飛行的每一刻，都是一個稍縱即逝的空間。這件作品從學生熟悉並熱愛的籃球出發，問的是球隨時間的運動能否轉化為空間。指導過程先引導學生把籃球重建為數位模型，轉到各種角度，並從每個視角描出球面上的線條，讓熟悉的物件在多重觀看中被重新認識。進入推演，鐵絲圈先描出曲線，木條沿曲線加入，彩色卡片再嵌入木條之間，線、面與色彩逐層建立秩序。最後，十六點五英寸的模型成為一片彎曲木條與鮮豔卡片的場域，穿過卡片的光投下粉紅與橙色的陰影。作品把一瞬間的運動攤開成可以停留的風景，讓觀者在光影之間，看見時間的形狀。

pins.title: Hero in Motion
pins.description:
Fighting moves are drawn as lines, then rebuilt as hinged stick modules that turn and fold into a wearable space.

Model and drawings | Motion study | Popsicle sticks, screws, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 動態英雄
zh-Hant.description:
打鬥動作先被畫成線條，再重建為可轉動、折疊的鉸接木條模組，形成可穿戴的空間。

模型與繪圖｜動作研究｜冰棒棍、螺絲、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student grew up with a screen hero and its battle moves. The project asks how those moves can become a space you wear.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生從小看著一位螢幕英雄與其戰鬥動作長大。這個專題探問，這些動作如何變成可以穿戴的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student acted out each move and traced its path. Each path was drawn as a short line sketch.
captions: Motion sketches traced from stills of the hero character.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生親自模仿每個動作並記錄其軌跡。每條軌跡都被畫成一張簡短的線條素描。
captions: 依英雄角色畫面描繪的動作草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Polygon modules were made from sticks with holes and screws. The screws let each joint turn and fold.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 多邊形模組以鑽孔木條與螺絲製成。螺絲讓每個接點都能轉動與折疊。

sections.heading: Outcome
