sections.body: The 31.4-inch model links many modules into one moving shell. White planes inside catch the light.
captions: Acting out the moves and wearing the stick modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個31.4英寸的模型把許多模組連成一個可動的外殼。內部的白色板面承接光線。
captions: 親身演出動作並穿戴竹籤模組。

sections.heading: The Wearable Hero - Folding Motion into a Shell
sections.body: A childhood hero leaves behind not only stories but movements the body remembers. Starting from the screen hero the student grew up with, the work asked whether those battle moves could become a space one wears. The guidance first led the student to study the body through the body: each move was acted out and its path recorded, then drawn as a short line sketch, so that motion was distilled into a readable form. In development, polygon modules were made from sticks with holes and screws, and the screws allowed every joint to turn and fold, turning movement into the logic of construction. Finally, the 31.4-inch model links many modules into one moving shell, with white planes inside catching the light. The work brings imagined power back to real joints, suggesting that space, like clothing, can sit close to the body and move along with it.

zh-Hant.heading: 可穿戴的英雄-把動作摺成外殼
zh-Hant.body: 童年的英雄留下的不只是故事，還有身體記得的動作。這件作品從學生從小看著長大的螢幕英雄出發，問的是那些戰鬥動作能否變成可以穿戴的空間。指導過程先引導學生以身體研究身體，親自模仿每個動作、記錄其軌跡，再把每條軌跡畫成簡短的線條素描，讓動態被提煉為可以閱讀的形式。進入推演，多邊形模組以鑽孔木條與螺絲製成，螺絲讓每個接點都能轉動與折疊，運動因此成為構造的邏輯。最後，三十一點四英寸的模型把許多模組連成一個可動的外殼，內部的白色板面承接光線。作品讓想像中的力量回到真實的關節，提示空間可以像衣服一樣，貼近身體並隨它移動。

pins.title: Vegetables and Architecture
pins.description:
Cut and stacked vegetables are read as points, lines and planes, then turned into paintings and a paper and stick model.

Model and paintings | Form study | Vegetables, PVC board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 蔬菜與建築
zh-Hant.description:
切開堆疊的蔬菜被解讀為點、線、面，再轉化為繪畫與紙板木條模型。

模型與繪畫｜形態研究｜蔬菜、PVC板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves to cook and looks closely at produce. The project asks how the shapes in vegetables can build space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛烹飪，也細心觀察食材。這個專題探問，蔬菜的形態如何構築空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Vegetables and fruit were cut and stacked to find points, lines and planes. Paintings turned them into flat shapes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生切開並堆疊蔬果，找出點、線與面。繪畫把它們轉化為平面形狀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stacks of produce and sticks were set up and painted. The density of points and lines was varied in each one.
captions: Assembling the curved paper walls by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 蔬果與木條被堆疊起來並加以描繪。每一組都改變點與線的疏密。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 23.6-inch model sets curved paper walls among wooden sticks. Open, half-open and closed areas form the space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個23.6英寸的模型把彎曲紙牆置於木條之間。開放、半開放與封閉的區域構成空間。

sections.heading: Architecture on the Chopping Board - Points, Lines and Planes in Produce
sections.body: The kitchen is the most everyday laboratory, and every cut reveals a hidden structure. Starting from the student's love of cooking and close attention to produce, the work asked whether the shapes inside vegetables could build space. The guidance first led the student to read vegetables and fruit by cutting and stacking them, finding points, lines and planes, then to turn these into flat shapes through painting, bringing organic form into the vocabulary of architecture. In development, produce and sticks were stacked and painted, with the density of points and lines varied in each arrangement, so that density became a variable for tuning spatial experience. Finally, the 23.6-inch model sets curved paper walls among wooden sticks, and open, half-open and closed areas together compose the space. The work shows that architecture need not begin with grandeur; a single vegetable, looked at with care, is enough to grow a grammar of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 砧板上的建築-蔬果裡的點線面
zh-Hant.body: 廚房是最日常的實驗室，每一刀切下，都揭露一個被隱藏的結構。這件作品從學生對烹飪與食材的細心觀察出發，問的是蔬菜的形態能否構築空間。指導過程先引導學生以切開與堆疊閱讀蔬果，從中找出點、線與面，再以繪畫把它們轉化為平面形狀，讓有機的形體進入建築的語彙。進入推演，蔬果與木條被堆疊、描繪，每一組都改變點與線的疏密，密度成為調節空間感受的變數。最後，二十三點六英寸的模型把彎曲的紙牆置於木條之間，開放、半開放與封閉的區域共同構成空間。作品證明建築的起點不必宏大，一顆被認真凝視的蔬菜，也足以長出一套空間的文法。

pins.title: Ephemeral Glaciers
pins.description:
Ice melting tests are photographed over time and turned into a tower of thinning white plates and clear sticks.

Model and experiments | Sea ice study | Clear plastic sticks, white paper, glass, ice | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 短暫的冰川
zh-Hant.description:
冰塊融化試驗被逐時拍攝，再轉化為一座由漸薄白板與透明細棒構成的塔。

模型與實驗｜海冰研究｜透明塑膠棒、白紙、玻璃、冰｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sea ice in the far north is melting as the climate warms. The project asks how that melting can be shown in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 隨著氣候暖化，北方海域的海冰正在融化。這個專題探問，如何在空間中呈現這種融化。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A drawing sorted thin ice, broken ice and thick ice. Each type plays a part in the life of the sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張繪圖區分了薄冰、碎冰與厚冰。每種冰在海洋生態中都扮演角色。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Broken ice and one large block were melted under warm air. Photos every few minutes were traced into shrinking outlines.
captions: A large block melting over time.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 碎冰與一塊大冰塊在暖風下融化。每隔幾分鐘拍下的照片被描成逐漸縮小的輪廓。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 16.9-inch tower shows the broken ice above and the large block below. The plates narrow as the ice grows thinner.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座16.9英寸的塔上半部呈現碎冰，下半部呈現大冰塊。板面隨著冰層變薄而收窄。

sections.heading: A Measure of Melting - A Tower for Vanishing Ice
sections.body: Ice disappears without a sound; only its outline retreats, little by little. Starting from the melting of northern sea ice in a warming climate, the work asked whether melting could be shown in space. The guidance first led the student to build a taxonomy of ice, distinguishing thin ice, broken ice and thick ice, and understanding the part each plays in the life of the sea. The process then moved into experiment: broken ice and one large block were left to melt under warm air, and photos taken every few minutes were traced into shrinking outlines, so that time left a measurable trace. Finally, the 16.9-inch tower presents the broken ice in its upper part and the large block below, its plates narrowing as the ice grows thinner. The work is a monument raised to disappearance; it does not describe catastrophe, but lets viewers follow layer after diminishing layer and watch how time carries the ice away.

zh-Hant.heading: 融化的刻度-為消逝的冰立一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 冰的消逝沒有聲音，只有輪廓一點一點地退後。這件作品從北方海冰在暖化中融化的現實出發，問的是融化能否在空間中被呈現。指導過程先引導學生建立冰的分類學，區分薄冰、碎冰與厚冰，理解每一種冰在海洋生態中各自的角色。接著進入實驗，碎冰與一塊大冰塊在暖風下融化，每隔幾分鐘拍下的照片被描成逐漸縮小的輪廓，時間因此留下了可測量的痕跡。最後，十六點九英寸的塔上半部呈現碎冰，下半部呈現大冰塊，板面隨冰層變薄而收窄。作品是一座為消逝而立的紀念碑，它不描述災難，只讓觀者沿著一層層縮小的形體，親眼看見時間如何帶走冰。

pins.title: Family Cohesion
pins.description:
Separate paper houses of many colours and textures break apart, then join again through a bridge into one connected home.

Model | Family and communication study | Coloured straws, metal, soft card | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 家庭凝聚
zh-Hant.description:
多種色彩與質感的紙屋各自分離、碎裂，再透過一座橋重新連結成一個相通的家。

模型｜家庭與溝通研究｜彩色吸管、金屬、軟卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A family film about a house that falls apart showed the student how much talking matters at home. The project asks how a home can break and be rebuilt through sharing.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部講述房屋崩解的家庭電影，讓學生明白家中溝通的重要。這個專題探問，一個家如何因分享而崩解又重建。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches traced a home breaking into pieces and a new home forming. Each piece got its own material, from straws to soft card.
captions: Stills from the animated film about a family whose house breaks apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖描繪了一個家碎裂成片，再形成新家的過程。每一片都有各自的材料，從吸管到軟卡紙。
captions: 關於家屋崩裂之家庭的動畫電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bright colours meet white paper and wood strips so the first houses feel apart. A bridge with gaps leads towards the new house.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鮮豔色彩與白紙、木條相遇，讓最初的房屋顯得疏離。一座帶著缺口的橋通往新的房屋。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 500 mm tall model links every room in the rebuilt house. Cut paper throws dappled light across the pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個500毫米高的模型讓重建房屋的每個房間彼此相連。鏤空紙在構件上投下斑駁光影。

sections.heading: Dialogue in the Cracks - Rebuilding a Home
sections.body: A home is not a house but an ongoing conversation between people; when the conversation stops, the walls begin to give way. Starting from a family film about a house that falls apart, the work asked how a home breaks through what is or is not shared, and how it might be rebuilt. The guidance first led the student to narrate through sketches, tracing a home splitting into pieces and a new one taking shape, and assigning each piece its own material, from straws to soft card, so that feeling was translated into texture. In development, bright colours met white paper and wood strips, setting the first houses apart from one another, while a bridge with gaps led toward the new house, writing distance and connection into the same structure. Finally, the 500 mm tall model links every room of the rebuilt house, and cut paper throws dappled light across the pieces. The work reminds viewers that repair is never a return to wholeness, but learning to meet again across the gaps.

zh-Hant.heading: 裂縫中的對話-重建一個家
zh-Hant.body: 家不是一棟房子，而是人與人之間持續的交談；當交談停止，牆便開始崩解。這件作品從一部講述房屋崩解的家庭電影出發，問的是一個家如何因分享而碎裂，又如何重建。指導過程先引導學生以草圖敘事，描繪家碎裂成片、新家逐漸成形的過程，並為每一片指定材料，從吸管到軟卡紙，讓情感被翻譯成質地。進入推演，鮮豔色彩與白紙、木條相遇，使最初的房屋彼此疏離，一座帶著缺口的橋通往新的房屋，距離與連結被同時寫進結構。最後，五百毫米高的模型讓重建房屋的每個房間彼此相連，鏤空紙投下斑駁光影。作品提醒觀者，修復從來不是回到完整，而是學會在缺口之間重新相遇。

pins.title: Reflection on the Facade
pins.description:
Reflections on a glass office facade are painted in black and white, cut out of card and folded into stacked rooms.

Model and drawing | Facade study | Wood, card board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 立面上的倒影
zh-Hant.description:
玻璃辦公大樓立面上的倒影以黑白繪出，再從卡紙裁出並折成層疊的房間。

模型與繪圖｜立面研究｜木材、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many office towers in the city have glass facades that mirror the sky and hold heat. The project records one facade to show this heat island effect.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 城市中許多辦公大樓以玻璃為立面，映照天空也蓄積熱量。這個專題記錄一面立面，以呈現熱島效應。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The facade was painted with reflections in black and clear glass in white. The contrast shows how much of the face reflects.
captions: A glass office tower reflecting the buildings around it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把立面上的倒影塗成黑色，未反射的玻璃留白。這種對比顯示立面有多大面積在反射。
captions: 映照周邊建築的玻璃辦公大樓。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The painting was pasted on card and every reflection was cut away. The card was folded into small rooms with windows.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 繪畫被貼在卡紙上，每塊倒影都被裁去。卡紙再折成帶窗的小房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 660 mm tall model joins the rooms with wood strips into one building. Shade on the glass becomes the windows of a house.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個660毫米高的模型以木條把房間連成一棟建築。玻璃上的陰影變成了房屋的窗。

sections.heading: The Other Side of Glass - Cutting a Heat Island into Windows
sections.body: The glass facades of the city mirror the sky while quietly storing heat; beauty and cost share the same surface. Starting from office towers clad in glass, the work asked how the heat island effect could be made visible. The guidance first led the student to record rather than comment: the reflections on one facade were painted black and the clear glass left white, so that the extent of reflection could speak for itself through contrast. In development, the painting was pasted onto card and every reflection was cut away; the card was then folded into small rooms with windows, carrying the question from surface into space. Finally, the 660 mm tall model joins these rooms with wood strips into a single building, and the shade on the glass becomes the windows of a house. The work performs a gentle reversal: a surface that once reflected heat is reimagined as openings for living and for letting light in.

zh-Hant.heading: 玻璃的反面-把熱島裁成窗
zh-Hant.body: 城市的玻璃立面映照天空，卻也悄悄蓄積熱量，美麗與代價共用同一個表面。這件作品從辦公大樓的玻璃立面出發，問的是如何讓熱島效應被看見。指導過程先引導學生以記錄代替評論，把一面立面上的倒影塗成黑色，未反射的玻璃留白，讓反射的面積在黑白對比中自行說話。進入推演，繪畫被貼上卡紙，每一塊倒影都被裁去，卡紙再折成帶窗的小房間，問題因此從平面走向空間。最後，六百六十毫米高的模型以木條把房間連成一棟建築，玻璃上的陰影成為房屋的窗。作品完成了一次溫柔的翻轉：原本反射熱量的表面，被重新想像為讓人居住、讓光進入的開口。

pins.title: Infinity Game
pins.description:
Badminton poses are reduced to lines and points, then built as stick figures under a curving net in an infinity shape.

Model and drawings | Motion study | Wood, string | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無限遊戲
zh-Hant.description:
羽球動作被簡化為線與點，再以木條人形搭建在一張呈無限形狀彎曲的網下。

模型與繪圖｜動作研究｜木材、細繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Badminton is a big part of life for the student and the family. The project asks how a repeated game can become one space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 羽球是學生與家人生活中重要的一部分。這個專題探問，反覆進行的比賽如何成為一個空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student watched recordings of the game and found the poses repeat. Each pose was reduced to lines and points.
captions: Frames from a video of playing badminton.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生觀看比賽錄影，發現動作會不斷重複。每個姿勢都被簡化為線與點。
captions: 打羽毛球影片的連續畫面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wood strips became the body parts of each figure. String was added to soften the moves.
captions: Building the stick figures and net by hand.
The net and sticks from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條成為每個人形的肢體。學生加上細繩讓動作更柔和。
captions: 親手製作竹籤人形與網面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 420 mm long model forms an infinity loop of figures and net. Seen from the side, it plays like a film of the game.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個420毫米長的模型以人形與網構成無限循環。從側面看，它像一部播放比賽的影片。

sections.heading: Endless Rally - A Looping Theatre of Badminton
sections.body: Repetition is not monotony but rhythm; the meaning of a match lies in return after return. Starting from the badminton shared by the student and the family, the work asked whether a game played again and again could become a space. The guidance first led the student to watch recordings of matches, recognise the poses that keep returning, and reduce each movement to lines and points, so that the body was distilled into structure. In development, wood strips became the limbs of each figure and string was added between them, giving rigid joints a softer transition. Finally, the 420 mm long model forms an infinity loop of figures and net; seen from the side, it plays like a film of the game that never stops. The work folds time into a ring, and lets viewers see, among motionless sticks, how movement gains a kind of permanence through repetition.

zh-Hant.heading: 無盡的回合-羽球的循環劇場
zh-Hant.body: 重複不是單調，而是一種節奏，一場比賽的意義正藏在一次又一次的回擊之中。這件作品從學生與家人共享的羽球生活出發，問的是反覆進行的比賽能否成為一個空間。指導過程先引導學生觀看比賽錄影，在影像中辨認出不斷重複的姿勢，再把每個動作簡化為線與點，讓身體被還原為結構。進入推演，木條成為人形的肢體，細繩加入其間，使剛硬的關節生出柔和的過渡。最後，四百二十毫米長的模型以人形與網構成無限循環，從側面看，它像一部持續播放的比賽影片。作品把時間折成一個圈，讓觀者在靜止的木條之間，看見運動如何在重複裡獲得永恆。

pins.title: Coffee-Ground Air Cleaner
pins.description:
Used coffee grounds glued to old wire mesh and fixed with scrap screws build a small deodorising tower on a stick frame.

Model | Waste material study | Coffee grounds, wood, metal | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 咖啡渣空氣清淨器
zh-Hant.description:
把用過的咖啡渣黏在舊鐵絲網上，以回收螺絲固定，搭在木條框架上成為一座小型除臭塔。

模型｜廢料研究｜咖啡渣、木材、金屬｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student noticed that daily waste, like street snacks, changes with what it is made of. The project tests what used coffee grounds and scraps can become.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生發現日常廢物就像街頭小吃一樣，會因材料而不同。這個專題測試用過的咖啡渣與廢料能變成什麼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Coffee grounds were glued onto different wrapping papers and old mesh. Screws and nuts from a scrap yard held the pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 咖啡渣被黏在不同的包裝紙與舊網上。來自廢料場的螺絲與螺帽固定這些構件。
captions: 以螺絲固定的咖啡渣方塊。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The screws alone could not hold a large sheet of mesh. Wood strips were added to brace the nets and link them.
captions: Shaping the coffee mesh and wood frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 單靠螺絲撐不住大片鐵絲網。學生加上木條來支撐並連結這些網。
captions: 親手塑形咖啡網片與木框。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 600 mm tall tower stacks mesh boxes in a light stick frame. The coffee grounds help soak up odours in the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這座600毫米高的塔在輕巧的木條框架中堆疊網箱。咖啡渣有助吸附空氣中的異味。

sections.heading: A Second Life for Residue - A Tower That Breathes
sections.body: Waste is not an ending but a material that has not yet been renamed. Starting from the student's observation of everyday waste, the work asked what used coffee grounds and scraps could still become. The guidance first led the student to replace assumptions with hands-on tests: coffee grounds were glued onto different wrapping papers and old mesh, and screws and nuts from a scrap yard fixed the pieces together, so the materials could answer for their own possibilities. In development, failure became a clue: screws alone could not hold a large sheet of mesh, so wood strips were added to brace and link the nets, and the structure grew out of the problem itself. Finally, the 600 mm tall tower stacks mesh boxes within a light stick frame, and the coffee grounds help soak up odours in the air. The work quietly rewrites the meaning of value, returning what was discarded to daily life, where it keeps working for the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 殘渣的第二生命-會呼吸的網塔
zh-Hant.body: 廢物並非終點，而是一種尚未被重新命名的材料。這件作品從學生對日常廢物的觀察出發，問的是：用過的咖啡渣與廢料還能成為什麼？指導過程先引導學生以手做實驗取代假設，把咖啡渣黏在不同的包裝紙與舊網上，並以廢料場的螺絲與螺帽固定構件，讓材料自己回答可能性。進入推演，失敗成為線索：單靠螺絲撐不住大片鐵絲網，於是木條被加入，支撐並連結這些網，結構在問題中長出來。最後，六百毫米高的塔在輕巧的木條框架中堆疊網箱，咖啡渣有助吸附空氣中的異味。作品安靜地重寫了價值的定義，讓被丟棄之物回到日常，繼續為空氣工作。

pins.title: Protecting Wild Habitats
pins.description:
A field of white grass grows inside a wire factory outline, showing how industry slowly takes over land that wild animals need.

Model and sketches | Habitat study | Wood, plastic, metal | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 守護野生棲地
zh-Hant.description:
一片白色草原在鐵絲工廠輪廓內生長，呈現工業如何逐漸佔據野生動物所需的土地。

模型與草圖｜棲地研究｜木材、塑膠、金屬｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A grass field in a wire cage.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A group study looked at how oil drilling in a cold northern region harms wild animals. The project asks how industry and nature can be balanced.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一項小組研究探討了北方寒冷地區的石油開採如何傷害野生動物。這個專題探問，工業與自然如何取得平衡。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many animals there lose their homes as drilling spreads. The harm comes slowly, not in one day or one year.
captions: A photo of the Alaska North Slope and maps of its protected areas.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 隨著開採擴張，當地許多動物失去家園。這種傷害是緩慢累積的，並非一天或一年造成。
captions: 阿拉斯加北坡照片及其保護區地圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sketches set boxes in rows behind fences and steps. A wire outline on one side stands for the factory.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把方盒排在圍欄與階梯之後。一側的鐵絲輪廓代表工廠。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 420 mm long model puts tall grass inside and around the wire walls. Bare patches show land with no life left.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個420毫米長的模型在鐵絲牆內外種滿高草。裸露的區塊表示失去生命的土地。

sections.heading: A Slow Wound - Between Wire and Wild Grass
sections.body: The deepest damage often makes no sound; it does not happen in a day or a year, but accumulates across countless ordinary days. Starting from oil drilling in a cold northern region, the work asked how industry and nature might find balance. The guidance first led the group to build facts through research, understanding how expanding drilling gradually takes homes away from animals, and recognising the temporality of that harm: it is slow. In development, sketches set boxes in rows behind fences and steps, with a wire outline on one side standing for the factory, so that order and boundary became the main language of the space. Finally, the 420 mm long model fills the inside and outside of its wire walls with tall grass, while bare patches mark land where no life remains. The work has no need to shout; by setting growth beside emptiness, it lets viewers read the cost in the gap between them.

zh-Hant.heading: 緩慢的傷口-鐵絲與荒草之間
zh-Hant.body: 最深的破壞往往沒有聲響，它不在一天或一年裡發生，而是在無數個平常的日子裡累積。這件作品從北方寒冷地區的石油開採出發，問的是工業與自然如何取得平衡。指導過程先引導小組以研究建立事實，理解開採擴張如何讓動物逐步失去家園，並辨認出傷害的時間性：它是緩慢的。進入推演，草圖把方盒排列在圍欄與階梯之後，一側的鐵絲輪廓代表工廠，秩序與邊界成為空間的主要語言。最後，四百二十毫米長的模型在鐵絲牆內外種滿高草，而裸露的區塊標示著失去生命的土地。作品不需要吶喊，它讓生長與空白並置，使觀者在兩者的落差裡讀出代價。

pins.title: Self-Rotation
pins.description:
A cube is twisted until its faces curl into soft ribbons, studied in renders, rotation drawings and an acrylic model.

Renders, drawings and model | Form study | Acrylic | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自轉
zh-Hant.description:
一個立方體被扭轉，直到各面捲成柔軟的緞帶，並以算圖、旋轉繪圖與壓克力模型研究。

算圖、繪圖與模型｜形態研究｜壓克力｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from twisting a cube. It asks how a hard square form can turn into soft curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題從扭轉一個立方體出發。它探問，堅硬的方形如何轉為柔軟的曲線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Rotating the cube recalled an old idea that the sky is round and the land is square. Drawings tracked how each face turns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 旋轉立方體讓學生想起天圓地方的古老觀念。繪圖記錄了每一面如何轉動。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each part was moved apart and set in a new place. This made the gap between sharp angles and soft faces bigger.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每個部分被拉開並重新排列位置。這放大了尖角與柔面之間的差異。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The 900 mm long study ends in a clear acrylic model. Thin fins fan out like a turning surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個900毫米長的研究以透明壓克力模型作結。細薄的鰭片如轉動的曲面般展開。

sections.heading: Square Turning Round - A Cube in Rotation
sections.body: Even the hardest geometry can learn softness within a single turn. Starting from the twisting of a cube, the work asked how a square form might become a curve. The guidance first led the student to read form through rotation, letting the ancient idea that the sky is round and the land is square serve as a coordinate for thought, while drawings recorded how each face turns, so that the motion itself became the object of study. In development, the parts of the form were pulled apart and set in new places, enlarging the difference between sharp angles and soft faces; tension no longer hid inside the whole but became a readable interval. Finally, the 900 mm long study concludes in a clear acrylic model, its thin fins fanning out like a surface in motion. The work reads like a fable of transformation: order is not overthrown, it simply puts on another posture through continuous rotation.

zh-Hant.heading: 方與圓的轉身-一個立方體的自轉
zh-Hant.body: 最堅硬的幾何，也可能在一次轉動裡學會柔軟。這件作品從扭轉一個立方體出發，問的是方形如何轉為曲線。指導過程先引導學生在旋轉中閱讀形體，並讓天圓地方的古老觀念成為思考的座標，以繪圖記錄每一面如何轉動，使動作本身成為研究的對象。進入推演，形體的各個部分被拉開、重新排列，尖角與柔面之間的差異因此被放大，張力不再隱藏於整體之中，而成為可以閱讀的間距。最後，九百毫米長的研究以透明壓克力模型作結，細薄的鰭片如轉動的曲面般展開。作品像一則關於轉變的寓言：秩序並未被推翻，只是在連續的旋轉中，悄悄換上了另一種姿態。

pins.title: Machine Mosaic
pins.description:
Hand-drawn machine parts are cut up and recombined into a mosaic, then rebuilt as a folded card model and a stick model.

Models and drawing | Form study | White card, wood strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 機械拼貼
zh-Hant.description:
手繪的機械零件被剪開並重新拼成拼貼，再重建為折紙卡模型與木條模型。

模型與繪圖｜形態研究｜白卡紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Giant robots in a science fiction film made the student curious about how machine bodies are put together. The project asks how those parts can become a new space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部科幻電影中的巨型機器人，讓學生好奇機械身體如何組合。這個專題探問，這些零件如何變成新的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew machine parts on a tablet and printed them out. The prints were cut into small pieces and recombined into a new mosaic drawing.
captions: Reference drawings of the giant robots from the film that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在平板上繪製機械零件並列印出來。列印稿被剪成小片，再重新拼成一幅新的拼貼繪圖。
captions: 啟發本案之電影中巨型機器人的參考繪圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The mosaic was read as a floor plan and folded from hard white card. Each folded piece was joined into one plane model.
captions: Cutting the card and gluing the sticks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 拼貼被當成平面圖閱讀，並以硬白卡紙折出。每個折出的構件再連成一個面的模型。
captions: 親手裁切卡紙並黏合竹籤。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The edges of the card model were traced in wood strips and glued into a line model. The 500 mm square pair shows one idea as planes and as lines.
captions: The stick model and its shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生沿卡紙模型的邊緣以木條描出，並黏合成線的模型。這對500毫米見方的模型以面與線呈現同一個構想。

sections.heading: Anatomy of a Machine - From Parts to Space
sections.body: A machine body is an assembled order, and every part hints at another possible arrangement. Starting from the giant robots of a science fiction film, the work asked whether those parts could be recombined into a new space. The guidance first led the student to draw machine parts on a tablet, print them, cut them apart and reassemble them as a new mosaic, so that the original image lost its meaning in the act of dismantling and became a pure vocabulary of form. In development, the mosaic was read as a floor plan and folded piece by piece from hard white card into a model of planes; its edges were then traced in wood strips and translated into a model of lines. Finally, the two 500 mm square models stand side by side, one of surfaces and one of lines, speaking the same idea. The work reveals that design is less about invention than translation: the same thought, carried into another material, becomes another way of seeing.

zh-Hant.heading: 機械的解剖-從零件到空間
zh-Hant.body: 機器的身體是一種被組裝的秩序，每個零件都暗示著另一種可能的排列。這件作品從科幻電影中的巨型機器人出發，問的是：這些零件能否被重組為新的空間？指導過程先引導學生在平板上繪製機械零件，列印、剪碎，再拼成一幅新的拼貼，讓既有的形象在拆解中失去原意，轉而成為純粹的形式語彙。進入推演，拼貼被當作平面圖閱讀，以硬白卡紙一片片折出，連成面的模型；隨後沿著卡紙的邊緣以木條描出，轉譯為線的模型。最後，兩座五百毫米見方的模型並置，一者是面，一者是線，說的是同一個構想。作品揭示設計的本質不在發明，而在轉譯：同一個念頭，換一種材料，便換一種觀看。

pins.title: Human Stream
pins.description:
People moving through a busy hall become spheres of comfort, then a layered wood stream cast into white plaster.

Model and renders | Movement study | Wood, plaster, silicone, PVC | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 人流
zh-Hant.description:
在繁忙大廳中移動的人群被轉化為舒適範圍的球體，再成為澆鑄在白色石膏中的層疊木流。

模型與算圖｜動線研究｜木材、石膏、矽膠、PVC｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In an open shopping hall, people move back and forth with no clear order. The project asks how much personal comfort space each person needs.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在開放的購物大廳中，人們來回移動，沒有明確的秩序。這個專題探問，每個人需要多少個人舒適空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student traced people crossing the hall over ten seconds. A larger sphere marks a larger comfort range at that moment.
captions: Frames from a ten-second clip of people moving through a shopping mall.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生追蹤人們在十秒內穿越大廳的路徑。較大的球體代表當下較大的舒適範圍。
captions: 商場人流十秒片段的連續畫面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The 3D model was sliced into strips of equal thickness and glued into solid wood. Silicone molds were made from the wood parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把3D模型切成等厚的條片，再黏成實心木塊。接著以木構件翻製矽膠模具。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Plaster was poured into PVC boxes around the molds and wood. The 400 mm square model shows people as a frozen stream.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 石膏被倒入圍住模具與木塊的PVC盒中。這個400毫米見方的模型把人群呈現為凝結的流。

sections.heading: A Frozen Stream - Ten Seconds of Distance
sections.body: A crowd looks disordered, yet every body carries an invisible ring of boundary around it. Starting from an open shopping hall, the work asked how much comfort space a person truly needs. The guidance first led the student to replace imagination with observation: people crossing the hall were traced over ten seconds, and spheres of different sizes marked each person's comfort range at that moment, so that psychological distance became a measurable volume. In development, the 3D model was sliced into strips of equal thickness and glued into solid wood, from which silicone molds were cast, turning digital flow into matter that hands can control. Finally, plaster was poured into PVC boxes around the molds and wood, and in setting it froze the passers-by into a single white stream. The work writes movement through stillness and writes the gaps through solid form, letting viewers see the distances people keep from one another in public space, distances that are always negotiated and never spoken.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝結的人流-十秒鐘的距離
zh-Hant.body: 人群看似無序，其實每個身體都攜帶著一圈看不見的邊界。這件作品從開放的購物大廳出發，問的是：一個人究竟需要多少舒適空間？指導過程先引導學生以觀察取代想像，追蹤人們在十秒內穿越大廳的路徑，並以球體的大小標記當下的舒適範圍，讓心理距離成為可以測量的體積。進入推演，3D模型被切成等厚的條片，黏成實心木塊，再翻製矽膠模具，數位的流動因此轉為手工可控的物質。最後，石膏倒入圍住模具與木塊的PVC盒中，在凝固裡把行人定格成一道白色的流。作品以靜止書寫移動，以實體書寫空隙，讓觀者看見公共空間中那些彼此避讓、卻從未被說出的距離。

pins.title: Running Through Gaps
pins.description:
Football running routes become a field of layered PVC walls, cut lower where a player runs faster.

Model and drawings | Movement study | PVC board, glue, spray paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 穿越縫隙
zh-Hant.description:
美式足球的跑動路線化為一片層疊PVC牆，球員跑得越快處，牆被切得越低。

模型與繪圖｜動作研究｜PVC板、膠、噴漆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In American football, players look for gaps to get through. Animals on the run and wind in a forest move in the same way.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在美式足球中，球員不斷尋找可以穿越的縫隙。逃跑的動物與林間的風也以同樣方式移動。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student mapped the running routes and four team moves on paper. The routes were then laid over each other as one flowing drawing.
captions: A football player crouched at the line, ready to run.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在紙上畫出跑動路線與四種團隊陣式。接著把路線疊合成一張流動的繪圖。
captions: 蹲在線上準備起跑的美式足球員。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each route became a wall, trimmed from above and below in a 3D model. The faster the player, the more of the wall top was cut.
captions: Testing the layered wall pieces by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每條路線在3D模型中成為一道牆，並從上下修切。球員越快，牆頂被切掉越多。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Every wall of the 500 mm model is built from hundreds of glued PVC layers. Small figures walk through the gaps like players.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個500毫米模型的每道牆都由數百層黏合的PVC板構成。小人像球員一樣穿行於縫隙之間。

sections.heading: A Poetics of Gaps - Walls Carved by Speed
sections.body: The true protagonist of motion is the gap: players, fleeing animals and wind in a forest all search for the same passable void. Beginning with American football, the work asked whether speed could leave a shape behind. The guidance first led the student to read the game as a drawing: running routes and four team moves were mapped on paper, then laid over one another into a single flowing image, so that split-second decisions surfaced as traces. In development, each route was raised into a wall and trimmed from above and below in a 3D model, with speed acting as the blade; the faster the player, the more of the wall top was cut away, and movement was translated into measurable terrain. Finally, the 500 mm model is built from hundreds of glued PVC layers, thin sheets accumulating like slices of time, while small figures pass through the gaps. The work does not depict a match; it invites the viewer into the emptiness a match leaves behind, and lets them feel how motion itself shapes space.

zh-Hant.heading: 縫隙的詩學-速度雕刻的牆
zh-Hant.body: 縫隙是運動的真正主角：球員、逃跑的動物與林間的風，都在尋找同一種可以穿越的空。這件作品從美式足球出發，問的是速度能否留下形狀。指導過程先引導學生把比賽讀成圖：跑動路線與四種團隊陣式被畫在紙上，再彼此疊合成一張流動的繪圖，讓瞬間的決策顯影為軌跡。進入推演，每條路線被立起為牆，在3D模型中從上下修切，而速度成為刀，球員越快，牆頂便被削去越多，運動因此被翻譯成可量度的地形。最後，五百毫米的模型由數百層PVC板黏合而成，層層累積的薄片像時間的切片，小人在縫隙之間穿行。作品不描繪比賽，而是讓觀者走進比賽留下的空，體會移動本身如何塑造空間。

pins.title: Tower of Memories
pins.description:
Clear resin blocks hold small pieces of school life, stacked on the ground and hung in the air around a stair.

Model | Memory study | PVC board, resin, wood, thread | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 記憶之塔
zh-Hant.description:
透明樹脂塊封存校園生活的片段，堆疊在地面，也懸掛在階梯周圍的空中。

模型｜記憶研究｜PVC板、樹脂、木材、細線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student has long liked images laid over one another. The project turns daily life at school into a tower of overlapping memories.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生一直喜歡影像相互疊合的形式。這個專題把校園日常轉化為一座記憶疊合的塔。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Memories were collected from trees, corridors, a bridge and ball games near school. Soil from a sports field and marbles were added as real pieces.
captions: Football and basketball games that fill the memories.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從校園附近的樹、走廊、天橋與球賽中收集記憶。運動場的泥土與彈珠也被當作實物加入。
captions: 充滿回憶的足球與籃球比賽。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Mixed resin was poured into silicone molds with the pieces set inside. After it cured, the blocks were matched and laid out.
captions: Casting the resin blocks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把調好的樹脂倒入矽膠模具，並把物件置入其中。硬化後，方塊被搭配並排列。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Some blocks hang from a wood frame on thin thread like a sky of memories. A stair leads up through them like a walk through the past.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 部分方塊以細線懸掛在木框上，像一片記憶的天空。一道階梯穿過其中，如同走過過去。

sections.heading: Frozen Time - A Campus Suspended in Air
sections.body: Memory is never a single photograph; it is the thickness left when many images settle over one another. The work began from the student's long affection for layered images and asked whether daily life could be kept as matter one can touch. The guidance first led the student back to the campus, gathering memories among trees, corridors, a bridge and ball games, and letting soil from a sports field and a handful of marbles stand as real evidence, so that recollection was no longer only a story. In development, resin became a preservative of time: objects were set into silicone molds and hardened into transparent moments, and the blocks were matched and arranged like a private chronicle being re-edited. In the end, some blocks hang from a wooden frame on thin thread, a sky of memories, with a stair rising through them. To climb it is to walk not through space but through the past; the work quietly suggests that growing up means passing through the moments that are still suspended.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固的時間-懸在空中的校園
zh-Hant.body: 記憶從來不是一張照片，而是許多影像彼此覆蓋後留下的厚度。這件作品從學生對疊合影像的長久偏愛出發，問的是：日常能否被保存成可以觸摸的物質？指導過程先引導學生回到校園，從樹、走廊、天橋與球賽之間採集記憶，並讓運動場的泥土與彈珠成為真實的證物，使回憶不再只是敘述。進入推演，樹脂成為時間的封存劑，物件被置入矽膠模具，在硬化中凝結成透明的片刻；方塊被搭配、排列，像在重組一段私人的編年史。最後，部分方塊以細線懸在木框上，成為一片記憶的天空，一道階梯穿過其中。觀者拾級而上，行走的不是空間，而是過去；作品安靜地提示，所謂成長，正是穿越那些仍然懸著的瞬間。

pins.title: Three Islands of Emotion
pins.description:
Joy, fear and anger become three small buildings, made from clay, wood sticks, PVC, steel wire and shimmering laser paper.

Models and sketches | Emotion study | Clay, wood sticks, PVC board, laser paper, paper, steel wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 情緒三島
zh-Hant.description:
喜悅、恐懼與憤怒化為三座小建築，以黏土、木條、PVC、鋼絲與閃爍的雷射紙製成。

模型與草圖｜情緒研究｜黏土、木條、PVC板、雷射紙、紙、鋼絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An animated film about feelings made the student imagine islands of joy, fear and anger. The project asks how a building can hold the memory of a dream and its feelings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於情緒的動畫電影，讓學生想像喜悅、恐懼與憤怒的島嶼。這個專題探問，建築如何承載一場夢的記憶與情緒。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student sketched each feeling with the materials that might carry it. Smoothness, form and colour were chosen as the signs of each emotion.
captions: Film stills and character art from the animated film that inspired the three islands.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生為每種情緒畫出可能承載它的材料。材質的平滑、形態與色彩被選為情緒的記號。
captions: 啟發三座島嶼的動畫電影劇照與角色圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Joy was made of soft clay wrapped in triangles of wood sticks and laser paper. The shining triangles hold dream memories that jump from one to the next.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 喜悅以柔軟的黏土製成，外圍包覆木條與雷射紙組成的三角形。閃亮的三角形封存著從一段跳到另一段的夢境記憶。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Fear is a strong but hollow frame of sticks, PVC boxes and wire-bound balls. Anger is a broken heap of sticks and paper with dark window frames.
captions: The fear model and its shadows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 恐懼是一個堅固卻中空的骨架，由木條、PVC盒與鋼絲纏繞的球組成。憤怒則是一堆破碎的木條與紙，配上深色的窗框。

sections.heading: Weather of the Heart - Building Three Feelings by Hand
sections.body: Feelings rarely arrive one at a time; they drift through a dream like weather, bright, then hollow, then splintered. The project started from a wish to give three of them a place to live, and the guidance asked first that each emotion be found in matter before it was found in form. Sketches paired every feeling with its materials, so that smoothness, colour and weight could speak where words fall short. Joy grew from soft clay, held inside a lattice of stick triangles faced with laser paper, its shifting colours echoing memories that leap from one scene to the next. Fear became a rigid frame with nothing at its core, a structure that looks secure yet offers no refuge, while wire-bound balls hang inside it like knots of worry. Anger was allowed to fall apart, a heap of sticks and torn paper with dark window frames marking what still stands. Placed together, the three models read less as buildings than as a quiet atlas of inner life, showing that architecture can begin with how a moment feels.

zh-Hant.heading: 心的天氣-以雙手搭建三種感受
zh-Hant.body: 感受很少單獨到來，它們像天氣一樣飄過夢境，時而明亮，時而空洞，時而碎裂。這個專題始於一個心願：為其中三種情緒找到可以居住的地方。指導過程首先要求，每種情緒必須先在物質中被找到，再談形態；草圖把每種感受與材料配對，讓平滑、色彩與重量說出語言說不出的部分。喜悅從柔軟的黏土長出，被包覆在貼著雷射紙的木條三角格網之中，變幻的光色呼應著在場景之間跳躍的記憶。恐懼成為一個核心空無的堅硬骨架，看似牢固，卻無處可躲，鋼絲纏繞的球懸在其中，如同糾結的憂慮。憤怒則被允許崩解，木條與撕裂的紙堆成一團，只剩深色窗框標示仍然站立之處。三座模型並置時，與其說是建築，不如說是一部安靜的內心地圖集，提醒人們建築可以從一個片刻的感受開始。

pins.title: Building Block
pins.description:
Nine verbs drawn from old building photos become a single wood-strip unit, stacked into a tower that rises like a growing crystal.

Models and drawings | Structure study | Dutch paper, wood strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 建築積木
zh-Hant.description:
從老建築照片中提煉出的九個動詞化為單一木條單元，堆疊成一座如晶體般生長的塔。

模型與繪圖｜結構研究｜荷蘭紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A history class asked the student to study an archive of old photos and pick a theme. The student chose architecture and asked how form and structure relate.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一堂歷史課要求學生研究一批老照片檔案並選定主題。學生選擇了建築，並探問形態與結構之間的關係。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Nine buildings that stood out were outlined in red pen. Nine keywords came from them: hide, distill, store, layering, chip, weave, support, gather and bond.
captions: Archive photos of nine buildings, traced in red pen and summed up in nine verbs.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以紅筆描出九棟特別突出的建築輪廓。從中歸納出九個關鍵詞：隱藏、提煉、儲存、層疊、削切、編織、支撐、聚集與連結。
captions: 九棟建築的檔案照片，以紅筆描繪並歸納成九個動詞。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The keywords were turned into three models built from paper and wood sticks. Their joints led to one new unit, a looped block of wood strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些關鍵詞被轉化為三個以紙與木條搭成的模型。它們的接合方式引出一個新單元：以木條圍成的環狀積木。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Hundreds of units were stacked into a tower about one metre tall. Each block holds the next, so the form grows without a separate frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 數百個單元被堆疊成一座約一米高的塔。每塊積木都承托著下一塊，形態因此無需另設骨架便能生長。

sections.heading: Grammar of Wood - From Old Facades to a Living Lattice
sections.body: Old photographs keep buildings the way a dictionary keeps words, waiting for someone to read them in a new order. The study opened with an archive of weathered facades, and the guidance steered the student away from copying styles toward naming actions. Tracing nine buildings in red, the student distilled verbs rather than images: to hide, to store, to weave, to support, to bond. This shift turned history into a working grammar, and the next step tested that grammar in paper and wood, three small models in which each verb had to become a joint, a layer or a frame. From those trials one modest unit emerged, a looped block of strips that could hold its neighbour. Repetition then did the rest, as hundreds of blocks climbed into a tower about a metre high, carrying itself without any hidden skeleton. Indoors it reads as a crystal; set on autumn grass it looks almost grown. The tower makes a patient case that structure is a sentence built from small, honest parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 木的文法-從舊立面到生長的格架
zh-Hant.body: 老照片保存建築的方式，就像字典保存文字，等待有人以新的順序閱讀。這項研究從一批斑駁立面的照片檔案開始，指導過程引導學生不去模仿風格，而是為動作命名。學生以紅筆描出九棟建築，提煉的不是影像而是動詞：隱藏、儲存、編織、支撐、連結。這個轉向讓歷史成為可以運作的文法；下一步便以紙與木條檢驗這套文法，在三個小模型中，每個動詞都必須化為一個接點、一層疊片或一道框。從這些試驗中，浮現出一個謙遜的單元：一塊可以扣住鄰居的木條環形積木。接著由重複完成其餘的工作，數百塊積木攀升成約一米高的塔，不靠任何隱藏的骨架便能自我承托。在室內，它像一枚晶體；放在秋天的草地上，又彷彿是自己長出來的。這座塔耐心地證明，結構是一句由微小而誠實的部件構成的句子。

pins.title: Human Organ Model
pins.description:
The folds of a brain, the bubbles of the lungs and a stretching throat become three models of wood strips, acrylic and movable joints.

Models and sketches | Body study | Acrylic sheet, wood strips, wood board, PVC | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 人體器官模型
zh-Hant.description:
大腦的皺褶、肺泡的氣泡與伸縮的食道，化為三個以木條、壓克力與活動關節構成的模型。

模型與草圖｜身體研究｜壓克力板、木條、木板、PVC｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The brain model and its shadows.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brain sends signals through the nerves to meet the needs of the body. The project turns the brain, the lungs and the digestive tract into spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 大腦透過神經傳遞訊號，回應身體的需求。這個專題把大腦、肺與消化道轉化為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew a top view of the brain and traced its folds. Sketches of the alveoli and the lungs followed, each read as a kind of room.
captions: Textbook diagrams of the brain and the respiratory system.
A brain sketch and first strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出大腦的俯視圖，並描出其中的皺褶。接著繪製肺泡與肺的草圖，每一幅都被當作一種房間來閱讀。
captions: 大腦與呼吸系統的教科書圖解。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wood strips of different sizes rose from the folds in three layers, so model and shadow lock together. The bubbly alveoli were cut in clear acrylic to show the tangled space inside.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同尺寸的木條沿著皺褶分三層升起，使模型與陰影彼此交錯。泡狀的肺泡以透明壓克力切製，呈現其內部交織的空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The throat became a frame of wood boards and screws that can stretch and shrink. Its tunnel changes shape each time it moves, and the three models together stand one metre tall.
captions: Holding up the finished esophagus model.
Tunnel views of the throat model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 食道化為以木板與螺絲組成、可伸可縮的框架。每次移動，它的通道都會改變形狀；三個模型合起來高約一米。

sections.heading: Rooms Within - Reading the Body as Architecture
sections.body: The body is the first building anyone lives in, though few ever walk its corridors. This project set out to enter three of them, and the guidance began by asking the student to draw before building, tracing the folds of a brain and the clustered bubbles of the lungs until each organ could be read as a plan. From that reading, structure followed function. In the brain, strips of wood rose from every fold in three tiers, and their shadows fell back into the gaps, so the dense grooves became both form and darkness. In the lungs, clear acrylic held the tangled hollows of a single alveolus, revealing how much space can hide inside something so small. In the throat, wood boards and screws formed hinged joints, letting the model stretch and contract like a living passage whose tunnel never holds one shape for long. Together the three studies argue, quietly and precisely, that every organ already contains an architecture, waiting only for an attentive eye to measure it.

zh-Hant.heading: 體內的房間-把身體讀作建築
zh-Hant.body: 身體是每個人居住的第一棟建築，卻很少有人走過它的廊道。這個專題試著走進其中三處；指導過程首先要求學生先畫再做，描出大腦的皺褶與肺泡簇擁的氣泡，直到每個器官都能被讀作一張平面圖。從這樣的閱讀出發，結構跟隨機能而生。在大腦中，木條沿著每道皺褶分三層升起，陰影又落回縫隙之間，使密集的溝回同時成為形體與暗影。在肺中，透明壓克力承載單一肺泡內交織的空腔，揭示如此微小之物竟能藏著多少空間。在食道中，木板與螺絲組成鉸接的關節，讓模型像活的通道一樣伸展與收縮，通道的形狀從不長久停留。三項研究安靜而精確地論證：每個器官早已包含一種建築，只等待一雙專注的眼睛去丈量。

pins.title: Visualized Sound
pins.description:
Music played into a drum makes a laser draw glowing loops, which are rebuilt in wire mesh, stretched fabric and heat-shaped PVC.

Models and light study | Sound study | Barrel, sticks, laser pointer, wire mesh, stockings, PVC sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 看見聲音
zh-Hant.description:
音樂傳入鼓面，使雷射畫出發光的線圈，再以鐵絲網、拉伸的布料與熱塑PVC重建。

模型與光研究｜聲音研究｜桶、木棍、雷射筆、鐵絲網、絲襪、PVC片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Music is heard but never seen. The project asks what the lines of a song would look like if sound could be drawn in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 音樂可以被聽見，卻無法被看見。這個專題探問，如果聲音能在空間中被畫出，一首歌的線條會是什麼模樣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student built a device from a barrel, sticks and a laser pointer, then played music into it. The shaking drum made the laser draw loops of light that were recorded.
captions: A live concert, the music that the sound model visualizes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以桶、木棍與雷射筆製作了一個裝置，再對著它播放音樂。震動的鼓面使雷射畫出光的線圈，並被記錄下來。
captions: 現場演唱會，即聲音模型所視覺化的音樂。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wire gave a frame that could bend, and stretched stockings gave smooth wave surfaces. Small forms tested how each loop of light could become a solid.
captions: Building the laser device and recording the light traces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲提供可以彎折的骨架，拉伸的絲襪則形成平滑的波面。小型形體測試每一圈光線如何成為實體。
captions: 製作雷射裝置並記錄光的軌跡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Clear PVC sheet was found to hold its shape after heating, so it joined the mesh and fabric. All the parts were assembled in a 400 mm box like music frozen in mid-air.
captions: The sound wave model from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生發現透明PVC片加熱後可以定形，於是把它與鐵絲網、布料結合。所有構件被組裝在一個400毫米的盒中，如同凝結在半空的音樂。

sections.heading: Frozen Music - Turning Vibration into Form
sections.body: Sound vanishes the moment it is made, which is exactly why it tempts a designer to hold it still. The study began with a homemade instrument of seeing, a barrel skin, a few sticks and a laser pointer, and the guidance pressed for evidence before invention: play the music, watch the light, record what it draws. The drum trembled and the beam answered with loops and knots that no hand would have chosen, giving the project a vocabulary taken straight from vibration. Translation came next and was treated as a question of material. Bent wire held the paths, stretched stockings turned them into smooth wave skins, and clear PVC, softened by heat, kept curves that fabric alone could not. Each material carried a different temper of the same song, taut, supple or glassy. Assembled within a white box, the pieces hang like a chord paused in mid-air, and the work leaves behind a simple, persuasive thought: listening closely enough can become a way of building.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝結的樂音-把振動化為形體
zh-Hant.body: 聲音在發出的瞬間便消逝，正因如此，設計者才會想要把它留住。這項研究從一件自製的「觀看樂器」開始：一面桶皮、幾根木棍與一支雷射筆；指導過程堅持先取證據、再談創造，播放音樂，觀察光，記錄它畫下的軌跡。鼓面顫動，光束以任何手都不會選擇的線圈與結回應，為專題提供一套直接取自振動的語彙。接著是轉譯，而轉譯被當作材料的問題。彎折的鐵絲承載路徑，拉伸的絲襪把路徑化為平滑的波面，受熱軟化的透明PVC則保住布料無法維持的曲線。每種材料都帶著同一首歌的不同性情：緊繃、柔韌或晶瑩。組裝在白色盒中，這些構件像一個停在半空的和弦；作品留下一個簡單而有說服力的想法：聽得夠專注，本身就可以成為一種建造。

pins.title: Microbial Space
pins.description:
Microorganisms seen through a lens are recreated in gelatin and glycerin, then pressed into white clay to form a living cave.

Model | Material study | Soft clay, glycerin, gelatin, water | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 微生物空間
zh-Hant.description:
透過鏡頭看見的微生物，以明膠與甘油重現，再嵌入白色黏土，形成一座有生命的洞穴。

模型｜材料研究｜軟陶土、甘油、明膠、水｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Microorganisms seen through a magnifying lens show rich shapes and colours. The project asks how those tiny forms can be built into a space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 透過放大鏡看見的微生物，呈現豐富的形狀與色彩。這個專題探問，這些微小形體如何被建造成空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied images of microorganisms and mixed water, glycerin and gelatin with colour. Thin sheets of gel copied the cells, bubbles and membranes.
captions: Microscope images of microorganisms that inspired the forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究微生物的影像，並把水、甘油與明膠和顏料調和。薄薄的凝膠片模仿細胞、氣泡與薄膜。
captions: 啟發造形的微生物顯微影像。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Soft white clay was kneaded into curved sheets of many shapes. The gel pieces were pressed into the clay while it was still soft.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色軟陶土被揉捏成各種形狀的彎曲薄片。凝膠片趁黏土仍柔軟時被嵌入其中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: All the pieces were joined into one 450 mm cave of holes and windows. Coloured gel glows in each opening like cells under glass.
captions: The microbial space from the front.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 所有構件被組合成一座450毫米、布滿孔洞與窗口的洞穴。彩色凝膠在每個開口中發光，如同玻片下的細胞。

sections.heading: A World Beneath the Lens - Building with the Invisible
sections.body: Some of the richest landscapes are too small to see, and this project chose to treat them as sites. It opened with images of cells and membranes, and the guidance soon moved the student from looking to making, asking that every colour and texture be proven in a material of its own. Water, glycerin and gelatin became a small laboratory: poured, tinted and left to set, they produced bubble skins, marbled sheets and translucent films that echo life under the lens without copying it. The next step was to give those fragments a body. Soft white clay was kneaded into curling shells, and the gel pieces were pressed in while the clay still yielded, so that each opening holds a glowing specimen. Joined together, the shells form a cave about half a metre across, pierced with windows and threaded with tiny red figures for scale. Walking through it in the imagination, one senses how architecture might borrow the patience and invention of the microscopic world.

zh-Hant.heading: 鏡下世界-以不可見之物建造
zh-Hant.body: 有些最豐富的地景小到肉眼看不見，這個專題選擇把它們當作基地。研究從細胞與薄膜的影像開始，指導過程很快把學生從觀看帶向製作，要求每一種色彩與質地都必須在專屬的材料中被證明。水、甘油與明膠組成一間小小的實驗室：澆注、染色、靜置凝固，產生氣泡膜、大理石紋薄片與半透明的膜，呼應鏡頭下的生命，卻不加以複製。下一步是為這些碎片找到身體。白色軟陶土被揉捏成捲曲的殼，凝膠片趁黏土仍柔軟時嵌入，使每個開口都承載一枚發光的標本。殼片組合後形成一座寬約半米的洞穴，布滿窗口，並以細小的紅色人偶標示尺度。在想像中穿行其間，人們能感受到建築如何向微觀世界借取耐心與創造力。

pins.title: Spider
pins.description:
A childhood fear of spiders becomes a giant frame of umbrella ribs, tangled wire and mesh, held steady by lines like a web.

Model and paint studies | Emotion study | Umbrella ribs, iron wire, mesh, salt, acrylic paint, cotton | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 蜘蛛
zh-Hant.description:
童年對蜘蛛的恐懼，化為由傘骨、糾結鐵絲與鐵絲網組成的巨大骨架，並以如蛛絲般的線穩住。

模型與繪畫研究｜情緒研究｜傘骨、鐵絲、鐵絲網、鹽、壓克力顏料、棉花｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Spiders have frightened the student since childhood. The project builds a spider in order to face that fear and break through it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 蜘蛛從童年起就讓學生感到害怕。這個專題透過建造一隻蜘蛛，來面對並突破這份恐懼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied webs and made paint studies with salt, acrylic, water and cotton. Splashes and stains showed how a web feels rather than how it looks.
captions: Photos of spider webs that inspired the wire web.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究蛛網，並以鹽、壓克力顏料、水與棉花進行繪畫研究。潑灑與暈染表現的是蛛網給人的感受，而非它的外觀。
captions: 啟發鐵絲網的蜘蛛網照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Umbrella ribs became the legs and claws, and a wire net formed the head and body. Wire was kneaded into a coiled tail.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 傘骨成為腳與爪，鐵絲網構成頭部與身體。鐵絲被揉捏成捲曲的尾部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Lines like threads hold the 600 mm spider steady in its corner. Under light, its shadow spreads across the walls like a web.
captions: The spider frame from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 如絲線般的拉線把這隻600毫米高的蜘蛛穩穩固定在角落。在光線下，它的影子像蛛網一樣在牆上展開。

sections.heading: Taming the Web - Building Toward What Frightens
sections.body: Fear tends to grow in the dark, and one way to shrink it is to bring it into the light and measure it. The project began from a fear held since childhood, and the guidance treated that feeling not as an obstacle but as a brief, asking the student to study the thing that frightened rather than avoid it. Paint studies with salt, acrylic, water and cotton came first, searching for the sensation of a web, its scatter, its sticky density, its trembling edges. Building followed with a practical, almost disarming choice: the ribs of an umbrella became legs and claws, a wire net shaped the head and body, and kneaded wire curled into a tail. Taut lines then fixed the creature in a corner, so that it could no longer move unexpectedly. Lit from one side, the frame throws a vast web of shadow across the walls, beautiful rather than threatening. The work suggests that making can be a form of courage, turning dread into structure one joint at a time.

zh-Hant.heading: 馴服蛛網-朝恐懼走去的建造
zh-Hant.body: 恐懼往往在黑暗中滋長，縮小它的一種方式，是把它帶到光下加以丈量。這個專題始於一份從童年延續至今的恐懼；指導過程並未把這份情緒視為障礙，而是把它當作設計任務，要求學生研究令人害怕的事物，而非迴避它。首先是以鹽、壓克力顏料、水與棉花進行的繪畫研究，尋找蛛網的感受：它的散落、黏稠的密度與顫動的邊緣。接著的建造做了一個務實、近乎令人卸下心防的選擇：傘骨成為腳與爪，鐵絲網塑出頭部與身體，揉捏的鐵絲捲成尾巴。繃緊的拉線再把這隻生物固定在角落，使它不再能出其不意地移動。從一側打光，骨架在牆上投下一張巨大的影之網，美麗而非威脅。作品提示，製作可以是一種勇氣，把畏懼一節一節地化為結構。

pins.title: Cat Space
pins.description:
Photos of a room taken from a cat's height are cut into shapes, then curled in thin PVC into a shelter and playground for cats.

Model and drawings | Animal space | PVC sheet, foam board, clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 貓的空間
zh-Hant.description:
以貓的高度拍下房間，剪出形狀，再以薄PVC片捲曲成貓的庇護所與遊樂場。

模型與繪圖｜動物空間｜PVC片、泡沫板、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People see a room from one height and rarely bend to look again. The project asks what a room becomes when it is read through the low, curious eyes of a cat.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 人們總從同一個高度看房間，很少彎下身再看一次。這個專題探問，當房間透過貓低矮而好奇的眼睛被閱讀時，會變成什麼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student photographed a room from a cat's eye level and cut interesting shapes from the prints. The pieces were arranged and rearranged into a collage, and its outline was traced as a drawing.
captions: Photos of the room taken from a cat's eye level.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從貓的視線高度拍攝房間，並從照片中剪下有趣的形狀。這些碎片被反覆排列成拼貼，再把輪廓描成線稿。
captions: 從貓的視線高度拍攝的房間照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Shapes were cut from thin foldable sheets and curled to the right curve before being glued together. Narrow tubes became paths to walk on, and hollow upward forms became climbing trees.
captions: Curling and gluing the PVC sheets by hand.
Curled sheets and a clay cat.
An opening like a cat tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 形狀從可彎折的薄片上切下，捲成合適的曲度後再黏合。狹窄的管狀成為可以行走的小徑，鏤空向上的形體則成為攀爬的貓跳台。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished shelter is a white tangle of ribbons, windows and stairs about forty centimetres tall. Spaces under the sheets stay dark and private, matching the hiding places cats love.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的庇護所是一團白色的緞帶、窗洞與階梯，高約四十公分。片材下方的空間保持幽暗而隱密，正對應貓喜愛的藏身之處。

sections.heading: Low Horizons - Designing from a Cat's Eye
sections.body: Architecture usually begins at the height of a standing adult, yet much of a room is lived closer to the floor. This project lowered the horizon on purpose. The guidance asked the student to photograph a familiar room from the eye level of a cat, then to treat each print not as a picture but as raw material, cutting out fragments, shuffling them and tracing their outlines until a new plan appeared. That plan was carried into space through thin sheets curled by hand, so that every curve kept the memory of a cut edge. Narrow tubes turned into paths along which a small body could balance, hollow upward forms became trees for climbing, and the shaded pockets beneath the sheets offered the privacy an animal seeks. The method is simple but searching: by changing the viewpoint before changing the form, the work shows that empathy for another body can be a rigorous tool of design, able to turn an ordinary room into a landscape of ribbons, shadows and refuges.

zh-Hant.heading: 低處的視野-從貓的眼睛出發設計
zh-Hant.body: 建築通常從成年人站立的高度開始，然而一個房間有許多部分其實是貼近地面被使用的。這個專題刻意壓低了地平線。指導過程要求學生從貓的視線高度拍攝熟悉的房間，再把每張照片視為原料而非影像：剪下碎片、反覆排列、描出輪廓，直到新的平面浮現。這份平面再透過以手捲曲的薄片帶入空間，使每一道曲線都保留著剪裁邊緣的記憶。狹窄的管道成為小小身體可以保持平衡的路徑，鏤空向上的形體成為攀爬的樹，片材下方的陰影角落則提供動物所尋求的隱密。方法簡單卻充滿探索：先改變視角，再改變形體，作品證明對另一種身體的同理可以成為嚴謹的設計工具，把平凡的房間化為緞帶、陰影與庇護交織的地景。

pins.title: Cobalt Chloride Equilibrium
pins.description:
A chemistry experiment in which pink turns to blue becomes a tower of wooden and clear acrylic triangles caught in one moment of change.

Model and studies | Science study | Wooden boards, acrylic boards, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 氯化鈷平衡
zh-Hant.description:
一場由粉紅轉為藍色的化學實驗，化為一座以木質與透明壓克力三角形構成的塔，凝結在變化的瞬間。

模型與研究｜科學研究｜木板、壓克力板、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: When acid is added to a pink cobalt solution, blue spreads through the test tube while the pink slowly fades. The project tries to hold that brief, lively moment of reaction in a solid form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 當酸加入粉紅色的鈷溶液，藍色會擴散到整支試管，粉紅則逐漸消退。這個專題試圖把這短暫而生動的反應瞬間，凝固為實體形式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student observed the colour moving through the tube and translated the drops into a web of points and lines. A drawing turned the swirling liquid into a cluster of triangles.
captions: Textbook diagrams of the cobalt chloride equilibrium and its molecules.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生觀察顏色在試管中流動，並把液滴轉譯為點與線的網絡。一張圖把旋動的液體化為一簇三角形。
captions: 氯化鈷平衡及其分子的教科書圖解。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small wire frames with wooden and acrylic faces were tested in many combinations. Each study was photographed with its shadow to judge how solid and clear parts balanced.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以鐵絲為框、貼上木片與壓克力的小型構件，被嘗試了許多種組合。每個研究都連同陰影一起拍攝，以判斷實與透的部分如何平衡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the finished tower, wooden triangles at the core stand for the new blue compound, while clear acrylic around them stands for the pink that has not yet reacted. Coloured versions show the same change in pink and blue light.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在完成的塔中，核心的木質三角形代表新生成的藍色化合物，周圍的透明壓克力則代表尚未反應的粉紅。彩色版本以粉紅與藍色的光呈現同樣的變化。

sections.heading: Frozen Reaction - Building a Moment of Change
sections.body: Chemistry is usually learned as equations, balanced on paper and soon forgotten, but a reaction seen in a test tube can stay in the mind for years. This project began with such a memory: a pink solution turning blue as a single drop of acid spreads through it. The guidance encouraged the student to treat the experiment as a spatial event rather than a formula, watching how colour travels and recording it as points, lines and finally triangles. Small frames of wire, wood and acrylic were tested in many arrangements and judged by their shadows, until a clear logic emerged. Dense wooden triangles gather at the core like the newly formed compound, while transparent pieces drift outward like the part of the solution still waiting to change. The tower therefore freezes an instant that in the laboratory lasts only seconds. It shows how a scientific idea can become an architecture of balance, where the solid and the clear, the finished and the pending, lean against one another.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固的反應-為變化的瞬間造形
zh-Hant.body: 化學通常以方程式學習，在紙上配平之後很快就被遺忘，但在試管中親眼看見的反應卻能在心中停留多年。這個專題從這樣的記憶開始：一滴酸擴散開來，粉紅色的溶液隨之轉藍。指導過程鼓勵學生把實驗視為一場空間事件而非公式，觀察顏色如何移動，並把它記錄為點、線，最後成為三角形。以鐵絲、木片與壓克力組成的小框架被嘗試了許多種排列，並以陰影來判斷，直到清楚的邏輯浮現。密實的木質三角形聚集在核心，如同新生成的化合物；透明的片材向外漂散，如同仍在等待改變的溶液。於是這座塔凝固了實驗室中僅持續數秒的一瞬。它說明科學的概念可以成為一種平衡的建築，實與透、完成與未完成，在其中彼此倚靠。

pins.title: Quantified Polonaise
pins.description:
Every note of a piano piece is measured by how hard it is played and rebuilt as a 3D-printed and paper landscape on a laser-cut base.

Models | Music study | 3D printing, Dutch paper, wooden strips, acrylic boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 量化的波蘭舞曲
zh-Hant.description:
依照彈奏的力度量測一首鋼琴曲的每一個音符，再以3D列印與紙片重建為雷射切割底座上的地景。

模型｜音樂研究｜3D列印、荷蘭紙、木條、壓克力板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Music is usually judged by ear, as something felt rather than measured. The project asks what a piano piece would look like if each note were given an exact height, width and shape.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 音樂通常以耳朵評判，是被感受而非被量測的東西。這個專題探問，如果每個音符都被賦予精確的高度、寬度與形狀，一首鋼琴曲會是什麼模樣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student modelled the notes on a computer according to the dynamics used when playing the piece, then 3D printed them. A base of acrylic boards was laser cut with sunken shapes that match each printed note.
captions: Sheet-music excerpts from the Chopin polonaise that the model quantifies.
A low view of the printed notes.
The printed notes from the side.
A detail of the printed notes.
The end of the printed piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生依照自己彈奏時的力度在電腦上建模音符，再以3D列印輸出。壓克力板組成的底座經雷射切割，留下與每個列印音符相對應的凹陷形狀。
captions: 模型所量化的蕭邦波蘭舞曲樂譜片段。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second model translated the same piece into thin paper pieces and wooden strips. The taller a piece, the stronger the force on the keys at that moment.
captions: The paper model on the diagonal.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二個模型把同一首曲子轉譯為薄紙片與木條。紙片越高，代表那一刻按下琴鍵的力量越強。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished models rise and fall like a city skyline that follows the music from beginning to end. Read together, they let a listener see the whole piece and its changing force at a glance.
captions: The paper model in the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型起伏如一道城市天際線，從頭到尾跟隨著音樂。兩個模型一起閱讀，讓聆聽者能一眼看見整首曲子及其變化的力度。

sections.heading: Measured Music - A Skyline of Touch
sections.body: Music is often described as something that cannot be held, a feeling that vanishes the moment it is heard. This project asked what would happen if a performance were treated instead as data with dimensions. The guidance began from the student's own hands at the keyboard: every note was assigned a height according to how firmly it was struck, and these values were modelled, printed and set into a base whose laser-cut hollows received each piece exactly. A second version translated the same measurements into thin paper and wooden strips, lighter and more fragile, so that loud passages rise like towers and soft ones settle into low terraces. Seen from one end, the work resembles a skyline. Seen from above, it becomes a score that can be read without sound. The result offers a different kind of beauty, concise and rational rather than emotional, and suggests that careful measurement, far from draining music of feeling, can reveal the hidden architecture already present in every phrase.

zh-Hant.heading: 被量測的音樂-觸鍵的天際線
zh-Hant.body: 音樂常被形容為無法掌握之物，一種在聽見的瞬間便消逝的感受。這個專題探問，若把一次演奏視為具有尺度的資料，會發生什麼。指導過程從學生自己在琴鍵上的雙手開始：每個音符依照按下的力度被賦予高度，這些數值被建模、列印，再嵌入一座底座，底座上雷射切割的凹槽恰好承接每一個構件。第二個版本把同樣的量測轉譯為更輕、更脆弱的薄紙與木條，使響亮的段落如高塔升起，柔和的段落則沉為低矮的台地。從一端看去，作品像一道天際線；從上方俯視，它成為一份無聲也能閱讀的樂譜。成果呈現另一種美，簡潔而理性，並暗示細心的量測不但不會抽乾音樂的情感，反而能揭示每個樂句中早已存在的隱藏建築。

pins.title: Four Stages of Salvation
pins.description:
A story of being trapped, breaking free, rebelling and being saved becomes one tall figure of clay, wire, yarn and pipe cleaners.

Model and sketch | Story study | Air-dry clay, wooden strips, iron wire, yarn, cellophane, pipe cleaners, cotton | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 救贖的四個階段
zh-Hant.description:
被困、突破、反抗與獲救的故事，化為一座由黏土、鐵絲、毛線與毛根構成的高大形體。

模型與草圖｜故事研究｜輕黏土、木條、鐵絲、毛線、玻璃紙、毛根、棉花｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A story about many worlds taught the student that the meaning of living is to cherish those who accept the mess of the world out of love. The project turns that lesson into a single figure built in four stages.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個關於多重世界的故事讓學生體會到，活著的意義在於珍惜那些因為愛而包容世界混亂的人。這個專題把這份體會化為一座分四個階段構成的形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A labelled sketch planned the parts: a rocky pedestal, a coloured net, rising pyramids, spheres and a knitted eye at the top. Each part was linked to one stage of the story.
captions: A film-strip of stills from the movie that inspired the four stages.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張標註草圖規劃了各個部分：岩石般的底座、彩色的網、上升的金字塔、球體，以及頂端編織的眼睛。每個部分都對應故事中的一個階段。
captions: 啟發四個階段的電影劇照膠卷。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A pedestal of paper clay and a net of yarn and pipe cleaners stand for the trap of high expectations. Wooden pyramids then push up through the net, showing a moment of release.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙黏土底座與毛線、毛根編成的網，象徵高期待所形成的牢籠。木質金字塔隨後向上穿出網面，呈現解脫的一刻。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three spheres show stages of fighting against the world, and a circle of wire, yarn and googly eyes forms the final salvation. Standing about seventy-five centimetres tall, the figure reads from bottom to top like the story itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三個球體呈現與世界對抗的各個階段，鐵絲、毛線與活動眼珠構成的圓環則是最終的救贖。這座約七十五公分高的形體，由下而上如故事本身般被閱讀。

sections.heading: Rising Through the Net - Story as Vertical Structure
sections.body: Stories are usually told in time, one scene after another, but this project asked how a story might be told in height. The guidance led the student to break a narrative of despair and recovery into four stages and to give each stage a material and a level. At the base, a rough pedestal of clay and a tight net of yarn express the weight of expectations that hold a young person down. Above it, wooden pyramids pierce the net, a structural gesture for the moment when pressure suddenly loses its grip. Higher still, bristling spheres carry the restless energy of resistance, and at the top a luminous ring of wire and bright fibres closes the figure like a gesture of embrace. Read from bottom to top, the work becomes a vertical sentence in which every joint and knot carries meaning. It demonstrates how personal feeling can be organised with architectural clarity, so that a soft and colourful object still holds the logic of a tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 穿網而上-以故事為垂直結構
zh-Hant.body: 故事通常在時間中講述，一幕接著一幕；這個專題則探問故事如何在高度中被講述。指導過程引導學生把一段從絕望到復原的敘事拆成四個階段，並為每個階段賦予一種材料與一個層次。在底部，粗糙的黏土底座與緊密的毛線網，表達壓住年輕人的期待之重。在其上方，木質金字塔刺穿網面，以結構的姿態呈現壓力忽然鬆手的瞬間。再往上，蓬亂的球體承載反抗時躁動的能量；最頂端，一圈以鐵絲與鮮亮纖維構成的光環收束整個形體，如同一次擁抱。由下而上閱讀，作品成為一個垂直的句子，每個接點與繩結都承載意義。它證明個人的情感可以用建築般的清晰來組織，使一件柔軟而多彩的物件仍保有一座塔的邏輯。

pins.title: Iteration through Joinery
pins.description:
Basic cubes are hollowed, rotated and linked by interlocking wood-joint logic, studied in renders and drawings and printed as a physical model.

Digital model, drawings and print | Form study | Rhino, 3D print | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 以榫接推演
zh-Hant.description:
基本的立方體被挖空、旋轉，並以木作榫接的邏輯互相扣合，透過渲染與圖面研究，再列印成實體模型。

數位模型、圖面與列印｜形體研究｜Rhino、3D列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A plain cube holds many possible forms if it is cut, turned and repeated. The project looks for those forms while linking each cube to the next with the logic of traditional wooden joinery.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個簡單的立方體，若被切割、旋轉與重複，便蘊含許多可能的形式。這個專題在尋找這些形式的同時，以傳統木作榫接的邏輯把每個立方體與下一個連結起來。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Hollow cubes with notched walls were modelled so that one could slot into another like delicate wooden joints. Rotation drawings recorded how the object and its details turn in space.
captions: Render, rotation drawing, line logic and animation frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生建模出牆面帶有缺口的中空立方體，使它們能像精巧的木榫般彼此嵌合。旋轉圖記錄物件與細部在空間中如何轉動。
captions: 渲染圖、旋轉圖、線框邏輯與動畫影格。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rendered views, an unrolled elevation and a composite plan and section tested the joints from every side. Animation frames showed the cubes gathering one by one into a chain.
captions: Second render, detail rotation and animation frames.
Zoom-in render, unrolled elevation, plan and section.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 渲染視角、展開立面以及平面與剖面的綜合圖，從各個方向檢驗接合。動畫影格呈現立方體如何一個接一個聚合成鏈。
captions: 第二張渲染、細部旋轉與動畫影格。
放大渲染、展開立面、平面與剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The design was printed as a physical model and photographed in strong light to show its atmosphere. Deep openings and interlocking walls cast sharp shadows that make the small object feel like a building.
captions: A close-up of the printed cubes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 設計被列印為實體模型，並在強光下拍攝以呈現其氛圍。深邃的開口與交扣的牆面投下銳利的陰影，使這件小物件感覺像一棟建築。

sections.heading: Locked Volumes - Joinery as a Method of Iteration
sections.body: Iteration in design is often treated as endless variation, but variation without a rule quickly loses meaning. This project found its rule in an old craft. The guidance asked the student to start from the simplest solid, a cube, and to explore how far it could be hollowed, notched and turned while still being able to lock firmly into its neighbour, following the patient logic of wooden joints that hold without nails. Each step was tested in more than one language of representation: rendered views gave weight and light, rotation drawings tracked movement, an unrolled elevation laid every face flat, and animation frames revealed how single pieces gather into a chain. The printed model then returned the study to physical space, where deep openings and crisp shadows give a palm-sized object the presence of a building. The work suggests that inherited craft knowledge, when read as a structural principle rather than a decorative style, can steer digital experiment toward forms that are both inventive and convincing.

zh-Hant.heading: 互扣的量體-以榫接作為推演方法
zh-Hant.body: 設計中的推演常被視為無止境的變化，但沒有規則的變化很快便失去意義。這個專題在一門古老的工藝中找到了它的規則。指導過程要求學生從最簡單的實體——立方體——開始，探索它能被挖空、刻出缺口與旋轉到什麼程度，同時仍能牢牢扣入相鄰的構件，遵循不用釘子也能穩固的木作榫接那份耐心的邏輯。每一步都以不只一種表現語言來檢驗：渲染圖賦予重量與光線，旋轉圖追蹤運動，展開立面把每個面攤平，動畫影格則揭示單一構件如何聚合成鏈。列印模型再把研究帶回實體空間，深邃的開口與俐落的陰影，讓一件掌心大小的物件擁有建築般的存在感。作品暗示，承襲而來的工藝知識若被讀作結構原則而非裝飾風格，便能引導數位實驗走向既有創意又令人信服的形式。

pins.title: Stairs of Unspoken Love
pins.description:
Stairs and arches wrapped in loops of wire and clear strips turn a quiet story of hidden feelings and two musical tones into a white tower.

Model | Story and music study | PVC, Dutch paper, PVC strips, iron wire, acrylic | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無聲之愛的階梯
zh-Hant.description:
被鐵絲與透明條帶纏繞的階梯與拱，把一段隱藏情感的安靜故事與兩種樂音化為一座白色的塔。

模型｜故事與音樂研究｜PVC、荷蘭紙、PVC條、鐵絲、壓克力｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Some feelings are deep but never said out loud. The project asks how the unspoken bond between two people could be built as stairs, arches and sound.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 有些情感很深，卻從未說出口。這個專題探問，兩個人之間未曾言明的連結，如何被建造成階梯、拱與聲音。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student linked the story to two wind instruments whose tones answer each other. Stairs and arches were chosen to stand for a hidden closeness and for the ensemble of brass and woodwind.
captions: A still from the anime film that inspired the stair tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把故事與兩種彼此應答的管樂器音色連結起來。階梯與拱被用來代表隱藏的親近，以及銅管與木管的合奏。
captions: 啟發這座樓梯塔的動畫電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: White stairs climb and turn around a central core, so paths meet and part without fully joining. Loops of iron wire stand for one tone, and a loop of clear acrylic strips stands for the other.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色的階梯環繞中央核心攀升與轉折，使路徑相遇又分開，卻始終沒有完全相連。鐵絲圈代表其中一種音色，透明壓克力條組成的圈則代表另一種。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower is about sixty centimetres tall and is wrapped in a storm of fine strips. The hesitant wire and the bold acrylic loop circle the same stairs, like two voices that finally sound together.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔高約六十公分，被一陣細條帶的風暴所包覆。遲疑的鐵絲與大膽的壓克力圈環繞同一組階梯，如兩個終於一起響起的聲音。

sections.heading: Two Voices - Stairs That Almost Meet
sections.body: Some relationships are defined less by what is spoken than by what is held back, and architecture has its own ways of expressing that restraint. This project explored them through stairs. The guidance encouraged the student to treat a quiet story of mutual but hidden affection as a problem of circulation: two routes climbing the same white core, turning, passing close, yet never quite merging into a single path. Arches open and close along the way like pauses in a conversation. The story was then given sound. One loop of thin iron wire traces the light, hesitant voice of one instrument, while a broader loop of clear acrylic strips carries the steadier tone of another, and both spiral around the same structure as if trying to find the same key. From a distance, the tower appears caught in a gust of fine lines. Up close, it reveals a careful score of steps and gaps. The work shows how circulation, rhythm and material can carry emotion as precisely as words, perhaps more gently.

zh-Hant.heading: 兩個聲音-幾乎相遇的階梯
zh-Hant.body: 有些關係的定義，與其說來自說出口的話，不如說來自被按捺住的部分；而建築也有表達這種克制的方式。這個專題透過階梯探索它們。指導過程鼓勵學生把一段彼此在意卻隱而不宣的故事，視為動線的問題：兩條路線攀上同一個白色核心，轉折、擦身而過，卻始終沒有真正匯成一條路。沿途的拱開了又合，如同對話中的停頓。故事隨後被賦予聲音。一圈細鐵絲描繪一種樂器輕盈而遲疑的聲音，一圈較寬的透明壓克力條則承載另一種樂器較為沉穩的音色，兩者盤旋於同一座結構，彷彿試著找到同一個調。遠看，塔像是被一陣細線的風捲住；近看，它展現一份由階與隙組成的細膩樂譜。作品說明動線、節奏與材料能像文字一樣精確地承載情感，甚至更為溫柔。

pins.title: Tower of Conflict and Truce
pins.description:
A metre-tall tower tells a story of struggle and reconciliation in stacked layers of painted cubes, circuit boards, tubes and coloured light.

Model and sketches | Story study | Wooden strips, wire, cotton, cardboard, LED beads, PVC, foam, window film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 衝突與和解之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一座高逾一米的塔，以彩繪方塊、電路板、管材與彩光層層堆疊，講述一段抗爭與和解的故事。

模型與草圖｜故事研究｜木條、鐵絲、棉花、紙板、LED燈珠、PVC、泡沫塊、窗膜｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The layered tower in white light.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A story of two opposing kinds of beings, one ruled by feeling and one by logic, unfolds in several stages. The project asks how such a story could be stacked into one tower, with each layer telling a different chapter.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一段關於兩種對立存在的故事，一方由情感主導，一方由邏輯主導，分成數個階段展開。這個專題探問，如何把這樣的故事堆疊成一座塔，讓每一層講述不同的篇章。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student chose the most vivid moments of the story and sketched four to five layers, noting a material and a colour for each. Early tests tried clay fragments and folded foam blocks.
captions: The poster of the film that inspired the tower.
Film stills chosen for parts 1 and 3 of the tower.
Film stills chosen for parts 2 and 3 of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生挑選故事中最鮮明的片段，畫出四到五層的草圖，並為每一層標註材料與顏色。早期試驗嘗試了黏土碎片與摺疊的泡沫塊。
captions: 啟發這座塔的電影海報。
為塔的第一與第三部分挑選的電影劇照。
為塔的第二與第三部分挑選的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: At the base, grey structures stand for the logical side and dripping painted cubes for the emotional side, with a broken tangle between them. Above, circuit boards, clear bubbles and green lights show a captive system, then white tubes and a ring of panels show a last refuge under attack.
captions: The middle layer in green light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 底層以灰色結構代表邏輯的一方，以滴染的彩繪方塊代表情感的一方，兩者之間是一團破碎的交纏。往上，電路板、透明泡泡與綠光呈現被囚禁的系統，再往上，白色管材與一圈板片呈現遭受攻擊的最後庇護所。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A crown of shining coloured film ends the story with a sign of truce. Lit in white or green, the same tower changes mood from a crowded city to a glowing machine.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一頂閃耀的彩色窗膜之冠，以和解的象徵為故事作結。在白光或綠光下，同一座塔的氣氛從擁擠的城市轉變為發光的機器。

sections.heading: Stacked Chapters - A Tower That Tells a Story
sections.body: Narrative and architecture both unfold in sequence, yet a story moves through time while a building must hold everything at once. This project tried to reconcile the two by turning chapters into floors. The guidance asked the student to choose only the most charged moments of a long tale of struggle and to give each of them a layer, a material and a colour, so that reading the tower from bottom to top would feel like turning pages. Dripping painted cubes set against grey frames open the conflict between feeling and logic; circuit boards, clear bubbles and green light describe a system that holds its prisoners; white tubes and a ring of panels portray a final refuge under siege; and a crown of shimmering film closes with a fragile truce. Lighting completes the narrative, since the same object reads as a crowded settlement in white light and as a humming machine in green. The work shows how vertical order, material contrast and atmosphere can carry plot, turning a model into a quiet theatre of rising chapters.

zh-Hant.heading: 堆疊的篇章-會說故事的塔
zh-Hant.body: 敘事與建築都依序展開，然而故事在時間中流動，建築卻必須同時容納一切。這個專題嘗試把篇章轉化為樓層，以調和兩者。指導過程要求學生只從一段漫長的抗爭故事中挑選最具張力的時刻，並為每一刻賦予一層、一種材料與一種顏色，使人由下而上閱讀這座塔時，彷彿正在翻頁。滴染的彩繪方塊對比灰色的框架，揭開情感與邏輯的衝突；電路板、透明泡泡與綠光描繪一個囚禁其居民的系統；白色管材與一圈板片刻畫被圍困的最後庇護所；而一頂微微閃爍的窗膜之冠，以脆弱的和解作結。燈光完成了敘事：同一件物體在白光下讀來像擁擠的聚落，在綠光下則像嗡嗡作響的機器。作品說明垂直的秩序、材料的對比與氛圍能夠承載情節，把模型化為一座篇章層層上升的安靜劇場。

pins.title: Frozen Swing
pins.description:
The path of a swinging racket is traced as fans of thin sticks, built up into a structure, and then cut back into photo collages of a new space.

Model, drawings and collages | Motion study | Wooden sticks, paper, wire, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 凝固的揮拍
zh-Hant.description:
揮動球拍的軌跡被描繪為細木條組成的扇形，堆疊成結構，再被剪回照片拼貼，成為一個新的空間。

模型、繪圖與拼貼｜運動研究｜木條、紙、鐵絲、紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The swing fan model from above.
從上方看揮拍扇形模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Paintings and sculptures cannot move, yet they can still make people feel movement. The project asks whether a motionless model could show the swing of a racket and the arc of a ball.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 繪畫與雕塑無法移動，卻仍能讓人感受到動態。這個專題探問，一件靜止的模型能否呈現球拍的揮動與球的弧線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student watched the tracks of a racket in different strokes and drew them as fans of straight lines bending into arcs. A wave study tested how rows of sticks could follow a curve.
captions: Photos of a tennis swing, the motion the model traces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生觀察不同擊球動作中球拍的軌跡，並把它們畫成由直線彎成弧線的扇形。一份波浪研究則測試成排的木條如何沿著曲線排列。
captions: 網球揮拍的照片，即模型所描繪的動作。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks were glued to paper to make fan shapes, with the longest stick in the middle marking the hardest moment of impact. To become three-dimensional, the fans were lifted on thin legs and stacked higher.
captions: Shaping a stick fan by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條黏貼在紙上組成扇形，中央最長的一根標示撞擊最猛烈的瞬間。為了成為立體，扇形被細長的支腳撐起並往上堆疊。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Photos of the model from many angles were cut and rejoined into collages. With small human figures added, the fragments turn into an irregular space that could become parts of buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從各個角度拍攝的模型照片被剪下並重新拼合。加上小小的人形後，這些碎片化為一個不規則的空間，有潛力成為建築的局部。

sections.heading: Traces of a Stroke - From Motion to Form and Back
sections.body: Still images have long carried motion, from carved figures caught mid-step to paintings that seem to breathe, and this project set out to learn that skill through a single gesture: the swing of a racket. The guidance asked the student to watch the stroke carefully and to record it not as a picture of a body but as a field of lines, straight where the arm is firm and curving where speed takes over.
