Those drawings became fans of thin sticks, the longest placed at the instant of impact, and the fans were raised on slender legs until a flat diagram began to stand like a structure. The study then reversed direction. Photographs of the model, taken from many angles, were cut apart and reassembled into collages, where tiny figures reveal stairs, canopies and voids that never existed in the original object. Moving from four dimensions to three and finally to two, the work treats time as a design material, showing how the memory of a movement can open unexpected architectural space.

zh-Hant.heading: 一擊的痕跡-從運動到形體再回返
zh-Hant.body: 靜止的影像自古便承載著動態，從凝結於跨步之間的雕像，到彷彿正在呼吸的畫作；這個專題試圖透過一個單一的動作——揮拍——來學習這項本領。指導過程要求學生仔細觀察擊球，並把它記錄為一片線的場域，而非身體的圖像：手臂穩定處為直線，速度接管處則彎成弧線。這些圖轉化為細木條組成的扇形，最長的一根置於撞擊的瞬間，扇形再被細長的支腳撐起，讓平面的圖解逐漸站立成結構。研究隨後反轉方向：從各個角度拍攝的模型照片被剪開、重新拼合，小小的人形在拼貼中揭示出原本物件裡並不存在的階梯、頂棚與空隙。從四維到三維，再到二維，作品把時間當作設計的材料，說明一個動作的記憶能夠開啟出人意料的建築空間。

pins.title: Deconstructed Fragments
pins.description:
Photo fragments of everyday buildings are traced and abstracted, then rebuilt in white PVC and wooden sticks as a tilted, stair-linked cluster.

Model and drawings | Architecture study | Wooden strips, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 解構的碎片
zh-Hant.description:
日常建築的照片碎片被描繪並抽象化，再以白色PVC與木條重建為一簇傾斜、以階梯相連的量體。

模型與繪圖｜建築研究｜木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Deconstructivist architecture breaks away from right angles and symmetry. The project asks how ordinary buildings could be taken apart and reassembled into a lively, disordered whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 解構主義建築擺脫了直角與對稱。這個專題探問，平凡的建築如何被拆解，再重組為一個生動而無序的整體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student cut photos of everyday buildings into small pieces and stuck them together into a collage. The collage was traced as a line drawing and abstracted into a bold black and white composition.
captions: A collage of building photos used as the source material.
The building photos cut into fragments and stuck together.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把日常建築的照片剪成小片並拼貼在一起。拼貼再被描成線稿，並抽象為一幅強烈的黑白構成。
captions: 作為素材的建築照片拼貼。
將建築照片剪成碎片後重新拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: From the drawing, a hallway, a block of housing and distant towers were picked as elements. White PVC pieces and sticks were cut and joined step by step, with a disordered structure growing in the middle.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從線稿中挑出走廊、一棟住宅與遠方的高塔作為元素。白色PVC片與木條被逐步切割與接合，一個無序的結構在中央生長。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the finished model, slopes and a stairway link the isolated parts and balance the composition. Curved walls with cut windows wrap around a tilted stick tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在完成的模型中，坡道與階梯連結各自獨立的部分，並平衡整體構圖。開有窗洞的彎曲牆面環繞著一座傾斜的木條高塔。

sections.heading: Broken Order - Reassembling the Everyday
sections.body: The buildings of daily life are so familiar that their logic becomes invisible, and one way to see them again is to take them apart. This project used collage as that tool of dismantling. The guidance asked the student to cut photographs of ordinary streets into fragments and to rejoin them without regard for their original order, then to trace the result as a line drawing and finally to compress it into a stark composition of black and white masses. Each translation removed detail and sharpened structure, until a corridor, a slab of housing and a distant row of towers remained as clear architectural ideas. Rebuilt in white sheets and slender sticks, these ideas collided around a disordered core, while slopes and a stair were added to tie isolated fragments into one walkable ensemble. The result is unruly at first glance yet carefully balanced. It suggests that a vocabulary of breakage and tilt is not a style to imitate but a method of looking, one that lets the everyday city reappear as something strange and full of spatial possibility.

zh-Hant.heading: 破碎的秩序-重組日常
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活中的建築如此熟悉，以至於其邏輯變得隱形；重新看見它們的一種方式，便是把它們拆開。這個專題以拼貼作為拆解的工具。指導過程要求學生把平凡街道的照片剪成碎片，不顧原本的秩序重新拼合，再把結果描成線稿，最後壓縮為一幅由黑白量塊組成的鮮明構成。每一次轉譯都去除細節、凸顯結構，直到一條走廊、一片住宅與遠方一排高塔，成為清晰的建築概念。以白色片材與細木條重建後，這些概念圍繞一個無序的核心彼此碰撞，坡道與階梯則被加入，把孤立的碎片繫成一個可以行走的整體。成果乍看桀驁不馴，實則經過細心的平衡。它暗示，破碎與傾斜的語彙並非可供模仿的風格，而是一種觀看的方法，讓日常的城市以陌生而充滿空間可能的面貌重新浮現。

pins.title: Growth Record
pins.description:
Five small models trace a growth from confidence to breakthrough, each emotion given its own material, from iridescent film to stocking mesh and stick webs.

Models and paintings | Emotion study | Paper, wooden strips, wooden and PVC boards, chameleon window film, stone plastic clay, stockings | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 成長紀錄
zh-Hant.description:
五件小模型描繪一段從自信到突破的成長，每種情緒各有材料，從幻彩膜到絲襪網與木條網架。

模型與繪畫｜情緒研究｜紙、木條、木板、PVC板、幻彩窗膜、石塑黏土、絲襪｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Over several years of living away from home, a student moved slowly from pessimism to openness. The project asks how the stages of that inner change, and the pressure of surroundings on it, could be shown as architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在離家生活的數年間，學生從悲觀慢慢轉向開放。這個專題探問，這段內在轉變的各個階段，以及環境對它的壓力，能否以建築呈現。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Five stages were named: confident, mutation, pressured, lonely and breakthrough. Each was first explored as a small painting, testing colour and texture before any model was made.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 五個階段被命名為自信、突變、受壓、孤獨與突破。每一階段先以小幅繪畫探索，在製作模型前測試色彩與質感。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Iridescent film was bent into flowing shells for confidence, white boards stacked into crowded cells for mutation, and clay twisted with wire for pressure. Stocking mesh stretched in a stick frame stood for loneliness, and a web of sticks for breakthrough.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 幻彩膜被彎成流動的殼代表自信，白色板材堆成擁擠的格子代表突變，黏土與鐵絲扭結代表受壓。撐開在木框中的絲襪網代表孤獨，木條編成的網架則代表突破。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished set reads as one story in five rooms. Light, crowded, heavy, hollow and finally open, the models let a viewer walk through a change of mood.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的系列讀來像五個房間裡的一個故事。輕盈、擁擠、沉重、空洞，最後敞開，這些模型讓觀者走過一段心境的轉變。

sections.heading: Rooms of Feeling - Material as Inner Weather
sections.body: Emotion rarely arrives with a shape, so the first task of this project was to find one. The guidance asked the student to treat each stage of a personal growth as a kind of weather and to search for the material that could hold it, beginning not with plans but with small paintings where colour and texture could be felt before they were built. From those studies a sequence of rooms emerged. Shimmering film curves upward in a mood of confidence, white cells multiply until they crowd one another, clay knots tighten around wire under pressure, a dark mesh hangs in an empty frame, and at last a lattice of sticks opens into light. Read together, the five models form a passage rather than a gallery, because each atmosphere depends on the one before it. The exercise shows that architecture can record an interior life, and that choosing a material is already an act of interpretation, translating an invisible change of heart into weight, transparency and tension that others can sense.

zh-Hant.heading: 情感的房間-作為內在天候的材料
zh-Hant.body: 情緒很少帶著形狀而來，因此這個專題的第一項任務便是為它找到形狀。指導過程要求學生把個人成長的每一個階段視為一種天候，並尋找能夠承載它的材料；起點不是平面圖，而是小幅繪畫，讓色彩與質感在被建造之前先被感受。從這些研究中，一連串的房間逐漸浮現：閃爍的薄膜在自信中向上彎曲，白色格子不斷增生直到彼此擁擠，黏土在壓力下纏緊鐵絲，一張深色的網懸在空框之中，最後一片木條網架向光敞開。合而觀之，五件模型構成一條通道而非一座展廳，因為每一種氛圍都仰賴前一種而存在。這個練習說明建築能夠記錄內在的生命，而選擇材料本身已是一種詮釋，把看不見的心境轉變譯為旁人可以感知的重量、透明與張力。

pins.title: Chained Freedom
pins.description:
Hundreds of small stick blocks link and twist into a long chain that wanders freely yet stays inside one great closed cage.

Model and renders | Concept study | Wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鎖鏈中的自由
zh-Hant.description:
數百個小木條方塊相扣、扭轉，連成一條長鏈，自由蜿蜒，卻始終困在一座巨大的封閉牢籠之中。

模型與渲染圖｜概念研究｜木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Inspired by a story of people fighting for freedom, the project starts from a hard idea: the dream of complete freedom may only be a reachable delusion. It asks how one structure could feel both free and confined.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 受一則人們為自由而奮鬥的故事啟發，這個專題從一個沉重的想法出發：完全自由的夢想，或許只是一種觸手可及的錯覺。它探問，一個結構如何同時讓人感到自由與受困。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student found that a chain block, a hollow box of crossed sticks, could stand for this state of mind. Digital studies tested the block as stretched floors, cantilevers, hatched slabs and linked chains.
captions: Two paintings of the escape to freedom that inspired the chain.
A render of the chain cage.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生發現，以交錯木條組成的中空方塊——鎖鏈方塊——能夠代表這種心境。數位研究把方塊試作延伸的樓層、懸臂、斜紋樓板與相扣的鎖鏈。
captions: 啟發這條鎖鏈、描繪逃向自由的兩幅畫作。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Sticks were cut to different lengths and glued into blocks, one by one, day after day. The chain grew longer and its direction was turned on purpose, so that it twisted as if searching for a way out.
captions: The chain on the cutting mat.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條被切成不同長度，一個接一個、日復一日地黏成方塊。鎖鏈越來越長，方向也被刻意轉折，彷彿在扭動中尋找出路。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model is a large closed cage made of small blocks that extend and rotate. The blocks seem free to turn, yet the whole is held inside one boundary.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型是一座由小方塊延伸、旋轉而成的巨大封閉牢籠。方塊看似可以自由轉動，整體卻被限制在同一道邊界之內。

sections.heading: Links and Limits - The Shape of a Hopeful Cage
sections.body: Freedom is often imagined as open space, yet this project suggests it may look more like a chain that keeps moving. Starting from a reading about people who struggled for liberty, the student reached a sober conclusion, that complete freedom can be a delusion within reach but never quite held. The guidance encouraged turning that thought into a single repeated unit. A hollow block of crossed sticks became the module, and each new block was linked to the last by hand, slowly, so that the making itself became a form of endurance. The chain was steered to bend and twist, as though testing every direction for a way out, while the overall figure quietly closed upon itself into one great enclosure. The result holds two readings at once. Seen close, every block turns with its own small liberty; seen whole, the line returns to its boundary. In that tension the model offers a modest hope, that persistence and movement still matter even when the outer walls remain.

zh-Hant.heading: 鏈結與界限-懷抱希望的牢籠
zh-Hant.body: 自由常被想像為開闊的空間，這個專題卻暗示，它或許更像一條不停移動的鎖鏈。從一段關於人們爭取自由的閱讀出發，學生得出一個清醒的結論：完全的自由可能是觸手可及、卻永遠握不住的錯覺。指導過程鼓勵把這個想法化為單一的重複單元。一個以交錯木條組成的中空方塊成為模組，每個新方塊都以手工緩慢地扣上前一個，使製作本身成為一種堅持。鎖鏈被引導彎折、扭轉，彷彿在每個方向試探出路，整體形態卻悄悄地自我閉合，成為一座巨大的圍籠。成果同時容納兩種讀法：近看，每個方塊都以自己的小小自由轉動；遠看，線條終究回到它的邊界。在這份張力之中，模型提出一種謙和的希望：即使外牆仍在，堅持與移動依然有其意義。

pins.title: The Moment of Precision
pins.description:
Three shooting stances are reduced to balance triangles, extruded into white solids and gathered into one dense cluster of leaning planes.

Models and diagrams | Balance study | PVC boards, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 精準的瞬間
zh-Hant.description:
三種射擊姿勢被簡化為平衡三角形，擠出為白色量體，再聚集成一簇由傾斜板面構成的密集量體。

模型與圖解｜平衡研究｜PVC板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In target shooting, prone, kneeling and standing stances each depend on a different kind of balance. The project asks how these balances could become architectural space that people feel in their own bodies.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在射擊運動中，臥姿、跪姿與立姿各自依賴不同的平衡。這個專題探問，這些平衡如何化為人們能以身體感受的建築空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each stance was traced as a set of triangles linking the points where the body and the rifle find support. Three diagrams, A, B and C, show tall, compact and long low balances.
captions: Figures of the prone, kneeling and standing positions.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每一種姿勢都被描繪為一組三角形，連結身體與槍枝獲得支撐的點。A、B、C三張圖解分別呈現高聳、緊湊與低長的平衡。
captions: 氣步槍射擊姿勢的照片。
臥姿、跪姿與立姿的示意圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The triangles were extruded into solids and combined in many ways. Small white models tested leaning walls, cantilevers and wedges, each giving a different sense of steadiness.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角形被擠出為量體，並以多種方式組合。小型白色模型試驗傾斜的牆、懸臂與楔形，各自帶來不同的穩定感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model gathers many solids into one cluster, like a body shifting its posture to find the best balance. A render shows the same idea as a stacked tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把眾多量體聚成一簇，如同身體調整姿勢以尋找最佳平衡。一張渲染圖則把同樣的概念呈現為堆疊的高塔。

sections.heading: Held Still - Balance as a Spatial Language
sections.body: A precise shot depends on a moment of perfect stillness, and that stillness is built from balance rather than strength. This project tried to give that hidden structure a visible form. The guidance asked the student to forget the image of the athlete and attend only to the points of support, drawing lines between elbow, knee, foot and rifle until each stance became a small constellation of triangles. Tall and narrow, compact and folded, long and low, the three diagrams already suggested different spatial characters. Extruded into white solids, they were combined again and again, and each small model revealed a new sensation, whether a wall leaning just beyond comfort or a slab hovering on a single support. The final cluster gathers these experiments into one restless figure, recording the many adjustments a body makes before it settles. The work shows how a sporting discipline can become a design method, and how balance, often felt but rarely seen, can be shaped into planes that invite the body to respond.

zh-Hant.heading: 屏息之間-作為空間語言的平衡
zh-Hant.body: 精準的一擊仰賴一瞬間的完全靜止，而這份靜止來自平衡，而非力量。這個專題試圖為那隱藏的結構賦予可見的形式。指導過程要求學生暫時放下運動員的形象，只關注支撐點，在手肘、膝蓋、腳與槍枝之間連線，直到每一種姿勢都成為由三角形組成的小小星座。高而窄、緊湊而摺疊、長而低，三張圖解已暗示出不同的空間性格。擠出為白色量體後，它們被一再重組，每一件小模型都揭示一種新的感受，無論是一面恰好越過舒適界線的斜牆，或是一片僅靠單點支撐而懸浮的板。最終的量體群把這些實驗收攏為一個躁動的形態，記錄身體在安定下來之前所做的種種調整。作品說明一項運動的紀律能夠成為設計方法，而常被感受、卻少被看見的平衡，也能塑造成邀請身體回應的板面。

pins.title: Hexahedron and Rectangular Prisms
pins.description:
A small folly cuts and folds intersecting cubes and prisms in white and violet paper, shaping uneven surfaces that bend the light.

Model and drawings | Folly study | Bristol paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 六面體與長方稜柱
zh-Hant.description:
一座小型裝置以白色與紫色紙張切割、摺疊相互交錯的立方體與稜柱，塑造出能彎折光線的起伏表面。

模型與繪圖｜小型構築研究｜卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A folly is a small building in a landscape, made more for looking and feeling than for use. The project asks how the meeting of a cube and rectangular prisms could frame views and guide light.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 小型構築是景觀中的小建築，存在更多是為了觀看與感受，而非使用。這個專題探問，立方體與長方稜柱的交會如何框出視野並引導光線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Plan and elevation sketches tested where the prisms would cut through the cube. Line drawings then showed the solids as wireframes, with triangles slicing across their faces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 平面與立面草圖測試稜柱會在何處穿過立方體。線圖接著把量體表現為線框，三角形斜切過它們的表面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: White paper studies folded the intersections into sharp crystal forms. Violet and lavender sheets were then added to mark where two similar squares blend together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色紙張研究把交會處摺成尖銳的晶體形態。接著加入紫色與淡紫色紙張，標示兩個相似方形彼此融合之處。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final folly, a violet cube rises from a sloping white base. The shades of colour link the parts and give a sense of progression through the space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終的小型構築中，一個紫色立方體從傾斜的白色基座升起。深淺不同的色彩連結各個部分，帶來穿越空間的推進感。

sections.heading: Folded Light - A Cube Among Prisms
sections.body: Small buildings without a practical task offer a rare freedom, since every decision can serve perception alone. This project used that freedom to study how solids meet. The guidance began with orthographic sketches, asking the student to locate exactly where rectangular prisms would pierce a cube, and then moved to wireframes in which slicing triangles revealed hidden edges and unexpected openings. Only after those intersections were understood did the work turn to paper. Folded in white, the forms looked almost mineral, their uneven facets catching light at shifting angles. Colour was then introduced with restraint. Two closely related shades of violet marked the place where similar squares merge, so that a visitor would sense one volume dissolving into another rather than simply crossing it. Set on a sloping base, the final folly rises like a crystal from the ground. The study demonstrates how careful geometry, paired with a single colour decision, can turn a modest paper model into a lesson on light, sequence and the quiet drama of intersection.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺疊的光-稜柱之間的立方體
zh-Hant.body: 沒有實際用途的小建築提供一種難得的自由，因為每個決定都可以只為感知服務。這個專題運用這份自由，研究量體如何相遇。指導過程從正投影草圖開始，要求學生精確找出長方稜柱刺穿立方體的位置，再轉向線框圖，讓斜切的三角形揭示隱藏的邊與意料之外的開口。唯有在理解這些交會之後，作品才轉向紙張。以白紙摺出的形態幾乎像礦物，起伏的晶面在變換的角度中捕捉光線。色彩隨後被節制地引入：兩種相近的紫色標示相似方形融合之處，讓來訪者感到一個量體溶入另一個，而非僅僅穿越。置於傾斜基座之上，最終的構築如晶體般從地面升起。研究說明縝密的幾何搭配單一的色彩決定，能把一件樸素的紙模型化為關於光、序列與交會之靜謐戲劇的一課。

pins.title: Playground of Innocence
pins.description:
Toy parts, colourful strips and twisting ladders gather into a carnival model that imagines a place where people forget worry and grow young again.

Model and sketch | Concept study | Toys, wooden strips, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 童心樂園
zh-Hant.description:
玩具零件、彩色條帶與扭轉的梯子聚成一座嘉年華模型，想像一個讓人忘卻煩憂、重返年少的地方。

模型與草圖｜概念研究｜玩具、木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Inspired by a cheerful song about growing old together, the project holds that love can keep people young at heart. It asks how a model could make visitors forget their worries and return to childlike wonder.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 受一首關於一同變老的輕快歌曲啟發，這個專題相信愛能讓人保有年輕的心。它探問，一件模型如何讓來訪者忘卻煩憂，重返孩童般的驚奇。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A carnival was chosen as the theme of a lifelong journey. A sketch imagined a tall carousel tower inside a protective dome, layered with rides and rooms.
captions: The topic sketch sheet with two reference illustrations of fantasy towers.
Packaged toys collected as parts for the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 嘉年華被選為一生旅程的主題。一張草圖想像一座位於保護穹頂內的高聳旋轉木馬塔，層層疊著遊樂設施與房間。
captions: 主題草圖頁，附兩幅奇幻高塔參考插畫。
為模型收集作零件的盒裝玩具。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Early tests mixed bent white strips with coloured toy parts. Colourful ribbons, coiled springs, a blue wheel and twisting ladders were added to build a sense of play.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 早期試驗把彎曲的白色條帶與彩色玩具零件混合。彩色緞帶、捲曲的彈簧、藍色輪子與扭轉的梯子陸續加入，營造遊戲感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model is a bright tangle of tracks, ladders and toys. Its colours and shadows create a playful, childlike atmosphere, like a small utopia.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型是一團由軌道、梯子與玩具交織的明亮形體。它的色彩與光影營造出俏皮而充滿童心的氛圍，宛如一座小小的烏托邦。

sections.heading: Joyful Tangle - Building a Utopia of Play
sections.body: Ageing is often described as a slow loss, yet this project chose to imagine it as a journey that can stay light. Prompted by a cheerful melody about love that outlasts the years, the student set out to design a place where adults might set aside worry and recover the curiosity of childhood. The guidance encouraged a theme broad enough to hold a whole life, and the carnival offered exactly that, a world of circling motion, bright surfaces and small surprises. A first sketch placed a carousel tower under a sheltering dome, while the model grew more freely, combining bent white strips with toy fragments, coiled springs, ribbons and ladders that twist as if in mid-dance. Instead of a single route, the result offers a tangle in which the eye keeps finding new paths. Colour and cast shadow do much of the work, giving even plain surfaces a festive glow. The piece suggests that delight is a legitimate design aim, and that found objects can carry memory and emotion straight into architectural form.

zh-Hant.heading: 歡樂的交纏-建造遊戲的烏托邦
zh-Hant.body: 衰老常被描述為緩慢的失去，這個專題卻選擇把它想像為一段可以保持輕盈的旅程。受一首歌頌愛能超越歲月的輕快旋律所觸動，學生著手設計一個讓成年人放下煩憂、找回童年好奇的地方。指導過程鼓勵選擇一個足以容納一生的主題，而嘉年華恰好提供了這樣的世界：旋轉的運動、明亮的表面與小小的驚喜。第一張草圖把旋轉木馬塔置於庇護的穹頂之下，模型則更自由地生長，把彎曲的白色條帶與玩具碎片、捲曲的彈簧、緞帶，以及彷彿正在起舞而扭轉的梯子結合在一起。成果不提供單一路徑，而是一團讓目光不斷發現新路線的交纏。色彩與投影承擔了大部分的工作，讓即使樸素的表面也散發節慶的光彩。作品暗示，喜悅是正當的設計目標，而拾得的物件能把記憶與情感直接帶入建築形式。

pins.title: Thorns of Desire
pins.description:
An orderly frame at the core bursts outward into tangled wire, iridescent film and a shell of stick thorns, tracing a mind pulled by desire.

Model and sketch | Character study | PVC sheets, wooden strips, iron wire, bamboo sticks, chameleon window film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 欲望之刺
zh-Hant.description:
核心處規整的框架向外爆裂為糾纏的鐵絲、幻彩薄膜與木籤刺殼，描繪一顆被欲望拉扯的心。

模型與草圖｜角色研究｜PVC片、木條、鐵絲、竹籤、幻彩窗膜｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A film follows a man trapped in a dull, repeated life who slowly loses control. Inspired by it, the project asks how such a change of mind could be built, moving from order to chaos.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 受一部電影啟發，片中一名男子困於乏味而重複的生活，逐漸失去控制。這個專題探問，如何建造這樣的心境轉變，從秩序走向混亂。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sketch split the model into three parts. Ordered rectangle wires sit at the centre, bubbles grow smaller and denser around them, and thick messy wires wrap the outside.
captions: Stills from the film that inspired the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張草圖把模型分成三部分。中心是排列整齊的矩形線框，周圍是越來越小、越來越密的泡泡，最外層則是粗而雜亂的鐵絲。
captions: 啟發這件模型的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Straight wooden frames and right angles were used for the boring routine inside. Around them, clear PVC and iridescent film were bent into bubbles, and iron wire was looped more and more wildly.
captions: Gluing the stick frame by hand.
Wrapping wire and film around the frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 筆直的木框與直角用來表現內部乏味的日常。在其周圍，透明PVC與幻彩膜被彎成泡泡，鐵絲則越繞越狂亂。
captions: 以手將鐵絲與薄膜纏繞在框架上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: On the outer layer, bamboo sticks burst out as clustering thorns. Under dark light the model glows with colour inside and bristles at its edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最外層，竹籤爆出成一簇簇的刺。在暗光下，模型內部閃耀色彩，邊緣則豎起尖刺。

sections.heading: From Grid to Thorn - The Anatomy of a Restless Mind
sections.body: A life of repetition can feel safe and suffocating at once, and this project set out to show what happens when that tension breaks. Drawing on a story of a man who escapes routine only to lose himself, the student was guided to read the character not as a plot but as a sequence of inner states, each needing its own geometry. The core was therefore made strict, a cage of straight strips and right angles standing for the dull rhythm of ordinary days. Moving outward, the order softens into bubbles of clear sheet and shimmering film, smaller and denser as if pressure were building, until iron wire loops without restraint. At the edge, bamboo sticks erupt into a crown of thorns, both defensive and violent. Making the piece, the student came to feel the character’s struggle and to ask how strongly people are steered by the material world around them. The model becomes a section through a mind, where the passage from grid to thorn reads as a quiet warning about desire.

zh-Hant.heading: 從格網到尖刺-躁動心靈的解剖
zh-Hant.body: 重複的生活可能同時讓人感到安全與窒息，這個專題試圖呈現這份張力斷裂時會發生什麼。借鑑一個男子逃離日常卻迷失自我的故事，學生被引導不把角色讀成情節，而是讀成一連串的內在狀態，每一種都需要自己的幾何。於是核心被做得嚴謹，以筆直木條與直角構成的籠子，代表平凡日子的乏味節奏。向外移動，秩序軟化為透明片材與閃爍薄膜組成的泡泡，越來越小、越來越密，彷彿壓力正在累積，直到鐵絲毫無節制地盤繞。在邊緣，竹籤爆發成一頂刺冠，既是防衛，也是暴烈。在製作過程中，學生感受到角色的掙扎，並開始追問人們受周遭物質世界牽引的程度。模型成為一道穿過心靈的剖面，從格網到尖刺的過渡，讀來像一則關於欲望的安靜警語。

pins.title: Mountain of Abandoned Things
pins.description:
A twisted mountain of white clay is piled with chairs, boxes, little houses and a crane, all set at odd angles to show a world of things left behind.

Model | Concept study | Stone clay, wooden strips, wooden boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 棄物之山
zh-Hant.description:
一座扭曲的白色黏土山上堆著椅子、箱子、小房子與一座吊車，全都以古怪的角度擺放，呈現一個被遺棄之物的世界。

模型｜概念研究｜石塑黏土、木條、木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The clay mountain with its crane.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Inspired by a climbing video game whose strange world is made of junk, the project starts from a feeling of frustration and abandonment. It asks how a model could show a place where too many things are made and thrown away.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 受一款攀爬類電子遊戲啟發，遊戲中奇異的世界由廢棄物構成，這個專題從一種挫折與被遺棄的感受出發。它探問，一件模型如何呈現一個製造太多、丟棄太多的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student began with the base, shaping stone clay into irregular pieces with holes and soft edges. These were tested to see how they might stack into a rocky mass.
captions: Screenshots from the video game that inspired the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從基座開始，把石塑黏土捏成帶有孔洞與柔和邊緣的不規則塊體。接著測試這些塊體如何堆疊成岩塊般的量體。
captions: 啟發這件模型的電玩遊戲截圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Everyday objects were then built in wood and board, including chairs, benches, a box, small houses and a tall crane. They were placed in random positions, tilted and half buried.
captions: Shaping the clay base by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 接著以木材與板材製作日常物件，包括椅子、長凳、箱子、小房子與高大的吊車。它們被隨意擺放，傾斜著、半埋著。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished mountain rises with a crane and wooden rooms on top. Its long shadows make it look bizarre and lonely, a reminder to care about waste.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的山體頂端立著吊車與木造房間。長長的影子讓它看來奇異而孤寂，提醒人們關注浪費。

sections.heading: Heaped Belongings - A Landscape of Leftovers
sections.body: Some landscapes are made not of rock and water but of the things a society no longer wants. This project drew on the absurd scenery of a climbing game, where a lone player struggles across heaps of furniture and debris, and turned the frustration of that climb into a reflection on excess. The guidance asked the student to establish ground before objects, so the work began with soft stone clay pressed into hollowed, irregular masses that stack like an eroded cliff. Only then were familiar things introduced, chairs, a bench, a box, a cluster of little rooms and a towering crane, each made carefully by hand and then placed carelessly, tilted, stranded or half swallowed by the mountain. That contrast between craft and neglect gives the piece its quiet force. Under a raking light, long shadows stretch across the wall and the model feels both comic and desolate. It shows how a playful source can open serious questions, inviting viewers to notice how much is produced, used briefly and left behind.

zh-Hant.heading: 堆疊的身外物-剩餘之物的地景
zh-Hant.body: 有些地景並非由岩石與流水構成，而是由一個社會不再想要的東西堆成。這個專題借鑑一款攀爬遊戲的荒誕場景，玩家獨自在家具與殘骸堆上掙扎前行，並把那份攀爬的挫折轉化為對過剩的反思。指導過程要求學生先建立地面，再放入物件，因此作品始於柔軟的石塑黏土，被壓成中空而不規則的量塊，像遭侵蝕的懸崖般堆疊。之後才引入熟悉的物件：椅子、長凳、箱子、一簇小房間與一座高聳的吊車，每一件都以手工細心製作，卻被漫不經心地擺放，傾斜、擱淺，或被山體吞沒一半。精心製作與隨意遺棄之間的對比，賦予作品沉靜的力量。在斜射的光下，長影橫過牆面，模型顯得既滑稽又荒涼。它說明一個遊戲般的起點也能開啟嚴肅的提問，邀請觀者留意有多少東西被生產、短暫使用，然後被遺留。

pins.title: Shoe Rhapsody
pins.description:
The hidden lines between a shoe and the foot inside it are drawn, sliced into curved cardboard pieces and multiplied into a tower like a science-fiction city.

Model and drawings | Object study | Cardboard, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鞋的狂想曲
zh-Hant.description:
鞋與其中的腳之間隱藏的線條被描繪出來，切成彎曲的紙板片，再大量複製成一座宛如科幻城市的高塔。

模型與繪圖｜物件研究｜紙板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A simple canvas sneaker has a strong, fashionable shape. The project asks what would happen if the inside of a shoe, and its hidden relationship with the foot, were turned into a solid figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一雙簡單的帆布鞋有著鮮明而時尚的造型。這個專題探問，若把鞋的內部，以及它與腳之間隱藏的關係，轉化為一個實體形態，會發生什麼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied how the foot sits in the shoe. The relationship was drawn as sweeping lines, layered in curves and hatches.
captions: The canvas sneaker that sparked the idea.
Photos of a foot moving through a step.
A diagram of the bones and ligaments of the foot.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究腳如何安放在鞋中。這種關係被畫成掃掠的線條，以曲線與排線層層疊加。
captions: 足部骨骼與韌帶的示意圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The lines were turned into three-dimensional slices of cardboard. Small modules of repeated curved slices were tested, then grouped and spread in different directions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 線條被轉化為立體的紙板切片。由重複彎曲切片組成的小模組先被試作，再成組地朝不同方向展開。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: All the parts were joined into one tall cluster on thin sticks. Viewed from inside, the slices form canyons, spirals and streets like a city from science fiction.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 所有部件以細木條支撐，接合成一簇高聳的量體。從內部看，切片形成峽谷、螺旋與街道，宛如科幻作品中的城市。

sections.heading: Inside the Sole - Curves That Became a City
sections.body: Everyday objects hide spatial worlds that rarely receive attention, and the interior of a shoe is one of the most intimate. This project began with admiration for the plain outline of a canvas sneaker, then turned inward to the unseen fit between sole, heel and arch. The guidance encouraged the student to draw that relationship as pure line rather than as an object, letting sweeping curves record pressure, support and movement. Those drawings were then sliced into thin cardboard ribs, like the sections of a hull, and repeated in small modules that could twist and fan out. As the modules multiplied and were set facing different directions, the logic of a single foot dissolved into something far larger. Raised on slender sticks, the final cluster reads as a vertical city of canyons, spirals and narrow streets. The student was surprised that broken parts could merge into one convincing whole. The work shows how analytical drawing can carry a humble object across scales until it becomes architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 鞋底之內-化為城市的曲線
zh-Hant.body: 日常物件中隱藏著鮮少受到關注的空間世界，而鞋的內部是其中最親密的一種。這個專題始於對一雙帆布鞋簡潔輪廓的欣賞，隨後轉向內部，探究鞋底、鞋跟與足弓之間看不見的貼合。指導過程鼓勵學生把這種關係畫成純粹的線，而非物件，讓掃掠的曲線記錄壓力、支撐與移動。這些圖接著被切成細薄的紙板肋片，如同船身的剖面，並以小模組重複，可以扭轉、展開成扇形。隨著模組增生並朝不同方向擺放，單一一隻腳的邏輯溶解為遠為龐大的事物。以細木條撐起後，最終的量體讀來像一座由峽谷、螺旋與窄街構成的垂直城市。學生驚訝於破碎的部件竟能融合為一個令人信服的整體。作品說明分析性的繪圖能把一件平凡物件帶過不同尺度，直到它成為建築。

pins.title: Tower of Notes
pins.description:
The notes of a guitar solo become curved cardboard strips on a grid fingerboard, then are cut, shifted and stacked into a dark, crashing tower.

Model and drawings | Music study | Cardboard, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 音符之塔
zh-Hant.description:
吉他獨奏的音符化為格狀指板上彎曲的紙板條，再被切開、錯動、堆疊成一座深色而相互碰撞的高塔。

模型與繪圖｜音樂研究｜紙板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Guitar solos are full of exciting runs of notes, yet notes cannot be seen. The project asks how sound, and the phrases of a solo, could be expressed as a form with space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 吉他獨奏充滿令人振奮的連串音符，然而音符看不見。這個專題探問，聲音以及獨奏中的樂句，如何被表現為具有空間的形式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Early drawings tried turning vibrating strings into bold and thin lines. In the end the student chose curves for changing notes and a grid for the fingerboard.
captions: A fretboard chart beside a guitar.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 早期的繪圖嘗試把振動的弦化為粗細不同的線條。最後，學生選擇以曲線表現變化的音符，以格網表現指板。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cardboard planes stood on a gridded board like strings, with curved strips running along them as phrases. Each short phrase was built as a separate part.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙板片像琴弦般立在格網底板上，彎曲的條帶沿著它們延伸，代表樂句。每一段短樂句都被做成獨立的部件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The parts were transformed and cobbled into towers. In the finished model the fragments seem to crash and cover each other, like a solo growing louder and softer with emotion.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 各個部件被轉化並拼接成塔。在完成的模型中，碎片彷彿彼此碰撞、覆蓋，如同一段隨情緒忽強忽弱的獨奏。

sections.heading: Frozen Phrases - Building with Sound
sections.body: Music and architecture have long been compared, yet sound offers no edges to hold, and that difficulty is where this project found its method. Starting from a love of electric guitar solos, the student tried several ways of drawing what cannot be seen, first thickening and thinning lines like vibrating strings, then settling on a clearer code in which curves trace the movement of notes and a grid stands for the fingerboard beneath them. The guidance encouraged working phrase by phrase. Each short run of notes was built as its own piece, upright cardboard planes rising from a gridded base with curved strips sliding along them. Only after the phrases existed separately were they shifted, rotated and cobbled together, so that their relationships, rather than any single melody, would shape the whole. The finished towers feel mysterious, their fragments crowding and overlapping as if competing to be heard. Seen in dark light, they recall the way a solo surges and fades, proving that rhythm and intensity can be given spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固的樂句-以聲音建造
zh-Hant.body: 音樂與建築向來常被相提並論，然而聲音沒有可以握住的邊界，而這份困難正是這個專題找到方法之處。從對搖滾樂中弦樂獨奏的喜愛出發，學生嘗試數種描繪不可見之物的方式：先像振動的弦一樣讓線條忽粗忽細，最後確立一套更清晰的符號，以曲線描摹音符的流動，以格網代表其下的指板。指導過程鼓勵逐句工作。每一小段連串的音符都被做成獨立的部件，直立的紙板片從格網底座升起，彎曲的條帶沿著它們滑行。唯有在各樂句分別成形之後，它們才被錯動、旋轉、拼接在一起，使彼此之間的關係，而非任何單一旋律，塑造整體。完成的高塔顯得神秘，碎片擁擠而交疊，彷彿爭相被聽見。在暗光中，它們令人想起獨奏的湧起與消退，證明節奏與強度能夠被賦予空間的形式。

pins.title: Paralleled World
pins.description:
A tall tower of stick mesh, zigzag tracks, foam cubes and glowing cotton clouds stacks the stages of one life into a dreamy parallel world.

Model and sketch | Concept study | Wooden strips, wire, laser paper, cotton, cardboard, coloured light beads, PVC board, foam blocks, frosted PVC sheets, markers | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 平行世界
zh-Hant.description:
一座以木條網架、鋸齒跑道、泡棉方塊與發光棉花雲構成的高塔，把一段人生的各個階段堆疊成夢幻的平行世界。

模型與草圖｜概念研究｜木條、鐵絲、雷射紙、棉花、紙板、彩色燈珠、PVC板、泡棉塊、霧面PVC片、麥克筆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project imagines a parallel world in which a person could live many different careers at once. It asks how those possible lives could be stacked into one building that keeps growing.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題想像一個平行世界，讓一個人能同時經歷許多不同的職業。它探問，如何把這些可能的人生堆疊成一座持續生長的建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A concept sketch divided the tower into zones for a stage, an arena, interior design, programming and architecture. Early tests tried laser paper on curved mesh, clusters of foam cubes and small card furniture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張概念草圖把塔分成舞台、競技場、室內設計、程式設計與建築等區域。早期試作嘗試了貼在曲面網上的雷射紙、成簇的泡棉方塊與小型紙板家具。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Laser paper squares on a wire mesh form a broken-mirror base, and interlocking wooden triangles rise above it. A zigzag cardboard track spirals through the middle while blue foam blocks gather like a network.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 貼在鐵絲網上的雷射紙方片構成如碎鏡般的基座，交錯的木條三角形在其上升起。鋸齒狀的紙板跑道盤旋穿過中段，藍色泡棉方塊則像網絡般聚集。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: At the top, frosted sheets, cotton clouds and coloured light beads form a colourful building that seems to keep growing. Lit in the dark, the tower glows from base to crown like a dream.
captions: The lit tower from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 頂部以霧面片材、棉花雲與彩色燈珠構成一座彷彿持續生長的彩色建築。在黑暗中點亮後，整座塔從基座到頂端都像夢境般發光。

sections.heading: Stacked Possibilities - A Life Built in Layers
sections.body: Young people often feel that choosing one path means losing all the others, and this project answers that anxiety by building every path at once. The student was guided to translate a personal history into vertical layers, so that the tower could be read from bottom to top like a biography. At the base, squares of laser paper on a curved mesh shimmer like a broken mirror, holding early worries about the future. Above it, a small stage recalls years of music, and a zigzag track of folded cardboard winds upward as a memory of competitive sport. Clusters of blue foam blocks suggest a world of information and networks, while the summit dissolves into frosted sheets, cotton clouds and coloured lights that seem never to stop growing. Interlocking triangles of wooden strip give the whole an elevation and keep the many materials in tension. When the room is darkened, the tower glows from within, and the parallel lives become one luminous structure. The work shows that uncertainty, given form, can become a place of hope.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊起的可能-層層建造的人生
zh-Hant.body: 年輕人常覺得選擇一條路就意味著失去其餘所有的路，而這個專題以同時建造每一條路來回應這份焦慮。學生被引導把個人經歷轉譯為垂直的層次，讓這座塔能像一部傳記般由下而上被閱讀。在基座，貼在曲面網上的雷射紙方片如碎鏡般閃爍，承載著對未來的早期憂慮。其上，一座小舞台喚起多年的音樂時光，摺疊紙板構成的鋸齒跑道向上盤旋，是對競技運動的記憶。成簇的藍色泡棉方塊暗示資訊與網絡的世界，而頂端則溶解為霧面片材、棉花雲與彩色燈光，彷彿永不停止生長。木條交錯而成的三角形賦予整體立面，並讓多種材料保持張力。當房間暗下，塔從內部發光，平行的人生化為一座明亮的結構。作品說明，不確定性一旦被賦予形式，也能成為希望的所在。

pins.title: Scenes Reassembled
pins.description:
Three scenes from a short film made by the student are redrawn as movement diagrams and rebuilt as a layered white PVC model of straight and curved strips.

Model, storyboards and diagrams | Narrative space study | PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重組的場景
zh-Hant.description:
學生自己拍攝的短片中的三個場景，被重繪成動線圖，再以直線與曲線條帶重建為層層疊合的白色PVC模型。

模型、分鏡與圖解｜敘事空間研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student had made a short film shot in three scenes. The project asks whether the scenes, and the movements of characters within them, could be turned into architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生曾拍攝一部由三個場景構成的短片。這個專題探問，這些場景以及其中角色的移動，能否被轉化為建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Storyboards broke each scene into key frames of objects, spaces and actions. The movement in each frame was then drawn as an abstract line diagram.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 分鏡把每個場景拆成物件、空間與動作的關鍵畫格。接著，每個畫格中的移動被畫成抽象的線條圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Straight and curved lines were cut from PVC foam board as separate elements. Small event models tested how the pieces could be recombined for each scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 直線與曲線以PVC發泡板切割成獨立的元素。小型事件模型則測試這些部件如何針對每個場景重新組合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model shows the whole film space in three layers of frames, ribbons and slatted planes. Its shadows add a further layer of movement as the light shifts.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以框架、彎帶與格柵板三個層次呈現整個影片空間。隨著光線移動，陰影又增添了一層動態。

sections.heading: Frames into Rooms - Choreographing Space from Film
sections.body: Film and architecture both choreograph bodies through space, and this project tested how directly one could be translated into the other. Working from a short film of the student’s own, made in three scenes, the guidance began not with form but with analysis. Storyboards isolated the objects, rooms and gestures of each key frame, and the movement within every frame was redrawn as a loose abstract diagram of crossing lines, hatches and dots. From these diagrams came a vocabulary of straight and curved strips cut from white foam board, simple enough to be recombined freely. Small event models tried out arrangements scene by scene, before the three studies were layered into a single structure of frames, ribbons and slatted planes. Built entirely in white, the model depends on light, and its shadows add a moving fourth layer that changes as the viewer circles it. The process taught the student to treat a story as a sequence of spatial events, and showed how notation can become a bridge between watching and building.

zh-Hant.heading: 從畫格到房間-從影像編排空間
zh-Hant.body: 電影與建築都在空間中編排身體的移動，這個專題測試兩者之間能被多直接地互相轉譯。以學生自己拍攝、由三個場景構成的短片為起點，指導過程並非從形式開始，而是從分析開始。分鏡把每個關鍵畫格中的物件、房間與姿態分離出來，每一格中的移動再被重繪成由交錯線條、排線與圓點組成的抽象圖。從這些圖中，發展出一套以白色發泡板切出的直線與曲線條帶語彙，簡單到可以自由重組。小型事件模型逐一為各場景試驗排列，之後三個研究被疊合為由框架、彎帶與格柵板構成的單一結構。整件模型全為白色，因此仰賴光線，陰影在觀者繞行時不斷變化，成為流動的第四層。這個過程讓學生學會把故事視為一連串空間事件，也說明記譜能成為觀看與建造之間的橋樑。

pins.title: Turning Corridor Tower
pins.description:
A corridor imagined as able to turn is rebuilt from PVC disks and modules, then stretched, rotated and crossed into a tower of arches and openings.

Model | Spatial transformation study | PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 旋轉走廊之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一條被想像為可以轉動的走廊，以PVC圓盤與模組重建，再經拉伸、旋轉與交錯，成為一座充滿拱形與開口的高塔。

模型｜空間轉化研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A camera frame limits what can be imagined of reality inside a picture. The project asks how a few elements inside a frame could be used to create something new outside it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 相機的畫框限制了人們對畫面中現實的想像。這個專題探問，如何運用畫框內有限的元素，在畫框之外創造新的事物。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Starting from a corridor scene in a favourite film, the student modelled the space digitally after learning the software on a summer course. A circular disk and base were then designed so that the corridor module could turn in reality.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以一部喜愛電影中的走廊場景為起點，在暑期課程學會軟體後，以數位方式建立了這個空間的模型。接著設計了圓盤與底座，讓走廊模組能在現實中轉動。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many identical modules were cut from PVC board and fitted with disks, arches and window openings. They were then stretched, rotated, crossed and combined.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 許多相同的模組以PVC板切出，並裝上圓盤、拱形與窗洞。接著它們被拉伸、旋轉、交錯並組合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower stacks the turning modules into a dense block of arches, with yellow and blue parts marking the hinges of rotation. Seen from below, its corridors seem to twist in every direction.
captions: The tower from a low angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔把可轉動的模組堆疊成一個密集的拱形量體，黃色與藍色部件標示出旋轉的關節。從下方看，走廊彷彿朝各個方向扭轉。

sections.heading: Beyond the Frame - A Corridor Set Free
sections.body: Every photograph is an act of exclusion, and this project began with a frustration about what a frame leaves out. A keen traveller who records journeys through a camera, the student wondered whether a few elements trapped inside a picture could be released to make something new. The starting point was a corridor scene from a favourite film, in which a hallway appears to rotate. Rather than copying the image, the student first rebuilt the corridor digitally, then asked what it would take for such a space to turn in reality. The answer was mechanical as much as visual, a circular disk and base wrapped around each module like a wheel. Dozens of identical units were cut from foam board, given arches and window openings, and then stretched, rotated, crossed and stacked. Yellow and blue parts mark the hinges where rotation happens. The resulting tower is dense and labyrinthine, its corridors twisting in every direction when seen from below, proving that a single framed moment can seed a whole architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 畫框之外-被釋放的走廊
zh-Hant.body: 每一張照片都是一次排除，這個專題始於對畫框遺漏之物的不滿。作為以相機記錄旅程的旅行愛好者，學生思考，被困在畫面中的少數元素能否被釋放出來，創造新的事物。起點是一部喜愛電影中的走廊場景，畫面中的長廊彷彿在旋轉。學生沒有複製影像，而是先以數位方式重建走廊，再追問這樣的空間要如何在現實中轉動。答案既關乎視覺，也關乎機械：一個圓盤與底座像輪子般包覆每個模組。數十個相同的單元以發泡板切出，開出拱形與窗洞，接著被拉伸、旋轉、交錯並堆疊。黃色與藍色部件標示出旋轉發生的關節。最終的塔密集而如迷宮，從下方看，走廊朝各個方向扭轉，證明一個被框住的瞬間也能孕育整座建築。

pins.title: Court in the Sand
pins.description:
The movements of a basketball game are traced as lines, folded into card and PVC modules, and enlarged into slatted towers rising from a bed of sand.

Model | Movement study | PVC boards, cardboard, tracing paper, sand | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沙中球場
zh-Hant.description:
籃球比賽中的動作被描成線條，摺入紙板與PVC模組，再放大成從沙床中升起的格柵高塔。

模型｜動作研究｜PVC板、紙板、硫酸紙、沙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Basketball was the sport the student loved most, and a desert film suggested a grand, empty landscape. The project asks whether the movement of the game could be combined with the scale of the desert.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 籃球是學生最喜愛的運動，而一部沙漠題材的電影帶來了壯闊而空曠的地景。這個專題探問，球賽中的動作能否與沙漠的尺度結合。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Moments of a friend playing were recorded with a camera, and the movements were traced as line segments on tracing paper. The traced figures were printed onto folding panels to study the motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生用相機記錄朋友打球的瞬間，並把動作以線段描繪在硫酸紙上。描出的人形被印在可摺疊的板面上，用來研究動作。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cardboard was folded and PVC foam board strips were pasted at different angles, creating interesting spaces inside. This prototype was then enlarged into four versions of the module.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙板被摺起，PVC發泡板條以不同角度黏貼，在內部創造出有趣的空間。接著這個原型被放大成四個版本的模組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Sand was added around the enlarged modules to complete the model. The slatted forms look like a spaceship born from the movement of the game and set into the desert.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在放大的模組周圍加入沙子，完成了模型。格柵狀的形體看來像一艘由球賽動作誕生、嵌入沙漠的太空船。

sections.heading: Motion Laid in Sand - Tracing a Game into Landform
sections.body: Sport is architecture in motion, a pattern of bodies that exists only for a moment before it vanishes. This project set out to capture that pattern and give it the permanence of landform. Moved by the vast, empty dunes of a desert film, the student imagined a court dissolving into sand, and began by photographing a friend in play. The figures were traced as line segments on translucent paper and printed onto folding panels, so that the movement could be read in sequence rather than as a single pose. Folding card and gluing foam-board strips at shifting angles turned those lines into interior spaces, compressed and layered like sedimentary rock. The guidance encouraged scaling up only once the prototype felt alive, and four enlarged modules followed. Set into a bed of sand and lit from one side, the slatted towers cast long shadows and resemble a vessel landed in the dunes. The project shows how a fleeting gesture, carefully notated, can be built into something monumental and strange.

zh-Hant.heading: 沙上的動勢-把球賽描成地形
zh-Hant.body: 運動是動態的建築，是身體瞬間形成又隨即消失的圖案。這個專題試圖捕捉這種圖案，並賦予它地形般的恆久。受到一部沙漠電影中遼闊空曠沙丘的觸動，學生想像一座溶入沙中的球場，並從拍攝朋友打球開始。人物被描成半透明紙上的線段，再印到可摺疊的板面上，使動作能被依序閱讀，而非凝固為單一姿勢。摺起紙板，並以變換的角度黏貼發泡板條，這些線條轉化為內部空間，像沉積岩般壓縮而層疊。指導過程鼓勵學生在原型顯得有生命力之後才放大尺度，隨後完成四個放大的模組。置入沙床並從一側打光，格柵狀的高塔投下長影，宛如一艘降落在沙丘中的船。這個專題說明，一個轉瞬即逝的動作，經過仔細記錄，也能被建造成宏偉而奇異的事物。

pins.title: Four Rooms of Farewell
pins.description:
A round miniature set is cut into four quarters, a lakeshore, a study room, a village of small houses and a quiet hall, each built with clay, wood and fallen leaves.

Model | Set design study | Wooden boards, putty, acrylic, sandpaper, bamboo strips, oil paint, coloured pencils, watercolour clay, dried leaves, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 告別的四個房間
zh-Hant.description:
一座圓形迷你場景被切成四個象限：湖岸、書房、小房子組成的村落與靜謐的大廳，各以黏土、木材與落葉製作。

模型｜場景設計研究｜木板、補土、壓克力、砂紙、竹條、油彩、色鉛筆、水彩黏土、乾葉、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A quiet film about a man facing the end of life made a deep connection with the student. Drawing on an interest in stage design, the project asks how its moods could be held in one miniature set.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於男子面對生命終點的安靜電影，與學生產生了深刻的共鳴。基於對舞台設計的興趣，這個專題探問，如何把影片中的情緒收納在一座迷你場景中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The round base was divided into four parts, each standing for one key setting. Materials were chosen for each mood, from rough putty rock to warm wooden floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圓形底座被分成四個部分，各自代表一個關鍵場景。每種情緒都選用相應的材料，從粗糙的補土岩石到溫暖的木地板。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The study room was built with shelves, a desk and a glowing window, and the village corner with small houses and scattered red leaves. A dark hall with two reclining chairs was given a mirror-like floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 書房以書架、書桌與發光的窗戶構成，村落一角則有小房子與散落的紅葉。一座幽暗的大廳擺放兩張躺椅，地面如鏡面般反光。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Put together, the four quarters form one circle that can be read like a sequence of scenes. Each part works as a small stage with its own light and atmosphere.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 組合起來，四個象限構成一個圓，可以像一連串場景般被閱讀。每個部分都是一座小舞台，擁有自己的光線與氛圍。

sections.heading: A Circle of Partings - Four Quarters of One Goodbye
sections.body: Saying goodbye is rarely a single moment, more often a slow passage through places that once mattered, and this miniature set treats farewell as a journey across four rooms. Inspired by a quiet film about a man facing the end of life, and drawing on experience behind the camera, the student chose to design a set rather than a building. The round base was divided like a clock into four quarters, each assigned a mood and a palette of materials. Rough putty and oil paint shape a dark lakeshore, polished wood and a glowing window warm a book-lined study, small houses sit among scattered red leaves, and a dim hall holds two reclining chairs above a reflective floor. The guidance stressed lighting as much as modelling, so each quarter was photographed as its own scene. Seen from above, the circle reads like a dial of memory, turning from wildness to domestic calm to stillness. The project reveals how set design can carry emotion through material, scale and light alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 離別之圓-一場告別的四個象限
zh-Hant.body: 告別很少只是一個瞬間，更常是緩慢穿越那些曾經重要的地方，而這座迷你場景把告別視為穿越四個房間的旅程。受一部關於男子面對生命終點的安靜電影啟發，並借鑑在鏡頭後的經驗，學生選擇設計一座場景，而非一棟建築。圓形底座像時鐘般被分成四個象限，各自被賦予一種情緒與一組材料。粗糙的補土與油彩塑造出幽暗的湖岸，打磨過的木材與發光的窗戶溫暖了滿是書架的書房，小房子坐落在散落的紅葉之間，昏暗的大廳則在反光地面上擺放兩張躺椅。指導過程對光線的重視不亞於模型製作，因此每個象限都被當作獨立的場景拍攝。從上方看，這個圓讀來像一面記憶的錶盤，從荒野轉向居家的寧靜，再轉向靜止。這個專題揭示，場景設計僅憑材料、尺度與光線，就能承載情感。

pins.title: Six Scenes of a Cosmic Voyage
pins.description:
Six small models of clay, mirror paper, PVC, paper strips and acrylic sticks are joined into one landscape that reads as a journey through outer space.

Model | Narrative space study | PVC boards, acrylic sticks and slices, paper, mirror paper, wooden sticks, stone clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 宇宙航程的六個場景
zh-Hant.description:
六件以黏土、鏡面紙、PVC、紙條與壓克力棒製成的小模型，接合成一片地景，讀來像一段穿越外太空的旅程。

模型｜敘事空間研究｜PVC板、壓克力棒與薄片、紙、鏡面紙、木籤、石塑黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A favourite science-fiction film left the student struck by the vast scenery of planets and outer space. The project asks how such a journey could be written as a brief spatial script.
captions: The science-fiction film poster that inspired the six scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部喜愛的科幻電影讓學生對行星與外太空的壯闊景象深受震撼。這個專題探問，如何把這樣的旅程寫成一份簡短的空間劇本。
captions: 啟發這六個場景的科幻電影海報。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Six key scenes were chosen and abstracted into six small models. An icy world was moulded in stone clay, and a tunnel of wooden sticks pulls everything toward the next scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生選出六個關鍵場景，並抽象化為六件小模型。冰封的世界以石塑黏土塑造，木籤構成的通道則把一切拉向下一個場景。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A cluster of mirror paper slices spirals around a tower like an uncontrollable vortex, and PVC geometry forms a station ringed by acrylic dust. Bluish paper strips are woven into waves, while dense acrylic sticks build rooms inside a final void.
captions: Building the model scenes in the workshop.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鏡面紙片簇群如失控的漩渦般繞著高塔盤旋，PVC幾何體則構成一座被壓克力塵埃環繞的太空站。淡藍紙條交織成浪，密集的壓克力棒則在最後的虛空中建出房間。
captions: 在工作室製作模型場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The six models are joined into one landscape, each scene linked to the next. Seen together, they read as a journey from icy ground to the heart of the void.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 六件模型連接成一片地景，每個場景都與下一個相連。合在一起看，它們讀來像一段從冰封大地到虛空核心的旅程。

sections.heading: Scripting the Void - Six Scenes in Space
sections.body: Science fiction often persuades through scale, and this project began with the student’s awe at landscapes too vast to inhabit. Rather than reproducing a story, the student was guided to write a spatial script, choosing six moments and asking what material could carry the feeling of each. Stone clay, pressed and smoothed by hand, became a frozen terrain of soft ridges. Mirror paper slices spiral around a slender tower, their changing density suggesting a force that cannot be controlled. Geometric PVC planes assemble into a station adrift in a cloud of clear acrylic fragments, while bluish paper strips, twisted and rolled, rise into a single towering wave. A tube of wooden sticks, every tip pointing forward, works as a hinge that drags the eye into the next scene, and the journey ends in a lattice of acrylic rods so dense that rooms seem to condense out of empty space. Joined on one base, the models become a landscape to be travelled. The work demonstrates how abstraction can hold narrative without illustrating it.

zh-Hant.heading: 書寫虛空-太空中的六個場景
zh-Hant.body: 科幻作品常以尺度說服人，這個專題始於學生面對大到無法居住的地景時所感到的敬畏。學生沒有重述故事，而是被引導撰寫一份空間劇本，選出六個瞬間，並追問何種材料能承載每一刻的感受。以手按壓、抹平的石塑黏土，成為一片起伏柔和的冰封地形。鏡面紙片繞著細長的塔盤旋，疏密的變化暗示一股無法控制的力量。幾何的PVC板片組成一座漂浮於透明壓克力碎片雲中的太空站，淡藍紙條則經扭轉與捲曲，升起成一道高聳的巨浪。一條木籤構成的管道，每個尖端都指向前方，像關節般把視線拉進下一個場景，旅程最終結束於一片極為密集的壓克力棒格網，房間彷彿從虛空中凝結而出。六件模型被接合在同一底座上，成為一片可以穿行的地景。作品說明，抽象能承載敘事，而無須圖解敘事。

pins.title: Maze City
pins.description:
Orthogonal line patterns are extruded into PVC walls, dressed with drawn shop windows and stacked into a dense, maze-like city with small open spaces.

Model | Pattern-to-space study | PVC boards, wooden sticks, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 迷宮城市
zh-Hant.description:
正交的線條圖案被擠出成PVC牆，貼上手繪的櫥窗，再堆疊成一座留有小型開放空間、如迷宮般密集的城市。

模型｜圖案到空間研究｜PVC板、木籤、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Complicated rectangles, lines and right angles often appear in favourite science-fiction films. The project asks whether such a pattern of lines could grow into a city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 複雜的矩形、線條與直角常出現在學生喜愛的科幻電影中。這個專題探問，這樣的線條圖案能否生長成一座城市。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew patterns of horizontal and vertical lines that never touch or cross. Shapes between the lines were then cut from PVC board and raised into walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出水平與垂直、彼此從不接觸也不交叉的線條圖案。接著把線條之間的形狀從PVC板切出，立起成牆。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were added as borders at right angles to sharpen the sense of extrusion. Cross-section drawings of homes on tracing paper were pasted on the walls like shop windows.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木籤以直角加在邊緣，強化擠出的立體感。描圖紙上的住宅剖面圖被貼在牆面上，宛如商店櫥窗。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Finally the pieces were folded, intersected and fixed on top of each other at high density. The whole looks like a crowded housing complex with a few open public spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最後，這些部件被摺疊、交錯，並以高密度相互疊合固定。整體看來像一座擁擠的住宅群，其中留有幾處開放的公共空間。

sections.heading: Lines That Never Touch - Density as Design
sections.body: Dense cities are often described as chaos, yet this project discovered that crowding can follow strict rules. The work began on paper with a single constraint, lines running only horizontally or vertically, never touching and never crossing. Within that discipline, the student drew labyrinths whose gaps became the true subject, and the shapes between lines were cut from foam board and lifted into walls. Thin wooden sticks set at right angles along the edges exaggerated each extrusion, and small section drawings of homes, traced on translucent paper, were pasted onto the facades like lit shop windows, giving the abstract walls a domestic scale. The guidance encouraged testing many small fragments before committing, and a series of photographed studies explored how a strip of maze might bend, turn back or open into a courtyard. In the final stage the fragments were folded and stacked at high density until they read as one crowded settlement, pierced by a few open terraces. The project shows how a graphic rule can generate a believable urban fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 永不相觸的線-以密度設計
zh-Hant.body: 高密度的城市常被形容為混亂，然而這個專題發現，擁擠也可以遵循嚴格的規則。作品從紙上的單一限制開始：線條只能水平或垂直延伸，永不接觸，也永不交叉。在這份紀律之中，學生畫出迷宮，而線與線之間的空隙才是真正的主題，這些形狀從發泡板切出，立起成牆。沿邊緣以直角加上的細木籤誇大了每一道擠出，描在半透明紙上的小幅住宅剖面圖被貼到立面上，像亮著燈的商店櫥窗，為抽象的牆賦予居家的尺度。指導過程鼓勵在定案前測試許多小片段，一系列拍攝下來的研究探索一段迷宮如何彎折、折返，或開展成庭院。在最後階段，這些片段被摺疊並高密度地堆疊，直到讀來像一座擁擠的聚落，其間穿插幾處開放的平台。這個專題說明，一條圖形規則也能生成令人信服的城市紋理。

pins.title: Offense and Defense
pins.description:
Tangled line drawings layered on transparent sheets become a thicket of paper strips and wooden sticks, two clusters bristling at each other like attack and defence.

Model and drawings | Form study | Wooden sticks, paper, transparent sheets | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 攻與守
zh-Hant.description:
層疊在透明片上的糾纏線條，化為由紙條與木籤構成的叢狀量體，兩團量體如攻與守般相互對峙。

模型與繪圖｜形態研究｜木籤、紙、透明片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 木籤與紙條的叢狀量體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Attack and defence are actions full of tension, yet they leave no lasting form. The project asks how that push and resistance could be shown in a spatial structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 攻擊與防守是充滿張力的動作，卻不會留下持久的形體。這個專題探問，如何以空間結構呈現這種推進與抵抗。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew small closed shapes and tangled lines, then traced them on transparent sheets. The sheets were layered so the lines could be read in depth.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出小型封閉形狀與糾纏的線條，再描到透明片上。這些透明片層層疊合，讓線條能在深度中被閱讀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bent paper strips were used for the open, curving forms, and sharp wooden sticks pierced through them. The two materials were built up into dense clusters that lean toward each other.
captions: Assembling the stick and strip thicket by hand.
Tracing line drawings onto layered sheets by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 彎曲的紙條用來表現開放而彎轉的形體，尖銳的木籤則穿刺其間。兩種材料被堆疊成密集的量體，彼此傾向對方。
captions: 以手組裝木條與紙條叢。
以手在疊層描圖紙上描繪線條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished thicket rises in two masses, one rounded and one spiked, with long shadows crossing between them. It reads as a frozen moment of attack and defence.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的叢狀量體分成兩團升起，一團渾圓，一團帶刺，長影在兩者之間交錯。它讀來像攻與守凝固的一刻。

sections.heading: Strip Against Stick - The Architecture of Tension
sections.body: Conflict is usually imagined as something to resolve, but this project treated tension itself as a material worth building. The student began by drawing small closed shapes and restless tangled lines, then tracing them onto transparent sheets that could be stacked and shifted, so that a flat sketch gained depth and the lines appeared to move through space. From these layered studies two vocabularies emerged. Thin paper strips, bent into loops and arches, carry the soft logic of shelter, while sharp wooden sticks thrust through them with the urgency of attack. The guidance asked that neither material dominate, and the student kept adjusting the balance as the clusters grew, letting one mass swell into rounded cages while the other bristled with points. Photographed under a low light, the two thickets lean into each other and cast long crossing shadows that extend the struggle across the ground. The model captures a single suspended instant in which pressure and resistance are held in equilibrium, showing how opposing gestures can produce a richer space than either alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 紙條對木籤-張力的建築
zh-Hant.body: 衝突通常被想像成需要化解的事，但這個專題把張力本身當作值得建造的材料。學生先畫出小型封閉形狀與躁動糾纏的線條，再把它們描到可以疊合、錯動的透明片上，使平面草圖獲得深度，線條彷彿在空間中移動。從這些層疊的研究中浮現兩套語彙。細薄的紙條彎成環與拱，承載庇護的柔和邏輯，尖銳的木籤則帶著攻擊的急迫穿刺其間。指導過程要求兩種材料都不能壓倒對方，學生隨著量體增長不斷調整平衡，讓一團膨脹為渾圓的籠，另一團則豎滿尖刺。在低角度的光線下拍攝，兩叢量體相互傾靠，投下長長交錯的影子，把這場角力延伸到地面上。模型捕捉了一個懸停的瞬間，壓力與抵抗在其中維持平衡，說明對立的姿態能比任何一方單獨存在時，創造出更豐富的空間。

pins.title: Rational City
pins.description:
Observations of a crowded station district become a model city section, with coils for traffic, foam blocks for buildings, and acrylic balconies and bridges linking them.

Model and sketches | Urban study | Plastic straws, wooden sticks, threads, foam, PVC boards, copper coils | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 理性城市
zh-Hant.description:
對一個擁擠車站街區的觀察化為一座模型城市剖面，以線圈代表交通、泡棉塊代表建築，並以壓克力陽台與天橋相連。

模型與草圖｜城市研究｜塑膠吸管、木籤、絲線、泡棉、PVC板、銅線圈｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A busy block around a railway station in the student’s home city suffered from very dense buildings and jammed traffic. The project asks how a more rational section of the city could be planned.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生家鄉城市中，一個火車站周邊的繁忙街區，建築極度密集、交通壅塞。這個專題探問，如何規劃出更理性的城市剖面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several site visits recorded water, trees, roads, buildings and the flow of people. Sketches turned the points of trees and roads into a net of lines over the block.
captions: Annotated site diagram of the block, tracking heat, wind and pedestrian flow.
A street-level view of the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 多次實地走訪記錄了水、樹木、道路、建築與人流。草圖把樹木與道路的位置轉化為覆蓋街區的線網。
captions: 街區基地分析圖，標示熱、風與行人動線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small models tested two directions, one on water and one on traffic and buildings. Straws and sticks stood for pipes and sap, while foam cubes, threads and a large wooden shade structure replaced crowded buildings, flows and trees.
captions: Building the model in the studio.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 小型模型測試兩個方向，一是水，一是交通與建築。吸管與木籤代表管線與樹液，泡棉方塊、絲線與一座大型木構遮陽系統則取代擁擠的建築、人車流與樹木。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets foam towers on a neat grid, with copper coils as traffic flows above. PVC balconies and pedestrian bridges link the buildings to give people open space between them.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把泡棉塔樓置於整齊的格網上，銅線圈在上方代表交通流。PVC陽台與人行天橋連接各棟建築，在其間為人們留出開放空間。

sections.heading: Untangling the Block - A Rational Section
sections.body: Cities rarely fail all at once, more often through small daily frictions of crowding, heat and congestion, and this project began by learning to see those frictions on foot. The student returned to one busy block several times, noting where water gathered, where trees offered shade, how roads cut through and where people struggled to pass. Rather than jumping to a design, the guidance asked for analysis made physical. Red straws stood for human circulation, dark and clear tubes for drainage and supply, blue sticks for the sap of trees, and connecting the trees on a plan produced a net that hinted at a new structure. A second study compressed the problem of density into foam cubes and silver threads beneath a broad timber canopy. From these tests came the final section, where pink-edged foam towers rise from a neat grid, copper coils loop overhead as lifted traffic, and clear acrylic balconies and bridges let pedestrians move freely between buildings. The model argues that careful observation can turn congestion into a calmer, more generous city.

zh-Hant.heading: 理順街區-一道理性的剖面
zh-Hant.body: 城市很少一夕之間失靈，更常是因擁擠、炎熱與壅塞等日常的細小摩擦，而這個專題從學會徒步看見這些摩擦開始。學生多次回到同一個繁忙街區，記下水在哪裡聚集、樹木在哪裡提供遮蔭、道路如何切穿。指導過程沒有讓學生急於設計，而是要求把分析化為實體。紅色吸管代表人的流動，深色與透明的管子代表排水與供水，藍色木籤代表樹的汁液，把平面圖上的樹連接起來，則得到一張暗示新結構的網。第二個研究把密度問題壓縮為泡棉方塊與銀色絲線，覆於寬闊的木構棚架之下。從這些試驗中誕生了最終的剖面：粉紅鑲邊的泡棉塔樓從整齊的格網升起，銅線圈在上空盤繞成架高的交通，透明壓克力陽台與天橋讓行人在建築之間自由穿行。模型主張，細心的觀察能把壅塞轉化為更從容、更慷慨的城市。

pins.title: Deconstruction of Football
pins.description:
A football is cut apart and reassembled, then reinterpreted twice, first as a wooden-strip lattice and then as a white PVC landscape of curling ribbons.

Model series | Deconstruction study | Football pieces, wooden strips, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 解構足球
zh-Hant.description:
一顆足球被剪開並重新組裝，之後再兩度重新詮釋，先成為木條格構，再成為由捲曲白色帶狀體構成的PVC地景。

系列模型｜解構研究｜足球碎片、木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Football had been the student’s favourite sport since early childhood, so it became the starting point of the portfolio. After reading about deconstructivist architecture, the student asked what would emerge if a football were taken apart and its pieces rebuilt.
captions: The deconstructivist architect and one of his concert halls, the starting point of the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 足球自幼便是學生最喜愛的運動，因此成為作品集的起點。讀到解構主義建築的文章後，學生追問，若把一顆足球拆開，再以碎片重新組構，會出現什麼。
captions: 解構主義建築師與其設計的音樂廳，本案的起點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The first model cut a real football into curved panels and assembled them without a fixed plan. The pieces were arranged loosely in the manner of a stadium, keeping their bright printed stripes.
captions: The first model from above, with the ball's printed logo still visible.
Cutting the football into pieces and assembling them by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 第一件模型把真正的足球剪成彎曲的片材，在沒有既定計畫下組裝。這些片材被鬆散地排列成類似體育場的樣子，保留了鮮豔的印刷條紋。
captions: 從上方俯看第一個模型，仍可見足球上的印刷標誌。
以手將足球切成碎片並組裝。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second model reinterpreted the first with wooden strips, and the straight, stiff material changed its shape dramatically. The arches dissolved into a dense lattice whose interior filled with tangled shadows.
captions: Bending and fixing the PVC boards by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二件模型以木條重新詮釋第一件，平直而硬挺的材料使形態大幅改變。原本的拱消融為一片密集的格構，內部布滿糾纏的光影。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model turned to thin PVC board, a uniform white material that bends more freely than the football pieces. Curling ribbons, stairs and shells now form a continuous landscape for small figures to move through.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型轉向薄PVC板，這種白色均質的材料比足球片更能自由彎曲。捲曲的帶狀體、階梯與殼體如今構成一片連續的地景，供小人偶穿行。

sections.heading: Undoing the Ball - Three Lives of a Form
sections.body: A football is among the most familiar objects of childhood, a sealed sphere built to roll, fly and survive countless kicks, and this project began by daring to open it. Cut along its seams, the ball released a set of curved, striped panels that no longer knew which way was up. Without a fixed plan, the student assembled them into a loose stadium of leaning arches, letting each panel’s natural curve decide where it could stand. The guidance then asked a harder question, what remains of a form when its material changes. Rebuilt in thin wooden strips, the arches lost their smooth skins and grew into a dense, almost organic lattice, its interior flooded with tangled shadows. A third version in white PVC returned to curvature but with new freedom, as ribbons rose into stairs, shells and floating bridges for tiny figures. Read together, the three models trace a single gesture translated through three materials, showing how deconstruction can become a patient method for discovering space.

zh-Hant.heading: 拆解一顆球-一個形體的三次生命
zh-Hant.body: 足球是童年最熟悉的物件之一，一顆為滾動、飛行並承受無數次踢擊而封合的球體，這個專題從勇於把它打開開始。沿著接縫剪開後，球釋放出一組彎曲而帶條紋的片材，不再分得清上下。學生沒有既定計畫，便把這些片材組成一座由傾斜拱構成的鬆散體育場，讓每片材料天生的弧度決定它能如何站立。指導過程接著提出更困難的問題：當材料改變時，一個形體還剩下什麼。以細木條重建時，拱失去了平滑的表皮，長成一片密集、近乎有機的格構，內部滿溢糾纏的光影。第三個版本以白色PVC回到曲面，卻擁有新的自由，帶狀體升起成階梯、殼體與漂浮的橋，供微小的人偶通行。三件模型並讀，描繪出同一個姿態在三種材料間的轉譯，說明解構可以成為發現空間的一種耐心方法。

pins.title: Wandering Rhapsody
pins.description:
Five traditional arcade shophouses are surveyed and drawn, translated into line patterns and materials, and joined into one imagined street of the future.

Model and drawings | Heritage reinterpretation | Plaster, acrylic strips, wooden strips, PVC board, stockings, straws, litmus paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漫遊狂想曲
zh-Hant.description:
五棟傳統騎樓店屋經測繪與描繪，轉譯為線條圖案與材料，再接合成一條想像中的未來街道。

模型與繪圖｜歷史建築再詮釋｜石膏、壓克力條、木條、PVC板、絲襪、吸管、石蕊試紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Arcade shophouses open to the street through a row of pillars, pairing historic facades with interiors that keep changing. The student, who often wandered past them at home, asked how such buildings could keep up with the times.
captions: Maps of the two old streets, Dongshan and Beijing Road, marking the five scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 騎樓店屋以一排柱廊向街道敞開，把歷史立面與不斷變化的室內結合在一起。學生在家鄉時常漫步經過這些建築，於是追問，它們如何才能與時俱進。
captions: 東山與北京路兩條老街的地圖，標示五個場景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Five favourite shophouses were surveyed and drawn as careful elevations. Each drawing was then matched with an abstract line pattern that captured its rhythm.
captions: Scene 1: the surveyed facade drawing beside the photo of the Qilou shophouse.
Scenes 4 and 5: photos of the Qilou buildings with their facade drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生測繪五棟最喜愛的店屋，畫成細緻的立面圖。每張立面圖再配上一幅抽象線條圖案，捕捉其節奏。
captions: 場景一：騎樓店屋的立面測繪與照片並列。
場景四與五：騎樓建築照片與其立面圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Materials were chosen to suit each pattern, from PVC board and straws to wooden strips, acrylic strips, stockings and plaster. Five scene models were built according to bending degree, line width and the other features of the drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生依每幅圖案挑選材料，從PVC板、吸管到木條、壓克力條、絲襪與石膏。五件場景模型依據彎曲程度、線條粗細與圖面的其他特徵建造。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The five models were put together into one street view imagined by the student. Old facades now rise behind tangled lattices, so that historic buildings carry new functions for the public.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 五件模型被組合成一條由學生想像的街景。舊立面如今在糾纏的格構後方升起，讓歷史建築為大眾承載新的功能。

sections.heading: Walking the Arcade - Memory Built Forward
sections.body: Some buildings are loved less for their grandeur than for the way they frame everyday life, and the arcade shophouse, with its shaded colonnade and shops behind, is one such type. This project grew from years of wandering past them and wondering how an old facade might hold a changing interior. The guidance encouraged slow looking first. Five favourite buildings were surveyed and drawn as precise elevations, then each was distilled into an abstract pattern, a broken grid, a field of lit windows, flowing curves, dense vertical hatching and overlapping frames. These patterns became the brief for choosing material, and qualities such as bending, line weight and density decided whether a scene would be built from straws, timber strips, acrylic rods, stretched stocking or cast plaster. The five scene models were finally joined into one imagined street where historic fronts stand behind exuberant new lattices. The work shows how drawing can turn affection for heritage into a design method that looks forward.

zh-Hant.heading: 漫步騎樓-向前建造的記憶
zh-Hant.body: 有些建築受人喜愛，並非因為宏偉，而是因為它們框住日常生活的方式，騎樓店屋連同遮蔭的柱廊與後方的店鋪，正是其中一種。這個專題源自多年來漫步經過這些建築時的好奇：舊立面如何容納不斷變化的室內。指導過程鼓勵先慢慢觀看。學生測繪五棟最喜愛的建築，畫成精確的立面圖，再把每一棟提煉為一幅抽象圖案：破碎的格網、一片亮著的窗、流動的曲線、密集的垂直排線與交疊的框架。這些圖案成為挑選材料的依據，彎曲、線條粗細與密度等特質，決定一個場景要以吸管、木條、壓克力棒、拉伸的絲襪還是澆鑄的石膏建造。五件場景模型最後接合成一條想像的街道，歷史立面立於繁茂的新格構之後。作品說明，繪圖能把對歷史建築的情感，轉化為一種面向未來的設計方法。

pins.title: Four Layers of a Dream Park
pins.description:
An imagined theme park of four dream levels is built as four linked models, a timber pavilion over acrylic, a rattan loop, a snowfield of cubes and a collapsing city around a blue lake.

Model | Narrative park design | Wooden strips, PVC and acrylic boards, rattan, iron wire, light clay, cement, corrugated paper, cardboard, slime | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 夢境四層樂園
zh-Hant.description:
一座想像中由四層夢境構成的主題樂園，被建成四件相連的模型：壓克力之上的木構亭閣、藤條迴圈、方塊組成的雪原，以及環繞藍色湖泊崩解的城市。

模型｜敘事樂園設計｜木條、PVC與壓克力板、藤條、鐵絲、輕黏土、水泥、瓦楞紙、紙板、史萊姆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 四部分的夢境樂園模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student loves fantasies of experiences that rarely happen in real life, especially adventures that require group work. The project asks how a theme park could let visitors step into layered dreams and take a break from reality.
captions: The film poster that inspired the dream park.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生熱愛想像現實中罕見的經驗，尤其是需要團隊合作的冒險。這個專題探問，主題樂園如何讓遊客走進層層夢境，暫時離開現實。
captions: 啟發這座夢境公園的電影海報。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A plan sketch arranged four zones on a ring, each standing for one dream level and linked by a bridge, a ramp or a lift. Each zone was then developed as its own model on the workbench.
captions: Film stills of the four dream levels behind the four parts of the park.
Process models of the four parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張平面草圖把四個區域排列在環上，每區代表一層夢境，並以橋、坡道或升降梯相連。之後每個區域都在工作檯上各自發展成模型。
captions: 四層夢境的電影劇照，對應公園的四個部分。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first part sets a timber pavilion above a flipping acrylic city washed by rain. The second wraps a corridor of stairs in rattan loops, suggesting the loss of gravity.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一部分把木構亭閣置於一座被雨水沖刷、翻轉的壓克力城市之上。第二部分以藤條迴圈包覆階梯廊道，暗示重力的消失。
captions: 壓克力之上的木構亭閣。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The third part scatters cement-like cubes across a snowfield among wire trees. The last uses three materials for buildings that stand complete, collapse and turn to wreckage around a blue lake.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第三部分把水泥般的方塊散布在雪原上，周圍是鐵絲做的樹。最後一部分以三種材料表現建築從完整、崩塌到化為殘骸的過程，環繞著一座藍色湖泊。

sections.heading: Descending Through Dreams - A Park in Four Layers
sections.body: Dreams have their own architecture, rooms that fold, corridors that turn and cities that dissolve, and this project asked whether such instability could be built and visited. Instead of reproducing scenes, the student was guided to translate each layer of a dream into a material condition. A ring-shaped plan sketched four zones joined by bridges, ramps and lifts, so that visitors would sink from one level into the next as a group. In the first zone, a pavilion of fine timber members rises above a transparent acrylic city, its coloured panels hinting at streets turned on their side. The second wraps a stair corridor in looping strips of rattan, so that the whole mass seems to drift without gravity. A third zone scatters grey cubes across a snowy ground pierced by wire trees, and the last arranges white towers, broken cardboard and fragments around a bright blue lake, staging a slow passage from order to ruin. Together, the four models show how narrative can become a sequence of tangible spatial atmospheres.

zh-Hant.heading: 穿越夢境-四層構成的樂園
zh-Hant.body: 夢境有其自身的建築，會摺疊的房間、會翻轉的廊道與會消融的城市，這個專題追問，這樣的不穩定能否被建造並供人造訪。學生沒有重現場景，而是被引導把每一層夢境轉譯為一種材料狀態。一張環形平面草圖畫出四個以橋、坡道與升降梯相連的區域，讓遊客結伴從一層沉入下一層。在第一區，細木構件組成的亭閣立於透明的壓克力城市之上，彩色板片暗示被翻轉側立的街道。第二區以迴旋的藤條包覆階梯廊道，使整個量體彷彿在失重中漂浮。第三區把灰色方塊散布在被鐵絲樹穿刺的雪地上，最後一區則把白色塔樓、破碎的紙板與殘片環繞一座鮮藍的湖泊，演出從秩序走向廢墟的緩慢過程。四件模型合在一起，說明敘事能化為一連串可觸及的空間氛圍。

pins.title: Floating Bark
pins.description:
The sprawling branches of a great shade tree are rebuilt as a triangulated lattice of wooden sticks floating above a thicket of thin iron wires.

Model | Natural form study | Iron wire, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮樹皮
zh-Hant.description:
一棵巨大遮蔭樹蔓延的枝條，被重建為一片以木籤三角化構成的格構，漂浮在細鐵絲組成的叢林之上。

模型｜自然形態研究｜鐵絲、木籤｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project grew from ordinary trees, and in particular the shade of a giant tree enjoyed on a sizzling summer day. The student was fascinated by the intricate branches spreading overhead as if they were alive.
captions: Tree and bark references, and an early stick study held up to the body.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源自日常的樹木，尤其是炎夏裡一棵巨樹所帶來的遮蔭。學生著迷於頭頂上蔓延交錯、彷彿有生命的枝條。
captions: 樹木與樹皮參考，以及貼近身體的早期木棒研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Bark textures and branch patterns were studied and abstracted into a net of short straight lines. Small triangles proved able to bend the net into a curved, shell-like canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究樹皮紋理與枝條圖樣，並將其抽象化為由短直線構成的網。細小的三角形證明能讓網彎曲成弧形、殼狀的頂棚。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were joined triangle by triangle into a canopy that swells and folds like bark. Dense thin iron wires were then set beneath it to lift the canopy off the ground.
captions: Weaving the wooden sticks onto the wire by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木籤一個三角形接一個三角形地接合，形成如樹皮般隆起與摺疊的頂棚。之後在其下方立起密集的細鐵絲，把頂棚托離地面。
captions: 以手將木棒編織到鐵絲上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished canopy seems to float above a forest of wires, casting a web of shadows on the floor. Small figures walking beneath it recall the cool shade of the tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的頂棚彷彿漂浮在鐵絲之林上，在地面投下網狀的影子。在其下行走的小人偶，喚起那棵樹下的清涼蔭影。

sections.heading: Shade Made Visible - A Canopy of Lines
sections.body: Shade is one of the most generous gifts a tree offers, yet it is usually felt rather than seen, and this project set out to give that feeling a body. The student began with memories of resting under a vast tree on a burning summer afternoon, looking up into branches that seemed to keep moving. Rather than copying branches, the guidance encouraged reading their logic, how countless short members, each straight, can together describe a curving surface. Bark and branching were reduced to a net of lines, and small triangles became the unit that allowed the net to bend without collapsing. Built stick by stick, the canopy swells, folds and thins like living bark. Beneath it, a thicket of fine iron wire lifts the whole structure until it appears to hover, its weight almost dissolved. Under light the lattice throws a second canopy of shadows across the floor, and tiny figures stand within a dappled interior. The model demonstrates how a simple repeated unit can capture the atmosphere of a natural shelter.

zh-Hant.heading: 讓蔭影可見-線條構成的頂棚
zh-Hant.body: 蔭影是一棵樹最慷慨的饋贈之一，卻通常只被感受而不被看見，這個專題便試圖為這份感受賦予形體。學生從記憶出發，回想炎夏午後在一棵巨樹下歇息，仰望那些彷彿仍在擺動的枝條。指導過程沒有讓學生臨摹枝條，而是鼓勵解讀其邏輯：無數根各自筆直的短構件，如何共同描繪出一個彎曲的表面。樹皮與枝序被簡化為一張線網，細小的三角形成為單元，使線網能彎曲而不崩塌。一根接一根地搭建，頂棚如活的樹皮般隆起、摺疊並變薄。在其下方，一片細鐵絲叢林把整個結構托起，直到它看似懸浮，重量幾乎消散。在光線下，格構在地面投下第二層由影子構成的頂棚，微小的人偶立於斑駁的室內。模型說明，一個簡單而重複的單元，便能捕捉自然庇護所的氛圍。

pins.title: The Wall
pins.description:
Memories of a hand-knitted sweater and a walk home through old streets become a soft woollen wall, pierced by small windows and lit from within.

Model and drawings | Memory and material study | Wool, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 牆
zh-Hant.description:
對一件手織毛衣與穿過老街回家之路的記憶，化為一道柔軟的羊毛牆，牆上開著小窗，並從內部透出光亮。

模型與繪圖｜記憶與材料研究｜羊毛、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The model began with a home-made sweater, a gift from a grandparent that felt full of love whenever it was worn. The most healing moment of childhood was the walk through old streets toward that home.
captions: The old street walked through on the way home, the starting point of the wall.
Knitting a home-made sweater by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件模型始於一件手織毛衣，那是祖父母送的禮物，每次穿上都感到滿滿的愛。童年最療癒的時刻，是穿過老街走向那個家的路。
captions: 回家途中走過的老街，這面牆的起點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A line drawing translated the rhythm of knitted stitches into folded fans of lines around square openings. Strands of wool were then photographed close up to study their texture under light.
captions: Folds of soft bedding as a reference for the woollen wall.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張線條圖把編織針目的節奏，轉譯為環繞方形開口、摺疊如扇的線條。學生接著近拍羊毛纖維，研究它們在光線下的質感。
captions: 柔軟寢具的皺褶，作為毛線牆的參考。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small square tubes of PVC board were set into a field at different angles to act as windows. Their density and tilt were tuned so that light would pass through in a soft, scattered pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: PVC板製成的小方管以不同角度嵌入一片場域，作為窗。學生調整它們的密度與傾斜，讓光以柔和而分散的方式穿透。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model, folds of wool drape over the wall and the windows glow like lit homes along a street. Looking at the blurry light coming out of them recalls the excitement of an awaited visit.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，層層羊毛垂覆於牆上，小窗如街邊亮燈的人家般發光。凝望窗中透出的朦朧光線，喚起一次被期待的造訪所帶來的雀躍。

sections.heading: Knitted Walls - Warmth Held in Material
sections.body: Some walls separate, while others hold, and this project imagined a wall that behaves like a garment, soft, warm and made by hand. The starting point was a sweater knitted by a grandparent and the walk home along old lanes, where lit windows promised that someone was waiting. The guidance asked the student to find a spatial language for that tenderness rather than illustrate the memory.
