A line drawing captured the rhythm of stitches as fans of folded lines circling square openings, and close studies of wool revealed how its strands glow and blur when light falls across them. These studies led to two complementary parts. A field of small PVC tubes, tilted at varied angles, became windows that scatter light into a gentle grain. Over them, wool was drawn and gathered into deep vertical folds, a surface that seems to breathe. Photographed in low light, the wall reads as a quiet street at dusk, each window a small promise of welcome. The work shows how memory can be translated into material and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 編織之牆-材料中的溫度
zh-Hant.body: 有些牆用來分隔，有些牆則用來擁抱，這個專題想像一道如衣物般的牆：柔軟、溫暖，並由手工製成。出發點是一件祖父母親手編織的毛衣，以及沿著老巷回家的路，沿途亮著的窗彷彿在說有人正在等候。指導過程要求學生為這份溫柔找到一種空間語言，而不是圖解回憶。一張線條圖把針目的節奏捕捉為環繞方形開口、摺疊如扇的線條，對羊毛的近距離研究則揭示其纖維在光線掠過時如何發亮與暈開。這些研究引出兩個互補的部分。一片以不同角度傾斜的小PVC方管成為窗，把光散射成細緻的紋理。羊毛被牽引並收攏成深深的垂直皺褶覆於其上，形成一個彷彿在呼吸的表面。在微光中拍攝，這道牆讀來像黃昏時一條寧靜的街，每扇窗都是一個小小的歡迎承諾。作品說明，記憶可以被轉譯為材料與光。

pins.title: Loop of Return
pins.description:
Three linked parts, an exploding hall, a racing loop and a concrete square with a stair of PVC ribbons, build a story in which time keeps folding back on itself.

Model | Narrative space study | PVC board, iron wire, concrete, wooden sticks, cotton, transparent coloured paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 回返之環
zh-Hant.description:
三個相連的部分，一座爆炸的大廳、一條追逐的迴圈，以及一座有PVC帶狀階梯的混凝土廣場，構成一個時間不斷回折的故事。

模型｜敘事空間研究｜PVC板、鐵絲、混凝土、木籤、棉花、透明色紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A favourite film about time running backward inspired the student to imagine a place where events repeat in a loop. The project asks how a model could hold the feeling of being trapped in an endless cycle of saving the world.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部關於時間倒流的電影，啟發學生想像一個事件不斷循環重演的地方。這個專題探問，一件模型如何承載受困於拯救世界的無盡循環之中的感受。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A hand sketch mapped three scenes along one route, from an exploding hall to a chase and finally a square. Each scene was given its own material so that the journey could be read in sequence.
captions: Film stills from the time-travel film behind the three parts of the loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張手繪草圖沿著一條路線鋪排三個場景，從爆炸的大廳到一場追逐，最後抵達一座廣場。每個場景各自被賦予材料，讓旅程能依序被閱讀。
captions: 啟發這個循環三個部分的時間旅行電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cotton clouds and tangled wooden sticks describe the first explosion, while curving PVC strips race between them as the chase. A square model of PVC was cast in concrete to form the last part.
captions: Building the model by hand: bending PVC, fixing sticks and drilling the concrete.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 棉花雲與糾結的木籤描繪第一場爆炸，彎曲的PVC條帶則在其間奔馳，代表追逐。PVC製成的方形模具中澆灌了混凝土，構成最後一部分。
captions: 以手製作模型：彎折PVC、固定木棒與鑽鑿混凝土。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A spiral staircase of PVC ribbons rises from the square, standing for a machine that lets people travel back and forth in time. The whole model conveys a figure caught in a loop with no other choice.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一座PVC帶狀的螺旋梯從廣場升起，象徵一部讓人在時間中往返的機器。整件模型傳達出一個困於循環、別無選擇的身影。

sections.heading: Folding Time - A Loop Built in Three Acts
sections.body: Stories about reversing time are thrilling because they bend cause and effect, and this project asked how such a bending might be built. Leaving the original narrative behind, the student was guided to design a sequence of spaces in which a visitor would feel time circling back. A sketch first plotted three acts along a single route. The opening act is an explosion rendered in billowing cotton and splintered wooden sticks, frozen at its loudest instant. The second is a chase, where white PVC strips sweep through the debris like tracks of speed. The final act settles into a square cast in concrete, solid and heavy, from which a spiral stair of PVC ribbon lifts away, a device for travelling in both directions at once. Coloured transparent paper adds flashes of light that hint at moments seen twice. Seen from above, the three parts join into one ring whose end returns to its beginning. The model shows how a sequence of materials can make an abstract idea of time tangible.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺疊時間-以三幕建成的環
zh-Hant.body: 關於逆轉時間的故事之所以扣人心弦，在於它們扭轉了因果，這個專題追問，這樣的扭轉要如何被建造。學生放下原本的敘事，被引導設計一連串空間，讓造訪者感到時間繞圈回返。一張草圖先沿著單一路線安排三幕。第一幕是一場爆炸，以翻湧的棉花與碎裂的木籤呈現，凝結在最響亮的那一刻。第二幕是一場追逐，白色PVC條帶如速度的軌跡般掃過殘骸。最後一幕沉靜為一座以混凝土澆鑄、厚實沉重的廣場，一座PVC帶狀螺旋梯從中升起，是一部能同時朝兩個方向行進的裝置。透明色紙添上幾道閃光，暗示被看見兩次的瞬間。從上方看，三個部分連成一個終點回到起點的環。模型說明，一連串材料能讓抽象的時間概念變得可以觸及。

pins.title: The Maze
pins.description:
A clear acrylic cube holds layer upon layer of maze walls, letting viewers watch from outside as figures wander within routes they cannot leave.

Model | Concept study | Acrylic board, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 迷宮
zh-Hant.description:
一個透明壓克力立方體容納層層疊疊的迷宮牆，讓觀者從外部看著人偶在無法離開的路徑中徘徊。

模型｜概念研究｜壓克力板、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The model asks whether human beings have free will or not. To the student, life seems to offer countless ways to go, yet every route ends at the same destination.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件模型追問人類是否擁有自由意志。在學生看來，人生似乎提供無數條路，然而每條路最終都通往同一個終點。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several small PVC mazes were built to test patterns of turns, dead ends and loops. Their plans were compared to find layouts that feel open yet allow only one true way through.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生製作多個小型PVC迷宮，測試轉彎、死路與迴圈的圖樣。比較它們的平面，以找出看似開放、卻只容許一條真正出路的配置。
captions: 小型壓克力測試立方體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Acrylic board replaced PVC so that people inside the maze could be seen clearly from outside. Mazes were stacked in many levels inside one cube, with figures placed along the routes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 壓克力板取代了PVC，讓迷宮中的人能從外部被清楚看見。多層迷宮堆疊在同一個立方體內，人偶沿著路徑擺放。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Lit against a dark ground, the walls turn into a tangle of glowing lines in which red figures wander. Viewers can see them confused, until they realise there is no choice but to follow the route set for them.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在黑暗背景下打光，牆面化為一團發光線條，紅色人偶在其中徘徊。觀者能看見它們的困惑，直到它們明白，除了沿著被設定好的路線前進之外別無選擇。

sections.heading: Walls of Glass - Choice Within a Cube
sections.body: A maze is a promise of choice that quietly withholds it, and this project used that tension to think about freedom. The student began with a question that philosophy has never settled, whether a life of many paths is truly free if every path leads to the same end. To make the question spatial, small mazes were first built in white PVC, testing turns, dead ends and loops until certain plans felt generous while still guiding walkers toward a single exit. The guidance then pushed for a change of material. Clear acrylic allowed the walls to vanish and reappear depending on the light, so that an observer outside could follow every hesitation of the tiny red figures inside. Stacked layer upon layer within one cube, the mazes multiply into a vertical city of corridors. Photographed against darkness, the edges glow like drawn lines and the figures seem suspended in a net of light. The model turns an abstract philosophical doubt into an experience of looking, showing how transparency can reveal the structures that shape a life.

zh-Hant.heading: 玻璃之牆-立方體中的選擇
zh-Hant.body: 迷宮是一種悄悄收回選擇的選擇承諾，這個專題借用這份張力來思考自由。學生從一個哲學始終未能解答的問題出發：倘若每條路都通往同一個終點，擁有許多道路的人生是否真正自由。為了把問題空間化，學生先以白色PVC製作小型迷宮，測試轉彎、死路與迴圈，直到某些平面讀來寬容，卻仍把行走者引向唯一的出口。指導過程接著促成材料的轉換。透明壓克力讓牆面隨光線消失又浮現，外部的觀察者因而能追隨內部微小紅色人偶的每一次遲疑。迷宮在同一個立方體中層層堆疊，增殖為一座垂直的廊道之城。在黑暗中拍攝，邊緣如畫出的線條般發光，人偶彷彿懸浮在一張光網之中。模型把抽象的哲學疑問轉化為一種觀看的經驗，說明透明性能揭示形塑人生的結構。

pins.title: Folding Geometry
pins.description:
Paper origami folds are translated into cubic frames of wooden sticks and iron wire, from twisted planes of lines to stacked rotating squares.

Model series | Geometry study | Iron wire, wooden sticks, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 摺疊幾何
zh-Hant.description:
紙摺紙的摺痕被轉譯為以木籤與鐵絲構成的立方框架，從扭轉的線面到層疊旋轉的方形。

系列模型｜幾何研究｜鐵絲、木籤、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Folding paper creates complex forms from a single flat sheet. The project asks how such folding could be carried from soft paper into rigid wood.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 摺紙能從一張平面紙張創造出複雜的形體。這個專題探問，這樣的摺疊如何從柔軟的紙轉移到堅硬的木材上。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Origami training served as the first step, with several folded paper forms photographed on black. Drawings then placed the folds inside cubic frames to study their geometry.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以摺紙練習作為第一步，把多件摺紙作品拍攝在黑色背景上。接著以繪圖把摺痕放入立方框架中，研究其幾何。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks and iron wire were used to rebuild the folds as cubes crossed by planes of parallel lines. Later frames filled the cube with stepped grids that rise like folded terraces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木籤與鐵絲重建摺痕，形成被平行線面穿越的立方體。後續的框架以階梯狀格網填滿立方體，如摺疊的台地般升起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final set, square frames are stacked and rotated step by step into a twisted ring. The rings show how a simple fold can grow into a rich spatial rhythm.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最後一組作品中，方形框架逐步堆疊旋轉，形成一個扭轉的環。這些環展示了一個簡單的摺疊如何生長為豐富的空間韻律。

sections.heading: From Crease to Frame - Geometry Learned by Hand
sections.body: Origami teaches that a flat sheet already contains a world of forms, waiting to be released by a sequence of creases, and this project set out to carry that lesson from paper into wood. The student first practised folding, photographing each paper study against black so that its ridges and valleys read clearly. Drawings followed, placing the creases inside the edges of a cube and revealing hidden diagonals and planes. The guidance then asked what happens when a fold can no longer bend. Wooden sticks and iron wire turned each crease into a straight member, so that a soft surface became a field of parallel lines stretched across a frame. Some cubes are sliced by twisting planes of lines, others filled with stepped grids that climb like folded terraces. In the final series, square frames are stacked and turned a few degrees at a time, until they spiral into rings that feel woven rather than built. The project demonstrates how disciplined repetition can turn a childhood craft into architectural thinking.

zh-Hant.heading: 從摺痕到框架-以手習得的幾何
zh-Hant.body: 摺紙教導我們，一張平面紙張早已蘊含一個形體的世界，等待一連串摺痕將其釋放，這個專題便試圖把這份領悟從紙帶進木材。學生先練習摺疊，把每件摺紙研究拍攝在黑色背景上，讓其山摺與谷摺清楚可讀。接著是繪圖，把摺痕放進立方體的邊框之內，揭示隱藏的斜線與平面。指導過程隨後追問：當摺疊不再能彎曲時，會發生什麼。木籤與鐵絲把每道摺痕化為一根直構件，柔軟的表面於是成為拉伸於框架間的平行線場。有些立方體被扭轉的線面切開，有些則被如摺疊台地般攀升的階梯格網填滿。在最後的系列中，方形框架每次轉動幾度地堆疊，直到盤旋成彷彿編織而非建造出來的環。這個專題說明，有紀律的重複能把童年的手藝轉化為建築思考。

pins.title: Tower of Five Layers
pins.description:
A tower rises from stone and clay through wood, acrylic and folded paper to a crown of clear bubbles, each layer standing for a different way a city is remembered.

Model | Memory and city study | Stone, clay, wood, acrylic, paper, iron wire, plastic balls | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 五層之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一座塔從石頭與黏土升起，經過木材、壓克力與摺紙，直到一頂透明泡泡之冠，每一層都代表城市被記憶的一種方式。

模型｜記憶與城市研究｜石頭、黏土、木材、壓克力、紙、鐵絲、塑膠球｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began from a reading about imagined cities, which led the student to think of cities as memories of the past, present and future. The question was how one vertical object could hold these different kinds of remembering at once.
captions: The cover of the novel that inspired the tower.
Souvenir fridge magnets from cities around the world.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題始於一段關於想像城市的閱讀，引導學生把城市視為對過去、現在與未來的記憶。問題在於，一個垂直的物件如何能同時容納這些不同的記憶方式。
captions: 啟發這座塔的小說封面。
來自世界各地城市的紀念冰箱磁鐵。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student noticed that a first image of a city often comes from souvenirs and pictures, which collapse once the real place is visited. Ideas of renewal and discarded waste were added, and sketches sorted the tower into stone, wood, acrylic, paper and bubbles.
captions: Sketches of real cities compared with the images on the magnets.
Photos of an artificial island built from construction waste.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生注意到，對一座城市的第一印象往往來自紀念品與圖片，而這些印象在真正造訪時便會瓦解。學生再加入更新與廢棄物的概念，並以草圖把塔分為石頭、木材、壓克力、紙與泡泡。
captions: 與磁鐵圖像對照的真實城市速寫。
以建築廢料堆成的人工島照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A base of stone and clay supports a wooden frame with spiral stairs and small rooms, which turns into translucent acrylic of the same structure above. Higher up the acrylic sticks grow irregular, folded paper points downward like a skin being shed, and bubbles strung on wire gather at the top.
captions: Assembling the acrylic and paper layers by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石頭與黏土的基座承托一座帶有螺旋梯與小房間的木構架，往上則轉為結構相同的半透明壓克力。再往上，壓克力桿件變得不規則，摺紙朝下指著如同正在脫落的外皮，而以鐵絲串起的泡泡聚集在頂端。
captions: 以手組裝壓克力與紙的層次。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower reads as a passage from solid ground to drifting thought, with tiny red figures climbing through every layer. The bubbles at the crown stand for feelings produced by cities yet unable to settle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔可被解讀為一段從堅實地面到飄浮思緒的通道，細小的紅色人偶攀爬穿越每一層。頂端的泡泡象徵由城市所生、卻無法安定下來的感受。

sections.heading: Layers of Remembering - A Tower from Stone to Air
sections.body: Every city is carried in the mind as several cities at once, the one imagined before arrival, the one met in the street and the one discarded as it renews itself. This project gave each of these a material and stacked them into a single tower. The student started from reading and from the gap between pictures of distant places and the experience of visiting them, then asked how memory changes as it rises away from the ground. Guidance focused on letting structure, not symbols, carry the idea. Stone and clay form a heavy origin, wood builds a habitable frame of stairs and rooms, and acrylic repeats that frame in translucent form, as present and past held side by side. Above, the order loosens, folded paper peels downward like an abandoned skin, and clear spheres float on threads of wire. The tower therefore becomes a vertical narrative in which density gives way to lightness. It shows how a sequence of materials can turn an abstract reading into an architecture of memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 記憶的層次-從石頭到空氣之塔
zh-Hant.body: 每一座城市在心中都同時是好幾座城市：抵達前想像的那座、在街上遇見的那座，以及在自我更新中被拋棄的那座。這個專題為每一座都賦予一種材料，並將它們疊成一座塔。學生從閱讀出發，也從遠方的圖片與親身造訪之間的落差出發，進而追問記憶在遠離地面上升時如何改變。指導重點在於讓結構而非符號承載概念。石頭與黏土構成沉重的起點，木材搭出可居的樓梯與房間框架，壓克力則以半透明的形式重複這個框架，讓現在與過去並置。再往上，秩序逐漸鬆動，摺紙如被遺棄的外皮向下剝落，透明球體漂浮在鐵絲的細線上。於是這座塔成為一段垂直的敘事，密實逐漸讓位給輕盈。它說明一連串材料如何能把抽象的閱讀轉化為記憶的建築。

pins.title: Sound Cone
pins.description:
Sounds heard on the way home are translated into cones of wood strips, iron wire, cotton and card, each apex marking where a sound begins.

Installation and model | Sound study | Wood, iron wire, cotton, white cardboard, litmus paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聲音之錐
zh-Hant.description:
回家路上聽見的聲音，被轉譯為由木條、鐵絲、棉花與卡紙構成的錐體，每個頂點都標示一個聲音的起點。

裝置與模型｜聲音研究｜木材、鐵絲、棉花、白卡紙、石蕊試紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Lying awake in the dark, the student liked to listen to night sounds and locate them only by hearing. The project asked whether sounds could be turned into visible forms that also record where they come from.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生喜歡在黑暗中醒著聆聽夜裡的聲音，只憑聽覺為它們定位。這個專題探問，聲音能否被轉化為可見的形體，並同時記錄其來源的位置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A recording of the walk home was replayed and drawn as lines of marks, then converted into a long scene of white models. Single sounds were identified first, and their combination was used to infer the surrounding environment.
captions: The sound path as a scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把回家路上的錄音重播，畫成一行行的記號，再轉化為一長列白色模型的場景。學生先辨認出單一的聲音，再以它們的組合推斷周遭的環境。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each sound was matched to a material, with cotton for voices, iron wire for scanners, wood strips for footsteps and rotating card for escalators. Because sound spreads from a point, every material was shaped into a cone whose apex is the source.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每種聲音都對應一種材料：棉花代表人聲，鐵絲代表掃描器，木條代表腳步聲，旋轉的卡紙代表電扶梯。由於聲音從一點擴散，每種材料都被塑造成以頂點為聲源的錐體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The cones are joined into one cluster that translates the journey home into a single object. Looking inside each cone reveals layered wood, wire and cotton that frame light like a sound fading away.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些錐體結合為一個群組，把回家的旅程轉譯為單一物件。望進每個錐體，可見層疊的木材、鐵絲與棉花，如漸弱的聲音般框住光線。

sections.heading: Listening Made Solid - Cones of the Way Home
sections.body: Sound is the most fleeting of materials, present for an instant and gone, yet it shapes our sense of place as strongly as walls do. This project tried to make that fleeting presence solid. The student began by listening in the dark and recording an ordinary walk home, then learned to separate a blur of noise into single voices, footsteps and machines. The guidance stressed a rule-based translation, so that each sound received a material whose texture matched its character. Soft cotton became speech, taut wire became electronic hum, stacked strips of wood became the rhythm of walking and turning card became moving stairs. Because a sound radiates outward from where it is made, the cone was chosen as the common form, its apex fixed at the source. Joined together, the cones form a dense cluster that can be read like a sentence of sounds. Peering inside, layered edges catch light and fade toward the tip. The project demonstrates how careful listening can become a method for describing space.

zh-Hant.heading: 把聆聽化為實體-回家之路的錐體
zh-Hant.body: 聲音是最短暫的材料，存在一瞬便消失，卻和牆一樣強烈地塑造我們對場所的感知。這個專題試圖讓這份短暫的存在變得堅實。學生從在黑暗中聆聽開始，錄下一段平凡的回家路程，並學會把模糊的噪音分辨為單一的人聲、腳步與機器聲。指導強調依循規則的轉譯，讓每種聲音都得到一種質感與其性格相符的材料。柔軟的棉花成為話語，繃緊的鐵絲成為電子的嗡鳴，層疊的木條成為行走的節奏，轉動的卡紙成為移動的階梯。由於聲音從發出之處向外擴散，錐體被選為共同的形式，頂點固定於聲源。結合之後，錐體形成一個密集的群組，可像一句由聲音組成的句子般閱讀。向內窺看，層疊的邊緣捕捉光線，並朝尖端漸漸隱去。這個專題說明，細心的聆聽能成為描述空間的方法。

pins.title: The Frame
pins.description:
Translucent coloured surfaces set inside a white resin frame overlap and cast shadows, turning one structure into many small framed artworks.

Model | Art and form study | White resin, litmus paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 框
zh-Hant.description:
置於白色樹脂框架中的半透明彩色表面彼此重疊並投下陰影，讓一個結構成為許多被框起的小型藝術作品。

模型｜藝術與形式研究｜白色樹脂、石蕊試紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After studying many kinds of art, the student concluded that artworks are recombinations of elements drawn from a list of forms and a list of themes. The project set out to prove this by rearranging extracted elements into a new piece.
captions: A collage of painted figures and fragments from the artworks studied.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在研究多種藝術之後，學生得出結論：藝術作品都是從形式清單與主題清單中抽取元素再重新組合。這個專題便試圖透過重新排列這些抽取出的元素，創作出一件新作品來證明這一點。
captions: 由所研究藝術作品中的人物與碎片構成的拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Colour, geometry, lighting and theme were extracted from a range of artworks and tested in sketches and study models. Overlapping transparent surfaces of the three primary colours produced a wider range of tones, while linear elements threw shadows of different widths.
captions: Artistic research: colours, geometric elements, lighting and themes taken from artworks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從多件藝術作品中抽取色彩、幾何、光線與主題，並以草圖和研究模型加以測試。三原色的透明表面重疊後產生更寬廣的色調，而線性元素則投下寬窄不一的陰影。
captions: 藝術研究：從藝術作品中擷取的色彩、幾何元素、光線與主題。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A white resin frame was designed to hold translucent coloured sheets at many angles. Light was then moved around the model to record how colours mixed and how the surfaces divided into blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生設計一個白色樹脂框架，以多種角度承托半透明的彩色片材。接著在模型周圍移動光源，記錄色彩如何混合、表面如何被分割成色塊。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each framed surface works as an independent artwork, divided into colour blocks by the surfaces overlapping it. The overall form shows different patterns from every angle.
captions: A long view of the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個被框起的表面都是一件獨立作品，並被與之重疊的表面分割成色塊。整體形式從每個角度看都呈現不同的圖樣。

sections.heading: Colour Held in Place - A Frame of Many Pictures
sections.body: A frame is usually the quietest part of a picture, yet it decides what is seen and what is left out. This project made the frame the subject itself. The student began from a bold idea, that works of art share a hidden grammar of forms and themes, and spent the research phase dismantling artworks into colour, geometry, light and mood. The guidance pushed those fragments toward a spatial test rather than a collage. Transparent sheets in primary colours were found to multiply into new tones where they overlap, and thin lines were found to cast shadows that vary with the light. A white resin frame then gathered these discoveries, holding coloured planes at shifting angles so that each opening becomes a small composition. As the viewer circles the model, blocks of colour slide over one another and the pictures continually rearrange. Light becomes the brush and the frame the canvas. The model demonstrates how analysis of existing art can generate an original spatial language.

zh-Hant.heading: 被安放的色彩-由許多畫面構成的框
zh-Hant.body: 畫框通常是一幅畫中最安靜的部分，卻決定了什麼被看見、什麼被留在外面。這個專題讓框本身成為主題。學生從一個大膽的想法出發，認為藝術作品共享一套隱藏的形式與主題文法，並在研究階段把藝術作品拆解為色彩、幾何、光線與情緒。指導把這些碎片推向空間的試驗，而非拼貼。學生發現，三原色的透明片材在重疊處會繁衍出新的色調，細線則投下隨光線變化的陰影。一個白色樹脂框架隨後匯集這些發現，以不斷變換的角度承托彩色平面，讓每個開口都成為一幅小小的構圖。當觀者繞著模型行走，色塊相互滑移，畫面持續重組。光成為畫筆，框成為畫布。這個模型說明，對既有藝術的分析能孕育出原創的空間語言。

pins.title: Momentary Eternal
pins.description:
Sand held in square pockets of plastic wrap is joined into a balancing cluster, freezing the movement of sand at every moment.

Model | Material study | Sand, plastic wrap, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 瞬間的永恆
zh-Hant.description:
裝在方形保鮮膜袋中的沙被連接成一個保持平衡的群組，把沙的流動凍結在每一個瞬間。

模型｜材料研究｜沙、保鮮膜、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project started from childhood play on a beach, where wet sand is shaped by the sea and then dries and flows again. A single grain is fixed in form while a mass of grains is fluid, which links sand to the passing of time.
captions: A childhood photo of playing with sand on the beach.
Shaping wet sand in a tray by hand, imitating sand washed by the sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源自童年在海灘上的遊戲，濕沙被海水塑形，乾了之後又再流動。一粒沙的形狀是固定的，但一堆沙卻是流動的，這讓沙與時間的流逝產生連結。
captions: 童年在海灘玩沙的照片。
以手在盤中塑造濕沙，模仿被海水沖刷的沙。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sand was mixed with glues in different types and proportions to imitate the patterns of washed sand. Plaster, plastic wrap, epoxy glue and iron wire were then used to cast positive and negative forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把沙與不同種類與比例的膠混合，模仿被沖刷的沙紋。接著使用石膏、保鮮膜、環氧樹脂膠與鐵絲，鑄出正形與負形。
captions: 以環氧樹脂膠固定的沙。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: To give the sand more freedom, ten square units of plastic wrap and sand were made, first hung inside a wooden frame. The wrap proved able both to restrict the sand and to be shaped by its weight.
captions: Making the plastic-wrap and sand units by hand.
Units hung in a wooden frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 為了給沙更多自由，學生製作了十個以保鮮膜和沙構成的方形單元，最初懸掛在木框中。保鮮膜證明既能限制沙的移動，也會被沙的重量所塑造。
captions: 以手製作保鮮膜與沙的單元。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model the squares connect directly to each other, deforming until the whole installation finds its balance. The rise and fall of each pocket carries a different trend of moving sand, like sea water frozen in an instant.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，方形單元直接彼此連接，變形直到整個裝置找到平衡。每個袋子的起伏承載著不同的沙流趨勢，彷彿在一瞬間被凍結的海水。

sections.heading: Time in a Grain - Sand Held in Suspension
sections.body: Sand is a paradox, each grain firm and fixed, while the mass slips, settles and reshapes itself without end, which is why it has long measured time. This project tried to hold that paradox still for a moment. The student returned to memories of shaping wet sand by the sea and began a patient series of trials, binding sand with glues, casting it in plaster and propping it on wire. These experiments taught that fixing the sand completely erased what made it alive. The guidance therefore turned toward a medium that could both contain and yield, and thin plastic wrap became that medium. Ten square pockets of wrap and sand were first suspended in a timber frame and finally joined only to one another, stretching and folding until they reached equilibrium. Each pocket records a different direction of flow, and light passing through the film reveals drifting veins of grain. The installation becomes a tide arrested mid-motion. It shows how material experiment can give lasting form to an instant.

zh-Hant.heading: 一粒沙中的時間-懸浮之沙
zh-Hant.body: 沙是一個悖論：每一粒都堅實而固定，整體卻不停滑動、沉積並重塑自身，這正是它長久以來被用來計量時間的原因。這個專題試圖讓這個悖論靜止片刻。學生回到在海邊塑造濕沙的記憶，開始一連串耐心的試驗：以膠黏合沙、以石膏鑄造沙、以鐵絲撐起沙。這些實驗讓學生明白，把沙完全固定，會抹去它之所以鮮活的特質。於是指導轉向一種既能容納又能順從的媒材，薄薄的保鮮膜便成為這種媒材。十個裝著沙的方形膜袋最初懸掛於木框中，最後只彼此相連，伸展、摺疊，直到達成平衡。每個膜袋記錄一個不同的流動方向，穿過薄膜的光揭示沙粒漂移的紋理。整個裝置成為一道在運動中被定格的潮水。它說明材料實驗能為一個瞬間賦予持久的形體。

pins.title: Pyramid and Hinge
pins.description:
Four hinged pyramids are unfolded in drawings and rebuilt with linear outer surfaces, so that stairs between them are striped with dramatic light.

Drawings and digital model | Geometry and light study | Line drawing, digital rendering | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 金字塔與鉸接
zh-Hant.description:
四個鉸接的金字塔在圖面中被展開，並以線性外表面重新構築，使其間的階梯灑滿戲劇性的條紋光影。

圖面與數位模型｜幾何與光線研究｜線圖、數位渲染｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explored how four primary pyramids could be linked by hinges into one spatial system. The challenge was to make the hinging legible and to let people move between the pyramids.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探索四個基本金字塔如何以鉸接方式連結為一個空間系統。挑戰在於讓鉸接關係清晰可讀，並讓人能在金字塔之間移動。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The pyramids were exploded in a rotational drawing and an unrolled elevation drawing to clarify how they hinge. A plan and section composite then showed how stairs connect the pyramids and where a skylight falls.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以旋轉圖與展開立面圖把金字塔爆炸展開，以釐清它們如何鉸接。接著以平面與剖面的複合圖，呈現階梯如何連接金字塔，以及天光落在何處。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Following an alternate surface logic, most outer surfaces were replaced with linear elements. Model views were studied to see how the lines would filter light into the interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 依循另一種表面邏輯，大部分的外表面被替換為線性元素。學生研究模型的多個視角，觀察這些線條如何把光線過濾進室內。
captions: 金字塔模型的多個視角。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Inside, the linear surfaces cast bands of shadow across walls and stairs, making the climb between pyramids dramatic. Small figures show how people would pass through the striped light.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在室內，線性表面在牆面與階梯上投下一道道陰影，讓穿越金字塔之間的攀爬充滿戲劇性。小比例人形顯示人們將如何穿過條紋光影。

sections.heading: Hinges of Light - Unfolding Four Pyramids
sections.body: The pyramid is among the most closed of forms, a solid that seems to admit neither movement nor light, and this project set out to open it. The student worked with four primary pyramids and the hinges that bind them, treating the joints as the real subject of the design. Before any space was imagined, the guidance asked for drawings that could explain the geometry, so the pyramids were exploded, rotated and unrolled until every fold could be traced. A combined plan and section then turned the abstract hinges into routes, revealing stairs that pass from one volume to the next and a skylight that marks a pause. The decisive step came with an alternate surface logic in which solid faces gave way to rows of thin members. Sunlight now enters in bands, sliding across walls and treads as the figures climb. Weight turns into rhythm, and enclosure becomes filtered openness. The work demonstrates how rigorous drawing can transform a closed solid into a choreography of light.

zh-Hant.heading: 光的鉸接-展開四座金字塔
zh-Hant.body: 金字塔是最封閉的形式之一，一個彷彿既不容許移動也不容許光線的實體，而這個專題便試圖將它打開。學生以四個基本金字塔及連結它們的鉸接為對象，把接合處視為設計真正的主題。在想像任何空間之前，指導先要求能解釋幾何的圖面，於是金字塔被爆炸、旋轉並展開，直到每一道摺線都能被追溯。隨後，平面與剖面的複合圖把抽象的鉸接轉化為路徑，揭示從一個量體通往下一個量體的階梯，以及標記停頓的天光。決定性的一步來自另一種表面邏輯：實面讓位給一排排細長的構件。陽光於是成帶狀進入，隨著人形攀升而滑過牆面與踏階。重量化為節奏，封閉成為經過過濾的開放。這件作品說明，嚴謹的繪圖能把一個封閉的實體轉化為光的編舞。

pins.title: A Room Repeated
pins.description:
Two drawn plans of the same small room, a year apart, become the start of a dreamlike journey in which each daily action is turned into a scene.

Drawings | Memory and everyday life | Pencil sketch, digital drawing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重複的房間
zh-Hant.description:
同一間小房間相隔一年的兩張手繪平面，成為一段夢境般旅程的起點，每個日常動作都被轉化為一個場景。

圖面｜記憶與日常生活｜鉛筆素描、數位繪圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The room in the first period.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: During two long periods of staying at home a year apart, the student felt that life was simply repeating itself in the same room. The project asked how to make visible the small differences hidden in that repetition, and how to escape its boredom.
captions: Photos of the daily objects and actions in the room: quilt, windowsill, uniform and hair tie.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在相隔一年的兩段長時間居家期間，學生感到生活只是在同一個房間裡不斷重複。這個專題探問，如何讓隱藏在重複中的細微差異變得可見，又如何擺脫其中的乏味。
captions: 房間中日常物件與動作的照片：棉被、窗台、制服與髮圈。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The room was drawn in detailed plan for both periods, recording a heavy quilt replaced by a thin one and objects moved by daily use. Comparing the two plans revealed how repeated actions slowly shifted the room.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以詳細的平面圖描繪兩段時期的房間，記錄厚被換成薄被，以及因日常使用而被移動的物件。比較兩張平面圖，揭示重複的動作如何慢慢改變了房間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Four repeated actions, at the windowsill, unfolding clothes, tumbling in the quilt and tying up hair, were drawn as studies of movement. Each study stressed one of the five senses that the action brings.
captions: A drawing of hands tying up hair.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 窗台前的動作、攤開衣物、在被中翻滾與綁頭髮，這四個重複的動作被畫成動態研究。每張研究都強調該動作所帶來的五感之一。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each action was turned into a digital scene, and the scenes were linked by a roller coaster into one journey through the room. The drawings offer a playful way of turning routine into an adventure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個動作都被轉化為一個數位場景，並以一條雲霄飛車把各場景串成一段穿越房間的旅程。這些圖面以充滿玩心的方式把例行公事變成一場冒險。

sections.heading: Dreaming Within Walls - A Ride Through Routine
sections.body: Repetition can make a familiar room almost invisible, as if the same gestures had worn away every detail. This project began in such a state, during two long stretches of staying indoors separated by a year, and turned that sense of sameness into material for design. The student first drew the room twice in careful plan, noting each fold of bedding and every object on the desk and sill, so that the drawings themselves could reveal what memory had missed. The guidance encouraged reading these small differences as traces of movement rather than as mere inventory. Four ordinary actions were then isolated and redrawn as studies of motion, each emphasising one of the senses it awakens. Finally, the actions grew into digital scenes threaded together by a looping roller coaster, transforming a confined bedroom into a landscape for wandering. The shift from precise observation to free invention is what gives the work its charm. It shows how close attention to routine can open a door to imagination.

zh-Hant.heading: 在牆內作夢-穿越日常的旅程
zh-Hant.body: 重複能讓一個熟悉的房間幾乎隱形，彷彿相同的動作磨去了每一個細節。這個專題正是在這樣的狀態中展開：兩段相隔一年的長時間居家，把那份千篇一律的感受轉化為設計的素材。學生先以細緻的平面圖兩度描繪房間，記下寢具的每道摺痕以及書桌與窗台上的每件物品，讓圖面本身揭示記憶所遺漏的事物。指導鼓勵把這些細微差異解讀為動作的痕跡，而不只是物件清單。接著，四個平凡的動作被分離出來，重新畫成動態研究，各自強調所喚醒的一種感官。最後，這些動作發展為數位場景，由一條迴旋的雲霄飛車串連，把狹小的臥室轉化為可供漫遊的風景。從精確觀察到自由創造的轉換，正是這件作品的魅力所在。它說明，對日常的專注能為想像打開一扇門。

pins.title: Campus Impressions
pins.description:
Hollowed PVC panels with cut pieces lifted into floating islands and layered like waves record the feeling of a favourite corner of school.

Model | Memory and campus study | PVC panels, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 校園印象
zh-Hant.description:
挖空的PVC板與被抬升為漂浮孤島的切片，如波浪般層層堆疊，記錄校園中一個最喜愛角落的感受。

模型｜記憶與校園研究｜PVC板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began from a favourite corner of a middle school campus that served as an emotional shelter in moments of joy or sadness. The question was how the feeling of such a place could be recorded as an abstract model rather than as a picture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源自中學校園裡一個最喜愛的角落，無論快樂或悲傷時，那裡都是情緒的避風港。問題在於，如何把這樣一個場所的感受記錄為抽象模型，而非一幅圖像。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Photos of the garden were studied to pick out elements such as flower branches, grass and notice boards, which were then segmented and recombined into closed geometries. Line studies of the sea and of the school corner tested how these fragments could be read as patterns.
captions: A photo of the sea, one of the two inspirations for the model.
A line study of the sea.
A line study of the school corner.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究花園的照片，挑出花枝、草地與布告欄等元素，再將其分割並重組為封閉的幾何形。對海面與校園角落的線描研究，則測試這些碎片如何被解讀為圖樣。
captions: 海的照片，是模型的兩個靈感來源之一。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Closed shapes were hollowed out of PVC panels, and following the principle of solid and void, cut pieces were pasted back above and below their original positions to form isolated islands. The rise and fall of waves was then added by trimming small triangles from each layer so that every level shrinks inward and seems to float.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生從PVC板中挖出封閉的形狀，並依循實與虛的原則，把切下的片材貼回原位的上方或下方，形成一座座孤島。接著，學生從每一層的邊角切下小三角形，讓每層向內收縮而顯得漂浮，藉此加入波浪的起伏。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three PVC panels connected by wooden strips enclose an undulating space in the middle, read as the essence of the comforting corner. Small figures wandering through the layers show the model as a landscape of drifting islands.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三片PVC板由木條連接，在中間圍出一個起伏的空間，可被解讀為那個撫慰人心之角落的精髓。在各層之間漫遊的小人形，讓模型呈現為一片漂移孤島的地景。

sections.heading: Islands of Shelter - Waves Cut from a Campus Memory
sections.body: Some places matter less for how they look than for how they steady the mind, and a quiet corner of a school can become such a refuge. This project set out to record that refuge without depicting it. The student began with photographs of a garden and searched them for ordinary elements, branches, grass and notice boards, then reduced each to a closed outline. The guidance encouraged turning these outlines into a rule of solid and void rather than a picture. Shapes were cut from sheets of PVC and returned slightly above or below their origin, so that each sheet became a field of small islands. Memory of the sea then suggested a second rule, as triangles trimmed from the edges made every layer retreat inward and appear to float. Three such layers, held apart by slender wooden strips, enclose a rolling space where small figures drift between fragments. The model shows how an emotional memory can be translated into a precise and repeatable method of making.

zh-Hant.heading: 庇護之島-從校園記憶切出的波浪
zh-Hant.body: 有些場所的意義不在外貌，而在於它如何安定人心，校園裡一個安靜的角落便可能成為這樣的庇護。這個專題試圖記錄這份庇護，卻不去描繪它。學生從花園的照片出發，尋找花枝、草地與布告欄等平凡元素，並把每一個簡化為封閉的輪廓。指導鼓勵把輪廓轉化為實與虛的規則，而非圖像。形狀從PVC板中切下，再略高或略低地放回原處，讓每片板材成為一片小島群。對海的記憶帶來第二條規則：修去邊緣的三角形，使每層向內退縮而彷彿漂浮。三層板材由細木條撐開，圍出起伏的空間，小人形在碎片之間漂移。這個模型說明，情感的記憶能被轉譯為精確而可重複的製作方法。

pins.title: Stone Game
pins.description:
Roadside pebbles collected on the way to school are stacked into pillars and then set climbing across triangular timber frames that link the pillars into an arch.

Model | Material and growth study | Stones, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 石頭遊戲
zh-Hant.description:
上學路上收集的路邊石子先被堆成柱子，再沿著三角形木框向上攀爬，木框把柱子連成一道拱。

模型｜材料與生長研究｜石頭、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The arch of frames and stones.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project grew from a daily habit of collecting small roadside stones on the commute between home and school. Each stone seemed as distinct as a person, so the question became how many different individuals could be gathered into one structure.
captions: A handful of the roadside stones collected on the way to school.
Naming each stone by its shape and colour.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源自每天往返家與學校途中收集路邊小石子的習慣。每顆石頭都像人一樣獨特，於是問題成為：如何把許多不同的個體聚集成一個結構。
captions: 上學途中收集的一把路邊小石頭。
依形狀與顏色為每顆石頭命名。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The stones were named by their shapes and colours, and a concept drawing imagined them gathering into a tower. Stacking tests then formed them into three pillars with round, triangular and square sections.
captions: A concept drawing of gathering stones.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生依形狀與顏色為石頭命名，並以概念圖想像它們聚集成一座塔。接著的堆疊測試把石頭堆成圓形、三角形與方形斷面的三根柱子。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: To link the pillars without stones falling, plank frames were built with small new triangles inside triangular structures, holding the stones and together forming an arch. Many more frames were then added as a base for growth, with stones placed so that they seem to climb along the bars one by one.
captions: Building the timber frames by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 為了連接柱子又不讓石頭掉落，學生以木板搭出框架，在三角形結構中再做出小三角形，用來承托石頭並共同形成一道拱。之後學生加入更多框架作為生長的基礎，並安置石頭，讓它們彷彿沿著木條一根根向上攀爬。
captions: 承托於三角形中的石頭。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model is a cluster of timber triangles over which stones spread and pile up freely toward the top. It depicts a mimic growth of stone, as if inanimate pieces had a conscious desire to climb.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型是一團木製三角形，石頭在其上蔓延，並朝頂端自由堆積。它描繪石頭的擬態生長，彷彿無生命的碎塊有了攀爬的意志。

sections.heading: Climbing Pebbles - A Game of Gravity and Growth
sections.body: A pebble picked up from the roadside is an ordinary thing, yet a pocketful gathered day after day becomes a collection of individuals, no two alike in shape or colour. This project treated those pebbles as characters in a game against gravity. The student first named the stones and imagined them assembling into a tower, then stacked them into three pillars of round, triangular and square section. The real difficulty arose in joining the pillars, since loose stones resist any bridge. The guidance directed attention to structure, and an experiment with plank frames answered the problem, as small triangles nested inside larger ones created pockets that could cradle stones and together form an arch. From there the frames multiplied into a lattice, and stones were placed to appear as though they were creeping upward bar by bar before heaping freely at the summit. Inert matter thus seems to acquire intention. The project demonstrates how a simple collection can evolve into a structural inquiry about balance, difference and growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 攀爬的石子-重力與生長的遊戲
zh-Hant.body: 從路邊拾起的一顆石子再平凡不過，日復一日收集起來，卻成為一群形狀與顏色各異的個體。這個專題把石子當作一場對抗重力之遊戲中的角色。學生先為石頭命名，想像它們聚成一座塔，再堆成圓形、三角形與方形斷面的三根柱子。真正的難題在於連接柱子，因為鬆散的石頭難以成橋。指導把注意力引向結構，木板框架的實驗給出答案：小三角形嵌入大三角形，形成承托石頭的凹處，並共同構成一道拱。框架隨後繁衍成格架，石頭彷彿沿著木條逐根上爬，最後在頂端自由堆積。無生命的物質似乎有了意圖。這個專題說明，簡單的收集能演變為關於平衡、差異與生長的結構探究。

pins.title: Urban Form
pins.description:
A dense lattice of wooden strips grows upward into planes and closed white boxes, recombining the elements of a city into a new vertical form.

Model | Urban form study | PVC panels, wooden strips, transparent pieces | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市形態
zh-Hant.description:
密集的木條格架向上生長為平面與封閉的白色盒體，把城市的元素重組為新的垂直形態。

模型｜城市形態研究｜PVC板、木條、透明片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: White boxes on a timber lattice.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how the original form of a city could be broken down and recombined into a new architectural form. It treated the relationship between architecture and people as something to be rethought through simple geometry.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，城市原有的形態如何被拆解，並重組為新的建築形態。它把建築與人之間的關係，視為可透過簡單幾何重新思考的對象。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Abstract colour compositions and a fractal approach to architecture were studied, in which built form echoes the forms found in natural matter. From these, a method of points, lines and planes was chosen to divide existing forms and recompose them.
captions: References: the painter's tricolour grid, the architect's portrait and building, and a city skyline.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究抽象的色彩構成，以及一種讓建築形式呼應自然物質中形態的碎形建築取向。由此，學生選定以點、線、面的方法來分割既有形態並重新組合。
captions: 參考：畫家的三原色格狀畫作、建築師肖像與其建築，以及城市天際線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: At the bottom, wooden strips were placed freely to make a dense composition of lines, and at connection points where strips could grow higher, PVC boards were added to combine line and plane. At the top, closed blocks of PVC were assembled in a mosaic-like pattern, while coloured transparent pieces and plants added detail.
captions: Building the model by hand: cutting panels and gluing timber strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在底部，木條被自由擺放，形成密集的線構成；在木條可以向上生長的連接點，學生加入PVC板，讓線與面結合。在頂部，封閉的PVC盒體以類似馬賽克的方式組合，有色透明片與植物則增添細節。
captions: 以手製作模型：裁切板材與黏合木條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model rises from a thicket of timber into a cluster of white boxes, moving between open and enclosed space. Small red figures occupy platforms at every level, showing the structure as a vertical city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型從一片木條叢林升起，直到一群白色盒體，在開放與封閉的空間之間轉換。小小的紅色人形佔據每一層的平台，讓這個結構呈現為一座垂直的城市。

sections.heading: A City Rewoven - Lines Growing into Rooms
sections.body: A city can be read not as a collection of buildings but as a grammar of points, lines and planes, waiting to be rearranged. This project adopted that reading and set out to compose a new urban form from first elements. Research into abstract colour compositions and fractal ideas of architecture suggested that built form might echo the branching orders of nature. The guidance encouraged a clear sequence of making, so that each element would have its own role. Thin wooden strips were laid freely at the base, forming a dense thicket of lines through which space could filter. Wherever strips reached higher, white boards were inserted, joining line to plane and creating a play between virtual and solid volume. Toward the top the boards closed into compact boxes gathered like tesserae, while tinted transparent sheets and dried plants softened the composition. Small red figures inhabit platforms at every height. The model demonstrates how a disciplined vocabulary can grow into a rich, habitable vertical landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 重新編織的城市-由線長成房間
zh-Hant.body: 城市可以不被讀作建築的集合，而被讀作一套等待重新排列的點、線、面文法。這個專題採用這樣的讀法，試圖從最基本的元素組構新的城市形態。對抽象色彩構成與碎形建築思想的研究提示，建成形式或許能呼應自然中分枝的秩序。指導鼓勵清晰的製作順序，讓每種元素各司其職。細木條在底部自由鋪排，形成密集的線之叢林，讓空間從中滲透。凡木條向上延伸處便插入白板，使線與面相接，造出虛實之間的對話。往上，板材閉合為如鑲嵌碎片般聚集的盒體，有色透明片與乾燥植物柔化了構圖。紅色小人形棲居於每個高度。這個模型說明，嚴謹的語彙能長成豐富而可居的垂直地景。

pins.title: Formal and Informal Space
pins.description:
Research on formality in culture is turned into two white models, one gathered around a central pyramid and one scattered freely across open ground.

Models | Spatial formality study | PVC panels | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 正式與非正式空間
zh-Hant.description:
關於文化中正式性的研究被轉化為兩個白色模型，一個圍繞中央的金字塔聚集，另一個則在開放地面上自由散落。

模型｜空間正式性研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The formal model with its central pyramid.
帶有中央金字塔的正式模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Earlier research comparing formality in business negotiations led the student to notice that space also carries degrees of formality. The project asked which spatial traits make architecture feel formal or informal, a topic rarely discussed.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 先前比較商業談判中正式性的研究，讓學生注意到空間同樣具有不同程度的正式性。這個專題探問，哪些空間特質讓建築顯得正式或非正式，而這是一個鮮少被討論的議題。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Information about formal and informal buildings was gathered and sorted by factors known to shape formality in culture, such as power distance and attitudes to uncertainty. Plans of a symmetrical formal building and an irregular complex were compared as the basis for a collage.
captions: Research sheet comparing formal and informal architecture through precedent buildings.
Plan of a symmetrical formal building.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生蒐集正式與非正式建築的資料，並依權力距離與對不確定性的態度等已知影響文化正式性的因素加以分類。一座對稱的正式建築與一個不規則建築群的平面被拿來比較，作為拼貼的基礎。
captions: 以先例建築比較正式與非正式建築的研究表。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The data showed that formal space has a centre of gravity stressing hierarchy and sets out a fixed journey for visitors, while informal space leaves paths open. Two PVC models were made, one gathering volumes around a remarkable central object and one scattering blocks freely across the ground.
captions: A low view of the blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 資料顯示，正式空間有一個強調階序的重心，並為來訪者設定固定的路徑，非正式空間則讓路徑保持開放。學生製作了兩個PVC模型，一個讓量體圍繞醒目的中央物件聚集，另一個則讓塊體在地面上自由散落。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the formal model a pyramid rises at the centre, with the surrounding volumes turned toward it. Set beside the loosely placed boxes of the informal model, the pair makes the contrast between guided and free movement visible.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在正式模型中，一座金字塔在中央升起，周圍的量體都朝向它。與非正式模型中鬆散擺放的盒體並置，這對模型讓受引導的移動與自由移動之間的對比變得可見。

sections.heading: Measuring Formality - A Pyramid and Its Scattered Twin
sections.body: Formality is usually discussed as a matter of manners and speech, yet buildings also ask people to behave in certain ways, to slow down, to follow a route, to recognise a centre of authority. This project began from that overlooked parallel. The student carried earlier research on formality in negotiation into architecture, collecting examples and sorting them by cultural factors such as distance from power and tolerance of uncertainty. The guidance urged that these findings become spatial rules rather than remain as notes. Formal space emerged as one that gathers around a dominant centre and prescribes a sequence for the visitor, while informal space withholds such direction and lets paths form freely. Two white models translate the rules directly. In one a pyramid presides over volumes that turn toward it, and in the other boxes drift across an open ground without hierarchy. Seen together, the pair becomes an instrument for reading space. The work shows how social research can be converted into architectural form.

zh-Hant.heading: 衡量正式-金字塔與散落的孿生
zh-Hant.body: 正式性通常被當作禮儀與言談的問題，然而建築同樣要求人以特定方式行事：放慢腳步、依循路線、辨認權威的中心。這個專題正是從這個被忽略的相似之處出發。學生把先前關於談判正式性的研究帶入建築，蒐集案例，並依權力距離與對不確定性的容忍等文化因素分類。指導強調讓這些發現成為空間規則，而不只停留於筆記。正式空間於是被界定為圍繞主導中心聚集、並為來訪者規定順序的空間，非正式空間則不給指引，任路徑自由生成。兩個白色模型直接轉譯這些規則：一個由金字塔統領朝向它的量體，另一個讓盒體在開放地面上無階序地散落。兩者並置，便成為閱讀空間的工具。這件作品說明，社會研究能被轉化為建築形式。

pins.title: Gravity Torsion
pins.description:
Dozens of white PVC stairs are twisted around one another and pinned with wooden sticks, so that each small figure seems to stand in its own direction of gravity.

Model | Space and gravity study | Wooden sticks, PVC board, mirror | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重力扭轉
zh-Hant.description:
數十段白色PVC樓梯彼此扭轉纏繞，並以木棒固定，讓每個小人形彷彿各自站在不同方向的重力之中。

模型｜空間與重力研究｜木棒、PVC板、鏡面｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project began from a story of people trapped on an endless staircase, unable to escape. It asked whether being stuck in stairs could be explained by gravity pulling in tangled directions, a condition that also suggests knotted feelings of regret.
captions: The collage made by accident that suggested many different gravities.
The title graphic of the film that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題始於一個人們被困在無盡樓梯上、無法逃脫的故事。它探問，被困在樓梯中的處境，能否被解釋為向糾結方向拉扯的重力，而這種狀態也暗示著糾纏的懊悔之情。
captions: 意外拼出的拼貼，暗示了多種不同的重力方向。
啟發本案的電影標題圖像。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: An accidental collage that seemed to hold many different gravities became the starting point. Many types of stair were then made as separate elements to test how each could turn and meet the others.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張偶然做成、彷彿夾雜多種重力的拼貼成為起點。學生接著把許多種類的樓梯做成獨立元素，測試每一段如何轉向並與其他樓梯相接。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each stair was cut with steps starting from one centimetre by six millimetres and growing larger downward. The pieces were connected in different ways, with wooden sticks, straight flights and some irregular planes.
captions: Testing the stair elements by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每段樓梯的踏階從一公分乘六公釐開始切割，並向下逐漸加大。各構件以不同方式相連，包括木棒、直跑樓梯以及一些不規則的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model stretches, curls and contracts into interlacing spaces with an air of mystery. Each figure stands in a distinct gravity, unable to reach any of the others.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型伸展、捲曲並收縮成交錯的空間，充滿神祕的氛圍。每個人形各自站在不同的重力中，無法觸及其他任何一人。

sections.heading: Tangled Gravities - Stairs That Lead Nowhere
sections.body: A staircase normally promises arrival, each step a small certainty that the next level is near. This project overturned that promise and asked what space would feel like if every flight obeyed a different pull. The starting point was a story of people trapped on endless stairs and an accidental collage in which directions of weight seemed to collide. The student read that collision as an emotional state, a knot of regret in which no one can help anyone else. The guidance encouraged building a vocabulary before a composition, so dozens of stair pieces were cut with steps that grow as they descend and tested for the ways they might join. Sticks, straight flights and irregular planes then bound the pieces into a single twisting mass resting on a mirror. Shadows multiply the confusion, and tiny figures stand at odd angles, each isolated in a private gravity. The model shows how a familiar architectural element can be estranged to express a complex inner condition.

zh-Hant.heading: 糾纏的重力-無處可去的樓梯
zh-Hant.body: 樓梯通常承諾抵達，每一階都是一份「下一層就在不遠處」的小小確定。這個專題推翻了這個承諾，探問若每段樓梯都服從不同的拉力，空間會是什麼感受。起點是一個人們被困在無盡樓梯上的故事，以及一張重量方向彷彿相互碰撞的偶然拼貼。學生把這種碰撞解讀為一種情緒狀態，一團誰也幫不了誰的懊悔之結。指導鼓勵先建立語彙再進行構圖，於是數十段樓梯被切出向下逐漸加大的踏階，並測試各種接合方式。木棒、直跑梯與不規則平面再把構件綁成一個置於鏡面上的扭轉量體。陰影加倍了迷亂，小人形以怪異角度站立，各自孤立於私有的重力中。這個模型說明，熟悉的建築元素能被陌生化，以表達複雜的內在狀態。

pins.title: Space and Sound
pins.description:
Arcs traced from guitar chord patterns are overlapped and given height, forming eight PVC forms whose exposed black parts read as a melody.

Model | Sound and form study | PVC board, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間與聲音
zh-Hant.description:
從吉他和弦圖樣描出的圓弧相互重疊並被賦予高度，形成八個PVC形體，其外露的黑色部分可被讀作一段旋律。

模型｜聲音與形式研究｜PVC板、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Sound forms on a light table.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explored the relationship between sound and space, starting from the fact that sound is vibration made of pitch and loudness. It asked how these two qualities could be given measurable form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探索聲音與空間的關係，起點是聲音是由音高與響度構成的振動。它探問，這兩種特質如何能被賦予可量測的形式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Guitar chord patterns were used to draw staggered circles, each with the shortest side at its point as radius. The arcs were traced on tracing paper where they overlapped once, twice and three times.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以吉他和弦的圖樣畫出交錯的圓，每個圓以該點最短的邊為半徑。接著在描圖紙上描出重疊一次、兩次與三次的圓弧。
captions: 由和弦圖樣畫出的圓弧。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Overlapping parts were given height to represent pitch, while their areas stood for loudness. Overlaps belonging to the same arc were then combined, since a harmonious sound was felt to be a process of superposition.
captions: Placing the sound forms on the light table by hand.
Forms placed on the arc drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 重疊的部分被賦予高度以代表音高，其面積則代表響度。屬於同一圓弧的重疊部分再被組合起來，因為和諧的聲音被感受為一種疊加的過程。
captions: 以手將聲音形體擺放在燈箱上。
放置於圓弧圖上的形體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Eight stacked forms stand in a row, each a column of curved PVC layers. The exposed black parts of each combination trace the melody.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 八個堆疊的形體排成一列，每個都是由彎曲PVC層構成的柱體。每個組合外露的黑色部分描繪出旋律。

sections.heading: Chords in Layers - Building the Shape of Harmony
sections.body: Music is usually heard rather than held, yet every chord has a structure as exact as a plan. This project tried to build that structure in space. The student began from the physics of sound, vibration measured as pitch and loudness, and searched for a drawing method that could carry both. Guitar chord charts provided a grid of points, and around each point a circle was drawn whose radius came from its nearest neighbour. Tracing where these circles overlapped once, twice or three times produced a field of lens-shaped fragments. The guidance urged consistent rules, so height was assigned to represent pitch and area to represent volume. Fragments sharing the same arc were then gathered and stacked, because harmony was understood as a leaping superposition of tones. Eight small columns resulted, each a tower of curving white layers. Where black edges show through, a melody can be read like notation. The work demonstrates how a careful translation can give tangible architecture to an invisible art.

zh-Hant.heading: 層疊的和弦-構築和聲的形狀
zh-Hant.body: 音樂通常被聽見而非被握住，然而每個和弦都有如平面圖般精確的結構。這個專題試圖在空間中構築這種結構。學生從聲音的物理出發，即以音高與響度衡量的振動，並尋找能同時承載兩者的繪圖方法。弦樂器的和弦圖提供一套點的網格，學生以每個點最近的鄰點距離為半徑畫圓。描出這些圓重疊一次、兩次或三次之處，便得到一片透鏡狀的碎片。指導強調一致的規則，於是高度代表音高，面積代表音量。共享同一圓弧的碎片被聚集並堆疊，因為和聲被理解為音的跳躍疊加。最終得到八個小柱體，每個都是彎曲白色層片之塔。黑色邊緣外露之處，可像樂譜般讀出旋律。這件作品說明，細心的轉譯能為無形的藝術賦予可觸的建築。

pins.title: Chambers of a Restless Mind
pins.description:
Four small spaces of brick, mirror, plaster bubbles and curving wooden slats each give form to a different emotional moment in a story.

Models | Narrative space study | Bricks, wire, wire mesh, cardboard, PVC board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 不安心靈的房間
zh-Hant.description:
磚、鏡面、石膏泡泡與彎曲木條構成的四個小空間，各自為一個故事中不同的情緒時刻賦予形體。

模型｜敘事空間研究｜磚、鐵絲、鐵絲網、卡紙、PVC板、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project recreated scenes from a novel, aiming for every space to mirror the emotions of its main character. The challenge was to express states such as caution, dizziness, guilt and rage through material rather than illustration.
captions: The cover of the novel that inspired the three spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題重現一部小說中的場景，目標是讓每個空間都映照主角的情緒。挑戰在於透過材料而非插圖，表達謹慎、暈眩、愧疚與憤怒等狀態。
captions: 啟發這三個空間的小說封面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A vintage room was imitated in miniature bricks, with only a bed described in the text and two colours of string marking an exchange of secrets. Below it, a well was imagined as a passage to other spaces, built as reflective geometry that creates a gloomy sense.
captions: An annotated concept sketch of the scenes and emotions.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生以迷你磚仿造一間老式房間，文本中只描述了一張床，兩種顏色的線則標示一段秘密的交換。在它之下，一口井被想像為通往其他空間的通道，並以反射的幾何構成營造陰鬱之感。
captions: 標註場景與情緒的概念草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A third space suspends a white bubble pulled and contracted by black ropes, standing for a memory of regret and constant struggle. The last space is a circle of surging wooden slats among wire trees, matching inner ups and downs during a fight in a forest.
captions: Making the mirror geometry and spaces by hand.
The white bubble held by ropes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第三個空間懸掛一個被黑繩拉扯與收縮的白色泡泡，代表一段懊悔的記憶與不斷的掙扎。最後一個空間是鐵絲樹林中一圈洶湧的木條，對應森林中一場打鬥時內心的起伏。
captions: 以手製作鏡面幾何與空間。
被繩索牽制的白色泡泡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Small red figures appear in all four spaces as bystanders who also drive the world little by little. Together the models form a sequence from quiet enclosure to violent motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 小小的紅色人形出現在全部四個空間中，既是旁觀者，也一點一點推動著世界。四個模型共同構成一段從安靜封閉到劇烈運動的序列。

sections.heading: Rooms of Feeling - From Well to Forest
sections.body: Fiction often unfolds as a passage through rooms, each holding a different weight of feeling, and this project set out to build such a passage. Working from scenes of a novel, the student chose four moments and asked how material alone could carry the mood of each. A small brick chamber recalls an old hotel room, almost empty, where two colours of string trace whispered warnings across a bed. Beneath it lies a well rendered in faceted mirror, a dizzying space where reflections fold the mind toward elsewhere. The guidance encouraged contrast between the pieces, so the third space becomes soft and suspended, a white swelling restrained by black ropes that reads as guilt. The final space bursts into motion as wooden slats surge in a ring through a grove of wire trees. Tiny red figures recur in every chamber as witnesses and quiet agents of change. The sequence demonstrates how narrative emotion can be translated into a coherent family of spatial experiments.

zh-Hant.heading: 情感的房間-從井到森林
zh-Hant.body: 小說往往如同穿越一個個房間般展開，每個房間承載不同重量的情感，而這個專題便試圖構築這樣的一段穿越。學生從一部小說的場景出發，選出四個時刻，探問僅憑材料能否承載各自的情緒。一間小小的磚室令人想起一間幾近空無的老旅館房間，兩色細線在床上描出低語般的警告。其下是一口以多面鏡構成的井，一個令人暈眩的空間，反射把思緒折向遠方。指導鼓勵各件作品之間的對比，於是第三個空間變得柔軟而懸浮，一團被黑繩牽制的白色膨脹，可讀作愧疚。最後的空間爆發為運動，木條在鐵絲樹叢中洶湧成環。紅色小人形在每個房間重複出現，既是見證者，也是安靜的改變者。這組序列說明，敘事情感能被轉譯為一個連貫的空間實驗家族。

pins.title: Against Gravity
pins.description:
Slender elastic wires are knotted into a twisted lattice sculpture whose powerful form seems to resist gravity.

Sculpture and digital image | Structure study | Elastic wire, digital editing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 對抗重力
zh-Hant.description:
纖細的彈性鐵絲被結成一座扭轉的格網雕塑，其有力的形體彷彿在抵抗重力。

雕塑與數位影像｜結構研究｜彈性鐵絲、數位編修｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The theme was against gravity, asking how a structure might look as if it pushes away from the ground. The intriguing contrast was to make a powerful shape out of very slender wires.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題的主題是對抗重力，探問一個結構如何看起來像是從地面推離。其中引人入勝的對比，在於以極細的鐵絲做出有力的形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Elastic wires were tested for how far they could bend and spring back when joined at small nodes. Triangles proved the most stable unit for building up a light network.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生測試彈性鐵絲在小節點相接時能彎曲並回彈的程度。三角形被證明是構築輕盈網絡最穩定的單元。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangles were linked into clusters that twist as they grow, so that tension in each wire holds the whole shape in place. The sculpture was then photographed and edited digitally to isolate its outline.
captions: Tying the elastic wires together by hand.
Building the wire lattice by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角形被連結成邊生長邊扭轉的群組，讓每根鐵絲中的張力把整體形狀固定。雕塑隨後被拍攝並以數位方式編修，以突顯其輪廓。
captions: 以手將彈性線綁接在一起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Seen from four sides, the lattice changes from a dense knot to an open cloud of lines. The views show how a delicate material can carry a strong sense of upward force.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從四個方向觀看，格網從密集的結轉變為開放的線之雲。這些視角顯示纖細的材料如何能承載強烈的向上力量。

sections.heading: Lines Against Weight - A Lattice That Lifts
sections.body: Gravity is usually felt as weight, a steady pull that every structure must answer, but a structure can also be made to look as though it argues back. This project pursued that argument with the lightest of means. The student chose elastic wire precisely because it seems too slender for strength, and the tension between delicacy and force became the subject of the work. Early tests examined how wire bends and recovers when tied at tiny joints, and the triangle emerged as the dependable cell. The guidance encouraged growth by rule rather than by sketch, so triangles were added one to another until the cluster began to twist of its own accord. Stored tension in each strand keeps the form taut, as if it were straining upward. Photographed from four directions and edited to stand out against a pale ground, the lattice shifts between knot and cloud. The work demonstrates how structural logic can turn fragile lines into an expression of resistance.

zh-Hant.heading: 對抗重量的線-向上抬升的格網
zh-Hant.body: 重力通常被感受為重量，一股每個結構都必須回應的穩定拉力，但結構也能被做得彷彿在反駁它。這個專題以最輕盈的手段追求這場反駁。學生選擇彈性鐵絲，正因為它看似過於纖細而無法承力，纖細與力量之間的張力便成為作品的主題。早期測試檢視鐵絲在微小節點相接時如何彎曲與回復，三角形隨之成為可靠的單元。指導鼓勵依規則而非依草圖生長，於是三角形一個接一個加入，直到群組開始自行扭轉。每股鐵絲中蓄積的張力讓形體保持緊繃，彷彿正奮力向上。從四個方向拍攝並經編修後，格網在淺色背景上於結與雲之間變換。這件作品說明，結構邏輯能把脆弱的線轉化為抵抗的表達。

pins.title: Stacked Divide: A Corrugated High-Rise
pins.description:
A tall corrugated-paper tower sets torn, patched shacks at its base beneath polished rooms and floating rings, giving form to the gap between rich and poor.

Model | High-rise residential study | Corrugated paper, wooden strips, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 堆疊的分野：瓦楞紙高樓
zh-Hant.description:
一座高聳的瓦楞紙塔，底部是撕裂拼補的棚屋，上方是精整的房間與漂浮的圓環，為貧富之間的差距賦予形體。

模型｜高層住宅研究｜瓦楞紙、木條、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project imagined a future city where the wealthy live in bustling buildings in the sky while the poor live in dilapidated houses below. It asked how this gap between rich and poor would shape the living environment of a single tower.
captions: The title of the sci-fi film that inspired the project.
Film stills of the rich city in the sky and the poor city below.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題想像一座未來城市，富人住在天空中繁華的建築裡，窮人則住在下方破敗的房屋中。它探問，這種貧富差距會如何塑造一座單一高樓的居住環境。
captions: 啟發本案的科幻電影標題。
電影劇照：天空中的富人城市與下方的貧民城市。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A detailed section drawing packed every floor with rooms, furniture and stairs to test how life would stack vertically. Small corrugated rooms were then cut and glued together as the basic units of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張詳細的剖面圖在每層塞滿房間、家具與樓梯，測試生活如何垂直堆疊。學生接著切割並黏合小小的瓦楞紙房間，作為高樓的基本單元。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: At the bottom, corrugated surfaces were torn apart so the rooms look like worn tin shacks. Window frames and shelves of wooden strips connect the lower and upper parts, and rings were added around the top.
captions: Building the corrugated paper rooms by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在底部，瓦楞紙表面被撕開，讓房間看起來像破舊的鐵皮屋。木條做成的窗框與架子連接上下兩部分，頂部周圍再加上圓環。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Barbed wire and wrapped columns finish the details of pipes and passages that thread through the floors. Tiny red figures climb a tower whose surfaces grow more refined the higher they rise.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲與纏繞的柱子完成了穿梭各層的管道與通道細節。紅色小人形攀爬著一座越往上表面越精緻的高樓。

sections.heading: Vertical Inequality - A Tower Read from Bottom to Top
sections.body: Cities often sort their inhabitants by height, and this project made that sorting visible in a single column of rooms. The student imagined a future where comfort floats above and scarcity gathers at ground level, and asked what such a divide would feel like to inhabit. A crowded section drawing came first, filling every floor with beds, tables and stairs so that daily life could be read layer by layer. Corrugated paper then became the sole building material, valued for its ability to look either crisp or ruined. The guidance encouraged letting one material carry the whole argument, so the lower rooms were torn and patched into tin-like shacks while the upper rooms received clean frames and generous windows. Wooden scaffolds, pipes of wrapped wire and floating rings bind the two worlds together without reconciling them. Tiny red figures climb through the structure as reminders of the people who live inside such contrasts. The tower demonstrates how a social question can be translated into a legible vertical gradient of craft.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直的不平等-由下而上閱讀的高樓
zh-Hant.body: 城市常以高度為居民分層，這個專題讓這種分層在一柱房間中變得可見。學生想像一個舒適漂浮於上、匱乏聚集於地面的未來，並探問居住在這種分野之中會是什麼感受。首先是一張擁擠的剖面圖，在每層填滿床、桌與樓梯，讓日常生活能被逐層閱讀。瓦楞紙隨後成為唯一的建材，因為它既能顯得挺括，也能顯得殘破。指導鼓勵讓一種材料承載整個論述，於是下層房間被撕裂拼補成鐵皮般的棚屋，上層房間則得到俐落的框架與寬大的窗。木構支架、纏繞鐵絲的管道與漂浮的圓環把兩個世界綁在一起，卻未使其和解。紅色小人形在結構中攀爬，提醒觀者這種對比之中住著真實的人。這座塔說明，一個社會問題能被轉譯為清晰可讀的垂直工藝漸層。

pins.title: Distance and Scale
pins.description:
Floors of ever finer grids are stacked and joined by a spiral stair, testing how a pattern changes as the eye moves closer or further away.

Model | Transition space study | Wooden strips, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 距離與尺度
zh-Hant.description:
網格越來越細密的樓板層層堆疊，並以螺旋梯相連，測試圖樣如何隨視線遠近而改變。

模型｜過渡空間研究｜木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Walking along a path beside home, every brick could be seen clearly, yet from a window above only the road as a whole was visible. The project asked how distance and scale affect what people see in a space.
captions: An image of the animated city that inspired the project.
A section diagram of the animated city's structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 沿著住家旁的小路行走時，每塊磚都清晰可見，但從上方的窗戶往下看，只能看到整條路。這個專題探問，距離與尺度如何影響人們在空間中所見。
captions: 啟發本案的動畫城市圖像。
動畫城市結構的剖面圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sequence of square grids was drawn, each layer dividing the cells of the one before into smaller openings. The finer grids were then cut as floor plates to see how the pattern dissolves into texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生畫出一系列方形網格，每一層都把前一層的格子再分成更小的開口。較細的網格隨後被切成樓板，觀察圖樣如何消融為肌理。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: On each grid floor, curved PVC walls, benches and shelves form small rooms where figures and animals pause. The walls ripple and fold so that the floors read as landscapes rather than flat plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在每層網格樓板上，彎曲的PVC牆、長椅與架子圍出小房間，人形與動物在其中停留。牆面起伏折疊，讓樓板讀起來像地景而非平面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A spiral stair wraps around the stacked floors and links them into one continuous transition space. Light falling through the grids casts patterns whose scale shifts from level to level.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一道螺旋梯環繞堆疊的樓板，將它們連成一個連續的過渡空間。穿過網格的光投下圖樣，其尺度在各層之間變化。

sections.heading: Near and Far - A Stair Through Changing Grains
sections.body: A paved path looks different depending on where it is seen from, and this project began with that simple observation. Close underfoot, every brick is distinct, but from a window above the same surface becomes a single ribbon of road. The student turned this shift of perception into a method by drawing grids that subdivide again and again, each layer finer than the last. Cut as floor plates and stacked, the grids allow a visitor to experience pattern at many distances within a few steps. The guidance encouraged pairing a rigorous system with a free gesture, so curved walls, benches and shelves were allowed to ripple across the strict lattices like soft terrain. A spiral stair then ties the levels together, turning vertical movement into a gradual zoom from coarse to fine. Light passing through the openings casts shadows that change their grain on every floor. The model shows how a personal moment of noticing can grow into a disciplined study of scale and transition.

zh-Hant.heading: 近與遠-穿越變化紋理的樓梯
zh-Hant.body: 一條鋪面小路因觀看位置不同而顯得不同，這個專題便從這個簡單的觀察開始。在腳下近處，每塊磚都清晰分明，但從上方窗口望去，同一片表面成了一條完整的路帶。學生把這種知覺的轉變化為方法，畫出一再細分的網格，每一層都比前一層更細密。這些網格被切成樓板並堆疊，讓參觀者在幾步之內就能在多種距離下體驗圖樣。指導鼓勵把嚴謹的系統與自由的手勢配對，於是彎曲的牆、長椅與架子得以像柔軟地形般在嚴格的格網上起伏。螺旋梯再把各層綁在一起，讓垂直移動成為由粗到細的漸進拉近。穿過開口的光投下陰影，在每層改變紋理。這個模型說明，個人的一次留意能成長為對尺度與過渡的嚴謹研究。

pins.title: Chain Castle
pins.description:
Dark bricks are laid in interlocking links to form a square chain, while wooden frames caught in its gaps stand for the rules that bind daily life.

Model | Material and meaning study | Brick, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鎖鏈城堡
zh-Hant.description:
深色磚塊以互扣的環節砌成一條方形鎖鏈，卡在縫隙中的木框則代表束縛日常生活的規則。

模型｜材料與意義研究｜磚、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The brick chain with wooden frames.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Chains symbolise confinement, and people often keep doing things the same way, just as houses have long been built with the same way of laying bricks. The project asked whether a new way of bricklaying could express the idea of breaking convention.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 鎖鏈象徵禁錮，人們常常以同樣的方式做事，正如房屋長久以來都以同樣的砌磚方式建造。這個專題探問，一種新的砌磚方式能否表達打破常規的想法。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Small bricks were combined into many interlocking units, each turning and crossing so that pieces hook into one another. These studies looked for links that could hold together like the rings of a chain.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把小磚塊組合成許多互扣的單元，每個單元轉向交錯，讓構件彼此勾連。這些研究尋找能像鎖鏈環節般相扣的連結。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chosen links were laid end to end to form a closed square chain of bricks. Wooden frames of different sizes were then inserted at the gaps to represent the things that restrict people in life.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選定的環節首尾相接，砌成一條封閉的方形磚鏈。不同大小的木框隨後被插入縫隙，代表生活中限制人們的事物。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: From the side, the frames rise above the heavy brick like a skyline of cages. From above, the square chain reads as a castle wall, expressing the hope that people will find courage to break the rules.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從側面看，木框在厚重的磚上升起，如一道籠子的天際線。從上方看，方形鎖鏈讀起來像一道城牆，表達人們終將鼓起勇氣打破規則的希望。

sections.heading: Bound Links - Breaking the Habit of Brick
sections.body: Brick has been laid in the same patient rhythm for centuries, and that very constancy became the subject of this project. The student read the familiar bond of a wall as a quiet image of habit, and the chain as the sharper image of confinement that habit can become. Rather than illustrate either idea, the work asked the material itself to change its manners. Dozens of small interlocking units were tested until pieces could hook through one another like links, a way of building that ordinary walls never use. The guidance encouraged keeping meaning inside the method, so the links were joined into a closed square that feels at once fortress and fetter. Light wooden frames were then wedged into its gaps, cages of many sizes standing for the rules that hold daily life in place. Seen from the side they form a restless skyline, and from above a defended enclosure. The model shows how a change in craft can carry a hopeful argument about courage and convention.

zh-Hant.heading: 受縛的環節-打破砌磚的習慣
zh-Hant.body: 磚塊數百年來都以同樣耐心的節奏砌築，這份恆常本身便成為這個專題的主題。學生把牆體熟悉的砌法解讀為習慣的安靜意象，而鎖鏈則是習慣可能化成的、更尖銳的禁錮意象。作品並不直接圖解這兩個概念，而是要求材料本身改變它的舉止。數十個小小的互扣單元經過測試，直到構件能像環節般彼此勾穿，這是一般牆體從不使用的建造方式。指導鼓勵把意義保留在方法之中，於是環節被接成一個封閉方形，既像堡壘又像枷鎖。輕盈的木框再被楔入其縫隙，大小不一的籠子代表把日常生活固定於原地的規則。從側面看，它們構成一道不安的天際線；從上方看，則是一圈設防的圍合。這個模型說明，工藝的改變能承載一個關於勇氣與常規的、充滿希望的論述。

pins.title: Rising from Demolition
pins.description:
Toy bricks, black sticks and red wire tracks are tangled into a restless structure that recreates a city where old neighbourhoods are torn down and new buildings rise.

Model | Urban change study | Toy bricks, wooden strips, iron wire, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從拆除中升起
zh-Hant.description:
玩具積木、黑色木條與紅色鐵絲軌道糾纏成一座躁動的結構，重現一座舊街區被拆除、新建築隨之升起的城市。

模型｜城市變遷研究｜玩具積木、木條、鐵絲、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The demolition of an old urban village and the rapid rise of new buildings in its place left a strong impression. The project asked how this cycle of destruction and construction could be recreated as an image of the city held in the mind.
captions: A collage of the urban village demolition and new construction.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座舊城中村被拆除、新建築隨即在原地迅速升起的景象，留下了深刻的印象。這個專題探問，這種破壞與建造的循環能否被重現為心中的城市意象。
captions: 城中村拆除與新建工地的拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A long habit of building robots from toy bricks provided a ready vocabulary of beams, gears and joints. These parts were combined with wooden strips, wire and cardboard to suggest cranes, scaffolds and broken frames.
captions: Earlier robots built from toy bricks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 長期以玩具積木組裝機器人的習慣，提供了一套現成的樑、齒輪與接頭語彙。這些構件與木條、鐵絲及卡紙結合，暗示起重機、鷹架與破碎的框架。
captions: 先前以玩具積木製作的機器人。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Black sticks were stacked into a dense frame like scaffolding around a construction site. Red wire tracks then loop through and around the frame, while gears and arms suggest machines still at work.
captions: Assembling the bricks and wires by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 黑色木條堆疊成密集的框架，像工地周圍的鷹架。紅色鐵絲軌道再穿繞框架，齒輪與機械臂則暗示仍在運作的機器。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Lit from the side, the model throws a large shadow that reads like a skyline of half-built towers. Tiny red figures stand among the beams, small against the speed of change around them.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從側面打光時，模型投下巨大的影子，讀起來像一片半完工高樓的天際線。紅色小人形站在樑柱之間，在周遭變遷的速度面前顯得渺小。

sections.heading: Cranes and Ruins - The City as a Machine in Motion
sections.body: A city under redevelopment rarely looks finished, since demolition and construction overlap in the same view. This project tried to capture that unsettled condition rather than any single building. The student drew on years of assembling robots from toy bricks, a play that had quietly trained a sense of joints, gears and moving arms. Those parts were mixed with black sticks, wire and cardboard so that familiar pieces would lose their toy-like innocence and begin to resemble cranes and scaffolds. The guidance encouraged density and risk, so the frame was allowed to grow tangled, with red wire tracks swooping through it like routes of machines that never stop. Gears suggest work in progress, while broken edges hint at what has already been cleared away. Under a single lamp the model casts a shadow larger than itself, a skyline of half-built towers on the wall. The work shows how personal play and urban memory can merge into a vivid model of transformation.

zh-Hant.heading: 起重機與廢墟-運轉中的城市機器
zh-Hant.body: 重建中的城市很少看起來是完成的，因為拆除與建造在同一視野中重疊。這個專題試圖捕捉這種不安定的狀態，而非任何單一建築。學生借用多年以玩具積木組裝機器人的經驗，那份遊戲早已悄悄訓練出對接頭、齒輪與活動臂的感覺。這些構件與黑色木條、鐵絲與卡紙混合，讓熟悉的零件失去玩具般的天真，開始像起重機與鷹架。指導鼓勵密度與冒險，於是框架被允許糾纏生長，紅色鐵絲軌道像永不停歇的機器路徑般穿梭其中。齒輪暗示進行中的工程，破碎的邊緣則透露已被清除的過往。在一盞燈下，模型投下比自身更大的影子，在牆上形成一片半完工高樓的天際線。這件作品說明，個人的遊戲與城市記憶能融合為一個生動的轉變模型。

pins.title: Floating Collage
pins.description:
Toy blueprints are cut, reassembled and extruded into white cardboard collages that bend upward like a city built on a rotating ground in space.

Collage model | Speculative city study | Cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮拼貼
zh-Hant.description:
玩具藍圖被切割、重組並拉伸為白色卡紙拼貼，向上彎折，如同一座建於太空中旋轉地面上的城市。

拼貼模型｜推想城市研究｜卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A childhood love of toy blasters led to collecting their technical blueprints. The project asked whether these drawings, once cut apart, could become the foundations of an imagined city.
captions: An image from the film that inspired the space city.
The toy blaster box whose blueprints were reused.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 童年對玩具發射器的喜愛，讓學生開始收集它們的技術藍圖。這個專題探問，這些圖紙被剪開後，能否成為一座想像城市的基礎。
captions: 啟發這座太空城市的電影畫面。
其藍圖被重新利用的玩具槍包裝盒。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The blueprints were cut and reassembled into new patterns that looked like plans of city foundations. Four collages were drawn, each tracing a different arrangement of parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 藍圖被剪開並重組成新的圖樣，看起來像城市基礎的平面。學生畫出四張拼貼，每張描出不同的構件排列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Buildings were extended upward from each collage by folding and slotting strips of white cardboard along its lines. The resulting reliefs cast dense shadows that make each plan read as a crowded district.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生沿著每張拼貼的線條折疊並插接白色卡紙條，讓建築從拼貼向上延伸。完成的浮雕投下濃密陰影，讓每張平面讀起來像一片擁擠的街區。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Imagining life in space, where the ground could bend into columns and rotate to simulate gravity, the parts were connected and the base was curved. The long model becomes a fragment of a space city whose streets turn up into walls.
captions: The maker with the finished model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 學生想像太空中的生活，地面可以彎成柱體並以旋轉模擬重力，於是把各部分相連並將底部彎曲。這個長形模型成為一座太空城市的片段，其街道向上翻轉成牆。

sections.heading: Folded Ground - A City That Curves Toward the Sky
sections.body: Children often see whole worlds in the diagrams that come with their toys, and this project took that way of seeing seriously. The student cut apart old blueprints of toy blasters and rearranged the fragments until they resembled plans of a dense urban foundation. Four collages were drawn, each a different negotiation between mechanical parts and imagined streets. From these drawings white cardboard strips were folded and slotted upward, so that every line became a wall and every cluster a district. The guidance encouraged pushing a method past its first result, and a further question soon arrived about how people might live where gravity must be manufactured. The answer was to bend the ground itself, curving the base so that the city wraps toward its own sky like the inside of a rotating drum. Shadows thicken the reliefs into crowded neighbourhoods. The work demonstrates how playful source material, treated with patience, can open into a speculative architecture of remarkable density.

zh-Hant.heading: 折疊的地面-彎向天空的城市
zh-Hant.body: 孩子常在玩具附帶的圖解中看見整個世界，這個專題認真對待了這種觀看方式。學生把玩具發射器的舊藍圖剪開，重新排列碎片，直到它們像一片密集的城市基礎平面。學生畫出四張拼貼，每張都是機械零件與想像街道之間不同的協商。從這些圖面出發，白色卡紙條被折疊並向上插接，讓每條線成為一道牆，每個群聚成為一片街區。指導鼓勵把方法推過第一個結果，於是一個新的問題隨之而來，即在重力必須被製造之處，人們該如何生活。答案是彎曲地面本身，讓基座彎曲，使城市如旋轉滾筒的內壁般朝自己的天空包覆。陰影讓浮雕加厚成擁擠的街坊。這件作品說明，帶有遊戲性的素材經耐心處理後，能展開為一種密度驚人的推想建築。

pins.title: Drumming Score
pins.description:
Drum notation is translated into stacked wooden trusses and layered white card, so that a rhythm can be read as a tower of beats and rests.

Model | Music and structure study | 400g white card, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鼓譜
zh-Hant.description:
鼓譜被轉譯為堆疊的木桁架與層疊的白卡紙，讓節奏能被讀作一座由拍點與休止構成的塔。

模型｜音樂與結構研究｜400g白卡紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project grew from a passion for playing drums and a wish to bring it into the study of architecture. It set out to extend the boundaries of what can be considered architectural.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源於對打鼓的熱愛，以及把它帶入建築研究的意願。它試圖拓展「何謂建築」這個概念的邊界。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A drum part from a rock song was transcribed and its bars were read as a sequence of hits, accents and rests. Each type of hit was assigned a structural element, from flat card plates to crossed wooden braces.
captions: A wireframe of the drum patterns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把一首搖滾歌曲的鼓聲部記譜，並把其中的小節讀作一連串的擊打、重音與休止。每種擊打都被指定為一種構造元素，從平坦的卡紙板到交叉的木斜撐。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Short study models tested how bars could be stacked, shifted and cantilevered while staying stable. Plates of card were piled on each level to show the density of hits in every beat.
captions: Study model of a short phrase.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 短小的研究模型測試小節如何在保持穩定的同時被堆疊、錯位與懸挑。卡紙板被堆放在每一層上，顯示每一拍中擊打的密度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final models rise as towers and spread as low platforms, each one a different passage of the song. By dissecting the drums, what is musical was translated into what is architectural, since both are constructions of rhythm.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的模型或升起為塔，或展開為低矮平台，每一座都是歌曲的不同段落。透過拆解鼓聲，音樂性的事物被轉譯為建築性的事物，因為兩者都是節奏的構築。

sections.heading: Beats in Timber - A Score That Stands Up
sections.body: A drum part is already a kind of plan, a grid of time in which every stroke has its precise place. This project took that grid literally and asked how far the idea of architecture might stretch to include it. Starting from a deep personal attachment to drumming, the student transcribed a rock passage and sorted its strokes into kinds, each matched with a structural member.
