Flat plates of card became the weight of hits, crossed sticks became the tension of accents, and empty bays recorded the rests. The guidance encouraged testing a rule through many small trials, so short phrases were built first and adjusted until they could shift and cantilever without collapse. Gradually the bars were stacked into towers and spread into low decks, each passage of the song acquiring its own silhouette. Seen together, the models resemble scaffolds for a performance that has already happened. The work shows how disciplined translation can turn a lived passion into a convincing architectural language.

zh-Hant.heading: 木中的拍點-站立起來的樂譜
zh-Hant.body: 鼓聲部本身已是一種平面圖，一張每次擊打都有精確位置的時間網格。這個專題照字面看待這張網格，探問建築的概念能延伸多遠以將其納入。學生從對打鼓深切的個人情感出發，把一段搖滾樂句記譜，並把其中的擊打分門別類，各自對應一種構造構件。平坦的卡紙板成為擊打的重量，交叉的木棒成為重音的張力，空著的開間則記錄休止。指導鼓勵透過許多小型試驗來檢驗規則，於是短樂句先被搭建，並反覆調整到能錯位與懸挑而不倒塌。小節逐漸堆疊成塔、鋪展成低台，歌曲的每個段落都得到自己的輪廓。放在一起看，這些模型像是一場已經結束的演出所留下的鷹架。這件作品說明，嚴謹的轉譯能把生活中的熱情化為具說服力的建築語言。

pins.title: Jazz Drumland
pins.description:
Curving white ribbons, spiral stairs and leaning wooden sticks form a restless landscape that gives the release of drumming a place for the mind.

Model | Music and emotion study | PVC board, wooden strips, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 爵士鼓樂園
zh-Hant.description:
彎曲的白色緞帶、螺旋梯與傾斜的木棒構成一片躁動的地景，為打鼓時的情緒釋放提供一處心靈之所。

模型｜音樂與情緒研究｜PVC板、木條、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After nine years of playing, drumming had become not only a hobby but a sanctuary and a way to release emotion. The project asked how that sanctuary could become a collective place for the mind.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 打鼓九年之後，打鼓不只是嗜好，也成了心靈的避風港與釋放情緒的方式。這個專題探問，這個避風港如何能成為一處集體的心靈場所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings of a drum kit were overlaid again and again on translucent sheets until drums, stands and cymbals dissolved into sweeping lines. These loops and arcs became the source of the curving forms in the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在半透明紙上一再疊畫鼓組，直到鼓、架與鈸消融為大幅的線條。這些環圈與弧線成為模型中彎曲形體的來源。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin PVC ribbons were bent into rings and swoops, while wooden sticks were driven in at many angles like drumsticks in motion. Iron wire traced lighter curves, and spiral stairs and platforms were threaded through the tangle.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 薄PVC條被彎成環圈與弧掠，木棒則以多種角度插入，宛如揮動中的鼓棒。鐵絲描出較輕的曲線，螺旋梯與平台則穿行於這片糾纏之中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Red figures climb, sit and wander across the platforms as if inside a frozen burst of sound. Shadows of the ribbons sweep across the walls and extend the energy of the model beyond its edges.
captions: A ring and a spiral stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 紅色人形在平台上攀爬、坐臥與漫遊，彷彿置身一陣凝結的聲響之中。緞帶的陰影掠過牆面，把模型的能量延伸到邊界之外。

sections.heading: Sanctuary in Motion - A Landscape for Release
sections.body: For anyone who plays an instrument for years, practice slowly becomes refuge, a place where feeling can be spent without words. This project set out to build such a refuge at the scale of a shared landscape. The student began by drawing the drum kit over and over on translucent sheets, layering until the familiar objects dissolved into loops, arcs and diagonals that recorded the gestures of playing more than the instruments themselves. Those traces were then given material form. Thin ribbons were bent into rings, wooden sticks were planted at restless angles like strokes caught mid-swing, and fine wire drew lighter phrases through the air. The guidance encouraged embracing complexity while keeping paths legible, so spiral stairs and small platforms were woven through the tangle to let figures climb and pause. Light from one side throws the ribbons across the walls as sweeping shadows. The model shows how an intensely personal practice can be opened outward into a generous spatial experience.

zh-Hant.heading: 運動中的避風港-為釋放而生的地景
zh-Hant.body: 對任何演奏樂器多年的人而言，練習會慢慢成為庇護，一處能不用言語而傾注情感的地方。這個專題試圖以共享地景的尺度構築這樣的庇護。學生先在半透明紙上一再描繪鼓組，層層疊加，直到熟悉的物件消融為環圈、弧線與斜線，記錄的與其說是樂器，不如說是演奏的手勢。這些痕跡隨後被賦予材料形體。薄條被彎成環圈，木棒以不安的角度插立，如同揮擊途中被定格的鼓棒，細鐵絲則在空中畫出較輕的樂句。指導鼓勵擁抱複雜，同時讓路徑保持可讀，於是螺旋梯與小平台被編織進這片糾纏，讓人形得以攀登與停留。側光把緞帶投成掠過牆面的陰影。這個模型說明，極其個人的練習能向外展開為慷慨的空間經驗。

pins.title: Fragmented Wind
pins.description:
Hundreds of small white card fragments are layered into rings that swirl into a vortex, an exploratory model built purely from the ring element.

Model | Form exploration | 400g white card | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 碎片之風
zh-Hant.description:
數百片白卡紙碎片層疊成環，旋繞為一道漩渦，這是一個純粹由環形元素構成的探索模型。

模型｜形式探索｜400g白卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project was inspired by the striking ring-shaped weapons of a toy series and an obsession with their design. It aimed to make an exploratory model purely from the ring element.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題的靈感來自一個玩具系列中醒目的環形武器，以及對其設計的著迷。它旨在純粹以環形元素做出一個探索模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Light trails were drawn in the dark to capture how a ring looks when it spins and overlaps itself. Small curled card studies then tested how a flat sheet could twist into a looping ring.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在黑暗中畫出光軌，捕捉環形旋轉並與自身重疊時的樣貌。小型捲曲卡紙研究隨後測試平坦紙張如何扭轉成迴旋的環。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Hundreds of small rectangles of card were cut and overlapped along curving paths, each piece tilted slightly from the last. The layered fragments built up into thick shells that bend around a hollow centre like gusts of wind.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生切出數百片小長方形卡紙，沿彎曲路徑重疊，每片都比前一片略微傾斜。層疊的碎片累積成厚實的殼，像一陣陣風般繞著空心的中央彎曲。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model reads as a frozen vortex with an inner ring and an outer sweep. Red figures standing beneath the shells reveal a space of shelter and motion at once.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型讀起來像一道凝結的漩渦，有內環與外圍的掃掠。站在殼下的紅色人形揭示出一個同時兼具庇護與運動的空間。

sections.heading: Gathered Gusts - A Ring Made of Pieces
sections.body: A ring is the simplest of closed forms, yet in motion it can suggest storms, orbits and the turning of breath. This project began with an admiration for the bold ring shapes of a toy series and turned that enthusiasm into a sustained formal inquiry. The student first drew with light in a dark room, spinning a glowing point so that its traces overlapped into tangled halos. Small curled sheets of card followed, testing how a flat surface might twist into a continuous loop. The guidance encouraged finding one strict element and letting the whole grow from it, so the ring was rebuilt from hundreds of small rectangles, each tilted slightly from its neighbour. Laid along sweeping paths, the fragments thickened into shells that curl around a hollow core like wind made visible. Red figures standing beneath the shells reveal unexpected rooms of shelter. The model demonstrates how a single repeated gesture can generate a complex space that feels both solid and in flight.

zh-Hant.heading: 聚集的風-由碎片構成的環
zh-Hant.body: 環是最簡單的封閉形式，但在運動中它能暗示風暴、軌道與呼吸的迴轉。這個專題始於對一個玩具系列中大膽環形的欣賞，並把這份熱情化為持續的形式探究。學生先在暗室中以光作畫，旋轉一個發光點，讓其軌跡重疊為糾纏的光暈。接著是小型捲曲卡紙，測試平坦表面如何扭轉成連續的迴圈。指導鼓勵找到一個嚴格的元素並讓整體由此生長，於是環形以數百片小長方形重新構成，每片都與鄰片略微錯斜。碎片沿掃掠的路徑鋪排，加厚成殼，如同可見的風般繞著空心的核捲曲。站在殼下的紅色人形揭示出意想不到的庇護之室。這個模型說明，單一重複的手勢能生成一個既堅實又彷彿飛行中的複雜空間。

pins.title: Nine Roofs
pins.description:
Impressions of roofs from three visited cities are collaged, traced into nine representative types and recombined into an imagined field of eaves and ridges.

Drawing | Roof and culture study | Pencil, Illustrator | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 九種屋頂
zh-Hant.description:
對三座造訪過的城市屋頂印象被拼貼，描繪成九種具代表性的類型，再重組為一片想像中的簷與脊。

繪圖｜屋頂與文化研究｜鉛筆、Illustrator｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The collage of nine roof types.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A classic treatise on architecture prompted the question of what roofs carry beyond shelter. The project set out to read roofs as bearers of cultural and functional meaning.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一部經典建築論著引發了屋頂在遮蔽之外還承載什麼的提問。這個專題試圖把屋頂讀作文化與功能意義的載體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Impressions of roofs seen in three cities were first collaged and then extended intuitively in pencil. Dense ink silhouettes helped to isolate the outlines that kept returning across the collages.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先把在三座城市所見的屋頂印象拼貼起來，再以鉛筆憑直覺延伸。濃重的墨色剪影幫助分離出在拼貼中反覆出現的輪廓。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: From these studies nine representative roof types were identified and traced out as clean line drawings. Each type was redrawn at a consistent angle so that they could be fitted together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從這些研究中辨識出九種具代表性的屋頂類型，並描繪為清晰的線稿。每種類型都以一致的角度重繪，讓它們能彼此拼合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The traced roofs were collaged into one continuous axonometric field that reads as a virtual space. Tiered eaves, flat terraces and pitched ridges overlap without a single ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 描繪好的屋頂被拼貼成一片連續的軸測場域，可被讀作一個虛擬空間。層疊的屋簷、平台與斜脊相互交疊，沒有單一的地面。

sections.heading: Eaves Without Ground - A Field of Remembered Roofs
sections.body: Roofs are often the first thing a traveller remembers and the last thing a plan describes, a crown that announces climate, craft and belonging. This project began from that gap and treated the roof as a cultural sign rather than a mere lid. Impressions gathered on journeys through three cities were cut, pasted and continued freehand, until the collage itself suggested which profiles mattered. Heavy ink silhouettes then stripped the scenes down to their outlines, revealing tiers, hips, ridges and flat terraces that recurred again and again. Nine of these types were distilled and traced with patient precision, each brought to a shared angle of view. The guidance encouraged moving between intuition and method, so the loose collage was followed by a disciplined catalogue and finally by an act of reassembly. In the resulting axonometric field the roofs float without walls or streets, layered like memories that refuse a single order. The drawing shows how careful observation can transform scattered impressions into a coherent spatial imagination.

zh-Hant.heading: 無地之簷-記憶中的屋頂之野
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂往往是旅人最先記住、而平面圖最後才描述的部分，像一頂宣告氣候、工藝與歸屬的冠冕。這個專題從這道落差出發，把屋頂視為文化符號，而非僅是一層蓋子。旅途中在三座城市收集的印象被剪下、拼貼並徒手延續，直到拼貼本身揭示哪些輪廓重要。濃重的墨色剪影隨後把場景簡化為輪廓，顯露出一再重現的層簷、廡殿、屋脊與平台。其中九種類型被提煉出來，以耐心而精確的線條描繪，並統一到同一個觀看角度。指導鼓勵在直覺與方法之間往返，於是鬆散的拼貼之後接著嚴謹的類型目錄，最後是一次重新組合。在完成的軸測場域中，屋頂沒有牆也沒有街道，彷彿層層疊起、拒絕單一秩序的記憶。這幅圖說明，細心的觀察能把零散的印象轉化為完整的空間想像。

pins.title: Tactics in Motion
pins.description:
The movements of three common basketball tactics are notated as lines and shapes, then extruded and melded into a single dynamic digital model.

Digital model | Movement notation study | Rhino, Illustrator | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 戰術的軌跡
zh-Hant.description:
三種常見籃球戰術的移動被記寫為線條與形狀，再被擠出並熔合為一個充滿動勢的數位模型。

數位模型｜移動記譜研究｜Rhino、Illustrator｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Inspired by an architectural experiment in notating events, the project asked whether movement itself could generate form. Three common basketball tactics were chosen as the moving subject.
captions: A basketball player silhouette, the starting point for the movement study.
The project title referencing the architectural text that inspired it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 受到一項記寫事件的建築實驗啟發，這個專題探問移動本身能否生成形式。三種常見的籃球戰術被選為移動的對象。
captions: 籃球員剪影，是動作研究的起點。
引用啟發本案之建築文本的專案標題。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The runs, passes and screens of each tactic were reinterpreted as lines, arcs and cutting shapes. Construction lines recorded the angles and distances of players on the court.
captions: Traced lines and arcs of the plays.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每種戰術中的跑位、傳球與掩護被重新詮釋為線條、弧線與切割的形狀。輔助線記錄了球員在場上的角度與距離。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each tactic was developed into a bold black and white drawing in which the paths overlap and splinter. The three drawings were then treated as plans to be extruded.
captions: Movement drawing of the first tactic.
Movement drawing of the second tactic.
Movement drawing of the third tactic.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每種戰術都被發展為一幅大膽的黑白繪圖，路徑在其中交疊與碎裂。這三幅繪圖隨後被視為可擠出的平面。
captions: 第一種戰術的移動繪圖。
第二種戰術的移動繪圖。
第三種戰術的移動繪圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: By extruding and melding the three drawings, a digital model of fins, blades and curved shells emerged. Its jagged profile embodies the movements and suggests constant dynamism.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 透過擠出並熔合三幅繪圖，一個由鰭片、刀刃與彎曲殼體構成的數位模型浮現。它鋸齒狀的輪廓體現了這些移動，並暗示持續的動勢。

sections.heading: Plays Made Solid - Notating the Speed of a Game
sections.body: A game unfolds as a rapid choreography that leaves no trace once the whistle blows. This project sought to hold that choreography still long enough to become architecture. Taking a cue from the idea that events and movements can be notated like music, the student studied three familiar tactics and translated each cut, pass and screen into lines and arcs measured against the court. Those notations grew into three dense drawings in which trajectories collide, split and reappear as sharp black wedges. The guidance favoured rigorous transformation over illustration, so each drawing was read as a plan and lifted into depth rather than simply decorated. When the three extrusions were melded, their conflicts produced fins, blades and curling shells that lean in the direction of play. The resulting model resembles a gust frozen in mid-sweep, legible from many sides yet never at rest. The work shows how a disciplined notation can carry the energy of the body into convincing spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固的戰術-記寫比賽的速度
zh-Hant.body: 一場比賽展開為一段快速的編舞，哨聲一響便不留痕跡。這個專題試圖讓這段編舞靜止得夠久，好成為建築。學生借鏡「事件與移動可以像音樂般被記寫」的想法，研究三種熟悉的戰術，把每次切入、傳球與掩護轉譯為以球場為尺度量測的線條與弧線。這些記寫發展成三幅緊密的繪圖，軌跡在其中碰撞、分岔，並以銳利的黑色楔形重現。指導重視嚴謹的轉化而非插畫，於是每幅繪圖都被讀作平面並被提升出深度，而不只是被裝飾。當三組擠出體熔合時，它們的衝突生成了朝比賽方向傾斜的鰭片、刀刃與捲曲殼體。完成的模型像一陣在掠過途中被凍結的風，從多個方向都能閱讀，卻從不靜止。這件作品說明，嚴謹的記譜能把身體的能量帶入具說服力的空間形式。

pins.title: Light as Distortion
pins.description:
Light is projected through transparent materials such as bubble wrap and tin, and the distorted shadows are gathered into an ambient digital collage.

Projection and collage | Light and material study | Bubble wrap, tin, water, Photoshop | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光的變形
zh-Hant.description:
光透過氣泡紙與錫片等透明材料投射，扭曲的陰影被收集成一幅氛圍性的數位拼貼。

投影與拼貼｜光與材料研究｜氣泡紙、錫片、水、Photoshop｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The way columns once cut long stone walls with their shadows raised the question of what projection could do. Because columns and their shadows are both solid, the project looked for materials that could make a projection reveal its own substance.
captions: A photo of an ancient stone colonnade and the shadows of its pillars.
A sketch of the projection idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 柱子以陰影切割長石牆的方式，引出投影能做到什麼的提問。由於柱子與其陰影都是實的，這個專題尋找能讓投影顯露自身質地的材料。
captions: 古代石柱廊與柱影的照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many transparent and translucent materials were tested under a single light, from plastics to water and coloured films. Each test recorded how the material changed the size, form and hue of its shadow.
captions: Testing projections by holding a light at different angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 許多透明與半透明材料在單一光源下被測試，從塑料到水與彩色薄膜。每次測試都記錄材料如何改變陰影的大小、形狀與色調。
captions: 以手持光源從不同角度測試投影。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Further experiments showed that the angle between light and subject controls the distortion, while distance controls the size. Section sketches mapped these relationships before the final projection was set up.
captions: Tests of light angle and distance.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 進一步的實驗顯示，光與物體之間的角度控制扭曲程度，而距離控制大小。在架設最終投影之前，剖面草圖先描繪出這些關係。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final projection was made with tin and water-filled bubble wrap, and its image became the base of an ambient collage. A coloured mock-up preceded the soft grey composition of the finished piece.
captions: A coloured mock-up of the collage.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的投影以錫片與注水的氣泡紙製作，其影像成為一幅氛圍拼貼的基底。在柔和灰調的完成作品之前，先有一幅彩色的試作。

sections.heading: Shadows With Substance - Light Through a Window of Matter
sections.body: A shadow is usually a simple absence, a dark copy of whatever stands in the way of the sun. This project asked what happens when the obstacle is not opaque but clear, rippled and full of water. Prompted by the memory of colonnades whose shadows divide a long wall into rhythm, the student set out to give projection a texture of its own. Plastics, films, liquids and foils were tried one by one, each image noting how a material swelled, bent or tinted the light. Out of this patient testing came a principle, that the angle of the beam governs distortion while distance governs scale, recorded in quick section sketches. The guidance encouraged treating light as a building material, so the final arrangement of tin and water-filled bubble wrap was tuned as carefully as a façade. Its photographed projection, softened into a grey ambient collage, reads like foliage or clouds suspended in a room. The work shows how close observation of light can redefine the nature of materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 有質地的陰影-穿過物質之窗的光
zh-Hant.body: 陰影通常只是一種缺席，是擋住陽光之物的黑暗複本。這個專題探問，當障礙物不是不透明，而是清澈、起伏且充滿水時，會發生什麼。學生想起柱廊的陰影如何把長牆分割成節奏，於是試圖賦予投影自身的質地。塑料、薄膜、液體與箔片被逐一嘗試，每張影像都記錄材料如何使光膨脹、彎曲或染色。從這番耐心的測試中歸納出一個原則：光束的角度主導扭曲，距離主導尺度，並以快速的剖面草圖記錄下來。指導鼓勵把光當作建築材料，於是錫片與注水氣泡紙的最終配置被調校得如同立面般仔細。拍下的投影被柔化為一幅灰調的氛圍拼貼，讀來像懸浮在房間裡的枝葉或雲層。這件作品說明，對光的細心觀察能重新定義材料的本質。

pins.title: Six Layers of an Island
pins.description:
Lines traced from a collage of a paper model become six layers that are extruded, rotated and stacked into an acrylic island suggestive of a natural environment.

Model | Abstraction study, summer programme | Acrylic sheets, 200 x 530 x 450 mm | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 島嶼的六層
zh-Hant.description:
從紙模型拼貼中描下的線條成為六個圖層，經擠出、旋轉與堆疊，構成一座暗示自然環境的壓克力島嶼。

模型｜抽象研究，暑期課程｜壓克力板，200 x 530 x 450 mm｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project, made in a summer programme, started from the belief that abstraction can be rational. It asked how a sequence of controlled steps could carry an abstract image towards a usable space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個在暑期課程中完成的專題，出發點是相信抽象可以是理性的。它探問一連串受控的步驟如何把抽象影像帶向可使用的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Elements of an earlier paper model were photographed and recombined into a dense collage. Six layers of lines were then traced from the collage, each isolating a different family of edges.
captions: The collage from the paper model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把先前紙模型的元素拍攝下來，重組為一幅緊密的拼貼。接著從拼貼中描下六層線條，每層分離出一組不同的邊緣。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The six layers were used to build three 3D explorations and then simplified into a space that could be occupied. Lines and forms were extruded, rotated and combined while sections tested the resulting rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 六個圖層被用來建構三個立體探索，再簡化為可被進駐的空間。線條與形體被擠出、旋轉與組合，剖面則檢驗由此產生的房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final acrylic model rises as a cluster of thin planes and stepped platforms. Its interlocking layers suggest cliffs, ledges and caves of a natural environment.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的壓克力模型升起為一叢薄板與階梯狀平台。它相互咬合的圖層暗示了自然環境中的峭壁、岩架與洞穴。

sections.heading: Rational Wilderness - Layers That Become Land
sections.body: Abstraction is often imagined as a leap of instinct, yet it can also be a ladder climbed one rung at a time. This project tested that second view during an intensive summer course. An earlier paper model was photographed and reassembled into a collage, a busy image that already held more edges than any single drawing could manage. Six layers were then traced from it, each one filtering out a particular family of lines, so the chaos was sorted without being erased. The guidance emphasised continuity of method, so every later move, from three spatial explorations to a simplified occupiable scheme, could be traced back to those layers. Lines were extruded into walls, rotated into ramps and combined into terraces, and sections confirmed where a body might stand or rest. Built in clear and frosted acrylic, the final model rises like a shard of coastline caught between geology and architecture. The work shows how a rational sequence can arrive at a place that feels convincingly natural.

zh-Hant.heading: 理性的荒野-化為土地的圖層
zh-Hant.body: 抽象常被想像為一次本能的躍進，但它也可以是一步一階攀上的梯子。這個專題在一門密集的暑期課程中檢驗了第二種看法。先前的紙模型被拍攝並重組為拼貼，一幅繁忙的影像，其中的邊緣已多到任何單一繪圖都難以承載。接著從中描下六個圖層，每層篩出一組特定的線條，讓混亂被整理而非被抹除。指導強調方法的連貫，於是之後的每一步，從三個空間探索到簡化後可進駐的方案，都能追溯回這些圖層。線條被擠出為牆，旋轉成坡道，組合為平台，剖面則確認身體可以站立或休息的位置。以透明與霧面壓克力製作的最終模型，像一片介於地質與建築之間的海岸碎片般升起。這件作品說明，理性的步驟序列也能抵達一處令人信服的自然之地。

pins.title: A Room Recast in Blocks
pins.description:
A familiar bedroom is broken into blocks the width of a palm, and the motion of a basketball layup is pressed into each façade to compose a new, dynamic space.

Digital model | Room and motion study | Rhino | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 以方塊重塑的房間
zh-Hant.description:
一間熟悉的臥室被拆解為一掌寬的方塊，上籃動作被壓印進每一面牆，組成一個全新而具動勢的空間。

數位模型｜房間與動作研究｜Rhino｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The most familiar room in the world had become tiresome through repetition. The project set out to redefine that room with a sense of dynamism.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 世上最熟悉的房間因日復一日而變得乏味。這個專題試圖以動勢重新定義這個房間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Because the room is mostly touched by hand, it was deconstructed into blocks whose side equals the width of a palm. The trajectory of a basketball layup was traced as a sequence of curves.
captions: Isometric studies of a figure and the room's furniture.
Silhouette studies of the motions of a basketball layup.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 由於房間主要是透過雙手接觸，它被拆解為邊長等同手掌寬度的方塊。上籃的軌跡被描繪為一連串曲線。
captions: 人物與房間家具的等角研究。
籃球上籃動作的剪影研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The traced motion was used to push and pull the blocks of each façade in turn. Stepped studies tested how deeply the motion could carve each wall.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 描下的動作被用來依次推拉每一面立面的方塊。階梯狀的研究測試動作能把每面牆雕刻得多深。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The carved façades were composed together into a new spatial interpretation of the room. Their rippling surfaces turn a static enclosure into a record of movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 雕刻後的立面被組合在一起，成為對房間的全新空間詮釋。起伏的表面把靜止的圍塑轉為動作的紀錄。

sections.heading: Palm and Leap - Unsettling the Familiar Room
sections.body: Familiarity can dull even the most intimate space, until its walls are no longer seen at all. This project treated that dullness as a design problem and sought to wake the room through the body. The student noticed that the room is known chiefly through touch, so the palm became the unit of measure and every surface was broken into blocks of that width. A second gesture, the springing arc of a layup, supplied the energy that the quiet room lacked. Traced as a chain of curves, the leap was pressed into the walls one by one, pushing some blocks outward and drawing others back. The guidance encouraged a strict rule applied with patience, so stepped studies measured how far the motion could carve before a wall lost its identity. When the four faces were reassembled, they formed undulating screens that seem to remember a body passing through. The work shows how personal habits can become precise generators of fresh architectural space.

zh-Hant.heading: 手掌與躍起-擾動熟悉的房間
zh-Hant.body: 熟悉感會讓最親密的空間也變得遲鈍，直到牆面再也不被看見。這個專題把這種遲鈍視為設計問題，試圖透過身體喚醒房間。學生注意到房間主要是透過觸摸而被認識，於是手掌成為量度單位，每個表面都被拆成這個寬度的方塊。第二個姿態是上籃時彈起的弧線，提供了安靜房間所缺乏的能量。這次躍起被描繪為一串曲線，逐一壓印進牆面，把一些方塊推出，把另一些拉回。指導鼓勵以耐心施行嚴格的規則，於是階梯狀的研究量測動作能雕刻多深，而不致讓牆失去身分。當四個面重新組合時，它們形成起伏的屏幕，彷彿記得一具身體曾經穿過。這件作品說明，個人的習慣能成為生成新鮮建築空間的精確動力。

pins.title: Shell Trusses
pins.description:
The mathematical structure of shells is dissected in layers, rebuilt as a vertical digital model and reinterpreted as a truss model of wooden sticks.

Digital and physical model | Natural structure study | Rhino, wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 貝殼桁架
zh-Hant.description:
貝殼的數學結構被分層剖析，重建為垂直的數位模型，並被重新詮釋為木棒桁架模型。

數位與實體模型｜自然結構研究｜Rhino、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Shells have structures so mathematical, yet they appear in such organic forms. The project set out to borrow that structure to create spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 貝殼的結構如此數學化，卻呈現出如此有機的形態。這個專題試圖借用這種結構來創造空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Shells were redrawn as wireframes that trace their spirals, ribs and growth lines. The drawings revealed how a simple rule of growth produces complex curvature.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把貝殼重繪為線框，描出其螺旋、肋紋與生長線。這些繪圖揭示了簡單的生長規則如何產生複雜的曲率。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The shell was dissected into horizontal slices, and a digital model stacked those layers on vertical levels. Each layer twists slightly from the last, producing a spiralling tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 貝殼被剖切為水平切片，數位模型把這些圖層堆疊在垂直的樓層上。每一層都比上一層略為扭轉，形成一座螺旋上升的塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The structure was then reinterpreted as trusses and built as a physical model of wooden sticks. Its triangulated web encloses a long, cave-like space.
captions: A close view of the truss joints.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 結構隨後被重新詮釋為桁架，並以木棒製作成實體模型。三角化的網架圍出一個狹長、如洞穴般的空間。

sections.heading: Growth Into Frame - From Shell to Shelter
sections.body: Few objects reconcile geometry and life as gracefully as a shell, whose curves are the residue of a patient rule repeated over time. This project tried to borrow that rule rather than its outward appearance. Careful wireframe drawings first traced the spirals, ribs and growth lines, showing how a single logic of accretion yields surfaces of great complexity. The shell was then cut into slices, and the digital model stacked them on vertical levels, each turning slightly from the one below until a spiralling tower emerged. The guidance stressed testing an idea across media, so the same geometry was translated a second time into straight members and triangulated joints. Built from thin wooden sticks, the truss model keeps the swelling silhouette of the shell while opening its interior into a long, sheltering void. Light passing through the web casts a dense lattice of shadows across the ground. The work shows how a natural structure can be understood deeply enough to become a constructive principle.

zh-Hant.heading: 生長成架-從貝殼到庇護
zh-Hant.body: 很少有物件能像貝殼那樣優雅地調和幾何與生命，它的曲線是一條耐心規則隨時間重複後留下的痕跡。這個專題試圖借用這條規則，而非它的外表。細緻的線框繪圖先描出螺旋、肋紋與生長線，顯示單一的累積邏輯如何產生極為複雜的曲面。接著貝殼被切成切片，數位模型把它們堆疊在垂直樓層上，每層都比下一層略為轉動，直到一座螺旋之塔浮現。指導強調在不同媒材中檢驗想法，於是同一套幾何再一次被轉譯為直線構件與三角形節點。以細木棒製作的桁架模型保留了貝殼鼓脹的輪廓，同時把內部打開為一個狹長而具庇護感的空腔。穿過網架的光在地面投下密集的格狀陰影。這件作品說明，對自然結構的深入理解能使其成為構築的原則。

pins.title: A Line with Weight
pins.description:
The way a single brushstroke holds definition and detail inspires a long undulating roof, built as a sequence of repetitive structures over a light frame.

Digital model | Line and roof study | Rhino | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 有重量的線
zh-Hant.description:
一筆筆畫中所蘊含的力度與細節，啟發了一道長而起伏的屋頂，以一連串重複的結構架在輕盈的框架上。

數位模型｜線條與屋頂研究｜Rhino｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In brush calligraphy a simple line should possess definition and details. The project asked how a single line could carry that richness into architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在毛筆書法中，一條簡單的線應當具有力度與細節。這個專題探問，一條線如何能把這種豐富帶入建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Rows of brushstrokes were studied for their thickening, thinning and ragged edges. Their profiles were then sculpted as small carved forms to read them in three dimensions.
captions: A carved model of a line.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究一排排筆畫的粗細變化與毛糙邊緣。接著把它們的輪廓雕塑為小型形體，以立體的方式閱讀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The line was drawn out as a series of roof variations over a simple frame, each with a different rhythm of rise and fall. Shadow studies tested how the twisting surface would read in light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這條線被拉展為一系列架在簡單框架上的屋頂變化，每一種都有不同的起伏節奏。陰影研究測試扭轉的曲面在光線下會如何被閱讀。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: To mimic the cragginess of the line in an industrial fashion, the roof was built from a sequence of repetitive structures. The final pavilion stretches the stroke into a long, rippling canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 為了以工業化的方式模仿線條的嶙峋，屋頂以一連串重複的結構構成。最終的亭子把筆畫延展為一道長而起伏的頂棚。

sections.heading: Ink Into Canopy - The Stroke That Learned to Span
sections.body: A brushstroke is never only a line, since its pressure, speed and dryness leave a record of the hand that drew it. This project took that record seriously and asked whether a roof could inherit it. The student began by examining rows of strokes, watching how each swelled at the start, thinned in motion and frayed at the end. Small carved forms then lifted these profiles off the paper so that the edges could be read in depth. Drawn out over a light frame, the stroke became a series of roof variations, each testing a different cadence of rise and fall, while shadow studies revealed how the twisting surface would catch the sun. The guidance encouraged reconciling expression with buildability, so the rough texture was finally rendered through a sequence of repeated ribs rather than freeform sculpture. The resulting canopy ripples above its slender columns like ink still wet on paper. The work shows how a traditional sensibility can inform a clear and constructible architectural idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 墨化為棚-學會跨越的筆畫
zh-Hant.body: 一道筆畫從來不只是一條線，它的壓力、速度與乾濕都記錄了書寫的手。這個專題認真看待這份紀錄，探問屋頂能否繼承它。學生先觀察一排排筆畫，留意每一筆如何在起筆處飽滿、在運行中變細、在收筆處散開。接著小型雕刻形體把這些輪廓從紙面抬起，讓邊緣得以在深度中被閱讀。這道筆畫被拉展在輕盈的框架上，成為一系列屋頂變化，各自測試不同的起伏節奏，陰影研究則揭示扭轉的曲面如何承接陽光。指導鼓勵調和表現與可建造性，於是毛糙的質感最終透過一連串重複的肋條呈現，而非自由雕塑。完成的頂棚在纖細的柱子上起伏，像紙上未乾的墨跡。這件作品說明，傳統的感受力能啟發清晰而可建造的建築構想。

pins.title: Village Stacks
pins.description:
A dense market village is recorded as a long section drawing and rebuilt as four stacked PVC models that can be piled up or set side by side.

Model and drawing | Urban village study | PVC board, pencil | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 村落堆疊
zh-Hant.description:
一座密集的市場村落被記錄為一張長剖面圖，再以四座堆疊的PVC模型重建，可上下疊放或並排組合。

模型與繪圖｜城中村研究｜PVC板、鉛筆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A village enclosed by the city supplies daily food to its neighbours through a crowded market. The project set out to record the structure of that market and imagine what happens inside it.
captions: Street photos of the market village that started the study.
Photos of the village's shops, salon, restaurant, playground, market and stalls.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座被城市包圍的村落透過擁擠的市場為鄰里供應日常食物。這個專題試圖記錄這個市場的結構，並想像其中發生的事。
captions: 啟發本研究的市場村街景照片。
村內商店、髮廊、餐廳、遊樂場、市場與攤位的照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A long section drawing traced shops, stairs and rooftops floor by floor, adding playful features such as a zoo and a diving pool. Stores, salons, eateries and stalls were catalogued as the typical programmes of the village.
captions: Left half of the village section.
Right half of the village section.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張長剖面圖逐層描繪商店、樓梯與屋頂，並加入動物園與跳水池等趣味元素。商店、髮廊、餐館與攤位被整理為村落的典型機能。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each building type observed on site was translated into its own stacked model of thin slabs and walls. Schools, shops and places of entertainment were slotted between floors that shift and overhang.
captions: The four models side by side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 現場觀察到的每種建築類型都被轉譯為一座由薄板與牆片堆疊而成的模型。學校、商店與娛樂空間被嵌入彼此錯動、懸挑的樓層之間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The models were piled up or placed side by side to compose new forms of the village. Every arrangement produced a different skyline of terraces, gaps and bridges.
captions: Arranging two of the stacked models side by side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型被上下堆疊或並排擺放，組合出村落的新形態。每一種排列都產生不同的平台、縫隙與天橋天際線。
captions: 將兩座堆疊模型並排組合。

sections.heading: Stacked Lives - Recomposing a Market Village
sections.body: Villages swallowed by the city often survive as tight clusters of shops and homes, where daily life spills across every threshold. This project began with such a market near home and treated its crowded order as something worth recording rather than erasing. A long section drawing became the first instrument, following stairs, counters and rooftops floor by floor while slipping in imagined delights such as a small zoo and a diving pool. From that record, distinct building characters were identified and each was rebuilt as a slender model of white slabs and walls, with shops, classrooms and places of play inserted between shifting floors. The guidance encouraged treating the models as pieces of a game rather than fixed objects, so they were stacked, paired and spread out to test new collective forms. Each arrangement revealed different gaps, terraces and bridges, suggesting how density could become generous instead of oppressive. The work shows how patient observation can turn an informal neighbourhood into a rich vocabulary for future urban design.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊起的生活-重組市場村落
zh-Hant.body: 被城市吞沒的村落常以密集的商店與住家群落存續，日常生活在每一道門檻間流淌。這個專題從住家附近的一座市場出發，把它擁擠的秩序視為值得記錄而非抹除的事物。一張長剖面圖成為第一件工具，逐層追隨樓梯、櫃台與屋頂，同時悄悄加入小型動物園與跳水池等想像中的樂趣。從這份紀錄中辨識出各具特色的建築性格，每一種都被重建為一座由白色薄板與牆片組成的纖細模型，商店、教室與遊戲空間被嵌入錯動的樓層之間。指導鼓勵把模型當作遊戲的棋子而非固定物件，於是它們被堆疊、成對擺放或攤開，以測試新的集體形態。每種排列都揭示了不同的縫隙、平台與天橋，暗示密度可以變得慷慨而非壓迫。這件作品說明，耐心的觀察能把非正式的街區轉化為未來城市設計的豐富語彙。

pins.title: Maze, Forest, Swirl
pins.description:
Landscape impressions are reduced in rapid tracing to lines, curves and circles, then built as three models: a cardboard maze, a forest of PVC strips and a floating swirl.

Model | 2D-to-3D translation study | Cardboard, PVC board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 迷宮、森林、漩渦
zh-Hant.description:
風景印象在快速描繪中被簡化為線段、曲線與圓，再建造成三件模型：紙板迷宮、PVC條森林與漂浮的漩渦。

模型｜二維到三維轉譯研究｜紙板、PVC板、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Landscapes seen on a journey left strong impressions that were hard to describe in words. The project asked how those impressions could be extracted and carried from the flat page into space.
captions: Landscape photos from a trip that inspired the three drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 旅途中看到的風景留下難以言喻的深刻印象。這個專題探問，這些印象如何被提取，並從平面帶入空間。
captions: 啟發三幅繪畫的旅途風景照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Working on tracing paper within sixty seconds at a time, every method was used to extract the elements of each scene. The results were reduced to three families of marks: line segments, curves and circles.
captions: Holding the cardboard maze up over a light table.
Cutting and assembling the strips by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在描圖紙上每次限時六十秒，用盡各種方法提取每個場景的元素。結果被簡化為三類筆觸：線段、曲線與圓。
captions: 將紙板迷宮舉在燈箱上方。
以手工切割並組裝紙條。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The curves became a maze of white cardboard, with a second layer built on top of the first. PVC strips cut to three thicknesses and many lengths were arranged in waves to form an urban forest.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 曲線成為一座白色紙板迷宮，第二層建在第一層之上。切成三種厚度與多種長度的PVC條依波浪排列，形成一片城市森林。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The circles were built as a ring of cardboard and wooden strips that lifts itself up like an arena. Its projecting sticks extend outward to suggest a floating city.
captions: The swirl as a floating ring.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 圓被建造成一圈由紙板與木條構成、如競技場般自行升起的環。向外伸出的木條暗示一座漂浮的城市。

sections.heading: Sixty Seconds of Landscape - Marks That Became Worlds
sections.body: Memories of landscape rarely arrive as complete pictures; they return as gestures, a ridge, a ripple, the curve of a shoreline. This project trusted those gestures and sought to give them bodies. Rapid tracings, each limited to a single minute, forced the hand to choose what mattered, and the sheets gradually settled into three families of marks: straight segments, flowing curves and concentric rings. The guidance encouraged letting each family find its own material, so the work grew into three distinct experiments rather than one. Curves were folded into white cardboard walls that wind like a maze and then doubled into a second storey. Short lines were cut from boards of three thicknesses and set in rising and falling waves, producing a dense forest that glows under light. Rings were assembled from card and timber strips into a swirling arena that seems to lift off its base. Together the models show how disciplined abstraction can turn fleeting perception into convincing spatial worlds.

zh-Hant.heading: 六十秒的風景-長成世界的筆觸
zh-Hant.body: 風景的記憶很少以完整的畫面回來，它們以姿態重返：一道山脊、一圈漣漪、一條海岸的曲線。這個專題信任這些姿態，並試圖賦予它們形體。每張只限一分鐘的快速描繪迫使手做出取捨，紙頁逐漸沉澱為三類筆觸：直線段、流動的曲線與同心環。指導鼓勵讓每一類筆觸找到屬於自己的材料，於是作品發展成三個各自獨立的實驗，而非單一模型。曲線被摺成如迷宮般蜿蜒的白色紙板牆，再加倍成第二層。短線從三種厚度的板材切出，以起伏的波浪排列，形成一片在光下發亮的密林。圓環則以卡紙與木條組成旋轉的競技場，彷彿要從底座升起。這些模型共同說明，嚴謹的抽象能把轉瞬即逝的感知轉化為具說服力的空間世界。

pins.title: A Home Measured in Basswood
pins.description:
A family home is measured, drawn as three hand-drafted floor plans and rebuilt floor by floor as a basswood model with tiles, wallpaper and stairs.

Drawing and model | Domestic space study | Basswood sheet, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 以木片量度的家
zh-Hant.description:
一個家被實地量測，繪成三張手繪平面圖，再以椴木片逐層重建為帶有磁磚、壁紙與樓梯的模型。

繪圖與模型｜居住空間研究｜椴木片、紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After years of living in the same home, the space had become almost invisible. The project set out to analyse that home as a body whose rooms depend on one another like organs.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在同一個家住了多年之後，這個空間幾乎變得看不見。這個專題試圖把這個家當作一個身體來分析，其房間像器官般相互依存。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Every room was measured and the structure was drawn to scale as three hand-drafted plans. Furniture, tiles and fittings were recorded so that each floor kept its own character.
captions: Rearranging the three floor models by hand while refining them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個房間都被量測，結構以比例繪製成三張手繪平面圖。家具、磁磚與設備都被記錄下來，讓每層樓保有自己的性格。
captions: 在修整過程中以手調整三層樓模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wood and cardboard were used to restore the basic structure of each floor as faithfully as possible. Wallpaper, tile grids and stairs were applied to the walls and floors of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生以木片與紙板盡可能忠實地還原每層樓的基本結構。壁紙、磁磚格線與樓梯被施加在模型的牆面與地面上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The three floors can be viewed apart as open plans or stacked to reassemble the whole house. Seen from above, the rooms read as a sequence of distinct but connected parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三層樓可以分開作為開放的平面觀看，也可以疊起重組整棟住宅。從上方看去，房間被讀作一連串各自獨立卻相互連結的部分。

sections.heading: Rooms as Organs - Reading the Familiar House
sections.body: The places lived in longest are often the least examined, their corners worn smooth by habit. This project began from a magazine on living space that prompted a fresh look at a family house, and it proposed an unexpected analogy: each room, with its own textures and duties, behaves like an organ in a body that cannot function without the others. To test the idea, every dimension was measured and translated into three carefully hand-drafted plans, in which tiles, cabinets and stairs are rendered with equal care. The guidance stressed accuracy as a form of respect, so the subsequent model in thin basswood and card restored walls, wallpaper and floor grids as faithfully as the material allowed. Separated, the floors read like open specimens on a table; stacked, they recompose a whole that suddenly seems strange and new. The exercise turned the everyday into a subject of study and gave a first vocabulary of plan, section and assembly. The work shows how a close reading of home can open a lasting interest in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 如器官的房間-閱讀熟悉的住宅
zh-Hant.body: 住得最久的地方往往最少被審視，它的角落已被習慣磨得光滑。這個專題從一本談居住空間的雜誌出發，重新凝視一棟家宅，並提出一個意外的類比：每個房間各有質地與職責，就像身體中的器官，彼此缺一不可。為了檢驗這個想法，每一個尺寸都被量測，並轉譯為三張細心手繪的平面圖，磁磚、櫥櫃與樓梯都被同樣用心地描繪。指導強調精確是一種尊重，於是隨後以薄椴木片與卡紙製作的模型，盡材料所能忠實還原了牆體、壁紙與地坪格線。分開時，各層樓像攤在桌上的標本；疊起時，它們重組為一個忽然顯得陌生而新鮮的整體。這項練習把日常變成研究的對象，也建立了平面、剖面與組裝的最初語彙。這件作品說明，細讀一個家能開啟對空間持久的興趣。

pins.title: Changeable Towers
pins.description:
Natural forms such as caves, waves, rocks and waste are extracted into foam and stick towers that can stand alone or join into one giant skyscraper.

Model | Future tower study | Foam, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 可變之塔
zh-Hant.description:
洞穴、波浪、岩石與廢棄物等自然形態被提取為泡棉與木棒塔樓，可各自獨立，也可接合為一座巨型摩天樓。

模型｜未來塔樓研究｜泡棉、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Spending whole days inside one building can make the changing weather outside almost unnoticed. The project imagined what a tower might become a century from now if it were integrated with nature.
captions: A collage of skyscraper history, from early towers to today's supertall buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 整天待在同一棟建築裡，幾乎會察覺不到外面天氣的變化。這個專題想像一百年後的塔樓若與自然融合，可能成為什麼。
captions: 從早期高樓到當代超高層建築的摩天樓發展史拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Caves, plains, waves, dunes and piles of waste were studied as the physical evolution of natural forms. Their contours were abstracted into quick line sketches and small foam tests.
captions: Photos of caves, plains, waves, dunes, rocks and waste used as source forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 洞穴、平原、波浪、沙丘與廢棄物堆被當作自然形態的物理演化來研究。它們的輪廓被抽象為快速的線條草圖與小型泡棉試驗。
captions: 作為形態來源的洞穴、平原、波浪、沙丘、岩石與廢棄物照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each form was built up as a tall tower of carved foam blocks with its own texture. A tower of wooden sticks around foam pieces explored emptiness so that people could touch the environment more easily.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每種形態都被堆成一座由雕刻泡棉塊組成、帶有獨特質地的高塔。一座以木棒圍繞泡棉塊的塔樓探索空無，讓人能更容易接觸環境。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The future skyscraper was proposed as changeable, its parts able to stand apart or combine. Stacked together, the towers form one very tall structure that rises higher than its maker.
captions: Renderings placing the towers among a real city skyline.
Joining the towers into one giant skyscraper by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 未來的摩天樓被提出為可變的，各部分可以分立或組合。疊在一起時，這些塔樓形成一座比製作者還高的巨大結構。
captions: 將塔樓置入真實城市天際線的渲染圖。
以手將塔樓接合為一座巨型摩天樓。

sections.heading: Weather Within the Tower - Nature as a Building Kit
sections.body: A day spent entirely indoors can erase the sky, and this project took that small loss as the starting point for a speculative tower. Rather than designing a sealed vertical machine, the student looked outward to caves, plains, waves, dunes and even heaps of discarded material, treating them as evidence of how forms evolve under natural forces. Their contours were caught in loose line sketches and then tested in soft blue foam, cut, torn and stacked until each tower possessed a distinct grain. One experiment set wooden sticks around suspended blocks, a framework of emptiness meant to let air, light and people pass through. The guidance encouraged thinking of a building as something that may change over time, so the towers were made as interchangeable parts. They stand alone as a family of textured columns, yet they can also be joined into a single giant spine that rises above head height. The work shows how speculation grounded in close observation can renew the familiar idea of the skyscraper.

zh-Hant.heading: 塔中的天氣-以自然為構件
zh-Hant.body: 整天待在室內能抹去天空，這個專題把這份小小的失落當作一座思辨塔樓的起點。學生沒有設計一部封閉的垂直機器，而是把目光投向洞穴、平原、波浪、沙丘，甚至成堆的廢棄物，把它們視為形態在自然力量下演化的證據。這些輪廓先被捕捉在鬆散的線條草圖中，再以柔軟的藍色泡棉試驗，經過切割、撕扯與堆疊，直到每座塔都擁有獨特的紋理。其中一個實驗以木棒圍繞懸置的方塊，構成一副空無的框架，讓空氣、光線與人得以穿過。指導鼓勵把建築想成會隨時間改變的事物，於是塔樓被做成可互換的構件。它們單獨站立時是一組質地各異的柱體，也能接合成一道高過頭頂的巨大脊柱。這件作品說明，立足於細心觀察的思辨能讓摩天樓這個熟悉的概念煥然一新。

pins.title: Symbol of My Own
pins.description:
Elements of growing up are cast as small brass frames, wrapped layer by layer in soy wax and burned as candles that slowly reveal what lies inside.

Object | Personal symbol study | Wood, clay, brass, soy wax | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 屬於自己的符號
zh-Hant.description:
成長中的元素被鑄成小巧的黃銅框架，以大豆蠟層層包覆，再作為蠟燭點燃，慢慢顯露其中的內容。

物件｜個人符號研究｜木、黏土、黃銅、大豆蠟｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked what shape could stand as a personal symbol. Instead of a single sign, it looked for a structure that could hold several stages of growth.
captions: The anime scene where a character's symbol turns into a teardrop.
Photos of people traced into sketches, asking what symbol each represents.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，什麼形狀能作為一個人的符號。它沒有尋找單一的記號，而是尋找一個能容納成長各階段的結構。
captions: 角色象徵化為淚滴的動畫場景。
將人物照片描繪為草圖，思考每個人代表的象徵。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Childhood comfort, a defensive spiny adolescence and a steadier adulthood were identified as key stages. Music, tears, sweat, a hole and a fingerprint were added as smaller elements to be wrapped together.
captions: A collage of personal growth elements, from a teddy bear to music and fingerprints.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 童年的安慰、帶刺而防衛的青春期與更穩定的成年被辨識為關鍵階段。音樂、淚水、汗水、孔洞與指紋被加入，作為一同包覆的較小元素。
captions: 從泰迪熊到音樂與指紋的個人成長元素拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Models of wood and clay were turned into wax moulds and cast in brass before polishing. All the brass structures were then wrapped in soy wax, layer after layer.
captions: Shaping the wax molds and brass pieces by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木與黏土模型被翻製成蠟模並鑄成黃銅，再經拋光。所有黃銅結構隨後被大豆蠟一層層包覆。
captions: 以手工塑造蠟模與黃銅構件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The candles were lit in four meaningful places, each burning like a birthday candle. As the wax melted away, the metal structures inside were gradually revealed.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 蠟燭在四個具意義的地方被點燃，每一支都像生日蠟燭般燃燒。隨著蠟漸漸融化，裡面的金屬結構逐步顯露。

sections.heading: Burning Toward the Core - A Self Wrapped in Wax
sections.body: Identity is seldom a single image; it accumulates like sediment, each season leaving a layer over the last. This project gave that idea a literal form by asking what object could carry the stages of a life. Childhood comfort, a spiny and defensive adolescence and a steadier adulthood were chosen as the principal chapters, joined by smaller traces such as music, tears, sweat, an opening and a fingerprint. Sketches in wire and early models in wood and clay were turned into moulds and cast in brass, a material chosen for its resilience and its quiet glow. The guidance encouraged letting time participate in the design, so the polished pieces were sealed inside successive coats of soy wax and shaped into candles. Lit in four places of personal meaning, the candles burned slowly, and as the wax slumped away the hidden frames emerged one by one. What remains is both an object and a record of duration. The work shows how material processes can express personal memory with clarity and restraint.

zh-Hant.heading: 燃向核心-以蠟包覆的自我
zh-Hant.body: 身分很少是單一的影像，它像沉積物般累積，每個季節都在前一層之上留下新的一層。這個專題探問什麼物件能承載一段生命的各個階段，為這個想法賦予具體的形式。童年的安慰、帶刺而防衛的青春期與更穩定的成年被選為主要章節，再加上音樂、淚水、汗水、一個開口與指紋等較小的痕跡。以鐵絲畫出的草圖和木與黏土的初步模型被翻成模具並鑄成黃銅，選用這種材料是因為它的堅韌與內斂的光澤。指導鼓勵讓時間參與設計，於是拋光後的構件被封進一層層大豆蠟中，塑成蠟燭。蠟燭在四個具個人意義的地方點燃，緩慢燃燒，隨著蠟漸漸塌落，隱藏的框架一一浮現。留下的既是一件物件，也是一段時間的紀錄。這件作品說明，材料的過程能以清晰而節制的方式表達個人記憶。

pins.title: Swollen World
pins.description:
A long struggle with a skin allergy is turned into clay faces pierced with needles and wrapped in dried herbs, ending in one sculpture with three swollen faces.

Sculpture | Body and emotion study | Clay, needles, dried herbs | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 腫脹的世界
zh-Hant.description:
一段與皮膚過敏的長期搏鬥被轉化為插著針、包裹乾燥草藥的黏土臉孔，最終成為一件擁有三張腫脹面孔的雕塑。

雕塑｜身體與情緒研究｜黏土、針、乾燥草藥｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A skin allergy that caused red, raised swelling after exercise had shaped daily life for three years. The project asked how the mixed feelings of that condition could be expressed as an object.
captions: A collage of the causes, feelings and treatments of urticaria, with photos of swollen skin.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一種運動後會引發紅腫隆起的皮膚過敏，三年來影響著日常生活。這個專題探問，這種狀況帶來的複雜感受如何被表達為一件物件。
captions: 以腫脹皮膚照片呈現蕁麻疹成因、感受與治療的拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The physical reactions and the emotions they caused, such as anxiety, tiredness and embarrassment, were mapped side by side. Needles and herbs were chosen to stand for traditional treatments, with clay as the main material.
captions: Research into Johnson Tsang's surreal faces and Tim Silver's cast busts.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 身體反應與其引發的焦慮、疲憊與尷尬等情緒被並列整理。針與草藥被選來代表傳統療法，黏土則作為主要材料。
captions: 研究 Johnson Tsang 的超現實臉孔與 Tim Silver 的翻模胸像。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A simple swollen face was modelled first, and herbs and needles were then pressed into its surface. Several small test faces in brown and white clay explored how the treatments might sit on the skin.
captions: Sculpting the clay faces by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生先塑出一張簡單的腫脹臉孔，再把草藥與針壓入其表面。幾張棕色與白色黏土的小型試作臉孔，探索療法如何附著在皮膚上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final sculpture joins three exaggerated faces wrapped in leaves, herbs and needles. Its slightly unsettling atmosphere records a process of coming to accept oneself.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終雕塑結合三張被葉片、草藥與針包裹的誇張臉孔。略帶不安的氣氛記錄了一段接納自己的過程。

sections.heading: Skin as Landscape - Making Peace with a Condition
sections.body: Illness is often hidden, yet a condition that marks the skin turns private discomfort into something others can see. This project began from years of living with recurring allergic swelling and chose to face that experience directly instead of concealing it. Mind maps placed bodily symptoms beside the feelings they provoked, from fatigue to embarrassment, and gave the work an honest emotional structure. Clay became the natural medium, soft enough to swell and fold like irritated skin, while needles and dried herbs entered as quiet references to traditional remedies. Early heads in brown and white clay tested how these treatments might sit on a face, piercing it, sprouting from it or settling into its hollows. The guidance encouraged exaggeration as a tool for truth, so the final piece gathers three distorted faces nested in leaves, each turned a different way. A faint sense of unease remains, but it reads as acceptance rather than fear. The work shows how sculpture can transform vulnerability into a calm and courageous statement.

zh-Hant.heading: 如地景的皮膚-與病症和解
zh-Hant.body: 疾病常被隱藏，然而在皮膚上留下印記的病症，會把私密的不適變成別人看得見的事物。這個專題源自多年與反覆發作的過敏紅腫共處的經驗，選擇正面面對而非掩飾。心智圖把身體症狀與其引發的感受並置，從疲憊到尷尬，為作品建立誠實的情感結構。黏土自然成為媒材，它柔軟得能像受刺激的皮膚般腫脹與皺摺，針與乾燥草藥則作為對傳統療法的安靜指涉加入其中。早期以棕色與白色黏土塑成的頭像，測試這些療法如何附著在臉上：刺穿它、從中生長，或沉入它的凹陷。指導鼓勵以誇張作為通往真實的工具，於是最終作品把三張扭曲的臉孔安置在葉片之中，各自朝向不同方向。一絲不安仍然存在，但它被讀作接納而非恐懼。這件作品說明，雕塑能把脆弱轉化為平靜而勇敢的表達。

pins.title: Cozy Island
pins.description:
Long waits outside public restrooms prompt a private island of calm, built as a lit base of foamed PVC rings carrying bent bamboo strips and a lattice of sticks.

Model | Comfort and privacy study | Bamboo cane, sticks, foamed PVC sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 舒適之島
zh-Hant.description:
在公共廁所外的漫長等待催生了一座寧靜的私人之島，以發光的PVC發泡板環形基座承載彎曲的竹條與木棒格架。

模型｜舒適與私密研究｜竹條、木棒、PVC發泡板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Endless queues outside public restrooms revealed how anxious and exposed shared spaces can feel. The project set out to design a private space that brings calm and relaxation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 公共廁所外無盡的排隊，揭示了共享空間可能令人多麼焦慮與暴露。這個專題試圖設計一個能帶來平靜與放鬆的私人空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches of crowded queues recorded the grumbling, fear and insecurity of waiting. A cozy household bathroom was compared with the public one to list the qualities of warmth, brightness and natural softness.
captions: A collage of a cozy household bathroom and its toiletries, compared with the public restroom.
Research into Sou Fujimoto's Envision pavilion and Vo Trong Nghia's bamboo pavilions.
A line drawing of a waiting queue.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 擁擠隊伍的速寫記錄了等待中的抱怨、恐懼與不安。學生把舒適的家用浴室與公共廁所比較，列出溫暖、明亮與自然柔和等特質。
captions: 以溫馨家用浴室與盥洗用品對照公共廁所的拼貼。
研究藤本壯介的 Envision 展亭與武重義的竹構展亭。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Bamboo cane, sticks and foamed PVC sheet were chosen, and the island base was cut as a set of nested rings. Straight sticks formed a rectilinear frame while thin bamboo strips were bent into sweeping curves.
captions: Weaving the stick lattice by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生選用竹條、木棒與PVC發泡板，並把島的基座切成一組相套的圓環。筆直的木棒組成直角框架，細竹條則被彎成舒展的曲線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished island glows from within as curving strips rise over a lattice of sticks. Small figures move between the frames, suggesting a soothing retreat open to anyone.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的島嶼由內部發光，彎曲的竹條在木棒格架上升起。小比例人在框架之間穿行，暗示一處向所有人開放的撫慰之所。

sections.heading: Waiting Turned Inward - A Refuge Grown from Queues
sections.body: Few moments feel as exposed as a long wait in a public corridor, where impatience and unease gather in a single line. This project took that ordinary discomfort seriously and asked what a truly restful room might be. Quick drawings of queues captured grumbling bodies and anxious faces, while a careful comparison with a home bathroom identified the qualities that soothe: warmth, light, natural materials and gentle scent. Rather than redesigning a facility, the student imagined an island, a separate ground set apart from the crowd. Rings cut from foamed sheet established the base, and the guidance encouraged pairing opposite structural characters, so a rigid lattice of sticks was set against bamboo strips bent into long, breathing arcs. Lit from below, the model glows like a lantern, its curves sheltering small figures who wander between frames. The island turns private comfort into a generous public offer. The work shows how close attention to everyday feeling can generate a tender and inventive spatial idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 轉向內在的等待-由隊伍長出的庇護所
zh-Hant.body: 很少有時刻像在公共走廊裡漫長等待那樣令人感到暴露，不耐與不安在同一條隊伍中聚集。這個專題認真看待這種日常的不適，並探問一個真正能讓人休憩的空間會是什麼。隊伍的速寫捕捉了抱怨的身軀與焦慮的臉孔，與家中浴室的細心比較則辨識出撫慰人心的特質：溫暖、光線、自然材料與柔和的氣味。學生沒有重新設計一座設施，而是想像一座島，一片與人群分開的獨立地面。以發泡板切出的圓環構成基座，指導鼓勵讓相反的結構性格並置，於是剛硬的木棒格架與彎成悠長呼吸弧線的竹條相互對照。從下方打光時，模型像燈籠般發亮，曲線庇護著在框架間漫遊的小人物。這座島把私密的舒適轉化為慷慨的公共給予。這件作品說明，對日常感受的細心關注能孕育出溫柔而富創意的空間構想。

pins.title: Street of Endless Stairs
pins.description:
Fragments of a wall plan are built as many small models of random height, combined into an unpredictable cluster and stitched together by winding stairs.

Model | Spatial link study | White board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無盡階梯之街
zh-Hant.description:
一張牆體平面的片段被建成許多高度隨機的小模型，組合為難以預料的群體，再以蜿蜒的階梯縫合起來。

模型｜空間連結研究｜白色板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The street of stairs from above.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A wall plan was taken as raw material, with the height of each piece left to chance. The project asked how the links between such unpredictable spaces could be discovered.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生以一張牆體平面作為原始材料，每個片段的高度交由機遇決定。這個專題探問，如何發現這些難以預料的空間之間的連結。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sections of the plan were extracted and built as a large set of small white models. Each one turned a few lines of wall into a corner, a gate or a room.
captions: The floor plan of Alvar Aalto's Villa Mairea (1939), used as the base for the wall models.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 平面的片段被提取出來，建成一大組白色小模型。每一件都把幾道牆線轉化為一個轉角、一道門或一個房間。
captions: 以阿瓦爾·奧圖 1939 年瑪麗亞別墅的平面圖作為牆體模型的基礎。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two or three small models were combined at a time to test new relationships. The pieces were then stacked and overlapped into a dense, tower-like composition.
captions: Building the combined wall model by hand at the desk.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生每次把兩到三件小模型組合，以測試新的關係。這些構件隨後被堆疊、交疊成一個密集如塔的構成。
captions: 在桌前以手組合牆體模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final street spreads the fragments across a wide base and links them with many stairs. Spiral and winding flights climb between platforms so that every space becomes reachable.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的街道把片段鋪展在寬闊的基座上，並以許多階梯連接起來。螺旋與蜿蜒的梯段在平台之間攀升，讓每個空間都能抵達。

sections.heading: Chance and Connection - Stairs That Bind a City
sections.body: Cities are rarely planned in one gesture; they gather from fragments whose relationships are discovered only later. This project staged that process in miniature. Pieces of a single wall plan were lifted out and built as dozens of small white models, each given a height decided by chance, so that no final shape could be predicted in advance. Photographed one by one, they read as corners, gates and rooms waiting for a context. The guidance encouraged working through combination rather than composition, and the models were paired and tripled, then stacked into a crowded vertical cluster where walls overlap and hover. The decisive step came when the fragments were spread across a broad base and connected by stairs. Spiral flights and long winding runs climb from platform to platform, turning isolated pieces into a continuous and playful street. Small figures pause on landings as if exploring an impossible town. The work shows how chance and patient connection can produce a rich and surprising urban order.

zh-Hant.heading: 機遇與連結-縫合城市的階梯
zh-Hant.body: 城市很少一筆畫成，它們由片段聚集而成，其間的關係往往事後才被發現。這個專題以縮小的尺度上演了這個過程。一張牆體平面的片段被取出，建成數十件白色小模型，每一件的高度都由機遇決定，因此最終的形狀無法事先預料。逐一拍攝時，它們被讀作等待脈絡的轉角、門與房間。指導鼓勵以組合而非構圖來工作，於是模型被兩兩、三三配對，再堆疊成一個牆體交疊、懸浮的擁擠垂直群體。關鍵的一步是把片段鋪展在寬闊的基座上，並以階梯連接。螺旋梯段與蜿蜒長梯從一個平台攀向另一個平台，把孤立的構件變成一條連續而有趣的街道。小人物在梯間平台上駐足，彷彿在探索一座不可能的小鎮。這件作品說明，機遇與耐心的連結能產生豐富而令人驚喜的城市秩序。

pins.title: Stories of the City
pins.description:
The crowded life of an urban village is told through a backlit section model, its stepped floors and stairs set against printed fragments of the streets.

Section model | Urban village study | White board, printed paper, light box | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市的故事
zh-Hant.description:
城中村擁擠的生活透過一座背光剖面模型來講述，階梯狀的樓層與樓梯襯在街道的印刷片段之前。

剖面模型｜城中村研究｜白色板材、印刷紙、燈箱｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A city shaped by waves of newcomers has produced dense urban villages where many lives are packed together. The project asked how the story of that city and its residents could be told through a single section.
captions: Site photos of a crowded urban village: stacked homes and shop signs.
A site photo of residents at work in a narrow lane.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座由一波波新移民塑造的城市，形成了許多人生活緊密相依的城中村。這個專題探問，如何以一個剖面講述這座城市與其居民的故事。
captions: 擁擠城中村的現場照片：層疊住宅與店招。
居民在窄巷中工作的現場照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Reference images and site observations recorded narrow lanes, stacked rooms and steep stairs. These fragments became a backdrop of drawn and printed street scenes.
captions: A reference drawing of a dense walled settlement.
A reference section drawing of packed rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 參考圖像與現場觀察記錄了狹窄的巷弄、堆疊的房間與陡峭的樓梯。這些片段成為由手繪與印刷街景組成的背景。
captions: 密集圍城聚落的參考圖。
擠滿房間的參考剖面圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: White floors and walls were cut and stepped so that every room opens toward the viewer. Small figures were placed on landings and in rooms to suggest daily routines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色的樓板與牆面被切割並錯層排列，讓每個房間都朝觀者敞開。小比例人被放在梯間平台與房間內，暗示日常的作息。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Lit from behind, the section glows like a lantern full of small stories. A second model of white walls in plan reads as the dense street pattern seen from above.
captions: A street model of white walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從背後打光時，剖面像一盞裝滿小故事的燈籠般發亮。另一座由白色牆片構成的平面模型，則被讀作從上方俯視的密集街道紋理。

sections.heading: Lives in Section - Lantern of a Crowded Village
sections.body: Dense neighbourhoods built by newcomers often escape official maps, yet they hold some of the richest stories a city can tell. This project chose the section as its narrative device, slicing through an imagined block so that rooms, corridors and stairways could be read at once like the pages of an open book. Observations of narrow lanes and stacked dwellings were gathered first, and their textures were printed and drawn onto a backdrop that hums with signage, windows and laundry. Over it, white floors step up and down, each room pulled slightly forward so that its interior becomes visible. The guidance encouraged a light hand, so the structure stays thin and the figures small, letting the eye wander from landing to landing as if following neighbours through the day. When the light box behind the model is switched on, the whole section glows, and private spaces turn into a shared lantern. A companion plan model of white walls shows the same density from above. The work shows how a simple cut can give dignity to overlooked urban lives.

zh-Hant.heading: 剖面裡的生活-擁擠村落的燈籠
zh-Hant.body: 由新移民建起的密集街區常常逃離官方地圖，卻承載著一座城市最豐富的故事。這個專題選擇以剖面作為敘事工具，切開一個想像的街廓，讓房間、走廊與樓梯能像攤開的書頁般一次被閱讀。學生先收集對狹窄巷弄與堆疊住宅的觀察，再把它們的質地印製、描繪在一張充滿招牌、窗戶與晾衣的背景上。白色樓板在其上起落，每個房間都被稍稍向前拉出，讓內部得以被看見。指導鼓勵輕盈的手法，於是結構保持纖薄、人物保持細小，讓視線能從一個平台遊移到另一個平台，彷彿跟隨鄰居度過一天。當模型背後的燈箱亮起，整個剖面便發出光來，私密的空間化為一盞共享的燈籠。另一座白色牆片的平面模型則從上方呈現同樣的密度。這件作品說明，一個簡單的剖切能賦予被忽視的城市生活應有的尊嚴。

pins.title: Possibility of Lines
pins.description:
Straight lines drawn by hand are extended into a field of parallel white walls and blocks, lit from below so that the gaps glow like the empty space of an ink painting.

Model | Line and space study | White board, dried branches, light | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 線的可能
zh-Hant.description:
手繪的直線被延伸為一片平行白牆與量體構成的場域，從下方打光，讓縫隙如水墨畫的留白般發亮。

模型｜線與空間研究｜白色板材、乾燥枝條、燈光｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A fascination with geometry led to a simple question about whether space could be built from straight lines alone. The project also asked how such lines might shape the relationship between space and people.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 對幾何的著迷引出一個簡單的問題：空間能否只由直線建構。這個專題也探問，這些線如何塑造空間與人之間的關係。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Rows of wavering lines were drawn by hand and then extended in sketches into walls, rooms and paths. The drawings tested how far a line could stretch before it became a place.
captions: A sketch of lines becoming space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生先以手繪畫出一排排微微顫動的線，再在草圖中把它們延伸為牆、房間與路徑。這些繪圖測試一條線能延伸多遠才會成為一個場所。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Parallel white walls of different heights were set in long rows, with blocks and bridges inserted between them. Small dried branches were added as trees among the corridors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 高低不一的白色平行牆被排成長列，量體與橋被插入其間。小段乾燥枝條則作為樹木加入廊道之中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A light source placed beneath the model turns the gaps between walls into bright voids. Seen from above, the city reads like the deliberate blank of a traditional landscape painting.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 置於模型下方的光源，把牆與牆之間的縫隙變成明亮的虛空。從上方看去，這座城市就像傳統山水畫中刻意的留白。

sections.heading: The Eloquent Blank - Building with Straight Lines
sections.body: A line is the most modest mark a hand can make, yet it already divides the world into here and there. This project took that elementary act and asked whether an entire spatial world could grow from it. Pages of trembling parallel strokes were drawn first, then pushed in sketches until they suggested corridors, rooms and thresholds. The model translated those strokes into long rows of white walls of varying height, punctuated by blocks, bridges and small branches that stand in for trees. The guidance encouraged restraint, so no curve was allowed to interrupt the rule of the straight line, and richness had to come from rhythm, spacing and height alone. The decisive gesture came at the end, when a light was placed beneath the base. The narrow gaps began to glow, and what had been leftover space became the protagonist, recalling the eloquent emptiness of classical ink landscapes. The project quietly reframes void as material. The work shows how disciplined limitation can open a poetic understanding of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 雄辯的留白-以直線築城
zh-Hant.body: 一條線是手所能畫出最謙遜的記號，卻已把世界分成此處與彼處。這個專題從這個最基本的動作出發，探問一整個空間世界能否由它生長出來。學生先畫滿一頁頁顫動的平行筆觸，再在草圖中推演，直到它們暗示出廊道、房間與門檻。模型把這些筆觸轉譯為一列列高低不一的白牆，其間點綴著量體、橋與代表樹木的小枝條。指導鼓勵節制，於是不允許任何曲線打斷直線的規則，豐富性只能來自節奏、間距與高度。決定性的一步出現在最後，當一盞燈被放到基座下方。狹窄的縫隙開始發光，原本剩餘的空間成為主角，令人想起古典水墨山水中雄辯的空白。這個專題靜靜地把虛空重新定義為材料。這件作品說明，嚴謹的限制能開啟對空間富有詩意的理解。

pins.title: Seaweed
pins.description:
The drifting, uncertain movement of seaweed is traced in sketches and rebuilt as twisting frames of thin wooden strips, combined at last into a tall lattice structure.

Model | Natural form study | Wooden strips, board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 海藻
zh-Hant.description:
海藻漂浮而不確定的動態被描繪於草圖中，再以細木條重建為扭轉的框架，最終組合為一座高聳的格架結構。

模型｜自然形態研究｜木條、板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Seaweed floats in water with a movement full of uncertainty. The project asked how that floating form could be expressed through an arrangement of wooden strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 海藻在水中漂浮，動態充滿不確定性。這個專題探問，如何透過木條的排列表達這種漂浮的形態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches followed the way fronds twist, gather and spread apart as they drift. Each gesture was then reduced to a simple frame that could be built from straight strips.
captions: A photo of a kelp forest, the floating seaweed that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖追隨葉片在漂流時扭轉、聚攏與散開的方式。每個姿態隨後被簡化為一個能以直木條建構的簡單框架。
captions: 啟發本案的海藻森林照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Test models twisted a column, lifted a floating frame and folded strips into a bowl. Each experiment explored how rigid pieces could still feel soft and unstable.
captions: Building the final stick frame by hand.
Joining the sticks of the frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 試驗模型扭轉了一根柱體、托起一個漂浮的框架，並把木條摺成一個碗形。每個實驗都探索剛硬的構件如何仍能顯得柔軟而不穩定。
captions: 以手搭建最終的木條框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The test models were combined into a tall lattice that leans and opens like a clump of seaweed. Under strong light its shadows spread across the base like rippling water.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 試驗模型被組合為一座高聳的格架，像一叢海藻般傾斜而舒展。在強光下，它的影子在基座上散開，宛如水波蕩漾。

sections.heading: Rigid Strips, Fluid Motion - The Logic of Drifting
sections.body: Underwater plants never hold still; they bend with every current and leave no fixed outline behind. This project accepted the paradox of trying to capture such restlessness with the stiffest of materials, thin straight strips of wood. Sketches first studied how fronds twist around one another, fan out and gather again, and each movement was translated into a frame of short members joined at shifting angles. The guidance encouraged building many small tests rather than one decisive object, so a twisted column, a lifted platform, a folded wave and a cradle-like bowl were made in turn, each probing how rigidity might still convey softness. Combined, these fragments grew into a tall lattice that leans, splits and opens as though swaying in a current. Its density changes from tight knots to open webs, and under a strong light the shadows ripple across the base like water. The finished structure feels alive without imitating any plant literally. The work shows how patient abstraction can turn natural motion into convincing spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 剛硬木條、流動姿態-漂流的邏輯
zh-Hant.body: 水下植物從不靜止，它們隨每一道水流彎曲，不留下固定的輪廓。這個專題接受了一個矛盾：試圖以最剛硬的材料，也就是細直的木條，捕捉這種躁動。草圖先研究葉片如何彼此纏繞、展開又再聚攏，每一種動態都被轉譯為由短構件以變化角度接合的框架。指導鼓勵製作許多小試驗而非一件決定性的物件，於是扭轉的柱體、托起的平台、摺疊的波浪與搖籃般的碗形依序被製作出來，每一件都探問剛性如何仍能傳達柔軟。這些片段組合後長成一座高聳的格架，它傾斜、分岔、舒展，彷彿在水流中搖曳。它的密度從緊密的結點變化到開放的網絡，在強光下，影子像水一般在基座上蕩漾。完成的結構顯得生機盎然，卻沒有字面地模仿任何植物。這件作品說明，耐心的抽象能把自然的動態轉化為具說服力的空間形態。

pins.title: Steampunk City
pins.description:
Imagined machines of pipes, gears and arms are drawn as engineering-style studies and then modelled digitally, turning flat drawings into a three-dimensional mechanical city.

Drawing and digital model | Speculative architecture study | Pen, digital modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 蒸汽龐克之城
zh-Hant.description:
由管線、齒輪與機械臂組成的想像機器被畫成工程風格的研究圖，再以數位建模，把平面繪圖轉化為立體的機械之城。

繪圖與數位模型｜思辨建築研究｜鋼筆、數位建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Visionary architectural drawings of fantastic structures inspired a wish to build an imagined city of machines. The project asked how such a city could move from the page into three dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 描繪奇幻結構的前衛建築繪圖，激發了建造一座想像機器之城的願望。這個專題探問，這樣的城市如何從紙面走進三維空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Engineering drawings and mechanical structures were studied as a vocabulary of parts. Pipes, wheels, clamps and arms were collected as pieces that could be assembled into buildings.
captions: Artworks by Lebbeus Woods that inspired the mechanical city.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 工程圖與機械結構被當作一套構件語彙來研究。管線、輪子、夾具與機械臂被收集為可以組裝成建築的部件。
captions: 啟發這座機械城市的 Lebbeus Woods 作品。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Large drawings assembled these parts into a radiating tower and a tall vertical machine. Smaller studies tested arms, claws and gears as separate components.
captions: A drawing study of an arm.
A drawing study of a claw.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 大幅繪圖把這些部件組成一座放射狀的塔與一部高聳的垂直機器。較小的研究則把機械臂、爪與齒輪作為獨立構件來測試。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The drawings were modelled on the computer to convert the two-dimensional images into space. The resulting forms show the tower, the arm and a platform as solid machine-buildings.
captions: The digital model of the tower.
The digital model of the arm.
The digital model of a platform.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些繪圖在電腦上被建模，把二維圖像轉化為空間。所得的形體把塔、機械臂與平台呈現為實體的機器建築。

sections.heading: Machines for Dwelling - Drawing a Mechanical Utopia
sections.body: Architecture has long dreamed in drawings before it builds in stone, and some of its boldest visions exist only on paper. This project entered that tradition by imagining a city assembled from the parts of machines. Engineering drawings were studied as a grammar of pipes, wheels, clamps and articulated arms, and these elements were recombined into fantastic structures that bristle, rotate and reach. A radiating tower sprouts cannon-like tubes from a stepped base, while a tall vertical machine stacks gears and housings into something between an engine and a building. Smaller sheets isolate single components, testing how an arm folds or how a claw grips. The guidance encouraged treating the drawings not as illustrations but as plans for construction, so each was rebuilt digitally, turning flat line work into volumes that cast shadows and occupy space. The resulting models remain strange and speculative, yet they gain weight and plausibility. The project embraces imagination as a serious design method. The work shows how drawing and modelling together can give form to visionary ideas.

zh-Hant.heading: 可棲居的機器-描繪機械烏托邦
zh-Hant.body: 建築在以石頭建造之前，長久以來先在繪圖中做夢，其中一些最大膽的願景只存在於紙上。這個專題走進這個傳統，想像一座由機器零件組裝而成的城市。工程圖被當作一套由管線、輪子、夾具與關節臂構成的文法來研究，這些元素被重新組合為鋒芒畢露、旋轉而伸展的奇幻結構。一座放射狀的塔從階梯狀的基座伸出如砲管般的管子，一部高聳的垂直機器則把齒輪與外殼堆疊成介於引擎與建築之間的存在。較小的圖紙分離出單一構件，測試一隻手臂如何摺起，或一隻爪如何抓握。指導鼓勵把繪圖當作建造的平面而非插畫，於是每一張都以數位方式重建，把平面線稿化為會投下陰影、佔據空間的量體。所得的模型仍然奇特而具思辨性，卻獲得了重量與可信度。這個專題把想像力視為嚴肅的設計方法。這件作品說明，繪圖與建模的結合能為前衛的構想賦予形體。

pins.title: The Racket Space
pins.description:
The shadow of a racket net cast by the sun is twisted, sketched and rebuilt in cardboard as looping triangulated shells that throw new patterns of light.

Model | Shadow and form study | Cardboard, racket frame and strings | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 球拍的空間
zh-Hant.description:
陽光穿過球拍網投下的影子被扭轉、描繪，再以紙板重建為迴旋的三角網格殼體，投射出新的光影圖案。

模型｜光影與形態研究｜紙板、球拍框與網線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The twisted net and its shadow.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Swinging a racket in the sun cast a shadow of the net onto the ground. The project asked whether that fleeting pattern could be twisted into a new spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在陽光下揮動球拍時，網的影子投在地面上。這個專題探問，這個轉瞬即逝的圖案能否被扭轉為新的空間形態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches twisted the net and traced the distorted shadows it might cast under light. A real racket frame was cut and reshaped with its strings to test the twist in three dimensions.
captions: Cutting the racket net and reshaping its frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖扭轉網面，並描繪它在光下可能投出的變形影子。學生把一支真正的球拍框切開，連同網線重新塑形，以在三維中測試扭轉。
captions: 剪開球拍網線並重塑框架。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The twisted shape was restored in cardboard, first as a simple looping band. Triangular openings were then cut into the band to recreate the pattern of the net.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 扭轉的形狀以紙板還原，起初只是一條簡單的迴旋帶。接著在帶上切出三角形開口，重現網的圖案。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Two final models curl through space as perforated shells. Lit again from one side, they cast large net-like shadows that complete the space created by the racket.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩件最終模型以穿孔殼體的形式在空間中捲曲。再次從一側打光時，它們投下巨大的網狀影子，完成了由球拍創造的空間。

sections.heading: Shadow into Shelter - Space Spun from a Swing
sections.body: Moments of play often contain unnoticed spatial lessons, and a single swing in the sun can reveal how light, mesh and ground interact. This project caught such a moment when the shadow of a racket net stretched across the court, and it refused to let the image fade. Sketches bent and twisted the net, imagining the distorted patterns it might cast, while a real frame was cut and reshaped with its strings to test the idea in three dimensions. The guidance encouraged moving back and forth between object, drawing and light, so every step was checked against a new shadow. Cardboard then took over: a simple looping band became a shell, and triangular openings were cut into its surface to rebuild the logic of the mesh. In the final pair of models the shells curl and overlap, and when a lamp is placed beside them they project enormous lattices onto the table, turning a fleeting pattern into an enclosing presence. The work shows how attentive play can lead to inventive and rigorous spatial thinking.

zh-Hant.heading: 由影成殼-揮拍中旋出的空間
zh-Hant.body: 遊戲的片刻常常蘊含未被察覺的空間課題，陽光下的一次揮拍就能揭示光、網與地面如何相互作用。這個專題捕捉了這樣的時刻：球拍網的影子在場地上延展，而學生不願讓這個畫面消散。草圖彎曲、扭轉網面，想像它可能投出的變形圖案，同時一支真正的球拍框連同網線被切開、重新塑形，以在三維中測試這個想法。指導鼓勵在物件、繪圖與光之間來回往返，於是每一步都以新的影子來檢驗。接著由紙板接手：一條簡單的迴旋帶成為殼體，表面切出三角形開口，重建網的邏輯。在最終的兩件模型中，殼體捲曲而交疊，當一盞燈放在旁邊時，它們在桌上投射出巨大的格網，把轉瞬即逝的圖案變成包覆的存在。這件作品說明，專注的遊戲能引出富創意而嚴謹的空間思考。

pins.title: Domes and Spires
pins.description:
Scenes of a vast imagined world are reinterpreted as a tall white tower of foam domes, Gothic spires, rock-like masses and floating stairs.

Model | Imagined architecture study | Foam, white board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 穹頂與尖塔
zh-Hant.description:
一個廣闊想像世界的場景被重新詮釋為一座白色高塔，由泡棉穹頂、哥德式尖塔、如岩石的量體與漂浮的階梯組成。

模型｜想像建築研究｜泡棉、白色板材、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower of domes and spires.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A fantasy world whose buildings span many eras and regions arranged them together in a surprisingly clever way. The project set out to restore some of those scenes through a personal understanding of their space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個奇幻世界的建築跨越許多時代與地域，卻以出人意料的巧妙方式排列在一起。這個專題試圖以個人對其空間的理解，重現其中一些場景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Concept sketches drew twisting ribbons, branching towers, spired halls and rocky shells. Each sketch isolated one architectural character to be built as a fragment.
captions: A collage of game scenes, ruins and arches that inspired the tower.
More game scenes with domes, cliffs and Gothic details.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 概念草圖畫出扭轉的帶狀物、分岔的塔、有尖塔的廳堂與岩石般的殼體。每張草圖都分離出一種建築性格，作為片段來建造。
captions: 啟發這座塔的遊戲場景、廢墟與拱的拼貼。
更多帶有穹頂、懸崖與哥德式細節的遊戲場景。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Fragments were modelled one by one, from curved white walls and timber stick grids to spired halls. Foam domes on slender stalks and carved rock-like masses completed the set.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 片段被逐一製作，從彎曲的白牆、木棒格架到帶尖塔的廳堂。細柄上的泡棉穹頂與雕刻出的岩石量體完成了整組構件。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The fragments were stacked into one tower about eighty centimetres high. Domes bristling with spikes, a stair winding between them and a stick scaffold at the base create a layered world of different eras.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些片段被堆疊成一座約八十公分高的塔。佈滿尖刺的穹頂、蜿蜒其間的階梯與基部的木棒鷹架，共同構成一個疊合不同時代的層次世界。

sections.heading: Eras in One Column - A Vertical Collage of Worlds
sections.body: Imagined worlds can teach real lessons about how buildings from different times might share a single ground. This project began from admiration for such a world, where halls, ruins and towers of many styles are woven together, and sought to restore its spirit through personal interpretation rather than copying. Sketches separated distinct architectural characters, from ribbons and branching towers to spired halls and rocky shells, so that each could be explored on its own terms. The guidance encouraged building fragments before composing them, and a family of studies followed: curving white walls, timber scaffolds, spired blocks, domes on slender stalks and carved masses that look weathered by time. These pieces were then piled into a single column almost a metre tall. Domes bristling with thin spikes hover over a stair that winds between them, while a stick framework at the base suggests construction still in progress. The tower reads as a vertical collage of eras held together by circulation. The work shows how imaginative reference can mature into confident compositional skill.

zh-Hant.heading: 一柱千年-世界的垂直拼貼
zh-Hant.body: 想像的世界能教人真實的課題：不同時代的建築如何共享同一片地面。這個專題源自對這樣一個世界的欣賞，其中各種風格的廳堂、廢墟與塔被編織在一起，學生試圖透過個人詮釋而非複製來重現它的精神。草圖分離出各具特色的建築性格，從帶狀物、分岔的塔到有尖塔的廳堂與岩石般的殼體，讓每一種都能依其自身的邏輯被探索。指導鼓勵先建造片段再進行構成，於是一系列研究隨之而來：彎曲的白牆、木棒鷹架、帶尖塔的量體、細柄上的穹頂，以及彷彿被時間風化的雕刻量體。這些構件隨後被堆疊成一根將近一公尺高的柱體。佈滿細刺的穹頂懸浮在蜿蜒其間的階梯之上，基部的木棒框架則暗示著仍在進行的建造。這座塔被讀作一幅以動線串連起來的時代垂直拼貼。這件作品說明，富有想像力的參照能成熟為自信的構成能力。

pins.title: The Blue Channel
pins.description:
The distance felt between oneself and others becomes a life-size channel of layered white panels and yellow strips, guarded by a dark crumpled mass.

Installation | Personal distance study | Foam board, yellow tape, black plastic, cable ties | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 藍色通道
zh-Hant.description:
自己與他人之間感受到的距離，成為一條由層疊白色板片與黃色條帶構成、由一團深色皺褶量體守護的實尺寸通道。

裝置｜人際距離研究｜泡棉板、黃色膠帶、黑色塑膠、束線帶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The space that arises when one person interacts with others is rarely visible but strongly felt. The project set out to represent that distance as a space that could actually be entered.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個人與他人互動時產生的空間很少被看見，卻能被強烈感受。這個專題試圖把這段距離表現為一個真正可以走進去的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Photographs of daily scenes were taken to compare different perspectives between oneself and others. Collages and idea drafts paired soft barriers with sharp black forms to express openness and fear.
captions: Personal photographs of everyday scenes that express distance and the idea of a channel.
An inspiration collage of danger, difference and struggle.
A collage of mirror refraction, distorted images and dark colours.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生拍攝日常場景的照片，以比較自己與他人之間的不同視角。拼貼與構想草稿把柔軟的屏障與尖銳的黑色形體配對，表達開放與恐懼。
captions: 表達距離與「通道」概念的日常場景個人攝影。
以危險、差異與掙扎為題的靈感拼貼。
以鏡面折射、扭曲影像與暗色為題的拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
