sections.body: Two small models were designed and assembled to test the idea, from a timber frame with hanging forms to a box of layered boards. The stronger version, with black pieces piercing a white shell, was chosen for full-size construction.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生設計並組裝兩件小模型來測試構想，從懸掛形體的木框到層疊板片的盒子。較具力量的版本，即黑色構件刺穿白色殼體的那一件，被選為實尺寸建造的方案。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished channel stands one metre eighty high so that visitors can step inside. Layers of white panels crossed by yellow strips open onto a dark crumpled mass that marks the edge of comfort.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的通道高一百八十公分，讓參觀者能走進其中。層層白色板片被黃色條帶交錯，通向一團標示舒適邊界的深色皺褶量體。
captions: 站在等身尺度的通道之中。

sections.heading: Measured Closeness - Walking Through the Gap Between People
sections.body: Every encounter carries an invisible measure, the distance at which another person feels welcome or intrusive. This project tried to give that unspoken measure a body that could be walked through. It began with everyday photographs taken from different vantage points, comparing what it means to look out at others and to be looked at in turn. Collages and idea drafts then paired yielding white layers with sharp, crumpled black forms, a visual language for openness and apprehension. The guidance encouraged testing alternatives before committing, so two small models were made, one a timber frame hung with fragments and one a box of stacked boards, and the more intense version was taken forward. Built at life size, the channel rises well above head height, its layered panels bound by bright yellow strips that zigzag like nervous handwriting. Beside it a mass of black plastic gathers like a storm. Entering the passage, the visitor feels both sheltered and watched. The work shows how a deeply personal theme can become an immersive and generous spatial experience.

zh-Hant.heading: 丈量的親近-走過人與人之間的縫隙
zh-Hant.body: 每一次相遇都帶著一把看不見的尺，衡量他人在什麼距離下令人感到歡迎或侵擾。這個專題試圖為這把未曾言說的尺賦予一個可以走過的形體。它從不同視角拍攝的日常照片開始，比較向外望向他人與反過來被注視的意義。拼貼與構想草稿接著把柔順的白色層次與尖銳、皺褶的黑色形體配對，形成一種表達開放與憂懼的視覺語言。指導鼓勵在定案前測試不同方案，於是學生製作了兩件小模型，一件是懸掛碎片的木框，一件是層疊板材的盒子，並選擇更具張力的版本繼續發展。以實尺寸建造的通道遠高於頭頂，層疊的板片被鮮黃色條帶綁住，像緊張的筆跡般曲折。一旁的黑色塑膠團塊如風暴般聚集。走進通道的人同時感到被庇護與被注視。這件作品說明，一個極為私人的主題能成為沉浸而慷慨的空間經驗。

pins.title: Timber Stands
pins.description:
The character of a football stadium is reinterpreted as a faceted structure of thin timber sticks and translucent paper panels, exploring new spaces for its tiers of seats.

Model | Stadium space study | Timber sticks, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 木構看台
zh-Hant.description:
一座足球場的特質被重新詮釋為由細木棒與半透明紙板構成的多面結構，探索其看台座席的新空間。

模型｜球場空間研究｜木棒、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A much-loved football stadium inspired a wish to understand what gives such a place its character. The project set out to restore that character with different materials and to improve the existing space in a personal way.
captions: Photos of Old Trafford, the football stadium that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座深受喜愛的足球場激發了理解其特質來源的願望。這個專題試圖以不同材料重現這種特質，並以個人的方式改善既有空間。
captions: 啟發本案的足球場老特拉福球場照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings studied the sweep of seating tiers and the steel frames that hold up the roof. A quick sketch reduced these elements to a few folded planes.
captions: A concept sketch of the stands.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 繪圖研究了看台座席的弧線與支撐屋頂的鋼構架。一張快速草圖把這些元素簡化為幾個摺疊的平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Thin timber sticks were joined into triangulated frames that twist and cantilever in many directions. Translucent paper panels were set into some of the frames to suggest seating and shelter.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 細木棒被接合為向各個方向扭轉與懸挑的三角框架。半透明紙板被嵌入部分框架中，暗示座席與遮蔽。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a faceted cluster that reads as both a grandstand and a sculpture. Seen from different sides, its paper planes and sticks cast intricate shadows across the ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型升起為一個多面的群體，既可被讀作大看台，也可被讀作雕塑。從不同側面觀看時，紙面與木棒在地面上投下錯綜的影子。

sections.heading: Roar in Timber - Reimagining the Grandstand
sections.body: Stadiums are among the most emotional buildings a city possesses, holding the collective breath of thousands at once. This project grew from devotion to one such ground and asked what makes its atmosphere so powerful, and how that atmosphere might be rebuilt in a lighter, more experimental language. Drawings traced the sweep of seating tiers and the frames that carry the roof, and a rapid sketch distilled them into a few folded planes leaning toward a shared centre. The guidance encouraged replacing heavy steel with delicate means, so thin timber sticks were joined into triangulated frames that twist, cantilever and stack, while translucent paper panels slip into some cells to suggest seating, shade and enclosure. The final model rises as a faceted cluster that belongs somewhere between grandstand and sculpture, and when light strikes it, a dense web of shadow spills across the ground. Familiar devotion becomes the engine of spatial invention. The work shows how a personal passion can be translated into rigorous structural and spatial exploration.

zh-Hant.heading: 木頭裡的歡呼-重新想像大看台
zh-Hant.body: 球場是一座城市最富情感的建築之一，同時承載著成千上萬人的集體呼吸。這個專題源自對其中一座球場的熱愛，探問是什麼讓它的氛圍如此強大，以及這種氛圍如何能以更輕盈、更具實驗性的語言重建。繪圖描繪看台座席的弧線與承托屋頂的構架，一張快速的草圖則把它們提煉為幾個傾向共同中心的摺疊平面。指導鼓勵以纖細的手段取代沉重的鋼材，於是細木棒被接合為扭轉、懸挑與堆疊的三角框架，半透明的紙板滑入部分格子，暗示座席、遮陽與圍合。最終模型升起為一個多面的群體，介於大看台與雕塑之間，當光線照在其上，一張綿密的陰影之網便灑落在地面。熟悉的熱愛成為空間創造的動力。這件作品說明，個人的熱情能被轉譯為嚴謹的結構與空間探索。

pins.title: The Beacon
pins.description:
A dismantled desk lamp is first staged as an old harbour crane and then reinvented as a timber beacon whose white triangular blades fold, lift and turn toward the sun.

Model | Object deconstruction study | Desk lamp parts, timber sticks, white board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 燈塔
zh-Hant.description:
一盞被拆解的檯燈先被布置成舊港口的起重機，再被重新發明為一座木構燈塔，白色三角葉片可摺疊、升起並轉向太陽。

模型｜物件解構研究｜檯燈零件、木棒、白色板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The movable joints and arms of a desk lamp suggested a structure that could become something else entirely. The project asked how a familiar object might be taken apart and turned into a new spatial device.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 檯燈可活動的關節與臂桿，暗示了一種能完全變成別的東西的結構。這個專題探問，一件熟悉的物件如何被拆開，並轉化為新的空間裝置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The lamp was dismantled piece by piece and every component was drawn as a reference. A short survey of lamps through history traced how containers for light changed from enclosed shapes to adjustable arms.
captions: A timeline of lamps, from early oil lamps and red lanterns to the hurricane lamp and modern desk lamps.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把檯燈逐件拆解，並把每個零件畫下作為參考。一段關於燈具歷史的簡短整理，追溯了盛裝光的容器如何從封閉的形體演變為可調整的臂桿。
captions: 燈具的時間軸：從早期油燈、紅燈籠到防風燈與現代檯燈。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In a first scene the lamp became an old crane in an abandoned harbour, converted into a small hotel and visited by tiny figures. Sketches then imagined a beacon whose blades open toward the sun by day and close together at night.
captions: Taking a desk lamp apart by hand to study its moving joints.
A sketch of the beacon blades.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在第一個場景中，檯燈成為廢棄港口裡的一座舊起重機，被改造成小旅館，並有小比例人在其間走動。草圖接著想像一座燈塔，其葉片白天朝太陽展開，夜晚則合攏在一起。
captions: 以手拆解檯燈，研究其可動關節。
帶有人物的起重機場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final timber beacon carries removable white triangles that fold and match with one another, while its platform can be lifted. Three configurations show it working as a lighthouse, absorbing solar energy and resting when not in use.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的木構燈塔帶有可拆卸的白色三角片，能彼此摺疊與拼合，平台也可以升起。三種組態分別展示它作為燈塔運作、吸收太陽能，以及停用時休息的狀態。

sections.heading: Joints That Remember Light - From Desk Lamp to Beacon
sections.body: An ordinary desk lamp is already a small piece of architecture, with a base, a column, articulated arms and a shade that frames light. This project began by taking such a lamp apart with patience, laying out springs, screws and hinges and drawing each one so that its logic could be understood rather than merely admired. Reassembled on a white stage, the fragments became a weathered harbour crane converted into a modest hotel, where miniature visitors wander between arm and base. The guidance encouraged pushing beyond representation toward invention, so sketches imagined a beacon whose blades behave like leaves, opening to catch the sun during the day and folding together after dark. The final timber tower answers that idea with removable white triangles mounted on slender frames, a lifting platform and crossed legs that steady the whole. Shown as a lighthouse, a solar collector and a dormant object, the same structure performs three roles. The work shows how careful dismantling can turn a domestic object into an inventive and adaptable architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 記得光的關節-從檯燈到燈塔
zh-Hant.body: 一盞普通的檯燈本身已是一件小小的建築，具備基座、立柱、關節臂與框住光線的燈罩。這個專題從耐心拆解這樣一盞燈開始，把彈簧、螺絲與鉸鏈逐一攤開並描繪下來，讓其邏輯被理解，而不只是被欣賞。在白色的舞台上重新組合後，這些碎片成為一座飽經風霜、被改造成樸素旅館的港口起重機，微小的訪客在臂桿與基座之間漫遊。指導鼓勵從再現邁向發明，於是草圖想像出一座燈塔，其葉片如樹葉般運作，白天展開以承接陽光，入夜後則收攏在一起。最終的木構塔以安裝於纖細框架上的可拆卸白色三角片、可升降的平台與穩定整體的交叉支腳回應這個構想。同一座結構分別以燈塔、太陽能收集器與靜止物件的姿態，扮演三種角色。這件作品說明，細心的拆解能把家居物件轉化為富有創意且可變的建築。

pins.title: Human and Nature
pins.description:
The conflict between nature and people is expressed through bare branches wrapped in wire and pierced by curled sheets of metal, set on small concrete blocks.

Sculpture | Nature and human conflict study | Branches, metal sheet, wire, concrete | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 人與自然
zh-Hant.description:
自然與人之間的衝突，透過纏繞鐵絲、被捲曲金屬片刺穿的枯枝來表達，並安置在小小的混凝土塊上。

雕塑｜自然與人類衝突研究｜樹枝、金屬片、鐵絲、混凝土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The branch and metal final piece.
樹枝與金屬的最終作品。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project questioned the familiar idea that people must protect the planet, suggesting instead that nature can thrive without humans and may fight back when mistreated. It asked how this tension between the two could be made visible.
captions: A collage of nature taking back a ruined city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題質疑人類必須保護地球這個常見的觀念，轉而提出自然沒有人類也能繁盛，並可能在受到傷害時反擊。它探問，兩者之間的這種張力如何能被看見。
captions: 大自然收復廢墟城市的拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Brainstorming sketches drew trees whose roots and trunks were bound, cased or pierced by manufactured materials. Studies of artworks that combine conflicting materials suggested ways to make them coexist uneasily.
captions: Artist research on the works of Jackie Brown and JC Ruggirello.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 腦力激盪的草圖描繪了根與樹幹被人造材料綑綁、包覆或刺穿的樹木。對結合衝突材料的藝術作品的研究，提示了讓它們不安地共存的方式。
captions: 對 Jackie Brown 與 JC Ruggirello 作品的藝術家研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Short sticks were combined with curled sheets of thin metal to test how hard industrial edges sit against bark. Long branches were then wrapped with loose coils of wire that cling to them like a net.
captions: Wrapping wire around branches and setting the base by hand.
A test of sticks and metal.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生把短木棒與捲曲的薄金屬片結合，測試堅硬的工業邊緣如何與樹皮並置。接著以鬆散的鐵絲圈纏繞長枝條，讓鐵絲像網一樣附著在枝條上。
captions: 以手將鐵絲纏繞樹枝並製作底座。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final pieces bundle branches, metal and wire into bursts and stems that rise from small concrete blocks. Each one shows nature and human material fighting for their own space within a single form.
captions: Two stems as a final piece.
A dense crown in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終作品把樹枝、金屬與鐵絲束成爆發狀與莖幹狀的形體，從小小的混凝土塊上升起。每一件都在單一形體中呈現自然與人造材料為各自的空間而角力。
captions: 枝條爆發狀的最終作品。

sections.heading: Bark Against Steel - Sculptures of an Uneasy Truce
sections.body: The language of environmental care often casts people as guardians and nature as a fragile ward, yet storms, floods and fires suggest a far less tidy relationship. This project turned that assumption around, proposing that the natural world does not need rescue so much as respect, and that it can strike back when pushed too far. Brainstorming sketches imagined trees bound in casings, roots tangled with rods and trunks pierced by manufactured pieces. Material tests followed, setting curled sheets of thin metal against short sticks and wrapping long branches in loose coils of wire. The guidance encouraged letting the materials argue rather than blend, so the bark stays rough, the metal stays sharp and the wire never quite settles. In the final series, bundles of twigs erupt from small concrete blocks, some bristling outward, others clenched into dark stems with shards of metal caught inside. Viewed together, they read like a field of wounded yet defiant plants. The work shows how simple found materials can carry a serious and provocative environmental argument.

zh-Hant.heading: 樹皮對抗鋼鐵-不安休戰的雕塑
zh-Hant.body: 環境關懷的語言常把人類描繪成守護者，把自然描繪成脆弱的被保護者，然而風暴、洪水與野火都暗示著一種遠不那麼工整的關係。這個專題翻轉了這個假設，提出自然世界需要的與其說是拯救，不如說是尊重，而且在被逼得太過時它會反擊。腦力激盪的草圖想像出被外殼綑住的樹、與桿件糾纏的根，以及被人造構件刺穿的樹幹。材料試驗隨之而來，把捲曲的薄金屬片與短木棒並置，並以鬆散的鐵絲圈纏繞長枝條。指導鼓勵讓材料彼此爭辯而非融合，於是樹皮保持粗糙、金屬保持鋒利，鐵絲也從未真正安定。在最終系列中，一束束細枝從小混凝土塊中迸發，有的向外張揚，有的緊握成深色莖幹，金屬碎片卡在其中。放在一起觀看時，它們像一片受傷卻不屈的植物原野。這件作品說明，簡單的現成材料也能承載嚴肅而具挑釁性的環境論述。

pins.title: The Layout of a Food Market
pins.description:
Field observation of a busy food market leads to a new layout of L-shaped counter units, tested in many arrangements and set inside a timber frame with a domed centre.

Model | Market layout study | White board, foam, cardboard, timber sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 菜市場的佈局
zh-Hant.description:
對一座繁忙菜市場的實地觀察，引出一種由L形攤位單元構成的新佈局，經過多種排列測試後，被安置在一個中央有穹頂的木框架內。

模型｜市場佈局研究｜白色板材、泡棉、紙板、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Online shopping is changing where people buy food, yet the traditional market remains a lively everyday place. The project asked how the layout of such a market could be improved to serve both stallholders and shoppers.
captions: A collage of shoppers and stalls in today's food markets.
Field photos of the existing market hall.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 網路購物正在改變人們購買食物的地方，然而傳統市場依然是充滿生氣的日常場所。這個專題探問，如何改善這類市場的佈局，以同時服務攤商與顧客。
captions: 現今菜市場中顧客與攤位的拼貼。
現有市場大廳的田野調查照片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Field research mapped the stalls and found two main problems in the existing hall. The smell of the seafood counters reached the cooked-food area, and the meat aisle was so wide that stallholders drifted to other counters to chat.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 實地調查繪製了攤位分布，並發現既有市場的兩個主要問題。海鮮攤的氣味會影響熟食區，而肉品通道過寬，使攤商常常移到別的攤位聊天。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Perspective sketches imagined a new hall with clearer aisles and a central gathering space. L-shaped counter units were then made and tested in several arrangements to choose the most effective layout.
captions: Sketches of the market streets and shop signs drawn before the design.
A sketch of the hall interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 透視草圖想像出一座通道更清楚、中央設有聚集空間的新市場。接著學生製作L形的攤位單元，並以多種排列方式測試，選出最有效的佈局。
captions: 設計前繪製的市場街道與店招草圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three layers of foam simulate the different floor levels, and cardboard stores with varied roofs line the aisles. The whole market is enclosed by a thin timber frame with a dome over its centre.
captions: Scenes of the market model with cut-out figures of shoppers and stall owners.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三層泡棉模擬不同的樓層高度，紙板製作的商店以多樣的屋頂排列在通道兩旁。整座市場由纖細的木框架包圍，中央覆蓋著一座穹頂。
captions: 放入顧客與攤主剪影人物的市場模型場景。

sections.heading: Aisles of Daily Life - Reordering the Market Hall
sections.body: Food markets are among the most democratic rooms a city offers, yet their layouts often grow by accident rather than design. This project looked closely at one busy hall, recording where people queue, where odours travel and where stallholders gather when trade is slow. Two problems emerged clearly from the mapping: strong smells from seafood counters drifting into areas for cooked food, and an aisle so generous that it emptied of purpose. Perspective sketches then imagined a calmer hall organised around a central gathering place. The guidance encouraged testing rather than guessing, so a family of small L-shaped counters was cut from white board and arranged again and again, each version photographed and compared. The chosen pattern was built at a larger scale, with stepped foam floors, cardboard stores crowned by varied roofs and a slender timber frame that encloses everything beneath a light dome. The result keeps the bustle of the market while giving its circulation clarity and rhythm. The work shows how patient observation can lead to practical and humane spatial design.

zh-Hant.heading: 日常的通道-重整市場大廳
zh-Hant.body: 菜市場是一座城市所能提供最平等的空間之一，然而它的佈局往往是意外生長而成，而非經過設計。這個專題仔細觀察一座繁忙的市場，記錄人們在哪裡排隊、氣味往哪裡飄散，以及生意清淡時攤商在哪裡聚集。調查清楚地浮現出兩個問題：海鮮攤的強烈氣味飄進熟食區，以及一條寬闊得失去用途的通道。透視草圖接著想像出一座圍繞中央聚集場所組織的、更從容的市場。指導鼓勵以測試取代猜測，於是一系列小型L形攤位從白色板材裁出，被一次又一次地排列，每個版本都被拍照並比較。選定的佈局以更大的比例建造，有階梯狀的泡棉樓板、頂著多樣屋頂的紙板商店，以及在一座輕巧穹頂下包覆一切的纖細木框架。成果保留了市場的熱鬧，同時賦予其動線清晰與節奏。這件作品說明，耐心的觀察能引出務實而富人情味的空間設計。

pins.title: Space and Texture
pins.description:
Three short studies explore texture and space, from cut and lifted cardboard and a cement slab that looks soft, to contorted triangle frames and a city of small wall units.

Models | Space and texture studies | Cardboard, cement, wooden sticks, paper, white board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間與質地
zh-Hant.description:
三個短篇研究探索質地與空間，從切割並翹起的紙板、看似柔軟的水泥板，到扭曲的三角框架與由小牆片單元構成的城市。

模型｜空間與質地研究｜紙板、水泥、木棒、紙、白色板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how a flat image or a single material could gain depth and become space. It also asked how texture, light and shadow could be shaped by simple geometric means.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，一張平面圖像或單一材料如何能獲得深度並成為空間。它也探問，質地、光與影如何能以簡單的幾何手法塑造。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A dense drawing of an imagined city was remade on cardboard and cut so that fragments could stand up. A landscape outline was then redrawn entirely in triangles to turn natural contours into simple geometry.
captions: City photos and a street sketch made from them, the starting point of part one.
A landscape photo from a trip, traced into triangles for part two.
Plans and models of the villa case study whose walls were taken apart in part three.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張密集的想像城市繪圖被重製在紙板上，並經切割讓碎片能夠立起。接著學生把一段地景輪廓完全以三角形重新描繪，把自然的輪廓轉為簡單的幾何。
captions: 城市照片與據此繪製的街景草圖，為第一部分的起點。
旅途中拍攝的風景照，在第二部分被描成三角形。
第三部分拆解其牆體的別墅案例平面與模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A cement slab was cast to look soft and crumpled, although it is completely stiff. Thin sticks and paper were joined into triangle frames that twist into a posture resembling a coiling creature.
captions: Pouring cement into the mould by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生澆鑄了一塊看似柔軟而皺褶的水泥板，實際上卻完全堅硬。細木棒與紙被接合成三角框架，扭轉成類似盤繞生物的姿態。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A field of small and large triangles cast changing patterns of light and shadow. Freestanding wall units extracted from a house plan were rearranged into a model that reads like a small city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一片大小不一的三角形投下變化的光影圖案。從一座住宅平面中抽取出的獨立牆片單元，被重新排列成一個像小城市般的模型。

sections.heading: Folds of Surface - Three Lessons in Texture and Space
sections.body: Texture is usually treated as a finish applied at the end, but it can also be the very origin of space. This project gathered three short studies that each begin from a surface and ask how depth might emerge from it. In the first, a crowded drawing of an imagined city was transferred to cardboard and cut so that its fragments could lift and stand, turning an image into a shallow relief. In the second, a landscape outline was translated into triangles and cast as a cement slab that appears soft and crumpled yet is entirely rigid, a quiet contradiction between look and touch. The guidance encouraged moving freely between drawing, casting and building, so the third study joined sticks and paper into triangulated frames that coil like a creature, alongside a sheet of triangles that throws shifting shadows. Finally, wall units drawn from a house plan were scattered and regrouped into a miniature city. The work shows how attention to surface can open unexpected and rigorous spatial possibilities.

zh-Hant.heading: 表面的皺褶-質地與空間的三堂課
zh-Hant.body: 質地通常被當作最後才施加的表面處理，但它也可以是空間的起源。這個專題集合了三個短篇研究，每一個都從一個表面出發，探問深度如何從中浮現。在第一個研究中，一張擁擠的想像城市繪圖被轉印到紙板上並經切割，讓碎片得以翹起站立，把圖像轉化為淺浮雕。在第二個研究中，一段地景輪廓被轉譯為三角形，並澆鑄成一塊看似柔軟皺褶、實則完全堅硬的水泥板，形成觀看與觸摸之間安靜的矛盾。指導鼓勵在繪圖、澆鑄與建造之間自由往返，於是第三個研究把木棒與紙接合成如生物般盤繞的三角框架，並配上一張投下變幻陰影的三角形板片。最後，從住宅平面抽取的牆片單元被打散並重組成一座微型城市。這件作品說明，對表面的專注能開啟意想不到而嚴謹的空間可能。

pins.title: Mapping Imagination
pins.description:
Puzzling questions about how a place can be described become a frame of hanging string peaks above newspaper platforms, then a contour drawing and a crumpled newspaper mountain.

Model | Spatial imagination study | Newspaper, wooden sticks, PVC, foam, KT board, cotton thread | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 描繪想像
zh-Hant.description:
關於如何描述一個地方的謎題，化為一座框架，懸垂的線之山峰位於報紙平台之上，再發展為等高線繪圖與一座揉皺的報紙山。

模型｜空間想像研究｜報紙、木棒、PVC、泡棉、KT板、棉線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Puzzles about describing a landscape from someone else's position raised the question of how imagined directions could become space. The project asked whether two divergent models could be joined into a place for shopping or living.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 從別人的位置描述一片地景的謎題，引出想像中的方位如何成為空間的問題。這個專題探問，兩件發散的模型能否被結合成一個購物或居住的場所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A first study imagined standing in the speaker's position and pulled threads down from sticks into a field of sharp peaks. Close views tested how red and black strings gather into points and spread across the base.
captions: The linguistics olympiad puzzle with a map of villages that inspired the project.
The string base in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 第一個研究想像站在說話者的位置，從木棒向下拉出線，形成一片尖銳的山峰。近景測試了紅線與黑線如何聚成尖點，並在基座上散開。
captions: 啟發本案、附有村落地圖的語言學奧林匹亞謎題。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second perspective turned the same terrain into a contour drawing and a layered mountain of crumpled newspaper. The newspaper surfaces were then combined with foam blocks into an inhabitable landscape.
captions: Holding up the string model by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二個視角把同一片地形轉化為等高線繪圖，以及一座由揉皺報紙層疊而成的山。報紙表面接著與泡棉塊結合，成為一片可居住的地景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The two models were joined into a frame where string peaks hang from the roof above floating newspaper platforms. A timber grid floor and small stairs suggest a mall or a home threaded between the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩件模型被結合為一座框架，線之山峰從頂板垂下，懸在漂浮的報紙平台上方。木格柵地板與小樓梯暗示一座穿插於層次之間的商場或住家。

sections.heading: Inverted Peaks - A Puzzle Turned into Place
sections.body: Language puzzles often ask a reader to reconstruct a landscape from fragments of description, and this habit of imagining space from words can be a powerful design tool. This project grew from that exercise of reasoning about where someone stands and what they might see. Threads pulled down from slender sticks formed a first terrain of sharp peaks, red and black lines converging like trails on an unseen map. A second reading of the same ground produced a contour drawing and a soft mountain of crumpled newspaper, its printed layers stacked like strata. The guidance encouraged joining divergent results rather than choosing between them, so both studies were brought into one frame. String peaks now hang upside down from the roof, while newspaper platforms float above a woven timber floor, connected by tiny white stairs. Read from below, the structure becomes a mall of drifting levels or a house of suspended rooms. Mental geography thus acquires weight and depth. The work shows how imaginative reasoning can become an inventive and coherent spatial structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 倒懸的山峰-把謎題變成場所
zh-Hant.body: 語言謎題常要求讀者從片段的描述中重建一片地景，而這種從文字想像空間的習慣，可以成為強大的設計工具。這個專題源自這樣的練習：推理某人站在哪裡、可能看見什麼。從纖細木棒向下拉出的線形成了第一片尖峰地形，紅線與黑線匯聚，如同一張看不見的地圖上的路徑。對同一片土地的第二次閱讀，產生了一張等高線繪圖與一座柔軟的揉皺報紙山，印刷的層次像地層般堆疊。指導鼓勵結合發散的成果而非從中取捨，於是兩個研究被帶進同一座框架。線之山峰如今從頂板倒懸而下，報紙平台漂浮在編織的木地板上方，以細小的白色樓梯相連。從下方閱讀時，這座結構成為一座層層漂移的商場，或一棟懸浮房間的住宅。心中的地理因此獲得了重量與深度。這件作品說明，富有想像力的推理能成為具創意而連貫的空間結構。

pins.title: Decay in Motion
pins.description:
Rust, concrete and broken parts are assembled into a small ruin where gears turn, a ribbon of film winds through bristling wire and tiny figures climb fragile stairs.

Model | Decay and time study | Cement, wooden sticks, toothpicks, metal parts, film, copper wire, PVC, rust paint, gears, mirror board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動中的衰朽
zh-Hant.description:
鏽蝕、混凝土與破損零件被組合成一座小小的廢墟，齒輪轉動，一條底片帶穿過叢生的鐵絲蜿蜒，微小的人物攀上脆弱的樓梯。

模型｜衰朽與時間研究｜水泥、木棒、牙籤、金屬零件、底片、銅線、PVC、鏽漆、齒輪、鏡面板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The concrete block and film ribbon.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Photographs taken with a slow shutter blur light into streaks that carry personal feeling. The project asked how this sense of time passing could be combined with the rust and broken elements of an abandoned building.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 以慢速快門拍攝的照片把光模糊成光痕，承載著個人的情感。這個專題探問，這種時間流逝的感覺如何能與一棟廢棄建築的鏽蝕與破損元素結合。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The rust and broken parts of old buildings were studied as traces that record decomposition through time. Clock parts, screws and gears were collected as fragments of mechanisms that once kept time.
captions: Slow-shutter street photos taken on a film camera at night.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 老建築的鏽蝕與破損構件被當作記錄時間中分解過程的痕跡來研究。時鐘零件、螺絲與齒輪被收集起來，作為曾經計時的機械碎片。
captions: 以底片相機在夜間拍攝的慢快門街景照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A rough cement block anchors the composition while thin sticks, metal plates and stairs climb beside it. A ribbon of film was threaded through bursts of red and blue wire like a streak of light.
captions: A tangle of gears and wire.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一塊粗糙的水泥塊錨定整個構圖，細木棒、金屬板與樓梯在一旁攀升。一條底片帶穿過紅藍鐵絲的爆發狀叢集，如同一道光痕。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Large black gears rise above the ruin, and a tiny figure stands inside one of them as if inside a clock. Under strong light the gears and wires throw long shadows that extend the scene onto the wall.
captions: A gear with a tiny figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 巨大的黑色齒輪聳立在廢墟之上，一個微小的人物站在其中一個齒輪內，彷彿置身時鐘之中。在強光下，齒輪與鐵絲投下長長的影子，把場景延伸到牆上。

sections.heading: Clockwork of Ruin - Time Made Visible in Rust
sections.body: Buildings age slowly enough that their decay usually escapes notice, yet rust, cracks and fallen parts quietly record every passing season. This project tried to compress that slow process into a single scene. It began from the experience of long-exposure photography, where moving lights smear into ribbons and an ordinary street becomes charged with feeling. Those ribbons found a material equivalent in a strip of film that winds through bursts of red and blue wire, while a rough block of cement provides the heavy, weathered ground. The guidance encouraged gathering found mechanisms as carriers of meaning, so clock parts, screws, plates and gears were assembled into stairs, platforms and frames that seem half built and half collapsing. Large black gears tower over the ruin, and inside one stands a tiny figure, dwarfed by the machinery of time. Under a strong lamp the shadows of wheels and wires spread across the wall, doubling the scene into memory. The work shows how found materials can turn an abstract feeling about time into a vivid spatial narrative.

zh-Hant.heading: 廢墟的發條-在鏽蝕中顯形的時間
zh-Hant.body: 建築老化得夠慢，使其衰朽通常不被察覺，然而鏽蝕、裂縫與掉落的構件靜靜記錄著每一個流逝的季節。這個專題試圖把這個緩慢的過程壓縮進單一場景。它從長時間曝光攝影的經驗出發，在那裡移動的光被抹成光帶，平凡的街道因此充滿情感。這些光帶在一條底片中找到了材料上的對應，它穿過紅藍鐵絲的爆發狀叢集蜿蜒前行，一塊粗糙的水泥則提供沉重而風化的地面。指導鼓勵把現成的機械收集起來作為意義的載體，於是時鐘零件、螺絲、金屬板與齒輪被組裝成看似半建半塌的樓梯、平台與框架。巨大的黑色齒輪聳立在廢墟之上，其中一個裡面站著一個微小的人物，在時間的機械前顯得渺小。在一盞強光燈下，輪子與鐵絲的影子在牆上散開，把場景加倍為記憶。這件作品說明，現成材料能把對時間的抽象感受轉化為生動的空間敘事。

pins.title: Circles of a Sentence
pins.description:
The mood swings within a single spoken sentence are expressed as a web of wooden sticks, with clear spheres carrying word fragments floating above it.

Model | Language and feeling study | Wooden sticks, acrylic spheres | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 句子的圓
zh-Hant.description:
一個句子之中的情緒起伏被表現為一張木棒之網，帶有文字片段的透明球體漂浮在其上方。

模型｜語言與情感研究｜木棒、壓克力球｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An imagined language in which one circle represents a complete sentence suggested that meaning could have a shape. The project asked how the feeling of writing such a circle could be expressed in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一種以一個圓代表一整句話的想像語言，暗示意義可以擁有形狀。這個專題探問，書寫這樣一個圓的感受如何能在空間中被表達。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The circle was read as a timeline of a sentence, with its swelling and thinning edge standing for rising and falling emotion. Lines drawn across the circle linked these moments into a network of triangles.
captions: The poster of the film Arrival, whose circular alien language inspired the project.
A film still of the circular alien writing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 這個圓被當作一個句子的時間軸來閱讀，邊緣的膨脹與收細代表情緒的起伏。穿過圓的線條把這些時刻連結成一張三角形網絡。
captions: 電影《異星入境》海報，其圓形外星語言啟發了本案。
圓形外星文字的電影劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were joined into triangulated frames that grow taller and denser where the feeling becomes stronger. A dome of sticks tested how the web could close around an empty centre.
captions: A circular logogram traced and divided into lines of the stick model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒被接合成三角框架，在情感越強烈的地方長得越高、越密。一座木棒穹頂則測試了這張網如何圍合一個空的中心。
captions: 描繪並分割成木條模型線條的圓形文字。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final web spreads as a jagged ring of peaks across its base. Clear spheres carrying fragments of words float above it as the imagined meaning of the sentence.
captions: The frame with spheres in the dark.
The stick landscape in the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的網在基座上展開為一圈參差的山峰。帶著文字片段的透明球體漂浮在其上方，作為這個句子被想像出來的意義。

sections.heading: Grammar of Feeling - Building the Shape of a Sentence
sections.body: Every sentence carries an emotional contour, rising with emphasis and softening as it closes, though writing usually flattens that motion into a neat line. This project imagined a script in which an entire sentence is written as one circle, and asked what it would feel like to draw it. The circle was treated as a timeline, its swelling and thinning edge read as moments of intensity and calm, and lines across it linked these moments into a triangulated network. The guidance encouraged letting structure express emotion directly, so wooden sticks were joined into frames that rise sharply where feeling surges and settle low where it fades. A domed study tested how such a web could enclose an empty heart, while the final piece unfolds as a jagged ring of peaks across a white base. Above it, clear spheres hang in the air, each carrying a fragment of a word like a thought that has not yet landed. The work shows how abstract linguistic ideas can be given a precise and poetic spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 情感的文法-建造一個句子的形狀
zh-Hant.body: 每一個句子都帶著一條情感的輪廓，隨著強調而升起，在收尾時趨於柔和，雖然書寫通常把這種起伏壓平成一條整齊的線。這個專題想像一種把整個句子寫成一個圓的文字，並探問畫下它會是什麼感受。這個圓被當作時間軸，邊緣的膨脹與收細被讀作強烈與平靜的時刻，穿過其間的線條把這些時刻連成三角形網絡。指導鼓勵讓結構直接表達情感，於是木棒被接合成框架，在情感湧現之處陡然升起，在情感消退之處低低沉落。一個穹頂研究測試了這樣的網如何圍合一顆空的核心，最終作品則在白色基座上展開為一圈參差的山峰。在其上方，透明球體懸在空中，每一顆都帶著一個字的片段，像一個尚未落地的念頭。這件作品說明，抽象的語言概念能被賦予精確而富有詩意的空間形式。

pins.title: Maze of Sixty Cycles
pins.description:
An ancient cycle of sixty paired signs becomes a hexagonal maze that grows upward in white card and wooden strips, bursting outward like a radial labyrinth.

Model | Cultural pattern study | White card, wooden strips, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 六十循環的迷宮
zh-Hant.description:
由六十組成對符號構成的古老循環，化為一座以白卡紙與木條向上生長的六角迷宮，如放射狀的迷陣般向外迸發。

模型｜文化圖式研究｜白卡紙、木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The radial maze in its final display.
最終展示中的放射狀迷宮。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A traditional system of sixty paired signs, used for calendars, arts and naming, was encountered in a history lesson. The project asked how such a rigorous cycle could be read as a labyrinth that keeps growing by fixed rules.
captions: A diagram of the sixty-sign cycle.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一套由六十組成對符號構成的傳統系統，用於曆法、藝術與命名，在一堂歷史課中被認識。這個專題探問，如此嚴謹的循環如何能被讀成一座依固定規則不斷生長的迷宮。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two maze diagrams were drawn from the cycle and translated into a PVC prototype in a square hexagonal format. Close views of the plate tested how short walls interlock into paths.
captions: Building the first maze model by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從這個循環畫出兩張迷宮圖，再轉譯為一件方形六角格式的PVC原型。板面的近景測試了短牆如何互相咬合成路徑。
captions: 以手製作第一個迷宮模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first version read only as a single interweaving, so lighter white card and wooden strips were introduced. The maze was then rebuilt to grow upward according to the original hexagonal rules.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個版本只呈現單一的交織，於是改用較輕盈的白卡紙與木條。迷宮接著依照原本的六角規則被重建為向上生長的形態。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model radiates from a central point into layers of tilted planes. Under light it reads as a labyrinth expanding in every direction at once.
captions: The upward maze in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型從一個中心點放射出層層傾斜的板面。在光線下，它讀起來像一座同時向各方向擴張的迷宮。

sections.heading: Labyrinth of Time - A Calendar Grown into Space
sections.body: Calendars usually appear as flat grids, yet the oldest systems of counting time were closer to wheels, turning through repeating combinations of signs. This project began from one such cycle of sixty paired units, an invention whose influence still reaches into calendars, mathematics and the naming of years. Seen through the eyes of a young designer, its interlocking logic resembled a maze governed by a fixed rule of play. Two circular diagrams became a first prototype in PVC, but that version only described a single crossing of paths rather than growth. The guidance encouraged a lighter material language, and white card with slender wooden strips allowed the hexagonal rule to climb rather than spread. Each layer tilts slightly away from the last, so the final form bursts outward like a frozen explosion of planes. Light falling through the gaps turns the structure into a field of shadows that seems to rotate. Time is thus experienced as depth rather than sequence. The work shows how a historical pattern can generate an inventive and coherent spatial language.

zh-Hant.heading: 時間的迷宮-長成空間的曆法
zh-Hant.body: 曆法通常以平面的格子出現，然而最古老的計時系統更接近輪子，在反覆的符號組合中轉動。這個專題從這樣一個由六十組成對單位構成的循環出發，這項發明的影響至今仍延伸到曆法、數學與年份的命名之中。在一位年輕設計者的眼中，它互相咬合的邏輯就像一座由固定遊戲規則支配的迷宮。兩張圓形圖解先成為一件PVC原型，但那個版本只描述了路徑的單一交錯，而非生長。指導鼓勵更輕盈的材料語言，白卡紙與細木條讓六角規則得以向上攀升，而非平鋪展開。每一層都比前一層稍微傾斜，使最終形態如同一場凝固的板面爆炸般向外迸發。穿過縫隙的光把結構化為一片彷彿在旋轉的影子場域。時間因此被體驗為深度，而非順序。這件作品說明，一種歷史圖式能生成具創意而連貫的空間語言。

pins.title: Stacked Vices
pins.description:
Seven words for human failings are interpreted through colour and shape, then piled with wooden bricks into a restless landscape of towers and tumbling blocks.

Model | Human nature and form study | Wooden bricks, coloured resin blocks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 堆疊的惡
zh-Hant.description:
七個描述人性缺陷的詞語透過色彩與形狀被詮釋，再與木磚堆疊成一片由高塔與翻落方塊構成的不安地景。

模型｜人性與形式研究｜木磚、彩色樹脂塊｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A suspenseful story about original sin led to a medieval poem that divides human failings into seven categories. The project asked whether these abstract words could be explained through personal spatial ideas.
captions: The poster of the film Se7en, with notes on the seven deadly sins.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個關於原罪的懸疑故事，引向一首把人性缺陷分為七類的中世紀長詩。這個專題探問，這些抽象的詞語能否透過個人的空間想法被詮釋。
captions: 電影《火線追緝令》海報與七宗罪筆記。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each of the seven words was assigned its own colour, texture and small model. The models were arranged as an index linking each word to a form.
captions: The concept board: breaking regular design with arbitrary spaces.
An index of the seven word models.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 七個詞語各自被賦予一種色彩、質感與一件小模型。這些模型被排列成一份索引，把每個詞語連結到一個形態。
captions: 概念板：以隨機空間打破規則設計。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A random stacking method was used to begin, with wooden bricks of four sizes forming the ground. Through repeated attempts the coloured pieces were placed where each failing seemed to gather.
captions: A view of the stacked blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以隨機堆疊的方法開始，四種尺寸的木磚構成地面。經過反覆嘗試，彩色構件被放在每一種缺陷似乎聚集的位置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final landscape rises into towers of coloured blocks above a sea of plain bricks. Tiny figures and stairs invite the viewer to wander through the consequences of each choice.
captions: A tower rising from the bricks.
A close view of the coloured towers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終地景在一片素木磚之海上升起彩色方塊的高塔。微小的人物與樓梯邀請觀者漫遊於每一種選擇的後果之間。

sections.heading: Architecture of Conscience - Seven Words in Wood
sections.body: Moral ideas are usually taught through stories, but stories can also be translated into the language of material and arrangement. This project grew from fascination with a tale of original sin and from reading an old poem that sorts human failings into seven kinds. Rather than illustrating them literally, the young designer gave each word a colour and a shape, building an index of small models that behave like characters in a silent drama. The guidance encouraged freedom within method, so the composition began with a deliberately random stacking of wooden bricks in four sizes. From that disorder, coloured resin pieces were gradually placed where envy, pride or greed seemed to gather, forming towers that lean, crowd and overhang. Tiny stairs and figures thread among them, suggesting that every passer-by might stumble into one of these clusters. The landscape becomes a reflection on how actions can harm oneself and others, and on the hope of loving life after its ups and downs. The work shows how ethical reflection can be expressed through an inventive and coherent spatial composition.

zh-Hant.heading: 良知的建築-木中的七個詞語
zh-Hant.body: 道德觀念通常透過故事被傳授，但故事也能被轉譯為材料與排列的語言。這個專題源自對一則原罪故事的著迷，以及閱讀一首把人性缺陷分為七類的古老長詩。這位年輕設計者沒有照字面圖解它們，而是給每個詞語一種色彩與形狀，建立一份小模型的索引，它們像一齣無聲戲劇中的角色。指導鼓勵在方法之中保有自由，於是構圖從四種尺寸木磚的刻意隨機堆疊開始。從那份無序之中，彩色樹脂構件被逐步放在嫉妒、驕傲或貪婪似乎聚集的地方，形成傾斜、擁擠與懸挑的高塔。細小的樓梯與人物穿行其間，暗示每一位路人都可能誤入其中一個聚落。這片地景成為一種反思：行為如何傷害自己與別人，以及在起伏之後仍熱愛生活的盼望。這件作品說明，倫理的思考能透過具創意而連貫的空間構成被表達。

pins.title: Life Orbit
pins.description:
Twenty-seven open cubes, each holding a staircase turned in its own direction, are linked into a field of crossing paths that reads as a map of many lives.

Model | Path and narrative study | PVC sheet, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生命軌道
zh-Hant.description:
二十七個開放的立方體，各自容納一座朝向不同方向的樓梯，被連結成一片交錯的路徑場域，讀起來像一張許多生命的地圖。

模型｜路徑與敘事研究｜PVC片、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The stair cubes in their final display.
最終展示中的樓梯立方體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The idea of an unexpected space hidden behind an unintended door or an endless stair suggested that every life follows its own path. The project asked how individual journeys could be shown crossing yet remaining separate.
captions: The poster of the film that inspired the project.
A reference drawing of a corridor that seems to lead nowhere.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個藏在不經意的門或無盡樓梯後方的意外空間，暗示每一個生命都走著自己的路。這個專題探問，個人的旅程如何能被呈現為彼此交錯卻又保持分離。
captions: 一條彷彿無盡走廊的參考圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each square cube was treated as a world in which one person lives, holding a single staircase in one direction. A primary model of twelve cubes tested different turns and climbs.
captions: The primary model of twelve cubes.
An interior view of the stairs.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每一個方形立方體被視為一個人居住的世界，容納朝向單一方向的一座樓梯。一件由十二個立方體構成的初步模型測試了不同的轉折與攀升。
captions: 十二個立方體的初步模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Twenty-seven cubes were then interconnected by staircases in different dimensions. The stairs grow longer and farther as they meet and miss one another.
captions: Building the stair cubes by hand.
A climbing view inside the cubes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 接著二十七個立方體以不同維度的樓梯互相連結。樓梯在相遇與錯過之間變得越來越長、越來越遠。
captions: 立方體內部的攀升視角。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final field of cubes was set outdoors on paving, where its white stairs stand out against the frames. Its maker stands outside it as a spectator, watching the trajectories of others and of oneself.
captions: Arranging the final stair cubes outdoors.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的立方體場域被放在戶外的鋪面上，白色樓梯在框架之間格外醒目。創作者站在場域之外作為旁觀者，觀看別人與自己的軌跡。
captions: 在戶外擺放最終的樓梯方塊。

sections.heading: Paths That Cross - Stairs as Lives in Motion
sections.body: A stair is perhaps the most intimate of architectural elements, measured step by step by a single body. This project imagined each life as a cube containing one staircase, a private route that only its owner can walk. Inspired by stories of unexpected spaces behind ordinary doors, the young designer first arranged twelve cubes in a grid, testing how a stair might twist, climb or fold back within its frame. The guidance encouraged moving from symbols toward relationships, and so twenty-seven cubes were joined in every dimension, their stairs reaching across boundaries to touch neighbouring worlds. Photographed from inside, the model becomes a vertiginous interior of bridges and landings, while outdoors it sits lightly on paving like a scaffold of memories. The designer adopts the position of spectator, watching others while recognising a personal trajectory among them. A gentle consolation closes the narrative: missing the sun need not mean missing the moon and stars. The work shows how a simple module can carry an inventive and coherent spatial story about life.

zh-Hant.heading: 交錯的路徑-作為移動生命的樓梯
zh-Hant.body: 樓梯或許是最親密的建築元素，由一個身體一步一步地丈量。這個專題把每一個生命想像為一個容納一座樓梯的立方體，一條只有其主人能走的私人路徑。受到平凡門後意外空間的故事啟發，這位年輕設計者先把十二個立方體排成格子，測試一座樓梯如何在框架內扭轉、攀升或折返。指導鼓勵從符號走向關係，於是二十七個立方體在每一個維度上被接合，樓梯跨越邊界去觸碰鄰近的世界。從內部拍攝時，模型成為一個由橋與平台構成的令人暈眩的內部空間，在戶外則輕輕坐落在鋪面上，如同一座記憶的鷹架。設計者採取旁觀者的位置，觀看別人，同時在其中辨認自己的軌跡。敘事以一句溫柔安慰收尾：錯過太陽，不必意味著錯過月亮與星星。這件作品說明，一個簡單的模組能承載關於生命、具創意而連貫的空間故事。

pins.title: The Wave Corridor
pins.description:
Curves extracted from an indoor mall become pattern drawings, wire and sponge studies, and finally a folded lattice-rib canopy that could replace a wall between a station and a mall.

Model | Element extraction study | PVC, wooden strips, white card, sponge panels, transparent sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 波浪廊道
zh-Hant.description:
從室內商場萃取的曲線化為圖樣繪圖、鐵絲與海綿研究，最終成為一座折疊的格肋頂篷，可以取代車站與商場之間的牆。

模型｜元素萃取研究｜PVC、木條、白卡紙、海綿板、透明片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A complex joining a station and a mall felt vague in function and confusing in space. The project asked whether a logical sequence of steps could turn that space into blocks with clear functions.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座連接車站與商場的綜合體，功能模糊、空間混亂。這個專題探問，一連串合乎邏輯的步驟能否把那個空間轉化為功能清楚的區塊。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Details such as the building layout and the airflow of air conditioners were abstracted into black and white pattern drawings. The curve emerged as the most important element of the interior.
captions: Photos of a shopping mall interior with curving floors and visitors.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 建築配置與空調氣流等細節被抽象為黑白圖樣繪圖。曲線浮現為室內空間最重要的元素。
captions: 曲線樓層與訪客的購物中心室內照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wire, bent sponge panels and a spiral plan translated the curve into walls whose height marks where people gather. PVC and transparent sheets let the plan grow into imagined interiors with scattered rows of wire for crowds.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲、彎折的海綿板與一張螺旋平面圖把曲線轉譯為牆，牆的高度標示人群聚集之處。PVC與透明片讓平面圖長成想像中的室內，散落的鐵絲列代表人流。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Experiments with different paper shapes led to a lattice rib that bends and rotates easily. The final canopy replaces the wall with a rippling corridor offering resting places and luggage storage for passengers.
captions: The lattice rib in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 以不同紙張形狀的實驗引向一種容易彎曲與旋轉的格肋。最終的頂篷以一條起伏的廊道取代牆，為旅客提供休憩處與行李存放空間。

sections.heading: Folded Threshold - Turning a Wall into a Wave
sections.body: Transport hubs often merge with shopping centres until their boundaries blur, leaving travellers in spaces that are busy yet hard to read. This project approached such a place with the patience of an analyst. Small observations about plan layout, circulation and even the drift of conditioned air were distilled into pages of black and white patterns, from which the curve emerged as the governing element. The guidance encouraged a logical sequence in which each step would push the next, like opening a nesting doll without knowing the final figure. Wire coils, folded sponge walls and a spiral plan translated the curve into heights that attract or disperse people, while transparent sheets layered the plan into imagined interiors. Paper experiments then revealed a lattice rib able to bend and twist without losing strength. In the final model this rib becomes a rippling canopy that replaces a dividing wall, sheltering benches and luggage alcoves beneath its folds. Passage itself becomes a place to pause. The work shows how disciplined abstraction can produce an inventive and coherent spatial proposal.

zh-Hant.heading: 折疊的門檻-把牆變成波浪
zh-Hant.body: 交通樞紐常與購物中心融合，直到邊界模糊，讓旅客置身於繁忙卻難以閱讀的空間。這個專題以分析者的耐心面對這樣的場所。關於平面配置、動線，甚至空調氣流飄移的細小觀察，被提煉成一頁頁黑白圖樣，曲線從中浮現為主導的元素。指導鼓勵一種合乎邏輯的順序，每一步推動下一步，就像打開一個套娃，卻不知道最後會出現什麼樣的人偶。鐵絲螺旋、折疊的海綿牆與一張螺旋平面，把曲線轉譯為吸引或分散人群的高度，透明片則把平面層疊為想像中的室內。紙的實驗接著揭示一種能彎曲與扭轉而不失強度的格肋。在最終模型中，這種格肋成為一座起伏的頂篷，取代分隔的牆，在其褶皺下庇護長椅與行李凹室。通行本身成為一個可以停留的場所。這件作品說明，有紀律的抽象能產生具創意而連貫的空間提案。

pins.title: Dancing Stairs
pins.description:
The flowing body language of a dance about mythical creatures becomes colour sketches, pink rib studies and a rotating symmetrical staircase that resembles both a mountain and an ancient temple.

Model | Dance and form study | PVC, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 舞動的樓梯
zh-Hant.description:
一支關於神話異獸之舞的流動肢體語言，化為彩色草圖、粉紅色肋片研究，以及一座既像山又像古老神殿的旋轉對稱樓梯。

模型｜舞蹈與形式研究｜PVC、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A dance telling the story of ancient mythical creatures expressed wind, water, grass and trees through soft body language. The project asked how the feeling of that solemn ritual could become architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一支講述古代神話異獸的舞蹈，以柔軟的肢體語言表現風、水、草與樹。這個專題探問，那場莊嚴儀式的感受如何能成為建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Leaping lines and scattered yet harmonious fragments were drawn almost unconsciously while watching. These sketches treated movement as symbols like those in ancient frescoes.
captions: Photos of the dance performance about ancient mythical animals that inspired the stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 觀看時幾乎無意識地畫下跳躍的線條與散落卻和諧的片段。這些草圖把動作當作如同古代壁畫中的符號來處理。
captions: 啟發本樓梯、以古代神獸為題的舞蹈演出照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Pink and white models tested curving ribs, spiralling stairs and open frames in many styles. A rotating symmetrical staircase was finally chosen and built at 1:25 scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 粉紅色與白色模型以多種風格測試彎曲肋片、螺旋樓梯與開放框架。最終選定一座旋轉對稱的樓梯，並以1:25比例製作。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model coils two openwork stairs around a bowl-like core pierced by arched doors and windows. Like the dance, its details change from every angle and reward slow viewing.
captions: A stair seen through an opening.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓兩座鏤空樓梯環繞一個碗狀核心盤旋，核心開有拱形門窗。如同那支舞，它的細節隨每個角度而變，值得慢慢觀賞。

sections.heading: Choreography in Stone - A Stair That Remembers a Dance
sections.body: Dance and architecture share a concern with rhythm, but one unfolds in seconds while the other must hold still for decades. This project tried to let a building remember a performance. Watching a dance about creatures from ancient myth, the young designer saw costumes and lighting fall away until only gestures remained, like figures leaping out of an old fresco. Those gestures were caught in quick sketches of looping lines and scattered colour, then tested in pink and white models of curving ribs and fragmentary stairs. The guidance encouraged choosing one clear spatial idea from many trials, and a rotating symmetrical staircase emerged as the strongest. Built at a scale of one to twenty-five, two openwork flights coil around a hollow core, and arched doors and windows frame glimpses of climbing steps. From one side the model resembles a mountain; from another, a temple approached by pilgrims. Movement is held in suspension rather than lost. The work shows how an ephemeral performance can inspire an inventive and coherent spatial form.

zh-Hant.heading: 石中的編舞-記得一支舞的樓梯
zh-Hant.body: 舞蹈與建築共同關注節奏，但前者在數秒間展開，後者必須靜止數十年。這個專題試圖讓一座建築記住一場演出。觀看一支關於古代神話異獸的舞蹈時，這位年輕設計者看見服裝與燈光逐漸退去，直到只剩下姿態，如同從古老壁畫中躍出的人物。這些姿態被捕捉在迴旋線條與散落色彩的速寫中，再以彎曲肋片與片段樓梯的粉紅色與白色模型加以測試。指導鼓勵從眾多嘗試中選出一個清晰的空間想法，一座旋轉對稱的樓梯脫穎而出。以二十五分之一的比例製作，兩段鏤空的梯段環繞一個中空的核心盤旋，拱形門窗框出攀升台階的片段景象。從一側看，模型像一座山；從另一側看，則像一座朝聖者前往的神殿。動作被懸置保存，而非消逝。這件作品說明，一場短暫的演出能啟發具創意而連貫的空間形式。

pins.title: Threads of Restraint
pins.description:
A wearable structure of tangled wire, thread and mirror fragments treats the body as a ground on which space is built, picturing the norms that bind a person and the reflections in which identity may be lost.

Model | Wearable spatial study | Wire, thread, spray paint, mirror pieces | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 束縛之線
zh-Hant.description:
一件由纏繞鐵絲、線與鏡面碎片構成的可穿戴結構，把身體當作建造空間的基地，描繪束縛一個人的規範，以及身份可能迷失其中的反射。

模型｜可穿戴空間研究｜鐵絲、線、噴漆、鏡片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wire structure in its refined form.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A background in fashion suggested that the human body could serve as a canvas and base land for building spaces. The project asked how a wearable piece could show the restrictions that society keeps adding to a person.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 先前的服裝設計背景，讓人想到人體可以作為建造空間的畫布與基地。這個專題探問，一件可穿戴作品如何呈現社會不斷加諸一個人的種種限制。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A loose wireframe was first bent into a dome that could sit around the head. Black thread was then stretched across the wire to multiply the lines into a dense net.
captions: A portrait collage with line drawings of faces, exploring the body as a base for building.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 先把一個鬆散的鐵絲框架彎成能環繞頭部的穹形。接著在鐵絲之間拉上黑線，讓線條倍增成一張密集的網。
captions: 以臉部線描構成的肖像拼貼，探索以身體作為建造的基地。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Spray paint darkened the frame so that it read as a single tangled drawing in space. Small mirror pieces were then fixed among the wires to catch and scatter reflections.
captions: Spray painting the wire frame by hand.
The mirror stage: adding reflective pieces to the frame.
A detail of the painted wire form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 噴漆讓框架變暗，使它讀起來像一幅在空間中的纏繞繪圖。接著把小鏡片固定在鐵絲之間，捕捉並散射反光。
captions: 鏡面階段：為框架加上反光片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The refined piece swells from the body like a cage of lines that both shelters and confines. Its mirror fragments stand for a self that may become lost after long suppression by convention.
captions: The wire and mirror structure worn on the body.
The worn structure photographed at sunset.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 精修後的作品從身體向外膨脹，如一座既庇護又禁錮的線之籠。鏡面碎片象徵一個在長久受慣例壓抑後可能迷失的自我。
captions: 穿戴在身上的鐵絲與鏡面結構。
夕陽下拍攝的穿戴結構。

sections.heading: Body as Ground - A Cage Drawn in Wire
sections.body: Architecture is usually imagined as something that stands on land, yet this project began by asking whether the body itself might serve as the ground. Drawing on an earlier training in fashion, the young designer treated the head and shoulders as a site and began to build upon them with wire. A loose dome came first, then black thread was pulled taut between its ribs until the lines multiplied into a net as intricate as a pencil drawing. Spray paint unified these strands into one dark gesture, and small mirrors were tucked among them so that every movement would throw back broken reflections. The resulting form is ambiguous by design. It encloses like a shelter, but it also tightens like a cage, echoing the social expectations and stereotypes that gather around a person over time. The glinting fragments suggest that identity can be scattered when it is too long confined. The guidance encouraged a reading beyond costume, insisting that space need not rest on the earth at all. The work shows how a wearable object can become an inventive and coherent spatial argument about freedom.

zh-Hant.heading: 身體為地-以鐵絲畫成的籠
zh-Hant.body: 建築通常被想像為立於土地之上的事物，這個專題卻從一個問題開始：身體本身能否作為基地。憑藉先前的服裝訓練，這位年輕設計者把頭部與肩膀當作一處基地，開始以鐵絲在其上建造。先成形的是一個鬆散的穹頂，接著把黑線在肋條之間拉緊，直到線條倍增成一張如鉛筆素描般繁複的網。噴漆把這些線統一成一道深色的姿態，小鏡片被塞進其間，使每一次移動都折射出破碎的倒影。最終的形態刻意保持曖昧。它像庇護所般包覆，卻也像籠子般收緊，呼應隨時間聚集在一個人身上的社會期待與刻板印象。閃爍的碎片暗示，身份若被禁錮太久，便可能四散。指導鼓勵超越服裝的閱讀，堅持空間根本不必安放在大地上。這件作品說明，一件可穿戴的物件能成為一個關於自由、具創意而連貫的空間論述。

pins.title: Four Rooms of a Changing Mood
pins.description:
The shifting tone of a dark story is distilled into four joined rooms of wire and foil, warm wood and fabric, iridescent bubbles and plain white board.

Model | Narrative space study | PVC, wire, thread, wooden strips, cement, acrylic balls, laser paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 情緒流轉的四個房間
zh-Hant.description:
一個黑暗故事中不斷轉變的基調，被提煉為四個相連的房間：鐵絲與錫箔、溫暖的木與布、虹彩泡泡，以及素白板材。

模型｜敘事空間研究｜PVC、鐵絲、線、木條、水泥、壓克力球、雷射紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The four joined rooms in the refined model.
精修模型中相連的四個房間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A suspenseful story moves through powerful changes of tone and atmosphere as its plot unfolds. The project asked how those changes could be converted into one model with four combined sections.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個懸疑故事隨著情節展開，經歷了強烈的基調與氛圍轉變。這個專題探問，這些轉變如何能被轉化為一件由四個區段組合而成的模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Major plot moments were collected and their colour schemes and spaces were extracted. Quick sketches then translated each mood into a room with its own character.
captions: Film stills from The Witch, annotated with moods and colour schemes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 收集主要的情節片段，並萃取其色彩配置與空間。快速草圖接著把每一種情緒轉譯為一個各具性格的房間。
captions: 標注情緒與配色的電影《女巫》劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Iron wire and tinfoil formed a dark room of entrapment, while wood, fabric and plastic made a warm and comfortable home. Plastic bubbles filled with holographic paper and wire became an invasion spreading through the space.
captions: The dark room of wire and foil.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 鐵絲與錫箔構成一個受困的黑暗房間，木頭、布料與塑膠則做成一個溫暖舒適的家。裝有全像紙與鐵絲的塑膠泡泡成為在空間中蔓延的入侵。
captions: 鐵絲與錫箔的黑暗房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The last room is a rigid structure of plain PVC whose whiteness recalls a sealed laboratory. Joined together, the four rooms let the viewer pass through the whole story as a sequence of atmospheres.
captions: The white room of plain board.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最後一個房間是由素PVC板構成的剛硬結構，其潔白令人想起一座封閉的實驗室。四個房間組合在一起，讓觀者以一連串氛圍走過整個故事。

sections.heading: Mood as Material - A Story Told in Four Rooms
sections.body: Stories move through time, but rooms hold still, so translating a narrative into space requires choosing which moments deserve to become walls. This project began by gathering the turning points of a tense story and extracting their colours and settings, much as a set designer might study a script. The young designer then gave each phase its own material voice. Iron wire and crumpled foil evoke a lightless enclosure of training and fear, whereas wood, fabric and soft plastics compose a domestic interior that feels warm and sheltered. Clear bubbles stuffed with holographic paper drift into the third zone like an infection, glittering yet unsettling. Finally a rigid assembly of white board recalls a sterile laboratory in which every surface seems to watch. The guidance encouraged contrast rather than illustration, so the rooms are joined edge to edge, and the eye travels abruptly from darkness to comfort to menace. Mood thus becomes something tactile and measurable. The work shows how narrative atmosphere can be turned into an inventive and coherent spatial sequence.

zh-Hant.heading: 情緒為材-以四個房間述說的故事
zh-Hant.body: 故事在時間中推進，房間卻保持靜止，因此把敘事轉譯為空間，必須選擇哪些時刻值得成為牆。這個專題從收集一個緊張故事的轉折點開始，萃取它們的色彩與場景。這位年輕設計者接著賦予每一個階段各自的材料聲音。鐵絲與揉皺的錫箔喚起一個沒有光、充滿訓練與恐懼的封閉空間，木頭、布料與柔軟的塑膠則組成一個溫暖而受庇護的居家室內。塞滿全像紙的透明泡泡如感染般飄入第三個區域。最後，一組剛硬的白色板材構成物令人想起一座無菌的實驗室，每一個表面似乎都在注視。指導鼓勵對比而非圖解，於是房間邊對邊地接合，視線從黑暗突然移到安適，再移到威脅。情緒因此成為可觸摸、可度量的事物。這件作品說明，敘事的氛圍能被轉化為具創意而連貫的空間序列。

pins.title: Triangles Into Space
pins.description:
Three drawings built from black, shaded and white triangles are carved apart, set up in parallel and joined with wooden sticks, holograms and reflective paper into a luminous three-dimensional field.

Model | Two-to-three-dimensional transformation | PVC, wooden strips, laser paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 走入空間的三角形
zh-Hant.description:
三張由黑色、灰階與白色三角形構成的繪圖被切開、平行排列，再以木條、全像紙與反光紙接合成一片發光的立體場域。

模型｜二維到三維的轉換｜PVC、木條、雷射紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 精修後的三角形框架模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project set out to explore how a flat drawing could be transformed into three-dimensional space. It asked whether special shapes inside an architecture could grow directly from a two-dimensional pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題著手探索一張平面繪圖如何能被轉化為三維空間。它探問，建築內部的特殊形狀能否直接從一個二維圖樣生長出來。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Experiments with simple lines and shapes led to three related drawings composed mainly of triangles. Black, shaded and white triangles were combined to create variance across each sheet.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以簡單線條與形狀的實驗，引向三張主要由三角形構成的相關繪圖。黑色、灰階與白色三角形相互組合，在每一張紙上製造變化。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Parts of the three drawings were carved out at random and posed in parallel layers. Wooden sticks, holograms and reflective paper were then used to connect them into a frame.
captions: A close view of the stick frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三張繪圖中的部分被隨機切出，並以平行的層次擺放。接著以木條、全像紙與反光紙把它們連結成一個框架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The reflective materials throw coloured light in many directions within the space. The layout makes the space exceptional and reinforces the triangles from the original drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 反光材料在空間中把彩色光線投向四面八方。這樣的配置使空間與眾不同，並強化了原始繪圖中的三角形。

sections.heading: Lifted Pattern - When a Drawing Learns Depth
sections.body: Every architect learns to move between the flat sheet and the built volume, yet the passage from one to the other is rarely made visible. This project staged that passage deliberately. It began with patient experiments in line and shape that settled into three related drawings, each a mosaic of black, shaded and white triangles that seem to pulse with tension. Rather than extruding them in a predictable way, the young designer cut fragments from all three at random and stood them up as parallel layers, as if the sheets had been lifted and spread apart. Slender wooden sticks then crossed between the layers, carrying holographic and reflective papers that catch light at every angle. The guidance encouraged trusting chance within a clear rule, and the outcome rewards that trust. Inside the frame, coloured reflections shift as one moves, and the original triangles recur at many scales, now as shadows, now as glinting planes. Depth is discovered rather than imposed. The work shows how a graphic exercise can mature into an inventive and coherent spatial composition.

zh-Hant.heading: 升起的圖樣-當繪圖學會深度
zh-Hant.body: 每一位建築師都要學會在平面的紙張與建成的體量之間移動，然而從一者到另一者的過程很少被看見。這個專題刻意上演了這段過程。它從線條與形狀的耐心實驗開始，最後落定為三張相關的繪圖，每一張都是由黑色、灰階與白色三角形構成的馬賽克。這位年輕設計者沒有以可預期的方式擠出它們，而是從三張圖中隨機切下片段，立成平行的層次。細長的木條接著在層與層之間交錯，承載在每個角度捕捉光線的全像紙與反光紙。指導鼓勵在清楚的規則之中信任偶然，而成果回報了這份信任。在框架內部，彩色反光隨人移動而變化，原始的三角形在多種尺度上反覆出現。深度是被發現的，而非被強加的。這件作品說明，一項圖像練習能成熟為具創意而連貫的空間構成。

pins.title: Bubbles of Infinity
pins.description:
Clear plastic spheres stitched together with wire and springs are arranged so that, from above, they trace an endless twisted strip, a micro world of floating bubbles.

Model | Infinity and form study | Plastic bubbles, springs, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無限的泡泡
zh-Hant.description:
以鐵絲與彈簧縫合在一起的透明塑膠球被排列成從上方俯瞰時描出一條無盡的扭轉環帶，成為一個漂浮泡泡的微型世界。

模型｜無限與形式研究｜塑膠泡泡、彈簧、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The bubble strip seen from above.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project grew from two simple attractions, the endless effect of a twisted one-sided strip and the joy of a childhood bubble toy. It asked how these two ideas could be combined into one architectural model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題源自兩個簡單的喜愛：一條單面扭轉環帶的無限效果，以及童年吹泡泡玩具的樂趣。它探問，這兩個想法如何能被結合成一件建築模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sketch traced the twisted strip from a flat band to a loop and then to a ring of bubbles. A second sketch imagined bubbles that mirror the world and hold a tiny city inside.
captions: A sketch of the twisted strip.
A sketch of a micro city in a bubble.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張草圖描繪扭轉環帶從平帶到迴圈，再到一圈泡泡的過程。另一張草圖想像泡泡映照世界，並在其中容納一座微小的城市。
captions: 泡泡中微型城市的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Clear plastic balls were sewn together with wire so that they seem to flow freely. Copper springs rise between them like bridges and threads of movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 透明塑膠球以鐵絲縫合在一起，使它們看起來自由流動。銅彈簧在球與球之間升起，如同橋梁與移動的絲線。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: From the aerial perspective the cluster of spheres reads as an endless twisted strip. Tiny red figures among the bubbles suggest a micro world that is both vast and very small.
captions: A close view of the bubble cluster.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從空中視角看，這群球體讀起來像一條無盡的扭轉環帶。泡泡之間的細小紅色人形，暗示一個既廣大又極微小的世界。

sections.heading: Endless Surface - A World Held in Bubbles
sections.body: Infinity is difficult to picture, yet mathematicians have long offered a small model of it in the twisted strip whose single surface never ends. This project placed that abstract figure beside a humble memory of childhood, the bubble wand that released fragile spheres into the air. Sketches show the reasoning clearly. A flat band twists, closes into a loop, and is then rebuilt from bubbles, while a second drawing imagines each sphere mirroring its surroundings and enclosing a miniature city. In the model, clear plastic balls are sewn together with fine wire so that the cluster seems to drift rather than rest. Copper springs coil upward like bridges between neighbours, and tiny red figures stand among the domes, giving an uncertain sense of scale. The guidance encouraged a single strong spatial idea, and here it is the aerial view, from which the loose heap resolves into an unbroken twisted path. Existence appears both immeasurably large and as small as a world inside a bubble. The work shows how playful materials can carry an inventive and coherent spatial meditation on the infinite.

zh-Hant.heading: 無盡之面-盛在泡泡裡的世界
zh-Hant.body: 無限難以描繪，然而數學家早已以一條單一表面永不終止的扭轉環帶，提供了它的小小模型。這個專題把這個抽象圖形放在一段樸素的童年記憶旁邊：那根把脆弱球體釋放到空中的泡泡棒。草圖清楚呈現了推理的過程。一條平帶扭轉、閉合成迴圈，再以泡泡重建；另一張繪圖則想像每一顆球體映照四周，並包覆一座微型城市。在模型中，透明塑膠球以細鐵絲縫合。銅彈簧如鄰近球體之間的橋梁般向上盤繞，細小的紅色人形站在圓頂之間。指導鼓勵一個強而清晰的空間想法，而在這裡，那就是空中的視角，鬆散的堆疊由此化為不間斷的扭轉路徑。存在顯得既無比廣大，又如泡泡中的世界般微小。這件作品說明，富有遊戲性的材料能承載一場關於無限、具創意而連貫的空間沉思。

pins.title: Garden in the Air
pins.description:
An underused neighbourhood park is mapped and reimagined as a stack of green platforms threaded with stairs, giving workers and residents places to eat, jog, rest and meet.

Digital design | Urban park proposal | Image editing, 3D modelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空中花園
zh-Hant.description:
一座使用率低的鄰里公園被測繪，並被重新想像為一疊以樓梯串連的綠色平台，讓上班族與居民有地方用餐、慢跑、休息與相遇。

數位設計｜城市公園提案｜影像編輯、3D建模｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A park in the neighbourhood held only some greenery and offered little practical use to its surroundings. The project asked whether it could become a creative space where people relax, exercise and communicate.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 鄰里中的一座公園只有一些綠地，對周邊環境幾乎沒有實際用途。這個專題探問，它能否成為一個讓人放鬆、運動與交流的創意空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A site map recorded roads, streets, shops, restaurants and other buildings around the park. It showed busy surroundings full of employees and residents with no shared outdoor place.
captions: A collage of street scenes, signs and people around Guangzhou East Station near the park.
The site map of the neighbourhood.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張基地圖記錄了公園周邊的道路、街道、商店、餐廳與其他建築。它顯示周邊繁忙，充滿上班族與居民，卻沒有共享的戶外場所。
captions: 公園附近廣州東站一帶的街景、招牌與人群拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Concept sketches tested floating green plates, open frames and slender towers carrying round platforms. Each layer was given a different function to meet the needs of different groups.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 概念草圖測試了漂浮的綠色板、開放的框架，以及承載圓形平台的細長塔體。每一層被賦予不同的功能，以滿足不同群體的需求。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final render stacks lawns, a lunch deck and a jogging loop between surrounding towers, linked by stairs and a glass core. A section shows the garden rising through the dense block like a green ladder.
captions: The section of the vertical park.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的渲染圖在周邊高樓之間疊起草坪、午餐平台與慢跑環道，以樓梯與玻璃核心相連。一張剖面圖呈現花園如一座綠色梯子般穿過密集的街廓向上升起。

sections.heading: Stacked Commons - Lifting a Park into the City
sections.body: A small urban park can be green yet strangely empty, a patch of planting that nobody quite knows how to use. This project began from such a place, observed on everyday walks, and from the question of what it might offer the people who pass it daily. A careful site map traced the roads, shops, eateries and offices pressing in from every side, revealing many potential users but no shared outdoor room. Concept sketches then explored ways to multiply the ground, from tilted green plates to open frames and thin towers balancing circular decks. The young designer resolved these into a vertical sequence in which each level serves a different rhythm of life, a lunch terrace for nearby employees, a looping track for joggers, quiet lawns for conversation. Stairs and a transparent core stitch the layers together, and the section shows the garden climbing between tall blocks like a green ladder. The guidance encouraged generosity toward the public, imagining a future in which such a plan could truly be built. The work shows how attentive observation can grow into an inventive and coherent spatial proposal for the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊起的公地-把公園舉進城市
zh-Hant.body: 一座小型的城市公園可以是綠色的，卻又奇異地空曠。這個專題從這樣一個在日常散步中觀察到的地方出發，追問它能為每天經過的人提供什麼。一張仔細的基地圖描繪了從四面八方擠壓而來的道路、商店、餐館與辦公室，卻沒有共享的戶外房間。概念草圖接著探索倍增地面的方式。這位年輕設計者把它們整合為一個垂直的序列，每一層服務一種不同的生活節奏：給附近上班族的午餐露台、給慢跑者的環狀跑道、供人交談的安靜草坪。樓梯與透明核心把各層縫合在一起，剖面則呈現花園如綠色梯子般在高樓之間攀升。指導鼓勵對公眾的慷慨。這件作品說明，細心的觀察能長成一個為城市而生、具創意而連貫的空間提案。

pins.title: Fabric City
pins.description:
A woven web of curved ribs rises over a circular sunken walkway, borrowing the bond of a spider web and the lifting vessels of a plant to make a place where people climb, cross and linger.

Architecture design | Urban web structure | PVC board model, Rhino | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 織網之城
zh-Hant.description:
一張由彎曲肋條編成的網，在一條圓形下沉步道上方升起，借用蜘蛛網的連結與植物導管的輸送，形成一個讓人攀爬、穿越與停留的場所。

建築設計｜城市網狀結構｜PVC板模型、Rhino｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The woven web tower over the walkway.
步道上方的編織網狀塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A circular sunken walkway at a busy junction was used only as a passage that people hurried through. The project asked how a light structure above it could give the crossing a sense of attachment and unity.
captions: The site: the circular underground walkway, seen from the street.
Site maps of the walkway and its surroundings in Guangzhou, with a legend.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 繁忙路口的一條圓形下沉步道，只被當作人們匆匆穿過的通道。這個專題探問，一個位於其上方的輕盈結構，如何能讓這個穿越處產生依附與整體感。
captions: 基地：從街道看圓形地下通道。
廣州地下通道與周邊的基地地圖及圖例。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two natural systems guided the idea, the spider web that binds many threads into one surface and the plant vessel that carries water from root to leaf. Line sketches turned these into curved ribs that gather, twist and climb.
captions: Inspiration: spiderweb photos and a diagram of plant vessels.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 兩個自然系統引導了這個構想：把許多絲線結成一個表面的蜘蛛網，以及把水從根部運送到葉片的植物導管。線條草圖把它們轉化為聚集、扭轉並向上攀升的彎曲肋條。
captions: 靈感：蜘蛛網照片與植物導管圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Conceptual models in slotted PVC board tested how a woven surface could make both form and space. Their shadows showed how the ribs would filter light onto the ground below.
captions: A slotted test model of the web.
The test model and its shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以開槽PVC板製作的概念模型，測試一個編織表面如何同時形成形體與空間。模型的影子顯示肋條如何把光線過濾到下方的地面。
captions: 網狀結構的開槽測試模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final design wraps the walkway in a tall lattice tower with stairs, bridges and seats held inside the mesh. Scenario sketches show people climbing a spiral stair, crossing a bridge, sitting in a pocket and playing games.
captions: A close view of the mesh.
Scenario sketches of climbing and crossing.
Scenario sketches of sitting and play.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終設計以一座高聳的格網塔包覆步道，樓梯、橋與座位都被容納在網中。情境草圖描繪人們攀登螺旋梯、穿越橋、坐在凹處與玩遊戲的場景。
captions: 攀爬與穿越的情境草圖。
坐下與遊戲的情境草圖。

sections.heading: Woven Ground - A Web for Lingering
sections.body: A sunken walkway is a place built for leaving, a ring of steps and tunnels that people cross without looking up. This project began by questioning that habit of haste and proposing that a city crossing might hold people the way a web holds dew. Two quiet teachers from nature shaped the reasoning, the spider web that ties countless threads into a single shared surface and the plant vessel that lifts water patiently from below. Sketches translate both into ribs that gather, twist and rise, and slotted board models test whether such a lattice can be at once wall, roof and room. Their shadows already suggest the dappled ground that the final tower would cast. In the proposal the mesh swells above the ring, carrying a spiral stair, small bridges and sheltered seats within its folds. The guidance favoured moving from a natural principle to a spatial one, and the scenario drawings confirm the result through ordinary acts of climbing, sitting and play. The work reveals how a borrowed structure from the living world can turn a passage into a gathering place.

zh-Hant.heading: 編織之地-為停留而織的網
zh-Hant.body: 下沉步道是一個為離開而建造的地方，一圈階梯與通道，人們穿越時從不抬頭。這個專題從質疑這種匆忙的習慣開始，並提出城市的穿越處也許能像網承接露水般承接人群。兩位來自自然的安靜老師形塑了推理：把無數絲線結成一個共享表面的蜘蛛網，以及從下方耐心提水的植物導管。草圖把兩者轉譯為聚集、扭轉並上升的肋條，開槽板模型則測試這樣的格網能否同時是牆、屋頂與房間。模型的影子已預示最終塔體將投下的斑駁地面。在提案中，網格在圓環上方膨起，在皺褶中承載螺旋梯、小橋與有遮蔽的座位。指導著重從自然原理走向空間原理，情境繪圖則透過攀爬、坐下與遊戲等日常行為印證了成果。這件作品揭示，從生命世界借來的結構，能把一條通道轉化為一處聚集之所。

pins.title: Adaptable Anatomy
pins.description:
The jumping leg of a leafy insect is studied and rebuilt as a sprawling frame of sticks, cloth and rubber rings that bends, holds and adapts like a living joint.

Physical model | Bionic structure study | Wood sticks, cloth, rubber rings, card paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 可調適的解剖
zh-Hant.description:
一種葉狀昆蟲的跳躍後腿被研究，並重建為一個由木棒、布料與橡皮圈組成的伸展框架，像有生命的關節般彎曲、支撐與調適。

實體模型｜仿生結構研究｜木棒、布料、橡皮圈、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final stick and cloth model.
最終的木棒與布料模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Small dwellings packed side by side often leave their residents with no flexible shared space. The project asked whether the anatomy of an agile insect could suggest a structure that adapts to changing needs.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 緊密並排的小型住所，常使住戶缺乏有彈性的共享空間。這個專題探問，一種靈活昆蟲的解剖構造，能否啟發一個能隨需求改變而調適的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A line drawing traced the body of a leafy insect related to the locust. Studies then examined how the muscles of its hind leg fold and release the joint.
captions: The leafy insect at the centre, a katydid, hidden among leaves.
A line drawing of the insect.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張線描勾勒出一種與蝗蟲相近的葉狀昆蟲身體。接著的研究檢視了其後腿肌肉如何摺疊與釋放關節。
captions: 隱身於葉間、位於中央的葉狀昆蟲螽斯。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small stick models were loaded and tilted to test stability, and a loose bundle of sticks tested flexibility. Rubber rings acted as tendons that let each joint bend and recover.
captions: A flexibility test of a stick bundle.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 小型木棒模型被施加荷重並傾斜以測試穩定性，一束鬆散的木棒則測試柔韌性。橡皮圈扮演肌腱的角色，讓每個關節能彎曲並回復。
captions: 木棒關節的穩定性測試。
一束木棒的柔韌性測試。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model spreads a dense frame of sticks over card blocks, with translucent cloth caught between the members. It reads as both a creature poised to leap and a shelter that can stretch.
captions: An oblique view of the final model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型在卡紙塊體上方展開一個密集的木棒框架，半透明布料被夾在構件之間。它既像一隻蓄勢跳躍的生物，也像一處能夠伸展的庇護所。

sections.heading: Living Joint - Shelter Poised to Leap
sections.body: The hind leg of a jumping insect is a small marvel of stored energy, a lever that folds tightly and then releases in an instant. This project turned that anatomy toward a human concern, the cramped dwellings that leave no room for shared and changing use. A careful line drawing of the insect opens the inquiry, and close sketches of the leg follow the path of muscle across the joint. From observation the work moves to testing. Little frames of sticks are tilted and weighted until they hold, while a loose bundle is flexed to discover how far it can give. Rubber rings become tendons, letting each member bend and return. The guidance asked for a principle drawn from nature to be proven through making, and the final model answers with a sprawling frame over solid blocks, threaded with pale cloth. It seems at once a creature about to spring and a canopy ready to extend. The work shows how biological insight can lend architecture a responsive and almost animate character.

zh-Hant.heading: 活的關節-蓄勢跳躍的庇護
zh-Hant.body: 跳躍昆蟲的後腿是儲存能量的小小奇蹟，一根緊緊摺起、又在瞬間釋放的槓桿。這個專題把這種解剖構造轉向一個人的關切：狹窄的住所沒有留給共享與變化用途的空間。一張細心的昆蟲線描開啟了探究，腿部的近距離草圖則追蹤肌肉跨越關節的路徑。作品從觀察走向測試。小小的木棒框架被傾斜、被加重，直到能夠站穩；一束鬆散的木棒則被彎曲，以探知它能退讓多少。橡皮圈成為肌腱，讓每個構件彎曲又回復。指導要求從自然汲取的原理必須透過製作來證明，最終模型以一個伸展於實心塊體上方、穿插淺色布料的框架作出回應。它彷彿同時是一隻即將躍起的生物，也是一頂準備延展的篷蓋。這件作品說明，生物的洞見能賦予建築一種回應環境、幾近有生命的性格。

pins.title: Experiencing Textiles
pins.description:
The steps of making silk, from silkworm to loom, become a landscape of mesh, ribbon and clay, followed by folded card models that turn the act of weaving into space.

Physical model | Textile process study | Card paper, film, thread, wire, clay, wood sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 體驗織物
zh-Hant.description:
製絲的步驟，從蠶到織機，化為一片由網、緞帶與黏土構成的地景，隨後以摺疊卡紙模型把編織的動作轉化為空間。

實體模型｜織物製程研究｜卡紙、薄膜、線、鐵絲、黏土、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The textiles model in four stages.
分為四個階段的織物模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Silk weaving is an old craft whose steps are rarely seen as a spatial sequence. The project asked how the journey from silkworm to cloth could be experienced as a series of spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 絲織是一門古老的工藝，其步驟很少被視為一個空間序列。這個專題探問，從蠶到布料的旅程，如何能被體驗為一連串的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: An old scroll painting of silkworm rearing and silk weaving was studied for its many types of machines. Freehand sketches then recorded how each loom pulls, twists and crosses its threads.
captions: The Painting of Silkworm Rearing and Silk Weaving, the earliest Chinese painting of these techniques.
Different types of weaving machines in the scroll.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一幅描繪養蠶與絲織的古老卷軸畫被研究，以了解其中多種機具。接著的手繪草圖記錄了每台織機如何拉、捻與交織絲線。
captions: 《蠶織圖》，中國最早記錄養蠶與織絲技術的畫作。
畫卷中不同類型的織機。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first model laid out four stages, silkworm, reeling, neatening and weaving, as clusters of clay cubes, wire mesh and iridescent ribbon. Interior views with small red figures showed how a visitor might walk through each stage.
captions: Close views of ribbon and mesh.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一件模型把養蠶、繅絲、整絲與織造四個階段，佈置為黏土方塊、鐵絲網與彩虹色緞帶的群組。帶有小型紅色人形的內部視角，呈現參觀者如何走過每一個階段。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Later models extended the idea of weaving into folded card triangles held on thin sticks. Seen from above and from the side, the planes interlock like threads crossing on a loom.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 後續的模型把編織的概念延伸為以細木棒支撐的摺疊卡紙三角形。從上方與側面看，這些面如同織機上交錯的絲線般相互咬合。

sections.heading: Thread Into Room - A Walk Through Silk
sections.body: Cloth is so familiar that the long labour behind it disappears, and a single thread hides the patience of rearing, reeling and weaving. This project set out to make that hidden journey visible as architecture. Study began with an old scroll painting that records each step of silk making, and freehand sketches followed the logic of its looms, the way a frame pulls, twists and crosses fibres into order. The first model arranges the process as a landscape. Clay cubes gather like cocoons, wire mesh stretches into drawn filaments, and iridescent ribbon sweeps through the air as finished silk. Tiny red figures placed inside reveal the intention, a route along which a visitor would experience the making of cloth with the body rather than the eye alone. The guidance encouraged a second, more abstract step, and folded card triangles on slender sticks answer it, interlocking like warp and weft. The work demonstrates how a traditional craft can become a rich and legible spatial narrative.

zh-Hant.heading: 從絲到室-穿行絲中的旅程
zh-Hant.body: 布料如此熟悉，以致其背後漫長的勞動消失不見，一根絲線隱藏了養蠶、繅絲與織造的耐心。這個專題著手把這段隱藏的旅程以建築的形式呈現。研究從一幅記錄製絲每個步驟的古老卷軸畫開始，手繪草圖接著追隨其織機的邏輯，也就是框架如何把纖維拉、捻、交織成秩序。第一件模型把製程佈置成一片地景。黏土方塊如繭般聚集，鐵絲網延展成抽出的細絲，彩虹色的緞帶則作為完成的絲綢掠過空中。置於其中的細小紅色人形揭示了用意：一條讓參觀者以身體而非僅以眼睛體驗製布過程的路徑。指導鼓勵再走一步、更加抽象，以細木棒支撐的摺疊卡紙三角形回應了這一點，如經線與緯線般相互咬合。這件作品展現，一門傳統工藝能成為豐富而清晰可讀的空間敘事。

pins.title: Space Within a Space
pins.description:
Section drawings of a dried loofah reveal pockets nested within pockets, an idea rebuilt as a curling card model and a dense illustration of a shoebox world.

Physical model and illustration | Observation to space | Card paper, ink | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間中的空間
zh-Hant.description:
乾絲瓜的剖面圖揭示了層層相套的孔隙，這個想法被重建為一件捲曲的卡紙模型，以及一幅描繪鞋盒世界的密集插畫。

實體模型與插畫｜從觀察到空間｜卡紙、墨水｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A loofah is a common household tool, yet its fibrous interior holds a remarkable structure of nested voids. The project asked how this hidden order could become a model of spaces within spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 絲瓜是常見的家用工具，然而其纖維內部蘊含著由層層相套的空隙構成的驚人結構。這個專題探問，這種隱藏的秩序如何能成為一件空間中的空間模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Section studies drew the loofah cut lengthwise and across, recording its veins and chambers. Overlapping circles and fragment sketches then abstracted these patterns into curved lines.
captions: The loofah, a common tool in Chinese homes for washing dishes or showering.
A section drawing of the loofah.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 剖面研究描繪了絲瓜的縱切與橫切，記錄其纖維脈絡與腔室。重疊的圓與碎片草圖接著把這些圖案抽象為曲線。
captions: 絲瓜絡的剖面研究（橫切）。
絲瓜絡，華人家庭中常用來洗碗或洗澡的工具。

sections.heading: Development
