sections.body: Strips of card were curled and set upright to turn the drawn curves into walls. The walls wrap small rooms inside larger ones, so that each pocket opens into another.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 卡紙條被捲曲並直立，把繪出的曲線轉化為牆。這些牆把小房間包在大房間之內，使每個凹處都通向另一個凹處。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A creative illustration then imagined the nested spaces as a shoebox world crowded with stairs, rooms and figures. Small panels at its side show fragments of the same dense city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 接著一幅創意插畫把層層相套的空間想像為一個擠滿樓梯、房間與人物的鞋盒世界。旁邊的小幅畫面呈現了同一座密集城市的片段。

sections.heading: Nested Hollows - Rooms Grown From a Gourd
sections.body: The most ordinary objects often conceal the most elaborate interiors, and a dried loofah, used daily for washing, is a labyrinth of fibre and void. This project began by slowing down to draw it. Sections taken along and across the gourd record veins that branch, chambers that open into further chambers, and a centre that is never quite solid. Overlapping circles and scattered fragments then distil the pattern into a vocabulary of curves. The physical model gives that vocabulary a body. Strips of card are curled and stood on edge until they form walls, and the walls wrap rooms within rooms so that every hollow leads to another. The guidance asked for a clear path from observation to spatial idea, and the sequence of drawing, abstraction and making traces it faithfully. A dense illustration carries the thought further, imagining a shoebox world packed with stairs and inhabitants. The work shows how patient looking at a humble object can open an inventive understanding of nested space.

zh-Hant.heading: 層套之空-從瓜中長出的房間
zh-Hant.body: 最平凡的物件往往隱藏最精巧的內部，一條每天用來清洗的乾絲瓜，就是一座由纖維與空隙組成的迷宮。這個專題從放慢腳步描繪它開始。沿著與橫越瓜身所取的剖面，記錄了分岔的脈絡、通向更多腔室的腔室，以及一個從未真正實心的中心。重疊的圓與散落的碎片接著把圖案提煉為一套曲線語彙。實體模型賦予這套語彙一個形體。卡紙條被捲曲並立起，直到形成牆，牆又把房間包在房間之內，使每一處空隙都通向另一處。指導要求從觀察到空間構想有一條清楚的路徑，繪圖、抽象與製作的序列忠實地描出了它。一幅密集的插畫把思考推得更遠，想像一個擠滿樓梯與居民的鞋盒世界。這件作品說明，耐心凝視一件樸素的物件，能開啟對層套空間富有創意的理解。

pins.title: Redefined Cells
pins.description:
The parts of a living cell are reimagined as a hand-sized sculpture of coloured clay, wire, wax and thread, where each organelle becomes a room, a channel or a shell.

Physical model | Cell structure study | Paper clay, wire, wax, thread, moldable plastic, oil paint | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重新定義的細胞
zh-Hant.description:
活細胞的各個部分被重新想像為一件手掌大小、以彩色黏土、鐵絲、蠟與線製成的雕塑，每個胞器都成為一個房間、一條通道或一層外殼。

實體模型｜細胞結構研究｜紙黏土、鐵絲、蠟、線、可塑性塑膠、油彩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A cell is usually met as a flat diagram in a textbook, its parts named but never inhabited. The project asked how its organelles could be redefined as spatial elements with their own character.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 細胞通常以教科書中的平面圖解出現，各部分有名稱卻從未被居住。這個專題探問，其胞器如何能被重新定義為各具性格的空間元素。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A pencil sketch studied the cell membrane, nucleus and folded inner structures. A coloured drawing then tested how these parts might stack as a single object.
captions: A pencil sketch of the cell.
A coloured drawing of the cell.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張鉛筆草圖研究了細胞膜、細胞核與摺疊的內部結構。接著一張彩色繪圖測試這些部分如何能堆疊成單一物件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Annotated sketches assigned a material to each part, such as clay for shells, wire for channels and wax for soft tissue. They also noted where each part should be rigid, flexible or translucent.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 附註的草圖為每個部分指定材料，例如以黏土做外殼、以鐵絲做通道、以蠟做柔軟組織。草圖也註明每個部分應該堅硬、柔韌或半透明的位置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished piece gathers a green folded shell, a purple core, orange strands and a dark textured block into one dense body. Upright, it reads like a small building whose rooms are grown rather than built.
captions: Holding the cell model by hand.
The cell model held from another side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的作品把綠色摺疊外殼、紫色核心、橘色細絲與深色質感塊體聚合成一個密集的形體。直立時，它讀起來像一棟小建築，其房間是長出來而非建造出來的。
captions: 從另一側手持的細胞模型。

sections.heading: Inner Dwelling - Organelles as Rooms
sections.body: Every living body is composed of cells, yet the cell is rarely imagined as a place, only as a diagram of labelled parts. This project asked what might happen if those parts were treated as rooms, passages and walls. A quiet pencil study begins the inquiry, drawing the membrane, the nucleus and the folded inner layers with the care of an architectural plan. A coloured drawing then gathers them into a single object, and annotated sketches assign each part a material and a behaviour, clay for protective shells, wire for channels, wax for soft and luminous tissue. The finished sculpture is small enough to hold, yet it carries the density of a city. A green shell folds over a purple core, bright strands spill outward, and a dark textured block anchors the whole. The guidance encouraged reading scientific form as spatial form, and the model answers with conviction. The work shows how the smallest unit of life can inspire a vivid and inventive architecture of the interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 內在居所-作為房間的胞器
zh-Hant.body: 每個生命體都由細胞組成，然而細胞很少被想像為一個場所，而只是一張標註各部分的圖解。這個專題探問，如果把這些部分當作房間、通道與牆，會發生什麼。一張安靜的鉛筆研究開啟了探究，以繪製建築平面的細心描繪細胞膜、細胞核與摺疊的內層。接著一張彩色繪圖把它們聚合為單一物件，附註草圖則為每個部分指定材料與行為：以黏土做保護的外殼，以鐵絲做通道，以蠟做柔軟而透光的組織。完成的雕塑小到可以握在手中，卻承載著一座城市的密度。綠色外殼摺覆在紫色核心之上，明亮的細絲向外溢出，深色的質感塊體穩住整體。指導鼓勵把科學的形態讀作空間的形態，模型以堅定的姿態作出回應。這件作品說明，生命最小的單位能啟發一種鮮明而富創意的內部建築。

pins.title: From 2D to 3D
pins.description:
A flat mesh of triangles is lifted, layer by layer, into a faceted cardboard landscape whose shards hang from above and climb from below.

Physical model | Geometric construction study | Cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從二維到三維
zh-Hant.description:
一片平面的三角形網格被逐層抬升，成為一座多面的紙板地景，碎片從上方垂掛、從下方攀升。

實體模型｜幾何構成研究｜紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The twin triangle model in full height.
雙層三角模型的全高視圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A triangle is stable, concise and able to form endless variations, yet on paper it has no thickness. The project asked how a flat triangular pattern could become a space that can be touched.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 三角形穩定、簡潔，並能形成無盡的變化，但在紙上它沒有厚度。這個專題探問，一個平面的三角圖案如何能成為一個可觸摸的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A line drawing covered a sheet with irregular triangles of many sizes. This mesh became the plan from which every vertical piece would grow.
captions: Inspiration: a crowded market stall with signs, the source of the triangle pattern.
A line drawing of the triangle mesh.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張線描以大小不一的不規則三角形鋪滿紙面。這張網格成為每一片垂直構件生長的平面依據。
captions: 靈感：掛滿招牌的擁擠市場攤位，三角形圖案的來源。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Vertical triangles of hard board were glued onto a cut base, turning the drawing into a faceted platform between two and three dimensions. A second platform was then made in the same way.
captions: Early stages of the board platform.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 硬紙板的垂直三角形被黏在切割好的基座上，把繪圖轉化為介於二維與三維之間的多面平台。接著以同樣方式製作了第二座平台。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The two platforms were joined face to face with vertical triangles rising from the centre. The finished model reads like two worlds of opposite gravity linked by a rocky spine.
captions: A low view of the joined model.
A frontal view of the model.
A close view of the shards.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩座平台面對面接合，垂直三角形從中心升起。完成的模型讀來像兩個重力相反的世界，由一道岩石般的脊線相連。
captions: 接合後模型的低角度視圖。

sections.heading: Stubborn Facets - Triangles Rising Into Space
sections.body: A triangle is the most stubborn of shapes, a figure that cannot be pushed out of form without breaking. This project took that stubbornness as its premise and asked how a flat field of triangles, drawn without thickness, might rise into a body that can be touched and entered. The reasoning begins on paper, where a mesh of irregular triangles is traced across the sheet like a map of tension. On a cut board base, vertical triangles are then glued edge to edge, producing a faceted platform that sits between drawing and object. Repeating the platform and joining two of them face to face completes the move into three dimensions. Shards now hang from above and climb from below, meeting along a rugged central spine. The guidance encouraged a single rule to be pushed until it produced space, and the resulting model invites speculative readings, from twin worlds with opposite gravity to a tower that binds two cities. The work shows how a modest geometric constraint can generate a rich and unexpected architecture of light and shadow.

zh-Hant.heading: 固執的面-升入空間的三角
zh-Hant.body: 三角形是最固執的形狀，一個不破裂便無法被推離原形的圖形。這個專題以這份固執為前提，探問一片沒有厚度、平面繪製的三角形場域，如何升起為一個可觸摸、可進入的形體。推理從紙上開始，一張不規則三角形的網格像張力地圖般鋪滿紙面。接著在切割的板材基座上，垂直的三角形邊對邊黏合，形成介於繪圖與物件之間的多面平台。重複這個平台，再把兩座面對面接合，便完成了走向三維的一步。碎片如今從上方垂掛、從下方攀升，沿著一道崎嶇的中央脊線相遇。指導鼓勵把單一規則推演到底直到產生空間，完成的模型也引發種種想像，從重力相反的雙生世界，到連結兩座城市的高塔。這件作品顯示，一個樸素的幾何限制，能生成一種豐富而出人意料的光影建築。

pins.title: Separation and Condensation
pins.description:
Small cardboard boxes are tested in many combinations and then hung at different heights inside a cubic frame of wooden sticks, each one both a room and part of a whole.

Physical model | Spatial unit study | Wooden sticks, PVC, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 分離與凝聚
zh-Hant.description:
紙板小盒以多種組合進行測試，再懸掛於木棒立方框架中的不同高度，每一個既是房間，也是整體的一部分。

實體模型｜空間單元研究｜木棒、PVC、紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The stick frame with suspended boxes.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A dwelling can be read as one container or as many small rooms that keep their own identity. The project asked how separate units could stay independent yet join into one rich interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一處居所可以被讀作單一容器，也可以是許多保有各自身分的小房間。這個專題探問，分離的單元如何能保持獨立，又結合成一個豐富的室內。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The analysis of a precedent made of stacked transparent rooms led to a set of small boxes in several sizes. These were arranged in dozens of trial positions and photographed side by side.
captions: The precedent: House NA by Sou Fujimoto.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 對一個由層疊透明房間構成的先例的分析，引出一組數種尺寸的小盒。它們被排列成數十種試驗位置，並逐一並列拍攝。
captions: 參考案例：藤本壯介的House NA。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were threaded through the boxes to tie them to an outer frame. Two small units and one large unit were then suspended at different heights.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒穿過盒體，把它們繫到外框上。接著兩個小單元與一個大單元被懸掛在不同高度。
captions: 由交錯木棒支撐的盒體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final cage holds the units in a lattice where light and sight pass freely between rooms. Shadows of the sticks layer the boxes and the ground below.
captions: The lattice against a dark ground.
A view down into the frame.
A close view among the units.
An elevation of the cubic frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的籠架把單元固定在格架中，光線與視線在房間之間自由穿梭。木棒的影子層層落在盒體與下方地面。

sections.heading: Suspended Rooms - Units Held in a Lattice
sections.body: A house can be imagined as a single container or as a gathering of many small rooms that keep their own identity while belonging to a whole. This project pursued the second idea, beginning with an analysis of a celebrated precedent of stacked, transparent living spaces and translating its lesson into a study of separation and cohesion. Small boxes in cardboard of several sizes were made and arranged in dozens of trial positions, each photographed to compare how volumes might touch, overlap or float apart. The decisive step came with a frame of wooden sticks. Rods pass through the boxes and anchor them inside a cubic cage, so that two small units and one large unit hang at different heights. Light falling through the lattice casts layered shadows, and paths of sight cross freely from one room to another. The guidance emphasised learning from a precedent without copying its form, and the outcome achieves this through a structure of its own. The work demonstrates how independence and connection can coexist within one carefully tuned spatial system.

zh-Hant.heading: 懸浮之室-格架中的單元
zh-Hant.body: 一棟房子可以被想像成單一的容器，也可以是許多小房間的聚集，各自保有身分，卻又屬於整體。這個專題追求後者，從分析一個以層疊、透明居住空間聞名的先例開始，並把其中的啟示轉譯為關於分離與凝聚的研究。數種尺寸的紙板小盒被製作出來，排列成數十種試驗位置，每一種都被拍攝下來，以比較量體如何接觸、重疊或彼此懸離。決定性的一步來自木棒框架。木棒穿過盒子，把它們固定在一個立方籠架之中，使兩個小單元與一個大單元懸掛於不同高度。穿過格架的光線投下層層陰影，視線也自由地從一個房間穿越到另一個房間。指導強調向先例學習而不複製其形式，成果正是以一套屬於自己的結構做到這一點。這件作品證明，獨立與連結能在一個仔細調校的空間系統中共存。

pins.title: Reconstitution of Soccer
pins.description:
A ball is taken apart along its seams, and its hexagon and pentagon panels are rejoined into curved canopies on wooden sticks, forming an open pavilion.

Physical model | Object disassembly study | Ball panels, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 足球的重組
zh-Hant.description:
一顆球沿著縫線被拆開，六邊形與五邊形的板片重新接合為木棒上的彎曲篷蓋，形成一座開放的展亭。

實體模型｜物件拆解研究｜球體板片、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The pavilion model as a whole.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An ordinary ball is built from twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons, a geometry hidden in an everyday object. The project asked what space could be made by taking that object apart and rebuilding it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一顆普通的球由二十個六邊形與十二個五邊形構成，這是隱藏在日常物件中的幾何。這個專題探問，拆開這個物件再重建，能創造出什麼樣的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The ball was dismantled along its sewn edges to obtain a flat material of linked polygons. Cutting and testing showed how far the panels could bend and still hold a shape.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 球沿著縫邊被拆解，得到一種由相連多邊形構成的平面材料。裁切與測試顯示板片能彎曲到什麼程度，仍保有形狀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Panels were seamed back into curved shells and raised on slender sticks. Each shell began to define a pocket of space beneath it.
captions: The process in five steps: dismantling, cutting, testing, creating space and seaming the football.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 板片被重新縫合為彎曲的殼，並以纖細的木棒撐起。每一片殼開始在其下方界定出一處空間。
captions: 五個步驟的過程：拆解、裁切、測試、創造空間與縫合足球。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model gathers the shells into a pavilion of canopies at different heights, with soft fibre drifting like clouds above. Small figures show sheltered pockets, thresholds and open ground for gathering.
captions: A cluster of seamed football panels.
The pavilion with lettered football panels.
A canopy raised on a stick.
A view under a curved shell.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把殼體聚集成一座高低不一的篷蓋展亭，柔軟纖維如雲般飄浮其上。小人形顯示出有遮蔽的凹處、門檻與供人聚集的開放地面。
captions: 帶有足球字樣片材的展亭。
帶有柔軟纖維雲朵的篷蓋。

sections.heading: Unstitched Sphere - Canopies From a Ball
sections.body: An ordinary ball is a quiet piece of geometry, twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons stitched into a sphere that most people never think to question. This project began by taking that familiar object apart along its seams, turning a closed surface into a family of flat panels that could be reassembled into something new. The process moved through stages of dismantling, cutting, testing, seaming and finally creating space. Panels were rejoined into curved shells and lifted on slender wooden sticks, so that the old skin of the ball became a series of canopies resting at different heights. Under the shells, small figures reveal sheltered pockets, gentle thresholds and an open ground for gathering. Soft fibre placed among the roofs suggests clouds drifting over a landscape. The guidance encouraged the disassembly of an everyday object as a route to spatial invention, and the model rewards this with a pavilion of generous light and openness. The work shows how reconfiguring a known form can yield architecture that feels both playful and structurally intelligent.

zh-Hant.heading: 拆線之球-從球而生的篷蓋
zh-Hant.body: 一顆普通的球是一件安靜的幾何作品，二十個六邊形與十二個五邊形縫合成一個球體，多數人從未想過要質疑它。這個專題從沿著縫線拆解這個熟悉的物件開始，把封閉的表面轉化為一組平面的板片，再重組為新的事物。過程經歷拆解、裁切、測試、縫合，最後創造空間等階段。板片被重新接合為彎曲的殼，並以纖細的木棒撐起，讓球原本的外皮成為一系列停駐於不同高度的篷蓋。殼體之下，小小的人形揭示了有遮蔽的凹處、柔和的門檻，以及供人聚集的開放地面。置於屋頂之間的柔軟纖維，彷彿雲朵飄過一片地景。指導鼓勵以拆解日常物件作為空間創造的途徑，模型則以一座充滿光線與開放感的展亭回應。這件作品顯示，重新配置一個已知的形體，能產生既富趣味又具結構智慧的建築。

pins.title: Walkway of Infinity
pins.description:
A spiral cut from a paper disc is twisted into a loop with one surface and then rebuilt in wooden slats as an endless walking path.

Physical model | Pavilion and path study | Paper, wooden slats | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無限之徑
zh-Hant.description:
從圓形紙片裁出的螺旋被扭轉成只有一個面的迴圈，再以木條重建為一條無盡的步行路徑。

實體模型｜展亭與路徑研究｜紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wooden slat path from above.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The cross section of a rolled cake shows one line spiralling out from its centre, a ring that could be pulled straight. The project asked how such a line might become a path that people walk.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 捲蛋糕的切面顯示一條從中心旋出的線，一個可以被拉直的環。這個專題探問，這樣一條線如何能成為人們行走的路徑。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A paper disc was cut into one continuous spiral and coaxed upward into a standing ribbon. A rendered pavilion tested how the ribbon could sit on open ground.
captions: The cut spiral lifted by hand into a standing ribbon.
A photomontage of the ribbon pavilion in front of the Broad Art Center.
A spiral cut from a paper disc.
A render of the ribbon pavilion.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張圓形紙片被裁成一條連續螺旋，再被引導向上成為站立的緞帶。一張展亭渲染圖測試了緞帶如何置於開放地面上。
captions: 以手提起、成為直立緞帶的剪紙螺旋。
緞帶展亭置於Broad Art Center前的合成照片。
從圓形紙片裁出的螺旋。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Instead of lifting the strip, its two ends were twisted and joined so the loop has only one surface. Paper studies with small red figures tested many such knots.
captions: Twisting and joining the paper loops by hand.
Gluing the wooden slats into the loop by hand.
A paper loop with one surface.
A loop with figures for scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不只是把紙帶提起，而是把兩端扭轉後接合，使迴圈只有一個面。帶有紅色小人形的紙模型測試了許多這樣的扭結。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rebuilds the loop in countless wooden slats set at shifting angles. The ribbon gains rhythm and grain and coils across the base like a path without end.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以無數角度變化的木條重建迴圈。緞帶獲得節奏與紋理，像一條沒有終點的路徑般在基座上盤繞。

sections.heading: Endless Ribbon - A Path With One Surface
sections.body: A rolled sponge cake, sliced across, reveals a single line spiralling outward from its centre, a ring that could in principle be pulled straight. This project began with that small observation and asked how such a line might become a path. A paper disc was cut into a continuous spiral and coaxed upward until the flat drawing stood as a three dimensional ribbon. The next move was more radical. Instead of simply lifting the strip, its two ends were twisted and joined, producing a loop with only one surface, and a series of paper studies tested many such knots with tiny red figures for scale. The final model translates this logic into countless wooden slats set at shifting angles, so that the ribbon gains rhythm, depth and a tactile grain. Seen from above, it coils across the base like handwriting. The guidance encouraged a sustained dialogue between drawing, folding and building, and the resulting path suggests a walk without end. The work reveals how a simple topological idea can open an architecture of endless movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 無盡緞帶-只有一面的路徑
zh-Hant.body: 把一卷蛋糕橫向切開，會看見一條從中心向外旋出的線，一個理論上可以被拉直的環。這個專題從這個小小的觀察出發，探問這樣一條線如何成為一條路徑。一張圓形紙片被裁成連續的螺旋，再被輕輕引導向上，直到平面圖形成為一條立體的緞帶。下一步更為大膽。不只是把紙帶提起，而是把兩端扭轉後接合，形成只有一個面的迴圈，一系列紙模型以微小的紅色人形為尺度，測試了許多這樣的扭結。最終模型把這套邏輯轉譯為無數以變化角度排列的木條，使緞帶獲得節奏、深度與可觸摸的紋理。從上方看去，它像書寫的筆跡般在基座上盤繞。指導鼓勵繪圖、摺疊與建造之間持續的對話，完成的路徑則暗示一段沒有終點的漫步。這件作品揭示，一個簡單的拓撲構想，能開啟一種無盡移動的建築。

pins.title: Tower of Four Turnings
pins.description:
Four phases of a story are distilled into symbols and stacked as a tall tower of sticks, branches, folded paper and netting, rising from a tangled base to a crown of shards.

Physical model | Narrative tower study | Wood sticks, branches, paper, stockings, coloured film, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 四轉之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一個故事的四個階段被提煉為符號，疊成一座由木棒、樹枝、摺紙與網構成的高塔，從糾結的基座升向碎片之冠。

實體模型｜敘事塔體研究｜木棒、樹枝、紙、絲襪、彩色膠片、鐵線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A story of revolt moves through four phases, from a first spark to a loop that returns to tyranny. The project asked how these phases could be stacked as spaces in one vertical structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個反抗的故事經歷四個階段，從最初的火花到重返暴政的循環。這個專題探問，這些階段如何能作為空間，疊放在一個垂直結構之中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Collages for each phase were reduced to symbols such as a cage, a spiral stair, a forest and a stage. A tall sketch then stacked these symbols into a single tower.
captions: A sketch stacking the symbols into a tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個階段的拼貼被簡化為牢籠、螺旋梯、森林與舞台等符號。接著一張高聳的草圖把這些符號疊成一座塔。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The top, the middle and the bottom were built as separate studies in folded paper, branches and sticks. A ring of curved paper was added as an element of flowing water around the core.
captions: Stages of the base and lower floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 頂部、中段與底部分別以摺紙、樹枝與木棒製作研究模型。一圈彎曲的紙帶被加入，成為環繞核心的流水元素。
captions: 基座與下層的各個階段。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final tower rises from a nest of branches and netting through rings of paper to a crown of coloured shards. Each level keeps its own material, so the climb reads as a passage through changing worlds.
captions: The tower against a dark ground.
The crown and the paper rings.
Sticks and coloured film at the base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的塔從樹枝與網的巢中升起，穿過紙環，抵達彩色碎片之冠。每一層保有各自的材料，使攀升讀來像穿越不斷變化的世界。
captions: 基座的木棒與彩色膠片。

sections.heading: Stacked Phases - A Story Built Upward
sections.body: Stories of revolt often move in circles, beginning with a spark of hope and ending in a new form of control. This project took such a narrative arc and asked whether its four phases could be translated into architecture arranged along a single vertical line. Collages for each phase were distilled into compact symbols, a cage, a spiral stair, a forest, a stage, and a tall sketch stacked them one above another. The making proceeded in parts. A crown of folded paper and coloured film, a middle zone wrapped in rings of curved paper that evoke flowing water, and a base of branches, sticks and netting were each tested before being joined. The resulting tower ascends from a tangled nest toward a glittering summit, and every level retains a distinct material voice. The guidance encouraged a disciplined passage from narrative to symbol and from symbol to structure, so that emotion is carried by matter rather than illustration. The work shows how storytelling can become a spatial sequence that is climbed, not merely read.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊層之境-向上建造的故事
zh-Hant.body: 反抗的故事往往循環往復，始於希望的火花，終於一種新的控制。這個專題取用這樣的敘事弧線，探問其四個階段能否被轉譯為沿著單一垂直線排列的建築。每個階段的拼貼被提煉為簡潔的符號，牢籠、螺旋梯、森林、舞台，一張高聳的草圖把它們逐一往上疊放。製作分段進行。以摺紙與彩色膠片構成的冠頂，以彎曲紙環包覆、喚起流水意象的中段，以及由樹枝、木棒與網構成的基座，都先各自測試再接合起來。完成的塔從糾結的巢穴升向閃爍的頂端，每一層都保有獨特的材料語彙。指導鼓勵一條嚴謹的路徑，從敘事到符號，再從符號到結構，讓情感由物質承載，而非由圖像說明。這件作品顯示，說故事可以成為一段被攀登、而不只是被閱讀的空間序列。

pins.title: Forest of Pressing Planes
pins.description:
Feelings of oppression are drawn as dense line compositions, cut into squares and rebuilt as a crowded field of thin board planes and arcs.

Physical model | Emotion-to-space study | PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 壓迫之林
zh-Hant.description:
壓迫的感受被畫成密集的線條構成，切成方格，再重建為一片擁擠的薄板與弧線場域。

實體模型｜情感空間研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished model of crowded planes.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Research and care work with patients led to four terms for feelings of depression, from sensitivity to hopelessness. The project asked how the feeling of oppression could be made into a space that presses on the body.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 研究與照護病患的經驗，歸納出描述憂鬱感受的四個詞，從敏感到絕望。這個專題探問，壓迫感如何能成為一個壓向身體的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: An abstract composition of dense, swirling lines was drawn over an imagined urban terrain. Two versions were combined into one restless field of texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張由密集旋繞線條構成的抽象構圖，畫在一片想像的城市地形之上。兩個版本被結合為一片躁動的紋理場域。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The drawing was cut into a grid of squares so that each fragment could become a block of space. Stacked strips then tested how the flat lines could rise into three dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 構圖被切成方格網，讓每一片段都能成為一塊空間。接著疊放的板條測試了平面線條如何升入三維。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model packs tall planes, fins and loose arcs onto one base until little open ground remains. Narrow gaps and steep walls make the space feel close and heavy.
captions: The model from the other end.
A low view of the planes.
A low view of the fins and arcs.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型在同一基座上塞滿高聳的板片、鰭片與鬆散的弧線，幾乎不留空地。狹窄的縫隙與陡峭的牆，讓空間顯得逼近而沉重。
captions: 鰭片與弧線的低角度視圖。

sections.heading: Crowded Fins - Oppression Given Form
sections.body: Oppression is felt before it is named, a weight that narrows breath and shrinks the world. This project began from careful research and from time spent caring for patients, distilling the experience of depression into four terms and choosing oppression as the one to be built. An abstract composition of dense, swirling lines was drawn across an imagined terrain, and two versions were merged into one restless field. Cutting the drawing into a grid of squares turned each fragment into a potential block of space, while early stacks of strips tested how a line might grow into height. The final model crowds tall planes, thin fins and loose arcs onto a single base, leaving almost no open ground. Narrow gaps and sheer walls make the interior close and heavy, and sweeping curves trap the gaze rather than release it. The guidance encouraged a responsible and empathetic translation of feeling into form, grounded in research rather than spectacle. The work demonstrates how architecture can give silent suffering a legible spatial presence.

zh-Hant.heading: 擁擠的鰭-被賦形的壓迫
zh-Hant.body: 壓迫在被命名之前便已被感受，那是一種使呼吸變窄、使世界縮小的重量。這個專題從細緻的研究與照護病患的時光出發，把憂鬱的經驗提煉為四個詞，並選擇以壓迫作為要建造的那一個。一張由密集旋繞線條構成的抽象構圖畫在一片想像的地形上，兩個版本再融合為一片躁動的場域。把構圖切成方格網，讓每一片段都成為潛在的空間塊體，早期的板條堆疊則測試線條如何長出高度。最終模型在單一基座上塞滿高聳的板片、薄鰭與鬆散的弧線，幾乎不留空地。狹窄的縫隙與陡直的牆讓內部逼近而沉重，掃過的曲線困住視線而非釋放它。指導鼓勵以負責而具同理的方式把感受轉譯為形式，立基於研究而非奇觀。這件作品證明，建築能讓沉默的痛苦獲得可被閱讀的空間存在。

pins.title: Layers of Drift
pins.description:
Flowing sketches of a feeling of aimlessness are built up as hundreds of thin layers of board into a twisting sculpture with hidden gaps.

Physical model | Emotion-to-space study | PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂移之層
zh-Hant.description:
描繪漫無目的感受的流動草圖，以數百層薄板堆疊成一件帶有隱藏縫隙的扭轉雕塑。

實體模型｜情感空間研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Aimlessness is a feeling of drifting with no clear way ahead. The project asked how a flowing form could leave visitors unsure of where each opening leads.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 漫無目的是一種沒有明確前路的漂移感。這個專題探問，一個流動的形體如何能讓參觀者無法確定每個開口通往何處。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Quick sketches tested flowing shells with gaps that close or open as the viewpoint changes. Notes on the page call for layers that overlap and point in different directions.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 快速草圖測試了流動的殼體，其縫隙隨視點改變而開合。頁面上的筆記要求層層重疊、指向不同方向。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A smooth concept model gave the form its overall twist. Rebuilding it in stacked thin layers added contour lines and soft shadows.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一個平滑的概念模型賦予形體整體的扭轉。以疊放的薄層重建後，增添了等高線與柔和的陰影。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A drawing of crossing lines imagined the interior as a web that reflects sensitivity. The final sculpture sweeps and folds so that its gaps are glimpsed only from certain angles.
captions: A drawing of the woven interior.
A close view of the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一張交錯線條的繪圖把內部想像為一張反映敏感的網。最終的雕塑掃動、摺疊，使其縫隙只能從特定角度瞥見。

sections.heading: Drifting Strata - A Form That Withholds Direction
sections.body: To feel aimless is to drift without a horizon, moving yet arriving nowhere. This project set out to give that sensation a body, asking how a form could leave its visitors uncertain about where each opening might lead. Rapid sketches explored flowing shells whose gaps appear and vanish as the viewpoint shifts, and handwritten notes urged layers that overlap and point in different directions. A smooth concept model first fixed the overall twist of the mass. Rebuilt in hundreds of thin stacked layers, the form gained contour lines, soft shadow and a sense of slow geological movement. A drawing of crossing lines then imagined the interior as a woven web, a registering of sensitivity beneath the calm skin. In the final sculpture, sweeping folds conceal and reveal passages, so that orientation must be continually renegotiated. The guidance encouraged moving between sketch, model and drawing to refine one precise emotional quality. The work shows how layering and curvature can make uncertainty itself a spatial experience.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂移的地層-拒絕給出方向的形體
zh-Hant.body: 感到漫無目的，就是在沒有地平線的情況下漂移，不斷移動卻無處抵達。這個專題著手為這種感受賦予形體，探問一個形體如何能讓參觀者無法確定每個開口通往何處。快速的草圖探索流動的殼體，其縫隙隨視點移動而出現又消失，手寫筆記則要求層層重疊、指向不同方向。一個平滑的概念模型先確定了量體整體的扭轉。以數百層疊放的薄片重建後，形體獲得等高線、柔和的陰影，以及一種緩慢的地質運動感。接著一張交錯線條的繪圖，把內部想像為一張編織的網，記錄著平靜表皮之下的敏感。在最終的雕塑中，掃動的摺疊隱藏又顯露通道，使方向感必須不斷被重新協商。指導鼓勵在草圖、模型與繪圖之間往返，以精煉一種精確的情感特質。這件作品顯示，層疊與曲度能讓不確定本身成為一種空間經驗。

pins.title: Loop Without End
pins.description:
A double helix is read as a loop that cannot be escaped and is built as a twisted cube of wooden sticks and cords around a spiral core.

Physical model | Emotion-to-space study | Wood sticks, black cords | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無盡之環
zh-Hant.description:
雙螺旋被讀作一個無法逃離的迴圈，並以木棒與繩索建成一個環繞螺旋核心的扭轉立方體。

實體模型｜情感空間研究｜木棒、黑繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Hopelessness can feel like being trapped in a loop or an endless path. The project asked how the twisting chain of a double helix could become a structure that holds the body inside it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 絕望可能像是被困在一個迴圈或一條沒有盡頭的路上。這個專題探問，雙螺旋扭轉的鏈如何能成為一個把身體包覆其中的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A two dimensional composition of looping curves explored entanglement. A beaded figure eight mapped traits of depression along a loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張迴旋曲線的二維構圖探索了糾纏。一個珠串構成的八字形，沿著迴圈標示憂鬱的特質。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A fan of sticks around a central axis mimicked the turning of a helix. This spiral became the core of the larger frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 繞著中心軸的扇形木棒模仿了螺旋的轉動。這個螺旋成為更大框架的核心。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final cube twists as straight sticks and cords cross from edge to edge around the spiral. The lines tighten toward the centre like chains closing in.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的立方體隨著直木棒與繩索從邊到邊環繞螺旋交錯而扭轉。線條向中心收緊，如同逐漸收攏的鎖鏈。

sections.heading: Bound Helix - Lines That Close Inward
sections.body: Hopelessness is often described as a loop, an endless path whose turns lead back to where they began. This project took that image literally and found in the double helix a figure of inheritance that cannot be shed, a chain inscribed in every body. A composition of looping curves first explored entanglement on paper, while a beaded figure eight mapped traits of depression along a closed circuit, turning clinical observation into a rhythmic diagram. A study of sticks fanned around a central axis then captured the turning motion of a helix and became the core of a larger construction. In the final model, straight sticks and black cords cross from edge to edge of a twisted cube, tightening toward the spiral at its heart like chains slowly closing in. Light passes through the frame, yet the sense of enclosure intensifies with every line. The guidance encouraged rigorous abstraction of a difficult emotion, avoiding melodrama in favour of structure. The work shows how a simple linear system can evoke confinement with clarity and restraint.

zh-Hant.heading: 受縛之螺旋-向內收攏的線
zh-Hant.body: 絕望常被描述為一個迴圈，一條轉折後又回到起點、沒有盡頭的路。這個專題把這個意象當真，在雙螺旋中找到一種無法擺脫的遺傳圖形，一條銘刻在每個身體裡的鏈。一張迴旋曲線的構圖先在紙上探索糾纏，一個珠串八字形則沿著封閉迴路標示憂鬱的特質，把臨床觀察轉化為富有節奏的圖解。接著一件繞著中心軸展開的扇形木棒研究，捕捉了螺旋的轉動，並成為更大構造的核心。在最終模型中，直木棒與黑繩從扭轉立方體的一邊交錯到另一邊，向中心的螺旋收緊，如同緩緩收攏的鎖鏈。光線穿過框架，包圍感卻隨著每一條線而加深。指導鼓勵嚴謹地抽象化一種艱難的情感，以結構取代煽情。這件作品顯示，一個簡單的線性系統能以清晰與節制喚起禁錮之感。

pins.title: Shell of Safety
pins.description:
A glass bowl is broken and rebuilt as a hard, mirrored shell, then set among tree roots and leaves so that it reflects its surroundings while hiding what lies within.

Physical model | Mixed-material spatial study | Broken glass, mirror, miniature figures | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 安全之殼
zh-Hant.description:
一只玻璃缽被打碎後重組為堅硬的鏡面外殼，再放進樹根與枝葉之間，映照周遭的一切，同時隱藏其內部。

實體模型｜複合材料空間研究｜碎玻璃、鏡面、微縮人偶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The shell of broken glass with miniature figures.
帶有微縮人偶的碎玻璃外殼。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project set out to give form to an inner sense of safety as a space. It asked whether a fragile material could be turned into a protective shell.
captions: The broken glass behind the project title.
The intact glass bowl before breaking.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題試圖把內在的安全感賦予空間形式。它探問，一種脆弱的材料能否被轉化為具保護性的外殼。
captions: 專題標題背後的碎玻璃。
打碎之前完整的玻璃缽。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Glass was studied for its many states, from clear vessel to reflective mirror. Transparency was read as exposure, while the mirror offered cover by returning the outside view.
captions: Two glass vessels studied as starting material.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究從透明器皿到反光鏡面，檢視玻璃的多種狀態。透明被理解為暴露，而鏡面則藉由反射外界景象提供遮蔽。
captions: 作為起始材料研究的兩只玻璃器皿。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The bowl was broken and its shards rebuilt into a hard, angular shell. Small red figures were placed inside to test the scale of the hidden space.
captions: The shell placed against a tree trunk.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 玻璃缽被打碎，碎片重組為堅硬而多角的外殼。內部放入紅色小人偶，用以測試隱藏空間的尺度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Set among roots and fallen leaves, the mirrored shell reflects its setting and almost disappears. The figures inside remain sheltered, yet the shell can no longer be pieced back into a whole vessel.
captions: The mirrored shell among tree roots.
Mirror shards and figures in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 置於樹根與落葉之間，鏡面外殼映照周遭而幾乎隱沒。內部的人偶得到庇護，然而外殼再也無法拼回一只完整的器皿。

sections.heading: Reflected Refuge - The Price of a Shell
sections.body: The search for shelter often begins with a wish to vanish into the surroundings. This project turned that wish into a material experiment, asking whether something as fragile as glass could become a place of protection. An intact bowl was broken deliberately, and its shards were reassembled into an angular, mirrored shell. Small red figures placed within tested the scale of a hidden interior, while the reflective surfaces returned images of bark, roots and leaves. Placed in the undergrowth, the shell dissolved into its setting, offering a quiet camouflage. Yet the act of protection carried a cost, for the broken vessel could never again be pieced into a whole. The work thus records both refuge and loss, a space that shields by fragmenting itself. The guidance encouraged a close reading of material behaviour, treating transparency and reflection as spatial conditions rather than surface effects. The study shows how an emotional idea can be pursued through careful making, so that the meaning of a space emerges from what the material is asked to endure.

zh-Hant.heading: 映照的庇護-外殼的代價
zh-Hant.body: 對庇護的追尋，往往始於想要隱沒於周遭的願望。這個專題把這份願望化為一場材料實驗，探問像玻璃這樣脆弱的東西能否成為一處保護之所。一只完整的玻璃缽被刻意打碎，碎片重新組合為多角的鏡面外殼。置於其中的紅色小人偶測試了隱藏內部的尺度，反光的表面則映回樹皮、樹根與枝葉的影像。放入林下之後，外殼消融於環境之中，形成一種安靜的偽裝。然而保護的行動帶有代價，破碎的器皿再也無法拼回完整。作品因此同時記錄了庇護與失去，一個藉由自身破碎來遮蔽的空間。指導鼓勵細讀材料的行為，把透明與反射視為空間條件，而非表面效果。這項研究顯示，情感性的構想可以透過細緻的製作來追索，使空間的意義從材料被要求承受的事物中浮現。

pins.title: Wave of Triangles
pins.description:
A drawn net of triangles is folded into paper forms and then rebuilt in wooden sticks, lifting a flat field into a curling wave that encloses a potential space.

Physical model | Geometric structure study | Paper, wooden sticks, glue | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角之浪
zh-Hant.description:
一張三角網格的繪圖被摺成紙的形體，再以木棒重建，把平坦的場域抬升為捲曲的浪，圍塑出一處潛在空間。

實體模型｜幾何結構研究｜紙、木棒、膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wooden stick wave on its base.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A photograph of dense plants against old walls suggested two layers that seem incompatible yet sympathetic. The project asked how this tension could be captured in one geometric structure.
captions: The source photograph: dense plants against old walls in the old city of Guangzhou.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一張茂密植物映襯舊牆的照片，暗示了兩個看似不相容卻彼此共鳴的層次。這個專題探問，如何以單一幾何結構捕捉這種張力。
captions: 來源照片：廣州老城區舊牆前茂密的植物。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The photograph was traced into a dense net of triangles drawn on paper. The net was then folded into faceted paper forms to test how flat geometry rises into volume.
captions: A sheet of paper form studies.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 照片被描摹為紙上一張密集的三角網格。這張網格接著被摺成多面的紙形體，測試平面幾何如何升起為體積。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each line of the pattern was rebuilt as a wooden stick, first as a flat field and then with rising peaks. The longest lengths were set vertically to connect back to the nearest points and frame the space.
captions: A close view of the stick lattice.
Peaks rising from the stick field.
The stick field seen from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 圖案中的每一條線都以木棒重建，先成為平坦的場域，再長出升起的尖峰。最長的木棒被直立放置，回接至最近的節點，框出空間。
captions: 從木棒場域升起的尖峰。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model lifts the field into a wave that curls over a sheltered hollow. Light passing through the triangles casts a second net of shadows on the ground.
captions: The wave seen from the front.
A smaller view of the curled lattice.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把場域抬升為一道浪，捲覆一處受庇護的凹室。穿過三角形的光線，在地面投下第二張陰影之網。

sections.heading: Folded Lines - A Field That Rises
sections.body: Some spaces begin not with a plan but with a way of seeing. Here a photograph of dense planting pressed against weathered walls prompted a study of two layers that resist each other yet seem to belong together. The image was traced into a net of triangles, a drawing that flattened foliage and masonry into a single geometric language. Folding that net in paper revealed how a plane can lift into faceted volume, and each fold suggested a new way of enclosing air. The next step translated every line into a wooden stick. A flat lattice gained peaks, and the longest members rose vertically to reconnect with nearby points, gradually defining a hollow. In the final model the lattice curls into a wave that shelters a quiet interior, while light filtering through the triangles draws a second net on the ground. The guidance emphasised a patient chain of translation, from image to drawing, from drawing to fold, and from fold to structure, so that every move remained legible.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺起的線-升起的場域
zh-Hant.body: 有些空間並非始於平面圖，而是始於一種觀看的方式。在這裡，一張茂密植栽緊貼斑駁牆面的照片，引發了一項關於兩個彼此抗拒卻又似乎相屬之層次的研究。影像被描摹為一張三角網格，這張繪圖把枝葉與磚石壓平為單一的幾何語言。以紙摺疊這張網格，揭示了平面如何升起為多面的體積，每一道摺痕都暗示了一種圍合空氣的新方式。下一步把每一條線轉譯為一根木棒。平坦的格構長出尖峰，最長的構件垂直升起，與鄰近節點重新連結，逐步界定出一處凹室。在最終模型中，格構捲成一道浪，庇護著安靜的內部，穿過三角形的光線則在地面畫出第二張網。指導強調一條耐心的轉譯之鏈，從影像到繪圖，從繪圖到摺紙，再從摺紙到結構，讓每一步都清晰可讀。

pins.title: The Bound
pins.description:
Twenty-two irregular paper modules are built on top of square boxes and combined like puzzle pieces into a dense cluster, with passages that let people move quickly between them.

Physical model | Modular cluster study | White card, paper, miniature figures | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 縛
zh-Hant.description:
二十二個不規則的紙模組建立在方盒之上，像拼圖般組合成密集的群體，其間的通道讓人得以在彼此之間快速移動。

實體模型｜模組群體研究｜白卡紙、紙、微縮人偶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The stacked cluster as a tower.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Highly functional buildings are often bound by utility into rigid square boxes. The project asked whether irregular forms could loosen this framework while keeping it useful.
captions: An early cluster of boxes and curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 高度功能性的建築往往被實用性束縛成僵硬的方盒。這個專題探問，不規則的形體能否在保持實用的同時鬆動這個框架。
captions: 早期由方盒與曲面構成的群體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Simple card frames were first tested as open boxes. Curved and folded additions were then sketched on top of the square to break its regularity.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 簡單的卡紙框架先被當作開放的盒子測試。接著在方形之上構想彎曲與摺疊的附加物，打破其規則性。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Twenty-two different modules were made, each a square base with its own irregular addition. Like puzzle pieces they could be combined in countless ways and linked by passages.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 製作了二十二個不同的模組，每個都是帶有獨特不規則附加物的方形基座。它們像拼圖般能以無數方式組合，並以通道相連。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final cluster reads as a dense field of boxes and curves, wrapped in creased paper. Figures placed in the gaps show narrow passages that allow quick movement between modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的群體讀來是一片由方盒與曲面構成、包覆著皺褶紙面的密集場域。置於縫隙中的人偶顯示了狹窄的通道，讓人能在模組之間快速移動。

sections.heading: Loosened Boxes - Freedom Within Limits
sections.body: Functional buildings are frequently reduced to square boxes, held in place by the demands of utility as if tied with string. This project accepted that constraint as a starting point rather than rejecting it. Each of twenty-two modules keeps a square base, yet carries its own irregular addition of curved walls, folded planes and overhangs. Treated like puzzle pieces, the modules could be combined in countless configurations, and the joints between them were tuned so that narrow passages link one unit to the next. Wrapped in creased paper, the assembled cluster gains a textile softness that tempers its density. Seen from above it reads as a compact field, while miniature figures in its gaps reveal the pace of movement through it. The guidance encouraged a rigorous system of rules paired with generous variation, so that limitation could become a generator of form. The work suggests that freedom in architecture may be found not by escaping a framework but by exploring the countless arrangements it still permits.

zh-Hant.heading: 鬆動的方盒-限制中的自由
zh-Hant.body: 功能性的建築常被簡化為方盒，被實用的要求固定在原位，彷彿以繩索綑綁。這個專題把這份限制當作起點，而非加以拒絕。二十二個模組各自保留方形基座，卻帶著由彎曲牆面、摺疊平面與懸挑構成的獨特附加物。這些模組被視為拼圖，可以組合成無數種配置，而它們之間的接合處經過調整，使狹窄的通道串連起一個又一個單元。包覆著皺褶紙面的組合群體，獲得一種織物般的柔軟，緩和了它的密度。從上方看，它讀來是一片緊湊的場域，縫隙中的微縮人偶則揭示穿行其間的節奏。指導鼓勵一套嚴謹的規則系統與豐富的變化相互搭配，使限制成為形式的生成器。這件作品暗示，建築中的自由或許不在於逃離框架，而在於探索框架仍然容許的無數種排列。

pins.title: The Skeleton
pins.description:
Thin wooden strips are joined into triangular frames and rotated step by step, building a twisting skeleton that rises, arches and folds back over itself.

Physical model and drawing | Structural rhythm study | 2 mm wooden strips, 1:1 drawing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 骨架
zh-Hant.description:
細木條被接合成三角形框架並逐步旋轉，構築出一副扭轉的骨架，向上升起、拱起，再折返覆蓋自身。

實體模型與繪圖｜結構節奏研究｜2 mm 木條、1:1 繪圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The twisting skeleton of wooden strips.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how a single repeated unit could grow into a continuous, twisting structure. It set out to give a light frame the presence of a living skeleton.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，單一重複的單元如何能長成連續而扭轉的結構。它試圖讓輕巧的框架具有活的骨架般的存在感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Flowing curves were first sketched in ink and then bent into small three-dimensional studies. A triangle was chosen as the unit, since it holds its shape while turning.
captions: Curve studies bent in three dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 流動的曲線先以墨水描繪，再彎折為小型立體研究。三角形被選為單元，因為它在轉動時仍能保持形狀。
captions: 彎折成立體的曲線研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangular frames of thin wooden strips were rotated a few degrees each and glued in sequence. The rotation produced an arch that climbs, turns and folds back over its own base.
captions: The skeleton against a dark ground.
A side view of the arch.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以細木條製成的三角框架每次旋轉幾度，依序黏合。這種旋轉生成一道拱，攀升、轉向，再折返覆蓋自身的基座。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model reads as a spine of repeated frames, dense where they overlap and open where they spread. A full-size drawing traces every frame as layered outlines.
captions: The skeleton from a low angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型讀來像一道由重複框架構成的脊骨，重疊處密集，展開處通透。一張等比例繪圖以層層疊合的輪廓描出每一個框架。

sections.heading: Turning Frames - A Spine of Repetition
sections.body: A skeleton is a structure in which repetition becomes movement, each bone a slight variation of its neighbour. This project explored that principle with the simplest of means, a triangle of thin wooden strips. Ink sketches of flowing curves and small bent studies first established the sense of motion, after which the triangle was adopted as a unit that keeps its rigidity while turning. Frame by frame, each triangle was rotated a few degrees and glued to the last, so that the sequence climbed into an arch, twisted and folded back over its own base. Where the frames overlap the structure thickens into shadow, and where they spread it opens to light, giving the model a rhythm close to breathing. A full-size drawing then recorded every frame as a layered outline, turning the object into a map of its own growth. The guidance emphasised patience with a single rule, so that complexity could arise from accumulation rather than from added ornament or arbitrary gesture.

zh-Hant.heading: 旋轉的框-重複的脊骨
zh-Hant.body: 骨架是一種讓重複化為運動的結構，每一根骨頭都是鄰近骨頭的些微變奏。這個專題以最簡單的手段探索這項原則，一個由細木條構成的三角形。流動曲線的墨水草圖與小型彎折研究先確立了運動感，之後三角形被採用為一個在轉動時仍保持剛性的單元。一框接著一框，每個三角形旋轉幾度後黏合在前一個之上，使序列攀升為一道拱，扭轉後又折返覆蓋自身的基座。框架重疊之處，結構加厚成陰影，展開之處則向光線敞開，使模型帶有近似呼吸的節奏。一張等比例繪圖隨後把每一個框架記錄為疊層輪廓，讓物件成為自身生長的地圖。指導強調對單一規則保持耐心，讓複雜性來自累積，而非來自附加的裝飾或隨意的姿態。

pins.title: Triangulated Chain
pins.description:
A random image is traced into a net of triangles, cut into pieces and rebuilt in wooden strips and card as a long chain of faceted cells that turns its inside out.

Physical model | Geometric transformation study | Cardboard, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角之鏈
zh-Hant.description:
一張隨機影像被描摹為三角網格，切分為片段，再以木條與卡紙重建為一條由多面單元構成的長鏈，把內部翻轉向外。

實體模型｜幾何轉化研究｜卡紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished chain of faceted cells.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked whether any image could become the seed of a spatial structure. It tested how a flat pattern might be opened into a sequence of enclosed cells.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，任何影像能否成為空間結構的種子。它測試平面圖案如何被展開為一連串圍合的單元。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photograph of flowers was traced into a dense net of triangles. The net was redrawn on a sheet and studied as a field of possible folds.
captions: The photograph and its triangle net.
The net redrawn on a sheet.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張花卉照片被描摹為密集的三角網格。這張網格被重新繪製在紙上，作為一片可能摺疊的場域加以研究。
captions: 重新繪製於紙上的網格。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The net was cut into continuous pieces and each piece was built as a frame of strips with card faces. Single pieces were then patched and connected into longer clusters.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 網格被切分為連續的片段，每一片都以木條為框、卡紙為面加以建構。單獨的片段接著被補綴並連接成更長的群組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stretches into a long chain whose cells alternate between open frames and closed card faces. Shadows cast through the frames show the inside of each cell turned outward.
captions: A cell from a low angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型延展為一條長鏈，其單元在開放框架與封閉卡紙面之間交替。穿過框架投下的陰影，顯示每個單元的內部被翻轉向外。

sections.heading: Folded Image - Cells Turned Outward
sections.body: Any image, however ordinary, contains a hidden geometry waiting to be drawn out. In this project a photograph of flowers was traced into a dense net of triangles, translating petals and leaves into a neutral field of lines. Redrawn on a sheet, the net became a territory of possible folds, and its continuous strands were cut into pieces that could stand alone. Each piece was then built as a frame of wooden strips, with some faces closed in card and others left open. Single pieces were patched together, connected and extended, until the cells formed a long chain that wanders across its base. Seen up close, the alternation of solid faces and empty frames lets the inside of each cell spill outward, and shadows project the original net back onto the ground. The guidance encouraged a chain of clear operations, tracing, cutting, building and connecting, so that an arbitrary starting point could still yield a disciplined spatial structure with its own internal logic and evident craft.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺起的影像-向外翻轉的單元
zh-Hant.body: 任何影像，無論多麼平凡，都藏著一種等待被描繪出來的幾何。在這個專題中，一張花卉照片被描摹為密集的三角網格，把花瓣與葉片轉譯為一片中性的線條場域。重新繪製於紙上後，網格成為一片可能摺疊的領域，其連續的線股被切分為能夠獨立的片段。每一片接著以木條建構為框架，有些面以卡紙封閉，有些則保持開放。單獨的片段被補綴、連接、延伸，直到單元形成一條橫越基座的長鏈。近看之下，實面與空框的交替讓每個單元的內部溢流向外，陰影則把原初的網格投回地面。指導鼓勵一串清晰的操作，描摹、切分、建構、連接，使一個隨意的起點仍能產生具有自身內在邏輯與明確工藝的嚴謹空間結構。

pins.title: Material Sudoku
pins.description:
Nine materials are drawn as textures on a three-by-three board and then made into small models, from brick and resin to cotton, wood and wire.

Physical models and drawing | Material study | Mixed materials as illustrated | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 材料數獨
zh-Hant.description:
九種材料先在三乘三的板上被繪成紋理，再製成小模型，從磚與樹脂到棉、木與鐵線。

實體模型與繪圖｜材料研究｜依圖示之複合材料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Three material models in a row.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how the character of a material could be read before it is used in a building. It treated nine materials as pieces on a single board.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，在材料被用於建築之前，如何解讀它的性格。它把九種材料當作同一塊板上的棋子。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each material was first drawn as a texture in one square of a three-by-three grid. The drawings ranged from perforated plates and brick to rammed earth and figured glass.
captions: The board of nine texture drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每種材料先在三乘三方格的一格中被繪成紋理。這些繪圖涵蓋從穿孔板與磚，到夯土與壓花玻璃。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small models were then built so that each material could be touched rather than only seen. Sticks, card, brick, resin, cotton and wire were each given a compact form.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 接著製作小模型，讓每種材料能被觸摸，而不只是被觀看。木棒、卡紙、磚、樹脂、棉與鐵線都各自被賦予緊湊的形體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Set side by side, the nine models form a material grid that mirrors the drawn board. Each piece shows a different way of holding weight, light and texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 並列之後，九件模型形成一個與繪製之板相互映照的材料方格。每一件都展現了承載重量、光線與質感的不同方式。

sections.heading: Nine Squares - Reading Matter by Hand
sections.body: Architecture is often drawn long before it is touched, and materials can remain abstract names on a drawing. This project set out to slow that process by placing nine materials on a single board, as if each were a piece in a puzzle. In the first stage every material was drawn as a texture within one square of a three-by-three grid, from perforated plates and brick to rammed earth, resin and figured glass. Samples were gathered alongside the drawings, so that the eye could compare image and substance. In the second stage each material was made into a small model, and sticks, card, brick, resin, cotton, cement and wire each received a compact form that reveals how it bends, stacks, binds or lets light through. Placed in rows, the models mirror the drawn board and turn it into an inventory of tactile qualities. The guidance stressed hands-on comparison, so that material choices could later grow from experience rather than from catalogue descriptions alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 九格之間-以手閱讀物質
zh-Hant.body: 建築往往在被觸摸之前很久就已被繪製，材料也可能只是圖面上的抽象名稱。這個專題試圖放慢這個過程，把九種材料放在同一塊板上，彷彿每一種都是謎題中的一枚棋子。第一階段，每種材料在三乘三方格的一格中被繪成紋理，從穿孔板與磚到夯土、樹脂與壓花玻璃。樣本與繪圖一同蒐集，使眼睛能夠比較影像與實質。第二階段，每種材料被製成小模型，木棒、卡紙、磚、樹脂、棉、水泥與鐵線各自獲得緊湊的形體，揭示它如何彎曲、堆疊、綑綁或讓光線穿透。成排放置後，模型映照繪製之板，把它轉化為一份觸覺特質的清單。指導強調親手比較，使日後的材料選擇能從經驗中生長，而不只依賴型錄的描述。

pins.title: Sliced Lattice Tower
pins.description:
A lattice box is stretched, skewed and waved into a twisting tower, then sliced by software into 129 floors of PVC and rebuilt layer by layer.

Physical model | Digital-to-physical fabrication study | 2 mm PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 切片格構之塔
zh-Hant.description:
一個格構方盒被拉伸、歪斜與波動成扭轉的塔，再以軟體切成 129 層 PVC，逐層重建。

實體模型｜數位至實體製作研究｜2 mm PVC 板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The sliced tower against a dark ground.
暗色背景前的切片之塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how a rigid lattice could be pushed into a fluid, twisting form. It also asked how such a form could be built by hand with precision.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，僵硬的格構如何被推向流動而扭轉的形體。它也探問，這樣的形體如何能以手工精準地建造。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A box of interlocking bars was rendered as the starting volume. Its grid was then stretched, skewed, waved and cut into in a series of plan diagrams.
captions: The grid stretched, skewed and waved.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一個由互鎖桿件構成的方盒被渲染為起始體量。其格網接著在一系列平面圖解中被拉伸、歪斜、波動與切入。
captions: 被拉伸、歪斜與波動的格網。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Several twisting versions were modelled digitally and compared. The chosen one was sliced into 129 floors with 996 parts, printed as templates and cut from PVC.
captions: Four digital versions of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 數個扭轉的版本以數位建模並加以比較。選定的版本被切成 129 層、996 個零件，印成樣板後從 PVC 板切出。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Stacked floor by floor, the PVC layers rebuild the tower with fine horizontal lines and deep window openings. The twist reads clearly as light catches each edge.
captions: A close view of the layered edges.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 逐層堆疊之後，PVC 層片以細密的水平線與深邃的窗洞重建了塔。當光線落在每一道邊緣上，扭轉便清晰可讀。

sections.heading: Counted Layers - Twisting a Rigid Grid
sections.body: A grid promises order, yet it can also be persuaded to move. This project began with a box of interlocking bars and asked how far such a rigid lattice could be pushed toward fluidity without losing its legibility. Plan diagrams stretched, skewed, waved and cut into the grid, and several twisting towers were modelled and compared digitally. The chosen version was then translated into something buildable by hand, sliced into 129 floors containing 996 parts. Each slice was printed as a template, fixed to sheets of PVC, cut, sorted, layered and assembled in sequence. The finished tower carries this process on its surface, with fine horizontal lines recording every floor and deep openings revealing the lattice within. Under raking light the twist becomes vivid, as though the grid were turning on its own axis. The guidance emphasised the bridge between digital exploration and physical craft, showing that careful organisation can make an ambitious form precise and achievable at the scale of a student studio.

zh-Hant.heading: 計數的層-扭轉僵硬的格網
zh-Hant.body: 格網承諾秩序，卻也能被說服而移動。這個專題從一個互鎖桿件構成的方盒出發，探問這樣僵硬的格構能被推向流動到什麼程度，而不失其可讀性。平面圖解對格網進行拉伸、歪斜、波動與切入，數座扭轉的塔以數位方式建模並比較。選定的版本接著被轉譯為能以手工建造之物，切成 129 層、共 996 個零件。每一片都印成樣板，貼於 PVC 板上，依序切割、分類、疊層與組裝。完成的塔把這個過程留在表面，細密的水平線記錄每一層，深邃的開口則顯露其中的格構。在斜射光下，扭轉變得鮮明，彷彿格網正繞著自身的軸線旋轉。指導強調數位探索與實體工藝之間的橋梁，顯示細心的組織能讓一個具野心的形體在學生工作室的尺度上精準而可行。

pins.title: Stacked Rooms of a Dense City
pins.description:
Inspired by an extremely dense walled settlement, small rooms are stacked into a PVC block and drawn as a long section full of hidden everyday life.

Physical model and drawing | Dense housing study | 2 mm PVC boards, parchment paper, digital drawing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 密城疊室
zh-Hant.description:
受一座極度密集的圍城聚落啟發，小房間被堆疊成一座 PVC 量體，並繪成一張充滿隱藏日常生活的長剖面。

實體模型與繪圖｜高密度居住研究｜2 mm PVC 板、羊皮紙、數位繪圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A famously dense walled settlement showed how many functions can hide in the deepest corners of a city. The project asked how such density could be captured in a compact model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座以密集聞名的圍城聚落，顯示了城市最深處的角落能藏著多少功能。這個專題探問，如何在一個緊湊的模型中捕捉這樣的密度。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Floors were studied as thin plates divided into many small rooms. Exploded views laid the plates apart to show how the cells were packed.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 樓層被研究為劃分成許多小房間的薄板。爆炸圖把板片分開，顯示單元如何被緊密排列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The plates were stacked in PVC and pushed in and out to form an uneven block. Close views tested the depth of the small rooms and their thin walls.
captions: A close view of stacked floors.
A detail of the thin walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 板片以 PVC 堆疊，並被推進拉出，形成不平整的量體。近景測試了小房間的深度與其薄牆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The block reads as a hive of rooms with plants spilling from its edges. A long section drawing fills each room with small scenes of everyday life.
captions: Part of the long section drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 量體讀來像一座房間的蜂巢，植物從邊緣溢出。一張長剖面繪圖在每個房間中填滿日常生活的小場景。

sections.heading: Packed Cells - Life in the Deepest Corners
sections.body: Some cities grow so dense that every corner holds a different life, and functions that elsewhere need whole buildings shrink into a single room. This project took such a walled settlement as its point of departure and asked how its density could be distilled into a compact object. Floors were first imagined as thin plates divided into many small rooms, and exploded views separated the plates to reveal how the cells were packed together. Built in PVC, the plates were stacked and shifted in and out, producing an uneven block whose edges catch light and shadow in quick succession. Close views examined the depth of each room and the thinness of its walls, while plants spilling from the edges hint at improvised gardens. A long section drawing then filled the rooms with small scenes of daily routine, giving the structure an inhabited voice. The guidance encouraged a dialogue between model and drawing, so that physical density and lived experience could be studied together.

zh-Hant.heading: 緊密的單元-最深角落裡的生活
zh-Hant.body: 有些城市密集到每個角落都容納著不同的生活，在別處需要整棟建築的功能，在這裡縮小為一個房間。這個專題以這樣的圍城聚落為出發點，探問其密度如何被提煉成一件緊湊的物件。樓層先被想像為劃分成許多小房間的薄板，爆炸圖把板片分開，揭示單元如何被緊密排列。以 PVC 建造之後，板片被堆疊並推進拉出，形成一座不平整的量體，其邊緣快速交替地捕捉光與影。近景檢視了每個房間的深度與牆的薄度，從邊緣溢出的植物則暗示著臨時的花園。一張長剖面繪圖接著在房間裡填滿日常作息的小場景，使結構獲得被居住的聲音。指導鼓勵模型與繪圖之間的對話，讓物理的密度與生活的經驗能被一起研究。

pins.title: Layered Plates Art Centre
pins.description:
An art centre is shaped as thin plates stacked in shifting layers, rising and splitting along a site among towers so that water, city and void meet in one low form.

Physical model | Cultural building massing study | 2 mm PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 層板藝術中心
zh-Hant.description:
一座藝術中心被塑造成以錯動層次堆疊的薄板，在高樓之間的基地上升起與分裂，使水、城市與虛空在一個低矮的形體中相遇。

實體模型｜文化建築量體研究｜2 mm PVC 板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The layered PVC plates of the art centre.
藝術中心的 PVC 疊層板。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A low cultural building was needed on a site surrounded by tall towers and a main road. The project asked how it could hold its own presence without competing in height.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座低矮的文化建築需要坐落在被高樓與主要道路包圍的基地上。這個專題探問，它如何能在不比拼高度的情況下保有自身的存在感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches explored themes of water, the city and vanishing through flowing lines and textures. Simple forms were drawn as separated and connected volumes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖透過流動的線條與紋理，探索水、城市與消逝的主題。簡單的形體被繪成分離與連接的量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The building was developed as stacked plates that slide over one another. Renders tested how the layers split and lift to open entrances and terraces.
captions: A render of the shifting layers.
A render of the lifted edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 建築被發展為彼此滑移的堆疊板片。渲染圖測試了層次如何分裂與抬升，以開出入口與露台。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model stretches as a long, low body of thin PVC layers that thicken and thin along its length. Gaps between layers read as bands of shadow and light.
captions: The edge of the stacked plates.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型延展為一個由薄 PVC 層構成、長而低的形體，沿其長度時厚時薄。層與層之間的縫隙讀來像光與影的帶狀。

sections.heading: Low Strata - A Quiet Body Among Towers
sections.body: A cultural building does not always need to rise to be noticed. On a site ringed by towers and bordered by a busy road, this art centre was imagined as a low body that gains presence through layering rather than height. Early sketches gathered three themes, water, the city and vanishing, and translated them into flowing lines, hatched textures and simple volumes drawn as separated or connected masses. From these studies emerged the idea of stacked plates that slide over one another, splitting and lifting at certain points to open entrances, terraces and views. Renders tested the rhythm of these shifts, and the physical model in thin PVC made the strata tangible. Along its length the building thickens and thins, while the gaps between layers form bands of shadow that soften its edge against the hard verticals around it. The guidance encouraged a measured response to context, showing how a modest section can hold its own among towers through clarity of idea and consistency of material.

zh-Hant.heading: 低伏的地層-高樓之間的安靜形體
zh-Hant.body: 一座文化建築並不總是需要升高才能被注意。在一塊被高樓環繞、毗鄰繁忙道路的基地上，這座藝術中心被想像為一個低伏的形體，透過層疊而非高度獲得存在感。早期草圖匯集了三個主題，水、城市與消逝，並把它們轉譯為流動的線條、排線紋理，以及被繪成分離或連接量塊的簡單體積。從這些研究中浮現出彼此滑移的堆疊板片之構想，在某些位置分裂與抬升，開出入口、露台與視野。渲染圖測試了這些錯動的節奏，以薄 PVC 製成的實體模型則讓地層變得可觸。建築沿其長度時厚時薄，層間的縫隙形成陰影的帶狀，柔化了它面對周圍堅硬垂直線的邊緣。指導鼓勵對脈絡做出有分寸的回應，顯示一個節制的剖面如何憑藉清晰的構想與一致的材料，在高樓之間站穩自己。

pins.title: The Wings
pins.description:
Inspired by insect wings, tangled iron wire is stretched over a light frame so that translucent membranes and dark veins rise from a flat drawing into space.

Physical model | Natural form study | PVC, iron wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 翅膀
zh-Hant.description:
受昆蟲翅膀啟發，糾結的鐵線被拉伸在輕巧的框架上，使半透明的薄膜與深色的翅脈從平面繪圖升起，進入空間。

實體模型｜自然形態研究｜PVC、鐵線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tangled wire wing in close view.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how the delicate structure of an insect wing could be carried from a drawing into a spatial model. It sought a material that could show both lightness and strength.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，昆蟲翅膀精巧的結構如何能從繪圖轉化為空間模型。它尋找一種能同時呈現輕盈與強度的材料。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many wings were drawn to study their outlines and vein patterns. The drawings were then deformed and combined into new compositions.
captions: An early wire wing on a white base.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 許多翅膀被描繪下來，以研究其輪廓與翅脈紋樣。這些繪圖接著被變形並組合成新的構圖。
captions: 白色底座上的早期鐵線翅膀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Silver wire traced the outer border of each wing while black wire tangled inside it. The tangles followed a loose natural order, much like the veins of a real wing.
captions: The curving edge of the wire wing.
A detail of tangled wire veins.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 銀色鐵線勾勒每片翅膀的外框，黑色鐵線則在其中糾結。這些糾結依循鬆散的自然秩序，猶如真實翅膀的翅脈。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model lifts two wing forms into a sweeping arc with small red accents. It reads as both a natural relic and a light, technical structure.
captions: The wing model seen from a low angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型把兩片翅膀形體抬升為一道舒展的弧線，並點綴著小小的紅色。它讀來既像自然的遺物，也像輕巧的技術性結構。

sections.heading: Tangled Veins - Lifting the Wing into Space
sections.body: An insect wing is a lesson in economy, a membrane so thin it almost disappears, held open by a network of veins. This project began from a long fascination with such wings and set out to carry their logic from paper into space. Pages of drawings recorded outlines and vein patterns, which were then deformed and recombined until new compositions emerged. Iron wire was chosen as the medium because it could suggest translucency while keeping a firm line. Silver wire defined the outer border of each wing, and black wire was tangled inside according to a loose natural order, so that density and openness alternated like veins across a membrane. As the work progressed, the flat drawings bent upward into a sweeping arc, and small red accents marked moments of tension along the strands. The resulting model sits between relic and machine, at once organic and quietly technical. The guidance emphasised observation as the root of invention, showing how patient study of a small natural form can open a generous spatial idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 糾結的脈-讓翅膀升入空間
zh-Hant.body: 昆蟲的翅膀是一堂關於節約的課，薄膜薄得幾乎消失，卻由一張翅脈之網撐開。這個專題源自對這類翅膀長久的著迷，試圖把它們的邏輯從紙面帶入空間。一頁頁的繪圖記錄了輪廓與翅脈紋樣，接著被變形與重組，直到新的構圖浮現。鐵線被選為媒材，因為它能暗示半透明，同時保持堅定的線條。銀色鐵線界定每片翅膀的外框，黑色鐵線則依循鬆散的自然秩序在其中糾結，使密與疏如翅脈般在薄膜上交替。隨著作品推進，平面的繪圖向上彎成一道舒展的弧線，細小的紅色點綴標示出線材上張力集中的時刻。最終的模型介於遺物與機械之間，既有機又含蓄地帶著技術感。指導強調觀察是發明的根源，顯示耐心研究一個微小的自然形態，能開啟一個寬闊的空間構想。

pins.title: Inverted Frames Tower
pins.description:
Small wooden-strip buildings are stacked upright and upside down inside a tall frame, so that rooms overlap, intersect and connect across shifting planes.

Physical model | Spatial overlap study | 2 mm PVC, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 倒置框架塔
zh-Hant.description:
以木條製成的小建築在高大的框架中正立與倒置地堆疊，使房間跨越錯動的平面而彼此重疊、相交與連接。

實體模型｜空間重疊研究｜2 mm PVC、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tall frame tower of stacked buildings.
堆疊建築構成的高大框架塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how buildings could overlap and turn upside down while still forming one connected space. It set out to build a model where several worlds share the same frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，建築如何能彼此重疊、上下顛倒，同時仍構成一個相連的空間。它試圖建造一個讓數個世界共用同一框架的模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Line drawings studied repetition, folding and crossing patterns. These studies suggested how flat planes might intersect and multiply.
captions: A still from the film Inception that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 線條繪圖研究了重複、折疊與交錯的紋樣。這些研究提示了平面如何相交與倍增。
captions: 啟發本案的電影《全面啟動》劇照。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Square wooden strips formed simple buildings covered with PVC panels, and two planes were made to intersect. Building heights on a grid-like ground were chosen at random and three buildings were joined at an angle.
captions: Intersecting planes in a study model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 方形木條構成以 PVC 板覆蓋的簡單建築，並讓兩個平面彼此相交。格網般地面上的建築高度隨機決定，三棟建築以特定角度接合。
captions: 研究模型中相交的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The tower holds layered rooms that hang, stand and cross each other within one cage. Views from inside reveal a dense lattice of floors and voids.
captions: A deep view through the lattice.
The whole tower against a dark ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 塔在同一座籠架中容納懸吊、站立與交錯的層疊房間。從內部看去，顯露出樓板與虛空交織的密集格構。

sections.heading: Folded Worlds - Rooms Turned Against Gravity
sections.body: Architecture usually agrees with gravity, placing floors below ceilings and rooms beside rooms. This project questioned that agreement by imagining buildings that overlap and turn upside down while still belonging to a single spatial system. Line drawings of repeating, folding and crossing patterns opened the inquiry, suggesting how flat planes might intersect and multiply. Square wooden strips were then assembled into simple buildings and clad with PVC panels, and two planes were made to pass through one another. On a grid-like ground, building heights were chosen at random, and three buildings were joined at a deliberate angle inside a tall frame. Triangular braces of strips and boards divided the interior into independent spaces that nonetheless connect from layer to layer. Seen from within, the tower becomes a dense lattice of floors and voids, where up and down lose their certainty. The guidance encouraged risk in spatial thinking, showing that a disciplined frame can host disorientation without collapsing into chaos.

zh-Hant.heading: 折疊的世界-逆轉重力的房間
zh-Hant.body: 建築通常順從重力，讓地板在天花板之下，房間在房間之旁。這個專題質疑這份默契，想像建築彼此重疊、上下顛倒，卻仍屬於單一的空間系統。重複、折疊與交錯紋樣的線條繪圖開啟了探究，提示平面如何相交與倍增。方形木條接著被組成簡單的建築並以 PVC 板覆蓋，兩個平面彼此穿越。在格網般的地面上，建築高度隨機決定，三棟建築以刻意的角度在高大的框架中接合。木條與板材構成的三角支撐把內部劃分為獨立的空間，卻仍層層相連。從內部望去，塔成為樓板與虛空交織的密集格構，上與下失去了確定性。指導鼓勵空間思考中的冒險，顯示一個有紀律的框架能容納迷失感而不陷入混亂。

pins.title: Shelter
pins.description:
A coral-like structure of PVC frames is softened with heat to show bleaching damage, then braced with wooden supports so that it can hold together and recover.

Physical model | Ecological support study | 4 mm PVC, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 庇護
zh-Hant.description:
以 PVC 框架構成的珊瑚狀結構經加熱軟化以呈現白化的損傷，再以木條支撐加固，使其得以維持整體並復原。

實體模型｜生態支撐研究｜4 mm PVC、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 珊瑚狀的 PVC 結構。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Bleached coral loses its strength and becomes easily broken by water and people. The project asked how a spatial structure could offer it a stable and safe place to repair itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 白化的珊瑚失去強度，容易被海水與人為破壞。這個專題探問，一個空間結構如何能提供它穩定而安全的自我修復之所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches gathered many circular coral cells into branching clusters. Small primary models tested how frames could grow into reef-like masses.
captions: A sketch of clustered coral cells.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把許多圓形的珊瑚單元聚集為分枝的群簇。小型的初步模型測試了框架如何長成礁石般的量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rectangles cut from PVC sheets were glued as sections, borders and rows to form the reef shape. Inside, separate spaces and platforms gave each branch a different character.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從 PVC 板切出的矩形以剖面、邊框與排列的方式黏合，形成礁石的形狀。內部各自分隔的空間與平台，讓每一分枝具有不同的性格。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Heat was used to soften parts of the structure, imitating the damage of bleaching, and wooden strips were added to brace them. After reinforcement the softened coral keeps its shape even when injured again.
captions: Softening the PVC with a heat gun by hand.
The heat gun bending the frames to imitate bleaching damage.
The reef seen from a low angle.
The softened structure braced with strips.
The reinforced coral under blue light.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 以熱力軟化結構的部分，模擬白化造成的損傷，再加上木條加以支撐。加固之後，即使再度受損，軟化的珊瑚仍能保持形狀。
captions: 以熱風槍彎曲框架，模擬白化造成的損傷。
以木條支撐的軟化結構。

sections.heading: Braced Reef - Care for a Wounded Form
sections.body: A coral reef appears solid, yet it is a living structure that can weaken and lose its colour when the sea grows too warm. This project responded to that fragility by asking how architecture might act as a form of care. Sketches first gathered circular cells into branching clusters, and small primary models explored how frames could accumulate into reef-like masses. Rectangles cut from PVC sheets were then glued as sections, borders and rows, producing a dense body with separate inner spaces and platforms, each branch shaped differently. To make the damage visible, parts of the structure were softened with heat, so that crisp frames slumped as if the reef were exhausted. Thin wooden strips were added as supports, linking two weakened corals and allowing them to share their remaining strength. Tested again, the braced structure barely deformed, suggesting a quiet scaffold for recovery. The guidance encouraged empathy with natural systems, showing how a model can stage injury and repair as one continuous narrative.

zh-Hant.heading: 支撐的礁-照料受傷的形體
zh-Hant.body: 珊瑚礁看似堅實，卻是一種活的結構，當海水變得太暖，便會衰弱並失去顏色。這個專題回應這份脆弱，探問建築如何能成為一種照料。草圖先把圓形單元聚集為分枝的群簇，小型的初步模型則探索框架如何累積成礁石般的量體。從 PVC 板切出的矩形接著以剖面、邊框與排列的方式黏合，形成一個密實的形體，內部有各自分隔的空間與平台，每一分枝形態各異。為了讓損傷可見，結構的部分以熱力軟化，使俐落的框架塌陷，彷彿礁石已精疲力竭。細木條被加上作為支撐，連接兩株衰弱的珊瑚，讓它們分擔殘存的力量。再次測試時，受支撐的結構幾乎沒有變形，暗示一座安靜的復原鷹架。指導鼓勵對自然系統的同理，顯示一個模型能把受傷與修復演繹成一段連續的敘事。

pins.title: Trace of the Wind
pins.description:
Plastic sheets shaped by blown hot air become moulds for cement casts, and clear blue resin is poured into their hollows so that wind and sea meet in one small block.

Physical model | Material and force study | Cement, clear resin | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 風的痕跡
zh-Hant.description:
經熱風吹塑的塑膠片成為水泥鑄件的模具，清澈的藍色樹脂被倒入其凹陷處，使風與海在一塊小小的量體中相遇。

實體模型｜材料與力量研究｜水泥、透明樹脂｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The cement cube with a blue resin sea.
帶有藍色樹脂之海的水泥方塊。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Wind drives every sail, yet it is invisible and colourless. The project asked how this unseen force could be given a physical form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 風推動每一面帆，卻無形也無色。這個專題探問，如何能賦予這股看不見的力量一個實體的形式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A falling sheet of tissue paper revealed how air resistance bends a soft surface into grooves. Hot air was then blown onto plastic sheets to recreate this effect.
captions: Watching a falling sheet of tissue paper bend in the air.
Blowing hot air onto plastic sheets by hand.
A cement form cast from a wind-shaped mould.
The first row of casts and moulds.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張飄落的面紙揭示了空氣阻力如何把柔軟的表面彎成溝槽。接著以熱風吹向塑膠片，以重現這個效果。
captions: 觀察落下的薄紙在空中彎曲。
以手持熱風吹向塑膠片。
以風塑模具鑄成的水泥形體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The shaped sheets served as moulds for small cement blocks, each recording a different pattern of folds. Casts and moulds were compared side by side to choose the strongest texture.
captions: The second row of casts and moulds.
The third row of casts and moulds.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塑形後的塑膠片作為小型水泥塊的模具，每一塊記錄不同的褶紋。鑄件與模具並列比較，以選出最有力的紋理。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Clear blue resin was poured into the hollows of the chosen cast to form a small ocean. The finished block shows a light wind passing over crystal water.
captions: The cube seen from the side.
A close view of the resin sea.
The finished cube on a white ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 透明的藍色樹脂被倒入選定鑄件的凹陷，形成一片小小的海洋。完成的量體呈現輕風拂過晶瑩水面的景象。
captions: 白色背景上完成的方塊。

sections.heading: Cast Air - A Small Sea Held in Stone
sections.body: Wind is felt everywhere but seen nowhere, and anyone who sails learns to read it only through its effects on water and cloth. This project set out to make that invisible force tangible. A chance moment, a sheet of tissue paper slipping away and folding in mid-air, revealed how resistance writes grooves into a soft surface. To recreate this, hot air was blown across thin plastic sheets until they rippled and sagged, and the shaped sheets then served as moulds for small cement blocks. Each cast preserved a different pattern of folds, and casts and moulds were laid out side by side so that the most expressive textures could be chosen. Reflecting that the wind arrives from the ocean, the work then joined both elements, pouring clear blue resin into the hollows of a cement cube. The finished block holds a miniature sea beneath a petrified breeze, heavy and weightless at once. The guidance valued attentive accident, showing how an everyday observation can grow into a rigorous material experiment.

zh-Hant.heading: 鑄造的風-石中所藏的小海
zh-Hant.body: 風無所不在地被感受，卻無處可見，航行的人只能透過它在水與帆布上的作用來閱讀它。這個專題試圖讓這股看不見的力量變得可觸。一個偶然的時刻，一張面紙滑落並在半空中折起，揭示了阻力如何在柔軟的表面寫下溝槽。為了重現這一點，熱風吹過薄塑膠片，直到它們起伏與下垂，塑形後的薄片接著成為小型水泥塊的模具。每一個鑄件保存了不同的褶紋，鑄件與模具並列排開，以便選出最具表現力的紋理。想到風來自海洋，作品於是把兩者結合，把透明的藍色樹脂倒入水泥方塊的凹陷之中。完成的量體在凝固的微風之下容納一片微型的海，同時沉重又輕盈。指導重視專注的偶然，顯示一個日常的觀察能長成嚴謹的材料實驗。

pins.title: Growing City from Machine Drawings
pins.description:
Traced drawings of old machines are cut apart and recombined into new plans, then built as a card city and a long landscape of stick frames.

Physical models and drawing | Machine-to-space study | Card paper, pencil, wooden sticks, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 機械繪圖長出的城市
zh-Hant.description:
舊機械的描摹圖被拆解並重組為新的平面，再建造成一座卡紙城市與一片長長的木棒框架地景。

實體模型與繪圖｜機械到空間的研究｜卡紙、鉛筆、木棒、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The long landscape of stick frames.
木棒框架構成的長形地景。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked whether the precise language of machine drawings could become a language of space. It set out to grow a city from the parts of engines and mechanisms.
captions: A reproduced engraving of a steam engine, one of the machines that inspired the project.
A modern car engine used as a reference.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，機械繪圖精確的語言能否成為空間的語言。它試圖從引擎與機構的零件中長出一座城市。
captions: 啟發本案的機器之一：蒸汽機版畫。
作為參考的現代汽車引擎。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Old machine drawings were traced by hand to understand every gear, pipe and joint. Notes beside the tracings tested ideas about how machines and cities might grow alike.
captions: A traced machine drawing with notes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 舊機械繪圖被逐一手描，以理解每一個齒輪、管線與接頭。描圖旁的筆記測試了機械與城市如何以相似方式生長的想法。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The tracings were cut and pieced together digitally into new plan drawings. These plans were built as a dense card model of curving walls, rooms and passages.
captions: A view of curving card walls.
The card model from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 描圖被數位切割並拼接成新的平面圖。這些平面被建造成一座由彎曲牆面、房間與通道構成的密集卡紙模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The spaces were then joined into a long sequence of wooden stick frames over white floor plates. The final model reads as a growing city whose skyline still echoes the machine.
captions: A close view of the stick frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些空間接著被串連為白色樓板上一長串的木棒框架。最終的模型讀來像一座生長中的城市，其天際線仍回響著機械。

sections.heading: Traced Gears - A City Assembled from Machines
sections.body: A machine drawing is a careful promise that every part will meet another, and this project wondered whether that promise could also hold a city. The work began with patient tracing, copying old drawings of engines and mechanisms line by line until each gear, pipe and joint was understood from within. Notes written beside the tracings tested a parallel between machines that transfer energy and cities that grow by connection. The tracings were then cut and pieced together digitally, producing new plans in which mechanical fragments became walls, rooms and passages. Built in card, these plans formed a dense model of curving surfaces, while a later stage stretched the spaces into a long sequence of wooden stick frames rising over white floor plates. Seen from a distance, the frames form a skyline that still remembers the rhythm of the machine. The guidance emphasised copying as a form of understanding, showing how close study of an existing language can become the ground for a personal spatial vocabulary.

zh-Hant.heading: 描摹的齒輪-由機械組裝的城市
zh-Hant.body: 一張機械繪圖是一份細心的承諾，保證每一個零件都會與另一個相接，這個專題好奇這份承諾能否也承載一座城市。作品從耐心的描摹開始，一線一線地複製舊的引擎與機構繪圖，直到每一個齒輪、管線與接頭都從內部被理解。寫在描圖旁的筆記測試了一種類比，傳遞能量的機械與藉由連結而生長的城市。描圖接著被數位切割與拼接，產生新的平面，機械的碎片在其中成為牆、房間與通道。以卡紙建造之後，這些平面形成一座彎曲表面密集交錯的模型，而後的階段則把空間延展為一長串在白色樓板上升起的木棒框架。從遠處看，這些框架構成一道仍記得機械節奏的天際線。指導強調描摹是一種理解的方式，顯示細讀一種既有的語言，能成為個人空間詞彙的基礎。

pins.title: Tower of Stacked Stories
pins.description:
A tall tower of card and wooden sticks stacks rooms, stairs and floors for different ways of life, so that many stories share one vertical container.

Physical model and drawing | Vertical narrative study | Wooden sticks, card paper, hard cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 層疊故事之塔
zh-Hant.description:
以卡紙與木棒構成的高塔，為不同的生活方式堆疊房間、樓梯與樓板，讓許多故事共用一個垂直的容器。

實體模型與繪圖｜垂直敘事研究｜木棒、卡紙、硬紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tall tower of stacked rooms.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asked how one building could hold the separate worlds of many different people. It set out to build a vertical container for stories that overlap but rarely meet.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探問，一棟建築如何能容納許多不同的人各自分隔的世界。它試圖為彼此重疊卻鮮少相遇的故事，建造一個垂直的容器。

sections.heading: Research
