sections.body: Scenes were pieced together like a jigsaw to suggest a crowded vertical world. A line drawing then translated these scenes into overlapping frames and floors.
captions: A jigsaw collage of film stills and street signs from the inspiring film.
The line drawing of overlapping frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 場景如拼圖般被拼接，以暗示一個擁擠的垂直世界。一張線條繪圖接著把這些場景轉譯為重疊的框架與樓板。
captions: 以啟發本案的電影劇照與街頭招牌拼成的拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many materials were tested at full height, and some failed before the right ones were found. For the stairs, four methods were tried before stacked squares of hard cardboard kept the right feeling.
captions: Folding the stairs and building the tower by hand.
The full-height tower in the workshop.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 許多材料在完整高度下被測試，有些在找到合適的之前就失敗了。樓梯嘗試了四種方法，最後以堆疊的方形硬紙板保留了恰當的感覺。
captions: 以手摺疊樓梯並搭建高塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower stacks white rooms, stairs and stick frames into a dense vertical city. Small red figures mark the separate lives held within it.
captions: A close view of stacked rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔把白色房間、樓梯與木棒框架堆疊成一座密集的垂直城市。小小的紅色人形標示出其中各自分隔的生活。

sections.heading: Vertical Crowd - Many Lives in One Container
sections.body: Some buildings are cities in themselves, holding guesthouses, shops and homes so close together that strangers live within a wall of each other. This project took that condition as its theme and imagined a tower as a container for stories that overlap but rarely meet. Scenes were first pieced together like a jigsaw to evoke a crowded vertical world, and a line drawing then distilled them into frames, floors and shifting levels. Built at a height taller than a person, the model demanded a long dialogue with materials, and several attempts failed before the right combination emerged. The stairs alone passed through four methods until squares of hard cardboard, sliced and stacked, preserved the intended feeling of worn steps. In the finished tower, white rooms and winding stairs interlock within stick frames, while small red figures mark the separate lives held inside. The guidance encouraged persistence through failure, showing that material testing is not a detour but the very way a narrative becomes architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直的人群-一個容器裡的眾多生活
zh-Hant.body: 有些建築本身就是城市，容納旅舍、商店與住家，彼此靠得如此之近，陌生人僅隔一牆而居。這個專題以這種狀態為主題，把塔想像為一個容器，裝著彼此重疊卻鮮少相遇的故事。場景先如拼圖般被拼接，喚起一個擁擠的垂直世界，一張線條繪圖接著把它們提煉為框架、樓板與錯動的層次。模型的高度超過一個人，需要與材料進行漫長的對話，數次嘗試失敗之後，合適的組合才浮現。光是樓梯就經歷了四種方法，直到切成方塊並堆疊的硬紙板保留了磨舊階梯的感覺。在完成的塔中，白色房間與蜿蜒的樓梯在木棒框架裡交扣，小小的紅色人形標示出其中各自分隔的生活。指導鼓勵在失敗中堅持，顯示材料測試並非繞路，而正是敘事成為建築的途徑。

pins.title: Lunabase
pins.description:
Inspired by natural caves, spaces are carved into blue foam with a hot pen and cast in plaster and resin, producing a rough, crater-like base.

Physical model and drawing | Material test | Blue foam, plaster, resin, pencil | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 月面基地
zh-Hant.description:
受天然洞穴啟發，空間以熱筆刻入藍色泡沫，再以石膏與樹脂鑄造，形成一座粗糙、如隕石坑般的基地。

實體模型與繪圖｜材料測試｜藍色泡沫、石膏、樹脂、鉛筆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The carved and cast cave form.
雕刻並鑄造的洞穴形體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Natural caves form slowly through water and time, yet their spaces feel both raw and protective. The project asked how such a natural form could be made by hand as a base for living.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 天然洞穴經由水與時間緩慢形成，其空間既粗獷又具庇護感。這個專題探問，如何能以手工製作這樣的自然形態，作為居住的基地。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A large drawing studied a cratered surface with pits and ridges. Pencil drawings explored rings, cracks and bursts of lines as patterns of erosion.
captions: Reference photos of natural cave and rock surfaces.
A drawing of a cratered surface.
A pencil study of radiating lines.
A pencil study of a split form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張大型繪圖研究了布滿凹坑與脊線的坑洞表面。鉛筆繪圖則把環形、裂紋與迸發的線條當作侵蝕的紋樣來探索。
captions: 天然洞穴與岩石表面的參考照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Spaces were carved into blue foam with a hot pen, and plaster was poured into them with acrylic glue sprinkled over. Removing the foam afterwards was the key step that revealed the natural texture.
captions: The cast held in the hand.
A fingertip beside the rough cast surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 空間以熱筆刻入藍色泡沫，再倒入石膏並灑上壓克力膠。之後移除泡沫是關鍵的步驟，它揭示了自然的紋理。
captions: 粗糙鑄件表面旁的指尖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The cast shows cavities, ridges and glassy blue pools like a small lunar landscape. Its long profile reads as a base sunk into rock.
captions: Cavities and pools in close view.
The long profile of the cast.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鑄件呈現凹洞、脊線與如玻璃般的藍色水池，宛如一片小小的月面地景。其長形的輪廓讀來像一座沉入岩石的基地。

sections.heading: Carved Hollows - Making a Cave by Hand
sections.body: A cave is architecture without an architect, a space hollowed by water over centuries that nonetheless feels made for shelter. This project asked whether such a form could be produced deliberately, within a few days and with ordinary studio materials. A large drawing first studied a cratered surface of pits and ridges, while pencil studies explored rings, cracks and bursts of lines as the marks of erosion. The making then reversed the logic of carving. Spaces were cut into blue foam with a hot pen, plaster was poured into the hollows, and acrylic glue was scattered over the surface. The decisive moment came when the foam was removed, leaving a cast whose cavities, ridges and glassy blue pools seemed to have formed naturally. Seen in profile, the object reads as a base sunk into rock, half geology and half habitation. The guidance valued material curiosity, showing how a controlled process can borrow the accidents of nature and turn a test into a convincing spatial proposal.

zh-Hant.heading: 刻出的空洞-以手造洞
zh-Hant.body: 洞穴是沒有建築師的建築，是水經過數百年掏空的空間，卻彷彿為庇護而造。這個專題探問，這樣的形態能否在數日之內、以工作室中尋常的材料刻意製造出來。一張大型繪圖先研究了凹坑與脊線交錯的坑洞表面，鉛筆研究則把環形、裂紋與迸發的線條當作侵蝕的痕跡來探索。製作過程接著反轉了雕刻的邏輯。空間以熱筆刻入藍色泡沫，石膏被倒入空洞，壓克力膠則灑落在表面上。決定性的時刻在於移除泡沫，留下一件鑄件，其凹洞、脊線與如玻璃般的藍色水池彷彿自然形成。從側面看，物件讀來像一座沉入岩石的基地，一半是地質，一半是居所。指導重視對材料的好奇，顯示受控的過程能借用自然的偶然，把一次測試轉化為具說服力的空間提案。

pins.title: Possibility of Space
pins.description:
A wave photograph is divided into a net of triangles, and its lines are extended into wooden sticks and card planes that enclose, half-enclose and open space.

Physical models and drawing | Point, line and plane study | Wooden sticks, card paper, metal sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間的可能
zh-Hant.description:
一張海浪照片被劃分為三角形的網，其線條延伸為木棒與卡紙平面，圍合、半圍合並打開空間。

實體模型與繪圖｜點線面研究｜木棒、卡紙、金屬棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An everyday photograph of a breaking wave sparked the question of how an image could become space. The project set out to systematise the picture into separate triangular models.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一張日常拍下的碎浪照片引發了一個問題，影像如何能成為空間。這個專題試圖把畫面系統化，轉化為一個個獨立的三角形模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The photograph was traced as a net of points and lines that divided it into many triangles. A second, finer net tested how density changes the reading of the wave.
captions: The net laid over the wave.
The finer net over the wave.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 照片被描成由點與線構成的網，把它劃分為許多三角形。第二張更細密的網，測試了密度如何改變對海浪的閱讀。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The planes were sorted into enclosed, half-enclosed and open blocks and cut from card. Lines on each surface were extended as wooden sticks that met to form new edges.
captions: Cutting and folding the card planes by hand.
Stick frames held in the hand.
Cut card pieces on the mat.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 平面被分為圍合、半圍合與開放的區塊，並以卡紙切出。每個表面上的線條延伸為木棒，彼此相交形成新的邊界。
captions: 以手裁切並摺疊卡紙面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Fixed to a board, the shards rise like a frozen wave of sharp planes and fine lines. Light cuts through the gaps and casts long, angular shadows.
captions: Sharp planes rising from the board.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 固定於底板之後，碎片如一道由銳利平面與細線構成的凝固海浪般升起。光線穿過縫隙，投下長而有稜角的影子。
captions: 從底板升起的銳利平面。

sections.heading: Frozen Wave - From Image to Plane
sections.body: A photograph holds a moment, but its surface can also be read as a field of edges waiting to be built. This project began with an ordinary picture of a breaking wave and asked how that image might be systematised into space. The photograph was traced as a network of points and lines, dividing its surface into triangles, and a second, finer net revealed how density alters the sense of motion. These drawings provided the rules for making. Planes were sorted into enclosed, half-enclosed and open blocks and cut from card, while the lines along each surface were extended as wooden sticks until they met and defined new edges. Fixed to a board, the shards rose into a crystalline landscape, as though the wave had been stopped at its peak and shattered into geometry. Under a single light, gaps between planes produce long, angular shadows that keep the movement alive. The guidance emphasised the discipline of point, line and plane, showing how a basic vocabulary can transform a fleeting image into an enduring spatial composition.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固的浪-從影像到平面
zh-Hant.body: 一張照片保存一個瞬間，但其表面也能被讀作一片等待被建造的邊界之場。這個專題從一張尋常的碎浪照片開始，探問這個影像如何能被系統化為空間。照片被描成點與線的網絡，把表面劃分為三角形，第二張更細密的網則揭示密度如何改變運動感。這些繪圖提供了製作的規則。平面被分為圍合、半圍合與開放的區塊並以卡紙切出，沿每個表面的線條則延伸為木棒，直到彼此相交並界定新的邊界。固定於底板之後，碎片升起成一片結晶般的地景，彷彿海浪在浪峰處被定格並碎裂為幾何。在單一光源下，平面之間的縫隙投下長而有稜角的影子，讓運動得以延續。指導強調點、線、面的紀律，顯示一套基本的詞彙能把稍縱即逝的影像轉化為持久的空間構成。

pins.title: Body Urbanism
pins.description:
A shirt is taken apart into twelve pattern pieces and paired with rotating wooden sticks, testing how soft fabric and stable timber can coexist like body and building.

Physical model and drawing | Body and structure study | Wood, cotton fabric, screws | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 身體都市
zh-Hant.description:
一件襯衫被拆成十二片版型，並與可旋轉的木棒結合，測試柔軟的布料與穩定的木材如何像身體與建築般共存。

實體模型與繪圖｜身體與結構研究｜木材、棉布、螺絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explored the likeness between the structure of the body and the structure of architecture. It asked whether ductile cotton and stable wood could work together in one piece.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題探索身體結構與建築結構之間的相似。它探問富延展性的棉布與穩定的木材能否在同一件作品中協同運作。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A shirt was taken apart into twelve pieces, and the contour of each piece was drawn to show how it curves around the body. A point-cloud drawing then mapped the soft volume of the garment.
captions: An exploded drawing of the garment pieces around a human figure.
Pattern pieces of the shirt drawn flat.
A point-cloud drawing of the garment and frame.
The shirt before it was taken apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一件襯衫被拆成十二片，每一片的輪廓都被描繪下來，以顯示它如何繞著身體彎曲。一張點雲繪圖接著描繪出衣物柔軟的體積。
captions: 環繞人體的服裝片爆炸圖。
衣物與框架的點雲繪圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks with five holes were joined with nails, screw caps and L-shaped pieces. Loose screws at right angles let each stick rotate and flex freely.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 開有五個孔的木棒以釘子、螺帽與 L 形件接合。直角處鬆開的螺絲讓每一根木棒都能自由旋轉與彎曲。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Layered over the fabric, the sticks change its shape while the fabric holds the sticks within range. Each turn of the frame pulls the cloth into new wrinkles.
captions: The stick-and-fabric frame held up by hand.
A close view of a rotating joint.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 木棒疊在布料之外，改變了它的形狀，而布料則把木棒約束在一定範圍內。框架的每一次轉動，都把布拉出新的皺褶。
captions: 以手提起的木棒與布料框架。

sections.heading: Soft Frame - Where Cloth Meets Timber
sections.body: Clothing is the first architecture of the body, a soft enclosure that bends with every movement, while buildings rely on frames that resist. This project placed these two logics side by side and asked whether they could coexist in a single object. A shirt was first taken apart into twelve pattern pieces, and drawing each contour revealed how cloth curves to fit shoulders, arms and back while remaining loose. A point-cloud drawing then translated the garment into a field of soft volume. In parallel, wooden sticks pierced with five holes were joined using nails, screw caps and small angled pieces, and loose screws allowed each joint to rotate. When the frame was laid over the fabric, both materials changed. The sticks pulled the cloth into new folds, and the cloth in turn held the sticks within a limited range, so that every rotation produced a distinct pattern of wrinkles. The guidance encouraged thinking across scales, showing how a garment can serve as a laboratory for structural ideas.

zh-Hant.heading: 柔軟的框-布與木相遇之處
zh-Hant.body: 衣物是身體的第一座建築，一種隨每個動作彎曲的柔軟圍合，而建築則依賴抵抗的框架。這個專題把這兩種邏輯並置，探問它們能否在單一物件中共存。一件襯衫先被拆成十二片版型，描繪每一道輪廓揭示了布料如何彎曲以貼合肩、臂與背，同時保持寬鬆。一張點雲繪圖接著把衣物轉譯為一片柔軟的體積之場。與此同時，開有五個孔的木棒以釘子、螺帽與小型角件接合，鬆開的螺絲讓每個接頭都能旋轉。當框架疊在布料之上，兩種材料都改變了。木棒把布拉出新的褶痕，布反過來把木棒約束在有限的範圍內，使每一次轉動都產生獨特的皺紋紋樣。指導鼓勵跨尺度的思考，顯示一件衣物能成為結構構想的實驗室。

pins.title: Encounter with Shadow and Space
pins.description:
Dappled shadows on a wall are traced into a net of lines and built as staggered frames of wooden strips, where light filters through overlapping layers.

Physical model and drawing | Light and shadow study | Wooden strips, PVC expansion sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 光影與空間的相遇
zh-Hant.description:
牆上斑駁的樹影被描成一張線的網，再以木條建造成錯落的框架，讓光穿過層層交疊的空間。

實體模型與繪圖｜光影研究｜木條、PVC 發泡板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final tower of staggered wooden frames.
錯落木框架構成的最終塔體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Light passing through regular gaps makes calm, even shadows, but light filtering through overlapping layers behaves very differently. The project asked how such layered shadow could become the logic of a space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 光穿過規則的縫隙會形成平靜而均勻的影子，但穿過層層交疊的光則截然不同。這個專題探問，這種層疊的光影如何能成為空間的邏輯。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The mottled shadows of trees on a wall were outlined and traced into a net of straight lines. The irregular triangles of this net became a plan for where frames could rise and overlap.
captions: The shadow pattern traced as a net of lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 樹木投在牆上的斑駁影子被勾勒出來，描成一張由直線構成的網。這張網中不規則的三角形，成為框架升起與交疊位置的藍圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The net was first built flat as a base of wooden strips that followed the traced lines. Strips were then raised and staggered in layers, so that each level twisted slightly away from the one below.
captions: The flat base following the traced lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 線網先以木條平鋪建造成一個底座，沿著描出的線條排列。木條接著被逐層抬升並錯開，使每一層都相對下一層略微扭轉。
captions: 沿描線排列的平面底座。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a tower of open frames with small figures on platforms at each floor. Light falling through the crossing strips casts a dense, shifting field of shadow inside.
captions: Frames clustered at the upper levels.
The crossing strips of the roof.
Figures on a platform among the frames.
A close view of stacked frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型升起為一座開放框架之塔，每層平台上都有小小的人形。穿過交錯木條的光，在內部投下一片密集而變幻的影子。

sections.heading: Mottled Light - Building with Overlapping Shade
sections.body: A walk beside a long wall under trees offered the starting point, where shadows moved across the surface like a second, softer architecture. The project noticed that light passing through neat gaps produces calm and regular patterns, whereas light filtering through overlapping layers creates something richer and less predictable. The mottled shade on the wall was therefore traced and reduced to a net of straight lines, and the irregular triangles of that net became a plan. Wooden strips first followed the lines as a flat base, then rose in staggered layers, each level twisting slightly from the one below, recalling an old image of bamboo joints climbing unevenly. The final tower of open frames carries small figures on platforms at every floor, suggesting how people might gather within a structure made almost entirely of shadow. As light crosses the strips, the interior fills with a dense and shifting field of shade. The guidance encouraged careful observation of ordinary moments, showing how a passing effect of light can be translated into a lasting spatial order.

zh-Hant.heading: 斑駁的光-以交疊的陰影建造
zh-Hant.body: 一次沿著樹下長牆的散步提供了起點，影子在牆面上移動，彷彿另一種更柔軟的建築。這個專題注意到，穿過整齊縫隙的光會產生平靜而規則的紋樣，而穿過層層交疊的光則創造出更豐富、更難預測的效果。牆上斑駁的樹影因此被描摹下來，簡化為一張直線的網，網中不規則的三角形成為一張平面。木條先沿著這些線條平鋪為底座，再以錯落的層次升起，每一層都相對下一層略微扭轉，令人想起竹節參差向上的古老意象。最終這座開放框架之塔在每層平台上都安置了小小的人形，暗示人們如何能聚集在一個幾乎全由影子構成的結構之中。當光穿過木條，內部便充滿一片密集而變幻的陰影。指導鼓勵細心觀察尋常的片刻，顯示一瞬即逝的光影效果能被轉譯為持久的空間秩序。

pins.title: Windows of Cast Light
pins.description:
A cardboard box is cut with polygon windows on every face, cast in plaster and lit from within, so that beams of light read as the true material of the room.

Physical model, casting and drawing | Light opening study | Cardboard, plaster, pencil | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 投光之窗
zh-Hant.description:
一個紙盒的每一面都被切出多邊形的窗，再以石膏鑄造並從內部打光，使一道道光束成為房間真正的材料。

實體模型、鑄造與繪圖｜開口與光線研究｜紙板、石膏、鉛筆｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Looking into the box through slanted planes.
透過傾斜的平面望入盒中。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Windows of many different sizes can turn a plain wall into an instrument for light. The project asked what a room would feel like if beams entered through openings of every shape and could be looked through from outside.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 大小各異的窗，能把一面素牆變成調度光線的器具。這個專題探問，若光束從各種形狀的開口進入，並能從外面望穿，房間會是什麼感覺。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Shaded triangles were drawn in pencil to test how sharp angles divide a surface. A set of black polygons was then cut out as a vocabulary of possible openings.
captions: A pencil study of shaded triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以鉛筆繪出的陰影三角形，測試銳角如何劃分一個表面。一組黑色多邊形接著被剪出，作為可能開口的詞彙。
captions: 陰影三角形的鉛筆研究。
剪出作為開口的多邊形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A rectangular box was cut with polygons on its four faces and joined by passages between opposite sides, then cast in plaster. Sectional sketches imagined how the openings might slice through a dense block of rooms.
captions: The cut box and its first cast.
Openings in the rough cast surface.
An imagined section cut by openings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一個長方形盒子的四個立面被切出多邊形，並在相對兩面之間設置連通的通道，再以石膏鑄造。剖面草圖想像這些開口如何切穿一個密集的房間量體。
captions: 切割後的盒子與第一次鑄件。
粗糙鑄造表面上的開口。
被開口切穿的想像剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Lit from inside, each polygon throws a sharp beam across the rough walls. Seen through the openings, the room appears carved by light rather than by walls.
captions: A dark opening seen from within.
A polygon framed by glowing walls.
A beam passing through a narrow opening.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從內部打光後，每個多邊形都在粗糙的牆面上投下一道銳利的光束。從開口望進去，房間像是由光而非由牆所雕刻而成。
captions: 從內部看見的暗色開口。
被發光牆面框住的多邊形。

sections.heading: Carved Beams - A Room Made of Openings
sections.body: Some of the most memorable rooms are defined less by their walls than by the way those walls let light in, and this project set out to test that idea at the scale of a box. Pencil studies of shaded triangles first explored how sharp angles divide a surface, while a set of black polygons, cut from paper, formed a small vocabulary of possible windows. A cardboard box was then cut on all four faces, with passages joining opposite sides, and the box was cast in plaster to give its walls weight and texture. Sectional sketches carried the inquiry further, imagining how such openings might slice through a dense block of rooms and stairs. When the cast was lit from within, every polygon threw a precise beam across the rough interior, and from outside the openings framed glowing fragments of space. The room no longer seemed built so much as carved by light. The guidance valued the patience of iterative making, showing how a simple box can become a laboratory for the relationship between solid, void and illumination.

zh-Hant.heading: 雕刻的光束-由開口構成的房間
zh-Hant.body: 有些最令人難忘的房間，與其說是由牆界定，不如說是由牆讓光進入的方式界定，這個專題試圖在一個盒子的尺度上測試這個想法。陰影三角形的鉛筆研究首先探索銳角如何劃分一個表面，而一組以紙剪出的黑色多邊形，形成了一套關於可能之窗的小小詞彙。一個紙盒接著在四個立面上被切割，並以通道連接相對的兩面，再以石膏鑄造，賦予牆面重量與質感。剖面草圖把探究推得更遠，想像這些開口如何切穿一個密集的房間與樓梯量體。當鑄件從內部被照亮，每個多邊形都在粗糙的內壁上投下精確的光束，而從外面看，開口框住了一片片發光的空間碎片。房間不再像是被建造，而更像是被光雕刻而成。指導重視反覆製作的耐心，顯示一個簡單的盒子能成為探討實體、空隙與光照關係的實驗室。

pins.title: Wandering Between Black and White
pins.description:
Inspired by a dance that circles endlessly, white PVC stairs spiral and loop in every direction, while their shadows follow like the black keys of a piano.

Physical model | Music and movement study | White PVC sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 黑白之間的漫遊
zh-Hant.description:
受一支無盡迴旋的舞蹈啟發，白色 PVC 樓梯朝各個方向盤旋迴繞，而它們的影子則如鋼琴的黑鍵般緊隨其後。

實體模型｜音樂與動態研究｜白色 PVC 板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Spiral stairs looping across the base.
在底座上迴繞的螺旋樓梯。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A dance can trace a flowing line through space, rising and turning without pause. The project asked whether that continuous movement could be built as stairs that never end.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一支舞能在空間中劃出流動的線，不停地升起與轉身。這個專題探問，這種連續的運動能否被建造成永不終止的樓梯。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The path of two dancers turning around each other was followed as a looping line. This line was translated into a long stair that curves, climbs and returns to itself.
captions: The stair loop seen from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 兩位舞者相互環繞的路徑被描成一條迴繞的線。這條線被轉譯為一道彎曲、攀升並回到自身的長樓梯。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stairs were cut from white PVC sheets and joined so that they appear continuous from every viewpoint. Thin rods support the upper flights, leaving the steps almost floating.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 樓梯以白色 PVC 板切割並接合，使它們從每個視角看來都連續不斷。細桿支撐著上層的梯段，讓階梯幾乎漂浮於空中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under strong light, the white steps cast dark shadows that echo every turn. The model reads as a pursuit that never ceases, like dancers who keep chasing one another.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在強光下，白色的階梯投下回應每一次轉折的黑影。這個模型讀來像一場永不停歇的追逐，如同彼此不斷追趕的舞者。

sections.heading: Endless Steps - Dancing in White and Shadow
sections.body: Music measures time while architecture measures space, and this project looked for a place where the two might move together. Its starting point was a dance in which two figures circle one another, rising and turning as though chasing a dream without end. The path of that dance was followed as a looping line, and the line was then translated into a long stair that curves, climbs and returns to itself. Built from white PVC sheets, the stairs were joined so that they appear continuous from every viewpoint, while thin rods hold the upper flights so lightly that the steps seem to float. Small figures placed along the route turn the model into a journey of pursuit and perseverance. Under strong light, the white treads cast dark shadows that follow every turn, so that the structure plays like a keyboard, its pale steps answered by black ones beneath. The guidance encouraged translation between art forms, showing how rhythm and emotion borrowed from performance can give a simple material a strong spatial narrative.

zh-Hant.heading: 無盡的階梯-在白與影之間起舞
zh-Hant.body: 音樂度量時間，建築度量空間，這個專題尋找兩者能一同移動的所在。它的起點是一支舞，兩個身影彼此環繞，升起又轉身，彷彿追逐一個沒有盡頭的夢。這支舞的路徑被描成一條迴繞的線，這條線接著被轉譯為一道彎曲、攀升並回到自身的長樓梯。以白色 PVC 板建造的樓梯被仔細接合，使其從每個視角看來都連續不斷，細桿則輕巧地托住上層梯段，讓階梯彷彿漂浮。沿路安置的小小人形，把模型變成一段關於追尋與堅持的旅程。在強光之下，白色踏面投下緊隨每一次轉折的黑影，使結構如同一副琴鍵，淺色的階梯與其下的黑色彼此應答。指導鼓勵在不同藝術形式之間轉譯，顯示借自表演的節奏與情感，能賦予簡單的材料強烈的空間敘事。

pins.title: City Collage in 3D
pins.description:
Hand drawings of machine components are collaged into a map, and the spaces between their lines are built up as a white city of curving walls and terraces.

Drawings and physical model | Collage-to-space study | Pencil, paper, white card | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 立體城市拼貼
zh-Hant.description:
機械零件的手繪圖被拼貼成一張地圖，線條之間的空間再被堆疊為一座由彎曲牆面與台地構成的白色城市。

繪圖與實體模型｜拼貼到空間的研究｜鉛筆、紙、白卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The white city model seen from above.
從上方看白色城市模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Industrial components hide intricate spaces inside their casings and channels. The project asked whether those hidden interiors could become the streets and walls of a small community.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 工業零件在外殼與管道之中藏著繁複的空間。這個專題探問，這些隱藏的內部能否成為一個小社區的街道與牆面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several machine components were drawn by hand in profile. The drawings were collaged together over contour lines that recall the outline of small hills.
captions: The collaged drawing over contour lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 數個機械零件以手繪方式描出剖面輪廓。這些繪圖被拼貼在一起，疊在令人想起小山丘輪廓的等高線之上。
captions: 疊在等高線上的拼貼繪圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Following the space between the drawn lines, mini buildings and walls were raised in white card. Layers of sheets were stacked to form public terraces between the parts.
captions: The model across the collage base.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 沿著繪線之間的空間，小型建築與牆面以白卡紙立起。層層紙片被堆疊，在零件之間形成公共的台地。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model reads as a dense city of curving walls, courts and rounded towers. Traces of the original drawings remain visible on the ground between them.
captions: Rounded towers and walls of the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型讀來像一座由彎曲牆面、庭院與圓形塔體構成的密集城市。原始繪圖的痕跡仍清晰可見地留在它們之間的地面上。

sections.heading: Hidden Chambers - A Community from Machine Profiles
sections.body: Machines are rarely seen from within, yet their casings conceal chambers, channels and curves as complex as any town. This project, prompted by a visit to an exhibition of industrial design, began by drawing several components in profile, slowly tracing each housing, gear and passage by hand. The drawings were then collaged over contour lines resembling the outline of small hills, so that mechanical parts and landscape merged into a single map. Reading the gaps between lines as potential space, the next stage raised mini buildings and walls from white card, while stacked sheets formed public terraces where the parts meet. The finished model resembles a dense settlement of curving walls, enclosed courts and rounded towers, with fragments of the original drawings still visible underfoot like a buried plan. Seen from above, the city appears both engineered and grown. The guidance emphasised drawing as a way of discovering space, showing how an attentive line can reveal an unexpected architecture already present inside everyday objects.

zh-Hant.heading: 隱藏的腔室-由機械剖面長出的社區
zh-Hant.body: 機械很少被從內部觀看，然而它們的外殼之中藏著腔室、管道與曲線，繁複程度不亞於任何城鎮。這個專題受一次工業設計展覽啟發，從描繪數個零件的剖面開始，以手緩慢描出每一個外殼、齒輪與通道。這些繪圖接著被拼貼在類似小山丘輪廓的等高線上，使機械零件與地景融合為一張地圖。把線條之間的空隙讀作潛在的空間，下一個階段以白卡紙立起小型建築與牆面，堆疊的紙片則在零件交會之處形成公共台地。完成的模型如同一座密集的聚落，由彎曲牆面、圍合庭院與圓形塔體構成，原始繪圖的片段仍在腳下清晰可見，宛如一張埋藏的平面。從上方看，這座城市既像被設計，又像自行生長。指導強調以繪圖發現空間，顯示專注的線條能揭示早已存在於日常物件之中、意想不到的建築。

pins.title: Interactive Theater
pins.description:
A piano piece is translated into a music box of scattered cylinders and acrylic columns, where hidden air holes lift floating gauze into waves of light.

Installation model and drawing | Music-to-space study | Organza, acrylic columns, painted cylinders, card | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 互動劇場
zh-Hant.description:
一首鋼琴曲被轉譯為一個由散落圓柱與壓克力柱構成的音樂盒，隱藏的氣孔把漂浮的薄紗吹成一道道光的波浪。

裝置模型與繪圖｜音樂到空間的研究｜歐根紗、壓克力柱、上漆圓柱、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The music box with floating gauze.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A romantic piano piece moves between bold leaps and quiet breaths. The project asked how its notes, strength and pitch could be turned into the layout, colour and movement of a small theatre.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一首浪漫時期的鋼琴曲在大膽的跳躍與安靜的呼吸之間流轉。這個專題探問，它的音符、力度與音高如何能轉化為一座小劇場的配置、色彩與動態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Notes from the score were placed on a staff drawn across the base of the box. Top and front views tested how high and low cylinders could stand for the rhythm of the melody.
captions: Note cylinders placed on the staff.
Top and front views of the box.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 樂譜上的音符被安置在畫於盒底的五線譜上。頂視與正視圖測試了高低不一的圓柱如何代表旋律的節奏。
captions: 安置在五線譜上的音符圓柱。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A first sketch fixed the box, its corner columns and its notes, and the top was painted in shades of blue. Gold and silver paint was used on the cylinders to bring a romantic shimmer.
captions: The first sketch of the box.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一張草圖確定了盒子、角落的柱子與音符，盒頂則被漆上層層藍色。圓柱塗上金色與銀色的漆，帶出浪漫的光澤。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Air blowing through small holes beneath some notes lifts the organza into flowing layers. When the gauze touches the blue top, the whole box seems to breathe like the music.
captions: Gauze rising toward the blue top.
The box as a lit stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 空氣從部分音符底下的小孔吹出，把歐根紗托起為流動的層次。當薄紗觸及藍色的盒頂，整個盒子彷彿隨著音樂呼吸。
captions: 漂浮於音符之上的薄紗。

sections.heading: Breathing Gauze - A Melody Given Air
sections.body: A piece of music unfolds in time, yet its rises and pauses can also be imagined as the outline of a place. This project took a romantic piano work as its score and attempted to translate its notes, strength, breath and pitch into an architectural ensemble. A staff was drawn across the base of a box, and cylinders of different heights were set upon it as notes, their scattered rhythm recording the leaps of the melody. Gold and silver paint gave the cylinders a romantic shimmer, transparent acrylic columns stood in the corners like the pipes of an organ, and the top of the box was painted in shades of blue. The decisive element, however, was invisible. Small holes hidden beneath some notes release a current of air that lifts sheets of organza into flowing layers, so that the gauze rises, folds and touches the blue sky above. The box appears to breathe with the music. The guidance encouraged imagining beyond the model, proposing that such an installation could tour as a portable theatre for pop-up performances.

zh-Hant.heading: 呼吸的薄紗-被賦予空氣的旋律
zh-Hant.body: 一段音樂在時間中展開，然而它的起伏與停頓，也能被想像為一個場所的輪廓。這個專題以一首浪漫時期的鋼琴作品為樂譜，試圖把其音符、力度、呼吸與音高轉譯為一組建築群。一道五線譜被畫在盒子底部，高低不一的圓柱作為音符立於其上，散落的節奏記錄著旋律的跳躍。金色與銀色的漆賦予圓柱浪漫的光澤，透明的壓克力柱如管風琴的音管般立於四角，盒頂則被漆上層層藍色。然而決定性的元素是看不見的。藏在部分音符底下的小孔釋放出一股氣流，把歐根紗托起為流動的層次，使薄紗升起、摺疊並觸及上方藍色的天空。整個盒子彷彿隨著音樂呼吸。指導鼓勵超越模型的想像，提出這樣的裝置可以作為巡迴的可移動劇場，承載快閃演出。

pins.title: Back to Nature
pins.description:
Following the three movements of a classical sonata, a journey leads from a grid of foam blocks into a climbing forest of branches and down a transparent slide.

Physical model and drawing | Music and narrative study | Branches, foam blocks, wood blocks, plastic sheet | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 回歸自然
zh-Hant.description:
依循古典奏鳴曲的三個樂章，一段旅程從泡沫方塊構成的網格出發，進入攀升的枝條森林，再沿透明滑道而下。

實體模型與繪圖｜音樂與敘事研究｜樹枝、泡沫方塊、木塊、塑膠片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Busy life in crowded cities often makes people forget the quiet of nature. The project asked how a journey from the city back to nature could be told through space, following the mood of a piece of music.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 擁擠城市中的忙碌生活，常讓人遺忘自然的寧靜。這個專題探問，如何依循一段音樂的情緒，以空間講述一趟從城市回歸自然的旅程。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The emotions and speed of three sonata movements were mapped as a storyline for a traveller. A drawing traced the route from dense blocks, up through a forest and down a long winding path.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 奏鳴曲三個樂章的情緒與速度，被描繪為一位旅人的故事線。一張繪圖描出路徑，從密集的方塊出發，向上穿越森林，再沿一條長長的蜿蜒小徑而下。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Neatly arranged foam blocks on sticks stood for the cold density of the city in the first movement. Interlaced branches were then gathered around them to recreate the shaded calm of a forest.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 整齊排列在細桿上的泡沫方塊，代表第一樂章中城市冷漠的密度。交錯的枝條接著被聚集在它們周圍，重現森林遮蔭下的寧靜。
captions: 聚集在方塊上方的枝條。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Wooden stairs and small platforms climb through the branches, offering places to pause on the way up. At the top, a transparent slide carries the traveller swiftly down, matching the fast and cheerful final movement.
captions: Stairs and platforms in the branch frame.
A spiral stair rising through the forest.
A close view of a winding stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 木樓梯與小平台在枝條間攀升，在向上的途中提供停歇之處。在頂端，一道透明滑道載著旅人迅速而下，呼應快速而歡快的最後樂章。
captions: 枝條框架中的樓梯與平台。
穿過森林升起的螺旋梯。

sections.heading: Three Movements - A Climb from Blocks to Branches
sections.body: A classical sonata unfolds in three movements, and this project read that structure as the outline of a journey from the city back to nature. The emotions and tempo of each section were mapped onto a storyline for a single traveller, and a drawing traced the route from a dense settlement, up through a forest and down a long winding path. In the first movement, neatly arranged foam blocks on thin sticks evoke the coldness of crowded housing, their regular grid holding little room for wandering. The second movement turns relaxed and mysterious, so interlaced branches were gathered around the blocks to recreate the shaded calm of woodland, with wooden stairs climbing upward and small platforms appearing at each turn as places to rest. At the summit the traveller sees the sun again, and a transparent slide, made from plastic sheets, carries the descent swiftly to the ground, matching the cheerful pace of the finale. The guidance encouraged narrative thinking, showing how musical form can shape a sequence of spaces that invites people to slow down and rediscover nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 三個樂章-從方塊攀向枝條
zh-Hant.body: 一首古典奏鳴曲以三個樂章展開，這個專題把這種結構讀作一趟從城市回歸自然之旅的輪廓。每一段的情緒與速度被對應到一位旅人的故事線上，一張繪圖描出路徑，從密集的聚落出發，向上穿越森林，再沿一條長長的蜿蜒小徑而下。在第一樂章中，整齊排列在細桿上的泡沫方塊喚起擁擠住宅的冷漠，其規則的網格幾乎不留漫遊的餘地。第二樂章轉為放鬆而神秘，於是交錯的枝條被聚集在方塊周圍，重現林地遮蔭下的寧靜，木樓梯向上攀升，小平台在每個轉彎處出現，作為歇息之所。在頂端，旅人再次看見太陽，一道以塑膠片製成的透明滑道載著下降的旅程迅速回到地面，呼應終曲歡快的節奏。指導鼓勵敘事性的思考，顯示音樂的形式能塑造一連串空間，邀請人們放慢腳步，重新發現自然。

pins.title: Natural Growth
pins.description:
A landscape photograph is reduced to triangles and built in wooden strips and PVC card, then doubled and joined into a tall tower of gathered spaces.

Physical model and drawing | Primitive structure study | Wooden strips, PVC cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然生長
zh-Hant.description:
一張風景照片被簡化為三角形，以木條與 PVC 卡板建造，再複製並接合成一座聚集空間的高塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜原始結構研究｜木條、PVC 卡板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final tower of triangulated frames.
三角化框架構成的最終塔體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The triangle of the primitive hut is one of the oldest ideas of shelter, while stories of people building upward speak of the power of gathering. The project asked how both could be joined in one structure that starts from the most basic form.
captions: Inspiration: Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Tower of Babel and the Primitive Hut theorised by Marc-Antoine Laugier.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 原始小屋的三角形是最古老的庇護構想之一，而人們向上建造的故事則訴說著聚集的力量。這個專題探問，如何能在一個從最基本形式出發的結構中，結合這兩者。
captions: 靈感：老彼得·布勒哲爾的《巴別塔》與洛吉耶提出的原始棚屋。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The elements of a landscape photograph were simplified into a net of triangles. Layered drawings then tested how the net could rise into a three-dimensional frame.
captions: The landscape photograph that was reduced to triangles.
The landscape reduced to a net of triangles.
Layered drawings of the rising net.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張風景照片中的元素被簡化為一張三角形的網。層疊的繪圖接著測試這張網如何升起為立體的框架。
captions: 被簡化為三角形的風景照片。
被簡化為三角網的風景。
升起中的線網層疊繪圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: PVC card triangles were cut along the net and wooden strips were added upright to form a first model of spiky peaks. The model was repeated to make a top and a bottom with the same structure.
captions: Shaping the strips and card by hand.
The first model of strips and card.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: PVC 卡板三角形沿著網切出，再豎立加上木條，形成第一個尖峰狀的模型。這個模型被重複製作，成為結構相同的頂部與底部。
captions: 木條與卡板構成的第一個模型。
疊合在一起的兩個半部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Horizontal planes were added between the two halves and along the strips so that small figures could stand on them. The final tower holds balconies, verandas and small rooms within its triangulated frame.
captions: The halves joined into one tower.
The combined tower on its base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 水平板被加在兩個半部之間以及木條之上，讓小小的人形能站立其上。最終的塔在三角化的框架中容納陽台、廊道與小房間。
captions: 接合為一座塔的兩個半部。

sections.heading: Gathered Triangles - Rising from the First Shelter
sections.body: Architecture is often traced back to a simple hut of leaning branches, a triangle that answers the most basic need for shelter. This project returned to that starting point while also reaching for the opposite image, a tower that rises because many people choose to build together. A landscape photograph was first reduced to a net of triangles, and layered drawings imagined how the net might lift off the page. PVC card triangles were cut along its lines, and upright wooden strips grew from their intersections into a field of spiky peaks. The model was then repeated, and the two identical halves were set one above the other as the top and bottom of a single body. Horizontal planes inserted between and along the strips allowed small figures to stand, transforming the structure into a vertical settlement of balconies, verandas, entrances and small offices. The final tower appears both raw and inhabited. The guidance encouraged thinking from first principles, showing how the most elementary form can be multiplied into a rich and gathered architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 聚集的三角-從最初的庇護升起
zh-Hant.body: 建築常被追溯到一座以斜靠枝條搭成的簡單小屋，一個回應最基本庇護需求的三角形。這個專題回到這個起點，同時也伸向相反的意象，一座因為許多人選擇共同建造而升起的高塔。一張風景照片先被簡化為三角形的網，層疊的繪圖則想像這張網如何離開紙面而升起。PVC 卡板三角形沿著網的線條切出，豎立的木條從交點長出，形成一片尖峰狀的地景。模型接著被重複製作，兩個相同的半部一上一下放置，成為單一形體的頂部與底部。插入其間與沿著木條的水平板讓小小的人形得以站立，把結構轉化為一座由陽台、廊道、入口與小辦公室構成的垂直聚落。最終的塔看起來既粗獷又有人居住。指導鼓勵從第一原理思考，顯示最基本的形式能被倍增為豐富而聚集的建築。

pins.title: Twisted
pins.description:
Pattern drawings of twisting lines lead to a cuboid wooden frame in which black and white stockings are stretched, turned and fixed with glue into a warped space.

Physical model and drawing | Distorted space study | Wooden strips, stockings, acrylic glue, drawing pins, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 扭轉
zh-Hant.description:
描繪扭轉線條的紋樣繪圖，引出一個長方體木框，黑白絲襪在其中被拉伸、旋轉並以膠固定，形成一個扭曲的空間。

實體模型與繪圖｜扭曲空間研究｜木條、絲襪、壓克力膠、圖釘、PVC 板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Stockings stretched and twisted in the frame.
在框架中被拉伸扭轉的絲襪。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A twist can turn a simple box into a space that feels in motion. The project asked how a fixed frame could hold a soft material that twists between its corners.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一次扭轉能把簡單的盒子變成一個彷彿在運動中的空間。這個專題探問，一個固定的框架如何能承載在其角落之間扭轉的柔軟材料。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Elements from fifty pattern pictures were quickly extracted as pencil drawings. Those that twisted to a certain degree were picked out as the seeds of a distorted space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從五十張紋樣圖片中迅速抽取元素，畫成鉛筆繪圖。其中扭轉到一定程度的被挑選出來，作為扭曲空間的種子。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A fixed cuboid frame of wooden strips was built on a thin PVC base. Black and white stockings were pinned to its edges and turned until they crossed in the middle.
captions: Twisted stockings seen from two sides.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以木條建造的固定長方體框架立於薄 PVC 底板上。黑白絲襪被釘在框架邊緣，並旋轉至在中央交錯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Acrylic glue poured over the stockings fixed their shape as a frozen twist. The surfaces narrow toward the centre and open again at the top and bottom like a turning column.
captions: Further views of the fixed twist.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 倒在絲襪上的壓克力膠，把它們的形狀固定為一個凝結的扭轉。表面向中央收窄，再於頂部與底部重新打開，宛如一根旋轉的柱。
captions: 固定後扭轉的更多視角。

sections.heading: Frozen Twist - A Soft Surface Held in a Frame
sections.body: A twist is a small gesture with large spatial consequences, turning a plain volume into something that seems to move. This project began with rapid brainstorming, extracting elements from fifty pattern pictures and redrawing them in pencil as blots, waves, zigzags and radiating lines. From this collection, the patterns that twisted to a certain degree were selected as the seeds of a distorted space. A fixed cuboid frame of wooden strips was then built on a thin board, offering a stable container for an unstable material. Black and white stockings were pinned to its edges and turned until they crossed at the centre, their fine mesh revealing every line of tension. Acrylic glue poured over the fabric fixed the gesture in place, so that the surfaces narrow toward the middle and open again at the top and bottom like a slowly turning column. Viewed from different sides, the frozen twist reads as both enclosure and movement. The guidance valued experiments with unexpected materials, showing how everyday textiles can carry precise spatial ideas.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝結的扭轉-框中被固定的柔軟表面
zh-Hant.body: 扭轉是一個微小的動作，卻帶來巨大的空間效果，把素樸的量體變成彷彿在移動的形體。這個專題從快速的腦力激盪開始，從五十張紋樣圖片中抽取元素，再以鉛筆重繪為斑塊、波浪、鋸齒與放射線條。從這批收集中，扭轉到一定程度的紋樣被挑選出來，作為扭曲空間的種子。一個以木條建造的固定長方體框架接著立於薄底板上，為不穩定的材料提供穩定的容器。黑白絲襪被釘在框架邊緣，旋轉至在中央交錯，其細密的網眼顯露出每一道張力線。倒在布料上的壓克力膠把這個動作固定下來，使表面向中央收窄，再於頂部與底部重新打開，宛如一根緩緩旋轉的柱。從不同側面看，這個凝結的扭轉既是圍合也是運動。指導重視以意想不到的材料進行實驗，顯示日常的織物也能承載精確的空間構想。

pins.title: Cave of Hanging Roots
pins.description:
The hanging roots of a fig tree and the dripping forms of a limestone cave are combined in moldable plastic softened in hot water and pulled over a wire frame.

Physical model and drawing | Material exploration | Moldable plastic, steel wire, super light clay, foam board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂根洞穴
zh-Hant.description:
榕樹垂掛的氣根與石灰岩洞穴中滴垂的形態，以熱水軟化的塑形塑膠結合，拉覆在鐵絲骨架之上。

實體模型與繪圖｜材料探索｜塑形塑膠、鋼絲、超輕黏土、泡沫板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final form of pulled plastic.
拉伸塑膠構成的最終形體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Some natural forms grow freely, like the prop roots of a fig tree or the dripping columns of a cave. The project asked which material could capture that free growth in a model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 有些自然形態自由地生長，如榕樹的支柱根或洞穴中滴垂的石柱。這個專題探問，哪一種材料能在模型中捕捉這種自由的生長。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches turned the hanging roots of a tree into loops and curtains of lines. Cave formations were drawn in the same way, and the two were merged in a conceptual drawing of the model.
captions: Inspiration: the hanging roots of Ficus microcarpa and a solutional cave.
The conceptual drawing of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把樹木垂掛的根轉化為線條的迴圈與簾幕。洞穴的形態也以同樣方式被描繪，兩者再合併為一張模型的概念繪圖。
captions: 靈感：榕樹的氣根與溶蝕洞穴。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A first model in light clay stretched well but could not reach the fine, branching form of roots. A second test used steel wire as a skeleton for moldable plastic softened in hot water.
captions: Pulling the light clay by hand in the first model.
Softening the moldable plastic in hot water and pulling it over the wire by hand.
The first model in light clay.
The wire skeleton of the second model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個以輕黏土製作的模型延展性良好，卻無法達到根系細緻分枝的形態。第二次測試以鋼絲作為骨架，承載以熱水軟化的塑形塑膠。
captions: 第一個模型中以手拉伸輕黏土。
以熱水軟化可塑塑膠，再以手拉覆於鐵絲上。
輕黏土製作的第一個模型。
第二個模型的鐵絲骨架。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The softened plastic was kneaded onto the wire and pulled into thin membranes and strands. Lit from within, the final form glows like a cave hung with roots.
captions: The final form from another side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 軟化的塑膠被揉捏在鐵絲上，拉成薄膜與細絲。從內部打光後，最終形體如一座垂滿根系的洞穴般發光。

sections.heading: Pulled Membranes - Growing a Cave by Hand
sections.body: Certain forms in nature are not designed but grown, and this project sought a way to make a model that behaves in the same manner. Its inspiration came from two sources, the prop roots that hang from a fig tree and the dripping columns that slowly form inside a limestone cave. Sketches turned the roots into loops and curtains of lines, cave formations were drawn in the same language, and a conceptual drawing merged both into a single mass. The first attempt used light clay, which stretched easily yet could not achieve the fine branching of roots. A second test therefore introduced a skeleton of steel wire and a moldable plastic that softens in hot water. Kneaded onto the wire while warm, the plastic could be pulled into thin membranes and strands that set as they cooled. Lit from within, the final form glows like a hollow hung with roots, its openings and fibres recording each movement of the hand. The guidance celebrated persistent material testing, showing how failure with one medium can lead to a discovery with another.

zh-Hant.heading: 拉伸的薄膜-以手長出洞穴
zh-Hant.body: 自然中的某些形態並非被設計，而是生長出來的，這個專題尋找一種製作模型的方法，讓模型以同樣的方式運作。它的靈感來自兩個源頭，榕樹垂掛的支柱根，以及在石灰岩洞穴中緩慢形成的滴垂石柱。草圖把根轉化為線條的迴圈與簾幕，洞穴形態以同樣的語言被描繪，一張概念繪圖再把兩者合併為單一的量體。第一次嘗試使用輕黏土，它容易延展，卻無法達到根系細緻的分枝。第二次測試因此引入鋼絲骨架，以及一種遇熱水即軟化的塑形塑膠。趁溫熱時揉捏在鐵絲上，塑膠能被拉成薄膜與細絲，並在冷卻時定形。從內部打光後，最終形體如一處垂滿根系的空洞般發光，其開口與纖維記錄著手的每一次動作。指導讚揚持續的材料測試，顯示一種媒材的失敗能引向另一種媒材的發現。

pins.title: Green Into the House
pins.description:
A black-and-white pattern cropped from a digital code becomes the floor of a wooden maze, where upright sticks, windowed planks and dried flowers let people and plants share one house.

Physical model and drawing | Coexistence study | Wood board, wooden strips, dried flowers | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 綠意入屋
zh-Hant.description:
一段從數位條碼中裁出的黑白圖案成為木造迷宮的地面，豎立的木棍、開窗的木板與乾燥花，讓人與植物共享一座房子。

實體模型與繪圖｜共存研究｜木板、木條、乾燥花｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model with dried flowers.
插上乾燥花的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People and plants live side by side, yet houses rarely leave room for both. The project asked how a small building could let human life and vegetation grow together.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 人與植物比鄰而居，房屋卻很少同時為兩者留下空間。這個專題探問，一座小建築如何能讓人的生活與植物一起生長。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A small black-and-white pattern was cropped from a digital code as a sign of human exchange. A first sketch set flowers and stems on top of this checkered ground.
captions: A first sketch of plants on the pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一小段黑白圖案從數位條碼中裁出，作為人際交流的象徵。第一張草圖把花朵與莖枝放在這片棋盤般的地面上。
captions: 植物立於圖案上的第一張草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were raised at the corners of each square to form a maze-like space. Planks with large windows were then placed on top to make rooms that can be reached and entered.
captions: Process models of sticks and planks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棍豎立在每個方格的角落，形成迷宮般的空間。開有大窗的木板接著被放在上方，構成可抵達、可進入的房間。
captions: 木棍與木板的過程模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Dried flowers and grasses were planted through the frames so that they rise among the rooms. Small figures move between stems and windows as if living inside a garden house.
captions: Frames and flowers in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 乾燥花與草穿過框架種下，在房間之間升起。小小的人形在莖枝與窗戶之間穿梭，彷彿住在一座花園之屋中。

sections.heading: Shared Rooms - A Maze Where Stems Grow
sections.body: A house is usually drawn as a boundary that keeps nature outside, and this project tried to imagine the reverse. It began with a modest gesture, cropping a small black-and-white pattern from a digital code as a sign of how people now meet and exchange. Laid flat, the checkered pattern became a ground plan, and a first sketch placed flowers and stems directly upon it. Wooden sticks were then raised at the corners of each square, so that the flat code grew into a maze of narrow passages and open courts. Planks pierced by large windows were set on top, offering rooms that small figures could climb toward and enter. Finally, dried flowers and grasses were inserted through the frames, rising between floors and leaning across openings until it became difficult to tell where architecture ended and planting began. The result reads as a tiny settlement shared by two kinds of inhabitants. The guidance encouraged a gentle, intuitive way of thinking, turning an everyday digital symbol into a hopeful picture of coexistence.

zh-Hant.heading: 共享的房間-莖枝生長的迷宮
zh-Hant.body: 房屋通常被畫成一道把自然擋在外面的邊界，這個專題則嘗試想像相反的情形。它從一個樸素的動作開始，從數位條碼中裁出一小段黑白圖案，作為今日人們相遇與交流方式的象徵。平放之後，這片棋盤般的圖案成為一張平面圖，第一張草圖便把花朵與莖枝直接放在其上。木棍接著在每個方格的角落豎起，讓平面的條碼長成一座由狹窄通道與開放庭院構成的迷宮。開有大窗的木板被放在上方，提供小小人形可以攀向並進入的房間。最後，乾燥花與草穿過框架插入，在樓層之間升起、斜倚過開口，直到難以分辨建築在何處結束、植栽從何處開始。成果讀來像一座由兩種居民共享的微小聚落。指導鼓勵一種溫和而直覺的思考方式，把日常的數位符號轉化為一幅充滿希望的共存圖景。

pins.title: Chairs
pins.description:
Drawings of everyday chairs are overlapped, coloured and built in white PVC ribbons and wooden stairs into a model that feels like an amusement park.

Physical model and drawing | Sketch-to-space study | PVC, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 椅子
zh-Hant.description:
日常椅子的繪圖被重疊、上色，再以白色 PVC 帶與木階梯建成一個宛如遊樂園的模型。

實體模型與繪圖｜草圖到空間研究｜PVC、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of curving ribbons.
彎曲帶狀構成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A chair is an ordinary yet loyal companion that is seldom noticed. The project asked whether the lines of everyday chairs could be turned into a space for people to inhabit.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 椅子是平凡卻忠實的伴侶，很少被注意。這個專題探問，日常椅子的線條能否被轉化為供人棲居的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Different types of daily chairs were observed and drawn in simple outlines. Colour studies then tested palettes for a layered composition of their parts.
captions: The collage made from chair pictures cut out of a magazine.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 各種日常使用的椅子被觀察並以簡單的輪廓描繪。色彩研究接著為其部件的層疊構圖測試配色。
captions: 以雜誌剪下的椅子圖片製作的拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chair outlines were overlapped into one dense drawing and then coloured as interlocking shapes. This flat image was read as a plan of ribbons, ramps and platforms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 椅子輪廓被重疊成一張密集的繪圖，再以互鎖的形狀上色。這張平面圖像被解讀為一張由帶狀、坡道與平台構成的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: White PVC strips were bent into arches and loops, and small wooden stairs connect their levels. Seen from above and inside, the model becomes a playful landscape of paths and viewpoints.
captions: Two views of the ribbon model.
The final model from the rear.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色 PVC 條被彎成拱與迴圈，小小的木階梯連接各個層次。從上方與內部看，模型成為一片充滿路徑與觀景點的趣味地景。

sections.heading: Ribbons of Rest - From Seat to Playground
sections.body: Few objects accompany daily life as faithfully as a chair, yet its shape is rarely looked at with care. This project began by observing that quiet companion, drawing many kinds of everyday chairs as simple outlines of legs, backs and seats. The outlines were then overlapped until they formed a dense tangle, and colour studies tested how the tangle could be divided into interlocking shapes. Once coloured, the flat image no longer depicted furniture; it suggested a plan of ribbons, ramps and platforms waiting to be lifted. White PVC strips were bent into arches and loops that follow those curves, while small wooden stairs were added to connect one level to the next. Viewed from above, the model resembles a swirling drawing; viewed from within, it offers balconies, tunnels and stairs where small figures pause and look out. The final piece feels like an amusement park grown from a sketch. The guidance valued close observation of ordinary things, showing how a familiar object can open into an unexpected spatial world.

zh-Hant.heading: 休憩的緞帶-從座椅到遊樂場
zh-Hant.body: 很少有物件能像椅子一樣忠實地陪伴日常生活，它的形狀卻很少被仔細端詳。這個專題從觀察這位安靜的伴侶開始，把各種日常椅子畫成椅腳、椅背與座面的簡單輪廓。這些輪廓接著被重疊，直到形成一團密集的線條，色彩研究則測試這團線條如何被分割為互鎖的形狀。上色之後，平面圖像不再描繪家具，而是暗示一張等待被抬起的帶狀、坡道與平台的平面。白色 PVC 條被彎成順著這些曲線的拱與迴圈，小小的木階梯則被加入，把一個層次連向下一個層次。從上方看，模型像一張旋轉的繪圖；從內部看，它提供陽台、隧道與階梯，讓小小的人形停下並向外眺望。最終作品宛如一座從草圖長出的遊樂園。指導重視對平凡事物的細心觀察，顯示熟悉的物件也能打開一個意想不到的空間世界。

pins.title: Re-Creation
pins.description:
Pattern tiles and brick stacking tests lead to a shared activity space of wooden bricks, where dried trees grow through openings left in the walls.

Physical model and drawing | Material and enclosure study | Wooden bricks, dried flowers, grass powder | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 再造
zh-Hant.description:
紋樣圖塊與磚塊堆疊測試，引出一個以木磚構成的共享活動空間，乾燥的樹從牆上留下的開口中長出。

實體模型與繪圖｜材料與圍合研究｜木磚、乾燥花、草粉｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final activity space of wooden bricks.
木磚構成的最終活動空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In many large public buildings, plants are squeezed into leftover corners and their growth is restricted. The project asked how a built space could open itself to nature instead of blocking it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在許多大型公共建築中，植物被擠進剩餘的角落，生長受到限制。這個專題探問，建成的空間如何能向自然打開，而不是阻擋它。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A grid of pattern tiles explored textures that might describe growth and confinement. One pattern was developed into a sweeping ink drawing of curved layers.
captions: Site photo collages and diagrams from Guangzhou South Railway Station.
An ink drawing of curved layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一組紋樣圖塊探索可能描述生長與受限的質感。其中一種紋樣被發展為一張彎曲層疊的流暢墨線繪圖。
captions: 廣州南站的基地照片拼貼與圖解。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The idea of a blockade led to bricks, which were stacked in many ways to test a sense of enclosure. Curved walls and small stacks showed how gaps could let light and growth pass through.
captions: Stacking the wooden bricks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 封鎖的概念引向磚塊，磚塊以多種方式堆疊，測試圍合的感受。彎曲的牆與小型堆疊顯示縫隙如何讓光與生長穿過。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model arranges wooden bricks into a porous shelter on a base of grass. Dried trees rise through its openings, and figures sit on loose blocks in the shared space.
captions: Blocks used as seats beneath a tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把木磚排成草地基座上一座多孔的庇護所。乾燥的樹從開口中升起，人形坐在共享空間中散置的木塊上。

sections.heading: Porous Walls - Letting Growth Return
sections.body: Large public buildings often treat plants as decoration placed in leftover corners, and this project questioned that habit. Its first step was a grid of pattern tiles, quick studies of texture that searched for ways to express both growth and confinement. One tile was developed into a sweeping ink drawing of curved layers, suggesting walls that bend rather than block. The idea of a blockade then pointed toward bricks, the most familiar unit of enclosure. Small wooden bricks were stacked in many configurations, from straight rows to hollow piers and curving walls, and each test was photographed to compare how much light and space slipped through the gaps. These experiments shaped the final model, a porous shelter of wooden bricks set on a ground of grass. Dried trees grow through openings left in its walls, while loose blocks become seats where small figures gather beneath the branches. The structure reads as a shared activity space that welcomes nature into its fabric. The guidance supported research driven by a clear question, turning criticism into a constructive spatial proposal.

zh-Hant.heading: 多孔的牆-讓生長歸來
zh-Hant.body: 大型公共建築常把植物當作放在剩餘角落的裝飾，這個專題質疑這種習慣。它的第一步是一組紋樣圖塊，以快速的質感研究尋找同時表達生長與受限的方式。其中一個圖塊被發展為一張彎曲層疊的流暢墨線繪圖，暗示會彎曲而非阻擋的牆。封鎖的概念接著指向磚塊，這個最熟悉的圍合單元。小小的木磚以多種組合堆疊，從直排到中空的墩柱與彎曲的牆，每次測試都被拍攝下來，比較有多少光與空間從縫隙中滲出。這些實驗塑造了最終模型，一座立於草地上、以木磚構成的多孔庇護所。乾燥的樹從牆上留下的開口長出，散置的木塊則成為座椅，讓小小的人形聚集在枝葉之下。這個結構讀來是一個把自然迎入其肌理的共享活動空間。指導支持由清晰問題驅動的研究，把批判轉化為具建設性的空間提案。

pins.title: Out of Shape
pins.description:
The paths of basketball players are traced, linked and coloured into abstract drawings, then cut from PVC and stacked with parchment layers into a sharp, mechanical maquette.

Physical model and drawing | Movement-to-form study | PVC, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 失形
zh-Hant.description:
籃球員的移動路徑被描繪、連結並上色為抽象繪圖，再從 PVC 切出，與層層羊皮紙疊合成一個尖銳而機械感的模型。

實體模型與繪圖｜動作到形式研究｜PVC、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The layered maquette with PVC shards.
帶有 PVC 碎片的層疊模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: On a basketball court, players constantly roam to attack and defend, creating shifting patterns in space. The project asked how these invisible movements could be given a three-dimensional form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在籃球場上，球員不斷移動以進攻與防守，在空間中形成變動的圖形。這個專題探問，這些看不見的移動如何能被賦予立體的形式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Court diagrams traced the paths of forward and defence players and marked their zones of attack and defence. Sheets of plays recorded several layouts side by side for comparison.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 球場圖描繪前鋒與防守球員的路徑，並標出雙方的進攻與防守區域。戰術圖紙把幾種布陣並排記錄，以便比較。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each defender was connected by a line to the nearest forward, producing an abstract web of triangles and arcs. These renders were coloured, framed and pasted onto PVC board.
captions: An abstract render of linked paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每位防守球員以一條線連向最近的前鋒，產生由三角形與弧線構成的抽象網絡。這些繪圖被上色、框起，再貼到 PVC 板上。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The boards were sliced into shards and reassembled into a sharp, mechanical sculpture. It was inserted into a box of stacked parchment layers, as if bursting through a building.
captions: The sliced sculpture inserted into a building, inspired by Lebbeus Woods' Neomechanical Tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 板材被切成碎片，重組為一個尖銳而機械感的雕塑。它被插入一個由層層羊皮紙疊成的盒子中，彷彿正衝破一座建築。
captions: 切片雕塑置入建築之中，靈感來自萊伯斯·伍茲的《新機械塔》。

sections.heading: Traced Pursuit - When Play Becomes Structure
sections.body: A game of basketball is a constant negotiation of space, with players drifting, cutting and covering one another in patterns that vanish the moment they form. This project set out to catch those fleeting relationships and hold them still. Court diagrams first traced the paths of forward and defence players and outlined the zones each side sought to occupy. Several plays were recorded on sheets so that their differences could be compared. The decisive step came when every defender was joined by a line to the nearest forward, turning a sporting tactic into an abstract web of triangles and arcs. These renders were coloured, framed and pasted onto PVC board, where they began to suggest planes rather than marks. Sliced into shards and reassembled, the boards formed a sharp, mechanical sculpture that was then pushed into a box of stacked parchment layers, as if movement were breaking through a calm building. The guidance valued translating personal passions into design, revealing how the logic of a game can generate unexpected architectural tension.

zh-Hant.heading: 追逐的軌跡-當比賽成為結構
zh-Hant.body: 一場籃球比賽是一場不斷進行的空間協商，球員漂移、切入、彼此盯防，形成一出現就消失的圖形。這個專題著手捕捉這些稍縱即逝的關係，並讓它們靜止下來。球場圖先描繪前鋒與防守球員的路徑，勾勒雙方各自爭取佔據的區域。幾種戰術被記錄在圖紙上，以便比較其差異。決定性的一步，是把每位防守球員以一條線連向最近的前鋒，把運動戰術轉化為由三角形與弧線構成的抽象網絡。這些繪圖被上色、框起並貼到 PVC 板上，開始暗示面而非筆跡。板材被切成碎片並重組，形成一個尖銳而機械感的雕塑，再被推入一個由層層羊皮紙疊成的盒子中，彷彿運動正衝破一座平靜的建築。指導重視把個人熱愛轉化為設計，揭示比賽的邏輯如何能產生意想不到的建築張力。

pins.title: X-Gravity
pins.description:
Looping studies of rotation lead to cubes of different sizes joined by wooden sticks and partly skinned in paper, forming a cluster that seems to float free of gravity.

Physical model and drawing | Anti-gravity study | Cardboard, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: X-重力
zh-Hant.description:
旋轉的迴圈研究，引出以木棍連接、部分覆上紙面的不同尺寸立方體，形成一個彷彿脫離重力而漂浮的群體。

實體模型與繪圖｜反重力研究｜卡紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Some sculptures seem to rotate and hover as if gravity no longer applied. The project asked how a structure of simple cubes could create the same impression of weightlessness.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 有些雕塑似乎在旋轉與懸浮，彷彿重力不再存在。這個專題探問，一個由簡單立方體構成的結構如何能創造同樣的失重感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Rough studies of looping strips explored rotating, tangled movement in space. A sketch of stacked boxes then tested how solid volumes might replace the loops.
captions: Photographs from the Antony Gormley exhibition that inspired the project, including Clearing and Lost Horizon.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 捲曲紙條的粗略研究探索空間中旋轉而纏繞的運動。一張堆疊盒子的草圖接著測試實體量體如何取代這些迴圈。
captions: 啟發本案的安東尼·葛姆雷展覽照片，包括《Clearing》與《Lost Horizon》。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cubes of varying sizes were built from wooden sticks and connected at their corners. Paper was pasted on only some faces so that solid and open sides alternate.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同尺寸的立方體以木棍建造，並在角落相互連接。只有部分面被貼上紙，讓實面與開放面交替出現。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The cluster branches outward and tilts in many directions, touching the ground at only a few points. Close views show small figures inside frames that seem to drift in the air.
captions: A close view of the frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這個群體向外分枝並朝多個方向傾斜，只在少數幾點觸及地面。近景顯示小小的人形身處彷彿在空中漂移的框架之中。

sections.heading: Suspended Cells - Building Against the Fall
sections.body: Gravity is the most constant force acting on architecture, so a structure that appears to ignore it immediately unsettles expectations. This project grew from the memory of sculptures whose rotating, tangled lines seemed to hover in a gallery, and it began with rough studies of looping paper strips that captured that sense of spin. A sketch of stacked boxes then asked whether solid volumes could carry the same energy. Cubes of varying sizes were built from wooden sticks and joined corner to corner, so that each new unit leaned away from the last. Paper was pasted on only some faces, letting closed and open sides alternate and making the cluster flicker between mass and void. As the arrangement grew, it branched outward and tilted in many directions while touching the ground at only a few points. Small figures placed within the frames appear to drift through the air. The guidance encouraged learning from artworks without copying them, transforming an emotional response into a clear structural experiment.

zh-Hant.heading: 懸浮的單元-逆著墜落而建
zh-Hant.body: 重力是作用在建築上最恆常的力量，因此一個看似無視重力的結構會立刻動搖人們的預期。這個專題源自對一些雕塑的記憶，那些旋轉而纏繞的線條彷彿懸浮在展廳之中，它便從捕捉這種旋轉感的捲曲紙條粗略研究開始。一張堆疊盒子的草圖接著探問，實體量體能否承載同樣的能量。不同尺寸的立方體以木棍建造，角對角相互連接，使每個新的單元都傾離前一個。只有部分面被貼上紙，讓封閉面與開放面交替出現，使群體在實與虛之間閃爍。隨著排列增長，它向外分枝，朝多個方向傾斜，只在少數幾點觸及地面。放在框架中的小小人形彷彿在空中漂移。指導鼓勵向藝術作品學習而不複製，把情感的回應轉化為清晰的結構實驗。

pins.title: Blind Boxes
pins.description:
The changing moods of opening a surprise box are drawn as six patterns and built as six cubic rooms of card, sticks, film and coloured planes, then spliced into one imaginary building.

Physical model and drawing | Emotion-to-space study | Paper board, wooden strips, museum board, strings, PVC | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 盲盒
zh-Hant.description:
打開驚喜盒子時起伏的心情被畫成六種紋樣，再以卡紙、木條、薄膜與彩色平面建成六個立方房間，拼接為一座想像的建築。

實體模型與繪圖｜情緒到空間研究｜紙板、木條、博物館板、繩線、PVC｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The mood boxes spliced into one building.
拼接成一座建築的情緒盒子。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Opening a surprise box brings anticipation, tension, delight or disappointment within seconds. The project asked how each of these passing moods could become a distinct small space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 打開驚喜盒子會在幾秒內帶來期待、緊張、喜悅或失望。這個專題探問，這些短暫的情緒如何各自成為一個獨特的小空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each mood was recorded as a hand-drawn pattern, from clustered hexagons for imagining to scattered triangles for disappointment. The drawings set the rhythm and density for every box.
captions: The six moods of opening a blind box, drawn around a blind-box figure.
The blind-box packaging that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每一種情緒都被記錄為一張手繪紋樣，從象徵想像的聚集六角形，到象徵失望的散落三角形。這些繪圖為每個盒子設定了節奏與密度。
captions: 圍繞盲盒公仔繪製的開盒六種心情。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Coloured papers, wooden strips and transparent film were cut into cubes, polygons and frames. These pieces were repeated, overlapped, intersected and pierced inside open cubic frames.
captions: Making the blocks and stick frames by hand.
Iridescent film on a stick frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 彩色紙、木條與透明薄膜被切成立方體、多邊形與框架。這些構件在開放的立方框架中被重複、疊合、交錯與穿透。
captions: 以手製作方塊與木條框架。
木條框架上的虹彩薄膜。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each finished box holds a different interior, from floating spheres to a chain of small frames. Placed together, the six rooms form a building that records a full cycle of feeling.
captions: Spheres and folded planes in one room.
Coloured planes scattered in a box.
A chain of small cubic frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個完成的盒子擁有不同的內部，從漂浮的球體到一串小框架。放在一起時，六個房間形成一座記錄完整情緒循環的建築。
captions: 一個房間中的球體與摺面。
散落在盒中的彩色平面。

sections.heading: Sealed Moods - Rooms for a Moment of Surprise
sections.body: The moment before a surprise box is opened compresses a whole drama of feeling into a few seconds, and this project treated that moment as material for architecture. It began by recording six moods as hand-drawn patterns, so that imagining appeared as clustered hexagons, tension as jagged peaks, excitement as rolling waves and disappointment as scattered triangles. These drawings were then read as instructions for space. Coloured papers, wooden strips, strings and transparent film were cut into cubes, polygons and fine frames, and each set of pieces was arranged inside an open cubic box. Repetition, overlap, intersection and piercing were used deliberately, giving every interior its own density and light, from a storm of sharp shards to a calm field of floating spheres. Finally, the six rooms were spliced together into a single imaginary building, where moving from one box to the next retraces the full cycle of anticipation and release. The guidance encouraged turning personal experience into a clear spatial method, showing how fleeting emotions can be measured, built and shared.

zh-Hant.heading: 封存的心情-為驚喜片刻而建的房間
zh-Hant.body: 驚喜盒子被打開之前的那一刻，把一整場情緒的戲劇壓縮在幾秒之內，這個專題把這一刻當作建築的材料。它從把六種心情記錄為手繪紋樣開始，於是想像化為聚集的六角形，緊張化為鋸齒般的尖峰，興奮化為起伏的波浪，失望則化為散落的三角形。這些繪圖接著被解讀為空間的指令。彩色紙、木條、繩線與透明薄膜被切成立方體、多邊形與細框，每一組構件都被安排在一個開放的立方盒子中。重複、疊合、交錯與穿透被刻意運用，讓每個內部擁有各自的密度與光線，從一場尖銳碎片的風暴，到一片漂浮球體的寧靜場域。最後，六個房間被拼接為一座想像的建築，從一個盒子走向下一個，便重新經歷期待與釋放的完整循環。指導鼓勵把個人經驗轉化為清晰的空間方法，顯示短暫的情緒也能被度量、建造與分享。

pins.title: Follow the Path
pins.description:
The daily routes of household pets are mapped in a home plan, rebuilt as frames and rows of sticks, and finally curled in strips of photographic film that race and chase across a base.

Physical model and drawing | Movement mapping study | Wooden strips, museum board, litmus paper, barbed wire, film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 追隨路徑
zh-Hant.description:
家中寵物的日常路線被標示在住宅平面上，再以框架與成排木條重建，最後化為一條條捲曲的攝影底片，在底座上競逐追趕。

實體模型與繪圖｜移動軌跡研究｜木條、博物館板、石蕊試紙、鐵絲、底片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Curled film strips chasing across the base.
在底座上追逐的捲曲底片。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Pets and people share a home, yet they move through it in very different ways. The project asked how these overlapping daily paths could be made visible as space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 寵物與人共享一個家，在其中移動的方式卻截然不同。這個專題探問，這些重疊的日常路徑如何能被呈現為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The living habits of the pets were observed and their routes marked on a hand-drawn plan of the home. Points, lines and angles stood for each animal and person.
captions: The three pets observed: Chuchu, Nana and Coffee.
Routes marked on a plan of the home.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 寵物的生活習性被觀察，牠們的路線被標示在一張手繪的住宅平面上。點、線與角分別代表每一隻動物與每一個人。
captions: 觀察的三隻寵物：Chuchu、Nana 與 Coffee。
標示在住宅平面上的路線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: One route was overlapped and rotated, with wooden strips marking positions and changes of speed. Another route was rebuilt in rows of sticks whose bending shows the feeling of chasing.
captions: Holding up the developed film strips by hand.
The frame model at an angle.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一條路線被疊合並旋轉，以木條標示位置與速度的變化。另一條路線以成排的木條重建，其彎曲程度呈現追逐的感受。
captions: 以手展示沖洗後的底片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Leftover photographic film was curled into loops and filled with collected hair and straw. Two strips start from one line and bend with speed, creating a playful space for animals to roam.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 剩餘的攝影底片被捲成迴圈，並填入收集的毛髮與稻草。兩條底片從同一條線出發，隨速度彎曲，創造一個讓動物漫遊的趣味空間。

sections.heading: Shared Tracks - Mapping the Pace of Companions
sections.body: A home is often drawn as rooms for people, yet it is crossed every day by quieter inhabitants whose routes go unrecorded. This project began by watching household pets closely and tracing their movements on a hand-drawn plan, where points, lines and angles distinguished each animal from each person. The resulting map revealed loops around the dining table, dashes toward the kitchen and long chases between bedrooms. One route was then overlapped with itself and rotated, while wooden strips of varying height marked where the animal paused or accelerated. Another route was rebuilt as rows of upright sticks, their bending amplitude expressing the excitement of pursuit. The final model turned to an unexpected material, leftover photographic film that still carried faint traces of memory. Curled into loops and filled with collected hair and straw, two strips set off from a single line and twist with speed as if racing, forming a small landscape for roaming. The guidance encouraged patient observation of daily life, revealing how affection and habit can shape a precise spatial language.

zh-Hant.heading: 共享的軌跡-描繪伴侶的步調
zh-Hant.body: 家常被畫成供人使用的房間，每天卻有更安靜的居民穿越其中，這些路線從未被記錄。這個專題從仔細觀察家中的寵物開始，把牠們的移動描繪在一張手繪平面上，以點、線與角區分每一隻動物與每一個人。所得的地圖顯示出繞著餐桌的迴圈、衝向廚房的短線，以及臥室之間長長的追逐。其中一條路線接著與自身疊合並旋轉，高度不一的木條標示動物停頓或加速之處。另一條路線則以成排直立的木條重建，其彎曲幅度表達追逐時的興奮。最終模型轉向一種意想不到的材料，仍帶著淡淡記憶痕跡的剩餘攝影底片。捲成迴圈並填入收集的毛髮與稻草後，兩條底片從同一條線出發，隨速度扭轉，彷彿正在競賽，形成一片可供漫遊的小小地景。指導鼓勵耐心觀察日常生活，揭示情感與習慣如何塑造精確的空間語言。

pins.title: Dystopian World
pins.description:
Four phases of The Hunger Games story are stacked into one tower of branches, paper, nets and coloured film.

Physical model | Film-to-space study | Wood sticks, tree branches, hard papers, silk stockings, coloured transparent paper, iron wire | 23×18×43 inch | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 反烏托邦世界
zh-Hant.description:
《飢餓遊戲》故事的四個階段，被堆疊成一座由樹枝、紙、網與彩色透明片構成的塔。

實體模型｜電影轉譯空間研究｜木棒、樹枝、硬紙、絲襪、彩色透明紙、鐵絲｜23×18×43 英吋｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project started from the film The Hunger Games. The question was how the central theme and the four phases of the story could be shown as one built object.
captions: The film poster and four photo collages: The Dawn, The Sacrifice, The Hope and The Loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 專題從電影《飢餓遊戲》出發，探問故事的核心主題與四個階段，如何以一件構築物呈現。
captions: 電影海報與四張拼貼：黎明、犧牲、希望與循環。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Four photo collages set out the phases: the dawn as the beginning of the revolution, the sacrifice as faith and mercy in the forest, the hope as the leader emerging, and the loop as revolution bringing new tyranny. Symbols from the film were then sketched as architectural elements.
captions: The tower sketch with symbols drawn as architectural elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 四張拼貼整理出四個階段：黎明是革命的開始，犧牲是森林中的信念與憐憫，希望是領袖的出現，循環則是革命帶來新的暴政。接著把電影中的符號畫成可被看見的建築元素。
captions: 將符號畫成建築元素的塔狀草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The top, the middle and the bottom were each tested as separate models. Curved paper strips in the middle became the element of water.
captions: Studies for the top, the middle and the bottom.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 頂部、中段與底部各自以獨立模型測試。中段彎曲的紙帶成為水的元素。
captions: 頂部、中段與底部的研究模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The four motif parts are joined into one tower. Folded paper shards and coloured film crown the top, paper rings spiral around a stick frame, and branches and a stretched net wrap the base.
captions: The four motif parts in one whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 四個母題部件組合成一座塔。折紙碎片與彩色透明片構成塔頂，紙環沿著木棒框架盤旋，樹枝與拉伸的網包覆基座。
captions: 四個母題部件合為一體。
基座下方的彩色透明片。

sections.heading: Four Phases - A Story Built Upward
sections.body: The work reads a film story as a sequence in height. Four collages first fixed the dawn, the sacrifice, the hope and the loop, and a sketch turned symbols from the film into architectural elements. The top, the middle and the bottom were then made and tested one by one. In the final model the four parts sit on one axis, from a base of branches and net to a crown of folded paper and coloured film.

zh-Hant.heading: 四個階段-向上搭建的故事
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品把一部電影的故事讀成一段高度上的序列。四張拼貼先確定黎明、犧牲、希望與循環，一張草圖再把電影中的符號轉為建築元素。頂部、中段與底部接著一一製作與測試。最終模型中，四個部分立在同一條軸線上，從樹枝與網的基座，升到折紙與彩色透明片的塔頂。

pins.title: Depressive Feeling 3
pins.description:
The curves of Antelope Canyon are traced through painting and drawing and built as a layered PVC sculpture.

Physical model | Emotion-to-space study | PVC boards | 14×11×10.5 inch | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 憂鬱感受 3
zh-Hant.description:
羚羊峽谷的曲線經由繪畫與素描被追溯，並建成一件層疊的PVC雕塑。

實體模型｜情感空間研究｜PVC板｜14×11×10.5 英吋｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This is the third study in a series on depressive feeling. It starts from the curves of Antelope Canyon and asks how they could be turned into a form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這是「憂鬱感受」系列的第三件研究。它從羚羊峽谷的曲線出發，探問這些曲線如何轉化為形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student photographed Antelope Canyon on a trip and made two oil paintings to mimic the curve of the canyon. Two pencil drawings set curves against straight lines.
captions: An oil painting of the canyon curves.
Pencil drawings of curves through straight lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在旅途中拍攝羚羊峽谷，並畫了兩幅油畫模仿峽谷的曲線。兩張鉛筆畫以曲線對比直線。
captions: 以直線穿過曲線的鉛筆畫。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Shapes were sketched from different angles, and a plaster concept model tested the form.
captions: Sketches of shapes from different angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生從不同角度速寫形體，並以石膏概念模型測試形態。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stacks PVC boards into a waving sculpture. A 2D composition records the canyon's curve and structure, and a drawing shows an interior of intersected lines that reflect the sensitivity of depressed patients.
captions: 2D composition of the canyon's curve and structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以PVC板層疊成一件波動的雕塑。一張二維構圖記錄峽谷的曲線與結構，另一張圖則呈現由交錯線條構成的內部，反映憂鬱患者的敏感。
captions: 峽谷曲線與結構的二維構圖。

sections.heading: Canyon Curves - Layers of Feeling
sections.body: The study moves from a place to a feeling. Photographs and oil paintings of Antelope Canyon captured its curves, pencil drawings set them against straight lines, and sketches and a plaster model tested the form from many angles. The final PVC sculpture builds the waves layer by layer, and a line drawing of its interior links the crossing lines to the sensitivity of depressed patients.

zh-Hant.heading: 峽谷曲線-感受的層次
zh-Hant.body: 這件研究從一個地方走向一種感受。羚羊峽谷的照片與油畫捕捉了它的曲線，鉛筆畫以直線與之對比，速寫與石膏模型則從多個角度測試形體。最終的PVC雕塑一層層堆出波動，一張內部線稿把交錯的線條連結到憂鬱患者的敏感。

pins.title: On the Top of the City
pins.description:
Inspired by Frank Gehry's LV Foundation building, a faceted structure is lifted over the rooftops around Cooper Triangle in New York.

Physical and SketchUp model | Columbia workshop project | Wood sticks, hard papers, PVC boards | 10×8×8 inch | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市之上
zh-Hant.description:
受 Frank Gehry 的 LV 基金會建築啟發，一個多面體結構被架在紐約 Cooper Triangle 周邊的屋頂之上。

實體與 SketchUp 模型｜哥倫比亞大學工作營作品｜木棒、硬紙、PVC板｜10×8×8 英吋｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The structure over the city blocks.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This individual work comes from a Columbia workshop. It looks for a way to build on top of the city, taking Frank Gehry's LV Foundation building as the inspiration.
captions: Inspiration: Frank Gehry's LV Foundation building.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這件個人作品來自哥倫比亞大學的工作營。它以 Frank Gehry 的 LV 基金會建築為靈感，尋找在城市之上構築的方式。
captions: 靈感：Frank Gehry 的 LV 基金會建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site is Cooper Triangle by Cooper Union. A site map and collage marked parks, popular places, traffic, institutions, churches and the mix of modern and traditional buildings around it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地是 Cooper Union 旁的 Cooper Triangle。基地地圖與拼貼標示了周邊的公園、熱門地點、交通、機構、教堂，以及現代與傳統建築的分布。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A study model of wood sticks rested a frame on white blocks. The digital design was developed in four steps, from the buildings around the site to supporting structures and the detailed design.
captions: Four steps of the design process.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一件木棒研究模型把框架架在白色量體上。數位設計分四個步驟發展，從基地周邊建築到支撐結構，再到細部設計。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final structure spans the rooftops on a few supports. A rendering notes light reflection in different colours at different angles and planting on the top of the buildings, and a diagram traces the circulation through it.
captions: Rendering with light reflection and rooftop planting.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終結構以少數支點橫跨屋頂。渲染圖標示不同角度呈現不同顏色的光線反射，以及建築頂部的植栽，另一張圖解則追蹤其中的動線。
captions: 呈現光線反射與屋頂植栽的渲染圖。

sections.heading: Above the Rooftops - A Faceted Canopy
sections.body: The project takes Frank Gehry's LV Foundation building as a starting point and sets its site at Cooper Triangle. Mapping and collage recorded the streets and buildings around it, a stick study model tested how a frame could rest on the blocks, and four digital steps moved from the surroundings to supports and detail. The result is a faceted structure that spans the rooftops, with its circulation, light and planting drawn out in diagrams and renderings.

zh-Hant.heading: 屋頂之上-多面的頂棚
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題以 Frank Gehry 的 LV 基金會建築為起點，把基地設在 Cooper Triangle。地圖與拼貼記錄了周邊的街道與建築，木棒研究模型測試框架如何落在量體上，四個數位步驟則從周邊環境推進到支撐與細部。成果是一個橫跨屋頂的多面結構，其動線、光線與植栽以圖解與渲染呈現。

pins.title: Columbia Summer Immersion
pins.description:
Three weeks of paper folding, High Line mapping and Rhino modelling lead to a porous structure of stairs and glass.

Paper folding, site mapping and Rhino model | Columbia summer program | Paper, digital model | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 哥倫比亞夏季沉浸課程
zh-Hant.description:
三週的摺紙練習、高線公園地圖分析與 Rhino 建模，發展出一個由樓梯與玻璃構成的多孔結構。

摺紙練習、基地地圖與 Rhino 模型｜哥倫比亞大學夏季課程｜紙、數位模型｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Design process: interior, glass, stairs, exterior, complete.
設計過程：內部、玻璃、樓梯、外殼、完成。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The program moved week by week from abstraction and imagination to analysis and synthesis, and then to speculation and intervention.
captions: Week 1: paper folding models and methods.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 課程逐週推進，從抽象與想像，到分析與綜合，再到推想與介入。
captions: 第一週：摺紙模型與方法。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Week 2 mapped the High Line as landscape and cover, marking commercial, residential and industrial areas, landscape features and cover features.
captions: Week 2: the High Line, landscape and cover.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 第二週以「地景與覆蓋」分析高線公園，標示商業、住宅與工業區、地景特徵與覆蓋特徵。
captions: 第二週：高線公園的地景與覆蓋。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Week 3 drew the exterior and two interiors, then set the form beside the High Line in elevations and a perspective view. An exploded axon split the design into its layers.
captions: Week 3: exterior and interior drawings with elevations.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第三週繪製外部與兩個內部，再以立面與透視把形體放到高線公園旁。爆炸軸測圖把設計拆解成各個層次。
captions: 第三週：外部與內部繪圖及立面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The Rhino model is built from an interior, glass, stairs and a porous exterior. A section plan and a series of views follow the stairs through the structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: Rhino 模型由內部、玻璃、樓梯與多孔外殼組成。剖平面與一系列視角沿著樓梯穿越整個結構。

sections.heading: Three Weeks - From Fold to Structure
sections.body: Each week of the program added a layer. Paper folding tested abstraction, a map of the High Line read the site as landscape and cover, and drawings of the exterior and interiors began the intervention. The Rhino model then assembled interior, glass, stairs and exterior into one porous structure, drawn in an exploded axon, a section plan and a sequence of views.
